articles.title: Los sitios web podrán prohibir en un solo paso que OpenAI, Google y Anthropic entrenen IA con su contenido
articles.text:
OpenAI, Google, Microsoft y Anthropic anunciaron el 30 de octubre de 2026 que respetarán una señal común en el archivo robots.txt, con la que los sitios web podrán prohibir en un solo paso que su contenido se use para entrenar sistemas de IA. Hasta ahora, cada sitio debía configurar sus reglas empresa por empresa.
El robots.txt es el archivo donde un sitio indica a los programas que recorren internet qué partes pueden visitar. Las empresas de IA ya lo consultaban, pero cada una con su propio nombre de rastreador, de modo que un editor que quería excluirse de todas debía mantener una lista de reglas separadas.
La nueva señal funciona como una etiqueta de política común. Según The Verge, las cuatro empresas dijeron que impedirán el acceso de sus rastreadores de IA a un sitio que la incluya. La propuesta se discute en el grupo de trabajo sobre preferencias de IA del Grupo de Trabajo de Ingeniería de Internet (IETF), el organismo que fija estándares técnicos de la red.
OpenAI aclaró que la adhesión es voluntaria y que la señal no reemplaza los controles que ya ofrece. Dijo que la aplicará “en los próximos meses” y que dará más detalles cuando lo haga. También instó a otros proveedores de IA a respetarla.
Cada empresa tiene su propio calendario
Anthropic ya adoptó la señal, según The Verge. Google y Microsoft planean admitirla el año próximo, de acuerdo con el mismo medio. OpenAI no dio fecha concreta. Por eso la herramienta todavía no protege a ningún sitio frente a las cuatro compañías a la vez.
Google explicó en su blog para desarrolladores que, si un sitio usa la señal para negarse al entrenamiento y no menciona Google-Extended (su control propio desde 2023), lo tratará como si el editor hubiera bloqueado ese rastreador. La empresa señaló que otros proveedores pueden aplicar un criterio similar.
Los controles individuales seguirán vigentes. Un sitio podría, por ejemplo, excluirse de forma general y a la vez permitir a Google usar su contenido.
Google precisó que los sitios que permiten expresamente Google-Extended pueden aparecer en las respuestas de la aplicación Gemini y recibir clics.
Microsoft, según The Verge, ofrecerá además controles más finos: los editores podrán negarse al entrenamiento o al llamado anclaje, el proceso que conecta a un modelo con una fuente verificada para reducir errores. Los sitios seguirán apareciendo en los resultados de Bing, sin importar su elección.
Meta apoya la idea
Andy Stone, jefe de comunicaciones de Meta, dijo que crear una señal común para varios proveedores es “un paso importante” y que su empresa quiere trabajar con otras compañías de IA en su implementación. The Verge señaló que Stone no aclaró si Meta respetará la señal.
Meta aplazó del 30 de octubre al 20 de noviembre de 2026 la vigencia de unos términos comerciales que autorizan a la empresa a tomar contenido de los sitios web asociados a cuentas empresariales de Facebook e Instagram. Editores y reguladores de Europa solicitaron que fueran suspendidos.
El anuncio llega mientras los editores enfrentan un flujo constante de rastreadores de IA. Anteriormente, habían surgido otras iniciativas: el estándar Really Simple Licensing, que permite a los sitios cobrar a los rastreadores que los visitan, y la decisión de Cloudflare, empresa de infraestructura web, de bloquear por defecto a estos programas.
Google sostuvo que su propuesta responde a pedidos de editores, organizaciones civiles y reguladores, y que es coherente con el código de buenas prácticas de la Unión Europea para modelos de IA de uso general, que reconoce el robots.txt como método para expresar preferencias legibles por máquinas.
Google describió el mecanismo como un borrador en construcción: el IETF sigue discutiendo el resto del vocabulario de preferencias de IA. Google y Microsoft esperan aplicar la señal en 2027, según el medio, mientras que OpenAI publicará los detalles de su implementación en los próximos meses.

articles.title: Syrian Hacker Behind Fake Tweet That Triggered $136 Billion Market Drop Gets 42 Months in Prison
articles.text:
Ahmad Umar Agha, a Syrian Electronic Army hacker known online as "Th3Pr0," has been sentenced by a U.S. federal court to 42 months in prison for his role in a hacking conspiracy that targeted Western news outlets.
The conspiracy was organized and led by members of former Syrian President Bashar al-Assad's inner circle, including the commander of Syria's General Intelligence Directorate, the U.S. Justice Department said on October 29.
The pro-Assad Syrian Electronic Army began its attacks in 2011. Its members sent phishing emails to steal employees' passwords, then used those passwords to deface websites, redirect web traffic, and hijack social media accounts, according to a 2014 FBI affidavit.
On April 23, 2013, the group hijacked the Associated Press's Twitter account and posted a false report that President Barack Obama had been injured in two explosions at the White House.
Twitter's message confirming a password reset for that account was sent to a Gmail account used primarily by Agha, the affidavit says.
The Justice Department said Agha carried out that hack, which caused a temporary $136 billion drop in the value of stocks in the Dow Jones Industrial Average. Agha later told Business Insider that a big drop in the Dow "was our goal of that hack attack" and that "it was a big victory for us."
Agha was first charged in June 2014 in a complaint that remained secret until March 2016. That month, the FBI added him and co-defendant Firas Dardar to its Cyber's Most Wanted list with a $100,000 reward. A federal grand jury indicted both men in May 2018.
Court Watch reported in December 2025 that Agha was in U.S. custody and had appeared in federal court the month before.
Three earlier public documents in the case do not describe Syrian officials organizing or leading the group: the 2014 FBI affidavit, the Justice Department's March 2016 announcement of the charges, and its May 2018 announcement of the indictment.
In the 2016 announcement, the department said the group acted "in support of" the Syrian government.
An early study of the group, published by the OpenNet Initiative, found no credible evidence directly linking the attackers to the Syrian government beyond the unspoken support any such group would need to operate on Syrian networks.
In announcing the sentence, the department also said the conspiracy collected intelligence for Assad's government, which fell in December 2024. "Agha deployed his hacking skills in the service of Assad's regime to silence reporting on the regime's atrocities, intimidate its opponents, and incite U.S. servicemembers to refuse their orders," said John A. Eisenberg, Assistant Attorney General for National Security.
In all, Agha hacked about 47 Western media outlets, businesses, non-profit groups, and U.S. and allied government bodies, the department said.
He got into the company that hosted the U.S. Marine Corps recruiting website and redirected its visitors to an image urging Marines to refuse their orders and fight alongside the Syrian Army. About 3,500 potential visitors saw that image instead of recruiting material.
He also twice tried to take over the White House's social media accounts by stealing White House staff email passwords. Once, he got into staff email but failed to trick other staff into giving him access.
The FBI affidavit describes the group breaking into a White House staff member's personal email account in July 2013 and says no official White House account was compromised.
Many victims spent large sums on cleanup and security upgrades, according to court filings cited by the department. One company that supplies online publishers with content, ads, and links lost about $35,000 a day for about six months. A global non-profit group lost $480,000, including about $250,000 on new network monitoring tools, and had to retrain more than 800 staff members.
Dardar remains a fugitive, the department said. He was also charged in a separate case with Peter Romar, a Syrian national then living in Germany. Romar was extradited to the U.S. and pleaded guilty in 2016.

articles.title: Acer Swift Air 14 : Boulanger allège de 300€ le prix de cet ultrabook poids plume pour le Black Friday
articles.text:
Avec son châssis léger et son écran de 14 pouces, l’ordinateur portable Acer Swift Air 14 est un modèle de portabilité. Même son prix est léger chez Boulanger : il passe de 899,99 € à 599,99 € pour le Black Friday.
Personne n’a envie de transporter un ordinateur portable lourd et encombrant lors de ses déplacements quotidiens. C’est pourquoi l’Acer Swift Air 14 se présente comme un modèle de choix pour les travailleurs nomades : il ne pèse que 1,19 kg. À l’occasion du lancement de son opération Black Friday, Boulanger le propose à 599,99 € au lieu de 899,99 €. C’est la version SFA14-I31-59JG du PC qui est concernée par cette offre : elle embarque un processeur Intel Core 5 320, 8 Go de mémoire vive et un SSD de 512 Go. Cette configuration bureautique fonctionne sous Windows 11.
L’Acer Swift Air 14 SFA14-I31-59JG est à 599,99 € au lieu de 899,99 € chez Boulanger.
Pourquoi choisir l’Acer Swift Air 14 ?
- Pour sa légèreté : ses 1,19 kg et son épaisseur d’environ 1,3 cm le rendent particulièrement facile à transporter au quotidien.
- Pour son écran fluide : la dalle IPS de 14 pouces monte à 120 Hz, ce qui améliore notamment la fluidité du défilement.
- Pour son stockage : le SSD de 512 Go permet de stocker de nombreux documents et d’installer vos logiciels de bureautique.
Un petit format qui soigne le confort de travail
L’écran du Swift Air 14 d’Acer est une dalle IPS qui affiche une définition de 1 920 × 1 200 pixels au format 16:10. Cette configuration permet de profiter d’un peu plus de hauteur pour lire les documents qu’un écran 16:9 plus classique, à largeur égale. La présence d’un traitement mat est également utile en déplacement, puisqu’il limite les reflets. Quant à son clavier rétroéclairé, il facilite la saisie en basse luminosité. Sa connectique comprend deux ports USB4 au format USB-C, un port USB-A et une prise casque. Pour les connexions sans fil, on trouve du Wi-Fi 6E et du Bluetooth 5.3.
Un ultraportable dont les 8 Go de RAM imposent des limites
Ce Swift Air mise sur la mobilité et l’affichage, mais il offre un peu moins de confort en ce qui concerne les usages multitâches. Notre test de l’Acer Swift Air 14 a d’ailleurs confirmé qu’avec 8 Go de RAM seulement, des ralentissements peuvent être constatés sous Windows 11.
✅ Les points forts
- Format léger de 1,19 kg.
- Écran IPS mat au format 16:10 et à 120 Hz
- Clavier rétroéclairé et connectique USB 4.
❌ Les limites
- 8 Go de RAM contraignants sous Windows 11.
- Chargeur secteur vendu séparément.
Pour le Black Friday, l’ultrabook Acer Swift Air 14 passe à 599,99 € chez Boulanger avec la livraison offerte.
L’Acer Swift Air 14 peut convenir aux étudiants et aux utilisateurs mobiles qui font de la transportabilité et du confort de lecture leurs priorités lorsqu’ils utilisent un ordinateur portable. Son clavier rétroéclairé est également un vrai atout.
Cependant, les utilisateurs qui ont l’habitude de jongler entre de nombreuses applications ou d’utiliser des logiciels créatifs risquent de se heurter bien vite aux limites de cette configuration, qui aurait mérité un peu plus de mémoire vive.

articles.title: HP Introduces Series 3 Pro 34-inch 120Hz Ultrawide Professional Monitor with 90 W USB-C Power Delivery
articles.text:
Friday, October 30th 2026
HP Introduces Series 3 Pro 34-inch 120Hz Ultrawide Professional Monitor with 90 W USB-C Power Delivery
HP has introduced the Series 3 Pro 334wp G2 to its monitor lineup, a 34-inch curved ultrawide model for office work. It features a VA panel with a 1500R curve, a WQHD (3440 x 1440) resolution, 120 Hz refresh rate, 3,500:1 contrast, and 300 nits of brightness. Using overdrive, the response time could reach 5 ms GtG. The monitor also works as a USB-C docking display, a single cable can carry video, data, and up to 90 W of power to a laptop. On the connectivity side, it has three USB-A 5 Gbps, one USB-C 5 Gbps with DisplayPort 1.2 Alt Mode, a USB-B upstream, one DisplayPort 1.2, one HDMI 2.0 and an audio jack. HP also added two 5 W speakers in case you need them. There's no webcam or HDR support, and the color gamut is a bit modest, just 85% NTSC coverage. With that color gamut, image or video retouching/editing is possible but not recommended, stick to documents and spreadsheets.
The HP Series 3 Pro 334wp G2 is priced at $329 in the U.S. and comes with a three-year warranty. For comparison, another 34-inch ultrawide docking monitor that just launched, the Lenovo ThinkVision T34WD-4v, is priced higher at €599. However, that model adds a built-in camera, wider color coverage, an ambient light sensor, and Gigabit Ethernet, to name a few.

What is NYT Connections?
NYT Connections is one of several increasingly popular word games made by the New York Times. It challenges you to find groups of four items that share something in common, and each group has a different difficulty level: green is easy, yellow a little harder, blue often quite tough and purple usually very difficult.
On the plus side, you don't technically need to solve the final one, as you'll be able to answer that one by a process of elimination. What's more, you can make up to four mistakes, which gives you a little bit of breathing room.
It's a little more involved than something like Wordle, however, and there are plenty of opportunities for the game to trip you up with tricks. For instance, watch out for homophones and other word games that could disguise the answers.

articles.title: Stickers y mensajes de Halloween para enviar por WhatsApp en 2026
articles.text:
Ya sea para saludar o simplemente pasar un buen rato con los amigos y familiares, los stickers simplifican y amenizan la comunicación por WhatsApp. Ahora, con motivo de Halloween, muchos usuarios disfrutan de enviarse figuras con un tinte más terrorífico.
Stickers para enviar en Halloween
Las siguientes imágenes se descargan en el teléfono. Luego, el usuario debe entrar a un chat de WhatsApp, presionar el botón de stickers, seleccionar “Crear sticker” y finalmente elegir la imagen descargada para hacer la conversión.
Mensajes con temática de Halloween
Para evitar el envío de cadenas de texto extensas, a continuación se detalla una recopilación de frases para WhatsApp. Las opciones se dividen en tres categorías temáticas (suspenso, humor y saludos formales), adaptables según el nivel de confianza con el destinatario.
Las frases fueron generadas por la IA Gemini. Si bien su nivel de creatividad es aceptable, se invita al usuario a crear sus mensajes propios con el inigualable toque humano.
Frases de suspenso y terror breve
- “Esta noche, asegúrate de cerrar bien las puertas. Feliz Halloween.”
- “Las sombras parecen más largas hoy. Que tengas una noche sin sobresaltos.”
- “No mires debajo de la cama antes de dormir. Feliz Noche de Brujas.”
- “Dicen que hoy los límites entre los mundos desaparecen. Mantente alerta esta noche.”
- “Si escuchas pasos a tus espaldas, no te gires. Feliz Halloween.”
- “Que el único terror que experimentes hoy provenga de una película.”
- “Cuidado con lo que invitas a entrar a tu casa durante esta madrugada.”
Mensajes basados en humor
- “Es el único día del año donde puedes mostrarte como eres sin asustar a nadie. Feliz Halloween.”
- “Mi disfraz de este año es el saldo de mi cuenta bancaria. Eso es verdadero terror.”
- “Prepárate para la sobredosis de azúcar. Feliz Noche de Brujas.”
- “No necesito disfraz; con mi cara de lunes por la mañana es suficiente.”
- “Reparte los dulces temprano antes de que termines consumiendo todo el inventario.”
- “Si ves un fantasma en tu casa, exígele que pague su parte del alquiler.”
- “Feliz Halloween. No aceptes tratos con entidades que no paguen impuestos.”
Saludos clásicos y cordiales
- “Te deseo un Feliz Halloween, lleno de dulces y buenos momentos.”
- “Que disfrutes de una noche de brujas segura y entretenida con tu familia.”
- “Feliz 31 de octubre. Que los disfraces superen las expectativas de este año.”
- “Un saludo especial en esta Noche de Brujas. Pásalo excelente.”
- “Deseo que tengas un Halloween divertido y sin contratiempos.”
- “Espero que disfrutes las celebraciones de esta noche. Feliz Halloween.”
‘Modo Halloween’ en WhatsApp
Aunque WhatsApp no cuenta con una función oficial centrada en Halloween, los usuarios de Android e iPhone pueden personalizar la aplicación con una estética temática mediante las herramientas de configuración habituales, sin instalar aplicaciones externas ni versiones modificadas.
Las opciones incluyen cambiar la foto de perfil por imágenes de calabazas, fantasmas o personajes disfrazados, modificar el fondo de pantalla de los chats con ilustraciones de bosques oscuros o casas embrujadas, y ajustar los colores de las conversaciones con tonos naranja, violeta, negro y verde oscuro. Antes de empezar, se recomienda actualizar la aplicación desde Google Play Store o App Store, ya que algunas funciones varían según el modelo del teléfono, la versión y la región.
Quienes tengan acceso a Meta AI dentro de WhatsApp también pueden generar imágenes personalizadas con descripciones de texto, como calabazas iluminadas o escenas de cementerios, para usarlas como fondos o compartirlas en los chats.
Todos estos cambios son exclusivamente visuales: no alteran la privacidad de los mensajes ni las medidas de seguridad de la cuenta. El artículo recomienda, no obstante, evitar fondos muy recargados que dificulten la lectura de los mensajes y tener cuidado al compartir información personal o imágenes de terceros al usar la inteligencia artificial.

articles.title: Official Claude Code Extension on Cursor Marketplace Trojanized with Persistent SSH Backdoor
articles.text:
Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed that a trojanized version of Anthropic's official Claude Code extension was distributed through the Cursor Marketplace as a legitimate update, attempting to install a persistent SSH backdoor on affected systems.
The malicious update, version 2.1.313, was distributed under the extension's legitimate publisher identity, prompting Cursor to temporarily shut down its marketplace to remove the compromised package. The exact method attackers used to introduce the unauthorized update remains unclear.
"We identified a security incident affecting a modified Claude Code VS Code extension accessed through our Cursor IDE extension marketplace, impacting at most 5,000 users," Cursor said. "This malicious version of the extension was not developed by Anthropic. It does not impact other extensions downloaded from the cursor[.]com/marketplace, Grok Bot, Grok, or our other SpaceXSI product.
However, Cursor's statement that the malicious version "was not developed by Anthropic" misses the point. The attackers distributed it as version 2.1.313 under Anthropic's legitimate Claude Code extension ID (anthropic.claude-code), rather than as a separate fake extension.
"The package identifies itself as anthropic.claude-code version 2.1.313, but its main JavaScript bundle contains a malicious 66-line loader inserted before the legitimate extension code," Jenn Gile, co-founder of OpenSourceMalware, said in a statement shared with The Hacker News.
The malicious update was distributed only through Cursor's marketplace, with no evidence that it reached Open VSX or Microsoft's official VS Code Marketplace. Users who installed Claude Code through either of those marketplaces are not known to be affected by this incident.
As of October 30, 2026, the malicious version has been removed, and Anthropic has published version 2.1.314 to both Open VSX and Microsoft VS Code Marketplace.
The extension is designed to activate after VS Code startup and when its webview opens, then proceeds to add an attacker-controlled key to the user's "~/.ssh/authorized_keys" file. The key is labeled "svc-telemetry" in an attempt to make it appear harmless.
Subsequently, it attempts to make the victim reachable through SSH across Windows, Linux, and macOS, establishes a reverse tunnel to "134.209.82[.]225," installs platform-specific persistence in the form of a scheduled task, crontab, and LaunchAgent, and transmits host reconnaissance data to "134.209.82[.]225:8099/beacon" on port 8099 over an unencrypted HTTP request.
"Turning on the local SSH service requires admin rights, which the malicious extension does not have on most macOS and Windows hosts," the SpaceXAI-owned company said in its own analysis of the incident.
"On those hosts the step fails and the attacker could not have logged in through the tunnel. The extension still adds the attacker's SSH key, installs persistence, and sends host details to the attacker. Follow the remediation steps below regardless."
The collected data includes -
- Public IP address from api.ipify[.]org
- Hostname and local username
- Operating system and CPU architecture
- Home directory and current working directory
- Global Git email from git config --global user.email
- Names of up to 40 environment variables containing KEY, TOKEN, SECRET, PASS, AWS, or GCP
"Environment-variable values are not placed directly in the initial beacon," security researcher Paul McCarty said. "Their names can still reveal which cloud providers, CI systems, and credential types are configured. More importantly, successful SSH access would allow the operator to inspect the account directly."
No other follow-on payloads have been observed. That said, the establishment of a reverse tunnel provides a pathway to the victim's SSH service, allowing the operator to issue commands or transfer files.
"It was pulled very quickly, but anyone who has their Claude Code instance set to auto-update could have consumed the malware," Gile said.
Cursor has revealed that the incident has affected at most 5,000 users who installed the malicious version between about 2:27 a.m. and 1:35 p.m. PT on October 29, 2026. The company also said that it will be reaching out to impacted users directly.
Users who have installed the compromised extension during the window are advised to isolate the hosts, remove the unauthorized SSH key and persistence mechanisms, and rotate credentials and sessions.
The disclosure comes a little over a week after an unknown attacker replaced the release binaries of five already-published versions of OVHcloud's official CLI ("ovh/ovhcloud-cli") with a secret-stealing malware after uploading them through a GitHub account of a legitimate OVH contributor ("HassenBF") hijacked in March 2026 as part of the GlassWorm operation.
(An earlier version of the story stated that the extension on the Open VSX registry was compromised. The incident has since been traced back to a compromise of the Cursor VS Code Marketplace.)

articles.title: Voitures électriques : au Portugal, elles pourraient bientôt être financées à 80% par l'État. Et en France ?
articles.text:
Les États veulent pousser le plus possible leurs citoyens vers les véhicules électriques. Au point de réfléchir à massivement aider au niveau financier !
Il faut le plus rapidement possible faire passer le parc automobile du thermique à l'électrique. Voilà l'idée générale en Europe. Mais pour y arriver, les stratégies sont multiples, des interdictions aux subventions. Dans ce domaine, si l'on a déjà de bonnes aides en France, on pourrait vite apparaître comme des petits joueurs avec ce qui pourrait se passer au Portugal !
Le Portugal voudrait subventionner jusqu'à 80% du prix d'un véhicule électrique pour les ménages les plus modestes
Au Portugal, on pourrait sortir l'artillerie lourde au niveau des aides pour les voitures électriques. À l'occasion des débats sur le budget 2027, la ministre de l'Environnement et de l'Énergie Maria da Graça Carvalho a ainsi indiqué que le gouvernement réfléchit à augmenter spectaculairement les aides.
Ainsi, les ménages les plus modestes du Portugal pourraient bien bénéficier d'un soutien qui représentera jusqu'à 80% du prix d'un nouveau véhicule électrique. Une façon de mettre fin au barrage représenté par le prix pour de nombreuses personnes.
Un plafond à 15 000 € HT imposé
Cette aide exceptionnelle pourrait concerner environ 20 000 véhicules. Il faut tout de même noter que les potentiels bénéficiaires ne pourront pas faire leur choix parmi tout ce qui existe. Ce soutien est réservé à l'acquisition d'un véhicule coûtant moins ou 15 000 € HT - ce qui pourrait par exemple inclure la Renault Twingo E-Tech.
À noter que le Portugal a aussi d'autres aides plus classiques, qui touchent elles l'ensemble de la population - le gouvernement veut ainsi allouer 50 millions d'euros aux enveloppes dédiées à l'ensemble des Portugais. La France pourrait-elle prendre exemple sur ce pays du sud de l'Europe, et doubler les aides actuelles avec un subventionnement beaucoup plus fort pour les ménages les plus modestes, qui peuvent à ce jour avoir jusqu'à 7700 euros d'aides ?
Source : Automobile Propre

articles.title: OLED TVs over 100 inches might finally be coming, and it might help bring the price of 77 and 83-inch sizes down too — LG Display and its partner are reportedly investing 1 billion extra yuan to upgrade large OLED panel production
articles.text:
The dream home theater TV? 111-inch OLED TVs might be coming, as LG finally explores going beyond the 97-inch limit — but what will the performance be like?
Giant OLED TVs could finally become affordable as LG Display commits to truly enormous OLEDs — but does bigger mean better?
- LG Display is investing heavily in OLED production up to 111 inches
- Current LG OLEDs top out at 97 inches
- Today's 97-inch panel is much older tech than smaller panels
If you're looking for home theater-size OLED TVs, you'll soon encounter two hard limits: availability and affordability. You can't currently buy an OLED larger than 97 inches because nobody makes them.
And you probably can't afford a 97-inch OLED TV because it's terrifyingly expensive: today LG is listing its 97-inch OLED for $19,999 (reduced from $24,999) / £15,999. But it looks like both of those things are about to change.
LG Display is reportedly investing big money in big OLED, though: it and its partner Guangzhou Development Zone Holding Group are reportedly investing an extra 1 billion yuan to upgrade its production facilities for giant OLED displays.
As FlatpanelsHD reports, the market analysis company TrendForce says that the announced upgrades mainly target "large-size OLED module manufacturing, with products covering 77-inch, 83-inch, 97-inch, and 111-inch," with the ability to debut a 111-inch panel being a "major highlight of the project."
Bigger and potentially more affordable TVs are always welcome. But we do have some questions.
What panel is LG intending to use?
The big question for us is whether the investment will mean improvements to the existing 97-inch panel's technology.
The 2026 version of LG's 97-inch OLED TV is a 4K native panel with a native refresh rate of 120Hz, but while the model is the LG G6, its panel is not the same as its smaller siblings: they all get LG's Primary RGB Tandem 2.0 panel, but the 97-inch is an older, non-Tandem panel — in fact it dates back to the LG G2 from 2022, so it's several generations behind. That means it isn't as bright and doesn't have the same color accuracy as the other models.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
That difference is important, because these large OLEDs are up against some of the best mini-LED and increasingly, RGB mini-LED TVs — and those TVs are exceptionally bright and accurate as well as increasingly affordable. It's possible to buy high-quality 98-inch Hisense TV for just $3,999, which is a lot for a TV but not a lot for a 98-inch one — and is obvious just a fraction of the 97-inch OLED price.
We're keeping our fingers crossed here: if LG Display breaks the size barrier and makes ultra-large Tandem RGB TVs that are less expensive to manufacture, that'd be great. The worst case scenario is that we get the same kind of panel that's currently in the 97-incher, but a bit bigger — but it seems like that the aim is to upgrade the technology, given that production of smaller sizes was mentioned as a goal as well.
And that might be the bigger win from the project for most of us: if the project succeeds in making producing 111-inch OLED viable, and therefore improves the process and lowers the cost of 77-inch and 83-inch models too, that's probably the real benefit.

articles.title: Hackers Actively Exploit Highly Critical Drupal Commerce Core Authorization Bypass Flaw
articles.text:
Drupal has warned that threat actors are exploiting a "highly critical" security flaw in its Commerce Core component.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-118539 (CVSS score: N/A), is a case of missing authorization affecting Commerce Core versions from 0.0.0 to 2.41 and from 3.0.0 to 3.3.13.
"This module enables you to sell goods and services to customers through an included shopping cart and checkout form or through decoupled applications via APIs," Drupal said in an advisory.
"The module doesn't sufficiently protect certain routes and entity fields, leading to an access bypass that may financially impact the vendor."
The open-source content-management framework acknowledged that the vulnerability is being "actively exploited in the wild," but provided no specifics about the nature of the activity or the extent of the campaign.
Users are being recommended to update to the latest version -
- Version 3.x - Upgrade to Commerce Core 3.3.13
- Earlier versions - Upgrade to Commerce Core 8.x-2.41
Drupal has credited researchers Dan Puccetti (dpuccetti), Marcus Johansson (marcus_johansson), and Robert Snyder (rsnyd) with reporting the flaw.
The development comes as two critical vulnerabilities in PHP, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS scores: 9.2), and collectively referred to as PHP2Shell, are witnessing active exploitation attempts in the wild.
As of October 25, the percentage of organizations significantly affected by PHP2Shell has declined to 52.1%, according to data from Google-owned Wiz.
The cloud security company said it has so far observed two types of activities, including attempts using the PHP2Shell exploit mechanism that match public proof-of-concept (PoC) exploits.
The other category refers to "PHP2Shell-branded tools unrelated to the vulnerabilities that instead relied on session poisoning and a separate local file inclusion (LFI) vulnerability in the application," Wiz researchers Yaara Shriki, Shahar Dorfman, Alma Blachsan, and Yaron Samuel said.
"Our observations show that triggering memory exhaustion alone is not enough to complete the exploit chain. Differences in PHP builds, memory limits and worker behavior can prevent subsequent stages from working. The challenge for opportunistic attackers is turning currently available public PoCs into similarly reliable operational tooling or developing it on their own."

articles.title: Steam regala un nuevo juego de terror por tiempo limitado: cómo descargar Asleep Acto 1
articles.text:
Steam ofrece gratis Asleep: Acto 1 por tiempo limitado. Los usuarios pueden añadir a su biblioteca este juego de terror psicológico antes de que concluya la promoción y conservarlo en su cuenta.
La oferta estará disponible hasta el día 2 de noviembre de 2026, según indica la página de Steam. El título, desarrollado por Black Hole Games y editado por CriticalLeap, fue lanzado el 9 de mayo de 2022.
Asleep: Acto 1 sitúa al jugador en el nordeste de Brasil durante los años 90 y sigue la historia de Ana Lúcia, una joven que se mueve entre pesadillas y una realidad perturbadora. El juego combina gráficos pixelados con animaciones fluidas y mecánicas de sigilo.
Cómo acceder a este juego gratis
Para obtener Asleep: Acto 1, los usuarios deben ingresar a la página del juego en la tienda de Steam e iniciar sesión con su cuenta. Allí aparecerá la opción “Añadir a la cuenta” junto al descuento del 100%.
Una vez seleccionada esa opción, el juego quedará asociado de forma permanente a la biblioteca del usuario, siempre que el proceso se complete antes de que venza la promoción.
Steam también ofrece una demostración de Asleep, aunque esta es una descarga distinta de la edición gratuita de Asleep: Acto 1. Para conservar el primer episodio, es necesario elegir específicamente la opción de añadir el juego a la cuenta.
De qué trata este juego gratis de Steam
La aventura pone al jugador en la piel de Ana Lúcia, una chica solitaria y confundida que intenta comprender qué ocurre en el universo que la rodea. Con poca información y una mente al límite, deberá reunir pistas en un cuaderno de bocetos y resolver acertijos.
La linterna es una de las herramientas centrales de Asleep: Acto 1. La luz permite descubrir objetos, iluminar zonas ocultas y reaccionar ante los enemigos que acechan en la oscuridad.
Cada monstruo responde de una manera diferente a la iluminación. Por eso, el jugador debe usar mecánicas de sigilo para evitar los peligros y aprender cuándo conviene atraer o esquivar a cada amenaza.
Qué requisitos deben cumplir las PC para jugar este título
En computadoras con Windows, Asleep: Acto 1 requiere un sistema operativo de 64 bits, Windows 7 o una versión posterior, un procesador Intel Core i3 M380, 1 GB de memoria RAM y una tarjeta gráfica Intel HD 4000.
El juego también necesita DirectX en su versión 10 y 1 GB de espacio disponible en el almacenamiento. Steam aclara que el cliente de la plataforma solo es compatible con Windows 10 y versiones posteriores.
Como configuración recomendada, la página de Steam mantiene el requisito de un procesador y sistema operativo de 64 bits, además de DirectX 10 y 2 GB de espacio disponible. El título no es compatible con realidad virtual.
Para macOS, el título requiere OS X Lion 10.7.5 en versiones de 32 o 64 bits, un procesador Intel Core i3 M380, 1 GB de memoria RAM y compatibilidad con OpenGL 3.0 o superior, o OpenGL 2.1 con extensiones ARB aceptables.
En equipos Mac, Asleep: Acto 1 necesita 1 GB de espacio disponible como requisito mínimo y 2 GB de almacenamiento recomendado.
CEO de Epic Games arremete contra los dueños de Steam
Tim Sweeney, CEO de Epic Games, acusó a Valve de frenar la industria de videojuegos para PC al mantener un ecosistema cerrado alrededor de Steam.
La disputa surgió tras críticas a la comisión del 30% que cobra la plataforma y a la dependencia de los estudios de sus herramientas y usuarios.
Sweeney defendió un modelo abierto que facilite la comunicación entre jugadores de distintas plataformas y permita colaboraciones entre juegos.
Cuestionó la obligación de Steam de informar si un título usó inteligencia artificial, al considerar que esas etiquetas podrían perjudicar a los desarrolladores.

articles.title: A human subject has been injected with an AI-designed virus aiming to kill antibiotic-resistant bacteria, so let's see how that turns out
articles.text:
A human subject has been injected with an AI-designed virus aiming to kill antibiotic-resistant bacteria, so let's see how that turns out
Welcome to clinical AI in 2026
- San Francisco lab Radical Numerics says its Omnii-1 model designed bacteriophages that were given to a patient with a drug-resistant infection, a world first
- The phages were built by rewriting the gene for T7's tail fiber, the protein the virus uses to latch onto bacteria
- Nobody outside the company knows whether it worked, because the results have not been published, peer-reviewed, or disclosed yet
Radical Numerics has announced its AI-designed viruses (bacteriophages) were given to a sick person, but has not provided much further insight about what happened next.
The San Francisco AI lab announced in October 2026 that bacteriophages designed by its new genome model had been administered to a human patient with an antibiotic-resistant bacterial infection, under a physician-led compassionate-use pathway authorized by the FDA.
If the claim holds, it is the first time an AI-designed organism of any kind has been put into a person as medicine.
Not a new phenomenon, but one that could do with AI assistance
Bacteriophages are viruses that infect bacteria and ignore human cells entirely. They have been used as therapy for more than a century, predating penicillin, and have enjoyed a quiet revival as antibiotics have begun to fail.
The World Health Organization considers phage therapy broadly safe, and unlike broad-spectrum antibiotics, a phage can target one bacterial strain while leaving the rest of your microbiome alone.
That precision is also the problem: each phage recognizes a narrow set of bacterial surface receptors, so treating a patient means finding one that matches their specific infection. Clinicians screen existing phage libraries, then environmental samples, then give up and try engineering as a last resort. For someone with sepsis, that search is not an academic exercise but an important life-or-death situation.
The scale of the underlying problem is not in dispute. The Global Burden of Disease project estimated that antimicrobial resistance was associated with roughly 4.7 million deaths in 2021, with projections indicating that between 2025 and 2050, close to 40 million deaths could be attributable to it.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Radical Numerics was founded by members of the team behind Evo and Evo 2, the Arc Institute genome models that generated the first entirely AI-written phage genomes. That earlier work produced 700,000 candidate genomes; 285 were synthesized, and 16 produced viable viruses. It was a proof of concept with a punishing, yet promising hit rate.
Omnii-1 is the follow-up, and the company's technical write-up describes a narrower, more surgical approach. Rather than inventing whole genomes, the model edits the targeting component. The team worked with T7, a well-characterized 40-kilobase E. coli phage, and rewrote gp17, the receptor-binding tail fiber.
The numbers the company is willing to share are genuinely interesting. At 11 to 15 amino acid changes from wild type, 69.9% of designed variants were recovered as viable phages, against 4.8% for random controls. Of 6,694 variants with measurable activity, 2,161 beat the original, including some carrying 28 amino acid substitutions.
A promising, but unproven and unpublished play
The company tested its designed cocktail against bacteria isolated from a real patient's infection, confirmed it eliminated that isolate in vitro, and then administered it. The patient reportedly had an E. coli infection that had resisted not only antibiotics but every available phage, which is effectively the worst position one can be in when it comes to infectious diseases.
Radical Numerics has since declined to describe the patient's clinical course, outcome, hospital, or physicians, citing patient privacy and the fact that even limited clinical detail could identify the patient.
The company self-published the technical report on its website and has not had it peer-reviewed, but has separately indicated the treatment is proprietary and something it hopes to commercialize.
That silence held as of October 29, nine days after the announcement, when trade coverage for infectious disease clinicians still reported no disclosed clinical course, no outcome, and no peer-reviewed publication. The technical write-up remains the only account of the case.
In fairness to Radical Numerics, its own write-up states plainly that single-patient observations cannot establish safety or efficacy, which is more cautionary than most product launches manage. CEO Eric Nguyen has also said the company intends to publish through peer review.
Outside experts have landed somewhere between intrigued and unconvinced, which is the correct place to land. Harvard microbiologist Michael Baym, who was not involved, said the result would be incredible if it works, but added that his instinct is skepticism until the treatment finishes and the viruses' novelty can actually be examined.
The commercial logic is much easier to establish; phage hunting is slow, and Radical Numerics believes it can compress design to days rather than months.
Ottawa Hospital infectious disease clinician Marisa Azad, who is collaborating with the company, has described the conventional search as remarkably time-consuming, and she is not wrong. If AI can reliably shorten that loop, it changes who gets treated in time, allowing for a more cost-effective and broader audience for said treatments.
There is cause for some concern too: a model that can design viruses to order is, structurally, a model that can design viruses to order. Radical Numerics acknowledges this directly by committing to biosafety, containment, and data-sharing measures scaled to the model's capability.
It is the same dual-use problem that has dogged every capable biological design tool, and one that AI labs have been publicly wrestling with as their systems get better at biology.
Engineered phages have reached patients before, most famously a 2019 case in which modified phages treated a disseminated drug-resistant Mycobacterium abscessus infection. What is new here is not the therapeutic concept but the design process, and the governance questions attach to the AI-driven process, not the concept itself.
AI has moved from reading biology to writing it and handing the result to a doctor. That is a different category of claim than an AI model proposing a cancer hypothesis or outperforming specialists on rare-disease diagnosis, both of which keep a human firmly in the loop before anything enters a bloodstream.
For now, however, a very clever experiment was run on a very sick person, and we still don't know how it went or when somebody decides to tell us. If it does pan out however, it will have massive rammifications for an industry that is only expected to grow across the next few decades.

articles.title: iPhone Air 2 : une nouvelle fuite révèle ses caractéristiques clés
articles.text:
On commence à en savoir plus sur le prochaine iPhone Air 2 d'Apple. Et il devrait ne pas décevoir niveau performances !
Au début de l'année prochaine, Apple continuera ses sorties de smartphones. Après les iPhone 18 Pro, puis le tout premier appareil pliable iPhone Duo, ce sont les iPhone 18, iPhone 18e et iPhone 18 Air qui vont voir le jour au printemps prochain. Et ce dernier commence petit à petit à se dévoiler, que ce soit au niveau de sa très grande finesse, ou, aujourd'hui, de ses spécificités techniques.
La même puce A20 que l'iPhone Duo au programme pour l'iPhone Air 2
Ceux qui aiment la finesse de l'iPhone Air 2 vont apprécier cette nouvelle fuite, qu'on doit au leaker chinois connu Digital Chat Station - qui a posté les informations dans un message sur le réseau social Weibo.
On apprend ainsi que l'iPhone Air 2 aura droit à une dalle OLED de 6,55 pouces, avec un taux de rafraîchissement de 120 hertz. Information capitale, ce modèle aura lui aussi droit sous le capot à la puce A20, gravée en 2 nanomètres, et qu'embarquent les monstres iPhone 18 Pro et l'iPhone Duo.
L'iPhone Air 2 aura droit à une plus grosse batterie
L'appareil photo sera lui amélioré, comme l'affirmaient les informations qui trainent depuis quelques temps sur internet. L'iPhone Air 2 aura ainsi droit à un double capteur pour son module photo arrière, avec un capteur grand angle de 48 Mpx et un ultra grand angle de 48 Mpx.
L'autonomie sera par ailleurs elle aussi revue à la hausse. Pour rappel, l'iPhone Air bénéficiait d'une batterie de 3 149 mAh. Cet iPhone Air 2 par contre lui arrivera sur le marché avec une batterie de 3 500 mAh. Enfin, toujours d'après la même source, il ne faudra pas s'attendre à une révolution dans l'allure de l'appareil, puisqu'il empruntera le design déjà connu de l'iPhone Air originel.
Source : GSMArena

articles.title: AMD Reportedly Plans Another Radeon GPU and GDDR6 Kit Price Hike for November
articles.text:
Friday, October 30th 2026
AMD Reportedly Plans Another Radeon GPU and GDDR6 Kit Price Hike for November
AMD is reportedly getting ready to raise prices on its Radeon GPU and GDDR6 memory kits again in November. According to a new post from Board Channels, the increase would follow an earlier adjustment in October, when AMD apparently started charging its board partners more for GDDR6 from October 1. The exact scope of the November hike isn't known yet. The main reason seems to be memory, since GDDR6 prices reportedly went up by around 8 to 10% in the third quarter. Board Channels also claims AMD now reviews its kit pricing every quarter to keep up with rising GPU and memory costs. AMD sells its GPUs to add-in board partners bundled with memory, so any increase there usually ends up in the price of the finished card. 
This would add to a long list of reported increases this year. A 10% hike on Radeon GPU kits was reported for July, another 10% increase across GPUs, chipsets, and possibly CPUs followed in September, and AMD's suggested Radeon prices in China went up in early October. Retail prices are already moving, too. According to Hardware Unboxed's latest pricing survey, cited by Videocardz, the RX 9060 XT 16 GB costs 17% more than it did in September, while the RX 9070 and RX 9070 XT are up 12%. Of course, AMD hasn't officially confirmed any of this. How much the November change affects store prices will depend on board partner pricing and existing inventory, so buyers who were already planning on a Radeon RX 9000 card might want to buy sooner rather than later.
Sources:

articles.title: CISA Adds Actively Exploited GitLab RCE and Cisco Firewall DoS Flaws to KEV
articles.text:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Thursday added two security flaws impacting Cisco and GitLab software to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV), citing evidence of active exploitation.
The vulnerabilities are listed below -
- CVE-2026-97229 (CVSS score: 10.0) - An integer overflow or wraparound vulnerability in GitLab Community Edition and Enterprise Edition that could allow an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary code on the GitLab server via a specially crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration due to insufficient regular expression validation.
- CVE-2026-76418 (CVSS score: 8.6) - An unchecked return value to NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in Cisco Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) Software and Secure Firewall Threat Defense (FTD) Software that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause the device to reload unexpectedly, resulting in a denial-of-service (DoS) condition.
The development comes after Cisco said it became aware of active exploitation of this vulnerability earlier this month. It has not publicly identified the attackers, the number of targeted organizations, or the actions taken by attackers after gaining initial access.
As for CVE-2026-97229, its addition relates to a security incident disclosed by Alpine Linux in which an unknown threat actor unsuccessfully attempted to exploit the flaw targeting its instance on October 20 and 21, 2026.
Specifically, the attacker probed an unpatched GitLab instance by sending crafted CI configurations, causing the GitLab worker processes to crash eight times. In four of those crashes, the exploit failed at the next step.
The threat actor also downloaded Alpine Linux's GitLab container image. Subsequent attempts by the attacker to get back in on October 25 and 26 were blocked.
"The attack came close to working," the maintainers of the security-focused Linux distribution said. "We have found no evidence that it succeeded, but we cannot rule it out, so we treated the instance as compromised and rebuilt it from scratch. Our checks show that the aports repository, packages, and the October 21 releases were not tampered with."
In light of active exploitation, Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies are recommended to apply the fixes by November 1, 2026.

articles.title: NVIDIA peut-il confisquer l’IA ? La justice enquête sur le rachat de Hugging Face à 13 milliards
articles.text:
Le géant de la tech prévoit de débourser près de 13 milliards de dollars pour la plateforme de modèles d’IA. Les autorités américaines enquêtent sur les avantages qu’il pourrait en tirer face à ses rivaux, qui utilisent eux aussi les services d'Hugging Face.
Déjà incontournable pour faire tourner les modèles d’IA, NVIDIA veut aussi acheter l’une des principales plateformes qui les distribuent. Annoncé le 3 septembre dernier pour 12,93 milliards de dollars, le rachat de Hugging Face fait l’objet, selon Reuters, d’une enquête du département américain de la Justice.
Les autorités cherchent à déterminer si cette acquisition donnerait au groupe de Jensen Huang les moyens de désavantager ses concurrents. Les deux entreprises espèrent boucler l’opération au premier semestre 2027, sous réserve des autorisations réglementaires nécessaires.
Une plateforme ouverte que les rivaux de NVIDIA utilisent aussi
Hugging Face, fondé par trois Français, est devenu un lieu de passage pour les développeurs d’IA, qui y trouvent des modèles et des jeux de données pour leurs projets. D’après les chiffres communiqués par NVIDIA, la plateforme rassemble plus de 18 millions d’utilisateurs et 200 000 entreprises, avec plus de trois millions de modèles hébergés. Parmi ses utilisateurs figurent aussi des fabricants de puces et des fournisseurs de puissance de calcul concurrents de NVIDIA.
L'entreprise assure toutefois que la plateforme restera ouverte aux autres fabricants de puces et que son matériel ne sera pas obligatoire pour y développer ou déployer des modèles.
Le rôle central de Hugging Face auprès des développeurs explique l’intérêt d’un rachat à près de 13 milliards de dollars, pour des revenus annualisés estimés à 150 millions de dollars. NVIDIA, déjà actionnaire minoritaire de la start-up depuis 2023, s’offrirait un accès privilégié à un vaste écosystème de développeurs. Hugging Face y gagnerait de son côté les moyens financiers et la puissance de calcul nécessaires à son développement. Clément Delangue, cofondateur et dirigeant de Hugging Face, a d'ailleurs expliqué sur CNBC avoir lui-même approché Jensen Huang durant l’été.
Une enquête qui dépasse largement Hugging Face
L'enquête porte notamment sur le pouvoir que NVIDIA pourrait exercer en contrôlant ce canal de diffusion des modèles, selon Reuters. CNBC a également confirmé l’existence de l’enquête auprès d'une autre source. Aucune infraction au droit de la concurrence n’est établie à ce stade.
Les autorités examinent plus largement les acquisitions, investissements et pratiques commerciales du groupe. Elles s’intéressent notamment à l’accord de 17 milliards de dollars conclu avec Groq en décembre 2025, qui prévoit une licence technologique non exclusive et le recrutement de nombreux salariés, sans rachat de l’entreprise. Les enquêteurs chercheraient à savoir si certains clients obtenaient davantage de puces NVIDIA en achetant aussi ses équipements réseau et des processeurs Groq.
Deux autres acquisitions sont par ailleurs scrutées : celles de Run:ai, dont les logiciels répartissent les ressources des puces graphiques, et de SchedMD, qui développe un logiciel libre pour organiser le travail de grands ensembles de serveurs. De quoi occuper quelques neurones naturels à Washington…
- Vaste catalogue de modèles IA
- Démonstrations accessibles dans le navigateur
- Hébergement de jeux de données

articles.title: Drones con tecnología láser descubren refugios aborígenes milenarios ocultos en los bosques de Australia
articles.text:
La protección de testimonios culturales milenarios enfrenta la barrera de la geografía agreste. En vastas regiones del planeta, valiosos sitios arqueológicos permanecen ocultos bajo densos mantos vegetales y precipicios inaccesibles para las búsquedas a pie. Frente a este desafío en Australia, un equipo científico logró identificar tres refugios aborígenes desconocidos mediante drones con tecnología láser en las Montañas Azules.
Este hallazgo marca un avance significativo para la preservación patrimonial, al comprobar que herramientas aéreas avanzadas pueden documentar enclaves históricos resguardados durante milenios por el aislamiento geográfico. Hasta el momento, rastrear estos abrigos rocosos, cavidades naturales en paredes de piedra que funcionaron como resguardo y espacios ceremoniales para las comunidades originarias, dependía de extenuantes caminatas de inspección terrestre.
La topografía accidentada y la densa vegetación de la cordillera impidieron durante décadas un registro sistemático. Aunque el área reúne más de doscientos refugios catalogados con vestigios de ocupación humana, los especialistas calculan que apenas el diez por ciento del territorio ha sido relevado a fondo. Esta limitación mantenía la incógnita sobre la cantidad real de yacimientos y su estado ante factores como la erosión, los incendios y el avance urbano.
El nuevo avance técnico resuelve esta dificultad mediante el uso coordinado de vehículos aéreos no tripulados, análisis informático de datos espaciales y verificación arqueológica en el terreno. La investigación, difundida en un estudio publicado en la revista Remote Sensing, demuestra que los sensores aerotransportados consiguen penetrar el follaje más cerrado para cartografiar formaciones geológicas antes invisibles. La relevancia del trabajo radica en el hallazgo de paneles de arte rupestre intactos y en la comprobación de un método veloz que agiliza la protección de bienes ancestrales sin perturbar el entorno natural.
La tecnología de pulsos láser penetra la espesa vegetación para revelar abrigos ocultos
El operativo se apoyó en un sensor aerotransportado de pulsos lumínicos acoplado a un dron industrial de gran porte. Este instrumental emite millones de haces de luz por segundo hacia el suelo boscoso. Gran parte de estos pulsos choca contra las copas de los árboles, es decir, el dosel superior que cubre los valles, pero una fracción se filtra entre el follaje y rebota en la roca sólida.
Al registrar el tiempo exacto que tarda cada destello en regresar, un programa informático calcula la elevación del terreno y descarta digitalmente las ramas, lo que permite advertir hendiduras que sugieren la existencia de cavernas bajo los farallones. La información captada en vuelo alimentó modelos digitales procesados en sistemas de información geográfica, esto es, programas diseñados para clasificar y cruzar variables espaciales en distintas capas analíticas.
“Este trabajo es emocionante porque ofrece una vía eficiente y precisa para localizar sitios en entornos escarpados que son notoriamente difíciles, costosos y lentos de relevar”, afirmó Jacob Bongers, arqueólogo digital de la Universidad de Sídney y autor principal de la investigación, según el comunicado de prensa.
El análisis aéreo permitió además rectificar coordenadas imprecisas en los registros oficiales. De este modo, “proporciona una metodología eficiente para corregir datos anteriores y localizar abrigos rocosos no registrados”, según se detalla en el estudio.
El trabajo conjunto con custodios tradicionales permitió registrar arte rupestre inédito
El sensor aéreo, sin embargo, solo detecta formas geológicas: no puede distinguir si una cavidad aloja restos culturales o carece de valor arqueológico. Por eso, la eficacia del proyecto radicó en el trabajo conjunto con la Corporación Aborigen de Custodios Dharug. Ambas partes conformaron la iniciativa Gulamada (cuyo principio fundacional es caminar a la par), que articula la ciencia con la tutela nativa sobre tierras ancestrales.
“Desde el principio, nuestra visión para el Proyecto Gulamada ha sido crear un verdadero nexo de ciencia y cultura. Este trabajo destaca la importancia de escuchar, aprender y trabajar juntos”, afirmó Wayne Brennan, codirector del proyecto y experto en arte rupestre indígena de la Universidad de Sídney, según el comunicado de prensa.
Guiados por las coordenadas del dron, los equipos marcharon hacia los puntos señalados para verificar el contenido de los recintos. La inspección sobre el terreno corroboró la posición exacta de seis refugios ya conocidos y descubrió tres abrigos rocosos jamás catalogados. En su interior hallaron herramientas de piedra y paneles con siluetas de manos en negativo elaboradas con pigmento rojo.
La participación directa de los custodios tradicionales garantizó que el registro de estas pinturas milenarias se realizara bajo protocolos de respeto comunitario, lo que previene que la difusión de datos espaciales exponga estos santuarios a visitas no autorizadas o actos de vandalismo.
La prospección aérea agiliza la protección de sitios amenazados en toda la región
La capacidad de relevar áreas agrestes con rapidez resulta crucial ante incendios forestales periódicos y meteorización, amenazas que deterioran bienes arqueológicos irremplazables. Disponer de cartografía tridimensional precisa antes de catástrofes naturales o desarrollos urbanos permite a las comunidades y a los organismos de preservación delimitar zonas prioritarias de resguardo con una exactitud inalcanzable para las cuadrillas terrestres en tiempos razonables.
Los especialistas prevén aplicar este método en otras regiones de Australia, como las sabanas de Arnhem y los sectores semiáridos de Nueva Gales del Sur, para salvaguardar territorios ancestrales antes de que ocurran daños ambientales.
De hecho, “nuestra metodología promueve un relevamiento específico y eficiente de abrigos rocosos que puede producir conjuntos de datos regionales beneficiosos para las comunidades locales, la arqueología y la gestión del patrimonio cultural”, el trabajo concluye.

articles.title: Mchose Launches Updated Ace68 V2 HE Keyboard as $69 Wooting 60HE Alternative
articles.text:
Friday, October 30th 2026
Mchose Launches Updated Ace68 V2 HE Keyboard as $69 Wooting 60HE Alternative
Mchose has officially updated its Ace68, its fan-favorite affordable alternative to the Wooting 60HE. The Ace68 V2 features the same 68-key layout and 60HE-inspired design—replete with a strap and an angled front edge—as the old Ace68, but there are a few additions that make the Ace68 V2 stand out. For one, there is now a dedicated hardware rapid trigger button on the back edge, making it much easier to switch between different tasks, like gaming and work or between different games where different rapid trigger configurations may be beneficial. In addition to the functional changes, there is also a new metal strip along the edge for a bit of visual flavor. 
The Mchose hasn't specified a case material for the Ace68 V2, but the weight and price suggest it has a plastic bottom case, although it lacks the flip-out feet of its predecessor. The Ace68 V2 comes in white, black, or pink, with each featuring matching frosted translucent PC keycaps. The pink and white versions are available with Star Ring or Royal Steed magnetic switches, while the black keyboard is restricted to the Royal Steeds. Both switches are linear, but the Star Ring features a box stem and 33 gf actuation force, while the Royal Steed has a cylindrical stem with 35 gf actuation force. The switches are fitted in an aluminium switch plate that is mounted in a tray-mount configuration.The inside of the Ace68 V2's case is stuffed with sound-damping materials, including a silicone sandwich pad, PET sheet, fiber switch pad, PET base pad, case foam, and silicone case pad. The keyboard itself measures in at 320 × 122 × 39 mm and weighs 804 g without the strap and 814 g with the strap. The Ace68 V2 has launched with an MSRP of $69 and a small launch discount bringing the price down to $62.10.The Mchose Ace68 V2 is compatible with Mchose M HUB, the browser-based customization utility that supports adjustable actuation, rapid trigger, SOCD, DKS, and customization of the south-facing RGB backlighting. The Ace68 V2 uses a wired USB Type-C connection and up to 8 kHz polling rate, and the Hall effect sensors support up to 0.001 mm precision and actuation distance customization of 0.1-3.4 mm. Mchose claims that the Ace68 V2 has a latency figure of just 0.08 ms.

articles.title: Binance Suffers Security Breach Affecting $6.3 Billion in Assets, Nearly $3 Billion Frozen
articles.text:
Cryptocurrency giant Binance said on Thursday that a "security incident" on its platform has impacted about $6.3 billion worth of assets.
The world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange said nearly $3 billion of those assets have been frozen on-chain so far.
Tether and Circle said they have frozen more than 1.567 billion USDT and 800 million USDC related to the incident, respectively. The Arbitrum Security Council is said to have executed a transaction to freeze about $30.5 million from the Binance Exploit.
"Initial investigation suggests that the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions," Binance said in an update.
The company said there is no evidence of a wallet private key leak, adding it will cover all losses from the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) fund and its own funds.
Out of an abundance of caution, Binance has also taken the following steps -
- Temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while security checks are completed
- Revoked the affected address authorization;
- Engaged law enforcement and blockchain intelligence partners to trace and recover funds
"We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice," Binance said.
In an update, Binance said it expects withdrawals to resume in 48 hours, after its team "completes a security revamp of the withdrawal service and its related addresses."
The development makes it the biggest cryptocurrency heist recorded to date, surpassing the theft of about $1.5 billion from Bybit in February 2025. The incident was subsequently attributed to North Korea.
"Our current estimate on the amount stolen is approximately $5.912 billion at time of theft, nearly 4x the amount stolen in the next largest crypto heist," blockchain intelligence firm Chainalysis said in an X post.
Attributed to North Korea's TraderTraitor
TRM Labs has attributed the record-breaking hack targeting Binance to threat actors from North Korea with high confidence. The blockchain analytics company linked it to TraderTraitor, which was also behind the 2025 Bybit heist, based on what it said were "robust on and off-chain intelligence sources."
"Several features of this attack match earlier North Korea-linked heists, including the Bybit hack and the KelpDAO hack in April 2026: small Tornado Cash withdrawals funding an operator wallet, staging that began well before the theft, and signatures obtained in advance then executed in one burst," TRM Labs said.
"The laundering observed so far, built on large swaps through market makers and lending protocols, differs from the bridge-heavy pattern that followed Bybit."
TRM Labs said preparation for the attack was underway at least 36 hours before the theft, with the attackers taking over a Binance hot wallet to send its "entire balance to an attacker-controlled address" -
At 20:20 UTC, the operator submitted a single transaction containing 50 authorizations. Each was signed by the Binance hot wallet, and each pointed it to a sweeper contract that accepts instructions only from the operator. Every wallet keeps a running count of its transactions, called a nonce, and an authorization works only at the count the wallet has reached at the moment it executes. The Binance hot wallet processes a steady flow of withdrawals, so its count keeps moving forward. By preparing signatures for 50 consecutive counts, the attacker guaranteed that one would still be valid when the transaction executed. One matched, which was all the attacker needed. The signatures were produced in advance as a batch.
Three minutes and 24 seconds after the delegation, the operator instructed the Binance hot wallet to send its entire balance to an attacker-controlled address. That single transaction moved 167,464 ETH and 63 tokens, including 1.615 billion USDT.
The most likely explanation is that the attacker gained the ability to make Binance's hot wallet signing system sign transactions of its choosing across chains. The batch of 50 pre-signed authorizations suggests the access may have been limited in time, or that signatures had to be requested through a system. Binance has yet to publish a root cause.
Chainalysis has also linked the hack to the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK) with a high degree of confidence, stating it "observed funds stolen by DPRK in last month's Bitget exploit commingling with funds stolen from Binance."
"The ability to quickly identify and understand illicit activity is increasingly important as North Korea increasingly uses sophisticated automation to move and obscure stolen funds," the company noted earlier this month. "Investigators must keep pace with these tactics while applying the judgment and expertise needed to make sense of complex on-chain activity."
So far, Tether, Circle, Ripple, and World Liberty Financial have frozen about $2.67 billion in stablecoins, and Arbitrum's Security Council has frozen about $30 million in ETH and ARB. The attacker continues to retain control of more than 420,000 ETH and 18,270 BTC, worth about $2.4 billion, plus smaller amounts on other chains.
Elliptic's chief scientist and founder, Dr. Tom Robinson, told The Hacker News cryptocurrency assets with a total value of $6.43 billion were stolen from Binance, assessing North Korea-linked actors perpetrated the theft, citing similar tradecraft and co-mingling of funds from another hack attributed to them.
"Rather than stealing Binance's private keys, the attacker appears to have been able to get Binance's own systems to sign transactions on their behalf," Elliptic said.
"This closely resembles the Bybit theft, in which North Korean hackers compromised a developer's machine at the wallet provider Safe{Wallet} and manipulated the transaction that Bybit's signers approved. In both cases, it was the infrastructure and people around the wallets that were compromised, not the cryptography."
The company also noted that 2.84 billion of funds have been frozen, while the attacker is in control of around $3.33 billion of assets that cannot be frozen by an issuer and are spread across about 43 wallet addresses. This includes 511,861 ETH (1.15 billion), 18,270 BTC ($1.43 billion), 233 million XRP, and 670 million TRX.
The links to North Korea are based on the following factors -
- Funds stolen from Binance and funds linked to the Bitget exploit have been sent to the same Ethereum address, 0x15104a9ce0f08a8f0075a0869ae80e795fe0feb7.
- Attackers funded their wallet with three small Tornado Cash withdrawals, tested the attack code in advance, and executed pre-signed transactions in a single burst, similar to what was observed in Bybit and KelpDAO exploits.
- The likely use of social engineering to trick employees into executing malware under the pretext of a coding test or a bogus project, a technique employed in DMM Bitcoin and Bybit hacks.
Despite these commonalities, Elliptic has urged caution in attributing the activity to North Korea, citing deviations from previously observed laundering patterns in terms of speed and methodology, as well as the absence of a root cause.
"DPRK launderers typically swap stolen stablecoins for native assets within minutes," Robinson said. "The attacker held the stolen USDT for 37 minutes on Ethereum and 46 minutes on Tron without converting most of it. North Korean-linked groups typically move funds faster and more efficiently. The use of market makers and DeFi lending protocols differs from the bridge-heavy laundering seen after the Bybit hack."
Chainalysis has also concurred with this assessment, stating it's observing never-seen-before laundering patterns with the stolen funds from the Binance exploit.
"Thousands of transactions in a short period suggest that the attackers are using automation to obscure the trail of funds," it said. "Rather than simply moving funds onward, they repeatedly circulate them among addresses, often sending funds back to addresses involved earlier in the sequence."
"Many addresses follow a consistent pattern: they receive exactly 1 TRX, then receive additional funds, then forward funds to other addresses. This repeated sequence suggests a programmatic process for moving and redistributing the stolen funds."
When asked if there were any indicators that could have helped identify and prevent this attack beforehand, Robinson said it was possible only in hindsight.
"The day before the attack, the attacker funded their wallet through the Tornado Cash mixer," Robinson added. "A few hours before, they tested their code on three wallets. None of this would have stood out at the time."
Assuming the Binance hack was orchestrated by North Korea, the development once again signals how the threat actors continue to operate with impunity despite continued law enforcement efforts and sanctions pressure.
"The rewards are huge and the risks to them are small," Robinson said. "The hackers are beyond the reach of law enforcement. North Korea is already heavily sanctioned, and crypto theft is one of the few ways it can still raise billions."
"They target people rather than technology, through fake job offers and malware, and it only takes one compromised laptop. They then launder the funds through mixers, bridges and OTC brokers, mostly out of reach of Western law enforcement. "However, tracing and freezing have improved, which makes each theft less profitable."
Binance has since revealed that its ongoing investigation has "uncovered additional points of breach" that goes beyond the compromised laptop, and that it's "doing all we can in coordination with law enforcement to resolve it."
The company has also disclosed that it's "recovering affected assets for users and continues to work with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms, and industry partners to trace, freeze and recover additional funds."
"Our initial investigation suggests this security incident may have started with a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop," Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said. "That gave an attacker access to a service container, where they submitted unauthorized withdrawal transactions."
"To be clear: the attacker did not simply use one engineer's permissions, and this was not a single 'one-click' action. It involved a more complex attack process. Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual."
(The story has been updated after publication to reflect the latest developments and additional insights from Elliptic.)

articles.title: Japan’s storage industry is spending billions on tape, memory and HDD
articles.text:
Magnetic tape storage is seeing a second lease of life thanks to AI — and now its largest manufacturer is planning a huge ramp-up in production
Fujifilm bets big on magnetic tape
- Fujifilm plans to multiply magnetic tape production fivefold by fiscal 2028
- The company is committing ¥10 billion ($63.3 million) to its Odawara plant expansion
- Offline tape copies can reduce exposure to remote cyberattacks on networked systems
Fujifilm has revealed plans to increase its magnetic tape production capacity fivefold by fiscal 2028 in response to rising data storage demands driven by AI.
The Japanese company has allocated ¥10 billion ($63.3 million) to expand its Odawara plant near Tokyo, marking its largest investment in tape production for approximately 20 years.
The project will concentrate on advanced cartridges capable of retaining up to 100TB, although Fujifilm has not disclosed its expected annual output following expansion.
Magnetic tape finds renewed purpose as AI data volumes surge
Magnetic tape remains commercially useful because organisations can store enormous quantities of information without keeping the medium continuously connected to computer networks.
Data centres, financial institutions and research organisations use it to preserve backups, particularly when information must remain available for years rather than immediate retrieval.
The technology dates back decades, with Fujifilm beginning development in 1954 for television broadcasting equipment before expanding into audio and video recording applications.
A 2026 IDC survey found that 94.7% of organisations reported storing larger volumes of information after adopting artificial intelligence technologies across their operations.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
It also estimates that global data generation could reach 718 zettabytes by 2030, approximately four times the 2024 volume.
Each zettabyte represents one billion terabytes, indicating the scale of storage capacity potentially required as digital activity expands.
Magnetic tape can help accommodate this growth by providing a relatively inexpensive way to retain large volumes of data offline for extended periods, without occupying costly high-speed storage.
Tape also offers protection against certain cybersecurity incidents because stored cartridges can remain disconnected from operational systems.
Keeping copies offline can reduce their exposure to remote attacks, although physical damage, mishandling and other risks remain possible.
Rising drive prices improve magnetic tape's cost advantage
The economics of competing storage technologies have strengthened tape's appeal as semiconductor shortages push up SSD prices and data centre demand increases pressure on hard-disk drive supplies.
According to Fujifilm’s analysis with Brad Johns Consulting, tape storage costs about 1 cent per GB, compared with 3–3.5 cents per GB for raw HDD storage.
This implies that storing 100 TB of data on magnetic tape costs approximately $1,000, compared with $3,000 to $3,500 using HDDs, potential savings of about 67–71%.
Japanese companies are now investing across several storage technologies, suggesting that they expect continued demand for different capacities, speed, and cost.
Kioxia plans to invest ¥5 trillion (~$37 billion) alongside American partner Sandisk over six years, to expand semiconductor memory production.
Toshiba intends to spend approximately ¥60 billion (~$380 million) enlarging its Philippine hard-drive factory, to double manufacturing capacity.
Hoya plans a ¥50 billion (~$317 million) investment in Vietnam for glass substrates used in hard drives, while NHK Spring has outlined an additional ¥35 billion (~$222 million) in production spending.
These investments indicate that magnetic tape's renewed appeal coincides with expansion elsewhere in the storage market, rather than a retreat from SSDs or HDDs.
Via Nikkei Asia
