articles.title: Ce TV Mini LED Samsung de 2026 ouvre le Black Friday de Boulanger sous les 450 €
articles.text:
Le Black Friday ne tombe que le 27 novembre, mais Boulanger a déjà ouvert le bal, et l’une des premières offres porte sur un téléviseur sorti cette année. Le TU50M72H fait entrer le MiniLED dans le bas du catalogue Samsung 2026 et repasse sous la barre des 450 € dans sa version 50 pouces, de quoi moderniser un salon sans viser le haut de gamme.
Avec la gamme M72H, Samsung propose sa technologie MiniLED dans l’entrée de gamme de son catalogue 2026. Le modèle de 50 pouces, mis en ligne fin avril 2026, s’adresse avant tout aux foyers qui veulent un vrai gain de contraste pour les films, les séries et le sport.
Pour le lancement de son Black Friday, Boulanger l’affiche à 449 € au lieu d’un prix de référence de 529 €, soit 15 % de remise, sur un produit neuf vendu et expédié par l’enseigne. C’est moins que les 499 € relevés chez Boulanger en juillet, et moins que les prix pratiqués actuellement chez Cdiscount, Darty ou la Fnac, autour de 500 €.
TV Samsung MiniLED TU50M72H à 449 € au lieu de 529 €
Pourquoi choisir le téléviseur Mini LED Samsung ?
- Un rétroéclairage MiniLED, qui apporte des noirs plus tenus et des hautes lumières mieux maîtrisées qu’un téléviseur LED d’entrée de gamme.
- Trois ports HDMI 2.1 compatibles VRR et ALLM, assez pour brancher une console et deux autres appareils.
- Sept ans de mises à jour gratuites, sécurisées par Knox.
- Les applications des box Bouygues, Free, Orange et SFR, ainsi que la compatibilité AirPlay 2.
- Un indice de durabilité de 8,2 sur 10.
Un 50 pouces taillé pour le salon, pas pour la compétition
Le TU50M72H a un profil assez clair : remplacer un vieux téléviseur Full HD par un modèle 4K qui apporte un vrai gain de contraste, sans viser le haut de gamme. Tizen centralise le streaming et donne accès aux applications des principaux opérateurs, ce qui permet de se passer du décodeur de sa box pour regarder la télévision, tandis qu’AirPlay 2 et le Bluetooth facilitent le partage depuis un téléphone ou l’envoi du son vers un casque. Les tuners TNT, satellite et câble sont aussi de la partie.
Le jeu vidéo est en revanche son point faible. Malgré trois ports HDMI 2.1, le VRR et l’ALLM, Boulanger annonce une fréquence de balayage native de 50 Hz, et la fonction Motion Xcelerator ne monte à 120 Hz qu’en 2K. La rédaction de Clubic estimait déjà que la gamme M72H est bien plus à l’aise avec les films, les séries et le sport qu’avec le jeu à haute fréquence. Côté son, les 20 W intégrés risquent de paraître justes dans une grande pièce, et les amateurs de cinéma noteront l’absence de Dolby Vision et de Dolby Atmos, habituelle chez Samsung. Enfin, le téléviseur ne propose pas de prise casque.
Le Mini LED descend en gamme, et ça se voit à l’écran
Un rétroéclairage plus fin pour mieux tenir les noirs
L’intérêt principal du TU50M72H tient à sa technologie Mini LED Pure Spectrum Vision AI. Le rétroéclairage, composé de diodes bien plus petites que sur un téléviseur LED classique, est piloté plus finement, ce qui permet d’afficher en même temps des noirs profonds et des blancs très lumineux. La dalle 10 bits affiche jusqu’à 1,07 milliard de couleurs, et le processeur Mini LED 4K se charge de la mise à l’échelle des contenus de plus basse définition, un point important quand une bonne partie de la télévision et du streaming n’est pas encore diffusée en 4K.
Sept ans de suivi pour durer
L’autre argument, moins visible mais tout aussi utile, est la durée de suivi. Samsung promet sept ans de mises à jour gratuites et sécurisées par Knox, et Boulanger indique une disponibilité des pièces détachées pendant sept ans à compter de la fabrication. L’assistant Vision AI Companion répond aux questions et propose des suggestions directement depuis le téléviseur, tandis que Bixby se charge des commandes vocales.
✅ Les points forts
- Rétroéclairage MiniLED rare à ce niveau de gamme chez Samsung.
- Trois ports HDMI 2.1 avec VRR et ALLM.
- Sept ans de mises à jour et indice de durabilité de 8,2.
- Applications des box opérateurs et AirPlay 2 intégrés.
❌ Les limites
- Fréquence native de 50 Hz, peu adaptée au jeu exigeant.
- Pas de Dolby Vision ni de Dolby Atmos.
- Son de 20 W un peu juste dans une grande pièce.
- Pas de prise casque.
TV Samsung MiniLED TU50M72H à 449 € au lieu de 529 €
Le TU50M72H ne s’adresse pas aux joueurs ni aux cinéphiles exigeants, mais il coche l’essentiel pour un salon de taille moyenne qui veut profiter du MiniLED et d’un suivi logiciel long. À 449 €, il fait partie des offres à surveiller de ce Black Friday anticipé, et les retours prolongés jusqu’à fin janvier laissent le temps de l’offrir ou de changer d’avis après les fêtes.
VPN, logiciels, abonnements : les promos à saisir en ce moment
Comment profiter des offres du Black Friday ?
Durant tout le mois de novembre, Clubic vous propose chaque jour des sélections thématiques regroupant les meilleures offres à saisir en direct.
Retrouvez tous les bons plans du Black Friday 2026 sur la page dédiée à l'événement.
Pour les aficionados de X, n'hésitez pas à suivre notre compte Clubic Bons Plans pour être au courant en direct des meilleures offres.

articles.title: Reddit sufre su peor día en Wall Street: sus acciones se desploman un 29,22%
articles.text:
Reddit sufrió su peor jornada en Wall Street desde que salió a bolsa en 2024: sus acciones se desplomaron un 29,22% este viernes 30 de octubre de 2026 y cerraron en USD 91,73, con una pérdida diaria de USD 37,87 por título.
La caída respondió a las previsiones de ventas para el cuarto trimestre, que quedaron por debajo de las expectativas de Wall Street.
La compañía proyectó ingresos de entre USD 1.000 millones y USD 1.030 millones, frente a los USD 1.050 millones previstos por los analistas.
El retroceso superó el anterior peor desempeño diario de Reddit, registrado el 31 de julio, cuando sus acciones habían caído un 20,99%.
La empresa indicó que sus ventas del tercer trimestre crecieron 53% interanual. Aunque superó las previsiones de ganancias e ingresos, el ritmo de expansión fue menor que el de los trimestres previos.
Qué inquietó a los inversores de Reddit
El mercado reaccionó a la proyección para los últimos tres meses del año, que quedó por debajo de los cálculos de los analistas. El resultado profundizó las dudas sobre la evolución del negocio publicitario de la plataforma.
Reddit también enfrenta cambios en el tráfico que recibe desde los buscadores.
Steve Huffman, director ejecutivo de la empresa, afirmó a CNBC que las visitas derivadas de Google disminuyeron de forma significativa durante el trimestre debido al avance de las respuestas generadas con inteligencia artificial en el buscador.
La compañía atribuyó parte de ese descenso a la expansión de AI Overview, la función de Google que ofrece resúmenes generados con inteligencia artificial dentro de los resultados de búsqueda.
El plan para exigir inicio de sesión a los usuarios en Reddit
Reddit anunció que probará exigir a los usuarios que inicien sesión para acceder a sus contenidos.
La medida representa un cambio para una plataforma identificada con el acceso abierto a debates y comunidades en internet.
Huffman explicó que la iniciativa apunta a incrementar la cantidad de usuarios registrados y activos, un factor relevante para el negocio de publicidad.
El ejecutivo sostuvo que Reddit es la última plataforma que todavía permite, en gran medida, el acceso sin iniciar sesión y que ese modelo responde a una decisión que él había defendido.
Consideró que los usuarios terminarán por entender el cambio como una adaptación al momento actual y a la evolución del funcionamiento de las plataformas digitales.
Acciones de Intel bajaron un 28,54%
Intel sufrió su peor jornada bursátil desde 1974: sus acciones cayeron 28,58% el viernes 30 de octubre de 2026 y cerraron en USD 65,76, frente a los USD 92,07 del día anterior. El desplome significó una pérdida de USD 26,31 por acción en una sola rueda.
El mercado castigó las previsiones de la compañía para el cuarto trimestre. Intel estimó ingresos de entre USD 15.000 millones y USD 16.000 millones, por debajo de los USD 17.070 millones esperados por los analistas consultados por LSEG.
Además, anticipó una ganancia ajustada de 25 centavos por acción, frente a los 43 centavos previstos por el mercado.
Durante la jornada, la acción abrió en USD 68,36, alcanzó un máximo de USD 68,77 y tocó un mínimo de USD 63,20. Tras el cierre regular, cotizaba en USD 65,23.
La empresa atribuyó parte de sus débiles perspectivas a la caída del mercado de computadoras personales y a la explosión ocurrida en octubre en su fábrica de Kiryat Gat, Israel. El incidente, que dejó dos trabajadores muertos y un tercero gravemente herido, obligó a detener la planta durante dos semanas.
Intel estimó que la explosión reducirá sus ingresos del cuarto trimestre en unos USD 300 millones y afectará el margen bruto en 200 puntos básicos. El impacto total podría alcanzar los USD 600 millones durante los dos próximos trimestres.
Pese a que los ingresos del tercer trimestre crecieron 21%, las ventas de chips para computadoras retrocedieron 5%. En contraste, el negocio de centros de datos e inteligencia artificial aumentó 78%. La baja también arrastró a otras empresas del sector, como Nvidia, Micron Technology, AMD y ASUS.

articles.title: MS Office 2024 Professional Plus Includes 6 Apps for a One-Time $49.97
articles.text:
Friday, October 30th 2026
MS Office 2024 Professional Plus Includes 6 Apps for a One-Time $49.97
Microsoft Office 2024 Professional Plus for Windows is on sale for $49.97 (MSRP $249.99) through Nov. 1. The offer reduces the price by $200 and provides a perpetual license for one Windows PC, with no ongoing subscription fees.
The suite includes Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, OneNote, and Access. Together, these apps cover document creation, spreadsheets, presentations, email, notes, and database management. Advanced data analysis and database tools also support work involving business information.The main purchasing distinction is the license type. This Professional Plus offer uses a non-binding, device-linked key, rather than the Microsoft account-linked binding key used by the Home and Business version. Lifetime access applies to the specific device associated with the license. That device-specific arrangement is part of what makes this offer more affordable.
It also differs from the ongoing payment model of Microsoft 365. Instead of paying subscription fees, buyers make a single payment for Office 2024 Professional Plus. For users who want these applications on one computer, this provides a defined upfront software cost.
Office 2024 Professional Plus emphasizes consistent functionality and long-term stability rather than frequent feature updates. It is designed for organizations that prefer a traditional perpetual license, including regulated industries and restricted environments where continuity matters.
The software includes a streamlined interface with dark mode, built-in security and compliance capabilities, and productivity tools designed for dependable performance. It also has minimal system requirements intended to accommodate a wide range of compatible hardware.
Compatibility is limited to Windows 10 and Windows 11 PCs. This license does not support Mac or macOS devices. Buyers receive instant access to the license key and download link.
Get six Microsoft Office 2024 Professional Plus apps for a one-time $49.97 payment through Nov. 1.

articles.title: ThreatsDay: Critical Firewall Flaws, Banking Trojans Rented, Weaponized PDF, Token Theft + 26 More Stories
articles.text:
Some attacks take real skill. Others just need someone to leave a door open. This week has both. Exposed passwords, old bugs still getting exploited, and trusted software doing things it shouldn't.
There's a strange mix of clever tricks and careless mistakes. Hackers are borrowing trust from familiar apps, websites, and AI tools. Some are using AI to speed things up. Others are leaving their own attack files exposed. Not exactly careful work.
Different stories, familiar weak spots. Here's what showed up this week.
The threats change every week. Subscribe, and we’ll alert you when each new ThreatsDay Bulletin is out.
- 
  
  PHP2Shell attacks persist WordPress security company Wordefence said it's not aware of any WordPress site compromised through PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) as of October 28, 2026. "We continue to see PHP2Shell-related requests across the more than 5 million sites we protect," it said. "Those requests show ongoing scanning and exploitation attempts; they do not show whether an attempt succeeded. Our site-cleaning and incident response teams have not handled a WordPress compromise attributed to these vulnerabilities."
- 
  
  40,573 secrets exposed Hudson Rock's investigation into the FortiBleed credential harvesting campaign has uncovered 975 newly identified domains and 40,573 exposed secrets, including 37,076 local-user records and 1,576 Active Directory LDAP bind records. The data comes from newly obtained 1,703 FortiGate source files associated with 1,689 host identifiers. "The configuration material dates to around February 2026, earlier than the likely May/June material examined in the first investigation," Hudson Rock said. The latest discovery has been codenamed FortiBleed 2.0.
- 
  
  Institutional DNS hijacked Threat actors have used domain shadowing to place illegal gambling content beneath legitimate school and government domains in two unrelated operations. "In both cases, an unauthorized party appears to have gained access to DNS administration and created records that the original domain owners may not have noticed," Infoblox said. "Because the resulting hostnames sat within established institutional namespaces, they provided especially useful infrastructure for search-engine optimization (SEO) and traffic acquisition." One cluster, linked to a threat actor called Hidden Hawk, has been found to add individual CNAME records that mapped institutional hostnames to gambling pages hosted largely on Cloudflare Pages. The second campaign exploiting an Indian government domain "delegated entire subzones to third-party authoritative nameservers and used a wildcard, allowing many hostnames to be managed outside the victim's DNS environment." Put differently, the unauthorized DNS access creates new institutional hostnames, which resolve to infrastructure serving illegal gambling doorway pages. The pages also leverage the established reputation of school and government namespaces to ensure that the malicious URLs show up prominently in search engine results.
- 
  
  AI banking credential warning Bank of America is reminding customers not to share banking credentials with AI agents. In an email blast to customers titled "Protecting your finances in the AI World," the financial institution urged customers to never share their username and password with another person or an outside service, "including an AI-enabled tool or agent that offers to act on your behalf."
- 
  
  Android tightens contact access Google has announced that an upcoming Android release will no longer be able to directly write to contacts with the WRITE_CONTACTS permission. "Instead, you can use the standard contact intents (ACTION_INSERT, ACTION_EDIT, and ACTION_INSERT_OR_EDIT)," Google said. "Currently, if your app needs to save even one contact, you might be requesting WRITE_CONTACTS. But that permission grants broad access, allowing an app to make widespread changes to contacts across the device in the background, even without user interaction. Most apps don’t need such broad permission."
- 
  
  26,400 live credentials exposed A scan of 7.25 million public repositories on Gitee, China's largest indigenous Git hosting platform, has uncovered 26,400 unique verified-live credentials, including an active organization-admin credential for a major enterprise AI platform and thousands of live cloud provider access keys, independent security researcher Ben Zimmermann said.
- 
  
  Critical Fortinet fixes released Fortinet has released a "coordinated set of security updates for FortiOS, FortiManager, and FortiAnalyzer" to address critical and high-severity flaws that were flagged using an AI-assisted vulnerability discovery approach. Details of the issues are being kept under wraps until November 10, 2026. With Fortinet devices becoming a favorite target for attackers, it's essential that users move quickly to apply the fixes.
- 
  
  Zero-permission token theft Details have emerged about a now-patched flaw in Microsoft Authenticator (CVE-2026-80097 aka AuthMask) that could be exploited by installing and running a malicious application on an affected Android device and convincing the user to complete an authentication flow in the app by claiming to be a trusted app and getting the corresponding tokens. The flaw could be exploited to take over work accounts without requiring additional permissions. "Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to obtain authentication tokens and access resources as the affected user," Microsoft said. According to Enclave, "an unprivileged Android app with zero permissions could impersonate any installed Microsoft first-party app and have the Microsoft Authenticator broker hand it that app's tokens. The setup is a device with Authenticator installed and one work account signed into it."
- 
  
  32 fake AI bots hunt secrets Attackers are disguising themselves as AI agents to steal credentials. Cequence said it has tracked a single actor running AI agent impersonation at scale by posing as about 32 different AI bots, including ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity, while searching for passwords, API keys, and cloud credentials. "The malicious scanner runs from a major cloud provider and rotates through about 32 AI bot identities, spanning crawlers and assistants from OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, Perplexity, and others," Will Glazier said. "It ignores web pages and requests files that commonly store secrets, including .env configuration files, cloud credential files, private SSH keys, and server environment data, working from a list of roughly 90 file paths. Each address sends a short burst of 50 to 190 requests in about eight seconds and then moves on. The scanner works through targets one at a time, around the clock, and first sends random nonsense paths to find websites that answer every request, a common scanning technique. It hit organizations in financial services, retail, telecommunications, energy, and software, and stayed active from at least late September through late October."
- 
  
  China-linked network intrusion The U.S. Embassy in Fiji has revealed that hackers linked to China broke into a regional organization based in Suva between July and August 2026. "Hackers with links to China maintained access to the organization's network over several days," it said. The embassy did not name the threat actor. Nor did it disclose what data the attackers may have accessed.
- 
  
  Camera software weaponized Attackers have been breaking into enterprise networks via camera management software, according to new research from security firm Huntress, which observed multiple incidents in September and October 2026 and traced them back to a compromised application. Source code artifacts point to a Korean company selling analog and IP cameras and digital and network video recorders. The activity abuses the legitimate "WpcMon.exe" binary to sideload DLLs that establish outbound connections to a remote server. "This activity demonstrates how attackers can blend malicious code with trusted Windows components to evade detection," Huntress said.
- 
  
  68 GB government data breach In a major operational security blunder, an unknown threat actor stole 68 GB from a Philippine government agency, maintained a detailed log of the transfer, then left that log open on the internet at 13.163.205[.]35:80. "The copy finished in under 24 minutes on September 6, 2026," Hunt.io said. "The transfer log records 27 SQL Server backups whose filenames correspond to the case-management systems of a Philippine overseas-employment and migrant-worker administration. Beside the log sat the operator's toolkit, a rebranded GodPotato build, a PowerShell stager, two payloads and a full Impacket environment."
- 
  
  AI model data exfiltration concerns Canadian AI company Cohere has claimed that it caught Alibaba's Qwen3.8-Flash-Next model unsuccessfully attempting to send data to China from its evaluation sandbox as part of a prompt instructing the LLM to detect malicious file download and execution by monitoring for curl processes downloading bash scripts to /tmp followed by bash execution. "Asked to write a defensive detection rule, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next ignored instructions and inventoried the machine it was running on and then tried to upload a probe file to an Alibaba Cloud storage bucket in Beijing," Cohere said. "We cannot answer whether this is deliberate or a leftover glitch from training." Cohere has also released a dataset containing the model trace and corresponding raw token IDs in connection with the behavior. "The exact output is not guaranteed all the time, and many trials may be required to reproduce the behavior," Cohere said, adding "there are similarly unexpected URLs that the model also tends to output, most containing aliyunc." However, the findings have also led to social media chatter that the company is resorting to geopolitical fearmongering and that they are an attempt to clamp down on open-weights models.
- 
  
  Post-quantum migration roadmap The U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has released guidelines that detail the timelines for transitioning away from quantum-vulnerable algorithms to quantum-resistant standards. "The report describes different use cases and says why one migration might take longer than another," said NIST mathematician Dustin Moody, who heads the PQC standardization project. "We understand there's not one strategy that fits all use cases, and we want to help people handle their migration while staying abreast of what's changing."
- 
  
  AI-powered ransomware operation exposed SOCRadar has uncovered the live workspace (i.e., open directory) of a threat actor tied to the n0n ransomware group, which exposed the operation's full workflow as of September 2026. The directory at 185.157.161[.]148 includes an AI coding agent configured with about 150 models to produce hundreds of attack scripts, with more than $7,216 in usage costs. "Entry points included a credential stuffing campaign against 305 FortiGate SSL-VPN devices, exposed AWS keys, weak RDP/WinRM credentials, and compromised hosting management portals," SOCRadar said. At least 23 organizations across 14 countries are said to have been identified in the workspace, including a U.S. sports retailer, a cloud provider, a teachers’ union, a Venezuelan ISP, an Argentine ministry and a pharmaceutical subsidiary.
- 
  
  Government AI access restricted The Swedish government has barred employees from accessing browser-based versions of ChatGPT or Claude on their work computers over security concerns relating to the processing of sensitive data. "Officials were concerned that entering sensitive information into these models without an agreement setting out how to protect and secure the data could lead to it being fed into the model and stored for training," Euro News reported.
- 
  
  42 repositories hijacked JFrog and SafeDep have uncovered a campaign in which threat actors hijacked third-party 42 GitHub repositories across 11 owners to deploy payload blobs large enough "to evade the GitHub search and API paths normally used to find this kind of compromise." JFrog said, "The repositories contain execution hooks for AI coding assistants and IDEs, plus 12.9 to 13.7 MB polymorphic wrappers that all decode to the same hidden CI-publisher payload." The activity is assessed to be related to a Miasma-family npm worm propagated under various packages ending with "testmetest." According to SafeDep, the worm "shares code with Miasma 'Phantom Gyp' from June 2026 and adds the token-revocation wiper from Mini Shai-Hulud. The malicious versions steal credentials, spread to other packages and repositories, and install a wiper that deletes the home directory when the victim revokes the stolen GitHub token." Unsuspecting developers who installed the packages had their data stolen and repositories compromised with malicious code to produce further malicious testmetest releases and run shellpanel workflows targeting cPanel systems through CVE-2026-41940, overlapping with a prior campaign detailed by Socket in July 2026.
- 
  
  Android banking malware-as-a-service A new Android malware operation called MR ROBOT is targeting customers of Indian banks and transforming banking fraud into a subscription business, with cybercriminals renting customized banking trojans to steal OTPs, card details, UPI PINs and credentials while secretly forwarding calls to bypass security checks. "It is not a single-actor campaign but a rented crimeware platform: a master operator leases access to affiliates, who use a Telegram bot ('APK Shield) and a web control panel (v7.0) to build personalized banking trojans on demand and distribute them through fake Play-Store-style pages and messaging-app lures," CloudSEK said. The kit impersonates around 36 lure apps, including banks, utility providers, and government services. One affiliate is estimated to have intercepted 5407 text messages from 153 infected devices.
- 
  
  MDM platforms abused for remote access Threat actors are abusing legitimate mobile device management (MDM) platforms, like Hexnode and Rippling, by using social engineering to enroll devices or install management agents, per Huntress. "Once established, MDM provides a trusted, privileged path for malicious activity, such as deploying rogue RMM tools and maintaining remote access," it said.
- 
  
  Critical Gotenberg RCE exploited Threat actors are exploiting CVE-2026-42589 (CVSS score: 9.8), a critical remote code execution flaw in Gotenberg, to deliver a Go-based reverse shell called "cache_base." The flaw was patched in May 2026. According to VulnCheck, the activity originated from a residential Japanese IP address in early October 2026. "The execution flow is straightforward: acquire a lock, collect host information, connect to C2, register the victim, and open a shell," VulnCheck said. Over the past 30 days, the vulnerability has recorded 1,358 exploitation events from 128 unique source IP addresses.
- 
  
  Discord discussions go public Discord has announced it will allow search engines to index discussions in Discoverable Servers and make them accessible on the web to users outside the platform without an account or invitation, starting mid-December 2026. "Discussions in Discoverable Servers will soon be easier to find when you search the web, so you can find the answer you're looking for and step straight into the conversation on Discord," it said. The changes apply only to Discoverable Servers and do not extend to private servers and direct messages.
- 
  
  800+ ransomware victims claimed The Gentlemen ransomware operation has claimed more than 800 victims across multiple regions and sectors, with most attacks targeting organizations in the U.S. and Europe. "The group supports multiple platforms, with ransomware variants targeting Windows, Linux, NAS, and BSD systems, allowing its affiliates to target a broad range of enterprise environments," Acronis said. "The group's operations include the use of EDR-killing tools. In a recent incident, a custom dropper was observed deploying vulnerable Safetica ProcessMonitorDriver [CVE-2025-70795] and Lenovo BootRepair.sys drivers to terminate security processes."
- 
  
  AI model loading RCE risk Pillar Security has disclosed an arbitrary-code-execution vulnerability in Unsloth's core model-loading path (CVE-2026-93348, CVSS score: 8.6). It has been fixed in unsloth_zoo 2026.8.14. "An attacker-controlled model configuration could cause Python code to execute during loading," researcher Ariel Fogel said. "The affected code ran inside the model-loading process, with access to whatever that process could read, modify, or authenticate to. In an AI development environment, that can include proprietary datasets, model artifacts, Hugging Face tokens, and cloud credentials. Exploitation required an affected loading path to process an attacker-controlled configuration."
- 
  
  Unauthenticated root-level RCE XBOW said it identified an unauthenticated, critical-severity remote code execution bug in a public web application belonging to the U.S. Election Assistance Commission (EAC). "The vulnerable application was a resource/logistics calculator, not a voting machine or voter registration system," XBOW researcher Ariel Walter Garcia said. "The flaw allowed an unauthenticated attacker to execute code as root inside the backend container, with access to locally protected resources and outbound network connectivity, a privileged foothold reachable via a crafted unauthenticated web request."
- 
  
  Session-hijacking RAT emerges A new remote access trojan called DarkCore comes with a dedicated browser that could let attackers access Gmail, WhatsApp, and MediaFire accounts using stolen sessions, while giving the impression that the activity is originating from the victim's own IP address. DarkCore was first advertised on cybercrime forums in August 2026. "The seller describes a browser that reuses those sessions to access work mailboxes, instant messaging apps, cloud storage and other services through the infected machine's IP address," BlackFog said. "The purpose is to make the access look like legitimate activity from the user."
- 
  
  AI-powered malware framework Cisco Talos has disclosed details of a new AI-integrated command-and-control (C2) framework called NIK C2. The implant features surveillance, theft, lateral movement, and evasion capabilities, including credential dumping, RDP session hijacking, process hollowing, and a C2-driven screen lock ransomware module. "NIK C2 contains a Windows implant, using which, an actor can dump credentials, stream the victim's keystrokes to collect the targeted victim's sensitive data, and instruct an integrated AI model to analyze the harvested data, all within the compromised session," Talos said. "In this framework, the actor has abused the OpenAI Chat Completions application programming interface (API), which is an HTTP endpoint that enables ChatGPT-style conversations programmatically. In addition to the features that enable theft, an actor can also deploy desktop screen-locking ransomware via the NIK C2 implant onto the victim machine, leading to a ransom demand in Bitcoin or USDT cryptocurrencies." Three different versions of the malware have been identified to date since August 12, 2026. Talos said NIK C2 alters adversary tradecraft by collapsing collection and exploitation into a single continuous session.
- 
  
  Malicious PDF delivers backdoor A phishing email using a FedEx tax invoice lure and containing a ZIP archive with a PDF has been observed triggering a multi-stage infection process to deliver a previously undocumented variant of the Sirius Backdoor. "The PDF abuses /OpenAction and /Launch objects to trigger an embedded Base64-encoded PowerShell command upon opening," Trellix said. "Execution relies on social engineering to trick the user into approving the PDF reader's security confirmation prompt. The PowerShell stager decrypts and reflectively loads a .NET assembly in memory. This loader performs process hollowing into legitimate Windows processes such as msbuild.exe, svchost.exe, etc., allowing the malware to operate under trusted process contexts." The final payload is SIRIUS, a Microsoft Visual C++ based backdoor with extended remote access capabilities.
- 
  
  AI reshapes ransomware economics A new analysis from Flare has revealed that threat actors are building a mixed AI toolkit, combining commercial models with local, open-weight, and jailbroken alternatives, as well as leaning on stolen AI credentials to shift costs to victims. "Where AI can help is with understanding systems, writing tools and troubleshooting. The threat actor still needs access, decisions and a way to obtain payment," Flare said. "If AI helps an affiliate write a working data-export script without hiring a specialist, the affiliate may avoid that specialist’s fee and the wait for their help. AI makes expertise cheaper to obtain only when the cost of using and checking its work is lower than the cost of the specialist help it replaces."
- 
  
  Emerging data-extortion threat A recently observed cyber-extortion actor named ScarlettGroup is publicly advertising alleged data compromises and uses negotiation deadlines and threatened disclosures to pressure targeted organizations. The group's dark web site listing includes victims from technology, education, government, and entertainment sectors. "ScarlettGroup demonstrates characteristics associated with financially motivated data-extortion operations, including public victim claims, deadline-based pressure, and underground forum activity," Foresiet said. "Its dedicated leak-site infrastructure and structured disclosure mechanism indicate an organized approach to promoting alleged compromises and exerting reputational pressure."
- 
  
  Infostealers evolve into RATs Following its disruption in June 2026 as part of Operation Endgame, StealC has returned four months later as Stadia. "This time it's not a stealer: it's a full remote access trojan," Varonis said. "The RAT's features include hidden desktop control, a live command shell, a file explorer, a process manager and an in-memory loader, with StealC's stealer welded on as one module among six. The actor behind Stadia is working hard to win back original StealC customers: every former StealC customer is offered a free month on the top ($900) tier." The development comes as Moonlock Lab revealed that the Icarus macOS stealer has similarly evolved from a smash-and-grab crypto and data stealer to a malware with remote-access capabilities. The new iteration is called ICMacOS. "The stealer is actively advertised on cybercrime forums by a Russian-speaking actor operating under the handle GlowComa, with feature updates regularly announced via Telegram," SOCRadar said. "GlowComa promotes ICMacOS alongside Icarus ClickFix, a companion panel designed to deliver payloads using malicious copy-and-paste terminal commands. The infection chain relies on initial dropper scripts to detect the host architecture and harvest administrator passwords using fake system dialogs before delivering the primary payload." Another macOS-focused stealer is Aokigahara, which goes beyond browsers, VPN clients, cryptocurrency wallets, FTP/SFTP clients, password managers, and email applications to also target AI applications and development tools. "The stealer collects authentication files, session data, and configuration files associated with Claude, ChatGPT Desktop, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, and other tools," Check Point said. "Stolen AI credentials could offer opportunities for monetization. Usable credentials or session tokens could enable unauthorized access to paid AI services or the resale of compromised accounts."
That's the week's mess. Some attacks were clever, some were painfully simple, and a few attackers made life easier for the people investigating them. The common problem? Too much trust in things nobody was watching closely.
AI is adding new tricks, but the old ones aren't going anywhere. Stolen credentials, weak access controls, and forgotten bugs still get plenty of work done. New tools, familiar mistakes.
The useful part is knowing where those mistakes keep showing up. That's usually where the next problem starts.

articles.title: Here's why the SteelSeries Arctis Nova Elite gaming headset remains the best gaming headset I've ever tested — and wins our Gaming Device of the Year award
articles.text:
There are only so many ways I can say how good the SteelSeries Arctis Nova Elite is, but perhaps the simplest way is the best: it is the greatest gaming headset I have ever tested and reviewed.
Yup, it still looks very familiar, and very SteelSeries Arctis on the outside, but this headset is like no other in the brand's lineup, or the wider market. Everything, every minute detail, has had time and consideration poured into it, and it really is the fullest realization of what a gaming headset can be, and a natural winner at the TechRadar Product of the Year Awards 2026.
First and foremost, as I laid out in my full SteelSeries Arctis Nova Elite review, it's got that brilliant out-of-the-box SteelSeries audio — but not quite as we all know it. The brand-new custom-made carbon fiber audio driver, held in place by a brass surround ring, makes for a different, but still breathtaking, flavor.
Combine that SteelSeries Arctis tuning with the new hardware combination, and you get unbelievable immersion, supremely accurate sound reproduction of anything and everything, and excellently rich and detailed certified Hi-Res Audio for a wireless gaming headset.
While I could talk about the audio alone for ages, the Elite backs up its brilliant sound with a faultless feature set.
Firstly, building on the brilliant DAC unit the Arctis Nova Pro headsets introduced, the Elite's GameHub with OmniPlay means you can be connected to every platform type, basically simultaneously.
It's fabulous. Utilizing this, as well as the headset's Bluetooth connection, you can actually connect to up to four different sources, and mix and listen to them altogether. You might never need four, but being connected to my console and PC, and having Bluetooth on to take phone calls, has been really useful for me.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
You've got two different microphone modes (a retractable boom, which is fantastic quality, and built-in ones for convenience), the 'infinite' battery supply due to a spare being charged in the GameHub all the time, and a host of EQ and other controls in the GameHub.
The Nova Elite feels fantastically premium, and joyous to wear and use. The cold-rolled steel and aluminum materials are superb, the leatherette cushions are sublime, the metallic volume wheel is a tiny but glorious touch, and every button and material finish feels worthy of the headset's lofty price tag.
Other headsets might tickle different fancies, or appeal to different priorities that folks might have; but for anyone looking for a premium, do-it-all headset for all of their devices that excels in every way, it has to be the SteelSeries Arctis Nova Elite. You simply will not find a better headset offering the same combination of design, features and audio quality. Buy it, and you will never look back.
Follow TechRadar on Google News and add us as a preferred source to get our expert news, reviews, and opinion in your feeds.
Rob is the Managing Editor of TechRadar Gaming and Streaming, a video games journalist, critic, editor, and writer, and has years of experience gained from multiple publications. Prior to being TechRadar Gaming's Managing Editor, he was TRG's Deputy Editor, and a longstanding member of GamesRadar+, being the Commissioning Editor for Hardware there for years, while also squeezing in a short stint as Gaming Editor at WePC just before joining TechRadar Gaming. He is also a writer on tech, gaming hardware, and video games but also gardens and landscapes, and has written about the virtual landscapes of games for years.

articles.title: Qué es la ansiedad por inteligencia artificial y por qué preocupa a los expertos
articles.text:
La ansiedad por la inteligencia artificial se instala en los consultorios de los terapeutas y los datos lo confirman: en una encuesta del Pew Research Center realizada en 2026 a más de 3.400 adultos en Estados Unidos, el 52% de los consultados dijo sentirse más preocupado que entusiasmado por el avance de la IA en la vida cotidiana, frente al 37% que expresó esa misma inquietud en 2021.
El fenómeno tiene nombre propio: ansiedad por IA. Según informó el Washington Post, los especialistas en salud mental advierten que llegó para quedarse. Los miedos van desde perder el trabajo hasta no poder distinguir lo real de lo fabricado por una máquina, y los terapeutas ya tienen respuestas concretas para quienes lo padecen.
La psiquiatra Tracy Foose, terapeuta en el Área de la Bahía de San Francisco, lo vivió en carne propia. Cuando empezó a publicar videos en redes sociales, algunos seguidores insistían en que era una influencer generada por computadora, algo que al principio le resultó halagador.
La sensación cambió cuando se puso a investigar. Descubrió que existen múltiples compañías que ofrecen crear dobles digitales capaces de replicar la voz y el rostro de cualquier persona.
“Me di cuenta de que alguien podría hacer un video que se apropiara tan completamente de mi imagen, mi voz, mi cara, que incluso yo podría creer que soy yo”, le dijo al Washington Post. El halago se transformó, según sus propias palabras, en “una forma de terror existencial”.
El 52% de los estadounidenses teme más de lo que se entusiasma con la IA
Ese terror no es un caso aislado. Sha Sajadieh, quien lidera el Índice de IA en el Instituto Stanford para la IA Centrada en el Ser Humano, explicó al medio que la mayor exposición a la tecnología produce un doble efecto: entusiasmo y alarma, casi a partes iguales.
“Con una adopción más amplia viene una mayor comprensión de lo que esta tecnología es capaz de hacer, lo cual puede ser muy emocionante como herramienta para muchos de nosotros, y también puede ser increíblemente abrumador cuando pensás en algunos de los posibles impactos a largo plazo”, señaló.
Un informe de Pew de 2025 refuerza esa tensión: cerca del 75% de los estadounidenses acepta que la IA los asista en tareas cotidianas, pero más de la mitad califica como alto el riesgo social que implica la tecnología.
Ese equilibrio frágil se sacudió aún más la semana pasada, cuando una publicación de un investigador de Anthropic (la empresa creadora del asistente Claude) se viralizó en la red social X al advertir que existe una probabilidad superior al 10% de que “la IA podría matar a todos los humanos”.
Hasta ese momento, las preocupaciones sobre una inteligencia superior que domine el mundo habían sido, en general, territorio de los propios especialistas del sector. Sajadieh aclaró, sin embargo, que la mayoría de las angustias vinculadas a la IA son más inmediatas: “más reales aquí y ahora”.
El miedo a perder el empleo y la identidad está en el centro de la angustia
La más extendida de esas preocupaciones concretas es el temor a la pérdida del trabajo. Vaile Wright, psicóloga y directora sénior de innovación en salud de la Asociación Americana de Psicología (APA), explicó al Washington Post que quedarse sin empleo no solo implica perder el sustento económico, sino también el propósito. “Muchas veces tu identidad está envuelta en la cantidad de inversión que pusiste en tu carrera”, afirmó.
A ese miedo se le suma otro, más difuso pero igual de corrosivo: ver a la IA ejecutar tareas consideradas propias de los seres humanos, como generar ideas o resolver problemas, puede sacudir la autoestima de forma más profunda. “Hay una parte de nosotros que quiere defender la creatividad y la inteligencia humanas y decir: ‘Soy mucho mejor’, pero frente a frente con la máquina, puede que no siempre se sienta así”, reconoció Foose.
Hay, además, un tercer factor que alimenta la angustia: la dificultad creciente para distinguir lo real de lo artificial. Thea Gallagher, psicóloga clínica y profesora asociada de psiquiatría en la Escuela de Medicina Grossman de la Universidad de Nueva York, señaló que la proliferación de contenido generado por IA desorienta a las personas y les genera miedo a ser estafadas o víctimas de una falsificación digital.
El informe de Pew de 2025 pone cifras a esa incertidumbre: el 53% de los estadounidenses no se siente capaz de detectar si algo fue producido por una persona o por una máquina.
La velocidad del fenómeno tampoco ayuda. La IA avanza en publicidad, contratación laboral y salud, muchas veces sin que la regulación pueda seguirle el ritmo. “Para la mayoría de nosotros, realmente no sabemos cómo funciona. A veces ni los propios desarrolladores lo saben”, indicó Wright. “Estar golpeados por tanta incertidumbre nos recuerda lo poco que podemos controlar”.
Los terapeutas recomiendan informarse, conectar con otros y ejercitar las habilidades propias
Frente a este panorama, los especialistas consultados por el Washington Post ofrecen herramientas concretas. El primer paso, según Wright, es mejorar el conocimiento sobre la IA: experimentar con versiones gratuitas de herramientas como ChatGPT o Claude, o tomar cursos introductorios. Conocer la tecnología ayuda a percibirla como un recurso utilizable, en lugar de una amenaza difusa.
La recomendación es preguntar en el trabajo cómo se usa la IA y reflexionar sobre el valor que cada persona aporta. Para los padres, hablar con docentes sobre la tecnología en el aula y medidas para preservar el pensamiento crítico.
Un segundo eje pasa por reconectar con el cuerpo y los sentidos. Foose subrayó que, a diferencia de la IA, los seres humanos son “seres vivos que respiran en un mundo físico”. Atender necesidades básicas como moverse, alimentarse y salir al aire libre ancla la mente en el presente y frena la espiral de pensamientos catastróficos.
“No tiene que ser una caminata de varios días en la naturaleza. Puede ser simplemente caminar por una calle de la ciudad con todo el ruido de los taxis”, ejemplificó. Gallagher, en la misma línea, subrayó el valor de “volver a la naturaleza, estar en el mundo” y recuperar el contacto con lo que se puede ver, tocar y sentir.
Cultivar vínculos reales y redescubrir las capacidades humanas es parte del antídoto
El tercer pilar es la conexión social. Wright advirtió que la tendencia a no querer cargar a los demás con los problemas propios es, en realidad, un obstáculo, porque “en realidad necesitamos buscar apoyo social”. Foose apuntó que el contacto presencial, “donde podemos tocarnos, vernos, olernos, por más extraño que suene”, puede ser restaurador.
Crear rituales, como ejercicio semanal o llamadas quincenales, sostiene la conexión. Si el círculo social se redujo, reconectar con viejos amigos o hacer voluntariado ayuda a ampliarlo.
Los terapeutas sugieren reivindicar las propias capacidades. Gallagher alienta a sus pacientes a “crear, hacer, producir”, algo que la IA no puede quitar. Foose invita a resolver problemas físicos, como reorganizar un cajón u ordenar el garaje, para recuperar la propia agencia.
Cuando el desánimo se instala, propone recordar la magnitud del cerebro humano: “Hace cuatrillones de cálculos por minuto y no depende de una planta de energía para hacerlo. Podemos llevarlo a la naturaleza. Podemos llevarlo bajo el agua. Podemos conectarlo a otros cerebros simplemente usando el lenguaje”, dijo. “La IA recién está aprendiendo a hacer eso”.

articles.title: Vous jonglez entre Claude Code, Codex et Copilot ? Vous allez apprécier ce petit logiciel gratuit
articles.text:
Les assistants de programmation IA ont chacun leurs plafonds et leurs compteurs. AI Limits les rassemble dans un widget pour Windows 11, histoire de savoir combien de marge il reste avant la prochaine réinitialisation.
Les outils de développement assisté par IA imposent des limites variables : sessions de cinq heures, plafonds hebdomadaires ou quotas propres à certaines fonctions. Pour connaître son solde, il faut consulter plusieurs interfaces. AI Limits propose de centraliser ces informations sur Windows 11.
- Pourcentages et échéances visibles
- Trois niveaux de détail
- Jetons réutilisés en lecture seull
Claude Code, Codex, Copilot et Antigravity dans un seul widget
AI Limits réunit les quotas de Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot et Google Antigravity. Il présente des jauges de consommation et les délais avant leur remise à zéro. Pour Claude Code, il suit notamment les fenêtres de cinq heures, les plafonds hebdomadaires et certains quotas par modèle. Copilot dispose de compteurs de requêtes et de complétions, tandis qu'Antigravity affiche des limites partagées entre modèles.
L'interface prend la forme d'un panneau flottant et translucide. Trois niveaux de détail, des jauges horizontales ou verticales et plusieurs palettes permettent de le personnaliser. On peut aussi le masquer : un indicateur prend alors le relais dans la zone de notification ou sur la barre des tâches. Une estimation du temps restant avant l'épuisement d'un quota est proposée en option.
L'application exploite les identifiants déjà enregistrés sur le PC par les outils officiels en ligne de commande. Si Claude Code, Codex CLI ou GitHub CLI sont connectés, nul besoin, en principe, de ressaisir ses accès. Les chiffres proviennent des fournisseurs concernés, et non d'un comptage local des requêtes.
Un utilitaire gratuit, avec quelques limites à connaître
AI Limits est gratuit et open source, sous licence GPLv3 ou ultérieure. Disponible notamment sur le Microsoft Store et en version portable, cet utilitaire en Rust sert de tableau de bord commun, comme les jauges d'un véhicule regroupées devant le conducteur plutôt que sur quatre écrans.
Cette simplicité suppose de passer par les outils pris en charge. AI Limits ne mesure pas toutes les conversations menées dans ChatGPT ou Claude depuis un navigateur : il suit les comptes connectés aux outils de programmation. Une clé API Claude ajoutée manuellement renseigne, quant à elle, les plafonds de l'API, pas les quotas d'un abonnement Pro ou Max.
Côté confidentialité, le programme lit les jetons d'authentification existants sans les modifier. Son développeur assure ne collecter aucune télémétrie. Le code public peut être examiné, mais l'accès à ces jetons reste à prendre en compte avant installation.
Les chiffres ne sont toutefois pas toujours actualisés. Quand un jeton expire ou qu'un fournisseur limite les consultations, AI Limits conserve le dernier relevé et le grise pour signaler son ancienneté. Mieux vaut cela qu'un faux compteur en temps réel.
- Pourcentages et échéances visibles
- Trois niveaux de détail
- Jetons réutilisés en lecture seull

articles.title: RTX 5080 Vanishes From NVIDIA's US Marketplace Two Weeks After the RTX 5090
articles.text:
Friday, October 30th 2026
RTX 5080 Vanishes From NVIDIA's US Marketplace Two Weeks After the RTX 5090
NVIDIA's US Marketplace no longer lists the GeForce RTX 5080. The GPU filter on the store's graphics card page now tops out at the RTX 5070 Ti, followed by the RTX 5070, RTX 5060 Ti, RTX 5060, and RTX 5050, with partner RTX 5080 models gone as well. The same thing happened to the RTX 5090 about two weeks ago and, barring a brief cameo at $5,599, the card still hasn't returned. NVIDIA has since denied that the RTX 5090 is discontinued, though it hasn't said anything about the RTX 5080 yet. Oddly enough, its RTX 5080 product page still says "Starting at $999."
The removal seems limited to the US for now. NVIDIA's UK Marketplace still has 13 RTX 5080 listings and two RTX 5090 cards. Of course, a missing listing could simply mean there's no stock left, since the RTX 5080 already costs close to $2,000 at US retailers, roughly double its MSRP. That leaves the RTX 5070 Ti as the fastest card on NVIDIA's US store, and it isn't cheap either. The seven listings there range from $1,269.99 to $1,499.99, well above its $749 launch price.Of course, this move is not really surprising. We recently covered a new report claiming NVIDIA is moving up the launch of a 24 GB RTX 5080 to December or January, and phasing out the 16 GB model in China. A leaker also claimed earlier this month that NVIDIA has January discontinuation dates set for the 16 GB card. None of this is officially confirmed, but it looks like US buyers looking for an RTX 5080 16 GB will have to rely on third-party retailers for now.

articles.title: I’m a certified barista, and these are the essential off-grid espresso makers I recommend for your emergency prepping kit if the power fails
articles.text:
Civilization may crumble, but bad coffee is optional — I test coffee makers for a living, and these off-grid espresso machines are perfect for preppers
So you've got your water, cash, canned food, and a wind-up radio, but something is missing from your prepping supplies. If the power goes out and your water supply is cut, how will you make your morning coffee? Put down that jar of instant granules — basic services might have failed, but your tastebuds haven't.
Drip coffee is an easy way to perk yourself up and boost your morale in a crisis (just pick up a ChemEx brewer or a simple dripper with some filter papers), but if you're aiming to conserve water then a shot of espresso is a better way to get your caffeine fix, so here I've focused on brewers for preparing shorter drinks.
Consider how you're going to store your emergency coffee supply, too. Whole beans will hold their flavor better than ground, and I recommend keeping them in an opaque, airtight container in a cool place (light, heat, air, and moisture are the enemies of aroma compounds). You'll need a grinder, too — look for one with burrs rather than blades so your coffee isn't chopped up in rough pieces.
If all that sounds like too much hassle in a crisis, opt for foil-sealed coffee pods instead. Both the Nanopresso and Dreame Ecceluxe Go below have adapters for brewing with single-serve capsules.
The Ecceluxe Go heats its own water, but if you pick a more basic brewer then you'll need a different way to get it up to temperature. As the former editor of an outdoor gear website, I recommend a simple gas camping stove like the MSR Pocket Rocket 2, which will get your water up to around 203F / 95C in approximately 3.5 minutes. Now, onto the brewers...
Wacaco NanoPresso
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
No power? No problem. The Wacaco Nanopresso generates up to 18 bars of pressure using nothing but elbow grease. It's small enough to tuck inside a pocket, and is hand-powered, so all you need is a source of hot water to create properly extracted espresso with thick crema (even if you have to use a flashlight to see what you're doing).
The standard Nanopresso uses ground coffee, which you can tamp down using the scoop (the brewer has a valve to release pressure if you accidentally tamp it too hard), but if you'd rather use pods then the NS adaptor allows you to use Nespresso Original style capsules instead.

It feels robust and solid in the hand, and is packed with thoughtful little features like an insulated water tank and cup to protect your hands from heat, and an easy-clean portafilter that needs minimal maintenance.
Dreame Ecceluxe Go
View Original

The Dreame Ecceluxe Go is a battery-powered brewer with a miniature boiler built-in. Just pour room-temperature water into the reservoir on top (measuring lines engraved inside will prevent you overfilling it and wasting precious resources), then pick the right adapter — Nespresso Original, Nestlé Dolce Gusto, ESE (Easy Serve Espresso), or fresh grounds — and you're ready to brew.
Preparing an espresso with room temperature water takes about six minutes from start to finish, and you can prepare two or three drinks before the Ecceluxe Go needs recharging (from a portable battery or solar generator during a power outage). The brew unit itself is smaller than a thermos flask, and comes in a compact carry case that you can tuck away with the rest of your emergency supplies.
The Dreame Ecceluxe Go is due to go on sale in Spain and Portugal very soon, with the US following shortly after. There's no plan for a UK launch yet, but it charges via USB-C, so there's no reason British preppers can't import one.
AeroPress and Manual Coffee Grinder

If you're planning to keep whole coffee beans in your emergency supplies, you need the AeroPress Manual Coffee Grinder. I've tested a lot of manual grinders in my time, and this is easily the best. It has proper burrs rather than cheap blades so coffee is ground rather than shredded, and they're adjustable so you can optimize the grind size to suit your brewing method.
The default setting is optimized for the AeroPress brewer, which you can use to make a short, strong shot of coffee to keep you awake, or a longer, smoother drink if you have water to spare. I have a plastic AeroPress in my locker at work (you never know what might happen), but if you want something extra tough then take a look at the rugged AeroPress Steel. If you're part of a whole family of coffee-lovers there's also the king-sized AeroPress XL, and if you need something you can also use on the road, the bijou AeroPress Go packs down into a compact travel cup.

articles.title: OpenAI restringirá lo que ChatGPT responde a adolescentes sobre armas, aunque la pregunta parezca inocente
articles.text:
OpenAI anunció el 30 de octubre que limitará la información sobre armas que ChatGPT entrega a usuarios menores de 18 años, incluso cuando la pregunta parezca inofensiva. La medida forma parte de un paquete de salvaguardas contra la violencia real, que la empresa empezará a aplicar en las próximas semanas.
Según la publicación oficial de la compañía, la versión de ChatGPT para adolescentes restringirá la información práctica sobre armas y sistemas de seguridad que pueda usarse para facilitar actos violentos. El límite rige aunque no haya señales de intención violenta en la conversación.
Las políticas de OpenAI ya prohibían ayudar a cualquier persona a planear o ejecutar actos de violencia, y limitaban la ayuda a adolescentes para conseguir armas. La nueva regla amplía esa protección a datos prácticos que antes no estaban cubiertos.
Los adolescentes podrán seguir usando ChatGPT para prevenir o desescalar la violencia, buscar apoyo y contactar a un adulto de confianza, precisó la empresa.
Cómo decidirá ChatGPT quién es menor de edad
OpenAI dijo que reforzó su sistema de predicción de edad, lanzado el año pasado. El sistema analiza varias señales, como los patrones de comportamiento, para estimar si un usuario es menor de 18 años, y traslada a los adolescentes a la experiencia con más protecciones.
Quien sea clasificado como menor por error podrá confirmar que es adulto con un trámite rápido a través de Persona, el socio de verificación de edad de la empresa. Así se le retirarán las protecciones adicionales.
La compañía agregó que busca aplicar los límites más estrictos también cuando prevea que una persona es menor, aunque sus conversaciones no muestren intención violenta.
Cambios que alcanzan a todos los usuarios
Para todos los usuarios, sin importar la edad ni el motivo de la consulta, ChatGPT dará menos detalle sobre ataques masivos del pasado. Eso incluye las armas y el equipo utilizados, cómo se obtuvieron y las comparaciones de magnitud del daño que puedan aumentar la notoriedad del atacante.
OpenAI aclaró que los usuarios podrán seguir pidiendo ayuda para entender esos hechos, el impacto en las víctimas y las señales de alerta que permiten prevenir nuevos casos.
Además, cuando una conversación muestre que alguien está obsesionado con la violencia o con causar un daño grave a otra persona, ChatGPT podrá cerrar el chat de forma automática. Si ocurre varias veces, la empresa podrá pausar la cuenta de manera temporal.
Con el control parental, los padres vinculan su cuenta a la de sus hijos. En julio, OpenAI amplió las alertas para avisarles si la cuenta del adolescente era desactivada por violar las normas sobre violencia. Ahora trabaja en notificarles también cuando la cuenta se pause por hablar de forma reiterada de violencia.
La empresa informó que realizó más de 200 denuncias a las autoridades en el tercer trimestre de 2026 por amenazas inminentes de violencia, y afirmó que esos avisos ayudaron a frustrar planes violentos.
El anuncio llega, según Reuters, en medio del escrutinio creciente a las empresas de IA por los riesgos de los chatbots para los jóvenes. La agencia recordó que este mes la organización sin fines de lucro Common Sense Media halló que la versión para adolescentes de ChatGPT avisaba a los padres tarde o nunca cuando las cuentas registraban conversaciones sobre suicidio, autolesiones o trastornos alimentarios.
OpenAI publicará su primer informe de seguridad comunitaria a principios de 2027, con datos del segundo semestre de 2026, y lo actualizará cada seis meses.

articles.title: AutoFull Unveils the C3 Pro Gaming Chair Series
articles.text:
Friday, October 30th 2026
AutoFull Unveils the C3 Pro Gaming Chair Series
AutoFull, a leading esports peripherals brand, today announced the launch of the C3 Pro Series, a new line of gaming chairs designed for a new generation of gamers. Guided by the idea of "The Gaming Chair to Start With," the series combines distinctive gaming aesthetics with adjustable lumbar support and a choice of configurations to suit different comfort needs and preferences.
The C3 Pro Series features two models: C3 Pro Standard and C3 Pro Advanced. While the Standard focuses on essential lumbar support for everyday gaming, the Advanced adds active seat ventilation and heating, a larger upgraded seat, and a retractable footrest for a more feature-rich comfort experience.Cool. Cozy. Custom Fit. Core Features of the C3 Pro Series
Cool: Lightning-Inspired Design
Inspired by the energy of a lightning strike, the C3 Pro Series features a bold silhouette and embroidered lightning motifs that extend across the backrest's side wings, bringing a dynamic, futuristic look to the gaming chair.
The series launches in two colorways: Flash, featuring a silver-and-black combination, and Flare, featuring black and gold. Both share the same distinctive design language, offering different expressions of the series' bold gaming aesthetic.
Cozy: Active Seat Ventilation and Heating
Available on the C3 Pro Advanced, the integrated seat ventilation and heating system gives players more control over their seating comfort across changing temperatures.
Dual fans circulate air through the seat to help reduce heat buildup during extended gaming sessions, while dual graphene heating pads provide adjustable warmth when the room gets chilly. Three ventilation levels and three heating levels let users tailor their experience. A 15-minute automatic shutoff and overheating protection provide additional safety features.
The C3 Pro Advanced also features a larger upgraded seat and a retractable footrest, giving players more room to settle in and another way to relax between matches.
Custom Fit: Adjustable Lumbar Support
Support is central to the C3 Pro Series. Adjustable lumbar support lets players fine-tune the position of lower-back support to suit their preferred sitting position, whether they are gaming, studying, or spending time at a desk.
The C3 Pro Standard focuses on essential lumbar support and everyday comfort, making it a practical starting point for first-time gaming chair buyers and those upgrading from a basic chair. The C3 Pro Advanced builds on that foundation with additional comfort features for players who want more flexibility in how they sit and relax.Choose Your C3 Pro
The C3 Pro Series offers two configurations designed around different needs and priorities.
- C3 Pro Standard—Essential Support: Designed for first-time gaming chair buyers and upgraders who want core lumbar support, distinctive styling, and the essentials for everyday gaming.
- C3 Pro Advanced—Enhanced Comfort: Adds active seat ventilation and heating, a larger upgraded seat, and a retractable footrest for players seeking a more feature-rich comfort experience.
Both models share the series' lightning-inspired design, while their distinct configurations help shoppers choose the features that matter most to them.
Availability
The AutoFull C3 Pro Series is now available in the United States through the AutoFull official website and Amazon, with availability in the EU beginning November 2, 2026. Both C3 Pro Standard and C3 Pro Advanced will be available through the respective regional stores.

articles.title: Boulanger n’attend pas le Black Friday et casse déjà les prix de cinq TV OLED et Mini LED
articles.text:
Pas question de patienter jusqu’à la fin du mois pour renouveler sa télé. Boulanger ouvre les hostilités du Black Friday avec plusieurs semaines d’avance et fait chuter le prix de cinq TV signées TCL, LG et Philips, de l’OLED compact pour joueurs au Mini LED géant pour le home cinéma.
Le Black Friday 2026 tombera officiellement le vendredi 27 novembre, mais comme chaque année, les enseignes n’attendent pas la date fatidique pour lancer leurs premières remises. Boulanger fait partie des marchands qui démarrent leurs promotions dès le début du mois, et l’enseigne frappe fort cette fois sur le rayon TV, l’un des plus scrutés de la période.
Au programme, cinq modèles 2026 qui couvrent à peu près tous les besoins : un OLED 48 pouces taillé pour le jeu, deux Philips Ambilight, un Mini LED TCL au rapport qualité-prix très solide et le vaisseau amiral de la marque chinoise en 75 pouces. De quoi trouver son bonheur, que l’on cherche une télé principale pour le salon ou un écran d’appoint pour la chambre. Et si aucun de ces modèles ne vous convient, nos bons plans TV sont mis à jour tout au long de la période.
- TCL 55C89L à 799 € au lieu de 1 099 € (-27 %) : le Mini LED polyvalent et bien équipé
- Philips 55OLED811 à 1 299 € au lieu de 1 599 € (-19 %) : l’OLED avec Ambilight pour les cinéphiles
- Samsung TQ75QN82H à 1 299 € au lieu de 1 499 € (-13 %) : le grand écran Mini LED polyvalent, idéal pour le jeu
- LG OLED48C6 à 999 € au lieu de 1 299 € (-23 %) : l’OLED compact idéal pour le gaming
- Philips The One 65PQS9001 à 699 € au lieu de 1 099 € (-36 %) : le 65 pouces Ambilight au meilleur prix
Une sélection qui ne laisse personne sur le carreau
Entre le Philips The One qui démocratise le 65 pouces Ambilight, la LG C6 taillée pour les joueurs et la TCL X11L réservée aux grands salons, cette première vague de Boulanger couvre un spectre particulièrement large. Les stocks étant souvent limités sur ce type d’opération, mieux vaut ne pas trop tarder si l’un de ces modèles correspond à votre projet.
TCL C89L : le Mini LED qui lorgne sans complexe vers le haut de gamme
Au sein de la gamme 2026 de TCL, que nous avons passée sur notre banc de test, la C89L cherche le juste milieu entre performances et accessibilité, avec un équipement qui flirte avec celui des modèles premium. Elle profite de la huitième génération de rétroéclairage de la marque, baptisée SQD Mini LED, associée à une dalle WHVA2 Ultra. Les joueurs apprécieront sa fréquence de 144 Hz, tandis que Google TV donne accès à l’ensemble des services de streaming.
Le son n’a pas été sacrifié pour autant, puisque cette version 55 pouces revendique 100 W de puissance avec un caisson de basses intégré et la compatibilité Dolby Atmos. Seule réserve, inhérente à la technologie, un LCD même très évolué ne rivalise pas tout à fait avec l’OLED sur la profondeur des noirs dans une pièce plongée dans l’obscurité.
✅ Les points forts
- Un rétroéclairage SQD Mini LED de huitième génération, associé à une dalle WHVA2 Ultra
- Une fréquence de 144 Hz pour le jeu, avec Google TV pour le streaming
- Un son de 100 W avec caisson de basses intégré et Dolby Atmos
Philips OLED811 : l’OLED qui prolonge l’image jusque sur vos murs
L’OLED811 coche toutes les cases des meilleurs téléviseurs OLED, avec une dalle 4K, un éclairage Ambilight sur trois côtés, Titan OS comme interface, AirPlay 2 et la compatibilité Matter pour la domotique. Sous le capot, on retrouve quatre ports HDMI 2.1 et une fréquence pouvant grimper jusqu’à 165 Hz, de quoi satisfaire les possesseurs de PS5 ou de PC gamer. Côté HDR, la liste est longue, du Dolby Vision 2 Max au HGiG en passant par le Dolby Vision Game.
Les premiers tests sont flatteurs : le site allemand Netzwelt a mesuré des pics à 1 470 nits et une couverture de 99 % de l’espace colorimétrique HDR, des résultats proches de ceux de la LG C6. Le même test note toutefois que les couleurs ont tendance à légèrement pâlir à luminosité maximale, un défaut plus visible sur les instruments de mesure qu’à l’œil nu.
✅ Les points forts
- Un Ambilight sur trois côtés qui prolonge l’image sur le mur
- Jusqu’à 165 Hz et quatre ports HDMI 2.1 pour les consoles et PC gamer
- Une image saluée par la presse, avec des pics mesurés à 1 470 nits et 99 % de l’espace colorimétrique HDR couvert
Samsung QN82H : le Mini LED XXL qui n’oublie pas les joueurs
Ce 75 pouces de la gamme Neo QLED 2026 repose sur un rétroéclairage Quantum Mini LED avec gestion fine de la luminosité par zones, associé à une définition 4K et au processeur NQ4 AI Gen2. Les joueurs y trouveront leur compte grâce à une dalle native à 100 Hz qui peut monter jusqu’à 144 Hz, quatre ports HDMI 2.1 et la prise en charge du VRR, de l’ALLM et du FreeSync Premium Pro.
Côté usage, Tizen gère les applications, avec un engagement de Samsung sur sept ans de mises à jour du système, tandis que Bixby et Alexa permettent de piloter la TV à la voix. AirPlay 2 et Chromecast sont également intégrés, et la fonction Vision AI Companion propose même une traduction instantanée dans six langues. Seule réserve, le son de 30 W compatible Dolby Atmos paraît un peu léger pour un écran de cette taille, et une barre de son sera la bienvenue pour profiter pleinement des films.
✅ Les points forts
- Un rétroéclairage Quantum Mini LED piloté par le processeur NQ4 AI Gen2
- Un équipement gaming complet : jusqu’à 144 Hz, quatre HDMI 2.1, VRR, ALLM et FreeSync Premium Pro
- Sept ans de mises à jour du système Tizen, avec AirPlay 2 et Chromecast intégrés
LG OLED C6 48 pouces : le format idéal pour jouer comme pour regarder
La C6 est la série OLED phare de LG cette année, et sa déclinaison en 48 pouces se distingue par une dalle Tandem OLED, que les autres tailles de la gamme n’embarquent pas. Ce format compact en fait d’ailleurs un choix prisé de ceux qui cherchent un écran de jeu pour PC et ses arguments parlent tout autant aux joueurs qui cherchent une TV pour PS5 ou Xbox Series. Elle s’appuie sur le processeur Alpha 11 Gen 3 et propose quatre HDMI 2.1 ainsi que l’ALLM et le Game Optimizer pour ajuster les réglages en un clin d’œil.
Seul vrai bémol, la C6 fait l’impasse sur le HDR10+, si bien que les contenus mastérisés dans ce format perdent un peu de contraste. Pour le reste, on tient là l’un des écrans les plus polyvalents du moment pour une chambre, un bureau ou un petit salon.
✅ Les points forts
- Une dalle Tandem OLED réservée à la version 48 pouces au sein de la gamme C6
- Un format compact très apprécié comme écran de jeu pour PC
- Quatre HDMI 2.1, l’ALLM et le Game Optimizer pour régler l’image en quelques secondes
Philips The One : le grand écran Ambilight à la portée de toutes les bourses
La gamme The One mise depuis toujours sur la simplicité, avec l’idée d’un téléviseur complet, performant et abordable qui ne demande pas de décortiquer une fiche technique. Le millésime 2026 embarque une dalle QLED 4K cadencée nativement à 120 Hz, le processeur P5 de septième génération et le Dolby Vision 2. L’Ambilight trois côtés est évidemment de la partie, y compris en jeu vidéo.
La connectique compte quatre entrées HDMI, et Titan OS se charge des applications de streaming avec Alexa intégrée. Le son repose sur un système 2.0 de 40 W compatible Dolby Atmos et DTS:X, correct pour un usage quotidien, mais une barre de son restera la bienvenue pour profiter pleinement des films sur un écran de cette taille.
✅ Les points forts

- L’Ambilight trois côtés, actif quelle que soit la source, jeu vidéo compris
- Le processeur P5 de septième génération et la prise en charge du Dolby Vision 2

articles.title: US police forces could soon get a major tech upgrade thanks to DT Research's new rugged laptops, which pack in Nvidia graphics and AI processing
articles.text:
US police forces could soon get a major tech upgrade thanks to DT Research's new rugged laptops, which pack in Nvidia graphics and AI processing
DT Research's LT365PA brings Nvidia RTX graphics to police crime scenes
- DT Research unveils the LT365PA, a 15.6-inch rugged laptop offering Nvidia RTX A2000 or RTX 5000 Ada graphics
- It targets crime scene, crash reconstruction, and command post work, and reaches resellers worldwide in Q1 2027 but has no published price yet
- Much of the design carries over from 2023's LT355, and PNY lists an end-of-life window for RTX A2000 modules in that same quarter
Police crash investigators could soon be processing 3D scans and drone footage at the roadside instead of back at the station, if DT Research gets its way.
The California company has unveiled the LT365PA, a 15.6-inch rugged laptop with optional discrete Nvidia graphics, aimed at crime scene investigators, crash reconstruction teams, and military command posts.
The pitch for potential customers is simple enough: the ability to crunch video, drone imagery, 3D scans, and sensor feeds where the data is collected, rather than waiting on a network connection or a distant data center.
A workstation GPU in a rugged shell
The official DT Research's product page says the LT365PA runs on an Intel Core Ultra 5 225H or Core Ultra 7 255H with 16GB to 32GB of LPDDR5 memory, up to 2TB of storage, and Windows 11 IoT Enterprise.
The 15.6-inch touchscreen is rated at 1,200 nits, with a 4K panel and two MIL-STD-3009 Class B night-vision displays (one for naked-eye use, one for night-vision goggles) available as options. The chassis is IP65 rated and MIL-STD-810H certified, and a CAC reader, RFID and NFC readers, GPS, 4G LTE, and a NIST-compliant BIOS round out the extras public-sector buyers often tend to prefer.
DT Research offers an Nvidia RTX A2000 or what it calls an "RTX 5000A," which appears to be the Ada Lovelace-based RTX 5000 Ada Generation. The gap between the two is large: PNY's embedded MXM line card lists the A2000 module with 2,560 CUDA cores and 8GB of memory, while the RTX 5000 Ada has 9,728 CUDA cores and 16GB at a 115W power rating, giving it more than four times the peak FP32 throughput.
That GPU does most of the AI processing in DT Research's pitch; the NPU inside Intel's Arrow Lake-H chips is rated at just 13 TOPS, as we noted when Intel announced the family, so the heavy video analytics and 3D work DT Research describes will fall to the Nvidia silicon.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Same premise, a different model number and upgrades under the hood
Agencies with long memories may recognize the LT365PA. DT Research's LT355, launched in 2023, was also a 15.6-inch rugged laptop with a 1,200-nit screen and embedded Nvidia RTX A1000 or A2000 graphics, and it too was pitched to law enforcement and the military. At the time, Tsai said DT Research had listened to customers and "developed the next version of our rugged laptop to include an NVIDIA graphics card."
Compare the two spec sheets side by side, and a lot carries over: display brightness, the night-vision options, the operating temperature range, the enclosure materials, and the ratings of the hot-swappable battery packs are identical, and the GPU version still ships with a 230W power adapter.
What has changed is the newer Intel platform, the RTX 5000 Ada option, a 1.1lb (0.5kg) weight saving, and 4K and IR camera options. There is a step back, too, at least on paper: the LT355's two memory slots supported up to 64GB, while the LT365PA tops out at 32GB of LPDDR5.
"Today's field teams need the same high-performance AI computing capabilities at the edge," DT Research president Daw Tsai said in the company's announcement, which says the LT365PA will reach authorized partners and resellers worldwide in the first quarter of 2027. Pricing has not been disclosed.
A crash investigation pitch is arguably the most persuasive part of DT Research's launch. According to the Federal Highway Administration, "every minute of incident delay multiplies traffic queues by a factor of four," and the likelihood of a secondary crash climbs 2.8% for each minute the original incident remains a hazard. Anything that lets investigators confirm their scans and photos are complete before a road reopens has real value.
Despite leaning on such a specific example, the laptop itself doesn't capture anything. Laser scanners and drones do that, and DT Research names no software partners or processing-time figures to show how much faster the LT365PA makes the job.
There are practical trade-offs as well. At 8.6lb (3.9kg), the LT365PA is heavier than our top-rated rugged laptop, the Panasonic Toughbook 40, at 7.4lb, and its IP65 rating is a notch below the IP66 rating of the Toughbook 40 and Getac's B360X lineup. DT Research cites MIL-STD-810H for shock and vibration but publishes no drop height or a fuller list of test methods, whereas Durabook itemizes a long list of 810H tests behind the Z14I-DX3, from altitude to explosive atmosphere.
DT Research also publishes no battery life figure. The two standard packs work out to roughly 123Wh combined, and the GPU model ships with a 230W adapter, nearly double the 120W unit supplied with the standard version, which suggests those hot-swappable batteries will earn their keep under sustained GPU load.
Whether US police forces actually get this upgrade is a separate question. As MIT Technology Review's James O'Donnell has written, "police departments in the US have extraordinary independence," with more than 18,000 of them each deciding what technology to buy, so there is no single customer to win here.
The AI angle deserves a bit of pushback: DT Research pitches on-device video analytics without saying which applications it has validated or tested against, and that is where police technology matters most. The same MIT Technology Review reporting covered an AI tool that tracks people by clothing and body attributes in a way that sidesteps local facial recognition bans. The LT365PA is only hardware, but what agencies run on it will determine how welcome it is.
For crash and forensic teams still working on 2023-era gear, an LT365PA with the RTX 5000 Ada would be a genuine step up. The RTX A2000 version is a far more modest refresh, however, and with shipments not starting until 2027 and procurement cycles to follow, most investigators will not be unpacking one for a while yet.
