articles.title: Qué hacía MrBeast anter de ser millonario y alcanzar más de 500 millones de suscriptores en YouTube
articles.text:
MrBeast es actualmente el youtuber con más suscriptores del mundo. Su canal principal tiene 524 millones de suscriptores y su patrimonio neto asciende a USD 2.600 millones, de acuerdo con Fortune. Pero ¿a qué se dedicaba el creador de contenido antes de ser millonario y famoso?
Jimmy Donaldson, de 28 años, comenzó a subir videos a internet a los 13 años. Sus inicios estuvieron marcados por una adolescencia común en Carolina del Norte, Estados Unidos: creció en un hogar de clase media con dificultades económicas, junto a una madre soltera que trabajaba en varios empleos, según CNN.
A qué se dedicaba MrBeast antes de la fama y el dinero
Antes de la fama y el dinero, MrBeast construyó su carrera con videos caseros, horas de análisis sobre YouTube y desafíos de resistencia que buscaban captar la atención de la audiencia.
Jimmy Donaldson comenzó a publicar contenido a los 13 años. En febrero de 2012 subió su primer video bajo el nombre de MrBeast6000 y, durante los siguientes cuatro o cinco años, experimentó con distintos formatos.
Sus primeros contenidos incluyeron gameplays (videos en los que jugaba videojuegos), vlogs, análisis sobre las ganancias de otros creadores y retos de menor escala. En paralelo, dedicaba largas horas a estudiar el algoritmo de YouTube, las visitas, las miniaturas y las tendencias de la plataforma.
Donaldson también ingresó a la Universidad de Carolina del Este, aunque abandonó sus estudios dos semanas después para dedicarse por completo a la edición de videos. En esa etapa, llegó a vivir o trabajar desde su propio automóvil.
El punto de inflexión llegó en 2017, cuando publicó un video en el que contaba hasta 100.000. El desafío le demandó cerca de 40 horas de grabación.
Ese contenido se volvió viral y cambió el rumbo de su canal. A partir de entonces, los retos de resistencia comenzaron a convertirse en una de las marcas de sus videos.
MrBeast dará asesoría financiera a creadores de contenido
MrBeast se alió con Mastercard para impulsar herramientas financieras y oportunidades de negocio destinadas a creadores de contenido y consumidores.
La iniciativa, desarrollada junto con Beast Industries, la compañía fundada por Jimmy Donaldson, contempla programas de tarjetas de marca compartida, beneficios exclusivos, recursos de educación financiera y experiencias vinculadas con la comunidad del youtuber.
El objetivo de la colaboración es ayudar a que las personas conviertan sus ideas y su presencia en línea en proyectos sostenibles.
Según Jeff Housenbold, director ejecutivo de Beast Industries, el acuerdo permitirá ofrecer habilidades prácticas y confianza para llevar adelante iniciativas propias.
Jill Kramer, directora de marketing y comunicaciones de Mastercard, sostuvo que la nueva generación está creando formas de comercio mientras moldea la cultura digital.
Donaldson pasó de publicar videos en YouTube a construir una empresa con presencia en medios de comunicación, productos de consumo, plataformas tecnológicas, servicios móviles y propuestas financieras.
La alianza busca aprovechar ese alcance para conectar cultura y comercio mediante servicios orientados a quienes buscan desarrollar negocios.
MrBeast pide un Tesla Roadster volador
MrBeast pidió a Tesla un Roadster con capacidad de vuelo para grabar un video, tras la presentación del nuevo deportivo eléctrico de la compañía. Jimmy Donaldson publicó la solicitud el 17 de octubre en X, pero Elon Musk y Tesla no respondieron públicamente.
El vehículo que interesó al creador es el Roadster Rocket, un monoplaza disponible solo por invitación.
Tesla afirmó que puede volar con 10 propulsores de gas frío, alerones activos y un sistema de succión bajo la carrocería. Sin embargo, el modelo no estará habilitado para circular en vías públicas y Musk advirtió que no fue optimizado para la seguridad.
La empresa prevé iniciar la producción en 2028. Musk también anunció una pista de pruebas con loopings en Texas, donde los propietarios podrían ensayar maniobras, incluidas funciones autónomas.

articles.title: Samsung pode lançar tablet dobrável com tela de 17 polegadas • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Samsung pode lançar tablet dobrável com tela de 17 polegadas
Rumores indicam que projeto avançou e pode dar origem ao Galaxy Z Tab. Dispositivo teria 8 polegadas quando fechado.
A Samsung parece realmente disposta a trazer sua tecnologia de display dobrável para outros segmentos mobile. Agora, rumores indicam que a companhia sul-coreana teria avançado no fabricação de um um tablet dobrável, com tela de 17 polegadas.
Segundo o vazamento, o aparelho fechado já se aproximaria do tamanho alcançado pelo Galaxy Z Fold 8 quando aberto, 8 polegadas. De acordo com o GSMArena, os primeiros relatos sobre o projeto surgiram no fim de agosto, quando a mesma fonte afirmou que um dobrável de 17 polegadas estaria em desenvolvimento na Samsung.
Há divergências, porém, sobre o formato da dobra. Uma das possibilidades seria usar uma única tela de 17 polegadas que dobraria no sentido oposto do que costumamos ver nos smartphones, desativando um dos lados. Nesse cenário, a tela permaneceria exposta e poderia facilitar danos em uma queda, por exemplo.
Outra seria adotar uma construção semelhante aos celulares, com uma tela grande na parte interna e um segundo display externo de aproximadamente 8 polegadas. Não há detalhes sobre especificações nem previsão de lançamento comercial.
Essa ideia não é nova dentro da Samsung. Durante a SID Display Week de 2021, a Samsung Display, divisão de telas da empresa, apresentou um conceito de dispositivo com painel OLED dobrável de 17 polegadas e proporção 4:3.
O protótipo podia ser usado totalmente aberto ou parcialmente dobrado, em uma posição semelhante à de um notebook. A tecnologia continuou aparecendo em demonstrações da divisão nos anos seguintes, sendo que, em 2023, rumores chegaram a apontar um possível Galaxy Z Tab. Antes disso, a companhia lançou um “tablet dobrável”, o Galaxy View, com apenas uma tela.
O possível tablet aparece em um momento no qual a Samsung testa novos formatos para sua linha de aparelhos dobráveis. A geração atual inclui o Galaxy Z Fold 8, em formato passaporte, e o Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, que mantém o design comprido das gerações passadas.
Vazamentos recentes já apontam o desenvolvimento de uma nova geração mais extensa para 2027. Espera-se que a Samsung lance um Galaxy Z TriFold 2 e um terceiro modelo da família Galaxy Z Fold 9, que pode ser uma versão mais larga ou com configurações mais básicas.
A expansão ocorre na esteira do lançamento do iPhone Duo, primeiro smartphone dobrável da Apple. Sob a liderança de John Ternus, a empresa também pode lançar outros dobráveis nas próximas gerações.

articles.title: Un musée et ses visiteurs piégés par l'IA de Google, qui l'annonçait fermé à tort !
articles.text:
L’aperçu IA de Google a annoncé à tort la fermeture du Centre Juno Beach, en Normandie, jusqu’en mai 2027. Le musée du Débarquement a démenti, mais corriger l’IA de Google s’est avéré bien plus compliqué que prévu.
Le Centre Juno Beach de Courseulles-sur-Mer, près de Caen, dédié au Débarquement, a découvert à ses dépens qu'une IA de Google pouvait informer sur la fermeture d'un musée sans demander l'avis de personne. En pleines vacances de la Toussaint, le résumé généré par le moteur de recherche annonçait une fermeture totale des lieux jusqu'en mai 2027, de quoi semer le doute chez les visiteurs. Selon toute vraisemblance, l’IA a confondu le musée avec un autre lieu de mémoire normand.
Quand l'IA de Google répond à la place du musée
Le téléphone a sonné, une fois, puis deux, etc. Au standard du musée consacré aux Canadiens de la Seconde Guerre mondiale, le Centre Juno Beach, les appels s'enchaînaient avec la même question : êtes-vous ouverts ? « On ne comprenait pas », raconte à France 3 Normandie Ophélie Duchemin, responsable de la communication. Elle a lancé une recherche sur Google, et « son IA répondait qu'on était fermé ». Sur la capture publiée par le musée, les horaires semblent sérieux, avec fermeture en janvier et le 25 décembre. Mais juste en dessous, pourtant, une mention en italique annonce des travaux du 1er septembre 2026 au 31 mai 2027.
Le jeudi 29 octobre, le musée s'est expliqué dans un post Facebook. Il y dément toute fermeture, explique que l'IA a « tout simplement déduit cette information… sans aucune source fiable », et demande aux internautes de corriger l'intox s'ils la croisent, tout en rappelant de toujours confronter les réponses d'une IA aux sources officielles, un sage conseil d'ailleurs. On a appris que les personnes qui ont appelé le musée pensaient avoir lu l'annonce sur le site du musée. Beaucoup ignorent encore que l'Aperçu IA de Google est automatiquement généré par le géant américain, de façon indépendante.
Faute de pouvoir joindre un humain pour régler le problème, Ophélie Duchemin a fini par interroger l'IA elle-même. Le chatbot a d'abord affirmé avoir trouvé l'information sur le site du musée, « mais c'était impossible », souligne-t-elle. Puis il a changé de ton, s'est dit désolé et a reconnu avoir « halluciné » et expliqué avoir confondu avec Pegasus et la Tapisserie de Bayeux.
Corriger l'IA de Google, un mode d'emploi très approximatif
D'après un guide touristique spécialisé, le Mémorial Pegasus, autre musée du Débarquement situé à Ranville, ferme pour rénovation du 31 août 2026 à mai 2027, des dates quasi identiques. Un internaute a d'ailleurs pointé cette piste sous le post. Le musée de la Tapisserie de Bayeux, lui, est fermé depuis septembre 2025 et ne rouvrira qu'en octobre 2027. Selon toute vraisemblance, l'IA a emprunté le calendrier d'un voisin, puis glissé une fausse piste dans ses excuses.
Pour réparer les dégâts, le chatbot a dit qu'il fallait écrire sur le site du musée, « le maximum de fois possible », qu'il n'était pas fermé pendant les travaux du projet Concordia. Il s'agit d'un projet bien réel, qui prévoit d'agrandir le bâtiment et d'aménager un parc mémoriel sur le terrain voisin. Ophélie Duchemin s'est donc exécutée. Autrement dit, c'est à la victime de l'erreur de réécrire ses pages pour que la machine se corrige.
Ce vendredi, Google semble avoir rectifié le tir. Lorsqu'on lui pose la question « le Centre Juno Beach est-il ouvert », il donne la bonne réponse, à savoir qu'il est ouvert de 9 h 30 à 18 h 00 en octobre. On le challenge alors, on insiste et on lui demande « le musée est-il fermé ». Il donne à nouveau la bonne réponse, indiquant même que le musée ne sera fermé que le 25 décembre ainsi que tout le mois de janvier, ce qui est exact. « C'est grave quand même, on a peut-être perdu des visiteurs », regrette Ophélie Duchemin, qui prévient : « Il faut que les gens fassent attention quand ils préparent leurs vacances. »

articles.title: AI semiconductor industry trends: from chips to systems - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
6 insights from the GSA Women’s Leadership Initiative: AI semiconductor industry trends turn the chip race into a systems race
For decades, the semiconductor industry competed on one thing: the individual chip. One of the biggest AI semiconductor industry trends now under way is the shift toward treating chips as components of much larger systems. Performance, cost and reliability are now determined across the package, the rack and the supply chain, not inside a single die.
That shift moves the hardest problems upstream. Packaging, connectivity, yield, sourcing and verification used to come after design, but now they shape it from the first day. AI is shortening development cycles at the same time as it adds to the complexity engineers have to manage. The next phase will be defined by how well companies coordinate across that whole system.
“I think the AI system is our new chips,” said Letizia Giuliano, vice president of product management and marketing at Qualcomm Technologies Inc. “If we were optimizing everything for the silicon in the past, now these days we’re optimizing everything for the system.”
Giuliano and other industry experts spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and co-host Alison Kosik at the GSA Women’s Leadership Initiative event in Palo Alto, California. The interviews covered AI semiconductor industry trends, optical interconnects, advanced packaging, AI-driven yield learning, physical AI, strategic sourcing and AI-assisted chip design.
Here are six standout insights from the event:
1. Connectivity overtakes compute as the bottleneck in AI infrastructure.
Moving data between chips, memory and racks now limits AI performance more than raw compute, according to Giuliano. At 200 gigabits per second per lane, half of the signal budget goes just to getting out of the package. That is pushing optical interconnect from rack-to-rack links into the rack, the blade and the package itself, with copper and optics in use side by side. Qualcomm has just launched High Bandwidth Compute, a low-power way to attach compute to memory that is tuned for tokens per watt. Building such products at hyperscale volume means product engineering has to join design-for-test, manufacturing and reliability planning early, explained Sophie Wang, senior director of product engineering at Marvell Technology Inc.
Check out theCUBE’s complete interview.
2. Advanced packaging moves from afterthought to system architecture.
The boundary of an AI system is shifting from the chip to the package, emphasized Nisha Ananthakrishnan, senior director of advanced packaging at Intel Corp. Intel uses its EMIB bridge technology to link chiplets and to scale packages from 3x to more than 10x form factors. Outsourced assembly and test providers are becoming system integrators, noted Patricia MacLeod, senior director of corporate communications and industry partnerships at Advanced Semiconductor Engineering Inc. She pointed to ASE’s VIPack platform, which supports technologies ranging from fan-out chip-on-substrate to co-packaged optics. Many of the chips AI depends on, such as power management chips and voltage regulators built at 12 to 28 nanometers, use mature nodes, added Tazrien Kamal, senior director of technology and innovation at GlobalFoundries Inc.
Watch the full interview from theCUBE.
3. AI-driven yield learning turns speed to volume into a competitive edge.
About 70% to 80% of the problems found when scaling up volume manufacturing could have been caught before tapeout, highlighted Preeti Prasher, chief operating officer of Stathera Inc. Using AI to analyze characterization, simulation and inline manufacturing data lets teams start new wafers before a bad lot reaches test. Adaptive testing also cuts test time. Lattice Semiconductor Corp. has released Lattice Prompt, its first AI design assistant, which turns a plain-language request into a field-programmable gate array design and recommends the best part for the form factor and cost, according to Iliana Chen, senior director of program management at Lattice. Demand from robotics and other markets has made volume Lattice’s biggest challenge, Chen noted.
See theCUBE’s full coverage.
4. Physical AI becomes a system-level challenge, not a chip war.
Physical AI is much broader than humanoid robots and covers any autonomous system that senses its surroundings, reasons and acts in the physical world, explained Gina Longoria, VP of external communications at Arm Ltd. The market is in its first inning, and no single company can build the architecture, security and safety standards it needs on its own, she stressed. Firmware is becoming the layer that ties GPUs, CPUs, network cards and Compute Express Link devices into one fleet-scale system, shared Lakshmi Ramagiri, partner for firmware engineering at Microsoft Corp. Security has to move beyond secure boot to continuous trust while a system is running, and the Open Compute Project and DMTF are the standards bodies to watch, Ramagiri added.
Don’t miss the full interview on theCUBE.
5. Strategic sourcing becomes a product decision as AI strains the supply chain.
Sourcing now goes well beyond negotiating prices and shapes product development, risk and customer experience, emphasized Alisa Wang, AVP of global planning and procurement at Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd. Because AI-driven demand can change within a year, suppliers have to be treated as strategic partners that receive product roadmaps early, she noted. Leading-edge logic capacity at Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. Ltd. is the tightest constraint, followed by packaging, specialty materials and critical equipment. In response, Credo is qualifying second-source suppliers and spreading its manufacturing footprint across more regions. Stathera’s Prasher highlighted dual sourcing for key segments and using supplier feedback during new product introduction to develop lower-cost products together.
Hear the full story on theCUBE.
6. AI agents compress chip design as development cycles shrink to six to nine months.
AI is moving from a productivity assistant to a built-in part of electronic design automation flows, explained Rimi Dasgupta, chief of staff for product management and markets at Synopsys Inc., and Vidya Neerkundar, director of product management at Siemens Digital Industries Software. Synopsys has seen verification closure on register-transfer-level designs accelerate as much as 50-fold and debug time drop by 40%, according to Dasgupta. Demand for workload-optimized custom silicon has also cut development cycles from 18 months to six to nine months. AI is probabilistic, but chips must be deterministic, so Synopsys pairs AI with multiphysics solvers from its Ansys acquisition and is working with OpenAI Group PBC on a dedicated GPT-Synopsys model. Multi-die design is the next big shift as chips hit reticle limits, Neerkundar noted.

articles.title: Attack Shark Unveils X60 Gaming Headset with RGB Wireless-Charging Dock
articles.text:
Friday, October 30th 2026
Attack Shark Unveils X60 Gaming Headset with RGB Wireless-Charging Dock
High-performance gaming peripheral brand ATTACK SHARK is set to introduce the X60 Gaming Headset, its latest premium audio offering built to meet the demands of competitive gamers and multi-device users. The headset combines advanced acoustic engineering, ergonomic comfort, low-latency wireless performance, and an RGB-enabled charging dock with integrated hub functionality. It is a complete desktop audio solution built for FPS gaming, entertainment, and extended daily use.
Built for Competitive Audio Performance
The X60 features a 53 mm dynamic driver with a PEN nano-polymer diaphragm, a material widely used in professional audio equipment for its ability to reduce distortion and improve clarity. Combined with a large independent acoustic chamber and airflow-balancing technology, the design delivers precise sound reproduction with clear layering and accurate positional cues, helping players react faster in competitive gameplay. Premium Audio Quality—Experience rich, immersive sound with crisp footsteps, detailed in-game effects, and enhanced audio depth.Beyond the hardware, ATTACK SHARK has refined the listening experience through professional acoustic tuning. Developed with input from audio engineers with over 20 years of experience, the X60 delivers a balanced sound profile that combines detailed reproduction, natural vocal presentation, and the impact required for immersive gameplay. The result is a versatile audio experience suited to competitive gaming, music, and everyday entertainment.
To complement its audio performance, the X60 also places strong emphasis on voice communication during gameplay. The headset features a proprietary AI audio-processing chip designed to enhance microphone noise reduction across multiple channels. Paired with a detachable 360° high-sensitivity microphone and AI voice-enhancement algorithms, the system helps capture speech clearly while reducing unwanted background noise, ensuring reliable team communication even in noisy environments.Users can further refine their experience through the companion software, which offers 7.1 virtual surround sound, spatial audio settings, preset EQ profiles, and customizable equalizer controls. Personalized audio settings can be saved and switched easily, allowing the X60 to adapt to different games, content, and listening preferences.
Engineered for Desktop Integration, Connectivity, and Comfort
One of the X60's defining features is its RGB touch-enabled wireless charging dock, designed to extend the headset beyond a standalone audio device. It supports convenient drop-and-charge functionality while minimizing charging heat, keeping the headset powered and ready for use. It also doubles as a desktop expansion hub with integrated USB and Type-C ports, helping address the growing demand for connectivity across modern gaming setups. Combined with customizable RGB lighting effects, the dock brings together charging, connectivity, and desktop aesthetics in a single solution.The X60 further enhances everyday versatility with ATTACK SHARK's upgraded proprietary 2.4 GHz wireless technology, engineered for low-latency performance and stable connections. Four connection modes, including 2.4 GHz Type-C, 2.4 GHz USB-A, Bluetooth 6.0, and wired USB-A, provide broad compatibility across PCs, laptops, smartphones, tablets, PS4, PS5, Switch, Xbox, and other mainstream gaming platforms. A built-in 1000mAh battery supports extended playtime and allows gaming while charging, while physical slide controls enable quick and intuitive switching between connection modes and key functions.
Comfort remains a central part of the design. A reinforced headband frame and aluminium alloy supports provide durability without compromising flexibility, while the 3D adjustment system allows the earcups to rotate up to 90° horizontally, tilt freely up to 37.5°, and adapt to different head sizes through three-level headband adjustment. Combined with breathable microfiber ear cushions and a memory foam headband, the design delivers a secure, pressure-free fit for extended gaming sessions.
The ATTACK SHARK X60 Gaming Headset will be available starting from November 4, 2026.

articles.title: “Si vas a entrar al mundo laboral, conviene empezar tu carrera en momento de grandes cambios”: Sam Altman, CEO de OpenAI
articles.text:
Sam Altman, director ejecutivo de OpenAI, afirmó que los jóvenes que ingresan ahora al mercado laboral tienen una oportunidad singular para destacar debido a la transformación que provoca la inteligencia artificial en el mundo del trabajo.
En una entrevista con la Escuela de Posgrado de Negocios de la Universidad de Stanford, el ejecutivo sostuvo que “si vas a entrar al mundo laboral, conviene empezar tu carrera en momento de grandes cambios cuando el terreno de juego está más abierto”.
Según Altman, numerosas tareas que hoy realizan personas serán ejecutadas de forma distinta, más rápida y económica por sistemas de inteligencia artificial. “Es totalmente cierto que una enorme cantidad de tareas que la gente hace hoy serán realizadas mejor, más barato y más rápido por la IA, y de manera completamente diferente”, señaló el directivo.
El empresario añadió que amplios sectores de los empleos actuales, tal como se desempeñan en la actualidad, quedarán completamente a cargo de sistemas automatizados.
La transición no será inmediata, pero abrirá oportunidades
Pese al alcance de los cambios que anticipa, Altman advirtió que la transformación no ocurrirá con la velocidad que muchos esperan. Sin embargo, consideró que ese proceso de reconversión puede generar oportunidades concretas para quienes estén dispuestos a dejar de lado las trayectorias profesionales tradicionales y evaluar qué tipo de negocios pueden construirse a partir de las nuevas herramientas tecnológicas.
El director ejecutivo de OpenAI cuestionó la actitud de quienes recién egresan de programas de posgrado en negocios. “Mi decepción crónica con los estudiantes de MBA es que siempre quieren hacer lo que era genial hace cinco años en lugar de intentar algo nuevo”, expresó. Para Altman, el momento actual representa una ocasión propicia para emprender proyectos inéditos antes que replicar modelos de negocio ya consolidados.
Nuevas empresas podrían superar en tamaño a OpenAI
El fundador de OpenAI planteó que la tecnología desarrollada por su compañía habilita la creación de negocios que resultaban inviables apenas unos años atrás. “Hay muchas empresas que se pueden construir sobre la tecnología que OpenAI ha puesto en el mundo que serán mucho más grandes y, espero, más importantes que OpenAI”, afirmó.
El empresario cuenta con experiencia previa en la fundación de compañías desde cero. En 2005 abandonó sus estudios de ciencias de la computación en Stanford para cofundar Loopt, una plataforma de redes sociales basada en geolocalización que luego fue adquirida por otra empresa. Posteriormente se incorporó a la aceleradora de startups Y Combinator, donde ejerció como presidente entre 2014 y 2019.
A partir de esa trayectoria, Altman planteó que la inteligencia artificial representa una oportunidad para que una nueva generación de emprendedores aborde problemas que antes parecían fuera de alcance. “Creo que las personas con alto potencial, impulso, ideas, una nueva forma de ver las cosas y nuevas habilidades tienden a desempeñarse relativamente bien cuando el terreno se mueve más”, señaló ante estudiantes de Stanford.
El planteo de Altman coincide con un repunte en la actividad emprendedora de Estados Unidos. Durante 2025, los ciudadanos estadounidenses presentaron 5,7 millones de solicitudes para iniciar nuevos negocios, la cifra anual más alta registrada por la Oficina del Censo en las dos décadas que lleva recopilando ese tipo de datos.
Referentes del sector tecnológico respaldan la postura de Altman
El cofundador de Reddit, Alexis Ohanian, coincidió en que los emprendedores que construyen sus proyectos con inteligencia artificial desde el inicio cuentan con una ventaja frente a quienes intentan adaptar la tecnología a estructuras empresariales ya existentes.
“Cualquiera que haya fundado una empresa en los últimos dos años ha estado construyendo una compañía en la era de la IA, y tiene una ventaja predeterminada, porque el ADN de su organización pertenece a este nuevo mundo”, declaró en una entrevista con la revista Fortune el año pasado. Ohanian agregó que existen fundadores con gran motivación dispuestos a competir con empresas ya establecidas, y que ese origen marca una diferencia sustancial en la capacidad de ejecución de los nuevos proyectos.
El empresario Mark Cuban, exinversor del programa Shark Tank, también instó a los emprendedores a utilizar la inteligencia artificial como ventaja competitiva. “Si no la estás usando para moverte más rápido o tomar decisiones más inteligentes, estás en desventaja”, dijo Cuban a Fortune en 2025.
El empresario definió a la tecnología como una herramienta de apalancamiento y sostuvo que “el emprendedor con más éxito será el que entienda cómo usar la inteligencia artificial de manera adecuada”.

articles.title: Apple’s Mac mini M4 makes the newer M6 hard to justify
articles.text:
I still think the Mac mini M4 is 'the best small form factor PC in the world' — and it’s $150 off at Best Buy
The cheapest way into the Mac ecosystem
The Apple Mac mini M6 may be catching all the headlines right now, but I still think for most people looking for a stylish and powerful mini PC, the Mac mini M4 is the optimal choice. It might lack the extra oomph of the M6, but for daily office tasks and content creation, it's way better value.
Case in point. The Apple Mac mini M4 is currently $650 (was $799) at Best Buy. If you want a fast, compact desktop for work, photo editing, or everyday use, and you already own a monitor and keyboard, the Mac mini M4 is the best-value Mac you can buy. Meanwhile, Best Buy has the Mac mini M6 for $799 (was $899).
• Best for: Professionals and creators upgrading an older Mac or Windows mini PC to a powerful, near-silent desktop without paying M6 prices. .
• Why we like it: We scored this machine 5 stars in our review, and wondered if it might actually be the best Mac ever. For most people, it will be. Apple’s speedy M4 chip, 16GB of unified memory for smooth multitasking and Apple Intelligence, a tiny five-inch-square design, and handy front-facing USB-C ports and a headphone jack.
A compact desktop with Apple’s M4 chip, 16GB of unified memory, and a 256GB SSD, with front USB-C ports and a headphone jack, plus Thunderbolt, HDMI, and Ethernet on the back. It supports Apple Intelligence and comes in silver.
Why we recommend it
In our Mac mini M4 review, our expert Matt awarded it an Editor’s Choice badge and full marks for value, praising its strong performance, much smaller design, and convenient front ports. He called it the cheapest way into the Mac ecosystem, though he noted it struggles with modern games and that its power button sits awkwardly on the underside. Our review unit had a 512GB SSD rather than this model’s 256GB, but it used the same M4 chip and 16GB of memory.
Price Context & Historical Value
Apple raised the Mac mini’s starting price to $799 earlier this year as memory costs surged, so this $150 discount is measured against Apple’s real current price rather than an inflated list price. It’s still more than the $599 the M4 Mac mini launched at, and well above the sub-$500 deals we saw before the price hike. Given today’s pricing, though, $649 is a strong deal and a good time to buy.
For comparison, the Mac mini M6 is currently down to $799 at Best Buy. For some workloads, it may be better. For general office tasks, the M4 is still worth considering for its value.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the Apple Mac mini M4 if... you want an affordable, powerful Mac desktop, you already have a monitor, keyboard, and mouse, or you want a near-silent machine for work, photo editing, or music production.
❌ Skip the Apple Mac mini M4 if... you need lots of local storage, since 256GB fills quickly; you want to play the latest PC games; or you don’t already own a monitor and accessories, which add to the total cost.

articles.title: Review da Sabala DR-500: uma caixa para festas em alto e bom som • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Review da Sabala DR-500: uma caixa para festas em alto e bom som
Caixa de som Bluetooth da Sabala se destaca pelos 500 W de potência, proteção contra água e bateria gigante; confira a análise
A Sabala DR-500 é uma caixa de som Bluetooth que promete experiência completa e extremamente potente para quem precisa de volume e qualidade de áudio em diversos ambientes, desde reuniões em casa até grandes encontros ao ar livre.
O modelo se destaca ao entregar 500 W de potência em um sistema de áudio de três vias, com uma bateria colossal de 81.000 mAh, capaz de funcionar inclusive como power bank para carregar outros dispositivos.
O Tecnoblog testou a Sabala DR-500 nos últimos dias e traz todos os detalhes sobre a qualidade de som e se vale a pena o investimento.
Aviso de ética
Esse é um conteúdo patrocinado. Isso quer dizer que a marca encomendou a nossa análise, mas não comprou o resultado dela. Por isso, mantemos os pontos positivos e negativos da Sabala DR-500 de forma clara e precisa, com o objetivo de ajudar você a tomar a melhor decisão de compra.
Para mais informações, acesse a nossa Política Editorial.
A embalagem da Sabala DR-500 impressiona pelo tamanho avantajado. Ao abrir o pacote, encontramos apenas a caixa de som, o cabo de energia para carregamento e o manual de instruções.
É importante destacar que não acompanham o produto cabos auxiliares do tipo P2 e nem microfone para uso na função de karaokê, exigindo que você utilize ou compre esses acessórios separadamente.
Para atender à proposta de mobilidade, o equipamento conta com uma alça integrada para transporte. Na parte superior, fica posicionado o painel de controles físicos.
As dimensões e peso são:
Durante os meus testes, senti que o peso compromete bastante a experiência com mobilidade. Se a sua intenção for ficar alternando a caixa de cômodo a todo momento ou transportá-la a pé por longas distâncias, como em trilhas, por exemplo, esse peso pode dificultar as coisas.
Os botões são emborrachados e bem distribuídos, permitindo ligar e desligar o aparelho, realizar o pareamento Bluetooth, acionar o modo Auracast, ajustar o volume, pausar ou dar play nas músicas.
Você também pode ativar o modo estéreo sem fio, alternar os efeitos de iluminação e mudar os modos de equalização.
Na traseira do dispositivo ficam instaladas as conexões físicas, todas protegidas por uma tampa de borracha vedada.
Essa proteção garante à caixa a certificação IP66 de resistência contra poeira e jatos fortes de água, permitindo o uso tranquilo à beira da piscina ou na praia sem medo de respingos.
O design conta ainda com iluminação RGB nas laterais, que oferecem efeitos luminosos dinâmicos alternando de cor conforme o ritmo da música ou de acordo com a sua escolha.
A qualidade de som cumpriu o esperado para um dispositivo com 500 W de capacidade. O aparelho entrega som estéreo 360 com excelente definição entre graves, médios e agudos, sem distorção mesmo com o volume no máximo.
Toda essa potência da caixa pode ser controlada pelos modos de equalização oferecidos tanto no app quanto no próprio produto. O modo interno ajusta a reprodução das músicas para que o som alto não incomode quem estiver escutando dentro de casa.
Já no modo externo, é possível notar um aumento na definição do som pra que todo mundo consiga escutar com clareza o que tá sendo reproduzido ao ar livre, por exemplo.
Segundo a marca, a DR-500 conta com um sistema de som de três vias:
Ela também possui três amplificadores de áudio, dedicados exclusivamente para cada canal sonoro. No geral, é um modelo voltado para diferentes perfis de uso, seja para escutar em casa, em encontros entre amigos, na praia ou em festas, tranquilamente.
A autonomia é outro destaque positivo da Sabala DR-500: são 81.000 mAh de capacidade. Isso permite até 46 horas de reprodução de músicas sem parar. Claro, isso pode variar — com o volume no máximo, foi possível chegar a aproximadamente oito horas de som.
Já o carregamento da caixa é relativamente demorado por conta dessa alta capacidade de bateria. Para carregar de 0 a 100%, são necessárias cinco horas na tomada.
Esses 81.000 mAh também permitem que você conecte seu celular, utilizando a caixa como um powerbank.
Mas o modelo vem equipado com apenas uma porta USB-A na parte traseira. Na prática, isso limita o uso simultâneo de acessórios.
Por exemplo: se você conectar um pendrive com músicas, não terá outra entrada disponível para carregar a bateria do seu celular ao mesmo tempo — exigindo que você escolha entre uma função ou outra.
No quesito conectividade sem fio, a caixa vem atualizada com o padrão Bluetooth 6.0. Durante todo o período de testes, a conexão se manteve estável em distâncias de até 10 metros, sem engasgos, atrasos ou quedas de sinal.
A DR-500 traz suporte às tecnologias Auracast e TWS. O recurso TWS permite parear duas caixas sem fio em modo estéreo.
Já o Auracast possibilita a transmissão simultânea do mesmo áudio para diversas caixas compatíveis em um mesmo ambiente.
No painel traseiro, há um pacote completo de conexões físicas: uma entrada auxiliar P2 tradicional, a porta USB-A para leitura de pendrives ou uso como power bank e uma entrada P10 para microfone ou para conexão de instrumentos musicais.
Aplicativo da Sabala permite usar todas as funções presentes no modelo remotamente, como o equalizador de ambiente, controle do Auracast e as personalizações de iluminação. Tudo com boa responsividade no Android ou iPhone (iOS).
Você também pode conferir a bateria, configurar um timer ou fazer o desligamento da caixa de som diretamente pelo celular.
Esses recursos, apesar de básicos, são importantes principalmente em festas ou confraternizações, já que você não precisa ficar indo até a caixa de som para aumentar ou diminuir o volume, por exemplo, ou fazer outros ajustes.
A Sabala DR-500 é uma escolha bastante atraente no mercado de áudio de alta potência.
Custando na faixa de R$ 2.300, o grande trunfo do modelo está na relação entre preço e potência bruta. Nessa mesma faixa de preço, concorrentes diretas como a JBL Boombox 4, entregam um nível de potência consideravelmente menor.
Com a DR-500, você leva impressionantes 500 W e um sistema de três vias pagando um preço menor que opções rivais. Além disso, a bateria gigante de 81.000 mAh com função power bank e a certificação IP66 contra água e poeira são importantes para quem organiza festas e eventos ao ar livre.
No entanto, o peso de 11,5 kg tornam o transporte constante um desafio, a recarga completa leva 5 horas e a embalagem não inclui cabos auxiliares ou microfone.
Se a sua prioridade for o volume mais alto e a maior autonomia, sem se importar com o peso para trasportar, a Sabala DR-500 entrega bom custo-benefício nesta categoria.
Agora, eu quero saber de você: o que achou da caixa de som? Deixe sua opinião na Comunidade do Tecnoblog!

articles.title: L'ancien patron d'Intel croit avoir trouvé une solution à la crise de la RAM
articles.text:
Avec le soutien de Pat Gelsinger, Nagare Labs développe une mémoire qui pourrait offrir cinq fois plus de capacité sur une même surface. Une promesse encore expérimentale, dont la commercialisation pourrait prendre de nombreuses années.
La crise des composants mémoire et la hausse des prix continuent d'impacter durement les divers appareils informatiques grand public. Smartphones, tablettes, PC… Tout a augmenté, même les consoles ! Cette crise, pas près de se terminer, pourrait toutefois trouver une issue grâce à une nouvelle technologie baptisée Z2RAM.
Développée par Nagare Labs, une entreprise cofondée par les professeurs Suman Datta et Shimeng Yu du Georgia Institute of Technology, elle bénéficie d'un financement de 5 millions de dollars mené par Playground Global, dont Pat Gelsinger, ancien PDG d'Intel, est un associé.
Une architecture combinant trois technologies de mémoire
La Z2RAM ambitionne de réunir la rapidité de la SRAM, la densité de la DRAM et les possibilités d'empilement vertical de la NAND, avec une consommation énergétique réduite et une fabrication nettement simplifiée.
La SRAM, utilisée dans les caches des processeurs, est rapide mais occupe beaucoup de place. La DRAM, utilisée dans les si chères barrettes de RAM, offre une densité supérieure, mais une vitesse moindre. Quant à la NAND des SSD, elle privilégie la densité grâce à son empilement vertical, au détriment des performances.
Contrairement à la DRAM traditionnelle, qui exploite un transistor et un condensateur par bit, la Z2RAM repose quant à elle sur deux transistors. La charge est stockée dans la capacité du second, supprimant le condensateur physique. Cette architecture autorise également une lecture non destructrice, sans réécriture systématique des données.
Nagare Labs prévoit de fabriquer plusieurs couches de mémoire sur une même puce, puis de relier celle-ci à la puce de calcul par collage hybride, une technique déjà employée par AMD pour le 3D V-Cache. Selon l'entreprise, cette conception offrirait une densité plus de cinq fois supérieure à celle de la SRAM, à bande passante équivalente. À surface équivalente, une zone qui accueille actuellement 64 Mo de SRAM pourrait alors contenir 320 Mo de Z2RAM.
Des applications ciblées sur l'intelligence artificielle
Alors, tout le monde va devoir changer les barrettes de mémoire de son PC ? Absolument pas, loin du grand public, cette technologie vise principalement les datacenters dédiés à l'intelligence artificielle. Ces derniers sont contraints à certaines limites de bande passante mémoire et de capacité.
Les LPU de Groq 3 de NVIDIA embarquent environ 500 Mo de SRAM par puce. Une mémoire plus dense pourrait permettre de répartir certains grands modèles sur moins d’accélérateurs, mais l’ampleur de ce gain reste à démontrer.
Une commercialisation encore lointaine
La Z2RAM demeure au stade des prototypes de laboratoire. Nagare Labs recherche un partenaire industriel pour poursuivre son développement et vise des premiers exemplaires fonctionnels d'ici quatre ans. La commercialisation pourrait toutefois prendre une dizaine d'années.
Des obstacles subsistent concernant la fiabilité des semi-conducteurs à oxyde et l'absence d'interface standardisée pour les accélérateurs. Nagare Labs pourrait donc devoir développer sa propre solution.
Pour Pat Gelsinger, ancien PDG d'Intel, l'expansion des infrastructures d'IA favorise l'émergence de nouvelles mémoires. Si la Z2RAM n'est pas la réponse immédiate aux pénuries de RAM pour le grand public, son potentiel développement pourrait libérer certaines lignes de production, afin de retrouver une offre et un tarif corrects pour nos tablettes, smartphones, et ordinateurs personnels.

articles.title: Epomaker Launches the EM3 Carbon-Fiber Composite Gaming Mouse
articles.text:
Friday, October 30th 2026
Epomaker Launches the EM3 Carbon-Fiber Composite Gaming Mouse
Built around the community's expectations for precise control, tactile quality, and convenient charging, the EM3 gaming mouse combines a lightweight body weighing about 56 g, a PAW3315 sensor, and up to a 1000 Hz polling rate with carbon-fiber-reinforced materials, flexible connectivity, and a magnetic charging dock. These elements bring gaming performance, refined feel, and everyday convenience into a single product.
Precision Tracking and Customization
The gaming mouse is powered by the PAW3315 sensor, supporting up to 16000 DPI for precise, consistent tracking. Polling rates of up to 1000 Hz are available in both wired and 2.4 GHz wireless modes, with four selectable levels available through the driver, giving the EM3 the responsiveness expected from a performance-focused gaming mouse. Further customization is available through the web-based Epomaker Hub and Epomaker Driver 3.0, where users can adjust functions including the Fire Key, button debounce, motion correction, and button response. For quick sensitivity changes, the physical DPI button also provides six DPI levels without the need to open the software.Carbon-Fiber Composite, Shaped for Control
The EM3 uses a carbon-fiber and ABS composite for its top shell and buttons, giving the mouse a solid, refined feel while keeping the overall construction lightweight. The conductive composite shell can be detected by capacitive touchscreens, enabling basic touch interactions such as swiping.
At approximately 56 g, the EM3 is designed for quick, controlled movement. Its medium-sized body suits small to medium hands and claw-grip users, while a fine spray coating helps maintain a dry, tactile feel during extended use. The material, weight, and surface treatment create a balanced, controlled feel in hand.
A Magnetic Dock for Charging and Storage
This mouse charges via direct contact when placed on its magnetic dock after use. The dock also serves as part of the EM3's visual identity, featuring an integrated RGB base and a dedicated button for lighting control without requiring software. Available in matching colors with the mouse, the dock combines charging, storage, and desktop presentation in one compact design.Tri-Mode Connection for Changing Setups
The EM3 supports wired, 2.4 GHz wireless, and Bluetooth connection modes, allowing it to work seamlessly across a wide range of modern devices. It is compatible with both Windows and macOS, offering added flexibility across different systems. A 600mAh battery provides extended battery life for reliable wireless use throughout the day.
It is available in black, silver, and pink. Each version carries the same performance foundation while offering a distinct visual character for different setups.
Price and Availability
The Epomaker EM3 is now available on the Epomaker official website, Amazon store, and AliExpress store. The mouse is available for just $35.99 on the official website.

articles.title: Extreme Networks wants the network to run AI, not just be run by it - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Extreme Networks wants the network to run AI, not just be run by it
At its recent AI Summit in Amsterdam, Extreme Networks Inc. shared early Agent ONE Coworker results and previewed Exchange zones, which put spare access points and switch compute to work as on-premises artificial intelligence infrastructure. Here’s what it means and what information technology pros should do about it.
Most of the conversation about AI and networking has flowed in one direction. AI comes in, examines the network and helps the network team run it better. That’s useful, but it treats the network as the patient, not as a resource.
At the summit, the company argued that there is a better way. The network should be managed by AI and serve as a place where AI runs, using data that most organizations currently throw away. This would let network teams stop being the people who merely keep the Wi-Fi up for the AI project and become the people who host it.
The news
Extreme made two announcements. The first was a progress report on Extreme Agent ONE Coworker, the ambient AI agent built into Extreme Platform ONE. In its first month, Extreme says, customers saved about 1,000 hours of troubleshooting, 41% of Platform ONE customers used it for daily tasks, and users responded to 98% of critical “nudges,” the proactive alerts the agent raises after running its own pre-investigation. Engagement was roughly 10 times that of Extreme’s first-generation conversational assistant.
The second was a preview of Extreme Exchange zones, planned for the first half of 2027. A zone combines an Extreme Universal Compute Platform or a customer-owned server with spare capacity from Extreme access points and switches already installed at a site. AI applications from the Extreme Exchange marketplace run locally on open-weight models by default, with cloud inference used only when policy allows and logged every time. Agent ONE Operator mode, the autonomous tier, also arrives in the first half of 2027.
Ambient beats conversational
The first wave of AI in networking wasn’t a smashing success because it relied on a chatbot built on fragmented data. During his talk, Nabil Bukhari (pictured), Extreme’s chief technology officer and president of AI platforms, called it a design flaw. “Conversational AI requires the user to have the question and the context, and you will be surprised how difficult that is when it comes to technology domains,” he said.
In Extreme’s focus groups, many administrators asked a powerful AI assistant how many devices they had, even though the number was already on the dashboard. Coworker flips that. “We have moved to the world where instead of you prompting AI, AI prompts you,” Bukhari said.
The best evidence came from a customer. Kevin Rocha, chief information officer at Hill College, described a wireless outage in a building housing HR, finance and enrollment. “Agent ONE Coworker told me exactly where to look: One access point needed attention, and several more were due for firmware upgrades. We resolved the issue in about 20 minutes rather than an entire morning,” he said. Platform ONE, he added, “is like having two or three more network engineers on staff.”
That’s the value of AI for networking in most enterprises. It doesn’t replace the network team. It gives a small team the reach of a larger one. Bukhari also admitted that there is more work to be done. He explained that 58% of support cases opened by Agent ONE arrive with all the evidence support needs. “Fifty-eight is pretty good, but 58 is still 58 and not 100.”
Governance has to live outside the agent
Andrew Grill, the opening keynote speaker and author of “Digitally Curious,” discussed the stakes. “When a chatbot gets it wrong, you might have a bad paragraph. If an agent gets it wrong, you have a bad Tuesday,” he said. His test for any deployment: “If your agent does something wrong at 2 in the morning, whose phone rings?”
Extreme’s Operator demo is subject to guardrails. Each of the 268 tools can be configured to auto-authorize, ask first or never use. Four baseline rules apply to everything: do no harm to the network, never expose a credential, never act outside your role and never act in another tenant. Every task has a full audit trace.
An important design criterion is that governance reside within Extreme Exchange, not Platform ONE. “You can’t govern something from within,” Bukhari said. “That is how you get rogue agents.” If the system running the agent also controls its permissions, you don’t have a control plane. You have an honor system.
Exchange zones are the bigger bet
Networks generate dense, real-time telemetry on location, movement and behavior that far exceeds what operations needs, and cloud platforms drop most of it because moving it is expensive. Bukhari said the valuable uses tend to hit four walls: sovereignty, localization, survivability and economics.
The innovation is where the compute comes from. Higher-end access points have four to eight cores and typically use only one, so organizations already pay for and power idle compute hanging from their ceilings. In one healthcare demo, a fall-detection app that combined camera feeds, Wi-Fi location and paging to find the closest responder ran entirely on access points. A second demo used Seattle Seahawks game data to predict gate congestion and showed that some fans faced a seven- to eight-minute walk to the nearest pro shop.
“This is not a network management use case,” Bukhari said. “These use cases are impossible without that rich, real-time telemetry.” That’s the strategic point. The return goes to operations, facilities and fan experience, giving network leaders something they’ve rarely had: a revenue story.
Zones will ship in 2027, and the demo apps were built in collaboration with design partners. The model needs a real application catalog, so Extreme is pairing it with a free, invitation-only forward-deployed engineering program. Pricing will be consumption-based, measured in “agent actions.” As Grill noted, most organizations haven’t priced the cost of their tasks today, so they’ll struggle to judge value.
Sovereignty is about permission
As expected, the most valuable insights came from the customer panel. Jonathan Monk, CIO of the Institute of Cancer Research in London, manages roughly 9 petabytes of data, but performance isn’t his primary reason for building sovereign AI. “When we ask people in our organization what’s the biggest thing that holds them back from using AI, it’s that I’m not sure if I’m allowed to,” he said.
Andrew Beynon, chief enterprise architect at Extreme partner ARO, linked that to shadow AI. The goal, he said, is “to make the journey for legitimate adoption of AI easier than the move to illegitimate adoption.” Monk called it building “paved roads.” The industry treats sovereignty as a compliance cost, but these customers see it as an adoption accelerator.
David O’Neill, director of IT operations at Liverpool Football Club, offered a balanced take on AI. “While AI is an answer, it’s not necessarily the answer.” Bukhari highlighted the next challenge: “Adoption is no longer the problem. It’s the optimization of adoption.” After AI-generated product specs ballooned to 200 pages, Extreme capped them at three pages.
Advice for IT pros
Include the network team in the AI plan. If it isn’t involved, decisions about traffic, inference location and data residency will be made without the people who understand them.
Separate governance from execution. Check whether agent permissions, audit logs and the kill switch are outside the system the agent runs in.
Inventory the data your network discards. Identify the location and occupancy telemetry you already generate, and which business units would pay to use them.
Pressure-test the edge-compute math. Ask how workloads are prioritized during RF demand spikes and which model sizes realistically fit on an access point.
Price your tasks first. Without a baseline cost for today’s work, it’s impossible to evaluate consumption-based AI pricing.
Final thoughts
Extreme can’t outspend its larger competitors, so it’s betting on speed and focus as a pure-play networking company. The Agent ONE numbers suggest that’s paying off on the operations side.
Exchange zones are the bolder idea. Turning installed access points and switches into a distributed, centrally governed inference fabric is more ambitious than anything I’ve seen from Extreme’s larger rivals. It’s also unproven, and 2027 is a long way off in AI time. As Beynon put it, “today’s knowledge has got an expiry date.”
The direction Extreme is headed is the right one. For 30 years, the network has been the most important infrastructure, yet nobody wanted to talk about it until it broke. AI makes the network the system that connects data, compute and people, and possibly the one that runs the AI, too. Network pros who see that early will have a much bigger role in where their organizations go next.
Zeus Kerravala is a principal analyst at ZK Research, a division of Kerravala Consulting. He wrote this article for SiliconANGLE.

articles.title: The Google Nest Wifi Pro is the simplest Wi-Fi 6e mesh router I know
articles.text:
The Google Nest Wifi Pro is the simplest Wi-Fi 6E mesh router I’d set up for non-techy family members — and it’s half price at Best Buy
Refreshingly easy to set up and manage through the Google Home app, and a single unit covers up to 2,200 square feet.
I don't know about you, but I'm sort of the gadget-man of the family. The tech-head. The makeshift IT consultant that gets called upon whenever there's an issue with technology. If you fall into the same category (or you never want to call on your family IT support again), I'd definitely recommend checking out the Google Nest Wifi Pro 6e Wi-Fi mesh router for $100 (was $200) at Best Buy.
The half-price deal makes it incredibly tempting. It's ridiculously simple to set up and manage, making it the ideal no-fuss mesh router pick if you or your family need better connections while working from home. If your home Wi-Fi is spotty and you don’t want to wrestle with complicated router settings, Nest Wifi Pro delivers fast, reliable coverage with minimal setup.
• Best for: home workers and families in small to midsize homes needing fast, easy-to-manage Wi-Fi with the option to add more units later.
• Why we like it: tri-band Wi-Fi 6E with a 6GHz band for less congestion, up to 2,200 square feet of coverage from one unit, effortless setup through the Google Home app, and support for adding more units to build a mesh.
A single tri-band Wi-Fi 6E (AXE5400) mesh router covering 2.4GHz, 5GHz, and 6GHz bands, with up to 2,200 square feet of coverage, support for up to 100 connected devices, WPA3 security, parental controls, and two Gigabit Ethernet ports. It’s managed through the Google Home app and also works as a Thread border router and Matter controller for smart home devices. Sold by Best Buy.
Why We Recommend It
Google built the Nest Wifi Pro for people who want Wi-Fi to simply work, and its app-based setup and automatic updates make it one of the least intimidating routers to own. We haven’t reviewed the Nest Wifi Pro, so this pick rests on Google’s track record with mesh networking and the router’s specs. Its 6GHz band is a real plus if you have newer phones and laptops that support Wi-Fi 6E, since it’s far less crowded than the older bands.
Price Context & Historical Value
Half off its $199.99 launch price is a strong deal, and $99.99 puts a Wi-Fi 6E mesh router within reach of almost any budget. Keep in mind that it launched in 2022, so it lacks the newer Wi-Fi 7 standard and multi-gig Ethernet found on pricier routers. For most homes with internet plans under 1Gbps, though, it’s a great buy at this price.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the Google Nest Wifi Pro if... you want fast Wi-Fi that’s easy to set up and manage, your home is under about 2,200 square feet or you plan to add more units, or you use Google Home and want a router that doubles as a smart home hub.
❌ Skip the Google Nest Wifi Pro if... you want Wi-Fi 7 or multi-gig Ethernet ports for a very fast internet plan, you need lots of wired ports, or you already own older Google Wifi or Nest Wifi units, which can’t join a Nest Wifi Pro mesh.

articles.title: El 31% de las pymes en América Latina perdió dinero por ciberataques: phishing y falsas aplicaciones de IA
articles.text:
El 31% de las pequeñas y medianas empresas (pymes) de América Latina sufrió pérdidas económicas tras ser víctima de ciberataques, según datos de Kaspersky, en un escenario donde la interrupción de sistemas puede afectar ventas, pagos, atención al cliente y acceso a información clave.
En países como Colombia, el 25% de las pymes registró incidentes de phishing, el 20% enfrentó ataques vinculados con vulnerabilidades de software y el 15% tuvo problemas asociados con accesos remotos externos.
A los anteriores riesgos se suman uno menos conocido: las aplicaciones falsas de inteligencia artificial (IA), que buscan instalar programas maliciosos bajo la apariencia de servicios conocidos.
Por qué las empresas pequeñas son un objetivo para los ciberdelincuentes
Carolina Mojica, gerente de Productos para el Consumidor para NOLA y SOLA en Kaspersky, afirmó que existe una percepción equivocada entre algunos empresarios: “Creen que no van a tener ciberataques porque son pequeñas y que no son un blanco, y por el contrario sí lo son”.
El tamaño de un negocio no reduce el interés de los ciberdelincuentes. Las pymes suelen manejar datos de clientes, transacciones, contactos de proveedores y archivos operativos que pueden ser utilizados para extorsión, fraude o venta ilegal.
Además, muchas cuentan con recursos limitados para incorporar grupos especializados o protocolos de respuesta ante incidentes. La vulnerabilidad aumenta cuando la protección queda relegada por falta de presupuesto o conocimiento, señaló Mojica.
Qué lugar ocupa el phishing entre las amenazas para pymes
Los correos, mensajes y enlaces fraudulentos siguen entre las principales puertas de entrada para un ciberataque. “Un mensaje que aparenta provenir de un banco, un proveedor o un colega puede inducir a un empleado a entregar contraseñas, descargar archivos infectados o ingresar datos en sitios falsos”, aseguró Mojica.
El problema no se limita al correo corporativo. Las comunicaciones por aplicaciones de mensajería y colaboración pueden ser utilizadas para engañar a las víctimas.
“Una persona puede con un simple clic abrir una puerta gigante de una vulnerabilidad”, señaló Mojica. El riesgo alcanza a computadoras, celulares y cuentas vinculadas con la operación cotidiana.
Cómo se usan las falsas aplicaciones de inteligencia artificial para estafas a pymes
La popularidad de herramientas de inteligencia artificial abrió otra vía para la distribución de software malicioso. Entre enero y abril de 2026, Kaspersky detectó más de 33.300 ataques a nivel mundial en los que programas maliciosos o no deseados se hacían pasar por aplicaciones como ChatGPT, Claude y DeepSeek.
A la par, los atacantes usan como señuelo servicios conocidos de comunicación, entre ellos WhatsApp, Telegram, Zoom y Microsoft Teams. Las falsas aplicaciones pueden solicitar permisos excesivos, capturar credenciales o instalar archivos dañinos.
A estos riesgos se suman las herramientas de inteligencia artificial que permiten crear mensajes, audios e imágenes que imitan a personas reales. Esto puede reforzar intentos de fraude en los que un supuesto familiar, socio o superior jerárquico solicita una transferencia urgente o información reservada.
Mojica sugirió detenerse ante pedidos inusuales y confirmar la información por otra vía. “Si llega un mensaje raro, si me están pidiendo una información que es rara, primero hay que pensar, llamar y corroborar”, indicó.
Cuánto puede costar un ataque a una pequeña empresa
Las consecuencias de un incidente varían según la información comprometida y la capacidad de recuperación de cada empresa. Mojica estimó que restablecer sistemas o información puede costar desde 500 hasta 3.000 dólares, aunque la cifra puede aumentar si se bloquea toda la infraestructura tecnológica o se paralizan las operaciones.
Asimismo, el ransomware, una modalidad que bloquea o secuestra archivos, puede agravar este escenario. Mojica señaló que contar con copias de seguridad verificadas, procedimientos de recuperación y dispositivos aislables reduce el alcance del daño.
Qué medidas pueden reducir la exposición a ciberataques
La falta de experiencia del personal de seguridad informática es uno de los factores de riesgo para el 26% de las pymes latinoamericanas consultadas. La capacitación de empleados es clave porque muchos ataques dependen de errores humanos: contraseñas débiles, enlaces abiertos sin verificación o permisos innecesarios.
Las medidas básicas incluyen identificar los activos esenciales del negocio, actualizar sistemas, restringir permisos y realizar respaldos periódicos. “La ciberseguridad es un hábito que deben tener todos los empleados”, afirmó Mojica.

articles.title: Le mystère d’Artemis : personne ne sait de combien de ravitaillements Starship aura besoin pour viser la Lune
articles.text:
Pour rejoindre la Lune, Starship doit d’abord faire le plein en orbite, mais personne ne sait vraiment combien de lancements cela demandera. Et le calendrier d’Artemis, lui, ne laisse presque aucune marge.
Starship occupe une place centrale dans le programme Artemis, puisque la NASA l’a sélectionné, aux côtés de Blue Moon de Blue Origin, pour poser ses astronautes sur la Lune. Et le 23 octobre dernier, l’agence a de nouveau ajusté sa feuille de route, tout en maintenant son objectif d’un retour sur notre satellite en 2028. Mais pour que ce plan tienne, SpaceX doit encore réussir une manœuvre qui n’a jamais été réalisée à cette échelle, rappelle Bloomberg.
Une station-service en orbite, et beaucoup d’inconnues
L’idée paraît simple sur le papier, elle l’est beaucoup moins dans les faits. Starship consomme tellement de carburant pour quitter la Terre qu’elle ne peut pas rejoindre la Lune d’une traite. SpaceX prévoit donc de faire décoller en premier un Starship « dépôt », une sorte de station-service vide en orbite, puis des Starship « citernes » viendront ensuite le remplir au fil de plusieurs lancements. Enfin, la fusée chargée de transporter les astronautes doit s’y amarrer pour se ravitailler avant de prendre la direction de notre satellite.
Mais combien de variantes citernes seront nécessaires ? C’est un sujet de discorde : la semaine dernière, un comité consultatif de la NASA a évoqué 22 vols. Un chiffre aussitôt contesté par Elon Musk, qui estime qu’il en faudrait entre 6 et 8. Problème, Jeremy Parsons, chef du programme Artemis, juge l’objectif du milliardaire d’« assez agressif », tout en estimant que « ce serait génial « de l’atteindre.
Cette approximation ne date pas d’hier. En 2023, un responsable de la NASA évoquait un chiffre » dans la haute dizaine », tandis qu’un cadre de SpaceX avançait « une dizaine environ » un an plus tard. À un an de la mission Artemis III, ce mystère ne semble toujours pas résolu.
Un calendrier qui ne laisse aucune marge
Plusieurs inconnues expliquent cet écart, à commencer par la capacité réelle de Starship. Elon Musk promet que la V3, celle qui est actuellement en phase de test, pourra emporter plus de 100 tonnes en orbite, mais ce n’est pas avéré pour le moment. De même, le carburant, conservé à très basse température, s’évapore en partie pendant le transfert comme pendant le stockage, ce qui pourrait obliger à lancer des citernes en plus.
La première démonstration de transfert de carburant entre deux Starship est visée début 2027, alors que la mégafusée vient simplement d’atteindre l’orbite pour la première fois. Cet essai devrait enfin donner un ordre de grandeur, encore faut-il qu’il soit tenu à temps. Car Blue Origin se tient en embuscade : son atterrisseur se passe de ravitaillement en orbite.

articles.title: Krafton-backed Ludo Robotics releases robot intelligence model designed around human intent - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Krafton-backed Ludo Robotics releases robot intelligence model designed around human intent
Ludo Robotics Inc., a subsidiary of major South Korean video game publisher Krafton Inc., today debuted Ludi 0.2, a robotics artificial intelligence system built to understand people and interact with them in the physical world.
Headquartered in Palo Alto, Ludo spun out of Krafton, a company that primarily publishes video games and is best known for the ultra-popular “PUBG: Battlegrounds.” Ludo also has a research and development lab in Seoul where it combines the efforts of researchers and engineers across robotics, machine learning and AI.
Krafton Chief Executive CH Kim also helms Ludo as CEO, with Krafton’s Chief AI Officer Kangwook Lee serving as its chief technology officer.
Why did a video game company form and back an AI robotics company? Krafton said it believes AI makes games more responsive and replayable. It also has strong roots in simulation, interaction and real-time systems, which have immediate applications in the bridge between the digital and physical, where the interaction between humans and robots lives.
“Robots are becoming increasingly capable of performing physical tasks, but understanding and responding to people remains a major challenge,” said Lee. “Ludi 0.2 represents another step toward our goal of bringing conversation, reasoning and physical action together so robots can better understand human intent, respond to feedback and adapt as situations change.”
The company introduced the first version of Ludi 0.1 in August 2026. It combines a vision-language model for reasoning and dialogue with specialized navigation and manipulation capabilities. Today’s next-generation model has advanced its capabilities, forming more natural human-robot interaction, including social intelligence, memory and reasoning, tool coordination, gesture interpretation, and physical movement.
The company said it’s working toward a final version of Ludi that will integrate perception, dialogue and physical action.
The objective is to integrate communication, reasoning and physical action into one “brain.” The model would watch what’s happening, listen to commands and speech, interpret those commands alongside human gestures and physical movements and reason about the environment. This would happen in real time, coordinating similarly to how another human decides on actions based on another person’s actions in their workspace.
This is the “Holy Grail” of physical AI, where intelligent robots can perform actions not just in industrial environments and warehouses, but also retail and domestic spaces such as restaurants, living rooms and kitchens.
Krafton said much of its work includes proprietary foundation models and co-playable characters developed in collaboration with Nvidia Corp., AI teammates designed to understand players in real time. Ludo builds on this foundation to develop the same kind of intelligence into real-world robots.
Startups are bringing the physical world to robots so they can see objects and grab and move them with increasing capability. Interpreting human intent and responding to social cues from people around the robot, however, remains elusive. Simulation makes it easy for physical AI to prepare robots to work with objects and around humans, but it doesn’t always prepare them to model human behavior.

articles.title: EA Cancelled Mass Effect To Fund Star Wars: Battlefront 3
articles.text:
Friday, October 30th 2026
EA Cancelled Mass Effect To Fund Star Wars: Battlefront 3
Not long after the news broke that EA was giving Mass Effect and BioWare the axe, it was revealed that LucasFilm was looking for a development partner for its next Star Wars: Battlefront game, ostensibly Battlefront 3. In that rumor, it was claimed that LucasFilm was considering either Sony's Bungie or EA's DICE for the project. Now, it appears as though EA move to shut down BioWare and cancel Mass Effect was part of a bet on Star Wars: Battlefront 3, according to a new report from Bloomberg's Jason Schreier. 
The report claims that, following EA's acquisition by the PIF group, which has already resulted in multiple rounds of layoffs, the executives at the gaming giant evaluated potential upcoming game projects and decided that Star Wars was the safer bet, with both Mass Effect and Battlefront 3 expected to cost hundreds of millions of dollars to produce. Part of the motivation for picking Star Wars over Mass Effect also appears to have been EA's historic preference for and experience with shooters, like Battlefield 6.The report also cites poor commercial performance of BioWare's Dragon Age: The Veilguard, which is described as "a last chance" for the studio. Mass Effect: Andromeda also had a messy launch and poor sales figures, and, along with the monumental Anthem disaster, added fuel to EA's cost-cutting decisions.
Source:
				Bloomberg			
	
	
	
		
	
		
8 Comments on EA Cancelled Mass Effect To Fund Star Wars: Battlefront 3
As well, given the leaked details of "ME5" following BioWare's closure showed it was just entering the concept phase with just a showcase teaser for the upper heads or investors, it wouldn't be any loss to cancel the project outright.Glad to see that even EA saw there was no saving BioWare. They would be much better off making some money back just licensing out ME and DA to other studios and letting others do the work of making a game that would actually sell.
Heck, at this point, with nothing left to lose, they could even go for the low effort Collabs with gatcha games, Fortnite, or even with competing games just to include characters or costumes inspired by DA1-3 or ME1-3. Crimson Desert and Black Desert Online could easily fit the DA aesthetic, maybe work with Sandfall Interactive on a mini-expansion into the Painting of Dragon Age and rewarding DA-themed gear and costumes. Or heck, paid costumes/skins in their Battlefield and Battlefront games. It'd be certainly better than leaving both ME and DA for dead, and EA does need the money as well.
Now ME has a bit more presence as a brand and its merch was still selling well, so I could see that farmed out.
Also looking back, it's humorous how DA2 was made because the devs at the time claimed DA1 was too stressful to make again, hence narrowing the focus and "telling a more personal story", but after the players revolted, the devs figured out how to make Inquisition closer to DA1 and recovered enough player good will to start on a DA4, which ended how it ended. The series really did suffer a rollercoaster of development and player emotion, ending with a crash and potentially permanent end. DA1 really was a lightning in a bottle moment that BioWare never recaptured.
Sigh. I pity the devs that have to work on this shitstain. I mean, you have to somehow figure out something to get players connected ALL OVER AGAIN. Forget building on foundations. New community. New sale. New everything. Its like a new school class every year except the class is the entire world, and they DO know what you taught them last year.
Insanity to think this can keep working out well, but apparently, it somehow does.
It also doesn't dawn on any of these bean counters that WoW, a single game with a string of expansions, has been and remains one of the most player-connected service games in the (western) gaming world. 10-15 $ of sub money every month from a dozen or two million players. Just like that; keep the servers running and add a boss or two every time. Over several decades now. If any company has gained trust in that sense.... and a dedicated customer base. How hard is it to just sell an expansion to that existing experience. I don't get it. Build on what you had. Make it insanely awesome. But no... we get the tutorial every single fucking goddamn time, and some 'easter eggs' to remind you that devs know you already played sixteen earlier installments and its Yet Again The Same Shit But Different.
There could just be a Battlefront update that they market as much as a new game, and I reckon players would be a lot happier. Just spoonfeed like they were used to getting it... There are countless examples of games that do this perfectly fine for many years.
Unironically, Mass Effect 1-3, despite 'starting over' with your progression 3 times, did have an overarching story. Star Wars, the trilogy... need I say more. They already know this shit works and gets people locked in... but nope. Just keep sticking numbers behind every yearly reskin and keep wondering why player attachment remains low - its like they want to slowly erode the faith people have in live service games they actually make buck on. Ubisoft is another such champion at this, and boy, are they doing well lately!
Destiny 1 for example, needed Destiny 2 because D1's engine just didn't have the capability for expansion and growth, and D2's engine did. However, they also chose to reset everything because it was too much tech debt to port over existing equipment and weapons based on save files.
You're right that some games like CoD and Battlefield (and Battlefront) should just be a live-service game that keeps getting updated as old content is brought up to standard or replaced just like classical MMOs, or even online games like Destiny (which also sees a regular change to the meta and content), Fortnite, or Overwatch/Marvel Rivals. Charge a DLC cost of like 40 USD, and it'd still sell. Moreso if new stuff is locked to the DLC leaving players with only the older content (again, pulling from Destiny's expansions) that gradually thins out on players because more and more bought the new DLC and moved to the new game modes or newer maps/guns. Then add the Battle Pass, Seasonal Content for Halloween, St. Patrick's, Valentine's, Winter Holidays, etc, and limited time events to keep player paying.
As well, some games are now able to outright update the game engine by basically deleting and redownloading the game, so there's even less need for a sequel just for a minor or major engine update.

L'innovation peut-elle se nicher dans la réinterprétation ? Ce qui apparaît comme un sujet de bac de philo trouvera peut-être une réponse après notre test du Dyson V8 Cyclone, la vision 2025 d'un aspirateur-balai sorti en 2016.

articles.title: Geekom's Air12 Lite is the cheap mini PC I’d set up for browsing and email
articles.text:
The Geekom Air12 Lite is the kind of tiny, low-cost PC I’d set up for basic browsing and email — and it’s $269 at Best Buy
A Windows 11 Pro mini PC built for day-to-day tasks
When it comes to our testing, Geekom has a strong track record in mini PCs. The range runs from high-performance machines for content creation and heavy workloads to compact machines built for general office duty, browsing, streaming, and other undemanding tasks.
The Geekom Air12 Lite, currently $269 (was $599) at Best Buy, falls into the latter camp. If you need a small, cheap PC for a kitchen counter, a kid’s homework desk, or a living room TV, the Air12 Lite covers the basics without taking up any space.
• Best for: anyone who needs a simple, compact computer for web browsing, email, documents, and streaming video.
• Why we like it: a tiny, quiet design, a quad-core Intel N95 processor that handles everyday tasks, a 256GB SSD, and Windows 11 Pro preinstalled.
• What you need to know: The Intel N95 is a low-power chip that’s built for browsing, email, office documents, and streaming, but it will feel sluggish with lots of tabs open or more demanding software.
A compact mini PC with a quad-core, four-thread Intel Processor N95 boosting to 3.4GHz, integrated Intel UHD graphics, 8GB of DDR4 memory, a 256GB SSD, and Windows 11 Pro. Sold and shipped by Geekom through Best Buy’s marketplace.
Why we recommend it
Geekom has built a solid reputation for well-made mini PCs, and the Air12 Lite is its entry-level model, designed for light everyday tasks rather than heavy workloads. We haven’t tested it ourselves, so this pick rests on Geekom’s track record and the specs. We have, however, tested the improved Air12, which features DDR5 RAM and Wi-Fi 6 connectivity. We scored that machine 4 stars in our review, and for general office tasks, expect performance to be about the same.
Price Context & Historical Value
Ignore the $599 comparison price, since that’s far more than an N95 mini PC with 8GB of RAM has ever been worth, and budget machines with this chip have typically sold for well under $300. Rising memory prices have pushed up the cost of mini PCs this year, so $269 is a reasonable price today rather than a steal. Buy it if you need a basic PC now, but don’t expect much more than browsing and email from it.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the Geekom Air12 Lite if... you need an inexpensive, compact PC for browsing, email, documents, and streaming, you want Windows 11 Pro preinstalled, or you’re setting up a simple machine for a family member.
❌ Skip the Geekom Air12 Lite if... you plan to multitask heavily or run demanding apps, since 8GB of RAM and the N95 chip will feel limited; you want to play games; or you’d rather spend a bit more for a mini PC with a faster processor.
