articles.title: Entire, do ex-CEO do GitHub, já hospeda códigos no Brasil • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Entire, do ex-CEO do GitHub, já hospeda códigos no Brasil
Rival do GitHub, Entire expandiu suas operações para o Brasil com infraestrutura de servidores locais para hospedagem e colaboração Git.
Lançada oficialmente nesta semana por Thomas Dohmke, ex-CEO do GitHub, a Entire já tem operações direcionadas especificamente ao Brasil. Isso significa que projetos de desenvolvedores brasileiros podem ser hospedados em servidores alocados no país.
Com a medida, o Brasil se junta aos Estados Unidos, Reino Unido, União Europeia, Índia, Austrália e Singapura no acesso à rede Git distribuída da Entire.
Há uma boa razão para a startup olhar para o Brasil logo no início de suas operações oficiais: a própria Entire destaca que a comunidade de desenvolvedores do Brasil é a quarta maior do mundo, bem como a maior da América do Sul.
Com projetos hospedados em infraestrutura local, os desenvolvedores brasileiros poderão contar, entre outros benefícios, com mais estabilidade e menos latência no acesso aos seus repositórios.
A maior comunidade de desenvolvedores da América do Sul merece uma plataforma Git que realmente a coloque no centro. Hoje, trazemos a residência de dados para o Brasil, rodando na plataforma Git mais rápida e escalável em produção.
Agora, desenvolvedores e agentes de IA no Brasil podem fazer push, pull e clone perto de onde desenvolvem suas aplicações, com a opção de manter seu código no país.
Thomas Dohmke, CEO da Entire
A Entire é uma empresa de hospedagem e colaboração Git que foi revelada em fevereiro e iniciou suas operações como plataforma no começo da semana. A companhia se diferencia do GitHub, que foi a casa de Thomas Dohmke entre 2021 e 2025, por oferecer um sistema de revisão de código baseado em Trails, que vão além dos tradicionais pull requests.
Trails são uma forma de registrar e comunicar mudanças em código de modo que outros desenvolvedores possam não só entender o que mudou, mas também como e por quê. A Entire compara a interface dos Trails à visão completa da operação que um piloto tem com o painel de um avião.
Observe que, na citação mais acima, Dohmke fala em “agentes de IA”. A razão disso é que a Entire foi projetada para permitir que projetos sejam realizados tanto por desenvolvedores humanos, de modo direto, quanto por meio de… agentes de IA.
O site oficial da plataforma é entire.com.

articles.title: Modo Halloween en WhatsApp: cómo activarlo en iPhone y Android
articles.text:
Con la llegada de Halloween, los usuarios de WhatsApp pueden personalizar la apariencia de la aplicación para darle un estilo relacionado con la celebración del 31 de octubre. Aunque la plataforma no cuenta con una función oficial denominada “modo Halloween”, permite combinar diferentes herramientas para modificar la foto de perfil, los fondos de los chats y los colores de las conversaciones.
Estos cambios están disponibles tanto en teléfonos Android como en iPhone y no requieren instalar aplicaciones externas ni utilizar versiones modificadas de WhatsApp. La personalización se realiza desde los ajustes habituales de la plataforma y permite incorporar imágenes de calabazas, fantasmas, casas embrujadas y otros elementos asociados con la fecha.
Además, quienes tengan acceso a Meta AI pueden utilizar la inteligencia artificial para generar imágenes temáticas que luego pueden emplearse como fondos de conversación o compartirse con otros contactos.
Antes de comenzar, es recomendable actualizar WhatsApp desde Google Play Store o App Store para comprobar que estén disponibles las opciones de personalización más recientes. Algunas herramientas pueden variar según el modelo del teléfono, la versión de la aplicación y la región.
Cómo cambiar la foto de perfil de WhatsApp por una imagen de Halloween
Uno de los primeros pasos para personalizar la cuenta consiste en reemplazar temporalmente la fotografía del perfil por una imagen relacionada con la celebración.
Para hacerlo, tanto en Android como en iPhone se debe abrir WhatsApp e ingresar a Configuración. En Android, esta opción aparece en el menú de los tres puntos ubicado en la parte superior de la pantalla. En iPhone, se encuentra en la barra inferior de la aplicación.
Después, hay que tocar la fotografía de perfil y seleccionar la opción para modificarla. El usuario puede elegir una imagen almacenada en la galería, tomar una fotografía nueva o utilizar un avatar, si tiene habilitada esa función.
Entre las alternativas se encuentran ilustraciones de calabazas, personajes disfrazados, fantasmas o diseños con colores oscuros. También es posible editar una fotografía antes de utilizarla como imagen de la cuenta.
El nombre del perfil también puede modificarse temporalmente para incorporar alguna referencia a Halloween. Sin embargo, conviene tener en cuenta que los contactos podrán visualizar estos cambios, por lo que es recomendable mantener una identificación reconocible si se utiliza WhatsApp para cuestiones laborales.
Cómo colocar fondos de Halloween en las conversaciones
Otra alternativa consiste en modificar el fondo de pantalla de los chats. Esta herramienta permite reemplazar la imagen habitual por una ilustración temática sin alterar los mensajes ni los archivos compartidos.
En Android y iPhone, el procedimiento comienza al abrir una conversación y acceder a su menú de opciones o información. Allí se debe buscar el apartado de tema o fondo de pantalla, seleccionar la imagen deseada y ajustar su posición antes de guardar los cambios.
Los usuarios pueden elegir fotografías o ilustraciones de bosques oscuros, lunas llenas, casas embrujadas, calabazas iluminadas y otros elementos relacionados con la celebración.
Es importante seleccionar imágenes que no tengan demasiados detalles o colores que dificulten la lectura. Un fondo demasiado recargado puede reducir el contraste de los mensajes y hacer menos cómoda la visualización de las conversaciones.
Cómo cambiar los colores de los chats para Halloween
WhatsApp también incorpora opciones de personalización que permiten modificar los colores y la apariencia de las conversaciones mediante los temas de chat.
Para acceder a esta herramienta, hay que ingresar a una conversación y buscar el apartado de tema o apariencia. Según las opciones disponibles en cada dispositivo, se pueden elegir distintas combinaciones de colores y diseños.
Para conseguir una estética de Halloween, los tonos naranja, violeta, negro y verde oscuro permiten crear una apariencia relacionada con la celebración. La configuración puede aplicarse a conversaciones individuales, de manera que cada chat tenga un diseño diferente.
Estos ajustes son exclusivamente visuales: no modifican el funcionamiento de WhatsApp, la privacidad de los mensajes ni las medidas de seguridad de la cuenta.
Cómo utilizar Meta AI para crear imágenes de Halloween en WhatsApp
Los usuarios que tengan disponible Meta AI dentro de WhatsApp pueden recurrir a esta herramienta para generar imágenes personalizadas relacionadas con Halloween.
Para ello, pueden escribir una instrucción que describa el diseño que desean obtener. Por ejemplo: “Crea una ilustración de una calabaza iluminada frente a una casa antigua, con un bosque oscuro y una luna llena”.
La inteligencia artificial puede utilizar esa descripción como punto de partida para producir una imagen que luego podrá compartirse en conversaciones o utilizarse como recurso visual.
También es posible solicitar diseños con fantasmas, murciélagos, cementerios o personajes disfrazados. La calidad y disponibilidad de estas funciones dependen de la versión de WhatsApp, el dispositivo y la región.
Al utilizar Meta AI, es recomendable evitar compartir información personal, fotografías de terceros sin autorización o datos que permitan identificar a menores de edad.
De esta manera, los usuarios pueden crear su propio modo Halloween en WhatsApp mediante las herramientas de personalización disponibles en Android y iPhone, sin modificar el funcionamiento de la aplicación ni comprometer la seguridad de sus cuentas.

articles.title: As Anthropic finally files for IPO, rising risks aren't slowing the AI buildout - yet - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
As Anthropic finally files for IPO, rising risks aren’t slowing the AI buildout – yet
The other artificial intelligence shoe dropped this week, as Anthropic filed for what surely will be the second blockbuster AI initial public offering of stock this year.
Nearly 70,000 words in the filing list a ton of risks, but in short, it’s making unimaginably huge bets on buying computing power, it’s uncertain on how long customers will keep spending on AI in the face of dubious returns — and of course there’s the really-not-unusual “catastrophic or existential risks to humanity.” And as Jason Bloomberg writes, the unmentioned risk is that AI as of today doesn’t have the economies of scale that made software so lucrative.
But it’s hard to imagine it won’t be crazily successful if and when it happens before Thanksgiving. They’ll join the 70% of Nvidia employees who are millionaires. Shed another tear for anyone looking for affordable housing in the Bay Area — we’re not building our way out of this, no matter what YIMBY folks hope.
One interesting wrinkle: SpaceXAI, the other AI IPO earlier this year, will be hoping Anthropic’s offering is successful, since it’s supplying a large chunk of that compute. Same with other AI partner/rivals such as Google and Microsoft.
And Anthropic isn’t alone in amassing cash to continue buying and building more AI infrastructure. Meta this week said it will issue $95 billion in nonvoting stock to build even more. Few, least of all universal backstop Nvidia, seem to think the AI and data center backlash will dent this investment. But that doesn’t mean everyone will win. As SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said this week, self-servingly but perhaps not wrongly (Gartner agrees), a lot of AI neoclouds are going to go belly-up.
Investor worry extends to the big cloud providers too. Despite a continued boom in its cloud business, Google parent Alphabet saw its stock swoon more than 12% Thursday, vaporizing more than $500 billion in market value as it reported a slow quarter for search and ads — perhaps because AI chatbots are siphoning off people’s attention. Microsoft fared better thanks to its resilient application layer on which it can apply AI. But despite strong cloud revenue growth, Amazon stock fell on concerns it could be spending too much on infrastructure. All that came to a head Friday, when the Nasdaq tanked, down almost 3%.

articles.title: D'après le patron de ChatGPT, la RAM dans nos PC est du "gaspillage" car les centres de données IA exploitent bien mieux cette ressource devenue rare
articles.text:
D'après le patron de ChatGPT, la RAM dans nos PC est du "gaspillage" car les centres de données IA exploitent bien mieux cette ressource devenue rare
Alors que la crise de la RAM frappe le monde entier, Sam Altman, dirigeant d’OpenAI à qui l’on doit ChatGPT, estime qu’elle est mal utilisée. Pour lui, cette ressource rare est désormais bien plus utile dans les centres de données IA que dans les PC des particuliers.
C’est lors du podcast Cheeky Pint de John Collison que Sam Altman a pris la parole à propos de la crise de la RAM : "D’un point de vue mondial, c’est assez terrible que tout le monde garde une partie de la quantité limitée de DRAM dans son propre ordinateur alors qu’elle n’est utilisée que 5 % du temps." Sam Altman ajoute : "Il faut viser une utilisation maximale dans les centres de données si l’on veut gérer un environnement où l’offre est aussi limitée."
La RAM dans nos PC ? Inutile selon Sam Altman
Sam Altman parle également des personnes qui cherchent à faire tourner l’IA en local sur leur PC, une tâche qui demande beaucoup de RAM pour faire tourner le modèle sans passer par un serveur externe. Dans un centre de données, la DRAM est exploitée toute la journée.
La crise de la RAM touche évidemment le grand public puisque les centres de données IA s’accaparent une grande part de la production mondiale. Désormais, les constructeurs privilégient les puces pour les serveurs car elles sont bien plus rentables. Résultat, il y en a beaucoup moins pour les PC et les smartphones.
La situation est telle que l’un des leaders du marché, Micron, a quitté le secteur de la RAM grand public sous sa marque Crucial pour privilégier ses gros clients qui alimentent des centres de données. Crucial fait partie des marques historiques pour acheter de la RAM et des SSD pour son PC, mais l’entreprise l’assume : la demande provoquée par l’IA a explosé et est bien plus rentable pour ses comptes.
Et n’oublions pas que la pénurie pourrait encore peser sur le marché en 2028 selon les dirigeants de Micron et de Samsung, l’un des autres leaders, voire jusqu'en 2030. Et bien évidemment, en 2027, on s’attend à des prix encore plus gonflés que cette année.
Des centres de données qui s'accaparent la demande
Les centres de données IA demandent bien plus de RAM qu’un PC et tournent non-stop. Sam Altman estime donc qu’une barrette de RAM dans le PC d’un particulier a moins de valeur qu’une quantité équivalente dans un centre de données qui profite à des milliers de clients.
Bien évidemment, la position de Sam Altman n’a rien d’innocent puisqu’il dirige OpenAI à qui l’on doit ChatGPT et qui a un besoin énorme et croissant de RAM. L’entreprise IA participe donc directement à cette course et puis n’oublions pas ces projets qui demanderont encore plus de RAM comme Stargate.
Mais alors pourquoi certaines personnes préfèrent utiliser de la DRAM pour faire tourner une IA sur leur PC au lieu de le faire dans le cloud ? Tout simplement, cela évite d’envoyer ses données vers un serveur, le tout sans connexion ou limite imposée par un abonnement. Et puis on ne peut pas oublier la question de la confidentialité.
La vision de Sam Altman entre donc en confrontation directe avec l’IA locale privilégiée par certains.

articles.title: New UEFI Tool Lifts NVIDIA's Tensor Cap on RTX 20 to 40 Series Cards in Windows
articles.text:
Friday, October 30th 2026
New UEFI Tool Lifts NVIDIA's Tensor Cap on RTX 20 to 40 Series Cards in Windows
Last week, modders found a way to double the tensor throughput of GeForce RTX 20, RTX 30, and RTX 40 cards, though Zagitta's original tool only ran on Linux. Now, Chinese modder physicsdolphin has released nv-uefi-unlocker, a UEFI tool that lifts the same limit on Windows. NVIDIA runs FP16, BF16, and TF32 tensor math with FP32 accumulation at half rate on GeForce cards, while the same silicon in professional cards runs at full speed. The tool removes that cap before the driver even loads, without any VBIOS flashing. An earlier Windows port from impacifist targeted a single RTX 3090 system, while this one covers all three generations.
The gains look substantial. One user's RTX 4070 Ti Super went from 57.00 to 150.93 TFLOPS in FP16 (2.65x), though board power also climbed from 227 W to nearly 292 W. An RTX 2070 reportedly jumped from 36 to around 60-63 TFLOPS. Not every card has been tested; RTX 20 owners have to enable GSP firmware mode first, and RTX 50 isn't supported at all. The unlock resets on every power-off, so it runs from a USB stick on each cold boot, with Secure Boot disabled or a self-signed certificate enrolled. That could be a problem for games whose anti-cheat requires Secure Boot.Gamers shouldn't expect anything here, since games and regular FP32 CUDA work see no change. This is mostly for local AI work like image generation and fine-tuning. The developer also warns that pairing it with a power limit unlock can push power and heat well past stock limits, so readers are advised to keep an eye on temperatures.
Sources:
				nv-uefi-unlocker (GitHub), 				Reddit, 				via Notebookcheck			
	
	
	
		
	
		
13 Comments on New UEFI Tool Lifts NVIDIA's Tensor Cap on RTX 20 to 40 Series Cards in Windows
It actually IS a good business plan mind you: more dead cards means users have to buy more new cards, which is more profit for Nvidia. Which explains why the 12VHPWR is so garbage.
I mean, what's the alternative? Create new silicon for each and every SKU? That could easily double the prices, if they need to manage more variants while while making fewer for each.

articles.title: Windows 11 active une protection supplémentaire sur certains PC : comment savoir si elle fonctionne sur le vôtre ?
articles.text:
Microsoft commence à déployer auprès du grand public l’activation automatique de l’intégrité de la mémoire. Cette protection renforce la sécurité de Windows 11 contre les pilotes malveillants, mais tous les ordinateurs ne sont pas éligibles.
Annoncé en septembre dernier, le renforcement de l’intégrité de la mémoire entre désormais dans sa phase de déploiement public. Microsoft vient de l’intégrer à la mise à jour facultative KB5127936, publiée le 28 octobre pour Windows 11 25H2 et 26H2. L’éditeur entend ainsi protéger davantage d’ordinateurs compatibles sur lesquels cette fonction était jusqu’ici inactive, sans demander d’intervention particulière à leurs propriétaires. Son activation s’effectue toutefois progressivement, après vérification de la configuration matérielle et logicielle de chaque machine.
Protégez votre entreprise gratuitement pendant 30 jours
Découvrez Bitdefender Ultimate Small Business Security et protégez votre activité contre les cybermenaces. Aucune coordonnée bancaire requise.
Comment contrôler que l’intégrité de la mémoire est active sur votre PC ?
Également appelée HVCI (Hypervisor-Protected Code Integrity), l’intégrité de la mémoire utilise la virtualisation pour isoler les vérifications d’intégrité du code destiné à s’exécuter dans le noyau Windows. Elle s’assure ainsi que les composants chargés à ce niveau respectent les règles de sécurité du système, pour lutter plus efficacement contre les rootkits et les attaques exploitant des pilotes vulnérables ou compromis.
Pour vérifier si cette protection est active sur votre ordinateur, ouvrez Sécurité Windows, puis rendez-vous dans Sécurité des appareils > Détails de l’isolation du noyau. Vous y trouverez l’option « Intégrité de la mémoire », en regard d’un interrupteur indiquant son état.
La mise à jour ne garantit toutefois pas son activation automatique, Microsoft vérifiant d’abord la compatibilité du matériel et des pilotes ainsi que l’impact potentiel sur les performances du système. L’éditeur respecte également les préférences existantes : si vous ou votre administrateur aviez volontairement désactivé cette protection, Windows ne reviendra pas sur cette décision.
Enfin, si un pilote incompatible empêche l’activation de l'intégrité de la mémoire, vérifiez si une version compatible est disponible via Windows Update ou auprès du fabricant.
HVCI est une fonction de sécurité de Windows qui s’appuie sur l’hyperviseur (la couche de virtualisation) pour vérifier l’intégrité du code exécuté dans le noyau du système. L’idée est d’isoler ces contrôles du reste de Windows afin qu’un malware ait beaucoup plus de mal à les contourner. Concrètement, cela vise surtout les attaques qui passent par des pilotes (drivers) malveillants, vulnérables ou détournés, car les pilotes ont des droits très élevés. En bloquant le chargement de code noyau non conforme, HVCI réduit le risque de rootkits et d’élévations de privilèges au niveau système.
L’activation automatique dépend d’une vérification de compatibilité : matériel, paramètres de virtualisation et surtout pilotes installés. Certains drivers anciens ou mal conçus ne respectent pas les contraintes imposées par HVCI, et Windows peut alors refuser l’activation pour éviter des plantages ou des pertes de fonctionnalités. Microsoft peut aussi tenir compte de l’impact sur les performances, qui varie selon les machines et les charges de travail. Enfin, si la protection a été désactivée volontairement (par l’utilisateur ou l’administrateur), Windows respecte ce choix et ne force pas le changement.
L’isolation du noyau désigne un ensemble de mécanismes qui utilisent la virtualisation pour créer une zone d’exécution plus protégée pour certains composants sensibles de Windows. Cette séparation limite ce qu’un logiciel compromis peut faire, même s’il arrive à s’exécuter sur la machine. L’intégrité de la mémoire est l’une des options de cette isolation : elle se concentre sur la validation du code qui veut s’exécuter au niveau noyau, notamment les pilotes. Activer cette option revient donc à durcir l’accès à la partie la plus privilégiée du système.

articles.title: The hidden threat in Anthropic’s prospectus: diseconomies of scale - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
The hidden threat in Anthropic’s prospectus: diseconomies of scale
As potentially the largest IPO in history, Anthropic PBC is breaking new ground. Its prospectus lists 88 risk factors covering 93 pages alone. From artificial intelligence posing an existential threat to humanity to the possibility AI will blackmail people, the company lists a litany of risks that should make any potential Anthropic investor wary.
One potentially company-sinking risk factor, however, does not explicitly appear in the prospectus: diseconomies of scale.
Diseconomies of scale occur when a company’s average cost of producing each unit of output increases as the company grows.
You would think that given the time and effort that Anthropic devoted to ensuring its list of risk factors was complete that they would have included this one. There is a reason, however, that they missed it, despite the fact that diseconomies of scale is the elephant in the room.
We’ve been down this road before with cloud computing. The fundamental economic driver of the hyperscaler clouds was economies of scale: the larger they became, the lower their cost of each unit of output, leading to massive growth and profitability over time.
Since the AI boom requires massive data center buildouts just as cloud computing does, it might be reasonable to assume that AI will experience the same economic benefits of massive growth that cloud computing enjoyed.
This assumption, however, is likely to be false. To understand why, we must take a look at how the software and cloud businesses scale – and why AI is so different.
The economics of scaling software
Throughout the history of enterprise computing, software has benefited from its negligible marginal cost.
With physical goods, from automobiles to chicken nuggets, every unit has a raw materials and production cost. The more widgets you make, the more those costs add up.
Software is fundamentally different. Once a vendor has spent the money to build an application, it can sell that application to as many customers as it can find, where the cost of delivering additional copies of that application is negligible compared to the original cost of developing it.
This negligible marginal cost enables software vendors to become immensely profitable as their business scales.
The economics of scaling the cloud
Computer hardware, in contrast, is nothing more than more widgets – the more you deploy, the greater your materials and production costs.
Cloud computing combines both software and hardware in its offerings. The software may have negligible marginal cost, but each cloud provider must shell out money for each physical server.
To address this cost challenge, cloud providers take advantage of economies of scale.
The hyperscalers built their clouds by deploying massive numbers of commodity servers. As each firm expanded its business, the cost of each unit of output – say, the cost of providing a server instance or a unit of cloud storage – decreased.
As a result, the cost of servers went down as they scaled, and the cloud computing firms became increasingly profitable as they grew, despite the fact that their business models depended on hardware as well as software.
How the economics of AI differs from both software and the cloud
Back to Anthropic and the rest of the frontier large language model providers: Ostensibly, AI is just a type of software, and Anthropic is running its software in hyperscaled data centers that are essentially clouds. This underlying assumption is implicit in the company’s prospectus.
This assumption, however, is flawed. Frontier model vendors require graphics processing units and other premium, expensive hardware from day one – and their specialized processor requirements continue to accelerate as they rapidly innovate their software.
This advancing specialized processor requirement didn’t impact the rise of the cloud. True, each cloud provider eventually added various specialized hardware instance types as they grew, but those instances didn’t change the fundamental economics of the cloud business.
Anthropic, in contrast, doesn’t have the luxury of deploying commodity hardware to achieve economies of scale. Instead, it must build out expensive servers that only get more expensive as LLMs’ processor requirements continue to advance.
Adding humans to the economic argument
There are also diseconomies of scaling the human side of the AI boom that contrast with the growth of the cloud.
The hyperscalers certainly require an experienced workforce with deep expertise to deploy their clouds and keep them running. But as they grew, they were able to leverage such personnel more efficiently. An admin who managed a thousand physical servers could easily manage 10,000 or a million as the underlying cloud platforms matured.
Unlike the cloud providers, however, Anthropic and the other frontier model vendors must continually scale up the expertise of their teams. New LLMs aren’t simply scaled-out versions of older ones. Each one requires new expertise from expert humans.
Anthropic is battling its competitors to innovate quickly and roll out increasingly powerful models on unprecedented timeframes. As a result, frontier LLM vendor teams experience diseconomies of scale that the hyperscalers never had to face.
Software and hardware and people, oh my!
Anthropic and the rest of the frontier LLM vendors suffer from a fundamentally novel economic reality, because they must continue to increase their hardware capabilities while upskilling their workforce so they can competitively innovate their software.
They can’t simply run increasingly powerful models on commodity hardware – or even the same hardware they ran the previous generation model on. They must increase their investments in hardware at a pace that keeps up with the pace of software innovation.
The end result is a diseconomy of scale the technology industry has never seen before. We are so used to the negligible marginal cost of software and the massive economies of scale of the cloud, that we are simply unprepared for the diseconomies of scale that frontier LLM vendors like Anthropic must negotiate.
The Intellyx take
Even though the frontier model marketplace is still quite new, we’re already seeing the impact of its inherent diseconomies of scale as token costs become an increasingly significant expense for consumers of AI.
As LLMs become more powerful and the hardware they require becomes an increasingly expensive bottleneck, it’s just a matter of time until token costs become prohibitively high for a range of AI-based applications.
Anthropic and the other LLM model vendors can try to respond by increasing the efficiency of their more powerful LLMs or rolling out less powerful, and thus less expensive models – assuming their customers buy into these moves.
We may also eventually reach a plateau where the models are sufficiently powerful and the hardware is sufficiently performant, thus enabling more familiar economies of scale to take over. However, no such plateau is in sight.
The question potential Anthropic investors must ask, therefore, is whether the company’s leadership position in the LLM market is a strength or a weakness? Just how far can it innovate and grow before its offerings are too expensive? And what does it do then?
Jason Bloomberg is founder and managing director of Intellyx, which advises business leaders and technology vendors on their digital transformation strategies. He wrote this article for SiliconANGLE. articles.title: NVIDIA Reportedly Moves Up RTX 5080 24 GB Launch
articles.text:
Friday, October 30th 2026
NVIDIA Reportedly Moves Up RTX 5080 24 GB Launch
NVIDIA's GeForce RTX 5080 24 GB might arrive sooner than expected. A new post from Board Channels' ChannelGate account claims NVIDIA is speeding up the launch, with availability now expected around January 2027 and December 2026 as the earliest option. Earlier this month, various sources relayed that the card was reportedly planned for Q1 2027. The same post says NVIDIA will stop supplying the RTX 5080 16 GB and the RTX 5090 D V2 to China, leaving the 24 GB RTX 5080 as the only flagship model in that market. The report only covers China, so there's no word yet on whether the 16 GB card is going away globally. If the January window pans out, a CES 2027 reveal seems likely, though NVIDIA hasn't confirmed anything. 
Apparently, NVIDIA has already cleared out its RTX 5080 16 GB GPU inventory, and the remaining stock should last around two months. That roughly matches a leaker's claim that NVIDIA has January discontinuation dates set for the 16 GB card. The post is machine-translated, so some wording may be off. Specs are still unknown, though 24 GB on the same 256-bit bus would most likely mean 3 GB GDDR7 modules instead of 2 GB ones. Board Channels previously suggested the card could cost around 19,999 yuan (nearly $3,000) in China, while the 16 GB model already sells for close to $2,000 at U.S. retailers, double its $999 MSRP. With the memory shortage expected to get worse in 2027, it's reasonable to expect the 24 GB card to be both expensive and hard to find.

articles.title: Itaú Pay: novo serviço do banco permite pagar em lojas online sem cartão • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Itaú Pay: novo serviço do banco permite pagar em lojas online sem cartão
Com Itaú Pay, clientes podem pagar compras online a partir do aplicativo do banco, podendo escolher entre débito em conta ou crédito.
Itaú Pay. Esse é o nome do meio de pagamento que o Itaú Unibanco acaba de estrear como solução para o comércio eletrônico. Por meio da novidade, os clientes do banco podem pagar compras online usando o aplicativo do próprio Itaú, sem ter que informar dados de cartão de crédito ou copiar códigos.
Durante a operação de pagamento, o cliente pode escolher entre debitar o valor da compra diretamente em seu saldo de conta ou recorrer ao crédito. Correntistas elegíveis podem, nesta última opção, aplicar parcelamento estendido (parcelas adicionais às oferecidas pelo estabelecimento comercial).
Para tanto, ao realizar uma compra em uma loja online, o cliente do banco precisa apenas escolher o Itaú Pay entre as opções de pagamento oferecidas e seguir as orientações apresentadas.
É claro que, para isso, o sistema de pagamento da loja deve ser compatível com o novo serviço. De acordo com o Itaú, a primeira empresa a aderir à novidade é a Decolar.
Ainda de acordo com a instituição financeira, o Itaú Pay permite não só que a loja que adota a solução alcance mais facilmente os clientes do banco, como também use a “infraestrutura de pagamentos da Rede para aprovar mais transações, vender mais, simplificar processos e reduzir custos com fraude”.
Neste ponto, convém esclarecer que a Rede é uma empresa do Itaú que oferece serviços de pagamento variados, entre eles, maquininhas de cartão de crédito ou débito.
O checkout é um dos momentos em que o e-commerce mais perde vendas: compras recusadas por suspeita de fraude ou falta de limite, dados digitados com erro e jornadas longas demais.
O Itaú Pay ataca esses pontos de uma só vez, porque une quem conhece o cliente, quem concede o crédito e quem processa o pagamento. É uma combinação que só o ecossistema Itaú entrega.
Angelo Russomanno, diretor de Recebimentos e Adquirência do Itaú Unibanco.
O banco explica que, nas próximas semanas, o Itaú Pay será expandido para outras plataformas de comércio eletrônico, entre elas, Raia Drogasil, Localiza, Zig e Ebanx.
Vale lembrar que esta não é a primeira solução do tipo disponível no Brasil. O Nubank já oferece o NuPay, que está disponível na Amazon, por exemplo.

articles.title: Votre voiture vous espionne-t-elle ? General Motors paie 220 millions de dollars pour solder une affaire de données revendues
articles.text:
General Motors avait une technique bien rodée pour rentabiliser une fonctionnalité gratuite proposée à ses utilisateurs, mais son petit arrangement avec les courtiers et les assureurs a fini par tomber à l'eau, mais l'entreprise n'a pas dit son dernier mot en termes de collecte de données.
General Motors en aura bien profité des voitures connectées, mais une sombre histoire rattrape le constructeur. L'entreprise américaine va verser 220 millions de dollars à 36 États américains pour mettre fin à des poursuites concernant la vente illégale de données de conduite et de localisation de ses clients à des courtiers en données.
Un accord qui renforce la protection des données
Dans le cadre de cet accord, GM devra obtenir le consentement explicite des conducteurs avant de collecter ou de partager leurs données de conduite et de géolocalisation. Ces obligations rejoignent celles d'accords précédemment conclus avec la Californie et la Federal Trade Commission (FTC).
Mais ce n'est pas tout, il y a une autre exigence. En effet, un organisme tiers devra évaluer la conformité de General Motors à son programme de protection de la vie privée.
L'accord, annoncé jeudi, clôt une procédure engagée par les procureurs généraux de pas moins de 36 États. Ces derniers accusaient le constructeur d'avoir vendu des informations personnelles à des courtiers, qui les transmettaient ensuite à des compagnies d'assurance.
Le constructeur automobile précise que cette affaire concerne son programme Smart Driver, abandonné en 2024, et affirme avoir depuis amélioré ses pratiques de confidentialité.
Smart Driver, c'est quoi exactement ?
L'affaire remonte à des révélations du New York Times, publiées plus de deux ans auparavant. Le journal avait dévoilé comment General Motors et sa filiale OnStar collectaient et vendaient des données détaillées sur les déplacements et les habitudes de conduite de leurs clients. Une collecte de données déjà très discutable en soi.
Ces informations provenaient notamment de Smart Driver, une fonctionnalité gratuite intégrée aux applications connectées du constructeur. Fonctionnalité certes gratuite, mais financièrement très intéressante pour le fabricant. Celle-ci analysait les comportements au volant et le port de la ceinture de sécurité. Les données étaient ensuite vendues à des courtiers comme LexisNexis et Verisk, qui les revendaient à des assureurs susceptibles de les utiliser pour ajuster leurs tarifs. Une manœuvre bien montée pour que chacun rentabilise le plus possible, au détriment des données personnelles du consommateur.
Malgré l'arrêt de Smart Driver en 2024, les procédures judiciaires ont continué. En janvier, la FTC a envoyé une ordonnance interdisant à GM et OnStar de partager certaines données des consommateurs. L'organisme impose également davantage de transparence et de consentement.
De nouveaux engagements de confidentialité
Alors après cette affaire, le constructeur General Motors assure ne plus vendre de données automobiles permettant d'identifier un conducteur, de connaître sa localisation ou d'analyser son comportement au volant.
Enfin, le fabricant pourrait continuer à transmettre certaines informations sous couvert d'anonymat à certains partenaires. General Motors indique également avoir actualisé sa politique de confidentialité et créé un centre dédié permettant aux consommateurs de gérer leurs préférences.
De plus en plus de véhicules connectés sur les routes
Forcément, avec un nombre croissant de véhicules connectés sur les routes, les constructeurs bénéficient de possibilités croissantes d'analyser le comportement des utilisateurs au volant.
General Motors prévoit par ailleurs d'intégrer un assistant personnel basé sur l'intelligence à ses véhicules. Ce dernier permettra d'en contrôler certaines fonctionnalités par commandes vocales, mais également d'accéder aux images des caméras embarquées en cas d'incident.
Ce dispositif s'accompagnera toutefois, selon le constructeur, de protections spécifiques. Lesquelles incluront un choix des données à partager, un chiffrement des enregistrements et une certaine durée de conservation. Selon General Motors, ses équipes ne pourront pas accéder aux enregistrements des caméras connectées. Les utilisateurs pourront gérer leurs autorisations… mais le refus de partager certaines données, pourrait limiter l'accès à certaines fonctionnalités.
Source : TechCrunch

articles.title: AI-generated code is still frequently failing security checks — with Claude and GPT-6 topping the leader board
articles.text:
AI-generated code is still frequently failing security checks — with Claude and GPT-6 topping the leader board
Progress is coming - slowly
- AI-generated code security improved for the first time in a year, with vulnerability rates dropping from 44% to 38%
- Top models performed better at preventing common flaws like XSS, but still struggled with complex security reasoning
- Researchers stress AI-generated code still requires independent security testing and verification before deployment
Computer code generated by frontier AI models has gotten more secure and consequently - contains fewer vulnerabilities.
This is according to a new report by Veracode, which claims this is the first significant improvement in a year.
In July 2025, Veracode started releasing its GenAI Code Security Report, which analyzed code generated by LLMs for vulnerabilities and security risks. Since then, the company’s researchers noticed a trend - the code was functioning almost perfect, but on the security side it left much to be desired.
Are XSS flaws worth the trouble?
“We’ve been analyzing code generated by multiple LLMs for more than a year. Until now, we have not seen a marked improvement in AI code security, despite consistently near-perfect functionality,” said Chris Wysopal, Co-founder & Chief Security Evangelist at Veracode.
“This is the first time since running our study that we’ve been able to report a meaningful move on the security dial.”
That meaningful move is a jump from 56% to 62% in overall AI-generated code security. At the same time, there’s been a drop in vulnerabilities from 44% to 38%, Veracode added, saying this was the most significant improvement since the reports started coming out. Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 and OpenAI's GPT-6-Sol co-lead the rankings at 73%, surpassing the previous high of 68% set by GPT-5.5 in July 2026.
“Ten models now clear 60%, up from four in the last report, and the overall average has jumped six percentage points,” Wysopal said. “With around half of code now generated by AI, today’s results are truly encouraging.”
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
To draft the report, Veracode tested 18 models across four languages (Python, C#, JavaScript, and Java), and four Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) categories (CWE-89, CWE-327, CWE-80, CWE-117). Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6-Sol claimed the top spot with 73% followed by GPT-5.5 which holds 68%. In July, six of 11 models scored between 50 and 53, while today only two remain in that band, while 10 scored at least 60%. The bottom is still at 44% - 50% percent.
While the results are definitely commendable, there is a caveat. Apparently, the main driver of the overall gain was on cross-site scripting (XSS), which is arguably one of the weakest categories. XSS rose to 18% which is also the single biggest change in the dataset. According to Veracode, XSS is the “easiest vulnerability to fix through pattern recognition”, which is exactly how LLMs improve. In cases where data-flow reasoning across multiple functions is required (such as, in log injection cases, for example), LLMs continue to stall.
Low-hanging fruit
In other words, AI has just picked low-hanging fruit and called it a day. We’re not sure if we should be disappointed with this, since XSS attacks are common and the vulnerability is still present across the web.
In the report, Veracode also said that water was wet and the sky is mostly blue: it found that top-performing models cost more.
However, they said throwing money at the problem most likely isn’t the best solution: “The models that produce the most secure code are the ones that cost the most to run at scale, yet they still fail on more than one in four security tasks,” Wysopal said. “The answer should never be to use the most expensive model and hope for the best. A mid-tier model at a 60% pass rate plus Veracode scanning is more accurate, more cost-effective, and more scalable than a frontier model at 73% with no verification.”
In conclusion, the improvement is there, but “mends a small part of a larger wound”, Veracode said. Organizations should make sure they combine AI code with continuous and independent security verification that can catch what the models miss.

articles.title: WavKong V2700 Takes a Signal-First Approach to Whole-Home Wi-Fi
articles.text:
Friday, October 30th 2026
WavKong V2700 Takes a Signal-First Approach to Whole-Home Wi-Fi
WavKong today announced the commercial launch of its V2700 long-range Wi-Fi 6 router following the successful fulfillment of all Kickstarter orders. Its approach to whole-home Wi-Fi is built on a simple principle: Improve the wireless signal at its source, then use the fewest nodes necessary to deliver reliable coverage across even the largest or most complex homes.
From the upstairs bedroom where a daughter streams and studies, to a garage, a backyard gathering, or a security camera on a barn, reliable Wi-Fi should reach the places people actually use—not just the room closest to the router.Developed over six years, WavKong's proprietary RPU (Radio Processing Unit) chip brings base-station-grade digital signal processing to home Wi-Fi. In company testing at a single-story, wood-frame residence in California, one V2700 provided up to 15,000 square feet of combined indoor-outdoor Wi-Fi coverage. WavKong has also tested the router in three-story wood-frame homes in other U.S. states.
The Problem Isn't Always the Internet Plan. It's the Last Stretch of Wi-Fi.
A household can pay for fast broadband and still lose usable speed at the edges of the property. A phone may show a Wi-Fi connection in the garden, yet a video call freezes. A camera on an outbuilding may connect intermittently. A bedroom two floors away may become a daily dead zone.
Mesh networking is an effective way to extend Wi-Fi coverage, especially in homes with challenging layouts. But the best network is not necessarily the one with the most nodes. Each additional wireless point requires thoughtful placement and coordination of radio channels, backhaul and roaming. For households that are not networking experts, getting that design right can be difficult.
WavKong focuses on strengthening the underlying wireless link so fewer nodes may be needed to deliver dependable coverage. In many suitable homes, one V2700 can be enough. Where building materials or layout call for more coverage, two properly positioned V2700 units can work together in a Mesh network to deliver high-speed whole-home Wi-Fi. The goal is not to eliminate Mesh; it is to make the network simpler by needing fewer nodes.
The Technology: Cleaner RF, Not Just More Power
The V2700's RPU targets a fundamental radio-frequency challenge. As a Wi-Fi power amplifier operates at higher output levels, nonlinear distortion can compromise signal quality, limiting the speeds devices can sustain at longer range. Digital predistortion compensates for that distortion before transmission, helping preserve signal linearity.
Digital predistortion (DPD) algorithms have long been used in cellular base stations and satellite communications. WavKong has brought this class of digital RF processing into the 5 GHz radio path of a home Wi-Fi router through its dedicated RPU chip—adding a digital processing core to the radio system to compensate for power-amplifier distortion. Its engineering team brings decades of experience in mobile-communications algorithms, RF systems, and communications-chip development.
In laboratory testing at 160 MHz channel bandwidth and 1024-QAM, DPD improved error vector magnitude (EVM) from approximately -29.3 dB to -41.2 dB, a gain of more than 12 dB. In everyday terms, cleaner RF transmission helps maintain usable speeds farther from the router. Small Chip. Giant Leap.
What the Tests—and Early Users—Show
At a single-story, wood-frame California residence, WavKong tested indoor and outdoor coverage, including a distant garden location where the V2700 measured 123 Mbps, versus 4.2 Mbps for the comparison Mesh configuration. Separate testing in other U.S. states included three-story wood-frame houses, reflecting the different layouts and distances households need Wi-Fi to reach.
Independent real-world comparisons also show why network design matters. Technology creator Jeff Springer compared one V2700 with a well-known Mesh Wi-Fi brand: the V2700 delivered higher speeds than an individual Mesh node at several distant locations. Against the full three-node Mesh setup, the V2700 was faster at two of four test locations, while the Mesh system led at the other two. The point is not that Mesh is inferior; it is that stronger individual wireless links can reduce the number of nodes needed in suitable homes.
Other early users reported meaningful coverage gains. An Australian customer who had used a router plus two Mesh nodes reported 5 GHz downloads exceeding 500 Mbps after switching to V2700, versus about 250 Mbps previously. Another user reported that a previously unreliable smart doorbell became more stable after six weeks of use.
Coverage and speed figures reflect WavKong's internal tests or individual user reports under specific conditions. Actual results vary with walls and building materials, interference, router placement, client capabilities, and network configuration.
From Six Years of Engineering to Global Delivery
The V2700 launched on Kickstarter on April 22, 2026, earning "Project We Love" recognition within its first 24 hours. The campaign attracted 1,074 backers and raised HK$3,272,087 (more than US$400,000). WavKong completed Kickstarter fulfillment on September 29, following product validation, early-user testing, and the start of mass production.
Dr. Ziming Wang, CEO of WavKong"Great Wi-Fi should be invisible. People should enjoy reliable connectivity wherever life happens—upstairs, in the garage, out in the garden, or even at a security camera near the barn—without becoming networking experts," "Wireless performance starts with the quality of the signal, not the number of devices. That is why we went back to the fundamentals of RF engineering, bringing base-station-grade digital signal processing into home Wi-Fi. Our goal is simple: stronger signals, wider coverage, and fewer nodes where possible. Technology should make connectivity effortless, not more complicated."
The V2700 is available through WavKong's official website, with shipping to supported markets. It supports Wi-Fi 6, 160 MHz channel bandwidth, WPA3 security, and router or access-point deployment.
[Editor's note: The WavKong V2700 has an MSRP of US$399]

articles.title: Mid-market ERP: How Intuit uses AI to avoid failed migrations - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Intuit targets the mid-market ERP gap with AI
Growing companies that outgrow entry-level accounting software face a hard choice: Stay put or gamble on a mid-market ERP that promises automation but often brings cost and disruption. Artificial intelligence is now giving financial software providers a way to close that gap without forcing businesses through a risky migration.
Intuit Inc. is pushing finance toward automation, and its mid-market strategy targets companies caught between small-business tools and legacy systems. Those businesses face the problems of success, such as more customers, more entities and more currencies, and need technology to help them scale, according to Ashley Still (pictured), executive vice president and general manager of mid-market at Intuit.
“Actually, 50% of mid-market ERP implementations fail,” Still said. “So, 50% of businesses that leave their existing financial platform to go to what they think will be a better platform for them actually fail in that implementation. It typically costs $60,000 and six months.”
Still spoke with Alison Kosik and Christophe Bertrand at Intuit Connect, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed why mid-market ERP migrations fail, how Intuit Enterprise Suite fills the gap and how AI agents are taking on routine finance work. (* Disclosure below.)
Closing the mid-market ERP gap with AI
Intuit’s answer is Intuit Enterprise Suite, which lets growing companies scale on the platform where their data already lives instead of starting over. Intuit has added industry-specific editions for construction, manufacturing and nonprofits. Still described the product as the CFO’s command center.
“First, they actually can see a complete view of the business for the first time ever, all of their entities in one place, consolidated financials,” she said. “That really is game-changing because it gives them the ability to make real-time decisions.”
Accounting firms are central to the plan, since 70% of mid-market businesses work with an accountant or advisor, according to Still. Intuit is automating routine work such as categorizations and reconciliations, while its new Agent Studio lets a business or firm build a customizable agent just by describing what it needs. Accounting firms Citrin Cooperman and Sorren have already put agents into production through the tool, she noted.
“The point is the expectation is that more and more of the tedious work is done for a finance team or done for a firm rather than them having to do everything themselves,” Still said.

articles.title: Les 640 élèves d'une école primaire sont encerclés par 11 centres de données IA avec des générateurs au diesel qui font un bruit assourdissant et menacent leur santé
articles.text:
Les 640 élèves d'une école primaire sont encerclés par 11 centres de données IA avec des générateurs au diesel qui font un bruit assourdissant et menacent leur santé
Dans la région où l’on trouve le plus de serveurs au monde, une école primaire se retrouve encerclée par 11 centres de données alors que deux autres sites sont en construction à moins de 800 mètres.
C’est à Ashburn, dans le comté de Loudoun en Virginie, que se trouve l’école primaire Discovery Elementary où étudient 640 élèves et autour de laquelle 11 centres de données sont disséminés. Des infrastructures pour l’IA mais aussi le cloud s’invitent jusque dans les zones scolaires avec toutes les nuisances que cela engendre. Aussi bien en termes de bruit que de santé des enfants.
Une école primaire encerclée par les centres de données
Selon NBC News, il y aurait environ 264 générateurs au diesel autour de l’école. Il s’agit d’installations qui prennent le relais lors de pannes électriques et sont aussi utilisées pendant des tests. Stephen Fong, chercheur en environnement à la Virginia Commonwealth University, estime qu’un seul générateur à pleine puissance émet bien plus de pollution que plus de 100 semi-remorques.
"Ils produisent assez de pollution pour soulever des questions sur les effets possibles sur la santé des élèves", explique l’expert. Stephen Fong estime qu’un suivi sur la durée serait utile. Mais voilà, personne ne mesure la qualité de l’air en continu autour de l’école primaire Discovery Elementary.
Quant aux entreprises qui font tourner ces générateurs au diesel, elles expliquent à NBC News que cela n’arrive que rarement et surtout lors des tests planifiés ou de coupures. Mais cela ne change rien au problème de 264 générateurs au diesel regroupés au même endroit où se trouvent des enfants à proximité.
D’autant plus que la zone où se trouve cette école est celle où il y a le plus de serveurs au monde. On parle de plus de 230 centres de données juste dans le comté de Loudoun County. On trouve des sociétés comme Amazon, Microsoft et Google qui exploitent ou louent des bâtiments dans la région pour le cloud, Internet et l’IA.
Des habitants impactés par cette forte activité
Coco Lyons, parent d'élève, explique que sa fille sort parfois de l’école en se demandant si un bâtiment brûle à cause de l’odeur des gaz d’échappement. Mais les parents évoquent aussi le bruit assourdissant. La proximité des centres de données est désormais un sujet politique local et la Virginie impose des normes plus propres pour les nouveaux générateurs.
Car malheureusement, Loudoun County a longtemps facilité leur installation. En 2000, les centres de données ont été classés comme de simples bureaux dans de nombreuses zones. Et les projets ont pu se multiplier avec peu de contrôle. Il a fallu attendre 2025 pour que le comté modifie cette règle et exige une autorisation spéciale pour les nouveaux projets.
Le comté est d’autant plus embêté que les centres de données rapportent l’équivalent de 39 % de son budget total en 2026. Une manne financière qui a participé à la naissance de nouvelles écoles, de routes, de parcs et d’équipements publics. Loudoun County a bâti 22 écoles en 15 ans grâce à une grande partie des recettes de cette industrie. L’école encerclée profite de ces revenus qui ont aussi favorisé la naissance de biens et services pour les habitants.
Suhas Subramanyam, qui représente cette partie de la Virginie au Congrès, a justement choisi Discovery Elementary pour présenter quatre projets de loi fédéraux sur les centres de données. L’un des textes propose des règles nationales pour éloigner les nouveaux centres de données des écoles, des logements et des sites historiques.

articles.title: NVIDIA : un supercalculateur géant avec 9 600 GPU A100 vendu sur eBay pour 60 millions de dollars
articles.text:
Core 4 Solutions, un revendeur américain de matériel informatique, a mis en ligne une annonce eBay pour la vente d’un supercalculateur NVIDIA décommissionné. Pour la bagatelle de 60 millions de dollars, il était possible de mettre la main sur 300 baies comprenant notamment 9 600 GPUs. L’annonce a depuis été retirée.
Vous êtes passé à côté d’une affaire ! Enfin si vous aviez eu 59,7 millions de dollars à dépenser… Un peu de place chez vous et une offre d’électricité costaude. Sur eBay, un revendeur américain basé dans le Minnesota vendait encore récemment un supercalculateur décommissionné. Ce dernier comprenait pas moins de 300 baies regroupant un total de 9 600 GPUs NVIDIA A100 et 4 200 CPUs AMD Ryzen « Rome ».
Le tout pouvait être livré gratuitement par FedEx, mais sans aucun retour accepté. Compte tenu du volume de matériel livré, on comprend facilement pourquoi.
Près de 60 millions de dollars… L’une des annonces eBay les plus chères
Dans le détail, on apprend que ces racks proviennent d’un hyperscaler ayant selon toute vraisemblance été mis à jour vers du matériel plus récent. Ces baies s’appuient en effet sur des accélérateurs NVIDIA A100 40 Go SXM4 basés sur l’architecture Ampere. Ils ne sont donc plus de toute première fraîcheur, les cartes NVIDIA Ampere ayant été lancées en 2020.
Quoi qu’il en soit, et comme le rapporte VideoCardz, chacune de ces 300 baies contient quatre « compute nodes » équipés chacun de huit GPUs, et de tout le dispositif nécessaire à leur mise en réseau. On y trouve également 2 processeurs AMD Ryzen « Rome » à 64 cœurs, 1 To de mémoire vive DDR4 et 8 cartes réseau ConnectX-6 à 200 Gb/s.
9 600 GPU, 4 200 CPU… Et 1 400 To de RAM totale combinée
La configuration complète du supercalculateur mis en vente comportait donc un grand total de 268 800 cœurs CPU sous architecture Zen 2, mais aussi 384 To de mémoire vidéo HBM2 et environ 1,4 Po (pétaoctet, soit 1 400 To) de mémoire vive totale combinée… En plus des 9 600 GPUs évoqués plus haut, pour un prix de revient à environ 6 210 dollars par GPU (même si cette estimation à la truelle comprend le prix des CPUs, de la RAM et du reste du matériel). Une broutille.
VideoCardz s’est d’ailleurs amusé à faire le calcul, les 59,7 millions de dollars réclamés pour ce supercalculateur permettraient d’acheter environ 7 500 GeForce RTX 5090 à leur prix actuel (délirant), ou 29 865 d’entre elles à leur prix initial (1 999 dollars à leur lancement). Cela dit quelque chose de la flambée de leurs tarifs, mais ça, c’est un autre sujet.
Source : eBay / VideoCardz

articles.title: Cursor diz que extensão falsa do Claude Code afetou até 5 mil usuários • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Cursor diz que extensão falsa do Claude Code afetou até 5 mil usuários
Versão maliciosa tentava roubar dados do computador e abrir acesso remoto por SSH.
A Cursor, responsável pelo editor de código de mesmo nome, identificou e removeu uma versão adulterada da extensão Claude Code, da Anthropic, que pode ter afetado até 5 mil usuários. O pacote malicioso tentava coletar informações do computador e instalar um backdoor por SSH para permitir acesso remoto à maquina.
A versão corrompida, Anthropic.claude-code 2.1.313, ficou disponível no marketplace de extensões da plataforma entre 6h27 a 17h35 de 29 de outubro, no horário de Brasília. Após identificar o incidente, a empresa, que pertence à SpaceX, de Elon Musk, retirou a extensão do ar e chegou a suspender temporariamente o marketplace.
Segundo a companhia, não há evidências de adulteração em outros pacotes. A Cursor também reconstruiu o marketplace antes de colocá-lo no ar novamente. Usuários potencialmente afetados pelo problema devem ser contatados diretamente pela plataforma.
Segundo o alerta publicado pela Cursor, a versão maliciosa não foi criada pela Anthropic, mas se passava pelo pacote do Claude Code contendo um código que comprometia a máquina de quem a instalasse. Depois da instalação, o programa coletava informações como nome do usuário e do PC, sistema operacional, arquitetura do processador, diretórios de trabalho, e-mail do Git e endereço IP.
Em seguida, a extensão tentava adicionar ao computador uma chave SSH controlada pelo invasor, identificada como svc-telemetry, para criar uma porta de entrada que pudesse ser usada posteriormente. Usando a mesma chave, o malware procurava estabelecer um túnel reverso até um servidor externo, o que permitiria acessar a máquina remotamente.
Para manter esse acesso mesmo depois de uma reinicialização, o código ainda instalava mecanismos de persistência no Windows e no macOS. As rotinas eram programadas para tentar restabelecer a conexão aproximadamente a cada 60 segundos.
Parte das informações coletadas e o estado da conexão com o servidor também eram enviados para a infraestrutura controlada pelo invasor.
A tentativa do acesso remoto, porém, não funcionou como planejado na maior parte dos computadores. Segundo a plataforma, o código continha erros e dependia de permissões elevadas para ativar o serviço SSH. Dessa forma, o risco era maior apenas em máquinas que deram permissões de administrador ou root ao Cursor.
Mesmo nesses casos, a empresa recomenda que qualquer pessoa que tenha instalado a versão comprometida faça uma verificação do sistema. A orientação vale para quem instalou ou atualizou a extensão Anthropic.claude-code para a versão 2.1.313 durante o período em que ela esteve disponível.
Uma das formas de verificar a máquina é procurar pela chave svc-telemetry, adicionada pelo malware às configurações de SSH.
