articles.title: Google quería levantar un centro de datos en Finlandia. Empezó talando 330 hectáreas y acabó bajo investigación penal
articles.text:
Cuando hablamos de los grandes centros de datos, solemos pensar en edificios repletos de servidores, sistemas de refrigeración y enormes cantidades de electricidad. Sin embargo, todo empieza bastante antes, en un terreno que debe prepararse para recibir una infraestructura de estas dimensiones. Esa primera etapa puede implicar la retirada de árboles, movimientos de tierra y modificaciones en los sistemas de drenaje. Son actuaciones que pueden formar parte de estos proyectos, pero no por ello quedan al margen de las exigencias ambientales. Y lo que sucede durante esos preparativos puede tener consecuencias mucho antes de que las instalaciones entren en funcionamiento.
En Muhos, una localidad del norte de Finlandia, esa fase previa ha colocado uno de los proyectos de Google bajo la lupa de la policía. El 29 de octubre, las autoridades finlandesas confirmaron una investigación penal por posibles infracciones de la legislación ambiental en los terrenos de un futuro centro de datos. Las actuaciones examinadas corresponden a Tuike Finland, filial de la compañía estadounidense. Según Reuters, los investigadores tratan de determinar si los trabajos realizados vulneraron la legislación sobre aguas y provocaron daños ambientales. Por ahora, hablamos de sospechas que todavía deben esclarecerse.
Lo ocurrido en Muhos va bastante más allá de marcar sobre un mapa dónde construir. En los terrenos del proyecto se han talado unas 330 hectáreas de bosque, de acuerdo con la información publicada por Yle, mientras avanzaban otras tareas de acondicionamiento del emplazamiento. Entre ellas figuran intervenciones sobre el suelo y los drenajes, que modifican las condiciones del espacio antes de levantar las instalaciones definitivas. La cuestión es que estos trabajos no solo tienen una dimensión técnica: también pueden tener implicaciones ambientales que deben evaluarse conforme a la legislación finlandesa.
De la preparación del terreno a una investigación por posibles daños ambientales
Las evaluaciones ambientales seguían pendientes cuando intervino el organismo finlandés de supervisión, conocido como LVV. El 6 de octubre, las autoridades requirieron a Tuike Finland que suspendiera los trabajos preparatorios capaces de alterar significativamente el entorno, tanto en Muhos como en otro proyecto situado en Kajaani-Otanmäki. La razón es que estos procedimientos deben permitir identificar los posibles impactos y estudiar alternativas antes de que se ejecuten determinadas actuaciones. Según Yle, Google confirmó el 14 de octubre que había suspendido los trabajos en ambos emplazamientos, aunque podía continuar con tareas de planificación, mediciones y estudios de escaso impacto.
La atención de las autoridades se concentra ahora en un elemento menos evidente que los árboles: el agua. Las zanjas de drenaje excavadas pueden alterar su circulación, y el regulador consideró insuficiente el plan presentado para controlar los efectos de lluvias intensas, el deshielo y la posible acidificación del agua asociada a la composición del suelo. Por ello, exigió a Tuike Finland un plan más detallado antes del 5 de noviembre. La policía investiga si esas actuaciones infringieron la legislación sobre aguas y provocaron daños ambientales. Según Reuters, una eventual condena podría acarrear una multa empresarial, mientras que la investigación se prolongará hasta 2027.
Google, por su parte, defiende que actuó conforme a su interpretación de la legislación finlandesa. El 13 de octubre, Antti Järvinen, responsable de la compañía en el país, pidió disculpas públicamente y afirmó que habían trabajado en colaboración con autoridades y especialistas, aunque evitó precisar qué organismos habían sido informados cuando se le preguntó por ellos. También negó que la empresa hubiera acelerado deliberadamente las talas para adelantarse a las evaluaciones ambientales. Tras conocerse la investigación penal, un portavoz aseguró a Reuters que la tecnológica cooperaría con la policía y seguiría atendiendo las exigencias de las autoridades.
El caso de Muhos se produce en medio de una apuesta económica mucho mayor que ese emplazamiento. Google anunció en septiembre una inversión de al menos 13.000 millones de euros en infraestructura digital en Finlandia para 2027 y 2028, incluidos centros de datos e instalaciones de apoyo. La compañía también presentó iniciativas relacionadas con la energía limpia. El país resulta atractivo por su clima frío y su electricidad de bajas emisiones, aunque esa expansión plantea exigencias a la red. Fingrid calcula que el consumo eléctrico nacional podría crecer hasta un 40% respecto a 2025 si se materializan todos los proyectos con acuerdos de conexión, no solo los de Google.
El calendario del futuro centro de datos tiene ahora dos incógnitas distintas. Una es administrativa: el organismo supervisor debe decidir sobre las autorizaciones necesarias para reanudar los trabajos, sin que exista todavía un plazo definido. La otra es penal: los investigadores han anunciado que informarán de sus avances en diciembre, aunque todavía deben determinar si hubo infracciones y daños ambientales. Que se resuelva una cuestión no significa automáticamente que la otra quede zanjada. Mientras tanto, el proyecto sigue condicionado por unas actuaciones que comenzaron mucho antes de levantar sus instalaciones.
Imagen destacada | Adarsh Chauhan
Ver 1 comentarios

articles.title: Fairphone Fairbuds 2 review: these AirPods rivals give me peace of mind because of what they're missing — and while it's a worthy cause, their sound quality isn't quite so stellar
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Fairbuds 2 are just as eco-friendly and repairable as the brand's other gadgets, but they also come without the toxic chemicals most headphones are dripping in. It's enough to make a very appealing package, even if the buds themselves are simply 'okay'. The ANC, app and carry case design are good, though the battery life and sound quality won't win any awards.
Reasons to buy
- + Eco-friendly and repairable
- + Relatively affordable
- + Useful EQ presets
Reasons to avoid
- - Below-average battery life
- - Sound quality won’t wow you
- - Plain looks
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Fairphone Fairbuds 2: Two-minute review
I don’t like Fairphone’s products because they’re more environmentally-friendly and repairable than anything else on the market (though they’re all definitely perks). I like them because they always offer something a little different to make them recommendable as some of the best wireless headphones by their own merits.
Last year’s Fairbuds XL 2025 over-ears, for example, had the best controls I’ve used on a pair of headphones before or since (and remain the best-looking cans I’ve reviewed too). And now the Fairphone Fairbuds 2 are here, with a little design decision I didn’t know I wanted so much.
Fairphone is best known for its mobiles, like the recent Fairphone 6 Plus; its whole modus operandi is making green tech (eco-friendly, not colored, although they’re usually also colored green). The brand dabbles in audio too, though, alternating between releasing new earbuds or headphones every other year, and after the original Fairbuds launched in 2024, a new pair are here.
Like the last pair, these are relatively affordable earbuds — 'expensive budget' or 'cheap mid-range' might suffice as definitions — which are great for eco-friendly buyers. They let you enjoy your listening safe in the knowledge that your buying choice was made from renewable energy, using plentiful recycled parts, and won’t impose planet-unfriendly, water usurping AI features on your device.
And then there’s the unexpected bonus. Earlier this year, a fairly shocking study revealed that basically all headphones are coated in PFAS, or forever chemicals, which had people wondering whether they're rubbing toxins on their ears and head. As someone who uses these products for a living, I was a little alarmed to read this, and I’ve been pretty conscious of my listening since then, usually opting for speakers over headphones when I can help it.
It won’t surprise you to learn that the Fairbuds 2 have none of these ‘forever chemicals’, and I could listen for as long as I wanted without worrying about the effects of doing so. It’s hard to put a price on peace of mind, but for music listening, the Fairbuds 2 provide just that.
But I’ve beaten about the bush long enough: beyond health and eco concerns, just how good are these things? Well, the reason I’ve beaten about the bush so much is that “yeah, they’re just fine,” isn't engaging copy.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Design-wise, these are pretty simple buds, with a hardy and light carry case, and pretty feature-light design. There’s little to distinguish them from other buds however, beyond their lack of discernible features. Being pretty plain isn’t the end of the world, and they fit fine.
They’re not the best-sounding earbuds I’ve tested by any stretch of the imagination, but they’re fine for the price if you can look past some rough edges.
I found the ANC pretty good, though it takes its toll on a battery life which roughly matches their price-competitive AirPods rivals (that is to say, it’s not very long). An app brings some extra features, including some of the most effective audio EQ presets I’ve heard from earbuds — if you like customizing your music but aren’t familiar with equalizers, it’s a great option.
If it wasn’t for the Fairphone touch, these would just be middling wireless earbuds that’d disappear behind the competition. But the eco-friendly appeal, their repairability plus the absence of toxic chemicals, all make them far easier to recommend.
Fairphone Fairbuds 2 review: Price and release date
- Released in October in Europe, November US
- Sells for $119 / £99 (about AU$200)
- Cheaper than AirPods 5, which is all that matters
Fairphone unveiled the Fairbuds 2 on October 14, 2026, roughly two years after the release of the original pair and a year after the reimagined Fairbuds XL 2025 over-ears. They went on sale immediately in Europe, but US buyers had to wait until November 2.
You can buy the Fairbuds 2 for $119 / £99 (about AU$200) — Fairphone doesn’t sell its tech in Australia. The brand is increasing its presence in the US; while the original buds did sell there, it only began selling phones earlier this year with the Fairphone 6 Plus.
That phone makes the Fairbuds 2 slightly pricier than their predecessors in the US, but cheaper in the UK; the original Fairbuds went for $99 / £129. Despite this reshuffle, they’re still more affordable than the cheapest version of AirPods 5 (which will set you back $129 / £129 / AU$219), and the Fairphone option actually has ear tips.
Fairphone Fairbuds 2 review: Specs
| Drivers | 11mm | 
| Active noise cancellation | Yes | 
| Battery life | 6 hours (ANC on), 8 hours (ANC off) | 
| Weight | 5.8g (buds) 64g (case) | 
| Connectivity | Bluetooth 6.0 | 
| Frequency response | 20-20kHz | 
| Waterproofing | IP54 | 
Fairphone Fairbuds 2 review: Features
- 6-hour battery life isn't amazing
- ANC is surprisingly solid
- App has EQ including useful presets
According to Fairphone, the earbuds last for 6 hours of listening with ANC on, or 8 hours off; that’s not a very competitive spec, all things considered. In my own testing, I’d say I got a little extra time on those figures, but not enough that I can call the battery life ‘good’. Apple's base model AirPods 5 only last for 4 hours with ANC; the step-up model with wireless charging support last 5 with ANC (or 7 without it) so it's a little better than that, but not by much.
The case provides up to 40 hours of battery life, which is a little better (Apple's step-up model only offers 22), but that spec is for ANC-off listening. An ANC-on figure isn’t provided, but I’d estimate it’s about 32 hours.
The ANC is more impressive — I’ll confess, I wasn’t expecting Fairphone to have created top-of-the-class noise cancellation. While this doesn’t match the likes of Soundcore or Bose, the Fairbuds 2 were surprisingly effective at stripping out noisy backgrounds or the kinds of sporadic sounds that other buds struggle with.
The Fairbuds app is pretty basic, but it’s not strictly necessary; I’d used the buds for two whole weeks before I decided to download it to my phone.
The app lets you toggle between ANC modes (on, off, or transparency), see the charge levels, play with an EQ and presets, and set up multipoint connectivity, although I couldn’t find the option to do so myself. There’s also a Find My Earbuds tool which lets you summon both the left or right bud, and this is a feature you don’t always see in earbuds.
The equalizer is a simple five-band one, but I was surprised how effective the five presets are: Balanced, Bass Boost, Treble Boost and Voice all had significant impacts on the sound profile, in a way that I see being really useful for those who like their audio a certain way and don’t want to play with the custom EQ mode. I found Voice useful for spoken-word content, as it did a great job at maintaining the reader’s voice while dampening other sounds.
- Features score: 4 / 5
Fairphone Fairbuds 2 review: Design
- Small, hardy carry case
- Simplistic buds which fit well
- Eco-friendly, chemical-free design
In one way, the Fairphone Fairbuds 2 are some of the most basic-looking buds there can be, but modest looks hide the real selling point of these options. But we’ll get to that later.
Firstly, the case: it’s a small cylinder, weighing 64g (when the buds are inside) and opening in a clam-shell form. You get the basics: a pairing button, a USB-C port, plus a handy three-LED strip to show you how charged your buds are. Handy! The case is made of plastic that’s so solid that I initially thought it was metal, and it feels more robust than most at protecting your buds.
Next, the buds: unlike the first-gen models, these are stem-toting options, and they look far too simplistic to be confused with AirPods: there’s the in-ear bud, a straight and flat stem, and nothing much else (well, other than some lovely responsive touch controls). They weigh 5.8g each.
When I first started testing them, the Fairbuds 2 felt a little loose in the ear; I thought I had another Samsung Galaxy Buds 4 Pro situation going on. But quite quickly they took to my ear, and after the second day they fit perfectly. So if you've just bought a pair, and are having problems, just give them time.
Now for the whole point of the Fairbuds: Fairphone’s eco credentials. The brand is at the forefront of eco-friendly tech, using eco-friendly materials and processes when possible, and in the buds that means the speaker magnets and solder is all recycled material, while the cobalt, copper, gold and silver are all fairly mined or sourced. The eco-friendly-ness doesn’t just keep your conscience clean, though, because it manifests in a few great ways.
Firstly, these things are completely repairable, so if they break you can buy and replace one part instead of needing new buds. There are seven parts in all, all of which can be replaced using a simple screwdriver. Also in the Fairbuds 2, the earbuds don’t use PFAS, or forever chemicals – you can listen for as long as you want without any fear of the chemicals and their as-yet-unknown effects on the human body.
You can buy the FairBuds 2 in green or black, but if you’re going for green tech, I don’t see why you shouldn’t also be buying green-colored tech. The buds themselves have an IP54 protection against dust and splashes, but the case doesn’t have an official rating.
- Design score: 4.5 / 5
Fairphone Fairbuds 2 review: Sound quality
- 11mm driver per bud
- Prominent bass downs out treble
- Supports LDAC playback on supported phones
The Fairphone Fairbuds 2 come with 11mm dynamic drivers, working as jacks of all trades to cover the audio spectrum.
As fairly affordable earbuds go, the Fairbuds 2 are just fine — you’re not getting any obvious issues like tinny audio, overblown bass or a lackluster sound profile, and so I can’t give them a bad sound score. But there are a few audible issues which it’s worth flagging.
I’d call these buds bass-first, because low-end has more heft than high-end, and it does mean that sometimes vocals can lack the sparkle they deserve. In something like Red Hot Chili Peppers’ Factory of Faith or Dispatch’s May We All, the singers sound like they’ve lost an argument with their bassists and rhythm guitarists, and in Macklemore’s Hind’s Hall the drums and bass keep distracting you from the lyrics.
Bass, while prominent, is perhaps not especially refined; the lack of a bespoke low-end-focused driver here is noticeable. Low-end has power prominence but less direction or distinction than you’d hope. It results in a low-end that sometimes sounds just fine, other times a little rumbly.
In Tom Petty’s Supernatural Radio, for example, the bass riff sounds meaty until the other instruments come in, making it sound indistinct. However with the later guitar and piano solo, the bass drowns out the higher-pitched parts.
These are the first buds I’ve tested in about a month in which I can really hear a song’s mids, though, so props go to Fairphone for not leaning too hard into popular sound profiles. However I did notice peaking in certain songs around the high-end.
It’s easy to point out the issues in the Fairbuds 2, because some rivals at this price point are putting out frankly incredible options, but I should clarify that the buds are still pretty good, and most people will be perfectly happy with them.
For some technical specs, the buds support LDAC if you’re using a compatible Android phone, and use the Bluetooth 6.0 standard.
- Sound quality: 3.5 / 5
Fairphone Fairbuds 2 review: Value
- You get what you pay for: solid, reasonably-priced earbuds
- However, there are some fantastic alternatives at the price
The Fairbuds 2 straddle the border between affordable and mid-range earbuds, but given that the brand's tech generally comes with a green premium, I'm happy to consider these a more affordable option.
If I were to close my eyes, and picture buds at this price, I'd basically envision the Fairphones; they audio quality, feature set and design all roughly match what you'd expect from the price. Fine value for money...
... if it wasn't for the fact that it's a really competitive market segment, with some stellar alternatives.
- Value: 4 / 5
Should I buy the Fairphone Fairbuds 2?
| Fairphone Fairbuds 2 score card |  |  | 
|---|---|---|
| Attributes | Notes | Rating | 
|---|---|---|
| Features | The ANC and app presets work well, though the battery life isn't great. | 4/5 | 
| Design | The eco-friendly and chemical-free build wins all the points, though the simple carry case and buds are charming in their own way. | 4.5/5 | 
| Sound quality | Audio is perfectly serviceable, though a few quirks will put off audiophiles. | 3.5/5 | 
| Value | They're fine value for money, though not the best in their market segment. | 4/5 | 
Buy them if…
You want eco-friendly tech
Fairphone is second-to-none with its green materials, production and sourcing.
You'll repair your earbuds if they break
Repairable tech is all the rage, and if you think you'd be up to fix broken buds, these are the ones to buy.
You like svelte carry cases
The Fairbuds 2 have one of the smallest carry cases I've seen in ages, and it's pretty protective too.
Don’t buy them if…
You're a staunch audiophile
If all you care about is the sound, I think you'll find the Fairbuds 2 a little disappointing.
You'd like something long-lasting
The Fairbuds are long-lasting in terms of the product life span, but the actual battery life isn't that great.
Fairphone Fairbuds 2 review: Also consider
Looking for alternative in-ears? Here are a few alternatives at the same price point.
| Header Cell - Column 0 | Fairphone Fairbuds 2 | Soundpeats H3 | Huawei FreeBuds Neo | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Drivers | 11mm | 12mm + dual balanced armatures | 11mm | 
| Active noise cancellation | Yes | Yes | Yes | 
| Battery life (ANC on) | 6 hours (buds) 32 hours (case) | 7 hours (buds) 37 hours (case) | 6 hours (buds) / 22 hours (case) | 
| Weight | 5.8g (buds) 64g (case) | 6g (buds) 53g (case) | 4.8g (bud) 31.4g (case) | 
| Connectivity | Bluetooth 6.0 | Bluetooth 5.4 | Bluetooth 6.0 | 
| Waterproofing | IP54 | IPX5 | IP55 | 
Soundpeats H3
For a tiny amount more, you can buy arguably the best-sounding earbuds at this price point. The H3 look funky, fit well and sound incredibly, but don't have the eco appeal of the Fairbuds.
Read our full Soundpeats H3 review
Huawei FreeBuds Neo
A Fairbuds 2 contemporary with pretty similar specs, the Neo sound better and are lovely and small, but the app barely works and the ANC isn't as good.
Read our full Huawei FreeBuds Neo review
How I tested the Fairphone Faurbuds 2
- Tested for three weeks
- Paired with Android phone for Bluetooth playback
- Used on holiday as well as use at home and around neighborhood.
I used the Fairphone Fairbuds 2 for about three weeks before writing this review; I used them back-to-back with the Huawei FreeBuds Neo, generally bringing them both with me on trips.
In this testing time I went on holiday, so they got time on flights, train and coach trips, and I also used them at the gym, at home and on walks around my local area.
For the entirety of the testing time, the buds were connected to my Samsung phone. I listened to Spotify, played from my high-res collection, played games, conducted video calls and watched videos to test them out.
I've tested most of Fairphone's gadgets since I joined TechRadar in 2019, including the Fairbuds XL 2025 last year, and also have experience reviewing plenty of other earbuds from a range of brands (including almost every other pair mentioned in the review)>

Beyond TechRadar, he has bylines on sites including GamesRadar, Digital Trends, Android Police, TechAdvisor, WhattoWatch and BGR. articles.title: Cash flow management gets real-time data for lending - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Beyond the books: Real-time data is driving a small-business lending surge
Small businesses have long treated cash flow management as an afterthought, tallying expenses after the money is gone. Now, financial platforms are folding payments, payroll, credit and lending into one system that can see money moving both ways — and predict where it is headed.
That shift puts software providers in direct competition with banks for small-business credit. Intuit Inc. says its view of both sides of the ledger, paired with AI pushing finance toward automation, gives it an edge traditional lenders cannot match, according to Todd Denbo (pictured), senior vice president of lending and commercial leader of Money at Intuit.
“We can see the expenses you’ve got queued up,” Denbo said. “For us, we can effectively predict that you’re going to have a cash flow shortage. That’s why we’ve got our lending businesses as well, so we can proactively offer lines of credit or a term loan to bridge that gap.”
Denbo spoke with theCUBE’s Alison Kosik and Christophe Bertrand at Intuit Connect, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how Intuit uses real-time financial data and AI to help small businesses manage cash flow and automate financial tasks. (* Disclosure below.)
Cash flow management meets real-time lending data
Intuit lent about $400 million a year four years ago and almost $7 billion in its most recent fiscal year, according to Denbo. That growth reflects data averaging 625,000 data points per small business across the 10 million companies already on the platform. Because those businesses manage their finances on Intuit’s platform, the company can see money coming in and going out as it happens.
“Most lenders in this space rely on outdated trends that are from the commercial credit bureaus or the personal credit bureaus, or they’re trying to infer data that is just very challenging to infer,” Denbo said. “All of that is real-time.”
Intuit has also added spending data through its QuickBooks-integrated business credit card, which lets owners control employee spending before money leaves. The company has extended QuickBooks into Claude and ChatGPT as well, though automation still stops short of moving money on its own, Denbo explained. AI can handle the financial groundwork while business owners retain the final say over actions involving their money.
“We are gathering the data, we’re analyzing the data, we are packaging a response or a draft,” Denbo said. “But when it comes to anything that is moving money or sending a draft out, that’s where we’re waiting for, effectively, a human intervention.”

articles.title: "Qapla', Captain Picard!"
articles.text:
Friday, October 30th 2026
"Qapla', Captain Picard!"
Sir Patrick Stewart has sadly died. He passed away at his home in Los Angeles, on the 28th, as announced by his family last night. According to his family, Stewart had a brief battle with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia. Born in Yorkshire, England; Steward is a decorated actor from the Royal Shakespeare Company to an illustrious career on Broadway, Hollywood, and television. We most fondly remember him for his role as Captain Jean Luc Picard, the main character of "Star Trek: The Next Generation," a monumental piece of science fiction and philosophy that shaped many of us here at TechPowerUp, which is why this feels like a personal loss. Although at the surface, TNG is a show about space exploration in the future, it teaches us that the final frontier is indeed the human condition, and we will never stop exploring it through our lives.
Qapla', Captain Picard!
45 Comments on "Qapla', Captain Picard!"
: (
I made a post in another thread about how greatly and positively I was influenced by ST:TNG as a teenager. I wouldn't be who I am without it.
Thank you for everything, good sir. Safe travels.
*Klingon Death Howl*
It is possible to commit no mistakes and still lose. That is not a weakness. That is life.
Also, we shouldn't forget his roles in Excalibur and Lynch's Dune, among many others.
Alas, no more "to baldly go where no man has gone before"...
P.s. Anyone remember this? 'Robin Hood: Men in Tights' by Mel Brooks - a great comedic performance of Sir Patric as King Richard.
RIP Jean Luc. I'm glad I got to see him live a couple of times and even chat briefly with him during an intermission. That man is what made TNG peak Star Trek. I'm sure the real credit goes to the screenwriters but this is one of my favourite Picard quotes:
Rest in peace.
TNG got me interested on scifi and then watched Babylon 5. Not many actors alive from that either.
Fucking Alzheimer disease!
I don't know how much Star Trek: The Next Generation still resonates with the younger audience. I didn't like original series, although it was circulating quite often on various TV channels available - it was simply too outdated when I first saw them in 1980'. I liked the movies though, and much later even begun to appreciate the original series, understanding better the context in which it was made.
Come to think of it, I saw original series less than 20 years since it was aired, and it seemed like a product from completely another era, with outdated effects and technology, and even acting. Star Trek: The Next Generation first aired in 1987, that is almost 40 years ago, I saw it shortly after that, and I can't view it as outdated, since it somehow cemented the look of Star Trek universe, at least to me.
"The acquisition of wealth is no longer the driving force in our lives. We work to better ourselves and the rest of humanity."
Make it so, Sir Patrick Stewart. Live well and at peace in the final frontier.

articles.title: Black Friday : jusqu’à 500€ d’économie sur ces 10 PC portables chez Boulanger
articles.text:
Boulanger n’attend pas le vendredi 27 novembre : son opération Black Friday, annoncée jusqu’au 30 novembre, fait déjà baisser les prix de son rayon PC portable. Nous avons retenu 10 machines vendues par l’enseigne, du portable bureautique au PC gamer, en ne gardant que des remises calculées sur le prix de référence affiché et en signalant les compromis de chaque modèle.
Le Black Friday tombe le vendredi 27 novembre, mais Boulanger a lancé son opération dès la fin octobre. Sur notre sélection, les baisses vont de 200 € à 500 €, soit de -15 % à -33 % par rapport au « prix de référence » affiché par l’enseigne, qui doit correspondre au prix le plus bas pratiqué sur les 30 jours précédant la réduction.
La liste couvre trois usages : six PC bureautiques vendus entre 499,99 € et 599,99 €, deux modèles Asus plus haut de gamme sous puce Snapdragon X, et deux PC gamer équipés d’une GeForce RTX 5060. Un détail revient sur huit fiches sur dix : le chargeur n’est pas fourni, prévoyez-en un compatible si vous n’en possédez pas déjà un.
Black Friday Boulanger : les 10 meilleurs PC portables en promo
- PC portable Asus Zenbook A16 16 pouces (Snapdragon X, 16 Go, SSD 1 To) à 1 099,99 € au lieu de 1 599,99 €
- PC hybride Asus Vivobook S16 Flip 16 pouces OLED tactile (Snapdragon X, 16 Go, SSD 256 Go) à 899,99 € au lieu de 1 199,99 €
- PC portable gamer HP Victus 15,6 pouces (Ryzen AI 5 340, RTX 5060, 16 Go, SSD 512 Go) à 1 099,99 € au lieu de 1 299,99 €
- PC portable gamer Asus TUF A16 (Ryzen 9 8940HX, RTX 5060, 32 Go, SSD 1 To) à 1 499,99 € au lieu de 1 799,99 €
- PC portable Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 14 pouces (Intel Core 3 304, 8 Go, SSD 512 Go) à 549,99 € au lieu de 799,99 €
- PC portable HP 16-bz0040nfx 16 pouces (Snapdragon X, 8 Go, SSD 512 Go) à 599,99 € au lieu de 849,99 €
- PC portable HP 16-bu0091nfx 16 pouces (Intel Core 5 120U, 8 Go, SSD 512 Go) à 499,99 € au lieu de 749,99 €
- PC portable Acer Aspire Go 15 (Intel Core 5 120U, 8 Go, SSD 512 Go) à 529,99 € au lieu de 749,99 €
- PC portable Asus X1704MA 17,3 pouces (Intel Core 3 304, 8 Go, SSD 256 Go) à 499,99 € au lieu de 749,99 €
- PC portable HP OmniBook 3 17 pouces (Intel Core 3 100U, 8 Go, SSD 512 Go) à 599 € au lieu de 799,99 €
VPN, logiciels, abonnements : les promos à saisir en ce moment
Six PC portables à regarder de plus près
Le Zenbook A16 signe la plus forte baisse en euros de la sélection, mais la version vendue par Boulanger n’est pas celle de notre test du Zenbook A16, qui portait une puce Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme et un écran 2,8K. Pour ce modèle comme pour les cinq autres, nous indiquons à qui il s’adresse et ce qui peut freiner l’achat.
- Asus Zenbook A16 : son châssis en Ceraluminum ne pèse que 1,2 kg pour un écran de 16 pouces, et il garde un lecteur de cartes SD. Cette configuration se contente d’un Snapdragon X à 8 cœurs et d’une définition de 1 920 × 1 200 pixels, sans chargeur dans la boîte. Sur la version que nous avons testée, nous avions relevé une charnière et un cadre d’écran fragiles.
- Asus Vivobook S16 Flip : son écran tactile de 16 pouces pivote à 360° pour passer en mode tablette, et Asus annonce jusqu’à 17 heures d’autonomie. Ses 256 Go de stockage se rempliront vite si vous gardez photos et vidéos en local, et le chargeur n’est pas fourni.
- HP Victus 15 : c’est le PC gamer le plus abordable de la liste, avec une GeForce RTX 5060, 16 Go de mémoire et un écran Full HD à 144 Hz, chargeur fourni. La remise reste modeste, à -15 %, et ses 2,3 kg le destinent plutôt au bureau qu’au sac à dos.
- Asus TUF A16 : pour 400 € de plus que le Victus, il double la mémoire à 32 Go et le stockage à 1 To, avec un Ryzen 9 8940HX à 16 cœurs et un écran de 16 pouces à 165 Hz. Son autonomie annoncée plafonne à 5 h 30 : c’est une machine à garder branchée pour jouer.
- Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 : avec 1,39 kg, ce 14 pouces est le plus léger des modèles bureautiques de la sélection, et Lenovo annonce jusqu’à 19 heures d’autonomie. Ses 8 Go de mémoire conviennent à la navigation et à la bureautique, beaucoup moins au multitâche lourd.
- HP OmniBook 3 17 pouces : il offre une grande dalle de 17,3 pouces et 512 Go de stockage, mais sa définition de 1 600 × 900 pixels est en retrait de celle des neuf autres modèles, tous en Full HD ou plus. Pour un grand écran à petit prix, l’Asus X1704MA affiche la même diagonale en Full HD pour 499,99 €, avec un SSD réduit à 256 Go.
Snapdragon, Intel ou RTX : comment choisir dans cette sélection
Trois modèles de la liste reposent sur une puce Snapdragon X de Qualcomm : les deux Asus haut de gamme et le HP 16-bz0040nfx. Ces puces ARM visent d’abord l’autonomie, et nous avions constaté lors de notre essai du Zenbook A16 que Qualcomm restait en retrait sur le plan graphique : elles conviennent mieux à la bureautique et au multimédia qu’au jeu.
Pour jouer, seuls le HP Victus et l’Asus TUF A16 embarquent une carte graphique dédiée. Pour un usage bureautique, les modèles Intel à 499,99 € et 529,99 € suffisent si vous acceptez 8 Go de mémoire. Pour situer ces machines face aux références que nous avons testées, notre comparatif des meilleurs PC portables fait le point par usage et par budget.
Vos questions sur les PC portables du Black Friday Boulanger
Ces PC portables sont-ils livrés avec un chargeur ?
Pas tous : d’après les fiches de Boulanger, seuls le HP Victus 15 et l’Asus TUF A16 sont livrés avec leur chargeur. Pour les huit autres, prévoyez un modèle compatible si vous n’en avez pas déjà un.
Que signifie le prix de référence affiché par Boulanger ?
C’est le prix qui sert de base au calcul de la remise : la loi impose qu’il corresponde au prix le plus bas pratiqué par le vendeur sur les 30 jours précédant la réduction. Les pourcentages de cette sélection sont calculés à partir de ces prix, relevés le 30 octobre.
Jusqu’à quand durent les offres Black Friday de Boulanger ?
La page de l’opération annonce des offres jusqu’au 30 novembre. Les prix peuvent toutefois évoluer d’ici là, et rien ne garantit qu’ils resteront identiques jusqu’au vendredi 27 novembre.
Comment profiter des offres exclusives du Black Friday ?
Durant tout le mois de novembre, Clubic vous propose chaque jour des sélections thématiques regroupant les meilleures offres à saisir en direct.
Retrouvez tous les bons plans du Black Friday 2026 sur la page dédiée à l'événement.
Pour les aficionados de X, n'hésitez pas à suivre notre compte Clubic Bons Plans pour être au courant en direct des meilleures offres.

articles.title: SpaceX quer comprar casas de vizinhos incomodados com seus data centers • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
SpaceX quer comprar casas de vizinhos incomodados com seus data centers
SpaceXSI estaria comprando casas próximas a uma usina que gera energia para seus data centers para tentar evitar queixas por ruído.
Não é incomum que pessoas que vivem próximas a data centers reclamem sobre esses lugares causarem transtornos. Para lidar com isso, a SpaceX parece ter encontrado uma solução, digamos, radical: estaria comprando casas localizadas nas proximidades de uma usina de energia que alimenta justamente data centers.
O caso em questão envolve, na verdade, a SpaceXSI, empresa resultante da incorporação de xAI pela SpaceX. A xAI foi fundada por Elon Musk em 2023 para desenvolver tecnologias e serviços de inteligência artificial, com destaque para o Grok, vale relembrar.
Pois bem, não é novidade que aplicações de IA demandam data centers dedicados. Por conta disso, a SpaceXSI construiu em 2024, ainda sob o nome xAI, instalações do tipo na região de Memphis, nos Estados Unidos.
Data centers demandam muita energia. Para atender a essa necessidade, a SpaceXSI montou uma estrutura de geração de energia com 69 turbinas temporárias movidas a gás na cidade de Southaven. O problema é que essas turbinas produzem muito barulho, incomodando enormemente os moradores da região (sem contar outros transtornos gerados, como a poluição do ar).
De acordo com o jornal The Guardian, a SpaceXSI passou a enviar corretores de imóveis a moradores das redondezas da usina de energia para oferecer uma proposta de compra de suas residências.
Um corretor teria dito a um dos moradores que o plano da companhia de Elon Musk consiste em comprar 418 casas da região, sendo que 18 já teriam sido negociadas. Outras cinco já teriam sido compradas pela MZX, subsidiária da SpaceX que opera a estrutura de energia.
Ainda de acordo com o jornal, as residências adquiridas serão usadas para abrigar funcionários da companhia. Ao que tudo indica, as propostas de aquisição têm valores próximos a US$ 180.000, que é a estimativa média de preço das casas da região.
Mas há uma condição: o morador que quiser vender a sua casa deve concordar em não processar a SpaceXSI por conta dos incômodos causados pela usina elétrica.
Na verdade, uma ação judicial coletiva contra a SpaceXSI está em curso desde junho desde ano. Nela, moradores da região reclamam que a usina gera um ruído constante e que, muitas vezes, se assemelha ao barulho de um avião. Nesse sentido, a compra das casas seria uma estratégia para não tornar o embate judicial um problema maior.
No mês seguinte, a empresa fechou um acordo com órgãos reguladores estaduais para transformar a usina em uma instalação permanente de geração de energia a gás. Essa mudança traria uma estrutura mais moderna que, como tal, diminuiria o ruído que hoje é gerado pelas turbinas temporárias.
A SpaceXSI também já havia se manifestado sobre a implementação de medidas de contenção dos transtornos, como construção de barreiras acústicas e ajustes de potência na geração de energia.
Mas a suposta estratégia de comprar casas na região levanta dúvidas sobre se, de fato, a companhia de Elon Musk pretende ser uma “boa vizinha”, como deu a entender.
Até o momento, a SpaceXSI não se manifestou sobre o tal plano de aquisição de imóveis.

articles.title: Blackstone advierte de que Anthropic se arriesga a salir a bolsa sin una buena calificación, un golpe para sus planes
articles.text:
En la carrera por la inteligencia artificial, Anthropic se ha convertido en una de las grandes promesas del sector. La compañía detrás de Claude ha conseguido atraer inversiones multimillonarias y se prepara para dar uno de los pasos más importantes de su historia: salir a bolsa. Sin embargo, hay algo que no debemos perder de vista en medio de tanto entusiasmo. Desarrollar modelos cada vez más avanzados exige enormes cantidades de dinero, y conseguir financiación para sostener ese crecimiento es una cuestión muy distinta de despertar el interés de los inversores.
Es precisamente en ese terreno donde ha surgido una advertencia que merece atención. Según Financial Times, Blackstone ha comunicado a sus inversores que espera que Anthropic reciba una nota crediticia situada en la parte alta del grado especulativo, probablemente en la categoría BB, después de salir a bolsa. El grupo financiero había transmitido antes una expectativa más favorable, la de alcanzar el grado de inversión tras el debut bursátil. No se trata de una rebaja decidida por una agencia de calificación, sino de un cambio en las previsiones de uno de los actores vinculados a su financiación.
La cuestión está en qué significa realmente obtener el grado de inversión. S&P Globa detalla que las agencias de calificación evalúan "la capacidad y disposición de los prestatarios para cumplir íntegra y puntualmente sus compromisos financieros". Es decir, no determinan cuánto vale una compañía en bolsa, sino el riesgo de que no pague sus deudas. En la escala de S&P, BBB− es la nota mínima del grado de inversión y BB+ queda justo por debajo, en el grado especulativo. Anthropic recibió precisamente un BB+ como emisor de KBRA en junio, según periódico británico, aunque esa evaluación no equivale a las de Moody's, S&P o Fitch.
Un escenario que apunta a dificultades de financiación
No alcanzar ese umbral no significa quedarse sin financiación, pero sí puede encarecerla. La Comisión de Bolsa y Valores de Estados Unidos (SEC) explica que los compradores de bonos suelen exigir mayores intereses cuando asumen más riesgo de impago. S&P Global añade que algunos inversores institucionales tienen restricciones para comprar deuda con calificaciones bajas.
También debemos tener en cuenta que para Anthropic hay una consecuencia adicional: su folleto bursátil establece que, si obtiene el grado de inversión de al menos dos agencias entre Moody's, S&P y Fitch, podrá optar por liberar las garantías que respaldan una de sus líneas de crédito.
Blackstone no es una agencia de calificación, sino uno de los grandes grupos de inversión que participan en la financiación de infraestructura para Anthropic. El pasado 26 de octubre, la firma anunció, junto a Bank of America, Citi y Morgan Stanley, una operación de 63.000 millones de dólares destinada a financiar la compra de equipos de Broadcom que después se alquilarán a la creadora de Claude.
Según el comunicado, Blackstone es el único proveedor de la parte comprometida de la financiación con garantías de segundo rango, que tiene menor prioridad de cobro que la deuda principal. En cualquier caso, la salida a bolsa de Anthropic ya ha dado un paso formal: el 26 de octubre, la compañía presentó ante la SEC su folleto para cotizar en el Nasdaq bajo el símbolo ANT, aunque todavía no había fijado cuántas acciones ofrecerá ni a qué precio.

articles.title: After Google cleared 330 hectares of forest for an AI data center, Finland has launched a criminal investigation into 'ambiguities and shortcomings in the drainage and water management'
articles.text:
A criminal investigation is now underway into Google's AI data center project in Finland, where 330 hectares of forest were torn down
The probe will take quite some time to complete, though
- Google's subsidiary Tuike Finland cleared and drained 330 hectares of forest at Muhos for a data center site
- The company failed to get the necessary environmental impact assessments completed before carrying out the felling
- A preliminary police investigation is now taking place, based on 'ambiguities and shortcomings in the drainage and water management', although the results of this won't be known until 2027
A preliminary police investigation is now underway into Google's clearing of a forest in Finland to make space for an AI data center.
As The Guardian reports, the allegation is that Google's subsidiary Tuike Finland cleared and drained 330 hectares of forest at the site in Muhos before it had ensured the necessary environmental impact assessments were completed.
Yle (Finland's public broadcasting company) further reports that the police have said that the investigation is into suspected environmental damage, but the other possible charges could be added depending on its ongoing findings.
Finnish police said: "Based on preliminary information, there have been ambiguities and shortcomings in the drainage and water management at the construction site of Tuike Finland Oy's datacentre project."
The investigation will be far from a short process, though, and won't be completed until some point in 2027.
Construction work was stopped on the data center in Muhos, and also at a second data center site at Kajaani-Otanmäki, on October 14. In both cases, the environmental assessments were apparently incomplete.
Antti Järvinen, who heads up Google Finland as country manager, apologized for the forest clearances, but said that Google had acted according to the "best understanding we had of the legislation at the time."
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Analysis: the rush for AI data centers
Some 400,000 trees have reportedly been felled across both sites (250,000 of those at Muhos). As The Guardian makes clear in a separate report from last week (via Tom's Hardware), there are a lot of very unhappy Finnish people, as you might imagine.
Many of them question the building of data centers at all, and the AI gold rush that's the driving force behind this activity. There's apparently little direct benefit for the people of the country where these projects are underway, with only a small number of local jobs created. As a professor of computer science at the University of Helsinki, Jussi Kangasharju points out, "Really, for Finland, there are no benefits. They are international companies serving international customers. Datacentres ultimately have little benefit for others except the datacentre operator."
Others obviously worry about the impact on wildlife. Finnish conservationists inform us that the three-toed woodpeckers in the forest have been displaced, and The Guardian highlighted that in Otanmäki, wolves that had nowhere to go when the trees were felled ended up coming into a local village.
It will be some time before the criminal investigation is completed, as noted, but you can bet that the results are going to be closely watched.

articles.title: PS5 desbloqueado vira “Steam Machine” e roda jogos de PC • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
PS5 desbloqueado vira “Steam Machine” e roda jogos de PC
Projeto instala Bazzite com interface da Steam, suporte ao Proton e até desbloqueio experimental de unidades da GPU.
Um projeto não oficial transformou um PlayStation 5 desbloqueado em uma máquina Linux voltada para jogos. O PS5 Bazzite Deck leva a distribuição Bazzite ao console da Sony com a interface Steam Gaming Mode. A novidade representa um avanço em relação às primeiras experiências com Linux no videogame.
Agora, o foco está em transformar o console em algo próximo de uma “Steam Machine”, com acesso à biblioteca de jogos de PC.
O projeto adapta a versão do Bazzite voltada a consoles portáteis para o PlayStation 5. Também é possível alternar para um desktop completo baseado no KDE Plasma. Apesar da aparência, não é o SteamOS oficial da Valve. O Bazzite é uma distribuição Linux independente que oferece experiência similar e utiliza tecnologias como o Proton para executar jogos criados para Windows.
O sistema inicializa a partir de uma unidade externa, como pendrive ou SSD, e não substitui o software original da Sony. Sem carregar o Linux, o PS5 volta normalmente ao sistema da Sony.
Uma demonstração no YouTube mostra o console executando Forza Horizon 6. O detalhe chama atenção porque o jogo, lançado até agora para Xbox Series X/S e PC, só chega oficialmente ao PS5 em janeiro de 2027.
Usuários também já conseguiram executar Horizon Zero Dawn, Palworld, Genshin Impact, RimWorld e XCOM 2. O desenvolvedor do projeto afirma no Reddit que Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Ethernet e DualSense já funcionam no Bazzite, assim como o áudio por HDMI e aceleração de vídeo por hardware.
Em consoles equipados com chip HDMI FLAVA3, o projeto oferece resolução 1440p e 4K a até 120 Hz, além de HDR e VRR. Outras revisões possuem limitações e podem ficar restritas a 4K a 60 Hz.
No PS5 original e Slim sim. A GPU possui fisicamente 40 unidades computacionais (CUs), mas a Sony comercializa o console com 36 delas ativadas. O projeto permite tentar habilitar as quatro restantes. Isso representa mais CUs ativas, mas não garante ganho de desempenho e pode causar instabilidade.
O próprio projeto alerta que a ativação pode provocar pontos verdes, cores alteradas, artefatos gráficos e travamentos. Se surgirem problemas, é possível voltar à configuração original.
É necessário ter um console com um firmware compatível e acesso a um método de jailbreak. O cenário de desbloqueio do PS5 avançou rapidamente nos últimos meses, com novos exploits e ferramentas compatíveis com diferentes versões do sistema.
Vale mencionar que o primeiro boot pode levar vários minutos e atualizações da Sony também podem alterar o funcionamento. O PS5 Pro também passou a ser reconhecido pelo Bazzite a partir da versão 1.8.4, mas o desenvolvedor ainda classifica esse suporte como inicial.

articles.title: Smartphone, écouteurs et bracelet : le pack Xiaomi 17T Pro passe en mode Black Friday (-31%)
articles.text:
Boulanger a lancé son Black Friday près d’un mois avant la date officielle du 27 novembre, et le Xiaomi 17T Pro, sorti à 999,99 € il y a cinq mois, fait partie des premières baisses. Le pack 512 Go passe à 749,99 € avec écouteurs, bracelet et coque : une offre solide pour s’équiper d’un coup, moins pertinente si vous avez déjà vos accessoires.
Boulanger n’a pas attendu le 27 novembre : son opération Black Friday est déjà en ligne, et le Xiaomi 17T Pro, le mieux doté de la série 17T avec sa puce Dimensity 9500, sa batterie de 7 000 mAh et son téléobjectif Leica, en profite. Le pack est proposé à 749,99 € au lieu d’un prix de référence de 1 089,99 €, avec des écouteurs Redmi Buds 8, un bracelet Smart Band 11 Active et une coque. L’ensemble coûte ainsi 250 € de moins que le seul smartphone à sa sortie, en mai.
L’offre vise ceux qui cherchent un Android haut de gamme endurant sans posséder d’écouteurs sans fil ni de bracelet d’activité. Déjà équipé, vous ferez plutôt le calcul sur le téléphone seul.
Le pack Xiaomi 17T Pro 512 Go, avec Redmi Buds 8, Smart Band 11 Active et coque, passe à 749,99 € au lieu de 1 089,99 €.
Pourquoi choisir le Xiaomi 17T Pro ?
- Deux jours loin du chargeur : La batterie silicium-carbone de 7 000 mAh, 27 % plus grande que sur la génération précédente, tient deux jours en usage courant selon plusieurs tests. La charge atteint 100 W en filaire et 50 W sans fil.
- Un vrai zoom optique : Le téléobjectif Leica de 50 Mpx, stabilisé, grossit cinq fois sans recadrage et filme en 4K à 60 images par seconde. Il rapproche une scène de concert ou un portrait en gardant du détail.
- Un écran lisible partout : La dalle AMOLED 1,5K de 6,83 pouces grimpe à 144 Hz et jusqu’à 3 500 nits annoncés. Elle reste exploitable en plein soleil.
Voyages, photo et jeux : ce que ce pack change au quotidien
Gravé en 3 nm, le Dimensity 9500 fait tourner les jeux exigeants sans difficulté d’après les tests, et 12 Go de mémoire vive laissent de la marge au multitâche. Les 512 Go, non extensibles, conviennent à ceux qui filment beaucoup en 4K. Le capteur principal de 50 Mpx au format 1/1,31 pouce reste le point fort photo, avec un traitement Leica jugé fiable. Écouteurs à réduction de bruit active et bracelet, piloté par l’application Mi Fitness, servent ensuite dans les transports et au sport.
Ce pack parle surtout au voyageur qui veut oublier son chargeur le temps d’un week-end et renouveler en même temps écouteurs et suivi d’activité. Le Smart Band 11 Active reste un bracelet d’entrée de gamme : écran TFT de 1,47 pouce, suivi cardiaque et SpO2, jusqu’à 8 jours d’autonomie en usage normal selon Xiaomi. Les amateurs de selfies seront moins gâtés, la caméra frontale de 32 Mpx manquant de précision en basse lumière selon Journal du Geek. Les longues sessions de jeu font aussi nettement chauffer le cadre en aluminium.
Face au Xiaomi 17T et au reste du haut de gamme
Le rival le plus direct vient de la même famille : le Xiaomi 17T standard, lancé à 749,99 €, se contente d’un capteur principal plus petit, d’une batterie de 6 500 mAh et d’une charge à 67 W, et nous l’avions relevé sous les 500 € sur AliExpress début septembre. Le 17T Pro en pack se défend donc surtout pour l’endurance et la photo. Il ne vise pas pour autant le sommet : dans notre comparatif des meilleurs smartphones, mis à jour le 21 octobre, c’est le Xiaomi 17 Ultra qui représente la marque pour la photo.

- Écran AMOLED 144 Hz très lumineux

articles.title: Role-based access control decides if AI agents can be trusted - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
The race to deploy AI agents finds a familiar hurdle in data access
Enterprises racing to put AI agents into production are discovering that role-based access control, not model choice, decides whether those agents can be trusted. Rising inference costs, privacy worries and sovereignty demands are also pulling more AI workloads back inside corporate data centers.
That shift favors companies that have spent years governing sensitive data at scale. Cloudera Inc. is betting on Cloudera Anywhere Cloud, a hybrid data and AI platform that spans public clouds and on-premises environments. The company has long been strong on governance, security and scalability but weaker on usability, a gap the new platform was built to close, according to Leo Brunnick (pictured), chief product officer of Cloudera.
“It turns out that the model is ultimately not going to be what separates your success from your competitor’s success,” Brunnick said. “The things that are going to separate you are, number one, your unique data. Your unique data and your unique processes, your alpha — what makes you a business.”
Brunnick spoke with theCUBE’s Rebecca Knight and Paul Gillin at EVOLVE26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed why AI agents must follow users’ data permissions, the forces pushing AI workloads back into corporate data centers and how packaged blueprints and partnerships can simplify private AI adoption. (* Disclosure below.)
Why role-based access control now extends to AI agents
Customers rarely want a new platform for its own sake, so Cloudera is selling solutions to specific problems instead. Its packaged blueprints and expanded partnerships with Mistral AI SAS, Nvidia Corp. and Vast Data Inc. target private AI use cases such as fraud detection. Mistral, which specializes in open-weight models for on-prem inferencing, also lends Cloudera something it has lacked in the AI market.
“Cloudera already had the capabilities. What we don’t have is a lot of credibility around AI. People don’t think of us as an AI company,” Brunnick said. “What Mistral is allowing us to do is increase our capabilities slightly and increase our credibility astronomically.”
The harder work lies in governance. Agents need to see data across the entire company to be useful, so each one must know who the user is and what that user is permitted to see, Brunnick explained.
“Since the agent needs to be able to see everything in the company, the agent needs to know who you are and what your permissions are,” Brunnick said. “That’s what they need to get right so they can actually put stuff into production that doesn’t blow up on them.”

articles.title: Intel Confirms "Nova Lake" Uses 18A-P Internal Node, More Details at CES
articles.text:
Friday, October 30th 2026
Intel Confirms "Nova Lake" Uses 18A-P Internal Node, More Details at CES
During the Q3 2026 earnings call, Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan confirmed that the company's upcoming flagship client CPU, codenamed "Nova Lake," will be produced by Intel Foundry using its 18A-P node. Initially, Intel planned to outsource the main compute tile production for "Nova Lake" to TSMC, utilizing its 2 nm N2 node. TSMC was expected to handle about 60-70% of the production, with the remainder produced in-house by Intel Foundry on the 18A node. This meant Intel would dual-source production for its next-generation chip. However, later supply chain information suggested that the company intended to bring the majority of "Nova Lake" compute tile production in-house, with these compute tiles being made on the Intel 18A-P node. Today, we received confirmation directly from the Intel CEO:
Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan"Nova Lake," our first Intel 18A-P client product, is tracking ahead of schedule, with design wins expected to be twice those of "Panther Lake" at launch. We look forward to sharing more at CES in January.
Intel is set to release SKUs with either one or two compute dies, each featuring up to 8 "Coyote Cove" P-Cores and 16 "Arctic Wolf" E-Cores, alongside 4 LPE-Cores that are integrated as part of the I/O die. Depending on the SKU, Intel can include a single compute die for a total of up to 28 cores or two compute dies for a 52-core CPU SKU. It's currently rumored that the single compute die version will be released first, with the dual compute die variants to follow. However, Intel will share more details at CES in January, so we'll have to be a bit more patient.

articles.title: Por qué el dolor de espalda crónico se siente tan personal: el cerebro lo trata como parte de quiénes somos
articles.text:
Las personas que conviven con el dolor de espalda crónico saben bien que, de un modo u otro, se ha convertido en parte de su personalidad. Despiertan cada mañana atentos a las sensaciones del nuevo día, cancelan planes por los dolores, dejan de practicar deportes que adoraban o incluso de coger en brazos a sus propios hijos… Es mucho más que un simple dolor. De hecho, está tan sumamente arraigado a la personalidad que, según un nuevo estudio, activa zonas del cerebro relacionadas con la autoconciencia. Es un descubrimiento interesante tanto por dar explicación a algo que en cierto modo intuíamos como porque puede abrir la puerta a nuevos y necesarios tratamientos.
Señales distintas en el cerebro. Para comprobar las diferencias entre el procesamiento cerebral de un dolor agudo o un dolor crónico, como puede ser el de espalda, un equipo de científicos de la Universidad de California San Diego reclutó a 114 personas que padecen dolor de espalda crónico. Es decir, un dolor lumbar que lleva más de 12 semanas sin resolución. Con el fin de provocar un episodio de dolor, se les hizo realizar una prueba de elevación de piernas. Pero también era necesario causar un dolor agudo en otra parte del cuerpo, así que se les aplicó un calor molesto en la pantorrilla.
Al estudiar su cerebro mediante resonancia magnética funcional, se vio que en el caso del dolor agudo disminuyó la actividad en un conjunto de regiones asociadas a la autoconciencia, conocido como red neuronal por defecto (DMN). En cambio, con el dolor lumbar ocurrió todo lo contrario: aumentó la actividad en dicha zona.
Los motivos. La DMN procesa todos esos pensamientos que forman parte de quiénes somos: las reflexiones sobre experiencias personales, los pensamientos sobre nuestra identidad, la observación de nuestras propias emociones… Son pensamientos casi constantes en nuestro día a día. Por su parte, el dolor agudo a menudo es una señal de alerta de que algo no va bien. Sentimos dolor al tocar algo muy caliente para poder apartar la mano y no quemarnos. Por eso, en casos de dolor agudo se desactiva temporalmente la DMN. Es necesario dejar espacio en el cerebro para procesar lo que ha causado la alerta.
En cambio, con el dolor crónico no hay nada externo a lo que haya que prestar atención. Forma parte de la persona y, además, puede traerle a la mente recuerdos de otras experiencias en las que sintió dolor o miedo a cómo lo percibirá en el futuro. Los autores del estudio creen que el dolor puede incluso generar un sentimiento de vergüenza por las actividades que no se pueden realizar. Todo eso lo procesa la DMN. Posiblemente esa es la causa por la que aumenta la actividad.
Aplicaciones. Los autores de este estudio han comenzado a realizar ensayos clínicos en los que se trata el dolor lumbar crónico mediante mindfulness y psilocibina. El primero es una técnica de meditación basada en la atención plena, mientras que el segundo es una sustancia psicodélica. Ninguno es capaz de eliminar el dolor, ni agudo ni crónico. Sin embargo, vistas las conclusiones de este estudio, sí que podrían tener aplicaciones interesantes en lo referente a la relación entre el dolor y la autoconciencia.
Por un lado, el mindfulness centra la atención en el ahora, de modo que la mente no vuela hacia experiencias de dolor pasadas o temores del futuro. Y, por otro, la psilocibina, como otros psicodélicos, es capaz de “abrir las puertas del cerebro” y modular su actividad. En este caso, se cree que podría reiniciar el sistema de dolor que integra traumas, experiencias pasadas y preocupaciones futuras para facilitar un reinicio. Todo esto, junto a los fármacos que sí van dirigidos directamente a la sensación de dolor, puede componer un tratamiento muy interesante para personas con dolor crónico.
Las cifras. Según una encuesta realizada por el INE en 2025, el dolor crónico lumbar afecta al 21,8% de las mujeres y al 13,6% de los hombres en España. Además, el barómetro de la lumbalgia de 2024 estimó que el 80% de los españoles tendrá algún episodio de dolor lumbar a lo largo de su vida, y que la edad media de los pacientes con dolor crónico y lumbalgia es de 51,3 años. Son muchísimas las personas que pueden verse beneficiadas por la comprensión de los mecanismos que están involucrados en este tipo de dolor. Solo así se podrán obtener tratamientos realmente transversales que no se centren únicamente en la sensación de dolor, sino también en cómo lo procesa nuestro cerebro.

Geely prépare une voiture électrique sur mesure pour 2027 afin de séduire les Européens
Fini les voitures chinoises simplement adaptées au Vieux Continent, Geely dévoilera en 2027 un modèle dessiné à Milan corrigeant enfin tous ses défauts logiciels décriés par les Européens.
Déjà bien implanté chez nous à travers Volvo, Polestar, Lotus et Smart, le géant chinois Geely passe à la vitesse supérieure pour imposer sa propre marque. Après avoir lancé ses premiers véhicules électriques et hybrides en adaptant simplement des modèles conçus pour la Chine, le constructeur dresse maintenant un constat lucide sur les attentes locales. Selon les informations d’Autocar, il présentera dès 2027 une voiture développée spécifiquement pour les automobilistes européens.
Une refonte logicielle et mécanique avant une production en Espagne
Avant même l’arrivée de cette nouvelle voiture électrifiée, Geely s’attaque aux défauts qui agacent régulièrement la presse et les conducteurs européens sur les modèles produits en Chine. Dennis Weinel, directeur des produits chez Geely Europe, reconnaît ainsi que le système multimédia actuel reste beaucoup trop calqué sur les habitudes du marché asiatique.
Dès l’année prochaine, la seconde génération de l’interface Flyme corrigera donc le tir avec du multitâche, un affichage en écran partagé, des widgets extensibles et une hiérarchisation plus claire des informations essentielles. Les ingénieurs revoient également les fameux bips incessants des aides à la conduite en retravaillant leur volume, leur tonalité et leur logique de déclenchement pour les rendre moins intrusifs, tout en respectant la réglementation. Les suspensions, le freinage et la direction profiteront quant à eux de nouveaux réglages pour offrir une tenue de route plus précise et dynamique.
C’est sur ces bases que sera lancée la future voiture européenne de 2027. Dessinée au centre de design de Milan, elle ciblera en priorité le Vieux Continent avant d’être exportée ailleurs. Si sa fiche technique demeure secrète, le constructeur envisage de l’électrique ainsi que d’autres motorisations électrifiées, suivant la même trajectoire que son rival BYD.
En parallèle, la gamme passera rapidement de trois modèles (E5, Starray et la récente citadine électrique E2) à cinq avec le SUV Monjaro PHEV et le Project KO11. Ce dernier sera une version adaptée à l’Europe du Galaxy Cruiser, un 4x4 rival du Land Rover Defender partageant sa base avec le futur Lotus Eletre PHEV. Enfin, Geely produira deux modèles électriques dans l’usine Ford de Valence, en Espagne, dès 2028.
Une stratégie d’implantation de la production en Europe portée par les taxes douanières de Bruxelles, et qui devrait faire passer le nombre de modèles chinois (tous constructeurs confondus) produits sur le Vieux Continent de 90 000 unités aujourd’hui à 1,5 million d’ici 2036.

articles.title: La Marine nationale a désormais un robot sous-marin capable de plonger à 6 000 mètres, conçu en un temps record
articles.text:
Le robot sous-marin ROV-DeepSea a bouclé ses essais de qualification au-delà de 5 000 mètres de profondeur. Conçu par LD TravOcean pour la Marine nationale, il dote la France d’un nouvel outil d’intervention dans les grands fonds marins.
Développé pour la Marine nationale sous la houlette de la Direction générale de l'armement (DGA), le robot sous-marin ROV-DeepSea est désormais qualifié pour explorer les grands fonds marins, a-t-on appris cette semaine. Long de trois mètres et pesant 3,6 tonnes hors de l'eau, il est conçu pour descendre jusqu'à 6 000 mètres de profondeur, là où la pression écraserait à peu près tout ce qui n'a pas été pensé pour elle. Et on ne retrouve pas un géant de l'armement derrière cet appareil, mais une entreprise de La Ciotat (dans les Bouches-du-Rhône), dont le métier consiste d'ordinaire à poser des câbles au fond de la mer.
Le robot sous-marin de la Marine nationale a tenu bon sous 5 000 mètres d’eau
Avant d’entrer au service de la Marine nationale, le ROV-DeepSea devait passer ses essais de qualification, avec une série de plongées pour vérifier qu’il fonctionne comme prévu, palier après palier. Ces tests ont été menés par DGA Techniques navales, le centre d’expertise et d’essais de la DGA dédié au naval, avec la Marine. En juillet, au large de Toulon, le robot a d’abord fait ses gammes jusqu’à 2 500 mètres, lors d’une campagne dite « petits et moyens fonds ». En septembre, il a mis le cap sur la Grèce, où la Méditerranée atteint ses plus grandes profondeurs. Il y a franchi la barre des 5 000 mètres.
ROV signifie Remotely Operated Vehicle . Autrement dit, on parle d'un engin sans pilote à bord, manœuvré depuis la surface, auquel il reste relié par un câble. Il est taillé pour opérer jusqu'à 6 000 mètres, de quoi couvrir 97 % des fonds océaniques. À cette profondeur, la pression avoisine 600 fois celle que l'on subit en surface. Pour ne pas couler comme une pierre, le robot embarque des blocs de mousse syntactique, un matériau truffé de microbilles creuses qui encaisse l'écrasement sans broncher.
Le ROV-DeepSea est un beau bébé qui mesure 3,07 mètres de long, 1,48 mètre de large et 2,5 mètres de haut, pour une puissance totale de 100 chevaux. Garni d'outils et d'instruments, il ne fait pas qu'observer, puisque développé sur mesure pour la Marine nationale, il doit l'épauler dans ses trois missions au fond des océans, que sont connaître, surveiller et agir.
LD TravOcean, des câbles sous-marins aux grands fonds
Son constructeur ne vient pas du monde de la défense. Née à Marseille en 1977 et installée aujourd'hui à La Ciotat, LD TravOcean compte près de 150 salariés. Sa spécialité, c'est l'installation et la protection de câbles sous-marins. Dès 1978, elle participait au projet IFA 2000, une liaison électrique entre la France et l'Angleterre. Elle a ensuite œuvré dans des secteurs comme les hydrocarbures, les télécoms puis l'éolien en mer, avec des filiales aux Émirats arabes unis, aux Pays-Bas et en Australie.
Le contrat avec la Direction générale de l'armement lui a été notifié en septembre 2024, et l'évolution a depuis été tout simplement impressionnante. Il n'a fallu que 21 mois seulement pour concevoir et fabriquer le robot. L'entreprise a travaillé main dans la main avec la DGA, l'état-major de la Marine et le GISMER, groupe d'intervention sous la mer rattaché au Centre expert plongée humaine et intervention sous la mer (CEPHISMER). Cette filiale du groupe LD Armateurs, qui exploite une trentaine de navires, rejoint ainsi la base industrielle et technologique de défense, ce cercle d'entreprises qui équipent les armées.
Dès 2023, le Secrétariat général pour l'investissement a confié son développement à la DGA, au titre de l'objectif de France 2030 consacré aux grands fonds marins. C'est un terrain où se croisent les intérêts économiques, environnementaux et les enjeux de sécurité. Le projet s'inscrit aussi dans la stratégie de maîtrise des fonds marins publiée en 2022 par le ministère des Armées. La suite est déjà connue. Dans le cadre du programme à effet majeur MFM, la DGA prépare la commande d'un deuxième système. Les abysses n'ont pas fini de recevoir de la visite.

articles.title: Amazon prorroga acesso grátis à Alexa turbinada • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Amazon prorroga acesso grátis à Alexa turbinada
Tecnoblog apurou que o chamado “acesso antecipado” à Alexa+ vai até fevereiro de 2027.
Os usuários da Amazon terão mais tempo para testar a Alexa+. O Tecnoblog apurou que a gigante da tecnologia decidiu ampliar o período do chamado acesso antecipado em alguns meses. Com isso, os clientes brasileiros poderão experimentar a nova versão da assistente sem pagar por isso.
O período de degustação estava previsto seguir “pelo menos” até outubro de 2026. Agora, a Amazon confirmou com exclusividade ao Tecnoblog que decidiu expandir o beta pelo menos até fevereiro de 2027.
A empresa declarou que “sempre” enxergou o acesso antecipado “como um período dinâmico, no qual oferecemos aos clientes interessados a oportunidade de experimentar a Alexa+ e compartilhar feedback para nos ajudar a refinar o produto antes da disponibilidade geral”. O posicionamento dá a entender que os feedbacks e ajustes ainda estão acontecendo.
Não custa lembrar, a Alexa+ foi anunciada em fevereiro de 2025, diretamente de um evento em Nova York, nos Estados Unidos. Nós estávamos lá e acompanhamos tudo em primeira mão. Na ocasião, executivos da Amazon explicaram que a nova tecnologia utiliza inteligência artificial generativa para dar respostas mais elaboradas.
Em outras palavras, acabou aquilo de pedir para a Alexa criar um timer, acender as luzes ou pular para a música seguinte.
Eu venho testando a Alexa+ desde a chegada (ainda em beta) no Brasil, com bons experimentos em andamento. A gestão de calendários, conectada à conta Google, está muito mais eficiente. Você pede e assistente consegue ajustar compromissos de acordo com o seu contexto.
Além disso, também é possível conversar sobre as condições meteorológicas. Ela diz se vai chover e recomenda peças de roupa.
Outro avanço da Alexa+ é a conversa mais amigável. Não preciso citar o nome da assistente a todo momento. A partir da primeira interação, é possível fazer perguntas ou dar comandos adicionais como se estivesse num bate-papo.
Por outro lado, o uso de IA generativa pode levar a uma demora maior para certas respostas, em especial quando faço perguntas mais elaboradas. A Alexa+ passa mais tempo “pensando” antes de retornar.
A Alexa+ estará inclusa na assinatura do Amazon Prime, que sai a partir de R$ 19,90 por mês. Também será possível assinar somente a assistente por R$ 99 mensais (condição que não faz sentido nenhum, diga-se de passagem).
Por ora, o cadastro se dá de forma voluntária para quem já é assinante do Prime. É preciso ter um dispositivo compatível, como o Echo Show 5, e entrar na fila de espera.
Com a postergação do acesso antecipado para fevereiro, a Amazon nos contou que não tem uma data para o acesso geral à ferramenta, mas disse que planeja “avisar os clientes com antecedência antes da transição”.

articles.title: Enterprise data platforms must get AI pilots into production - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
AI’s production push puts data platforms on the hook for results
Enterprise data platforms must turn AI pilots into measurable business returns while overcoming the data access, sovereignty and cost barriers that stand between experimentation and production.
The conversation is shifting from what AI can do to how companies make it pay off. One data platform provider has responded by folding its post-sales teams under a single leader, giving customers one voice from onboarding through renewal, according to Patricia Bogoevici (pictured), chief customer officer of Cloudera Inc. The mandate now is to align those teams with customers’ business objectives and help them make better use of the technology they have already paid for.
“When I look at things in terms of customers, for me, technology makes sense only when customers are using it,” Bogoevici said. “I am measured on how customers realize value with Cloudera.”
Bogoevici spoke with theCUBE’s Rebecca Knight at Cloudera EVOLVE26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed moving AI into production, improving customer adoption and measuring business value. (* Disclosure below.)
Why enterprise data platforms shape AI’s path to production
The barriers customers face fall into three categories, starting with data access, according to Bogoevici. A study of more than 1,300 information technology specialists found that roughly 80% named data access as the biggest obstacle. Governance and sovereignty come next, because data sits scattered across silos with differing rules on where it can live.
“Not [all] data can be moved to cloud. Not [all] data needs to be in every place,” she said. “It’s about protection, it’s about sovereignty, it’s about on-prem and it’s about air-gap environment.”
The final hurdle is scale. A pilot running on a subset of data rarely shows what a full deployment will cost or return, which leaves total cost of ownership and return on investment unclear, she explained. Cloudera’s answer is Anywhere Cloud, which it plans to release in November, alongside a partnership with Mistral AI SAS that brings open-weight models into the platform.
“It’s one thing to run the pilot in a subset of data,” Bogoevici said. “It’s a completely different thing to run it [at] full scale and understand the results you get from the AI models and understand the value and how you calculate it.”

articles.title: Nvidia store quietly pulls the RTX 5080 following RTX 5090 removal — street prices climb to 2.2X MSRP
articles.text:
Nvidia store quietly pulls the RTX 5080 following RTX 5090 removal — street prices climb to 2.2X MSRP
First, it was the GeForce RTX 5090, and now the GeForce RTX 5080 – two of the best graphics cards have gone dark. After the Blackwell flagship left Nvidia's marketplace, the GeForce RTX 5080 followed suit. Prices for the sub-flagship have exploded to more than 2.2X its original $999 MSRP, and the Blackwell-powered graphics card is slowly going out of stock at various U.S. retailers.
As with the recent disappearance of the GeForce RTX 5090 on Nvidia’s marketplace, the listings and filters for the GeForce RTX 5080 have also disappeared. While its absence does not necessarily mean Nvidia has discontinued the graphics card, it does raise questions about its status and future availability. This move is especially fishy because other Blackwell SKUs, such as the GeForce RTX 5070 Ti and GeForce RTX 5070, remain listed on the marketplace, albeit marked as “Out of Stock.”
The continued presence of the GeForce RTX 5070 Ti and GeForce RTX 5070 suggests that Nvidia wants to keep the products visible even when they are not immediately available so that consumers can anticipate restocks. The complete removal of the GeForce RTX 5090 and GeForce RTX 5080 breaks that pattern. It fuels rumors that Nvidia has allegedly stopped production of the GeForce RTX 5090 and possibly the GeForce RTX 5080 too, in favor of a rumored GeForce RTX 5080 24GB.
Rumors claim Nvidia allegedly stopped producing the GeForce RTX 5090 to repurpose the valuable GB202 silicon into the chipmaker’s RTX Pro Blackwell lineup, which fetches higher margins. This has a lot of credence, since many agree that Nvidia stopped being a gaming hardware vendor long ago and has transformed into an AI provider.
Rather than simply discontinuing the GeForce RTX 5090, Nvidia purportedly intends to introduce the GeForce RTX 5080 24GB as the new flagship gaming graphics card. The thing is, a 24GB variant of the GeForce RTX 5080 would solve one of the biggest consumer gripes with the graphics card: the lack of memory. While a GeForce RTX 5080 24GB would offer the same memory as the GeForce RTX 5090, it simply isn't a direct drop-in replacement. The former has 2X fewer CUDA cores, a substantial performance gap that even a 50% memory increase can't make up for.
How much money are you willing to spend during the Black Friday sales?
The GeForce RTX 5080 launched in January of last year with an MSRP of $999. Demand quickly outpaced supply, and with the rapid price hikes due to the memory shortage, the market price has more than doubled its original MSRP. As of this moment, the most affordable GeForce RTX 5080 in stock, the PNY GeForce RTX 5080 ARGB Epic-X RGB OC, retails for $2,199.99, which is 2.2X over the original launch price.
While some stock remains, it’s selling out fast, and the remaining units will only get more expensive as availability dwindles. At this rate, the GeForce RTX 5080 is unlikely to be available by Black Friday. If you are set on a GeForce RTX 5080, you may have little choice but to act quickly and buy at today's elevated prices.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
If the GeForce RTX 5080 24GB is indeed legitimate, the graphics card will almost certainly debut at a substantial premium over the original GeForce RTX 5080. Although Nvidia maintains that the RTX 5090 is still alive, the reality suggests otherwise. We have contacted the company for comment regarding the GeForce RTX 5080’s status.
