articles.title: Reddit Will Protect its "Extremely Valuable Corpus of Data" from Google's AI Search With Forced Logins
articles.text:
Friday, October 30th 2026
Reddit Will Protect its "Extremely Valuable Corpus of Data" from Google's AI Search With Forced Logins
Since before the advent of AI-powered web search, Google has leaned heavily on Reddit in particular, often with mixed results, and this was, by-and-large, a mutually beneficial relationship, with Google's AI Overview driving traffic to the forum site. However, as of Reddit's latest Q3 2026 financial results, this arrangement appears to be changing. Following the release of the financial results, there was a Q&A session in which Reddit's CEO, Steve Huffman explained that Reddit would be locking its data behind a login requirement in order to protect it from a changing web landscape.
Web search is evolving from a gateway to the web to becoming an AI-powered destination itself. While extraordinarily useful and powerful, AI search solves a different problem than Reddit. AI does not fulfill people's fundamental need for community, connection, and belonging with other people, and it lacks context and nuance... Logged in and app dial are our most valuable users, and they are our primary focus.
The Reddit experience captures the human experience in a way that no other platform can replicate. Only Reddit can help people navigate life's journey through the lens of other people's lived experiences. Only Reddit can help you feel both like a multifaceted, unique individual and a part of a greater whole, and do so without needing to reveal your real-world identity. That's why Reddit is, and always has been, a distinct and direct destination. People seek out Reddit because we meet a universal need they simply can't get anywhere else online. Our work now is about doubling down on what makes Reddit Reddit, and making Reddit more of a daily habit. We come into that work with clear advantages and revenue momentum in the business, and you can see that in the exceptional commercial results we delivered in the third quarter.
Huffman goes on to explain that Reddit has seen an average decline of over a million weekly referrals from search traffic, and he largely attributes this to Google's changing relationship with the web and how it handles search and referrals. Reddit's shift to a logged-in experience will start rolling out in the US, but the platform will also be testing to see if there is any value in a "lite" version of Reddit that does not require a login.
The biggest impact was on logged out and web traffic, but some of the impact flows through to logged in and app traffic, since search referral is a common source of re-engagement for users. The company helped to offset the declines by both driving reach, primarily through user marketing, and also by continuing to improve the product. These declines have continued into the early part of Q4. During October, we have seen that search traffic has dropped by more than 1 million referrals on average per week. If this rate of decline continues, current trends would suggest that total DAUq could fall in Q4 by a low double-digit percentage from our current base of 130 million DAUq. However, search referral trends do not determine our relevancy, and they do not define our future. Logged in and app dial are our most valuable users, and they are our primary focus.
Addressing a question about the driver behind the changes, Huffman explained Reddit's view of the repercussions of Google's push for AI Overviews:
Thanks, Josh. On the change from Google, our hypothesis is twofold. The biggest one is the AI Overviews or AI Mode. Both have evolved a lot, and particularly recently, they appear to be expanding them quite aggressively in the U.S. and outside. What started as a feature is now the full search experience, and at the minimum, it pushes everyone down the search page. Then on top of that, the experiences themselves are not traffic drivers. These things combined with the rollout just means Google has really shifted in their relationship with the rest of the internet. There is a second factor, which we believe our machine translation content is also being ranked lower. This primarily would affect us outside the U.S.
Sources:
				Reddit Investors, 				via PC Gamer, 				via Stock Analytics

Meanwhile, people from my VR days reach out to people from my Steam just to contact me on my Steam.
Anyone else find it more than a little weird that we can never seem to have a peaceable ecosystem for chat?
Forums aren't exactly the best but it feels like this is the only thing that hasn't really changed.
OpenAI probably wants all the data just for them, while Reddit itself would like you to sign in just like on social media platforms
But Discord has to be one of the worst, if not the worst ways of getting any information, there isn't any good way to archive or search for results.
Huffman's reaction seems childish, he can' t stop google or others from indexing reddit content because it's public.
That being said this is not a a good thing if more and more websites allow people to see their content only with account.
Theyre just going to lock people out of their site and slowly turtle it into the ground. Which theyre already doing, to be fair, this just accelerates it.

articles.title: You can get up to $350 off the Pixel 11 series at Amazon today — I'd be surprised if this record-low is beaten over Black Friday
articles.text:
The Google Pixel 11 series just hit a record-low price ahead of Black Friday — and I'd be surprised if it gets cheaper
You can get up to $350 off an unlocked device
We're seeing the first round of 'early' Black Friday deals this week as retailers look to ease into the end-of-year madness. Both Amazon and Best Buy have some genuinely worthwhile listings right now, but a real highlight is the Google Pixel 11 for $699 (was $899).
This is a record-low price for Google's latest flagship, which is only a few months of as of writing. Up until now, we've seen $100 discounts and the usual trade-in rebates, but today's discount is arguably a Black Friday-quality deal if you're looking for a cheap(er) unlocked device.
I would be surprised if the device got any cheaper than this over November too, considering the Pixel 11 range came out back in late August this year. The Pixel 11 is definitely a real bargain at this price, considering it's packing the latest Tensor chipset, more RAM, and a few new eye-catching shades.
If you'd prefer a higher-end device, then you can also get the Pixel 11 Pro for $799 (was $1,099) and the Pixel 11 Pro XL for $949 (was $1,299), which are again record-low prices for either device. All these deals are also available at Best Buy today for the same price.
New record-low Google Pixel 11 deal at Amazon
We've been waiting for a decent price cut on the Google Pixel 11 — and here it is, finally. Available right now is a healthy $200 price cut across all color variations, which is a fantastic discount on this expensive device. The higher price was one of our main complaints about the Pixel 11, so this makes it an easy recommendation, considering you get the very latest chipset in this device, plus the interesting new HiLight feature.
What's new with the Google Pixel 11 series?
The Google Pixel 11 is definitely more of an iterative upgrade than some previous generations, but it's still an excellent option if you're looking for a flagship device that doesn't break the bank.
All devices in the range feature the Tensor G6 chip, plus 12GB of RAM, which should aid with both performance and efficiency. The standard Pixel 11 gets a larger 48MP main camera sensor, while the Pro devices get a 50MP main, 48MP ultrawide and 48MP telephoto cameras, with zoom extending to an ambitious 120x, assisted by AI processing. The Pro devices also get the new HiLight feature, which is an LED array around the flash that can glow in different colours.
If you'd like to read more about the Pixel 11 series, I'd recommend checking out our Google Pixel 11 Pro review and Google Pixel 11 Pro XL review pages.

articles.title: Hemos normalizado el uso del móvil en los estadios de fútbol. En Alemania, Vodafone está consiguiendo lo contrario
articles.text:
Hace tiempo que el móvil se convirtió en una extensión de nuestro cuerpo hasta el punto de que, en muchas ocasiones, vivimos las experiencias a través de su pantalla en vez de verlas con nuestros propios ojos. Si no sabéis a lo que me refiero, echad un vistazo a vuestro alrededor en un concierto o en cualquier otro tipo de espectáculo.
Fijaos, por ejemplo, qué hacen los aficionados en campo de fútbol cuando su equipo va a lanzar un penalti. O cuando va a levantar el trofeo de campeón (de la Champions, del Mundial o de lo que sea). Miles de teléfonos se alzan para capturar ese instante y compartirlo inmediatamente en redes sociales en lugar de disfrutar del momento.
Y eso es precisamente lo que se ha propuesto evitar el Borussia Dortmund en colaboración con Vodafone, su patrocinador. Para ello, el equipo alemán ha lanzado una solución que recompensa a los aficionados que no usen el móvil durante los partidos.
Camiseta, bufanda... y móvil. Qué tiempos aquellos cuando íbamos al estadio a animar a nuestro equipo. Hoy en día, gran cantidad de aficionados están más pendientes del móvil que de lo que sucede en el terreno de juego.
En 2023, Vodafone realizó una encuesta a mil personas que asisten habitualmente a los estadios y el 63% de ellos reconoció usar su teléfono regularmente durante los partidos. Hablamos de casi dos tercios de los aficionados y ese porcentaje ha aumentado aún más en los últimos años.
'Detox' digital en el fútbol. Utilizar constantemente en teléfono en el estadio no sólo provoca que los aficionados se pierdan goles y jugadas, sino que reduce la animación de la grada. Por eso, el Borussia Dortmund y Vodafone han decidido tomar cartas en el asunto.
Su solución ha sido incorporar el nuevo 'Fan Mode' (modo fan) en la aplicación oficial 'BVB' del club germano. Es una función que, básicamente, anima a dejar el móvil en el bolsillo durante los partidos en el Signal Iduna Park, el estadio del Borussia Dortmund. ¿Cómo? Con recompensas por usarlo, claro.
Ponte en 'Modo Fan' para ganar. Cuando vaya a empezar el partido, el usuario debe activar el nuevo modo 'Fan' dentro de la app 'BVB' y bloquear la pantalla del móvil. Mientras la pantalla permanezca bloqueada, irá sumando puntos, de manera que, cuantas menos veces desbloquees tu móvil durante el encuentro, más puntos ganarás.
En el descanso, está permitido usar el teléfono, pero cuando arranque la segunda parte, hay que volver al 'Fan Mode' para seguir acumulando puntos hasta el pitido final. Después, puedes canjearlos por tarjetas regalo para la tienda del club o por camisetas firmadas por los jugadores.
Todo un éxito. El 'Modo Fan' se utilizó por primera vez durante el partido en casa contra el Eintracht Frankfurt y ha tenido tan buena acogida que el club tiene previsto utilizarlo en todos los encuentros que el Borussia Dortmund dispute en su estadio.
La idea, según Carsten Cramer, CEO del Borussia Dortmund, es "proteger una experiencia que ninguna tecnología puede reemplazar. Más de 81.000 personas en el estadio, cantando, animando y conteniendo la respiración juntos". Muchas veces la tecnología debe pasar a un segundo plano, y no hay duda de que el deporte en directo es una de ellas. ¿No estáis de acuerdo?

articles.title: Qué es la dirección IP, cómo encontrarla y por qué es importante para navegar por internet
articles.text:
Cada vez que una persona ingresa a una página web, utiliza una aplicación o conecta su celular a una red Wi-Fi, su dispositivo necesita identificarse para intercambiar información. En ese proceso interviene la dirección IP, un número que permite reconocer a los equipos dentro de una red y hacer posible la comunicación a través de internet.
Aunque suele pasar desapercibida, esta identificación digital cumple una función fundamental en la navegación cotidiana. También puede resultar útil cuando una conexión presenta fallas, se necesita configurar una impresora o cámara de seguridad, o se quiere comprobar si una red privada virtual (VPN) está ocultando la dirección habitual.
Conocer la dirección IP no requiere instalar programas ni tener conocimientos avanzados de informática. Existen herramientas gratuitas en internet que permiten consultar la dirección pública, mientras que la dirección privada puede encontrarse directamente desde la configuración de una computadora o un teléfono.
¿Qué es una dirección IP y para qué sirve?
La dirección IP, sigla de Internet Protocol (protocolo de internet), es una identificación numérica asignada a un dispositivo cuando se conecta a una red. Su función consiste en permitir que los equipos envíen y reciban información, de manera que los datos puedan llegar al destino correcto.
Por ejemplo, cuando una persona abre una página web desde su celular, la conexión utiliza direcciones IP para identificar los dispositivos y servidores que intervienen en el intercambio de información.
Existen dos tipos principales de direcciones IP:
- Dirección IP pública: es la identificación con la que una conexión o red se comunica con internet. Los sitios web pueden verla cuando una persona los visita.
- Dirección IP privada: identifica a los dispositivos dentro de una red local, como la que se utiliza en una casa u oficina. Permite que una computadora, un celular y una impresora puedan comunicarse entre sí.
Además, existen dos versiones principales de este protocolo. IPv4 utiliza direcciones numéricas de cuatro bloques, mientras que IPv6 incorpora una estructura más extensa para permitir una mayor cantidad de identificaciones.
Cómo encontrar tu dirección IP pública
Consultar la dirección IP pública es un procedimiento sencillo que puede realizarse desde cualquier dispositivo con acceso a internet.
Una alternativa consiste en abrir un navegador y escribir en el buscador la pregunta “¿Cuál es mi dirección IP?“. En algunos casos, Google muestra directamente el número en la parte superior de los resultados.
También existen páginas especializadas que identifican automáticamente la dirección pública de la conexión. Al ingresar a una de estas herramientas, el sistema muestra la IP y permite conocer si corresponde al protocolo IPv4 o IPv6.
Esta consulta puede realizarse desde una computadora, una tablet o un teléfono celular, sin necesidad de descargar aplicaciones.
Cómo encontrar la dirección IP privada en Windows, Mac y celulares
A diferencia de la dirección pública, la IP privada se consulta desde los ajustes de red del dispositivo. Los pasos cambian según el sistema operativo.
En Windows: hay que ingresar al menú Inicio, abrir Configuración y seleccionar Red e Internet. Después, se debe elegir la conexión Wi-Fi o Ethernet y revisar sus detalles para encontrar la dirección IPv4. Otra opción es abrir el símbolo del sistema, escribir ipconfig y presionar Enter.
En Mac: se debe ingresar a Configuración del Sistema, seleccionar Red y elegir la conexión utilizada, ya sea Wi-Fi o Ethernet. En los detalles aparecerá la dirección IP asignada al equipo.
En Android: hay que abrir Configuración, ingresar a los ajustes de Wi-Fi y seleccionar la red a la que está conectado el teléfono. En sus detalles se encuentra la dirección IP. La ubicación exacta de esta opción puede variar según el fabricante y la versión del sistema operativo.
En iPhone o iPad: se debe abrir Configuración, ingresar a Wi-Fi y tocar el ícono de información que aparece junto al nombre de la red. Allí se puede consultar la dirección IPv4.
Por qué es importante conocer tu dirección IP
Saber cuál es la dirección IP puede resultar útil en diferentes situaciones. Una de las más habituales es solucionar problemas de conexión. Cuando internet presenta interrupciones o funciona con lentitud, esta información permite realizar comprobaciones y facilitar el diagnóstico de posibles errores de red.
También es necesaria para conectar determinados dispositivos, como impresoras, cámaras de seguridad o equipos que funcionan dentro de una misma red local. En estos casos, conocer la IP privada ayuda a configurar correctamente la comunicación entre los aparatos.
Otra utilidad está relacionada con las VPN. Estas herramientas permiten establecer una conexión cifrada y mostrar una dirección IP pública diferente de la habitual. Consultarla antes y después de activar el servicio permite comprobar si el cambio se realizó correctamente.
Por último, algunas aplicaciones de acceso remoto necesitan conocer la dirección IP para establecer una conexión con una computadora o una red desde otra ubicación.
¿Alguien puede rastrear tu dirección IP?
La dirección IP pública puede revelar información aproximada sobre la conexión, como el país, la región o la ciudad desde donde se accede a internet. También puede ofrecer datos sobre el proveedor de servicios de internet.
Sin embargo, esto no significa que cualquier persona pueda conocer la ubicación exacta de un usuario mediante ese número. Las herramientas de geolocalización de IP utilizan bases de datos que ofrecen estimaciones, pero no permiten identificar necesariamente una vivienda o la ubicación física precisa de un dispositivo.
Por eso, aunque la dirección IP es necesaria para navegar por internet, conviene conocer qué información puede revelar y utilizar herramientas de protección de la privacidad cuando sea necesario.

articles.title: This art festival reveals why the creative economy is as much about audiences as creators
articles.text:
This art festival reveals why the creative economy is as much about audiences as creators
In this photo essay, we showcase more highlights from the Contemporary Now arts festival in Chennai, along with director insights.
Launched in 2014, PhotoSparks is a weekly feature from YourStory, with photographs that celebrate the spirit of creativity and innovation. In the earlier 1,025 posts, we featured an art festival, cartoon gallery. world music festival, telecom expo, millets fair, climate change expo, wildlife conference, startup festival, Diwali rangoli, and jazz festival.
Chennai recently hosted the third edition of the art festival 'Contemporary Now', with collaboration from art galleries of Kolkata, Ahmedabad, New Delhi, and Mumbai as well. A diverse range of artworks was exhibited in 10 venues across the city, as shown in this photo essay.
The artist lineup included Ashwini Bhat, Prajakta Potnis, Khageswar Rout, Amitesh Shrivastava, Sandeep Mukherjee, Saju Kunhan, Pratap Morey, Benitha Perciyal, Natasha Preenja, and many others.
“Now is a good time to be in art. Aspiring artists as well as audiences today are much more connected to art, thanks to social media,” mixed-media artist Benitha Perciyal tells YourStory.
Earlier, art catalogues and visits to a few galleries were the only available options. “You had to simply wait to get access and exposure, or travel to other cities, which was quite expensive,” she recalls.
“Today, online access is immediate and global. But at the same time, too much online exposure can be confusing or intimidating,” she cautions.
Digital platforms and AI make things much easier and faster now for art. “But it also takes away from the satisfaction of finding or creating something after a lot of effort,” Perciyal says.
The art festival’s directors are Ashvin Rajagopalan and Priyanjoli Basu. Both express satisfaction with the event’s achievements for the art community of Chennai and beyond.
“We had collectors who usually have not come out much, but engaged with us at the festival. We had many art fans and students who could see what was happening in the rest of the country thanks to our institutional partners in other cities,” Rajagopalan says.
There are plans to have more editions of the festival. “We may end up having two or three editions of Contemporary Now. One, of course, in Chennai, but others could be in Ahmedabad, Baroda or Shantiniketan,” he adds.
“The festival’s level of contemporary artwork has probably not been shown in Chennai earlier. A lot of feedback I got was that there are major art events in Delhi and Mumbai but not as much in Chennai,” Basu observes.
The art community felt this event should happen more often in Chennai. “It should not be a once-a-year thing. The displayed artworks should be shown elsewhere also, to continue the conversation,” she adds.
As trends in the art market in India today, she points to more appreciation of art about politics, gender and climate change. “People are trying to engage with a new narrative, a new trend. The works of a lot of young women artists are also being collected,” Basu says.
“Many contemporary artists have been responding to what is happening around the world. Art collectors are also responding to such art because it makes them feel something and moves them. Knowledgeable collectors are able to find more artists making such work,” Rajagopalan adds.
Both directors see a growing importance for the role of art today, as well as a need for more art appreciation in society. “Artists voice the world’s uncertainty and conflict for us. Engaging with such art reflects your concern about such issues,” Rajagopalan says.
Basu calls on audiences to discuss art with people they meet, attend art events, and visit art galleries. “When you go on holiday, make sure you see a city’s art galleries also,” she suggests.
“And of course, if you are traveling abroad, it is very important to go and see their museums. That is how we can improve art appreciation and knowledge of art right here in India,” Basu signs off.
Now what have you done today to pause in your busy schedule and harness your creative side for a better world?
(All photographs taken by Madanmohan Rao on location at 'Contemporary Now' venues in Chennai.)

articles.title: Boulanger avance le Black Friday : le Dyson V16 Piston Animal passe à -23%
articles.text:
Boulanger affiche déjà « C’est parti pour le Black Friday », près d’un mois avant le 27 novembre. Voici donc le Dyson V16 Piston Animal, pensé pour les poils d’animaux, qui passe à 649 € au lieu de 849 € : très puissant sur le papier, mais lourd, mais pas encore testé par nos soins.
Le Dyson V16 Piston Animal est, sur le papier, l’aspirateur balai sans fil le plus puissant de la marque, avec 315 AW annoncés, et sa brosse a été conçue pour les poils d’animaux. Boulanger a lancé son Black Friday avec près d’un mois d’avance, et le V16 Piston Animal y passe à 649 € au lieu de 849 €, soit 200 € de moins que chez Amazon, Cdiscount et Darty, selon notre relevé de ce matin. C’est aussi 50 € sous le tarif de 699 € auquel nous l’avions relayé pendant les soldes d’été.
L’offre parle d’abord aux foyers avec un chien ou un chat, et aux logements où tapis et moquettes occupent une bonne place. Pour un petit appartement aux sols durs, son poids et son prix restent difficiles à justifier.
Black Friday avant l’heure chez Boulanger : le Dyson V16 Piston Animal passe à 649 € au lieu de 849 €, vendu en neuf par l’enseigne, hors place de marché.
Pourquoi choisir le Dyson V16 Piston Animal ?
- Une brosse qui ne s’emmêle pas : Ses deux rouleaux coniques démêlent poils et cheveux pour les envoyer vers le collecteur, au lieu de les laisser s’enrouler. Vous évitez la corvée des ciseaux sur la brosse, surtout avec un animal à poils longs.
- De la réserve pour les tapis : Avec 315 AW annoncés, il dépasse les 280 AW du Gen5 Detect et les 240 AW du V15 Detect. Cette puissance vise d’abord les moquettes et les tapis épais, où la poussière et les poils s’incrustent.
- Un collecteur qu’on vide moins souvent : Un piston compacte la poussière dans le collecteur de 1,3 litre à mesure que vous aspirez. Les vidages s’espacent, ce qui compte quand un animal perd ses poils toute l’année.
Chien, chat, moquettes : là où il a sa place
Dyson annonce jusqu’à 70 minutes d’autonomie. Quand nous l’avions relayé cet été, nous indiquions 63 minutes en mode Eco et seulement 16 minutes en mode Boost : assez pour un tapis encrassé, pas pour toute la maison à pleine puissance. Les brosses se détachent d’une simple pression sur un bouton, et plusieurs accessoires sont fournis. Dyson promet aussi une filtration qui retient 99,9 % des particules jusqu’à 0,1 micron, un argument si vous êtes sensible à la poussière.
Il s’adresse surtout aux grands logements et aux foyers où un animal laisse des poils partout. Il convient moins à un studio ou à un intérieur sans tapis : avec 3,4 kg, il pèse nettement plus qu’un balai d’entrée de gamme. Nous avions aussi noté qu’il peine à passer sous les meubles et dans certains coins. Enfin, il faut l’associer à l’application MyDyson avant de s’en servir, une application qui se contente d’un résumé peu utile.
Face au Shark PowerDetect et au Dyson V15 Detect
Dans notre comparatif des meilleurs aspirateurs balais, la première place revient au Shark PowerDetect Clean & Empty, dont la station vide le bac à votre place, et Dyson n’y figure qu’avec le V15 Detect Absolute, à 240 AW et 3,1 kg. Le V16 Piston Animal apporte davantage de puissance et un collecteur de 1,3 litre, contre 0,76 litre pour le V15. Il ne supprime pas les vidages, il les espace. Si la légèreté prime, le Dreame V20 Pro, à 1,6 kg sans accessoire, reste plus maniable.
✅ Les points forts
- 315 AW annoncés, au-dessus du Gen5 Detect et du V15 Detect
- Brosse à rouleaux coniques qui démêle les poils
- Collecteur de 1,3 litre avec compactage de la poussière
- Brosses interchangeables d’une pression sur un bouton
❌ Les limites
- 3,4 kg, un poids sensible sur les longues séances
- Environ 16 minutes seulement en mode Boost
- Peine à passer sous les meubles et dans certains coins
- Application MyDyson obligatoire et peu utile
Relevé ce matin à 649 € chez Boulanger, ce prix de Black Friday avant l’heure peut encore bouger d’ici le 27 novembre.
À 649 €, le Dyson V16 Piston Animal ne devient pas un achat léger, mais il n’a pas attendu le Black Friday pour perdre 200 €. Une nouvelle baisse d’ici le 27 novembre n’est pas exclue, et l’écart rend déjà ce Dyson plus défendable. Nous ne l’avons pas encore testé nous-mêmes : les constats d’usage ci-dessus viennent de la fiche du constructeur et de nos précédents articles.
L’achat se justifie si vous vivez avec un animal qui perd ses poils et que tapis ou moquettes couvrent une partie de vos sols. Si vous cherchez un balai léger pour un petit appartement, un modèle comme le Dreame V20 Pro sera plus agréable à manier. Et si vider le bac vous rebute, une station d’autovidage comme celle du Shark sera plus confortable au quotidien.

articles.title: Intel’s woes wipe out $1 trillion of semiconductor market cap in one day — PC market bloodbath leaves few chip stocks unscathed
articles.text:
Intel’s woes wipe out $1 trillion of semiconductor market cap in one day — PC market bloodbath leaves few chip stocks unscathed
$1 trillion in semiconductor market capitalization wiped out.
Intel's shares plunged 30% on Friday, wiping out nearly $150 billion in market capitalization in a single day, the largest single-day loss in the company's history. The decline followed a disappointing financial outlook, largely driven by an anticipated drop of more than 20% in sales at Intel's client computing group (CCPG), the company's main cash cow. The declines quickly spread across the semiconductor industry. Although losses elsewhere were nowhere near as severe as Intel's, approximately $1 trillion in semiconductor market capitalization was wiped out on Friday, according to intraday estimates by Benzinga.
Fire sale
The PHLX Semiconductor Sector Index (SOX), which tracks the stock performance of 30 major semiconductor companies, is one of the key indicators of the industry's financial health. On Friday, the index plunged 9.14%, or 1,052.82 points, to 10,465.38 points as of 2:31 PM ET, as Intel's disappointing outlook triggered a massive selloff across the semiconductor industry.
Intel was by far the biggest loser, as other chip-related stocks, while Arm (-12.68%), AMD (-12.48%), Qualcomm (-12.14%), Applied Materials (-8.73%), ASML (-8.13%), Lam Research (-8%), Micron (-7.28%), and Broadcom (-7.1%) suffered considerably less. Then again, while Nvidia lost 5.66% of its market cap, this translates to around $270 billion, which is a massive amount of money. Paradoxically, Nvidia lost more market capitalization in absolute dollar terms than Intel.
In an unexpected turn of events, the downturn extended to server manufacturers and cloud giants too, as Dell (-12.67%), HPE (-8.10%), Supermicro (-6.96%), and Oracle (-6.88%) lost nearly 7% to 13% of their value. Reuters noted that investors increasingly question the scale of capital investments required to expand AI infrastructure as well as the sustainability of that spending.
Gloomy outlook
Intel’s client computing and physical AI group (CCPG) generated $8.1 billion in revenue during Q3 2026, down 5% year-over-year and 9% sequentially. Weaker demand and increased competition reduced client processor shipments by 14% year-over-year, which was partially offset by a 9% increase in average selling prices. CCPG accounted for nearly half of Intel's revenue of around $16.5 billion and the company's main source of cash. As strong demand for server processors only partially offsets declining client sales, Intel guided its Q4 revenue to be between $15 billion and $16 billion.
Intel expects the client market to deteriorate further in Q4 2026 and into 2027 as elevated memory prices and shortages of other components impact PC prices and demand. In general, Intel expects the client PC market to decline 10% in 2027 compared to 2026, which will inevitably have an effect on CCPG performance. While Intel expects its data center business to continue growing in 2027, industry-wide supply constraints will limit its ability to fully capitalize on demand.
2026 has been a mixed bag for Intel so far. On the one hand, the company achieved its highest market capitalization ever — $673.43 billion in mid-June — on growing sales of data center CPUs, strong sales of client products, and a return to profitability (if the $12.5 billion non-cash accounting charge associated with shares issued to the U.S. government is excluded). On the other hand, the company's capitalization has dropped by nearly 50% to $338.91 billion since mid-June (with $148.68 billion in just one day), as investors began to realize that the performance of Intel's CCPG heavily depends on memory prices, as customers and businesses tend not to like overpriced systems. Yet on the other hand, now that Intel sells fewer client processors, it can sell more expensive data center CPUs.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
What about Apple?
Surprisingly, Apple (-1.66%), which only sells client products, was nearly unaffected by the performance of Intel's client computing group, as investors probably believe that the world's largest supplier of consumer electronics is more immune to memory prices than Intel. Ironically, if we count the A-series SoCs used in iPhones (which tend to outperform mainstream laptop CPUs), Apple sells substantially more processors than Intel, making Apple by far the world's largest supplier of microprocessors. Despite this, Apple's shares were largely unaffected by the semiconductor selloff.
There are several reasons for this distinction. Firstly, Apple's business model is fundamentally different. Intel sells processors to PC manufacturers, whereas Apple designs its own processors and sells them as part of finished products. Consequently, Apple captures revenue from the entire device rather than just the processor. Secondly, the two companies face different demand dynamics. Intel depends heavily on the PC market, while Apple's iPhone business follows the smartphone replacement cycle. Rising memory prices could affect both, but not necessarily to the same extent and at the same time.
There is an additional irony: Apple is also a major customer of TSMC, so its processor supply chain overlaps with those of AMD, Intel, and other semiconductor companies whose shares declined sharply.
While we should not directly compare Apple and Intel, the comparison illustrates that investors were not necessarily abandoning companies that design or use semiconductors, but were rather concerned about the profitability and growth prospects of these high-tech companies. And if we take a look at the situation from this point of view, the whole thing will start looking completely different.

Anton Shilov is a contributing writer at Tom’s Hardware. Over the past couple of decades, he has covered everything from CPUs and GPUs to supercomputers and from modern process technologies and latest fab tools to high-tech industry trends.

articles.title: Corea del Norte se ha convertido en una superpotencia del ciberataque y lo está utilizando para autofinanciarse
articles.text:
Es uno de los países más aislados y herméticos del planeta. Su comercio exterior se limita a unos pocos países afines, arrastra sanciones desde hace años y casi nadie sabe qué ocurre realmente más allá de las fronteras. Aun así, Corea del Norte se ha revelado como una auténtica superpotencia en el cibercrimen.
Aunque todavía no se puede confirmar de forma oficial, algunos indicios y coincidencias apuntan Pyongyang podría estar tras el incidente de ciberseguridad que esta madrugada ha hecho desaparecer unos 6.360 millones de dólares de las carteras de Binance. No es el primer ataque de este estilo que se atribuye a grupos de ciberdelincuentes altamente especializados que actúan a las órdenes de Corea del Norte.
Binance, un robo récord con firma conocida. El impacto total del golpe a Binance se calcula cercano a los 6.300 millones de dólares, y podría haber sido mayor si no fuera porque la mitad quedó congelada. Tether bloqueó unos 1.600 millones y Circle más de 800 millones en USDC. Esta cifra cuadruplica la del anterior récord en el robo de criptomonedas: el de Bybit de 2025 en el que se esfumaron unos 1.500 millones de dólares en criptodivisas.
La firma de ciberseguridad TRM Labs tiene "alta confianza" en que el autor del robo es TraderTraitor, un grupo vinculado a la red de ciberdelincuentes Lazarus. Según TRM LAbs, "varias características de este ataque coinciden con robos anteriores vinculados a Corea del Norte". Otros investigadores apuntan en la misma dirección. Conviene ir con cautela ya que la atribución es todavía preliminar y el FBI no se ha pronunciado oficialmente al respecto.
Bybit y un régimen que cobra en cripto. Sin embargo, el precedente más reciente es Bybit. En febrero de 2025 se esfumaron 1.500 millones de dólares en Ether, y el FBI lo atribuyó a Corea del Norte días después. Los ladrones repartieron parte del botín obtenido entre miles de direcciones de varias cadenas de bloques para blanquearlo. Los investigadores han vinculado el ataque de Bybit con el de Binance porque algunas de las direcciones que se han utilizado en este último golpe, también se usaron en el de 2025.
Chainalysis calculó que los hackers vinculados al régimen habían robado unos 2.020 millones de dólares en criptodivisas solo en 2025, un 51% más que el año anterior y el mayor total registrado. El acumulado histórico llegaba a los 6.750 millones de dólares. Washington ya acusó en 2021 a tres programadores militares de robar 1.300 millones.
Cifrado poscuántico para esconder su rastro. Kaspersky documentó en una investigación la Operación FlashHole, activa desde al menos julio de 2025 y dirigida a empresas surcoreanas de software, construcción y telecomunicaciones. Los atacantes usaron un currículum falso con una foto probablemente creada con IA. Una artimaña bastante sencilla que sirve como señuelo para ataques Phishing. Sin embargo, la novedad es una herramienta de Lazarus que protege la descarga de nuevos programas con ML-KEM-1024, un algoritmo poscuántico.
Sojun Ryu, investigador de Kaspersky, dijo a El País que esta tecnología "se considera la criptografía del futuro, está diseñada para seguir siendo segura contra computadoras cuánticas". ML-KEM es uno de los tres estándares que NIST finalizó en agosto de 2024. Ningún ordenador cuántico conocido rompe aún el cifrado actual, así que Lazarus se cubre de un riesgo futuro. Para Ryu, eso revela que los ciberdelincuentes en nómina de Pyongyang tienen un nivel de conocimientos y especialización muy avanzado, y utilizan las tecnologías más vanguardistas para "que sus cargas maliciosas no queden expuestas ante defensores o investigadores".
El dinero tiene destino. La directora de Inteligencia Nacional de EE UU, Tulsi Gabbard, dijo ante el Congreso que esos robos ayudan a financiar al régimen de Kim Jong-un y a su programa de armas estratégicas. Un informe de la ONU de 2024 calculó que el robo de criptomonedas podía aportar hasta la mitad de las divisas que recibe el país.
Sin embargo, Corea del Norte cuenta con otra fuente de ingresos de divisas mucho más discreta: el teletrabajo. Informáticos norcoreanos consiguen empleo remoto con identidades robadas y usan portátiles de la empresa alojados en casas de cómplices en EEUU, las llamadas "granjas de portátiles". El Departamento de Justicia detalló un esquema que afectó a más de 70 empresas y generó unos 3 millones de dólares. En Texas, el FBI registró más de 40 viviendas y se incautó de unos 187 dispositivos.

articles.title: Chips para notebooks baratos estão esgotados, revela Intel • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Chips para notebooks baratos estão esgotados, revela Intel
Intel afirma que escassez de memória não deve melhorar ao longo de 2027.
A Intel afirma ter esgotado a oferta dos processadores da linha Wildcat Lake, voltados principalmente a notebooks de custo intermediário com fichas técnicas mais avançadas. A demanda pela linha, lançada como Core Série 3, aumentou com a tentativa das fabricantes de compensar a alta nos preços das memórias.
A situação foi comentada por executivos durante a apresentação de resultados financeiros da Intel. O diretor financeiro David Zinsner afirmou que a Intel registrou um crescimento significativo na procura por estes chips para colocar em notebooks que não precisam dos componentes mais avançados.
Alguns modelos com o chip também adotam apenas 8 GB de memória RAM, configuração que reduz custos, mas pode limitar o desempenho, segundo o The Verge.
Wildcat Lake é o codinome dos Intel Core Série 3, apresentados pela fabricante como uma opção para notebooks de custo intermediário. Eles ficam abaixo dos Core Ultra Série 3, voltados a máquinas mais avançadas, e usam o processo de fabricação Intel 18A. Os modelos têm cinco ou seis núcleos de CPU, gráficos integrados e NPU de até 17 TOPS.
Alguns notebooks com esses processadores estão no Brasil, como o Dell XPS 13, com preço sugerido de R$ 8.999, e o IdeaPad Slim 3i, que sai a partir de R$ 4.399,99. Ambos carregam o Intel Core 5 320 por dentro.
O aumento da procura pelos processadores intermediários ocorre em meio à escassez de memórias que afeta a indústria de computadores. Questionado sobre o fornecimento dos componentes, Zinsner afirmou que a Intel não espera uma melhora significativa no próximo ano.
“Teremos que ver em 2028 se as coisas melhoram, mas nossa expectativa é que isso não melhore em 2027”, afirmou. Fornecedoras de chips de memória têm revelado que a capacidade produtiva para os próximos anos já está sendo vendida. A SK Hynix, por exemplo, anunciou nesta semana que esgotou os lotes esperados até 2029. A companhia sul-coreana espera que o desequilíbrio siga até 2030.
Lip-Bu Tan relacionou a escassez à forte demanda por infraestrutura de inteligência artificial, que absorve uma parcela crescente da produção de componentes.
Segundo o CEO, a indústria enfrenta “uma das faltas de componentes mais significativas da história”, impulsionada pelos investimentos em infraestrutura para IA.

articles.title: Agentic AI helps Prosper Global speed crisis research - SiliconANGLE A
articles.text:
AI agents cut critical research time for humanitarian teams in conflict zones
Humanitarian groups working in conflict zones are finding that agentic AI can shorten the research cycle between a crisis and an informed response.
Cloudera Inc. has built its AI strategy around deployment flexibility, and one nonprofit partner is testing that approach on the front lines. But the aim is to give analysts a faster starting point, not to automate research, according to Aaron Eubank (pictured), director of data science at Prosper Global, formerly Mercy Corps.
“It’s not the final report that’s going to be pushed out to the humanitarian community and teams, but rather a starting point that analysts can use to continue to iterate on their own research,” Eubank said. “We want to keep the agency in the hands of the researchers themselves.”
Eubank spoke with theCUBE’s Rebecca Knight and Paul Gillin at EVOLVE26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how multi-agent AI is accelerating humanitarian research, VERA’s early results in conflict zones and the importance of keeping researchers in control. (* Disclosure below.)
Agentic AI meets the humanitarian fog of war
Prosper Global works in about 30 countries with communities facing conflict, climate change and economic hardship. Its crisis analysts’ research could take days to weeks, so the organization built VERA with Cloudera, a multi-agent research engine that uses Cloudera AI Studios, runs on Amazon Web Services Inc. and taps models from Anthropic PBC. Agents pull from sources such as ReliefWeb, conflict tracker ACLED and local news, and a final agent assembles the findings, Eubank explained.
“Agents allow us to really kind of tailor the process for how this research is done,” Eubank said. “Then it will allow us to then add further resources in the future and really have a curated research process that we wouldn’t have had with some of the earlier iterations of generative AI.”
In Sudan, VERA cut desk research for an agricultural report from five or six days to two, saving about $1,500, Eubank noted. In Colombia, an employee with no security background produced an election security report in a few hours. VERA, launched in June, also runs in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Ukraine.
“The risks and the contexts are different in each place that we work,” Eubank said. “It’s important to really take a measured and slow approach as we go through that.”

articles.title: 'It’s 100 percent a national security threat': Accenture contractor connected an AI agent to the Pentagon’s secure network, and then sent data to a high-risk website
articles.text:
'It’s 100 percent a national security threat': Accenture contractor connected an AI agent to the Pentagon’s secure network, and then sent data to a high-risk website
Stop giving AI agents your credentials
- An AI agent was connected to a secure internal Defense Department network
- The agent was given login details to allow it to perform coding tasks, but also allowed it to bypass security controls
- The agent sent sensitive information, including the credentials, to a high-risk third party website
An Accenture contractor at the Department of Defense is in hot water over an AI agent that was given access to the Pentagon’s secure internal network.
The Claude Code agent then collected data from the network - which is used by multiple intelligence agencies - and sent it to a third-party website.
Login credentials were confirmed to have been leaked by the agent, with other controlled unclassified information potentially put at risk.
Don’t connect unauthorized agents to secure networks
According to a source familiar with the matter who spoke to Wired, “It puts all the data that’s in there at risk. There could be somebody out there with the ability to log into a secure environment without anyone knowing,” the source said.
“It’s 100 percent a national security threat and could cause irreparable harm.”
Despite Claude currently being banned from use for Defense Department staff due to Anthropic's supply chain risk designation, the Accenture employee is alleged to have given their personal Claude account access to a secure production environment in order to write and deploy code.
For two months, the AI agent had access to the secure internal network before the risk was identified and patched - but sources say once the connection was discovered it was not treated as severe or urgent by Accenture employees.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The contractor is alleged to have given the AI agent login credentials to the DoD’s Non-classified Internet Protocol Router Network (NIPRNet) in order to allow it to write code. But in order to function properly, the AI agent also needed the internet to perform its tasks.
The login credentials give the AI agent the ability to bypass the security controls enforced by the login process, and the AI agent then sent the credentials and a map of NIPRNet to a third party website.
“We are in a conflict with Iran right now,” the source added. “It’s the worst time to be having this kind of cavalier attitude.”
Both employees and contractors for the DoD are required to report any cybersecurity incidents within 72 hours, but according to the source, the Accenture employee did not raise the alarm.
“The Department does not comment on the status of its networks or systems,” the DoD told Wired.
“We take all concerns seriously. These allegations were thoroughly and independently investigated and found to be without merit. We fully complied with our legal and contractual obligations,” an Accenture spokesperson said.

Benedict provides detailed analysis on state-sponsored threat actors, APT groups, and the protection of critical national infrastructure, with his reporting bridging the gap between technical threat intelligence and B2B security strategy.

articles.title: Pile-ins, payouts, and pacing pressure: the investors behind the VCs open up | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The limited partners who provide the capital to venture firms — the “money behind the money” — are feeling great right now. They’re in uncharted territory in many ways, but also potentially exceedingly lucrative territory.
Normally, LPs typically spread their bets across many firms to diversify their own portfolios. They write checks to emerging managers and established ones, to generalist firms and specialists. The goal is a strong return, but also to minimize risk.
That’s the typical playbook. But typical is out the window. OpenAI and Anthropic’s valuations have shot up so quickly that nearly everyone has piled into the same two companies on the way up, often inside the same venture firm, despite the longstanding venture convention of avoiding investments that conflict with one another. No one is complaining, either. The LPs I speak with seem unbothered by this big gamble, given the potential returns; they’re expecting a bonanza.
But they do see danger ahead, even if they describe this as a “yellow light” situation, and they’re uneasy about how quickly VCs are coming back to raise new funds.
I talked about all of it recently with Beezer Clarkson of LGT Capital Partners, a Zurich-based diversified asset manager, and Amit Bhatti of TrueBridge, a Chapel Hill firm that focuses solely on venture. This conversation has been edited for length.
These are strange days — exciting but also scary. How are you feeling about your roles right now, and your place in this startup ecosystem?
Beezer Clarkson: It’s very busy, but I wouldn’t say it’s scary. There’s a lot of change and a lot of variables at play. I love venture, so I find the chaos fun. I’ve been doing this for a couple of decades, so seeing the cycles makes it less scary. You appreciate that these things happen, and that we should enjoy the upside, because sometimes there’s downside, and the up is a lot more fun than the down.
Amit Bhatti: If anything, it’s exciting. Venture is sometimes looked at as a niche, and now that AI is all-consuming, all the attention is on venture. This feels like our moment more than it is like, “Oh gosh, what’s going to happen?” The pace of investing and the valuations may be different, but really meaningful stuff is happening, and all the attention is focused on this corner of private equity.
Your funds all hold the same brands now, OpenAI and Anthropic, multiplied across however many funds you back, and your job is to keep your institutions diversified. How do you think about that? Obviously it’s great right now, but if things turned, it would be less great.
Amit Bhatti: Venture has always been a power law business, so I actually view the concentration as a good thing. If we were getting to the maturity of one of our funds and there were still lots of tiny positions, something’s gone wrong. Our funds that are 10-plus years old are starting to consolidate into a few names. There’s a lot of Databricks, a lot of SpaceX, a lot of Stripe. In this generation of funds, I would hope there’s a lot of Anthropic and a lot of OpenAI. That’s a feature, not a bug. Not every one of these companies is going to work out, but that consolidation is typical. What’s different is how quickly it’s happened. I don’t view it as an immediate panic signal.
Beezer Clarkson: At the early stage, you still see quite a diversity of opportunity sets, and the dollars are smaller. It aggregates up into the same companies, but early-stage funds obviously aren’t doing the big late-stage stuff, so you have more diversity there, if that’s what you’re looking for.
Funds that invested on four-year cycles have shrunk that to three, then two, then 18 months. Is the pacing okay, or is it concerning?
Beezer Clarkson: We’re seeing funds come back on one-year pacing, which is fast. The norm was probably two to two and a half years. Some funds are deploying much faster because they’re taking concentrated, big-check positions. That could be a worrisome sign. It could work out, we don’t know, but it’s typically harder to do a one-year vintage and get it right.
Amit Bhatti: Similar for us. I would have said 24 to 36 months was roughly normal. Now 12 to 18 is not crazy for some of the funds going really quickly. A lot of funds are bumping up their fund sizes mid-cycle, which is definitely unusual. That’s partly because rounds have gotten so large. If Anthropic is raising a giant quantum of capital and you put 20% of the fund into it, you’re obviously going to be ahead of pace. Seed round sizes have gone up almost 2x, too, so if you want to lead, you’re writing 2x the check. It’s definitely a yellow light. It gives us a little bit of heartburn.
But when we look at what these managers actually bought, the numbers are different. The last time we had accelerated pacing, there was a lot of investing in zero-revenue crypto moonshots. Now we’re seeing a lot of companies go from zero to $100 million in revenue, which was totally unheard of before.
If you’ve got a great manager who comes back every year but the returns are still on paper, can you say “call me next time,” or do you lose your seat at the table?
Beezer Clarkson: It’s very hard to leave a manager and then come back. It happens, but it’s more typical to downsize your check. In 2021, a lot of LPs said, “If I was going to give you $10 million, I’ll do $5 million, because $10 million was for two years.” In our portfolios, the pacing gets pulled through, so we think about our pacing as well as yours.
Amit Bhatti: Same here. We’re building out a calendar of when we expect to make commitments, so if someone goes way off that map, we need to make sure the capital is there. You see people downsize or communicate it up front. It’s hard to say you’re sitting it out altogether, because then you’re not reliable capital. That’s also why you’re seeing upsizes; managers don’t want to come back and say they’re raising a whole new fund, so they bump up the old one.
Beezer Clarkson: People also rotate out of venture sometimes because capital calls keep running with no distributions coming back, and they still have to meet operating commitments, whether it’s the endowment, the hospital, or the foundation. That puts a lot of strain on those situations.
LPs like time diversification, yet a lot of funds were raised in recent years, including that backed startups at high valuations during the pandemic. How are those funds doing, and how would you describe 2026 so far?
Beezer Clarkson: The 2021 vintages are still early, five years in, but they argue against doing one-year funds. Some will catch a piece of an AI company and look excellent, but your odds of getting it right in one year are just tougher, and the valuations were extreme.
Amit Bhatti: If I look at the last 15 years of our portfolio, I wouldn’t bet on the COVID vintage being the best one. But a couple of breakouts will come from it. OpenAI was around in that era, and Cursor started pretty far back, so they’re in some of those funds. And liquidity has started flowing. The past two years were definitely slower, but SpaceX is the headline, Cerebras was a big exit this year, there have been a couple of other IPOs, and a lot of M&A. We’re seeing $10 billion-plus M&A exits, a $60 billion one [with Cursor]. Liquidity is going beyond just IPOs.
How are your venture fund managers thinking about secondaries? If I were a VC, I’d have been tempted to take money off the table in OpenAI or Anthropic.
Beezer Clarkson: Secondaries have become much more sophisticated in venture over the last, call it, five years. It’s localized in the top handful of companies, but it’s much more prevalent than before, which I think is good, because the ecosystem needs liquidity options. Venture is predicated on that, and if you wait 20 years for an IPO, that is not what structurally we all thought it could be. They’re also happening at multiple levels now. LPs sell stakes of their GPs, a strip of their portfolio, and the taboo around it is less.
Amit Bhatti: It’s the third leg of liquidity now: IPOs, M&A, secondaries. Private equity has always had a well-developed secondaries market, and venture didn’t. It was kind of a dirty word. You were only selling if you were distressed. Then people were holding the bag in 2021 and thought, “I should have sold.” Now more managers use it as a tool, and more judiciously. If you still believe it’s the power law company, you’re probably not exiting the whole position. But if you can sell 20% of your position and return your fund, you should probably do it.
There’s a lot of founder selling and employee tenders — often very early into the company’s “journey.” How do you feel about that?
Amit Bhatti: We were talking before about the analogy to crypto, where things got very difficult in part because employees were paid in tokens that were liquid immediately. What’s your motivation to stick around when things get hard? So I think it’s great that there are employee tenders, especially for companies that have been around a long time, like Stripe and Databricks, with a very clear financial picture. For them to offer partial liquidity to employees is totally reasonable. But a lot of the enforcement falls on the lead investors. Investors we back have told companies, “We don’t want you to do an employee tender right now.” Those conversations are happening behind the scenes, and people have learned some lessons from last time. It’s all based on leverage, though. If the founder has incredible leverage . . .
Forget it.
Amit Bhatti: Yeah.
When these companies go public and employees get liquid, will they become partners or competitors to your venture managers? These employees have amazing networks.
Beezer Clarkson: We’ve seen it multiple times: when a company becomes very productive, employees can become LPs or GPs themselves. It’s entirely possible there’ll be a whole new raft of emerging managers backed by people coming out of OpenAI and Anthropic. It happened in the Google days. But being an LP means signing up for many millions of dollars and a multi-decade business.
Amit Bhatti: The real estate part [given the soaring cost of home prices in San Francisco] is going to be tough. But those people stay in the ecosystem, investing in others, building new companies, starting new firms. That’s why no other place is taking SF’s place anytime soon.
Housing costs here in San Francisco have shot up so fast. Do we price out the next generation of founders, and does the next hub end up in New York or somewhere else?
Beezer Clarkson: History would argue that the density effect in the Bay Area is a great pull. Maybe it moves out of San Francisco and back into the suburbs. Back in the day, YC was in Mountain View. New York obviously has its own very deep tech scene, but there’s such a density here that it’s been really hard to push back against.
A handful of venture funds now lock down most of the committed capital from limited partners. Is there a wedge in for emerging managers?
Beezer Clarkson: There are still first-time and emerging managers, funds one through three, being raised this year, last year, the year before. You still need a differentiated point of view, a reason for being. Fundraising has gotten harder, but we see them being funded, and the fund sizes are just smaller. Fifty percent of the money might go to the big funds, but if your average first fund is $25 million to $50 million, there can still be enough of those to add up to $1 billion.
Amit Bhatti: There are people raising $5 million or $10 million right here in SF, maybe formalizing their angel investing. A lot of really well-known funds started with a $5 million fund. It’s much better for an emerging manager to build the track record, prove out the thesis, your access and your judgment with whatever capital you have, and then fund two will be easier to raise. If you try to raise $50 million or $100 million on day one, you’re creating a giant hill to climb.
Beezer Clarkson: If you’ve only angel invested, that’s a different story from spinning out of a platform where you have an installed base of LPs who know you. Those managers typically raise more.
Can you talk about specific kinds of emerging managers you’ve backed, and what made you write the check?
Amit Bhatti: People define “emerging” very differently. We’ve backed founders who are still running their companies and investing on the side. We’ve backed people leaving a bigger firm for something earlier. And we’ve backed extremely young GPs, 22 and 23 years old, who have really close access to the next generation of AI-native founders. They started an accelerator program at MIT, Harvard, and Stanford, and the first couple of batches had Cursor and Mercor in them. They’re young, but they’re around an incredible density of talent. The VC job is sourcing, picking, winning, and they did a pretty decent job of picking when there was no money involved. Success begets success in venture, so we were happy to give them a shot.
Beezer Clarkson: There’s much more flexibility now. I remember a time when an LP wouldn’t fund somebody who had a job and was also investing, and people are open to that now. I’ve been investing in emerging managers, along with established ones, for 14 years, and they run the whole gamut, from an operator-turned-investor raising $10 million, to a spinout raising a few hundred million [dollars]. It’s interesting when they’re still operating, because it gives them insights. The trick is whether they’re doing what they need to do to win the right to be on the best cap tables.
Amit Bhatti: Especially early stage, there’s no one-size-fits-all. You can be part-time, you can be diversified, you can be concentrated. There are more outs in the deck, if you will, for returning something that’s small and experimental.
What’s the smallest check you’ll write to a fund, and how much of a fund will you take?
Beezer Clarkson: Given our program, it’s hard to do less than $5 million. I’ve generally taken the view that if you’re [representing] too much of a fund, there are challenges for the GP going forward, so I’d want to be no more than 20%. There are situations where I’d consider more.
Amit Bhatti: Three to five million for us, and on occasion smaller in very specific scenarios. We don’t really care about concentration if it’s the right scenario. We’ll do half or all of it. But Beezer’s right that it’s not ideal for the GP, and we tell them up front to diversify their LP base. We’ve done a fund where we were half the capital, and the next fund we were closer to 20%, because they did well.

articles.title: Google y la NASA desarrollan un robot que podría acompañar a los astronautas en sus viajes a Marte
articles.text:
La exploración espacial se prepara para una nueva etapa en la que los robots podrían convertirse en aliados fundamentales de las tripulaciones. Google Public Sector y distintos equipos de la NASA trabajan en un sistema robótico diseñado para asistir a los astronautas durante futuras misiones al espacio profundo, con especial atención a los viajes a Marte, donde la distancia con la Tierra dificultará la atención médica y la resolución de problemas en tiempo real.
El proyecto busca desarrollar un robot capaz de realizar tareas de mantenimiento, organizar herramientas y gestionar equipos dentro de una nave espacial. Sin embargo, su función no se limitaría a labores logísticas: también podría brindar asistencia física a los astronautas en determinados procedimientos médicos, como la toma de constantes vitales o la realización de ecografías sencillas.
La iniciativa forma parte de los avances tecnológicos que buscan preparar a las agencias espaciales para misiones de larga duración, en las que los tripulantes deberán resolver situaciones cotidianas sin depender constantemente de instrucciones desde la Tierra.
El desarrollo cuenta con la participación del Programa de Investigación Humana de la NASA, el equipo de Robótica del Centro Espacial Johnson y el Laboratorio de Propulsión a Chorro (JPL), en colaboración con Google Public Sector.
Cómo funcionará el robot desarrollado por Google y la NASA
El sistema está concebido como un manipulador de carga versátil, es decir, un dispositivo robótico capaz de interactuar con objetos y realizar diferentes tareas dentro de espacios reducidos. Entre sus funciones principales se encuentran transportar equipos, organizar herramientas, asegurar compartimentos y colaborar con el mantenimiento de los módulos espaciales.
La característica más importante es que podrá cambiar de función según las necesidades de la tripulación. Cuando no esté ocupado con las tareas rutinarias, el robot podría utilizarse para brindar asistencia física a los astronautas durante procedimientos médicos.
Para conseguirlo, el sistema combina inteligencia artificial, modelos de entrenamiento y herramientas de reconocimiento del entorno. Según Google, la tecnología utiliza instancias de Google Cloud G4 para acelerar el entrenamiento de los modelos que controlan sus movimientos y capacidades.
Una vez preparados, estos modelos pueden ejecutarse localmente en dispositivos perimetrales compactos y de bajo consumo energético. Esto resulta especialmente importante para las misiones espaciales, donde los equipos deben funcionar con recursos limitados y no pueden depender permanentemente de una conexión con servidores terrestres.
Además, el robot incorpora herramientas de inteligencia para el conocimiento de la situación espacial, que le permiten interpretar su entorno tridimensional y desplazarse con mayor precisión.
Antes de interactuar con objetos reales, puede practicar movimientos complejos en entornos virtuales de alta precisión. De esta manera, los investigadores buscan reducir los errores y comprobar que el sistema pueda operar de forma segura cerca de los astronautas.
Por qué los astronautas necesitarán asistencia robótica en Marte
Uno de los principales desafíos de una misión tripulada a Marte será la distancia que separa al planeta rojo de la Tierra. A diferencia de lo que ocurre en la Estación Espacial Internacional, donde existe una comunicación relativamente rápida con los centros de control, los viajes marcianos tendrán importantes demoras.
Google advierte que una comunicación de ida y vuelta entre Marte y la Tierra podría tardar hasta 44 minutos. Esto significa que, ante una emergencia médica, los astronautas no podrían depender de una respuesta inmediata de los especialistas que permanecen en nuestro planeta.
Por ese motivo, la autonomía de las tripulaciones será fundamental. Los astronautas deberán contar con herramientas que les permitan atender problemas de salud, realizar tareas de mantenimiento y resolver imprevistos sin esperar instrucciones terrestres.
En ese contexto, el robot podría convertirse en un apoyo físico para los procedimientos médicos. Por ejemplo, estaría preparado para ayudar a tomar constantes vitales o realizar ecografías básicas bajo la supervisión de un médico de la tripulación.
La tecnología no busca reemplazar a los profesionales de la salud ni tomar decisiones clínicas por su cuenta. Su objetivo es ejecutar determinadas acciones físicas que pueden resultar difíciles para un astronauta que necesite asistencia o que deba atender a otro integrante de la misión.
Las pruebas para llevar robots a futuras misiones espaciales
El desarrollo todavía se encuentra en una etapa de investigación y pruebas. Google informó que, durante los últimos años, el equipo evaluó aproximadamente 15 dispositivos de computación perimetral para identificar cuáles podían funcionar de manera eficiente con el hardware ligero y de bajo consumo que requieren las futuras misiones a Marte.
El objetivo final es conseguir que los astronautas puedan controlar el robot mediante instrucciones de voz sencillas, siempre bajo su supervisión y mando directo. Esto permitiría asignarle tareas sin necesidad de que los tripulantes tengan conocimientos especializados de programación o robótica.
La iniciativa se integra en los preparativos de la NASA para ampliar la presencia humana en la Luna y avanzar hacia futuras expediciones tripuladas a Marte. El programa Artemis busca establecer las condiciones para una exploración lunar sostenida y utilizar esa experiencia como parte del camino hacia misiones más lejanas.
En ese escenario, los robots con inteligencia artificial podrían desempeñar un papel importante: no como sustitutos de los astronautas, sino como herramientas capaces de asumir tareas físicas, reducir la carga de trabajo y mejorar las condiciones de seguridad durante viajes espaciales que podrían extenderse durante años.

articles.title: "Hubble a encore une science importante devant lui" : la NASA a jusqu'en 2032 pour le sauver de la chute
articles.text:
Hubble va retomber sur Terre : la NASA appelle à l’aide pour sauver son télescope légendaire, vieux de 36 ans
Sans moteur et freiné chaque jour par la haute atmosphère, le télescope spatial le plus célèbre du monde a une chance sur deux de replonger vers la Terre d’ici fin 2033. La NASA invite les industriels à le remonter, à le réparer ou à lui offrir une fin maîtrisée. Seule ombre au tableau : la dernière tentative de ce genre a viré au fiasco cet été.
La NASA a publié le 29 octobre un appel à informations adressé à l'industrie spatiale pour décider du sort de Hubble. Les entreprises ont jusqu'au 30 novembre pour expliquer comment elles relèveraient son orbite, moderniseraient ses équipements ou piloteraient sa rentrée dans l'atmosphère. Le calendrier est serré. Faute de propulsion, Hubble devrait rentrer dans l'atmosphère entre 2033 et 2034, selon le communiqué de l'agence, et toute mission devra donc avoir lieu d'ici 2032.
	
Hubble a encore une science importante devant lui, et nous devrions examiner chaque occasion raisonnable de le faire travailler le plus longtemps possible.
Le patron de l'agence a de bonnes raisons d'insister. Malgré Webb et le tout nouveau télescope Roman, aucun successeur capable d'observer dans l'ultraviolet et le visible avec la même finesse n'est attendu avant les années 2040.
Pourquoi Hubble perd de l'altitude depuis 2009
Entre 1993 et 2009, cinq équipages de la navette spatiale sont venus réparer l'observatoire, et en ont profité pour le remonter. Depuis la retraite des navettes en 2011, personne ne lui a redonné d'altitude. Le Soleil, au sommet de son cycle d'activité, gonfle la haute atmosphère et accélère le freinage.
En janvier, lors du congrès de l'American Astronomical Society, le Space Telescope Science Institute, qui gère le programme scientifique de Hubble, a placé la date médiane de rentrée en 2033.
One note from the STScI town hall at #AAS247 today: the median reentry date for Hubble, based on current modeling, is 2033; a <10% chance of reentry by 2029.
— Jeff Foust (@jeff_foust) January 7, 2026
Hubble n'a pas été conçu pour rentrer de façon contrôlée, et c'est là que tout se complique. Une étude technique de la NASA estime à 1 sur 330 le risque de faire une victime lors d'une rentrée en 2033, alors que la norme de l'agence impose 1 sur 10 000 au maximum.
Le dossier concerne aussi l'Europe. Hubble est un projet commun de la NASA et de l'ESA, et les astronomes européens disposent d'au moins 15 % de son temps d'observation.
Rehausser Hubble : un projet refusé en 2024, relancé par Jared Isaacman
L'idée a déjà été étudiée. En 2022, SpaceX et le programme Polaris de Jared Isaacman ont proposé de remonter le télescope avec une capsule Crew Dragon, aux frais du milliardaire. Au printemps 2024, une enquête de NPR a révélé les fortes réticences des ingénieurs de la NASA. Isaacman a répliqué sur X.
I also did not love how they pulled my quotes from podcasts. What the article does not capture is the official position of the joint study and hopefully that comes out. On surface it looks like "billionaire wants to touch Hubble and NASA said hell no", but that is not what…
— Jared Isaacman (@rookisaacman) May 18, 2024
Quelques semaines plus tard, Mark Clampin, alors directeur de l'astrophysique à la NASA, a refermé la porte : "après avoir exploré les capacités commerciales actuelles, nous n'allons pas poursuivre de rehausse", avait-il déclaré, d'après Space.com. Entre-temps, le milliardaire a pris la tête de l'agence.
Le précédent de Swift pèse lourd sur ce dossier. La NASA avait confié 30 millions de dollars à la jeune pousse Katalyst pour remorquer ce télescope à rayons gamma, lui aussi dépourvu de moteur. Lancé le 3 juillet par l'ultime fusée Pegasus XL, le robot LINK s'est rapidement mis à tournoyer sur lui-même, avec deux roues de réaction sur trois hors service. Isaacman refusait alors de baisser les bras.
We are not giving up yet. A lot of credit goes to the Katalyst Space and NASA teams working to recover the spacecraft, rendezvous with Swift, and boost the observatory.
This remains a very cool, very low-cost, high-potential, high-reward mission, and another step toward a more…
— NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman (@NASAAdmin) July 30, 2026
Le 19 août, la NASA a fini par jeter l'éponge. LINK est retombé dans l'atmosphère fin septembre, et Swift doit le suivre début novembre.
NASA and Katalyst Space have determined that Katalyst’s LINK spacecraft will not capture or boost our Swift observatory to a higher altitude to extend its science mission, due to an ongoing attitude control issue with the spacecraft. However, LINK will still attempt to conduct… pic.twitter.com/STMFzVdODX
— NASA Universe (@NASAUniverse) August 19, 2026
Hubble garde tout de même un atout que Swift n'avait pas. Depuis 2009, il porte un anneau d'amarrage installé précisément pour qu'un engin vienne s'y arrimer un jour.
