articles.title: GTA 6 revela a sus protagonistas: quiénes son Jason, Lucia y los personajes que llegarán a Vice City
articles.text:
Rockstar Games confirmó nuevos detalles sobre los personajes que darán vida a Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6), el próximo lanzamiento de una de las franquicias más populares de la industria de los videojuegos. La historia tendrá como protagonistas a Jason Duval y Lucia Caminos, una pareja que intentará construir una nueva vida en medio del crimen organizado, los negocios ilegales y los conflictos que dominan Vice City.
El elenco también incluirá narcotraficantes, atracadores profesionales, empresarios vinculados al entretenimiento nocturno y artistas que buscan hacerse un lugar en la escena musical. Estos personajes tendrán diferentes conexiones con los protagonistas y ayudarán a desarrollar una trama que combinará robos, ambición, relaciones personales y violencia.
El videojuego llegará el 19 de noviembre de 2026 a PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S. Aunque Rockstar todavía no ha confirmado una versión para PC, ya ha presentado información sobre buena parte de los personajes que participarán en esta nueva aventura.
Jason Duval y Lucia Caminos: los protagonistas de GTA 6
Jason Duval es uno de los dos personajes principales de GTA 6. Creció rodeado de delincuentes y estafadores, pero intentó alejarse de ese entorno cuando ingresó al ejército. Sin embargo, su pasado terminó llevándolo nuevamente al mundo criminal.
Después de abandonar la vida militar, se instaló en los Cayos, donde trabaja para narcotraficantes de la zona. Su situación cambia cuando conoce a Lucia, una mujer que podría representar una oportunidad para comenzar de nuevo o convertirse en el origen de nuevos problemas.
Por su parte, Lucia Caminos ha enfrentado dificultades desde pequeña. Su intención de proteger a su familia terminó llevándola a la penitenciaría de Leonida, de la que finalmente consiguió salir.
Ahora busca tomar el control de su futuro y alcanzar la estabilidad económica que siempre deseó. La relación con Jason aparece como una posible oportunidad para conseguirlo, aunque ambos deberán enfrentarse a situaciones peligrosas para cumplir sus objetivos.
La historia de los dos personajes recuerda a la dinámica criminal de Bonnie y Clyde: una pareja que construye su camino a través de robos y decisiones arriesgadas.
Los personajes que rodearán a Jason y Lucia
Además de los protagonistas, Rockstar presentó a varios personajes que tendrán vínculos con el mundo criminal y los negocios de Vice City.
Cal Hampton: es amigo de Jason y socio de Brian Heder. Prefiere mantenerse en casa, donde pasa el tiempo vigilando comunicaciones de la guardia costera y navegando por internet. Su personalidad está marcada por las teorías de conspiración y la desconfianza.
Boobie Ike: es uno de los empresarios más conocidos de Vice City. Consiguió transformar su pasado en las calles en un negocio que incluye propiedades inmobiliarias, un club nocturno y un estudio de grabación. Aunque suele mostrarse sonriente, su actitud cambia cuando debe negociar.
Dre’Quan Priest: es un aspirante a empresario musical que busca dejar atrás sus actividades ilegales. Su objetivo es impulsar Only Raw Records, el sello discográfico que comparte con Boobie Ike, y conseguir el éxito dentro de la escena musical de la ciudad.
Real Dimez: el dúo está integrado por Bae-Luxe y Roxy, dos amigas que encontraron en la música y las redes sociales una manera de ganar dinero. Después de conseguir popularidad con sus canciones de rap, firmaron con Only Raw Records y buscan recuperar el éxito.
Raul Bautista: es un atracador profesional que destaca por su carisma y capacidad para organizar golpes. Su ambición aumenta con cada robo, por lo que busca personas dispuestas a asumir riesgos cada vez mayores para conseguir grandes recompensas.
Brian Heder: es un narcotraficante que opera desde un astillero en los Cayos junto a su esposa Lori. Después de pasar años en el negocio, ahora deja que otros realicen buena parte del trabajo ilegal. También mantiene una relación cercana con Jason, a quien permite vivir en una de sus propiedades a cambio de colaborar en algunas actividades.
Qué papel tendrán los personajes en la historia de GTA 6
El conjunto de personajes muestra que GTA 6 no estará centrado únicamente en los delitos que cometan Jason y Lucia. Rockstar plantea una historia en la que los negocios, la música, las relaciones personales y el crimen organizado estarán conectados.
Los protagonistas comenzarán desde una posición económica y personal complicada: Lucia acaba de salir de prisión y Jason depende de los vínculos que mantiene con narcotraficantes para sostenerse. A partir de esa situación, ambos buscarán oportunidades para mejorar sus vidas, aunque deberán enfrentarse a personas con intereses diferentes.
Los personajes secundarios también permitirán explorar distintos sectores de Vice City, desde los negocios nocturnos hasta las actividades ilegales que se desarrollan fuera del centro urbano.
Por ahora, Rockstar no ha detallado cómo se relacionará cada personaje con las misiones principales ni qué decisiones podrán tomar los jugadores durante la historia. Lo confirmado es que GTA 6 llegará el 19 de noviembre de 2026 a PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S, mientras que su lanzamiento en PC continúa sin fecha oficial.

articles.title: C’est déjà le Black Friday chez Boulanger : le Samsung Galaxy S25 FE s’affiche avec 250€ de moins sur le site
articles.text:
Avec son grand écran AMOLED et son équipement photo polyvalent, le Samsung Galaxy S25 FE se présente comme un smartphone attractif, surtout si l’on tient compte de la remise de 250 € dont il bénéficie chez Boulanger pour le lancement du Black Friday.
Boulanger n’a pas de temps à perdre : le Black Friday a déjà démarré sur le site de l’enseigne. Parmi les premières offres intéressantes, on trouve celle qui concerne le smartphone Samsung Galaxy S25 FE de 128 Go, disponible à 499 € au lieu de 749 €. Ce modèle équipé d’un processeur Exynos 2400 et de 8 Go de RAM se destine aux utilisateurs en quête d’un mobile polyvalent et abordable sous Android 16.
Le Samsung Galaxy S25 FE 128 Go est à 499 € au lieu de 749 € au lancement du Black Friday chez Boulanger.
Pourquoi choisir le Samsung Galaxy S25 FE ?
- Pour son grand écran : la dalle AMOLED de 6,7 pouces à 120 Hz est idéale pour lire, regarder des séries et naviguer.
- Pour son zoom optique : le téléobjectif 3x complète le capteur principal de 50 mégapixels et l’ultra grand-angle.
- Pour son suivi logiciel : Samsung prévoit sept générations de mises à jour du système et sept ans de correctifs de sécurité, à compter du lancement du modèle.
Un smartphone confortable pour les loisirs et la photo
L’écran AMOLED de 6,7 pouces qui équipe le Galaxy S25 FE est son premier atout. Il offre une surface d’affichage généreuse pour regarder des vidéos, surfer sur les réseaux sociaux et utiliser de nombreuses applications, dont des jeux mobiles. Côté photo, on trouve trois capteurs de 50, 12 et 8 mégapixels. La qualité des prises de vue en extérieur fait partie des points forts relevés au sein de notre test, qui accorde la note de 8 sur 10 au Samsung Galaxy S25 FE. Sa batterie de 4 900 mAh accepte une recharge filaire jusqu’à 45 W, mais l’adaptateur secteur est vendu séparément.
Une porte d’entrée dans la gamme Galaxy S
À 499 €, le Galaxy S25 FE se présente comme une porte d’entrée abordable au sein de la gamme Samsung Galaxy S. Son téléobjectif et ses fonctions Galaxy AI sont notamment appréciables. En revanche, il embarque une puce Exynos 2400 moins puissante que le Snapdragon 8 Elite des Galaxy S25 et S25+, ce qui le rend notamment moins adapté aux jeux mobiles les plus gourmands avec les réglages poussés au maximum.
✅ Les points forts
- Écran AMOLED de 6,7 pouces à 120 Hz.
- Téléobjectif avec zoom optique 3x.
- Suivi logiciel longue durée annoncé par Samsung.
❌ Les limites
- Stockage de 128 Go non extensible.
- SoC vieillissant.
Boulanger fait passer le prix du Samsung Galaxy S25 FE de 749 € à 499 € à l’occasion du Black Friday.
Si vous disposez d’un budget de moins de 500 € et que vous désirez changer de smartphone pour un modèle Samsung récent, alors le Samsung Galaxy S25 FE de 128 Go pourrait bien correspondre à ce que vous recherchez.
En revanche, les amateurs de petits smartphones, de stockage abondant ou les joueurs souhaitant pousser les réglages au maximum devraient se mettre à la recherche d’un terminal un peu plus adapté à leurs besoins. Après tout, le Black Friday ne fait que commencer.

articles.title: 12 € pour GTA VI, 0,45 € pour un film : une taxe inédite sur les données adoptée à l'Assemblée
articles.text:
Netflix, Steam, cloud : vos abonnements et téléchargements bientôt plus chers à cause d'une nouvelle taxe ?
Malgré l’avis défavorable du gouvernement et du rapporteur général, les députés ont adopté un amendement socialiste créant une taxe au gigaoctet sur les fournisseurs de contenus en ligne. Une mesure aux répercussions potentielles étendues.
Le vote s'est joué à une voix près dans l'hémicycle : 11 voix contre 10. L'amendement n° I-1358 au projet de loi de finances, déposé par le groupe Socialistes et apparentés, entend instituer une contribution assise sur les volumes de données acheminés vers les utilisateurs français. Fixée à 0,055 euro par gigaoctet, cette fiscalité vise à générer jusqu'à 10 milliards d'euros de recettes en ciblant l'activité réelle des acteurs du numérique.
Un prélèvement au volume mesuré par les opérateurs télécoms
Le fonctionnement du dispositif confie aux fournisseurs d'accès à internet (FAI) la responsabilité de relever chaque trimestre les volumes émis par chaque acteur, sous le contrôle conjoint de l'Arcep et de la Direction générale des finances publiques. Le texte inclut également les réseaux de diffusion de contenu (CDN) afin de mesurer les flux issus des serveurs relais situés au plus près de l'utilisateur.
Pour éviter d'asphyxier les services à forte consommation de bande passante mais aux marges plus mesurées, un plafonnement a été intégré. Le montant réclamé ne pourra excéder 15 % du chiffre d'affaires réalisé en France, ou 2 % du chiffre d'affaires mondial. En complément de l'objectif budgétaire, les auteurs mettent en avant une dimension écologique, estimant que ce coût incitera les éditeurs à optimiser et compresser leurs flux.
De la vidéo aux jeux dématérialisés : les services dans le viseur
Si l'amendement précise que l'impôt est acquitté par les fournisseurs de contenus et non par les internautes, la liste des plateformes et services techniques susceptibles d'entrer dans le champ d'application couvre une part considérable des usages numériques quotidiens :
- Streaming vidéo et direct : Les plateformes comme Netflix, YouTube, Disney+, Prime Video, Twitch ou TikTok représentent l'essentiel du trafic descendant, aux côtés des plateformes de télévision et replay (TF1+, France.tv, MyCanal).
- Jeux vidéo et divertissement interactif : Les boutiques en ligne telles que Steam (Valve), l'Epic Games Store, le PlayStation Network ou le Xbox Network manipulent des fichiers d'installation et des mises à jour pesant fréquemment entre 50 et 150 gigaoctets.
- Intelligence artificielle et dépôts de code : Les services d'hébergement de modèles et jeux de données comme Hugging Face ou GitHub génèrent des transferts de plusieurs dizaines de gigaoctets par fichier, souvent distribués gratuitement.
- Services de cloud et synchronisation : Les espaces de stockage et de sauvegarde tels que Google Drive, OneDrive, iCloud ou Dropbox, ainsi que les infrastructures d'hébergement (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud).
- Réseaux sociaux et communication : Les applications comme Instagram, X, Discord ou les outils de visioconférence (Teams, Zoom).
- Réseaux de diffusion de contenu (CDN) : Les prestataires d'infrastructure comme Cloudflare, Akamai ou Fastly, expressément visés pour leurs points de livraison de données.
- Mises à jour de systèmes : La distribution des correctifs pour Windows, macOS, iOS ou les distributions Linux.
Des répercussions prévisibles pour les utilisateurs
Bien que les consommateurs ne soient pas directement taxés, les entreprises soumises à ce prélèvement pourraient adapter leur modèle économique. Pour compenser la charge financière ou éviter d'atteindre le plafond légal, certains acteurs pourraient répercuter le coût sur les prix des abonnements, restreindre la bande passante vers les connexions situées en France ou instaurer des limitations sur les téléchargements de fichiers très volumineux.
Adopté de justesse en séance publique à l'Assemblée, le texte doit encore poursuivre son parcours législatif. Il sera soumis à l'examen du Sénat et devra surmonter les réserves exprimées par l'exécutif avant une éventuelle intégration définitive dans la loi de finances.

articles.title: Salesforce’s M&A spree continues with a reported $375M deal for defense tech startup Rune | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Salesforce has agreed to acquire Rune Technologies, a startup that builds AI software to help the U.S. military predict supply needs and manage logistics from the field, for $375 million in cash and stock, Resilience Media reported.
The acquisition underscores Salesforce’s push into defense tech through Missionforce, its business unit serving national security and defense agencies. Since Missionforce launched last year, its business has grown 80% year over year, driven in part by a new 10-year, $5.6 billion contract with the U.S. Army, the company said in a blog post. By integrating Rune’s frontline logistics data, Missionforce will extend beyond back-office administrative planning to support battlefield operations.
Since its founding in 2024, Rune has raised a total of $30 million from investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Point72 Ventures, and IQT, a CIA-backed nonprofit venture firm formerly known as In-Q-Tel. The startup was last valued at $127 million when it raised a Series A led by Human Capital last year, according to PitchBook.
Salesforce has been on an acquisition spree this year. In addition to Rune, the CRM giant agreed to buy AI agent platform Fin (formerly Intercom) for $3.6 billion, bought Qualified for $1.2 billion, and signed an agreement to buy Listen Labs after the startup walked away from a $125 million Series C term sheet at a $1.5 billion valuation, as TechCrunch reported.
Salesforce didn’t respond to a request for comment.

articles.title: Disney Plus stellt wieder scharf – aber wohl nur temporär
articles.text:
Tech-Trick mit Haken: Disney Plus bringt HDR zurück – aber Millionen schauen in die Röhre
Nach einer einstweiligen Verfügung wegen der Verletzung von Patenten im November 2025 hatte Disney Plus zunächst die High-Dynamic-Range-Formate Dolby Vision und HDR 10 Plus sowie 3D-Filme aus seinem Streamingangebot gestrichen. Ein weiterer Gerichtsentscheid sorgte Mitte Juni 2026 dafür, dass Nutzer:innen bei Disney Plus auch auf 4K UHD und HDR verzichten müssen.
Patentstreit um Videocodec HEVC
Konkret geht es bei dem Patentstreit um die angeblich widerrechtliche Nutzung des Videocodecs HEVC durch den Streaminganbieter. Die Patente beansprucht das US-Technologieunternehmen Interdigital für sich. Im September 2026 hatte Interdigital Disney wegen ausgebliebener Lizenzgebühren auf einen Schadenersatz in der Höhe von 101,7 Millionen Euro verklagt.
Disney Plus war derweil ins Visier von Verbraucherschützer:innen geraten, weil es die Technologien zwar gestrichen, seinen Kund:innen aber keinerlei Entschädigung dafür angeboten hatte. Jetzt versucht der Streaminganbieter, das Problem technisch zu lösen, wie hdtvtest.co.uk berichtet.
Disney Plus setzt auf Workaround
Demnach setzt Disney Plus jetzt auf die HEVC-Alternativen VP9 und VP9-2. Dem Unternehmen zufolge sollen mittlerweile alle Titel in 4K-Auflösung mit VP9 statt HEVC zur Verfügung stehen. Das Gleiche soll mit HDR 10 via VP9-2 geschehen sein. Dolby Vision fehlt bei dieser Lösung aber weiterhin.
Ein Problem an dem Workaround ist, dass Millionen TV-Geräte und Media-Player die Codecs VP9 oder VP9-2 nicht unterstützen. Das gilt sowohl für Samsung-, Panasonic- und LG-Geräte sowie Apple TV 4K oder Spielkonsolen wie Nvidia Shield. Unterstützt werden die Codecs dagegen von neueren Android-, Amazon-Fire- und Google-TV-Geräten sowie Hisense-Fernsehern.
Weiteres Gerichtsurteil droht
Darüber hinaus könnte es sein, dass Disney Plus diesen Tech-Trick bald wieder aufgeben muss. Denn Interdigital ist auch im Besitz von Patenten, die die beiden VP9-Codecs betreffen – und soll schon eine entsprechende Beschwerde eingereicht haben. Käme es zu einem weiteren Gerichtsentscheid pro Interdigital, könnten die Premium-Inhalte erneut verschwinden.

articles.title: How Much Deep Sleep Do You Need? What Sleep Researchers Say Before You Buy a Sleep Tracker - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Two different sleep trackers can read the same night and print two different deep-sleep percentages, and the internet’s reference numbers argue among themselves the same way, with figures from 10 to 25 percent all claiming to be the norm. How much deep sleep you need comes down to one benchmark: healthy adults spend about 13 to 23 percent of total sleep in deep sleep. The disagreement has a structure, and it takes about five minutes to learn. What follows is the benchmark, why wrist readings of sleep stages wobble, and a five-question check to run before paying for any tracker.
How Much Deep Sleep Do Adults Need? Two Bands Behind the Conflicting Percentages
Two citation bands explain most of the conflict in deep-sleep numbers. Under the AASM staging framework, healthy adults spend about 13 to 23 percent of total sleep in the N3 stage, while 10 to 20 percent is the looser band many sources still quote. A quoted 25 percent usually means retelling inflated the range.
The fix is a two-second reading habit, check the band’s origin before the percentage. AASM staging figures put N3 at 13 to 23 percent of total sleep, commonly cited figures answer with the looser 10 to 20 percent band, and the number 25 percent is what inflated retelling looks like. Results on the high end usually come from sources quoting the wider bands, so the argument never ends until the reader checks which one is in use.
Structure gives the percentages their meaning. Deep sleep percentages conflict because sources quote two bands — AASM’s N3 range at 13 to 23 percent of total sleep versus the looser 10 to 20 percent. Deep sleep loads toward the first half of the night while REM leans late, and the night moves in four to five cycles of roughly 90 to 120 minutes each, so where the deep sleep sits matters as much as how much of it there is.
The concern behind the search is common, and it is measured. The 2025 national healthy-sleep white paper, compiled with the China Sleep Big Data Center and iResearch under technical support from the China Sleep Research Society, from a 31-province sample of 2,500 respondents, put short deep sleep among its three most typical complaints, 49 percent of the 1,554 respondents reporting sleep troubles, with light or easily broken sleep ahead of it at 55 percent, and 66 percent of the full sample calling wake-up refreshment their clearest picture of a good night.
Ranges this wide are population coordinates. Personal baselines differ with age and sleep efficiency, and a single night’s percentage was never meant to grade anyone. The individual read that matters is the trend on your own timeline, which is where the rest of this piece goes.
Can You Trust the Deep-Sleep Number on Your Wrist?
Partly, and the trustworthy part is the trend. Sleep researchers’ archived commentary on consumer devices calls stage estimates rough, with heart rate and movement standing in for the brain signals that define the stages. The night-to-night pattern survives the estimation layer, and it is the part worth reading.
The short answer from the research side is blunt. Sleep researchers advise ignoring absolute deep-sleep readings from wrist trackers — the night-to-night trend beats any single percentage. In archived commentary by sleep researchers who reviewed a reader’s digest of fourteen laboratory studies, consumer wrist and ring devices were called “generally not great” at staging sleep, the advice for N3 readings was to “just entirely ignore” them, and the reasoning was that the devices “base it on averages” and let the arithmetic stand in for the stage.
The mechanism is no secret. As a sleep scientist writing in The Conversation lays it out, a wrist tracker reads movement with an accelerometer and heart rate with an optical sensor, then estimates stages from those signals, while the overnight wiring of a laboratory study adds the brain-wave readings that define the stages in the first place. Estimating a stage from its physiological neighbors is a genuine technical feat, and it remains an estimate, which is why two devices can split one night.
The literature puts numbers on the wobble. A 2019 systematic review and meta-analysis in the Journal of Medical Internet Research, covering 22 studies of Fitbit-class wristbands with 8 feeding the quantitative synthesis, assessed the devices against overnight lab monitoring and found the nonsleep-staging models overestimated total sleep time by roughly 7 to 67 minutes, while concluding that stage estimates are convenient gross estimates of limited specificity. A companion systematic review in Current Sleep Medicine Reports, pooling 7 studies of commercially available trackers, reported objectives and methods that varied widely, a spread its authors flagged as a reason to read the field with care.
Johns Hopkins Medicine’s consumer guidance lands in the same place, framing wrist trackers as collectors of useful patterns with real limits on what any single number can tell you. None of this argues for putting the watch in a drawer. It argues for knowing which layer of the reading is measurement and which is arithmetic, and the five questions below sort that out before money changes hands.
Before You Buy: A Five-Question Accuracy Check for Any Sleep Tracker
Run five questions before buying any tracker, and the spec sheet answers most of them. What the device measures, what the research says about that class, what your own baseline is, what action the numbers feed, and whether the trend line survives a rough night all filter the field fast. A device that clears all five earns its place.
The check works at the category level, brand agnostic, and it takes one sitting.
-  What does it actually measure? A wrist device infers stages from heart rate and movement, while a sensing layer collects readings directly, and the route decides what the number is. An estimate and a reading deserve different levels of trust.
2. What does the research say about this class? Look for systematic reviews of the device category, conditions and limits attached, and treat a product page’s own claims as one voice among many.
3. What is your baseline? Heart-rate variability runs in tens of milliseconds between individuals, with no universal passing grade, so decide what you will compare against before you buy. For the deeper drill on reading metrics against your own baseline, the official walkthrough how to read sleep tracker metrics against your own baseline carries the method.
4. What will the number make you do? A number that feeds a decision, an earlier bedtime, a cooler room, a quieter week, is worth paying for, and a number that feeds no decision is decoration.
5. Where does its accuracy break? Ask whether the device still shows a usable trend after a short or restless night, because the trend is the part that survives the estimation layer.
The check is a filter, and a friendly one. Most devices miss one question and pass four, and the miss tells you how to use the device. The correct usage, trend against baseline, is the next section’s whole business.
What the Numbers Are Still Good For — and the Non-Wearable Route
The numbers stay worth reading once they are read correctly. Log nights under fixed conditions, compare each reading to your own running baseline, and let a real drift trigger one concrete adjustment. Single nights belong to the benchmark, personal meaning belongs to the trend line, and both have a job.
A reader who tracked every sleep variable for ninety straight days distilled the value question into one line, people want measurement that serves a decision, and measurement that serves nothing else wears out its welcome. The archived record and the indicator-value argument built on it arrive at the same test. An indicator matters when it is wired into something adjustable, and a trend line is where the wiring shows.
In practice the method runs three steps. Record under consistent conditions, a set bedtime, a set room, the same device. Read relative changes against your own running baseline. Let a sustained offset trigger one change at a time, in schedule, load, or bedroom. Percentages borrowed from population tables step out of the way, and the trend does the talking.
The measurement route also has more than one lane. Wrist devices estimate stages from the outside, the way a meter reader might infer which rooms are in use from the power draw, while sensors built into the mattress read heart rate, breathing readings, and sleep stages through the night with nothing to charge, wear, or remember. The two lanes serve the same habit, a readable record of the night, waiting in the app.
On the tiers from DeRUCCI’s T11+ up, that record carries visible quality gates. A daily report generates once a night holds at least three hours in bed with two of actual sleep, the overseas recording window runs 20:00 to 10:00 local time, and per the brand’s official documentation the T11+ sensing layer detects heart rate with 97% accuracy. The gates matter as much as the readings, they define which data earns a place in the trend line. For the wider arc from sleep problems to mattress decisions, the sleep problems to mattress guide collects the official walkthrough.
Your Deep-Sleep Numbers: FAQ
How much deep sleep do adults need?
About 13 to 23 percent of total sleep for the N3 stage in healthy adults under the AASM framework, with 10 to 20 percent still commonly cited as a looser band. The figures here match DeRUCCI’s published sleep-guide article on the question, and both bands are population coordinates, and neither grades a person.
What should I check before buying a sleep tracker?
Five things, what the device physically measures, what systematic reviews say about its class, what your own baseline is, what action the numbers will feed, and whether the trend line survives a rough night. The full list sits in the section above, and it applies to wrist and non-wearable devices alike.
Why do different sources give different deep-sleep numbers?
Mostly because the bands get mixed, the AASM staging range of 13 to 23 percent of total sleep versus the looser 10 to 20 percent band many sources quote. A quoted 25 percent usually reflects inflated retelling, and it is rarely a new finding. Check which band a source is using before comparing it with another.
How accurate is the deep-sleep percentage on a wrist tracker?
Sleep researchers call it the weakest estimate in the chain, since the stage is inferred from heart rate and movement, with the stage itself going unmeasured. Their archived advice treats absolute single-night percentages as rough and the night-to-night trend as the trustworthy part, and a 2019 meta-analysis found even total sleep time can be overestimated by minutes at a stretch.
What are deep-sleep numbers still good for?
Direction and drift. Read against your own baseline, a sustained change tells you whether an adjustment worked, and that is the decision the measurement exists to feed. The population benchmark says what normal looks like, and your trend says what changed.
Can you track trends without wearing anything?
Yes, mattress-integrated sensing is the established non-wearable lane, reading heart rate, breathing, and stages from the sleep surface. Such systems carry their own quality gates, on T11+ and above a night needs three hours in bed and two of sleep before a daily report generates, so the trend line holds data that cleared the bar.

articles.title: Após jailbreak, jogos de Nintendo Switch 2 rodam em PC e até iPhone • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Após jailbreak, jogos de Nintendo Switch 2 rodam em PC e até iPhone
Projetos de código aberto permitem rodar títulos exclusivos em outras plataformas, mas exigem uma cópia original dos games.
Uma semana após o primeiro jailbreak do Nintendo Switch 2 via software, diversos jogos exclusivos da Nintendo já rodam em outras plataformas. Publicações no X/Twitter mostram títulos do console funcionando em PCs, no iPhone 18 Pro e até em um computador com macOS.
Ferramentas de código aberto têm facilitado o processo, como o software ns2jb, disponibilizado em 22 de outubro. Jogos como Mario Kart World, Dragon Age e Zelda foram disponibilizados em ports no GitHub sob a licença MIT, que permite o acesso ao código para pesquisa e testes. São projetos que não incluem os jogos em si: para executá-los, é necessário ter uma cópia original de cada título.
Por isso, a disponibilização dos ports, por si só, não configura pirataria. A infração ocorre quando há distribuição ou download não autorizado das imagens ISO dos títulos.
A Nintendo, porém, tem um histórico de ações contra emuladores e ferramentas de acesso a seus jogos. Em 2024, a empresa conseguiu derrubar o Yuzu, conhecido emulador de Nintendo Switch, e pediu a remoção de outras ferramentas semelhantes hospedadas no GitHub.
Mais recentemente, um usuário do Reddit foi condenado a pagar US$ 4,5 milhões (pouco mais de R$ 24 milhões) por violações envolvendo mais de 30 jogos exclusivos do Switch.
No fim de setembro, dois jailbreaks funcionais para o PlayStation 5 foram publicados e provocaram uma onda de ports distribuídos pela internet. Também surgiram aplicativos que oferecem gratuitamente milhares de jogos para rodar no console.
A facilidade com que os sistemas da Sony foram desbloqueados levantou suspeitas sobre o uso de inteligência artificial no processo de análise e exploração do código do console. É possível que o primeiro jailbreak do Switch 2 também tenha contado com ajuda de IA, embora isso ainda não esteja confirmado.
Em meio ao jailbreak do Switch 2 e relatos de games rodando em outras plataformas, novas ferramentas que levam exclusivos do Switch original para PC e celulares ganharam destaque. É o caso do nxnative, projeto open source disponível via GitHub que permite rodar jogos da Nintendo direto no iPhone.
Segundo o TechSpot, isso acontece porque tanto o celular da Apple quanto o console têm chips ARM, facilitando a tradução das informações entre sistemas.
Outros projetos também aproveitam a semelhança para rodar os games exclusivos no celular e mesmo no PC. Dois deles, d2r-mobile e MacNativeGames, estão disponíveis na plataforma de desenvolvedores e têm licença do MIT.

articles.title: Segway renueva su gama alta de patinetes: potencia todoterreno, 80 km de autonomía real y nuevo estándar de certificación
articles.text:
El mercado de los patinetes eléctricos ha dejado de ser un terreno enfocado únicamente al ocio para convertirse en una alternativa real de movilidad diaria para miles de usuarios. Sin embargo, uno de los mayores dolores de cabeza a la hora de comprar un vehículo de movilidad personal (VMP) sigue siendo la brecha entre la autonomía que promete el fabricante y los kilómetros reales que se recorren.
Para solucionar este desajuste y reforzar su posición en la gama alta, Segway ha presentado sus dos nuevos buques insignia: el todoterreno Segway ZT3 MAX (disponible en reserva por 999 euros) y el modelo de larga distancia Segway Ninebot MAX G3 Pro (que se puede prereservar por 1.099 euros). Ambos llegarán al mercado español este mes, acompañados de un nuevo estándar de homologación respaldado por TÜV Rheinland y un plan de garantía posventa mejorado.
Segway ZT3 MAX
Segway MAX G3 Pro
Adiós a los kilómetros teóricos: el estándar de autonomía a velocidad máxima
La principal novedad conceptual que acompaña a estos dos lanzamientos no está únicamente en sus motores o chasis, sino en la transparencia de sus fichas técnicas. Hasta ahora, la autonomía declarada por la mayoría de fabricantes se calculaba en circuitos cerrados, a velocidades muy reducidas (15 km/h o modos Eco) y con usuarios de peso liviano.
Segway ha implantado, junto a la entidad independiente TÜV Rheinland, el sello "Range at Max. Speed". Este procedimiento prueba los patinetes y los exprime al 100% a la velocidad máxima permitida (25 km/h en Europa) y detiene la medición en cuanto el vehículo no es capaz de mantener al menos el 60% de esa velocidad. De este modo, las cifras anunciadas reflejan el rendimiento real que obtendrá el usuario en sus trayectos cotidianos.
Dos perfiles de uso: respuesta todoterreno o viajes de larga distancia
Segway ZT3 MAX
Este patinete está pensado para quienes transitan por carreteras irregulares, vías con adoquines, caminos de tierra o calles con desniveles pronunciados. El ZT3 MAX da un salto importante en rendimiento frente a generaciones anteriores:
- Potencia bruta: su motor entrega picos de 2.200 W, lo que le permite subir pendientes de hasta el 30% de inclinación sin perder empuje.
- Amortiguación avanzada: incorpora una doble suspensión hidráulica de dos etapas acompañada de una horquilla delantera de doble corona.
- Ruedas XL: monta un neumático delantero de 12 pulgadas y uno trasero de 11 pulgadas, diseñados para absorber baches urbanos con firmeza.
- Autonomía real: 60 km a la velocidad máxima sostenida de 25 km/h.
Segway ZT3 MAX
Ninebot MAX G3 Pro
Diseñado para sustituir los desplazamientos interurbanos o cruzar grandes ciudades de punta a punta sin dependencia del cargador:
- Gran capacidad de batería: integra un paquete de 899 Wh (19,2 Ah) que ofrece 80 km de autonomía real a 25 km/h.
- Carga simplificada: prescinde de transformadores externos voluminosos; incluye un sistema de carga rápida integrado con cable directo e incluso soporte para carga de doble entrada.
- Cuadro inteligente: cuadro digital con pantalla TFT a color de 2,4 pulgadas que muestra la ruta mediante navegación giro a giro directo en el manillar.
- Protección frente al agua: cuenta con certificación IPX6 para el cuerpo general del patinete e IPX7 para la batería, junto con neumáticos autosellantes para evitar sobresaltos por pinchazos.

articles.title: Once again, NASA is asking for ideas to rescue Hubble from certain death
articles.text:
The Hubble Space Telescope still shines in the eyes of astronomers after 36 years in orbit, but it is not as nimble as it once was. Left alone, the observatory will plunge back into the atmosphere in the early-to-mid-2030s, closing the book on one of the most famous scientific instruments of the century.
NASA last raised the orbit of Hubble in 2002, when the Space Shuttle Columbia visited the observatory for a servicing mission. The final shuttle servicing flight in 2009 did not reboost the telescope’s orbit, and with the retirement of the shuttle fleet two years later, Hubble has steadily lost altitude with no way to stave off eventual destruction.
The space agency released a Request For Information (RFI) on Thursday asking commercial companies for ideas on how to reboost, service, or a controlled disposal of Hubble. Responses are due November 30. Specifically, NASA is looking for information about companies’ current and near-term capabilities for capturing Hubble and boosting it to an altitude of at least 373 miles (600 km), enhancing the telescope’s performance, or guiding Hubble to a controlled reentry.
“The requirement includes that the boost and/or servicing mission must not harm the HST and that this mission is expected to occur by 2032,” NASA wrote in the RFI. The contractor would be responsible for providing the launch vehicle, servicing spacecraft, mission operations, and “crew if applicable.”
No commitments yet
NASA is not committing to buying a Hubble rescue mission, but officials want to know who might be interested in mounting such a mission, how much it would cost, and which companies would have a realistic shot at reaching Hubble before it falls out of orbit and burns up on reentry. Orbital dynamicists currently predict that it will likely happen in 2033 or 2034 without intervention, but reentry forecasts can change based on solar activity.
It took 24 years for Hubble, which lacks onboard propulsion, to glide from its 2002 altitude of 362 miles (583 km) to its current orbit some 292 miles (470 km) above Earth. A reboost to NASA’s requirement of 373 miles (600 km) would likely keep Hubble in orbit for at least 25 more years.

articles.title: PsiQuantum turns its photonics know-how into an optical switch for supercharging AI data center GPU networks — 8x8 lab prototype loses less light than rivals, with plans to develop larger devices
articles.text:
PsiQuantum turns its photonics know-how into an optical switch for supercharging AI data center GPU networks — 8x8 lab prototype loses less light than rivals, with plans to develop larger devices
Google’s mirror switches have 136 ports; PsiQuantum’s chip has eight, with larger devices in development.
PsiQuantum, a quantum computing company, announced in a release earlier this week that it has turned its low-loss silicon photonics into an optical switch for use in AI data centers. Every optical switch typically comes with loss of light: the more light a switch receives, the less reaches the other side, with the amount of light lost measured in decibels. Typical data center optics can tolerate half the light (3 dB) being lost. PsiQuantum's switch debuted with a demo that typically loses only 1.2 dB of signal, or about a quarter of the light in lab tests, and the all-optical switch can achieve it without an amplifier. The prototype is, however, comparatively small, with eight inputs and outputs (8x8) against competitors’ 32 to 300, but the company says larger devices are in development.
The optical circuit switch (OCS) passes light straight through, from fiber to fiber, without converting it to or from electrical signals. Regular data center switches make that conversion at every hop, which takes power and adds latency. An OCS, instead, uses a fixed light path that it maintains until a change is ordered. Its main penalty comes down to how much light is lost when passing through the switch. PsiQuantum’s switch, which uses circuits etched on a silicon chip with no moving parts, unlike Google’s and Lumentum’s tiny mirrors, or microelectromechanical systems (MEMS), would be used alongside regular packet switches.
Skipping those conversions matters more as AI clusters grow, because moving data between GPUs is quickly becoming a bottleneck. Optics are a high-bandwidth improvement over copper, which has limitations in reach, although a shortage of lasers is a problem for the alternative. Improving communication bandwidth and distance is the goal, so that different racks of GPUs can talk at speed and act as one.
Switches similar to PsiQuantum’s made by Salience Labs and iPronics use built-in amplification and, at least in the former case, are also rated at under 2 dB, or under 37% of the light lost. Google’s mirror-based switch, Palomar, can also typically stay under 2 dB and has 136 ports. Salience’s switch sits at 32 and Lumentum’s at 300, which leaves the eight-port prototype a ways behind on how many fibers it can handle.
| Optical circuit switches by loss and size |  |  |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Switch | Ports (in × out) | Insertion loss, and what the figure is | Reconfiguration | How it switches | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PsiQuantum 8×8 demo | 8×8 | 1.2 dB (about 24% of the light lost), typical in the company’s lab tests | Under 3 ms | Silicon photonics chip, no amplification, no moving parts | 
| Google Palomar | 136×136 | Typically under 2 dB (under 37% lost) across all port pairings; 2 dB worst case | Milliseconds | MEMS mirrors (moving parts) | 
| Lumentum R300 | 300×300 | Close to 1.5 dB (about 29% lost), typical at start of life, Lumentum’s switching GM told Gazettabyte | Not stated | MEMS mirrors (moving parts) | 
| Salience Labs OC-32M | 32×32 | Under 2 dB (under 37% lost) port to port, a ceiling, after built-in amplification | Under 300 µs | Silicon photonics chip with amplification | 
| iPronics ONE-32 | 32 (layout not stated) | Not published | Under 300 µs | Silicon photonics chip with optical amplifiers | 
PsiQuantum's switch is an 8x8, meaning eight in and eight out, and “every input can reach every output.” It’s also “strictly non-blocking,” so a new connection never disturbs ones already in place. In the lab, it measured a typical 1.2 dB insertion loss, 40 dB of crosstalk (about 0.01% of the light leaking to other ports), and under 3 ms of reconfiguration time, all of which exceed “initial targets set for these devices.” The loss figure is measured fiber to fiber, which includes getting light onto and off the chip but not connector losses, PsiQuantum told Tom’s Hardware Premium.
The platform loses very little light at each component, which matters because a quantum computer can tolerate only so much lost light. PsiQuantum’s 2025 Nature paper reports silicon nitride waveguides losing as little as 0.5 dB per meter (about 11% of the light per meter), splitters 0.5 millidecibels, and crossings 1.2 millidecibels, the last two a few hundredths of a percent of the light or less each.
The company also says chip-to-fiber coupling has reached about 60 millidecibels, roughly 1.4% of the light lost, in its best published lab results, although without a full fiber array attached. Those figures set a best case, not a worst case, for a 64-port switch, since light crosses more components as ports are added and the losses add up.
How much loss is acceptable varies with the optics at the end of each link. Coherent, an optics maker, says that using an OCS can add “up to 3 dB additional insertion loss,” but its transceivers are able to work with that. Lumentum told Gazettabyte that 3 dB is good enough to work with off-the-shelf FR4, DR4, and DR8 optical modules using the switch; those are the standard plug-in options used to link GPU servers and switches, at distances of 500 meters to 2 kilometers. PsiQuantum’s 8x8 is built for the O-band, the wavelength range those modules use. PsiQuantum told Semafor that, to be workable, its switch needed insertion loss under 2 to 3 dB.
The 8x8 prototype was designed for conventional data center traffic and comes in well below the 3 dB loss target in a request from Nvidia for proposals, the company says. The port count marks it as a demonstration vehicle, but PsiQuantum has a 64x64 version taped out with a 72x72 underway and is “actively developing larger devices.” With crossings that lose so little light, the scale-up might hold. PsiQuantum declined to share details on future products, though it says the loss, which may be slightly higher, will stay very low.
Speed remains less important than insertion loss for how OCSes are currently used. Google, which has the most deployments, numbering in the “tens of thousands,” uses its switches to resize TPU pods or to route around failed chips, a job its “millisecond-scale” MEMS switches handle. PsiQuantum’s under 3 ms is within that class, but Salience and iPronics claim less than 300 microseconds for their amplified chip switches, which iPronics highlights for mid-workload network rewiring to hide the switch time while chips compute.
There is quite a lot of room for speed to improve, and PsiQuantum already has a material for that, used in an existing 64-port switch for its quantum systems, which need to switch light at gigahertz rates. The material, barium titanate (BTO), changes how it bends light when a voltage is applied, and the company chose it over lithium niobate, a more common selection, because BTO had the strongest effect it could find. This keeps switching elements short and losses low at speeds roughly a million times faster than the demo. BTO is “not required for the demonstration vehicle or initial products,” which use a thermally switched silicon nitride platform, but it is “an additional path to faster, more advanced future products.”
An argument for starting now is that building thousands of such switches for conventional applications would reduce the risk for the packaging, assembly, and supply chain of parts PsiQuantum builds for quantum computing. AI and quantum computing are “complementary technologies,” it says, and this is the chance to put its technology into action. When PsiQuantum hired Rob Soderbery as an executive vice president in July, it said he would advance its silicon photonics platform, “accelerating its application across AI networking and other next-generation computing infrastructure,” hinting at the roadmap. The company’s CHIPS award was finalized in September for “high-performance optical switches,” among other components.
Co-founder Pete Shadbolt praised Google’s alternative MEMS switch but would prefer to have similar-quality switching on a monolithic chip that needs no moving parts. Nvidia has a stake through its venture arm, NVentures, and collaborates with PsiQuantum on “GPU-QPU integration,” that is, graphics and quantum processing units, as well as silicon photonics. Nvidia also joined rival iPronics’ $125 million round in September to develop its second-generation optical switch.
Right now, inside Google, OCSes rewire AI clusters, and research firm Cignal AI expects most deployments to stay there through the end of the decade; outside of Google, OCS is still at “proof-of-concept and early trial.” The firm raised its market estimates earlier this year, though, roughly threefold for 2026 and by more than 40% for 2029. An opening exists for PsiQuantum in GPU networks, which ties into Nvidia’s interest, though adoption there is expected to be limited until then. The company says samples and testing kits have already gone to several computing companies, including GPU vendors and hyperscalers.
PsiQuantum should have commercial products “announced in the coming months,” along with updates on larger devices, while competitor Salience has already demonstrated 64 ports at this year’s European Conference on Optical Communication. Salience’s roadmap already has 128- and 256-port products. Scaling is always an issue, but if PsiQuantum’s figures, which haven’t been independently verified, hold up at 64 ports without amplifiers, then larger monolithic OCSes are on the way.
Shane Downing is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware, covering consumer storage, PC hardware, and AI.

articles.title: Six ans après, un smartphone sur dix est toujours sur Android 11
articles.text:
Google ne publie plus de tableau de bord public régulier sur la répartition des versions d’Android depuis 2018. Les seules données officielles se nichent dans Android Studio, son environnement de développement, et une nouvelle fournée vient d’y apparaître à l’occasion de l’Android Dev Summit des 28 et 29 octobre. Elle recense les appareils actifs ayant contacté le Play Store sur une période de sept jours.
Android 16 prend enfin la tête
Android 16 équipe désormais 25,4 % des appareils, contre 7,5 % en décembre 2025, date de la précédente mise à jour de ces statistiques. À l’époque, Android 15 occupait encore la première place, avec 19,3 % du parc. La version lancée en juin 2025 prend désormais la tête, devant Android 14 (15,3 %) et Android 15 (14,7 %). Au total, 56,4 % des smartphones tournent sur Android 14 ou plus récent. Les chantiers engagés par Google pour accélérer les mises à jour, comme Treble et Mainline, qui rendent une partie du système indépendante des constructeurs, finissent par porter leurs fruits.
Android 17, disponible depuis le 16 juin, ne dépasse pas 1 % du parc après plus de quatre mois. Google a certes publié ses chiffres plus tôt dans le cycle que l’an passé. Android 16 avait bénéficié de près de six mois de déploiement avant la photographie de décembre 2025, contre quatre mois et demi pour son successeur aujourd’hui. Android 8.1, sorti en 2017, fait pourtant mieux, à 1,5 %.
Android 11, l’increvable qui embarrasse
Lancé en septembre 2020, Android 11 reste indéboulonnable et équipe encore 10,5 % des appareils actifs. Six ans après sa sortie, il devance Android 12 (9,6 %) et talonne Android 13 (11,8 %). Mises bout à bout, ces lignes signifient que plus de 30 % du parc tourne sur Android 13 ou une version plus ancienne.
Google a cessé le suivi d’Android 13 en mars 2026 : les appareils concernés ne reçoivent plus de correctifs de sa part, sauf geste de leur fabricant. Un smartphone sur dix fonctionne donc avec un système abandonné de longue date, exposé aux failles découvertes depuis. Depuis juin 2025, l’Union européenne impose pourtant aux constructeurs au moins cinq ans de mises à jour de sécurité après la fin de commercialisation d’un modèle. Cette obligation couvre les modèles récents, et laisse de côté le parc ancien déjà en circulation.

articles.title: 'If the PS5 turns out to have been the perfect Steam Machine all along it would be so funny': custom Linux OS lets you play PC games on your PS5 — but I wouldn't recommend it
articles.text:
Can't afford a Steam Machine? You can now turn your PS5 into one with a new spin on Linux — but I really wouldn't recommend it
As it involves jailbreaking your console
- PS5 Bazzite Deck is a new spin on this gaming-focused version of Linux
- It allows you to boot your PS5 to a Steam Deck interface and play PC games
- You need to jailbreak your Sony console to run it (via the PS5 Linux loader), and that's a risky path to take for a number of reasons
Don't want to fork out all that cash for a Steam Machine? If you've got a PS5, you could turn it into a spin on Valve's gaming PC thanks to a custom version of a Linux distro — although the major catch is you'll need to jailbreak your console.
TechPowerUp noticed the PS5 Bazzite Deck project on GitHub, which takes this flavor of the gaming-focused Bazzite distro and adapts it for Sony's console. (Bazzite Deck is different from vanilla Bazzite, as it was built specifically for handhelds to offer an experience similar to SteamOS for the likes of the Asus ROG Ally — but without some of the headaches of running Valve's OS on that portable).
When PS5 Bazzite Deck is run on a jailbroken console, it'll boot straight into the Steam Deck interface (Steam Gaming Mode), and you can play your PC games from there.
You don't need to install the PS5 Bazzite Deck OS, either; you can just run it from a USB stick (via the PS5 Linux loader). As the developer VivaLaVent explains, when you next restart the PS5, it'll boot its own operating system again, and you'll be back at Sony's welcome hub.
So the PS5 isn't modified by running this OS as such, except for the fact that you have to jailbreak the console (then run the PS5 Linux Loader).
This project is compatible with the base PS5 and PS5 Pro consoles, and you can also switch to a desktop mode running KDE Plasma on your PS5, should you wish.
Of course, game compatibility is going to be hit-and-miss, although a gamer on Reddit observed that they've successfully run Horizon Zero Dawn, Palworld, Genshin Impact, and Rimworld — although Marvel Rivals was a non-starter.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Analysis: interesting times
I should make it very clear up front that I wouldn't recommend jailbreaking your console even as an experiment. There are potential legal ramifications (depending on where you live) with doing so, the possibility of Sony banning your account, and a whole raft of risks (including the third-party software involved, of course). So, if you do want to turn your PS5 into a take on a Steam Machine in this way, proceed at your own risk.
That said, there's an increasing amount of activity around getting the PS5 to run PC games, as you might have seen, so clearly this is something that quite a few gamers are interested in. Most notably, we've seen Playden, which is a very different way of running PC titles on a PS5, by using a compatibility layer (a custom port of Wine) to pull this off. PS5 Bazzite Deck differs in that it replaces the entire OS with a new one, as opposed to running on top of Sony's system.
By all accounts, PS5 Bazzite Deck is pretty slick. One Redditor shares their experience: "I've been using this distro for 4 days, and WOW! Seriously, it's way better than the others. There are constant updates that bring bug fixes."
The DualSense controller support is also niftily implemented by all accounts, as you can pair to both Linux and the PS5 system (saving you from unpairing when switching between the two). The controller's touchpad works like a mouse on the PS5 Bazzite Deck, and seemingly waking from sleep takes only two seconds (much faster than the PS5's normal wake time).
Another gamer on Reddit declares: "If the PS5 turns out to have been the perfect Steam Machine all along, it would be so funny."
But I refer you back to my previous advice on jailbreaking (and game compatibility). Still, this kind of modding is attention-grabbing, to say the least, and we're also seeing it in reverse, with a breakneck pace of development for PS5 emulation on the PC (very much accelerated by the use of AI, it's worth noting).
That effort is, of course, generating a ton of interest given that GTA 6 is nearly here, and indeed there are theories floating around that the work on that PS5 emulator could force Rockstar to launch the PC port much earlier than intended (before an emulated version is up and running). The rumor mill reckons we could see the PC version of GTA 6 early in 2027 as a result.

articles.title: How a GLP-1 Companion App Can Simplify Daily Health Logging - Tech Guide
articles.text:
A meal photo in your camera roll rarely tells the whole story. The portion you finished, the water you drank and a note about how you felt might live in three different places. Finding those details again takes more effort than recording them.
Glowise is a GLP-1 companion app designed to bring medication records, meals, protein, water, weight, activity and side-effect notes together. For adults using prescribed GLP-1 medication, that creates a practical place to maintain daily records and prepare questions for their healthcare professional.
Give Each Type of Information a Clear Home
Start by deciding where each record belongs. Keep medication entries in the medication log, meals in the food record, and observations in dated notes. Use calendar reminders to prompt an action, then record what actually happened separately.
This distinction matters when reviewing a busy week. A scheduled alert shows what you planned; a completed entry shows what you recorded doing.
Glowise supports people using injections or oral medication. Enter the routine prescribed for you and check the details before saving. Questions about changing a dose, missing medication or altering timing should go to your prescriber or pharmacist.
You also do not need to copy every old note into a new system. Choose a starting date and retain earlier information somewhere accessible. That gives the new record a clear beginning.
Choose the Easiest Input Method for the Moment
Typing every ingredient is awkward when lunch is getting cold. Glowise offers VoiceLog, food-photo recognition, barcode and nutrition-label scanning, and menu scanning to reduce manual entry.
Each method suits a different situation. A spoken description works when your hands are occupied. A package label provides a reference for a packaged food. A photograph preserves a visual reminder of a mixed meal.
Try these methods with food you regularly eat:
| Situation | Recording approach | Detail to verify | 
| Homemade lunch | Photo or spoken description | Ingredients and the portion eaten | 
| Packaged snack | Barcode or nutrition-label scan | Product variant and serving quantity | 
| Restaurant meal | Menu scan and personal note | Additions, substitutions and leftovers | 
| A drink during the day | A brief entry | Amount and unit used | 
Choose the method that requires the least correction for that meal. There is little value in using an impressive feature if fixing its output takes longer than a simple entry.
Check AI Estimates Before Saving
A food photograph contains incomplete information. It may show a bowl of soup without revealing the recipe, or a plate before you leave part of the meal unfinished.
Review the proposed food, portion and nutrition estimate. Correct the details you know and preserve uncertainty where you do not have reliable information.
For example, if you photographed a full sandwich but ate half, the saved quantity should reflect that difference. If the filling was misidentified, correct it before relying on the nutrition estimate.
Use protein, nutrition and hydration targets agreed with your healthcare professional. Logging features help retain information; their estimates do not establish your individual requirements.
Add Context While It Is Still Fresh
A short note made at the time is easier to interpret than a reconstruction several days later. Include when something happened, what you noticed and how it affected an ordinary activity.
“Felt uncomfortable after lunch and left part of the meal” offers a clearer observation than “bad day.” Keep the wording descriptive rather than assigning a cause.
Recording two events close together does not establish that one caused the other. A clinician can help interpret concerns using the broader medical context.
For symptoms or concerns requiring attention, contact an appropriate healthcare professional. Save the record for that conversation without waiting for a weekly review.
Turn a Week of Entries Into Useful Questions
Set aside a short period to review the records you have collected. Begin with completeness: identify missing days, duplicate meals or an incorrect unit before interpreting a chart.
A GLP-1 tracker such as Glowise keeps several types of information available for this review. Find the dates behind an observation, then write down the question you want to ask.
For instance, instead of trying to explain a vague memory of several difficult meals, identify the relevant entries and ask what additional information would help your clinician understand the situation.
Keep questions concise. A date, an observation and the point you need clarified make a more usable discussion note than a long, unfiltered history.
Check how information can be accessed during an appointment. Verify any sharing or export options in the current app before depending on them.
Keep the Routine Manageable on Busy Days
Decide which entries matter most for the tracking plan you have agreed with your healthcare professional. Complete those first when time is limited.
Avoid creating precise-looking records from uncertain memories. If you cannot remember a portion, leave an explanatory note rather than presenting a guess as a measurement.
A brief daily check can catch common mistakes:
- Confirm medication entries reflect what was recorded, rather than scheduled reminders.
- Check meal quantities and obvious recognition errors.
- Keep water measurements in consistent units.
- Add dates and context to personal observations.
- Leave missing information identifiable.
The aim is a record you can understand later. An incomplete entry with honest context is more useful than an apparently perfect history built from guesses.
Check the Practical Details Before Committing
Read Glowise’s current privacy information and subscription terms before entering sensitive records. Check requested permissions, account controls and the process for deleting data.
Confirm compatibility with your device and country’s app store. If wearable access or integration with another health service is important, verify that specific capability in the current product information.
Glowise’s appeal is the combination of several records and flexible food-entry methods. Test those features through an ordinary week, including a busy day, and judge whether they reduce the work of recording and retrieving your own information.
FAQ
What does Glowise bring together?
Glowise combines medication and dose records, food and nutrition, protein, water, weight, activity and side-effect notes.
Can I use voice or photos to record meals?
Glowise offers VoiceLog and food-photo recognition, alongside scanning options. Review the suggested entry before saving.
Does Glowise explain the medical cause of a symptom?
It provides a place to record observations. Medical interpretation and treatment decisions belong with a qualified healthcare professional.
Do I need to record everything perfectly?
Keep entries accurate where possible and mark uncertainty clearly. Follow the tracking priorities discussed with your healthcare professional.
