articles.title: Windows 11 ne démarre plus ? La réinstallation sans clé USB débarque enfin pour tout le monde
articles.text:
Après plusieurs mois de tests, Microsoft commence à déployer Cloud Rebuild auprès du grand public. Cette nouvelle fonction permet de réinstaller Windows 11 depuis Internet, même lorsque le système refuse de démarrer.
Depuis sa présentation en juillet, Cloud Rebuild a gagné plusieurs fonctions, dont une option d'effacement sécurisé des données et la possibilité pour les administrateurs informatiques de déclencher une réinstallation à distance. Ces nouveautés, jusqu'ici réservées aux versions expérimentales de Windows 11, arrivent avec la mise à jour facultative KB5127936, publiée le 28 octobre pour les versions 25H2 et 26H2. Leur déploiement sera toutefois progressif, si bien que même après avoir installé la mise à jour, certains PC devront patienter avant de pouvoir en profiter.
Une réinstallation complète, même lorsque Windows est inaccessible
Pour rappel, Cloud Rebuild permet de réinstaller Windows 11 en téléchargeant directement depuis Windows Update une image du système et les pilotes nécessaires à l'ordinateur. L'opération se déroule dans l'environnement de récupération Windows (WinRE), accessible après plusieurs échecs de démarrage. Plus besoin de préparer une clé USB sur un autre PC ni de disposer d'une image de récupération locale. Vous pouvez également lancer la fonction lorsque Windows fonctionne encore, depuis les Paramètres > Système > Récupération.
Microsoft profite de ce déploiement pour améliorer la connexion Internet depuis WinRE. L'environnement de récupération peut désormais réutiliser automatiquement certains profils Wi-Fi déjà enregistrés dans Windows, y compris des réseaux professionnels compatibles. Une nouveauté bienvenue pour les outils de réparation qui doivent accéder aux serveurs de Microsoft, sans obliger l'utilisateur à reconfigurer sa connexion. Il faudra néanmoins que WinRE fonctionne correctement et dispose de pilotes réseau compatibles.
Attention toutefois à ne pas confondre Cloud Rebuild avec une réparation classique. La procédure reformate le disque système et supprime les fichiers locaux, les comptes, les applications et les paramètres. Deux possibilités sont proposées : une suppression standard ou un effacement sécurisé reposant sur les capacités du matériel de stockage, destiné, par exemple, aux ordinateurs que l'on souhaite revendre ou recycler. Les données déjà sauvegardées dans OneDrive ne sont pas concernées.
La mise à jour KB5127936 étant facultative, rien ne vous oblige à l'installer immédiatement. Vous pourrez également récupérer ces changements avec le Patch Tuesday du 10 novembre.

articles.title: Óscar Puente, ministro de Transportes: "El sistema LZB se ha caído 170 veces este año, está dentro de la normalidad europea"
articles.text:
Una rueda de prensa de más de hora y media da mucho de sí. La última comparecencia de Óscar Puente ha versado sobre los problemas del sistema ferroviario español, el señalamiento del operador de Atocha responsable de la línea o de si va o no a dimitir.
Y entre tantas declaraciones, una llama especialmente la atención.
170 veces. Son las ocasiones en las que el sistema LZB de seguridad que se utiliza en la línea de alta velocidad Madrid-Sevilla se ha caído en lo que llevamos de año. Así lo ha asegurado Óscar Puente durante su intervención. Eso quiere decir que, de media, en los 300 días que discurren entre el 1 de enero y el 28 de octubre de 2026, el sistema reflejó algún problema más de la de mitad de los días.
Dentro de la normalidad. Según Puente, esta cifra entra dentro de la normalidad europea. Incluso, asegura, los datos de problemas con el sistema son estables y en los dos últimos años se ha registrado cierto descenso en el número de interrupciones en la señal.
Lo que no ha confirmado Puente es si estos problemas son mayores o menores que en las líneas donde el sistema ERTMS está instalado. Este protocolo se pondrá en marcha, según el ministro de Transportes, en enero de 2027. Tampoco se han dado datos de qué número de fallos en el sistema tienen en Europa, sólo que está "dentro de la normalidad".
Interrupciones de señal. Tanto maquinistas consultados por Xataka como los portavoces del Sindicato Español de Maquinistas Ferroviarios (Semaf) han confirmado que los problemas de transmisión con el sistema LZB son recurrentes.
Eso sí, nos aseguran que generalmente estas pérdidas de transmisión son momentáneas. Nos lo describen, de hecho, como un ordenador que colapsa y se cierra inesperadamente pero que apenas unos segundos después está ya funcionando. La diferencia esta vez es que el sistema se cayó en un tramo de más de 60 kilómetros y eso, señalan desde el Semaf y los maquinistas consultados, no es habitual.
En la declaración simplemente se ha apuntado a que hay 170 incidencias registradas en lo que va de año con el sistema LZB pero no se ha entrado a valorar cuántas de ellas fueron tan graves como las del pasado 28 de octubre.
Seguro pero obsoleto. En la rueda de prensa también se ha insistido en recalcar que el sistema LZB es seguro y que no se sustituye por el ERTMS por esta cuestión. La línea, que debía tener este sistema activo más moderno, se actualiza porque el LZB está obsoleto: se fabrican menos recambios y la Unión Europea obliga a contar con este sistema por una cuestión de interoperabilidad entre países, imprescindible con las liberalizaciones ferroviarias.
Preguntados sobre esto, los maquinistas han recalcado a Xataka que el sistema es seguro y confirman las declaraciones de Puente. Aunque el sistema LZB lleve instalado desde 1992 en la línea y la tecnología sea de 1970, el LZB es igual de seguro que el más moderno ERTMS.
Los responsables de circulación, sin embargo, con los que hemos hablado tienen una opinión ligeramente diferente. Confirman también que el sistema es seguro y que el cambio es una cuestión de mandato europeo pero señalan que las versiones más modernas del ERTMS ofrecen facilidades que reducen los riesgos. Es igual de seguro pero más fiable.
Menos riesgo de fallo. Parte de esos riesgos, nos señalan desde el Sindicato de Circulación Ferroviaria (SCF), está en los componentes físicos del sistema LZB. El cable contiene cobre por lo que es más atractivo para robarlo. También explican que las conexiones con el sistema ERTMS son más fiables por lo que el número de interrupciones en la señal debería ser menor.
Desde Semaf comparten esta opinión y señalan que cuantas menos interrupciones menos tendrá que intervenir un humano para gestionar el tráfico en la línea, lo que debería reducir las oportunidades en las que se comete un error.

articles.title: A University of Kentucky employee asked to be exempted from using AI for his 'religious' beliefs
articles.text:
Editor's take: Many research and enterprise organizations are trying to force staff to use AI tools wherever and whenever they can. Needless to say, the backlash is as strong as the C-suite's stubborn determination to push AI, even where there is absolutely no need for it.
David Durman might be the first employee to receive a special exemption from using AI tools on religious grounds. The 45-year-old research administrator at the University of Kentucky identifies as a humanist, a belief system that apparently requires him to avoid AI-based workflows. Durman's job doesn't require AI either, which is likely the main reason the university ultimately agreed to his unusual request.
Durman decided to take the religious route after his university's administrators began asking all employees to adopt AI in their work. In a recent interview, Durman said that he felt the request ran counter to his fundamental ideas about what it means to be human. In his view, the university was asking a fully conscious adult to offload his entire thought process to a chatbot to perform his daily duties.
Durman stated that "the process and work involved in thinking through situations, through my work, through my ethics, through the way I handle other people, is a key component in being able to develop myself as a moral person." Offloading that process to a commercial LLM tool was essentially undercutting his agency as a moral and conscious being.
Broadly speaking, humanism is neither a religion in the conventional sense nor a clearly defined philosophical movement. Rather, it is a philosophical stance shared by various intellectual traditions that emphasize universal human qualities, the pursuit of knowledge, and the improvement of individual and social conditions.
Durman's "quest" was supported by the American Humanist Association (AHA), with both parties seeking a religious accommodation from the University of Kentucky under Title VII. Federal law allows employees to request workplace accommodations that enable them to adhere to their religious beliefs.
The university agreed to Durman's request in September, granting the administrator special permission to avoid using Copilot, ChatGPT, and other LLM-based "stochastic parrots" in his work. Before working with the AHA, Durman sent a letter to university administrators in which he quoted the Humanist Manifesto III, which the organization first published in 2003.
In the interview, Durman confirmed that he could do his job without resorting to chatbots. At the university, he helps researchers with grant applications and related tasks. According to AHA attorney Alexandria Huiskens, the parties had a "very collegial" meeting during which Durman confirmed that avoiding AI would not burden his department or reduce its productivity.
Recent polls suggest that employees are increasingly stressed by organizations' efforts to fully integrate AI into their workflows. Durman argues that AI could have a very negative impact on society as a whole, while humanist principles run counter to what he sees as a turbo-capitalistic, nihilistic approach to exploiting human nature. In this regard, Huiskens said Durman's "religion" could be considered a "comprehensive way of life," much like Christianity and Islam.

articles.title: Supersonic airliner in doubt as company shifts to powering AI data centers
articles.text:
Boom Supersonic CEO Blake Scholl recently declared “it’s time for a renaissance in energy and in supersonic flight” as the supersonic airliner company unveiled a Colorado factory dedicated to making gas turbines for AI data centers. But Boom may be facing turbulence after early backers for both ventures have questioned the company’s delivery timeline or backed out entirely.
One of the company’s first customers, United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby, has expressed doubts about Boom’s original plan to deliver the first Overture supersonic airliner in 2029. Kirby’s latest frank assessment came during an interview with the Office Hours: Business Edition podcast that appeared on October 28, 2026.
“‘29 is their official timeline,” Kirby told podcast host Monica Langley. “It’s not going to happen in ‘29—it’s going to take longer.”
Boom first made headlines for flying its XB-1 demonstrator aircraft in 2024 and 2025 to demonstrate a “boomless cruise” concept that harnesses the Mach cutoff phenomenon. Such a feat involves flying just beyond supersonic speeds at higher altitudes under specific atmospheric conditions, so that the aircraft’s shockwaves refract upward and minimize the impact on the ground.
The company’s plan to revive supersonic air travel has been backed by the Trump administration via efforts to ease regulations. In June 2026, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) proposed a new rule overturning a long-standing ban on commercial supersonic flights over the United States, following an executive order from President Donald Trump.
Boom’s press releases have previously described achieving aircraft certification and carrying the first paying customers by 2029. The company has conditional agreements with American Airlines, Japan Airlines, and United Airlines involving non-refundable deposits of unknown amounts that would allow the airlines to fully purchase the Overture aircraft once it becomes commercially available.

articles.title: A primer to key LLM concepts — KV cache, weights, quantization, and more
articles.text:
A primer on key AI LLM concepts — KV cache, weights, quantization, and how inference actually works
Everyone knows about hallucination, but a handful of topics are often unclear. We'll fix that.
As hardware for running local AI models continues to move to the forefront, such as Nvidia's RTX Spark, a new set of acronyms, definitions, and terminology is popping up. Given the pace of releases, we've put together a list of AI's new nomenclature to familiarize you with new concepts and pieces of terminology that you'll likely see in Tom's Hardware Premium articles.
This primer should get you started on the world of AI and be handy the next time news on the topic comes around, and possibly when you're downloading some models to try out and tweak for yourself. For the context of this article, we're going to stick with notions related to text LLMs, or in common parlance, chat, programming, and most agentic bots.
Model
This is probably the easiest one: a model is the LLM itself (a Large Language Model), computed from training sets of mostly text data on the scale of terabytes to petabytes. That training information comes from the internet, books, video and audio transcripts, and other sources.
The model is roughly analogous to a set of highly advanced layers of statistical analysis of relationships between tokens — words or parts of words, computer code, punctuation, and other symbols. The tokens themselves aren't part of the model, but they are packaged along with it. An AI model generates tokens in its outputs.
Weights
Those computing layers within an AI model would be useless without corresponding weights, which represent how strong the connection is between sections of tokens, sort of like how a pathway between neurons is more traveled than others. When the model runs, these values end up establishing how tokens end up relating to each other.
Example: the weights of the connections between "na" and each next part for "naval", "nachos", or "naruto" will all be different, and the higher the weight, the more often that word appears in training data. Importantly, weights cannot change without re-training the model, or parts of it.
When you see LLM specs online, you'll see something like "4B", "8B+", "20B", and so on and so forth. That shows how many parameters, or weights, the model uses, and it's generally measured in billions for consumer-grade models, and trillions for frontier models like GPT, Claude, and Kimi.
Note that a model having more weights than another doesn't automatically mean it's smarter. Just like with CPU clock speeds, it's not just about getting a higher number — bigger is usually better, yes, but you want those weights to be meaningful for the output.
You may also have heard about "open-weight" models versus "closed" models. Those refer to models like Llama, DeepSeek, and Kimi, which are effectively free-to-use, since the entities behind them freely publish the weights online. You can tweak the weights to your heart's content, if you wish, and come up with your own spin on things, as long as you have the hardware to run it. Note that downloading a free model doesn't reveal anything about how it was trained or how the weights were calculated — think downloading a free customizable application, not open-source software.
Data types and quantization
FP16, INT8, FP4, all sound like acronyms in some military handbook, but they're simple to interpret. All programs use numbers of varying width and precision, depending on their purpose: a simple money counter in your favorite game might be fine with a 32-bit integer that can represent 0 to 2^32 (INT32), while a value held in memory for a highly precise scientific measurement may need floating-point 64-bit arithmetic (FP64).
As memory is an exceedingly finite resource, good developers try to use the smallest units they can get away with, a notion that's particularly important in the VRAM-limited world of GPUs. Predictably, these chips became particularly adept at handling lower-precision values as a tradeoff between processing speed and numerical accuracy. A particular datatype isn't better or worse, as that assessment will depend on what it's used for.
When training an AI model, the labs will want to use as high a precision as they can for the weights, but keeping that in the final version would make for a prohibitively large and slow LLM. That's where the concept of quantization comes in, which is a fancy word for "clever rounding." As one of the steps after training, several passes are made to transform highly precise weights. Each AI lab has its own secret sauce about how to do this, as it's a critical step.
Frontier models predominantly use relatively high precision for their weights (BF16), in order to maintain response quality, nuance, and reasoning ability (an analogy would be deciding how accurate you want a GPS location to be — miles or inches). Open-weight models often have several versions with different quantization levels depending on what your hardware can bear — for example, Llama 3.3 70B can be run in full BF16 or quantized INT4 flavors.
The lower the precision, the more likely it can be run on consumer hardware. AI models listed on Hugging Face may have several quantization levels to fit certain levels of hardware, trading response accuracy for size. Consumer-grade models use smaller data types so they can fit on your Mac Studio, RTX Spark, or graphics card.
Context window
"Context window" is another term you've heard a lot and probably seen firsthand, likely in Claude Code's UI as a broad indicator of how long your session can go before the bot starts acting a little dumb. It's measured in tokens, with one million being a common number for frontier models, and it's almost directly analogous to RAM in a computer.
The context window is the LLM's thinking space, and it needs to contain everything associated with your session, not just the current question. Along with all your questions and its replies, it contains system-level prompts, all files you uploaded, the content of links it looked up, plus any associated data.
Crucially, while for you all these things are distinct concepts, for the LLM, they get reduced to tokens in one large pile: the context window. This is also why separating "data" from "code" is technically impossible — the best that modern models do is an approximation of that distinction.
LLMs don't think — when answering a new question, they re-run a statistics program over all the tokens and predict the next handful, so having a larger context window is beneficial (at the cost of VRAM), hence the one-million figure that's currently popular. But even statistical algorithms have their limits.
Even if you increase the window to, say, three million tokens, you may find that your LLM's prediction starts breaking down even though it hasn't run out. This is amusingly called the "lost in the middle" effect, where the bot will pay attention to the start and end of the conversation but will forget things down the middle. Thus, each model is finely tuned to the size of its context window.
KV Cache
If you've looked into using LLMs locally, or by way of running a remote GPU, you may have heard about the "KV cache" time and again, and that you need to reserve VRAM for it, or store it on a fast SSD if you absolutely must. This is a set of data that's created when the model runs, but that's actually reusable between queries in the same session.
The data that's saved and reused can be described as "the relations between tokens for this session." For example, the ever-popular sentence "you're right to push back" can be tokenized as "you-'re-ri-ght-to-pu-sh-back". The dashes between each token represent a vector (or array), called KV for key-value, that is used for determining which token gets picked next.
Since the text generation is linear, the math for calculating each new token needs every KV preceding it. Thus, if you're asking repeated questions in the same session, you'll want the KVs reused to avoid the expense of recalculating them over and over again not just with each round of conversation, but with each additional token.
Remember, an LLM doesn't simply answer the question you just posted — it always analyzes the entire conversation from the top to eventually generate tokens for your response. In a long conversation with 300,000 tokens, not having the cache would mean recalculating the KVs for all of them, a slow operation that gets disproportionately slower still as the interactions grow. This excellent blog post has a more detailed example.
Remember quantization? That's also applied here — modern models reduce the precision of the KV cache's content compared to their initial values, trading a minor accuracy loss for all new tokens in the session, in exchange for keeping VRAM usage down. In fact, with large context windows and conversations, the KV cache may well eat more space than the model and weights themselves.
Mixture-of-Experts (MoE)
Previously, AI firms touted how many more parameters their newest model had. Now, the race seems to have shifted to who can include more experts in any given model. That description may conjure a mental image of many tiny scientists living inside a knowledge laboratory, each handling a specific topic, but that's not quite how it works.
Mixture-of-experts, or MoE, is essentially a set of sub-models within the main model. When training starts, all sub-models get the same dataset, but the choice of weights is randomized ever so slightly for each one. Each sub-model will value tokens a bit differently from the rest, and due to how the training process reinforces patterns (called the "rich-get-richer" effect), related tokens will tend to converge together, so you end up with "experts" on sets of tokens.
A common misconception is to think that these experts are related to topics (like programming), but they're only establishing relations between tokens, meaning they'll be more accurate for certain words and text patterns, but devoid of any concept of what they're about. The fact that an expert might offer pretty good responses in regard to landscape painting is a happy accident, not a feature.
You may be thinking that this makes the models larger, and that maybe just the one generalist expert may prove a wiser choice. That's correct, but the trick is that the models only activate certain experts, meaning that only a portion of the model is actually running, thus at higher speed than a generic LLM.
This model selection happens on a per-token basis, too, as a router re-selects experts for each incoming token. For visualizing this, think of brain scan patterns where different areas light up depending on words heard. In practical terms, it means the model can answer more accurately in certain sections, while answering the question faster — albeit at the cost of higher VRAM usage.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
RAG is a concept that's pretty easy to describe, and yet one of the most powerful ones when used with any given model. In short, it can be described as: your chat application runs a few Google searches, feeds them to the model, and voila, there's now much more and fresher information to answer your question. This additional information can come in most any form: company documents, reports, emails, or spreadsheets — anything that you might supply to the model yourself, directly tokenized into its context window.
While broadly speaking most contemporary LLM chat applications run searches, activating RAG, usually triggered by selecting a "web search" switch or sometimes enabling "thinking" or "high effort" mode, will explicitly instruct the application to find as much data as it believes necessary to answer a query. Given that pure context is often key to answering many questions, and do so in an informational manner, RAG is among the most powerful tools available.
Fun fact: the search queries the application will search for are usually generated by a smaller, separate model that will, for example, say what web searches are bound to give the best results, or what to look for in a linked Office 365 account.
The main drawback is that it can be extremely computing-intensive, as the text for your questions and responses may consume, say, 10,000 tokens, yet the information in the retrieved webpages can take hundreds of thousands of tokens all on their own. For example, the Perplexity service was built with an emphasis on RAG usage, and judging from personal experience and user reports, it's usually much more competent and context-aware when answering questions, even though it's underpinned by the same models as everyone else.
Inference, Prefill and Decode
Inference is the act of using a trained model to generate outputs or tokens. It happens every time you send a prompt, and it's where all of the elements that we've discussed above come into play. Inference can be split into two primary parts: Prefill and Decode.
Prefill is the first phase of inference. Essentially, all of the input history (or your prompt) is tokenized and then processed by an AI model. This can include documents, code, and more. These inputs also dictate what gets put into your KV cache. Prefill is processed all at once in parallel, which often means that prefill times are often faster than overall outputs.
Prefill is a large part of the overall workload when measuring how long it takes for a specific chip or piece of hardware can take to output its first token, also known as "time to first token" (TTFT), a common AI benchmark, usually reported alongside prefill tokens per second. Longer prompts take longer to prefill, and context, KV cache, and everything else we've discussed are taken into account.
Decode is the second phase of inference. After a prefill has processed your input and has built the KV cache, the AI model then generates its response one token at a time, which must be done sequentially in order to determine the ones that come after, which means that the step cannot be performed in parallel, unlike prefill. Decode is usually also dictated by context, and reads from a model's KV cache during this step. Decode is usually limited by memory bandwidth, instead of raw compute, as streaming single tokens from weights and reading the KV cache is a bandwidth-intensive task, meaning memory speeds matter more. You'll usually see Decode speeds referred to as tokens-per-second (TPS).
Speculative Decode is a technique that makes those single tokens in the decode step stream faster, without changing the overall output. A drafting mechanism guesses several upcoming tokens, and then the model attempts to verify them in a parallel pass (almost like an additional prefill step). The model then verifies the pass itself; if the guesses are good, then the model's outputs are indeed correct, you get tokens for less of a computational cost during a given decode pass, and when they're bad, they are rejected by the main model during verification, since the main model's output is always what's kept.
Multi-token prediction (MTP) attempts to predict the next set of tokens at once, rather than only serving the next token. This is often built into AI models when they are trained with multiple steps. This can serve as the built-in drafting mechanism required for speculative decode.
This is a non-exhaustive list of concepts critical to understanding how AI models and LLMs work, but it is by no means complete. We will continue to update and refine this article as we add more.
Bruno Ferreira is a contributing writer for Tom's Hardware. He has decades of experience with PC hardware and assorted sundries, alongside a career as a developer. He's obsessed with detail and has a tendency to ramble on the topics he loves. When not doing that, he's usually playing games, or at live music shows and festivals.

articles.title: Chinese hackers build PHP2SHELL exploit, use it to root 25 servers, breach US government-affiliated firewalls
articles.text:
Chinese hackers build PHP2SHELL exploit, use it to root 25 servers, breach US government-affiliated firewalls
Palo Alto Networks firewalls running outdated OS seem to be the target
- Researchers report the first confirmed PHP2Shell compromises, targeting organizations linked to the US government
- Attackers chained PHP2Shell with a Linux privilege-escalation flaw to gain root access and persistence
- Breaches progressed from initial compromise to Active Directory attacks within minutes, underscoring patching urgency
We now have confirmation of the first successful exploits of the infamous PHP2Shell vulnerability discovered earlier this month.
The news comes courtesy of cybersecurity outfit Dream, who claim to have seen attackers breach organizations affiliated with the US government.
PHP2Shell is a name given to two critical-severity vulnerabilities found in PHP. When they were first disclosed, most of the cybersecurity community went full panic mode, given that PHP powers roughly 70% of all websites and web apps on the internet, and there was no patch at the time. The flaws allegedly enabled complete website takeover, and some government and education organizations in Europe even preemptively shut down their websites, in anticipation of mass exploitation attempts.
But after the dust settled, a strange thing happened - there were no successful attacks. Researchers were seeing attempts and probes, but no successful breaches. Amazon said it observed first attacks four days before the patch, and Cloudflare later tracked “thousands” of attempts in the 10 hours before the patch was announced. This grew to tens of thousands within an hour of disclosure, and hundreds of thousands within two hours. Now, it’s gone into the millions.
Some said exploiting the bugs was easier said than done, and that threat actors were hitting different roadblocks, including Address Space Layout Randomization, a security feature that randomly changes where a program’s code and data are stored in memory every time it runs. Still, they warned that all of that might be temporary, and that a successful hit was a question of “when”, not “if”.
Targeting firewalls
Now it seems the claims were on point, as Dream says Chinese threat actors successfully chained PHP2Shell with a Linux kernel privilege-escalation flaw against Palo Alto Networks firewalls, breaching 25 servers, some allegedly belonging to US government-affiliated organizations.
The attacks started on October 23 2026, probing firms in the US, Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea, and soon focused on Palo Alto Networks’ PAN-OS-powered devices, running an older, vulnerable version of the OS.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
According to Dream, the crooks chained PHP2Shell with Fragnesia, a local privilege escalation flaw that allows unprivileged users to obtain root access. It was disclosed in mid-May this year and is tracked as CVE-2026-46300.
After breaking into the devices, the attackers ran some 40 custom post-exploitation scripts, Dream added.
“Within hours of compromising a US government-affiliated firewall, they had tunneled into the internal network, compromised a third server using the same PHP2Shell exploit, and launched a full Active Directory attack campaign - all through a chain that started with a single unauthenticated HTTPS request to a management interface that should never have been exposed to the internet,” the company’s report reads.
Not automated
To make matters worse, the researchers believe the attackers still have unabated access.
“The total chain - from unauthenticated HTTPS connection to persistent root webshell - completes in under 15 minutes,” Dream said. The researchers could not say what the endgame was here because that information was not found in the artifacts they retrieved. Besides the obvious, which seems to be persistent access and credential theft, the threat actors could do anything from dropping backdoors to exfiltrating sensitive information.
In the context of “Black October”, and the fact we’re seeing a significant increase in automated attacks, it is also worth mentioning that this incident was likely not AI-powered.
Dream did find evidence of AI usage but believes it was not fully automated. Claude Code was installed, as was an offensive security platform called AIscan, which was configured with Chinese AI models DeepSeek and Kimi. Furthermore, they found API keys for FOFA, a Chinese counterpart to the Shodan search engine.
With the help of FOFA, the attackers allegedly identified around 19,000 internet-connected Palo Alto Networks firewalls, which they used as a starting point for their attacks.
Via The Register

articles.title: What Happens to Your Systems at 3am: Lessons From People Who Watch Networks Overnight - Tech Guide
articles.text:
The Quiet Hours: Why Overnight Network Monitoring Matters
When most of us are asleep, the unseen guardians of the digital world are wide awake, watching over the networks and systems that power our businesses. These overnight hours, particularly around 3am, are critical for IT infrastructure because this is when unusual activity often surfaces, whether due to cyberattacks exploiting off-peak vulnerabilities or system failures that quietly escalate. Despite the stillness outside, the digital realm is vibrant with activity-some routine, some threatening, and all vital to understand.
Understanding what happens during these quiet hours can offer invaluable insights into maintaining robust, resilient networks. IT teams who specialize in overnight monitoring have unique perspectives on system behavior, risk mitigation, and proactive maintenance – lessons that any business relying on digital operations can benefit from. Their vigilance helps prevent small issues from snowballing into costly incidents, ensuring systems are ready to support daily operations when the workday begins.
The Night Shift: What IT Professionals Observe
Overnight network watchers often see patterns that daytime operations might miss. For example, automated backups typically run during off-hours, but if these processes fail silently, the consequences can be disastrous for data integrity and recovery efforts. Similarly, cybercriminals frequently target the early morning hours, exploiting reduced staffing to launch attacks such as ransomware, phishing campaigns, or data exfiltration attempts. These threats exploit the natural lull in human oversight to maximize impact.
These professionals must be adept at identifying anomalies in network traffic, server performance, and application behavior. A sudden spike in outbound data, unexpected login attempts, or unusual use of system resources can all be early warning signs of larger problems. Detecting these signs early requires a combination of sophisticated monitoring tools and experienced analysts who understand the context and potential implications of each alert.
Businesses looking to strengthen their overnight monitoring capabilities are often hiring TISDCS, leveraging the expertise of specialized IT service providers to ensure constant vigilance and rapid response. Outsourcing to skilled providers with a focus on overnight network supervision can significantly reduce downtime and security risks. These providers bring advanced technologies and a dedicated workforce trained to detect and respond to incidents in real-time, offering an added layer of protection that many organizations find difficult to maintain internally.
Real-World Insights From Industry Leaders
According to the CEO of Treasure Valley IT, maintaining a proactive overnight monitoring strategy is essential for protecting business continuity. Their experience highlights how many companies underestimate the volume and complexity of issues that arise during these hours. For example, network latency problems that develop overnight can impact morning operations if not addressed promptly. Delays in detecting and resolving such issues can cascade, affecting customer experience and internal workflows.
Moreover, the CEO emphasizes the importance of combining automated monitoring tools with human expertise. Automated alerts can detect many problems, but human analysts are vital for interpreting data contextually and prioritizing incidents for immediate action. This hybrid approach balances efficiency with insight, enabling faster resolution and minimizing false positives that can otherwise overwhelm IT teams.
The Cost of Ignoring the Night Watch
Ignoring overnight network monitoring can lead to significant financial and operational consequences. Studies show that 60% of data breaches go undetected for months, with many initial intrusions occurring during off-hours when monitoring is minimal. This delay in detection allows attackers to establish persistent footholds, increasing the potential damage.
Furthermore, downtime costs businesses an average of $5,600 per minute, underscoring the urgency of rapid incident detection and resolution. The financial impact of outages is compounded by lost productivity, reputational damage, and regulatory penalties, making proactive monitoring a critical investment.
By investing in robust overnight monitoring, companies can reduce mean time to detection (MTTD) significantly-some report improvements of up to 50%-which translates into faster containment and remediation of incidents. Faster detection not only limits damage but also enables IT teams to learn from incidents, strengthening defenses over time.
Common Overnight Network Events and How to Handle Them
- Backup Failures: Automated backups are scheduled during low-traffic hours to minimize disruption, but hardware failures, software bugs, or network issues can interrupt these processes. Prompt alerts and verification mechanisms are essential to ensure data integrity. Regular testing of backup systems and restoration drills can prevent unpleasant surprises when data recovery is needed most.
- Unauthorized Access Attempts: Cyber attackers often test credentials or exploit vulnerabilities in the early morning. Multi-factor authentication (MFA), strict access controls, and continuous monitoring can mitigate these risks. Analysts must investigate suspicious login patterns promptly to prevent breaches.
- System Resource Spikes: Unexpected CPU or memory usage spikes may indicate malware activity, resource-hungry processes, or misconfigured applications. Early detection allows IT teams to isolate and resolve the problem before it affects users or leads to system crashes.
- Network Latency and Outages: Infrastructure issues such as hardware degradation, faulty cables, or routing problems can cause slowdowns or outages. Monitoring tools that provide real-time diagnostics help identify root causes quickly, enabling targeted maintenance or rapid failover to backup systems.
- Software Updates and Patches: Many organizations schedule updates overnight to reduce downtime. However, failed or incomplete updates can introduce vulnerabilities or cause compatibility issues. Careful monitoring of update processes ensures that patches are applied successfully and systems remain stable.
Best Practices for Overnight Network Monitoring
To maximize the effectiveness of overnight monitoring, organizations should adopt a combination of strategies:
– Combine Automation With Human Oversight: Automated systems are indispensable for detecting anomalies, but human analysts provide the nuanced judgment needed to prioritize and respond effectively. This synergy reduces false alarms and ensures critical incidents receive immediate attention.
– Implement Clear Escalation Protocols: Define procedures for alerting on-call personnel and escalating incidents to senior staff or external responders. Clear communication channels and decision trees help avoid delays in incident response.
– Perform Regular Testing: Simulate overnight incidents to verify that monitoring tools and response teams are prepared. Drills can reveal gaps in detection or communication, allowing proactive improvements.
– Invest in Training: Keep overnight monitoring staff up-to-date with the latest security threats, troubleshooting techniques, and emerging technologies. Continuous education strengthens their ability to respond to evolving challenges.
– Leverage Advanced Analytics: Use machine learning and behavioral analytics to identify subtle patterns that may indicate emerging threats or system degradation. These technologies enhance detection capabilities beyond traditional rule-based alerts.
– Maintain Comprehensive Documentation: Detailed logs and incident reports support forensic analysis and compliance requirements. Documentation also facilitates knowledge sharing within teams and with stakeholders.
The Human Element: Why People Still Matter
While sophisticated monitoring platforms continue to evolve, the human element remains crucial. Overnight analysts bring context, intuition, and decision-making skills that technology alone cannot replicate. Their ability to interpret ambiguous signals, correlate disparate data points, and coordinate response efforts often makes the difference between a minor incident and a major crisis.
For instance, an automated alert might flag a spike in network traffic, but only a skilled analyst can determine whether this is a benign software update or an indication of a data breach. Human judgment ensures resources are allocated efficiently and that communication with other departments or external partners is handled appropriately.
Outsourcing the overnight monitoring function can be an effective strategy for businesses without the resources to staff 24/7 in-house teams. Providers specializing in this service bring expertise and economies of scale that enhance overall system reliability. They also often have access to cutting-edge tools and threat intelligence feeds that improve detection and response capabilities.
Conclusion: Learning From the Night Watchers
The hours around 3am may seem quiet, but for IT infrastructure, they are anything but. The lessons learned from those who watch networks overnight emphasize the importance of vigilance, swift response, and a balance of technology with human expertise. Whether through internal teams or by outsourcing to specialized providers, businesses can strengthen their resilience against threats and disruptions that emerge during these critical hours.
As the notes, investing in overnight monitoring is not just about preventing problems-it’s about ensuring that when the sun rises, your business is ready to operate without interruption. In today’s digital economy, that peace of mind is invaluable. Organizations that embrace comprehensive overnight monitoring strategies position themselves to reduce risk, minimize downtime, and maintain customer trust in an increasingly interconnected world.

articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (October 30, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: daily roundup (October 30, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here’s the roundup for Friday, October 30, 2026.
From Pixxel deepening its US push with a dedicated federal subsidiary to Binance estimating a $6.3 billion impact from a security breach, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.
Latest news
Binance estimates $6.3B impact from security breach
Cryptocurrency exchange Binance has estimated the total impact of a major security incident at around $6.3 billion, with approximately $3 billion worth of affected digital assets frozen on-chain in coordination with blockchain partners.
In an update issued on October 30, 2026, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange by trading volume said its preliminary investigation suggested that the incident may have originated from a compromised laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer. The attacker allegedly used the access to enter a service container and submit unauthorised withdrawal transactions.
Pixxel deepens US push with dedicated federal subsidiary
Bengaluru-based spacetech startup Pixxel has established Pixxel Federal, a US subsidiary aimed at expanding its business with American civilian, defence and intelligence agencies.
The move reflects the growing role of privately operated satellites in government operations, from national security and resource mapping to environmental monitoring. It also signals Pixxel’s ambition to move beyond supplying specialised satellite imagery towards offering a broader combination of sensing technologies, software, and satellite systems.
Other news
Virat Kohli’s stake in Agilitas Sports rises to 6.4% after one8 merger
Virat Kohli’s stake in Agilitas Sports has increased to 6.4% from 1.8% following the NCLT-approved merger of one8 Sports with Agilitas. Kohli had previously invested Rs 40 crore in the company and will continue as one8’s co-founder.
The merger gives one8 access to Agilitas’ capabilities in product development, design, research, manufacturing and retail. The brand plans to expand into new sporting categories and international markets, including the US, UK, Canada and Australia, with the ambition of building a global sportswear business from India.
77 student teams shortlisted for IN-SPACe rocket and satellite competitions
Seventy-seven teams have been shortlisted from 115 registrations for the IN-SPACe Model Rocketry and CAN-7USAT student competitions 2026. The grand finale will be held in Kushinagar, Uttar Pradesh, from October 31 to November 3, organised by IN-SPACe with ISRO and SSDF.
The rocketry challenge requires teams to launch a 1 kg payload to an altitude of 1 km, while CAN-7USAT teams must develop functional can-sized satellites weighing under 1 kg. Experts from ISRO, IN-SPACe, DRDO, academia and industry will assess the entries. An employment fair will also run from November 1 to 3, connecting students with aerospace employers.
Netpoleon India partners with QNu Labs to advance quantum-safe cybersecurity
Netpoleon India has partnered with Indian deep-tech firm QNu Labs to accelerate quantum-safe cybersecurity adoption among Indian enterprises. The collaboration combines QNu Labs’ expertise with Netpoleon’s network of channel partners and system integrators. At its centre is QShield 2.0, QNu Labs’ platform for cryptographic risk profiling, operations, governance and AI-driven security.
It aims to help organisations identify cryptographic vulnerabilities, strengthen security management and prepare for risks posed by quantum computing. The partnership will target sectors including banking, government, defence, telecommunications and critical infrastructure. QNu Labs has also demonstrated Quantum Key Distribution over 5.56 km and deployed the technology in a live defence network.
Amazon.in records 6x growth in two-wheeler sales during Great Indian Festival 2026
Two-wheeler sales on Amazon.in have grown 6x their average-day pace during the Great Indian Festival 2026, with over 60% of sales coming from non-metro cities. Electric two-wheelers grew 8x, everyday commuters 13.5x and premium motorcycles 2.5x. Popular brands include Chetak, Ampere, Hero MotoCorp, Bajaj, KTM and Triumph.
The platform offers over 200 two-wheeler models, alongside financing options, bank discounts and cashback. Its Automotive Store has recorded 2.2x growth, offering over 1 lakh products from 200 brands. AI tools Rufus and Part Finder support product discovery and vehicle-specific accessory recommendations.
IIT Kanpur’s C3iHub to establish and operate Rs 104.28 Cr UP Cyber Security Operations Centre
C3iHub at IIT Kanpur will establish and operate the Uttar Pradesh Cyber Security Operations Centre (UP-CSOC) for an initial three years under a Rs 104.28 crore project approved by the state Cabinet. The centre will provide 24x7 cybersecurity monitoring, threat detection, vulnerability assessment and incident response across government IT and operational technology systems.
It will use AI, machine learning, SIEM, SOAR and network detection technologies to identify and manage cyber threats. The initiative will also include security audits, cyber drills and departmental training. C3iHub has previously deployed security operations centres for SAIL Bhilai, NHAI and the Indian Ports Association.
(This article will be updated with the latest news throughout the day.)

articles.title: Google Discloses PageBreak AI Security Agent That Found 500+ XSS Bugs
articles.text:
According to a paper published by Google, its AI-powered security agent has uncovered more than 500 XSS vulnerabilities across its web applications since entering full operation in January. Google PageBreak uses Gemini models to autonomously investigate potential vulnerabilities, but reports them only after deterministic validators successfully reproduce the exploit against a running application, resulting in a near-zero false-positive rate.
With PageBreak, every vulnerability hypothesis is tested against a running environment with a real exploit, such as executing JavaScript for XSS, writing to a world-readable location for path traversal, or triggering outbound DNS for RCE. Michał Bentkowski, information security engineer at Google, explains:
Early on in the development of PageBreak, we made a conscious decision to prioritize deterministic validation. Rather than simply hypothesizing bugs based on code patterns, the system closes the loop by verifying potential flaws against running environments. This approach results in a near-zero false positive rate, ensuring that we avoid overloading product teams with unverified vulnerability reports.
Google also retains non-deterministic findings internally to seed deeper future scans, identify gaps in its validation capabilities, and guide the development of new validators. These unverified candidates are not sent to product teams, keeping their attention focused on high-confidence vulnerabilities. Bentkowski writes:
While deterministic validation is our gold standard, we are aware that our validators are currently lacking in capabilities to cover all vulnerability types or complex scenarios. This comes with the risk of false negatives that might have otherwise been caught by non-deterministic validators.
In the separate article, "Google’s PageBreak Project – Real-World Findings," on Google Bug Hunters, Bentkowski describes three technical cases found by PageBreak: an XSS vulnerability, a cache-poisoning issue caused by a service misconfiguration, and a path-traversal vulnerability. On LinkedIn, Lukas Weichselbaum, senior staff information security engineer at Google, stresses the importance of reducing false positives:
A lot of AI-generated bug reports sound convincing but turn out to be wrong, and the teams that get them waste time checking each one. In PageBreak, the model can suggest whatever it likes, but a finding only counts once a validator confirms it with a real payload. The validators are plain code written by security engineers, not by the model and live outside the agent loop.
Bentkowski says PageBreak benefits from Google's engineering environment, particularly Google’s monorepo end-to-end code visibility, security signals that connect live HTTP traffic to source code, and existing scanning infrastructure that provides authenticated access to its web applications.
With the longer-term goal of reducing product-team involvement to validating AI-generated fixes, Google is integrating PageBreak with other agentic security initiatives such as CodeMender to automatically generate fixes for the vulnerabilities it discovers.
No independent validation of the 500+ vulnerabilities has been provided.

articles.title: Hackers vaciaron las billeteras de unos 700 usuarios de Polymarket y robaron al menos USD 2,7 millones
articles.text:
Polymarket suspendió durante cerca de una hora las operaciones de su plataforma internacional el 29 de octubre, después de que hackers vaciaran las billeteras de cientos de usuarios. Según firmas de análisis de datos cripto, unos 710 usuarios perdieron al menos USD 2,7 millones. La empresa prometió reembolsar a todos los afectados.
Polymarket es una plataforma donde los usuarios apuestan sobre el resultado de eventos, desde las elecciones legislativas de Estados Unidos hasta la fecha de lanzamiento de un videojuego. La versión internacional funciona con criptomonedas y está prohibida en Estados Unidos y en otros países, según Wired.
La empresa informó que uno de sus proveedores externos fue vulnerado y que derivó el caso a las autoridades. “Cualquiera que haya sido afectado será compensado”, escribió en un comunicado citado por BleepingComputer. Polymarket pasó a un modo en el que solo se permitía cancelar órdenes a las 14:05, hora del Este de Estados Unidos.
Las operaciones volvieron a la normalidad a las 15:05, según el relato de la propia empresa recogido por BleepingComputer. Los primeros reclamos de billeteras vaciadas aparecieron cerca de las 13:30, de acuerdo con The Washington Post, y varios traderes conocidos se quejaron de pérdidas en la red social X.
El código malicioso venía de una herramienta de medición web
Una persona al tanto del caso dijo a CNBC que el problema se originó en DebugBear, un servicio de monitoreo del rendimiento de sitios web con sede en el Reino Unido. DebugBear confirmó en X que sufrió un “incidente de seguridad” y pidió a sus clientes retirar su código de monitoreo de las páginas.
BleepingComputer analizó el script (un programa que se ejecuta en el navegador del usuario) y concluyó que fue alojado en la infraestructura de DebugBear. El código comprobaba si el visitante tenía una sesión abierta en Polymarket y, si era así, usaba esa sesión para operar en su nombre.
Según ese análisis, el programa intentaba vender las posiciones de los usuarios en los mercados de apuestas o transferir sus fichas a una billetera controlada por el atacante. También intentaba convertir las criptomonedas de la víctima en activos que pudieran enviarse a esa billetera.
La firma de seguridad Hudson Rock identificó la billetera del atacante. BleepingComputer rastreó que transfirió unos 28,6 millones de POL, una criptomoneda valuada en cerca de USD 2,57 millones, a otras tres billeteras. Hudson Rock también halló un cambio en el código de Polymarket, fechado a las 13:59, que eliminaba la integración con DebugBear.
Entre 700 y 710 afectados y un monto aún sin confirmar
Las firmas Betting Intelligence y Polysights, citadas por CNBC, calcularon que una cuenta retiró al menos USD 2,7 millones de 710 billeteras. La firma de análisis Bubblemaps estimó unos 700 afectados y la misma cifra de dinero, según Wired. BleepingComputer, por su parte, rastreó cerca de USD 2,5 millones hasta una billetera sospechosa.
Polymarket se negó a decirle a Wired cuántos usuarios se vieron afectados o cuánto dinero se perdió. La plataforma para usuarios dentro de Estados Unidos, que opera como un mercado financiero regulado y es independiente de la internacional, no sufrió el ataque.
Los usuarios a quienes se les retiraron menos de USD 10.000 recibirían la restitución de sus fondos el 30 de octubre, según lo que Polymarket comunicó a los usuarios en Discord, citado por CNBC. Quienes perdieron más de esa cifra deberán firmar un formulario de renuncia a reclamos para recibir el reembolso.

articles.title: Reddit exigirá login após 20 anos de acesso aberto • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Reddit exigirá login após 20 anos de acesso aberto
Mudança busca reduzir scraping não autorizado e ampliar a personalização da experiência e dos anúncios.
O Reddit começará a exigir login para que usuários consigam ver posts e navegar pela plataforma. A mudança encerra quase duas décadas em que grande parte do conteúdo podia ser acessado diretamente pela web, mesmo sem uma conta.
O anúncio foi feito pelo CEO Steve Huffman durante a divulgação de resultados financeiros do terceiro trimestre de 2026. Segundo o The Verge, os primeiros testes ocorrerão nos próximos meses em mercados selecionados fora dos Estados Unidos, ainda sem previsão para uma implementação global.
Segundo Huffman, a empresa pretende testar diferentes formas de restringir a navegação deslogada antes de decidir como o sistema funcionará definitivamente. Hoje, grande parte das páginas do fórum ainda pode ser aberta sem cadastro ou autenticação.
Como alternativa para quem não quiser associar algo ao próprio perfil, o Reddit também está reconstruindo o modo anônimo dentro do app oficial.
Um dos principais motivos citados pela empresa é a proteção de seus dados contra scraping de IA não autorizado. Segundo Huffman, a maior parte desse tipo de acesso ocorre por páginas abertas a visitantes deslogados.
A empresa quer dificultar a coleta automatizada por robôs e outros serviços externos, mas continuará permitindo o acesso ao conteúdo por meio de acordos comerciais. Atualmente, o Reddit mantém contratos de licenciamento inclusive com Google e OpenAI, inclusive para que informações em posts de dentro dos fóruns apareça nas respostas de chatbots.
Huffman afirmou ainda que o login ajudará a empresa a cumprir regras de segurança e oferecer uma experiência mais personalizada.
O Reddit reconhece que a mudança tem impacto no negócio de publicidade, mas positivamente. Mais de 80% da monetização do Reddit já vem de usuários ativos diários que utilizam o aplicativo ou estão logados, segundo o Huffman.
O executivo afirma que a empresa não precisa saber necessariamente a identidade real de cada usuário, mas ter uma sessão associada a uma conta permite entender melhor a navegação e mostrar anúncios mais relevantes. No terceiro trimestre, a receita publicitária da empresa cresceu 54% em relação ao ano anterior, para US$ 847 milhões (cerca de R$ 4,5 bilhões).
O anúncio também ocorre em momento de queda de visitas que chegam por buscadores, como o Google. Em outubro, as referências vindas de pesquisas caíram, em média, mais de 1 milhão por semana.

articles.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
articles.text:
An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers’ machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident.
The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont. Both Beaumont and the CTO and co-founder of security firm Phorian said that version 2.1.313 was distributed through Anthropic’s official account on Cursor. So far, neither Cursor nor Anthropic has explained how the attackers gained control of the account.
In search of cloud credentials
“It was a supply-chain compromise where the attacker gained access to the official distribution channel,” Phorian CTO and co-founder Luke Roberts told Ars. “The malicious version 2.1.313 was posted to the official Anthropic account, effectively superseding 2.1.312. Extensions auto-update in Cursor by default, but users can configure this in settings.” Phorian has more details here.
Anthropic has yet to issue public notice of the incident to customers.
Cursor said that the malicious extension attempts to install a persistent SSH backdoor using an added attacker-controlled SSH key, enabling the local SSH service, and opening a reverse SSH tunnel. The code was written to work on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Because Cursor extensions run with the permissions of the tool’s Integrated Development Environment, the backdoored version likely would gain access to local files, source code, and developer tooling once it was installed.

articles.title: London, Ontario is Canada's number one city for partying: report
articles.text:
According to a recent report by Uber, Ontario is home to Canada’s top partying destination, but it’s not Toronto that holds the honour.
Releasing its fifth annual Nightlife Index on Wednesday, Oct. 28, the ridesharing app revealed that, of all places, London, Ontario, is the number one city in the country for partying.
It makes sense, given the city’s substantial student population, but a city’s got to be really good at partying to dethrone one like Toronto, which boasts a population nearly 10 times the size.
This marks the fourth time the Ontario city has landed the first-place slot, after being dethroned just once by Toronto in 2024.
Toronto didn’t even manage to land in the top three Canadian cities for partying, as it turns out. Winnipeg secured a second-place finish, while Lethbridge, Alberta, came in third.
Toronto ended up in fifth place, sandwiched between Kitchener-Waterloo in fourth and Halifax in sixth. And as someone who has lived in both Halifax and Toronto, I’d argue that those two positions ought to be swapped.
Since the list was created using aggregated and anonymized data from Uber and Uber Eats, such as late-night trips and food orders, I guess I stand corrected.
The study also showed that New Year’s Eve, Halloween Night and Halloween Weekend are the three biggest holidays for partying (no surprise there), and that, on average, Canadians stay out the latest on Halloween.
As for hangover cures, Canadians have been ordering those in spades, too. The most popular? None other than classic hot coffee, followed, as it so often is, by hash browns, breakfast wraps, bagels, and iced coffee.
Here’s to another year of partying, Canada!

articles.title: Applebee's exposed customers' personal data after leaving database password in app | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Applebee’s has fixed a security flaw that allowed anyone to access the personal information of its registered customers, after a researcher found a password for an internal database inside Applebee’s mobile app, TechCrunch has learned.
The popular restaurant chain confirmed on Thursday that it had taken action to address the security issue to prevent any unauthorized access to its customer database.
TechCrunch withheld publication of this story until the bug was confirmed to be fixed.
Robert Wiggins, a U.K.-based cybersecurity researcher at What Security, discovered the security lapse earlier this month. Wiggins is no stranger to discovering security issues, including exposed or sensitive information that should not be publicly accessible.
For this latest discovery, Wiggins used AI to help find the credential buried inside thousands of lines of source code in Applebee’s Android app, which has more than a million downloads on Google Play. The credential allowed access to the company’s customer database.
Storing a password or private key in software, known as hardcoding credentials, is one of the most severe types of security vulnerabilities because anyone with the app can extract the key and use it to log in to a remote system as if they were an authorized user.
Wiggins said that the hardcoded credential could have also allowed a malicious attacker to modify customer data in the database.
TechCrunch verified Wiggins’ findings by downloading and decompiling Applebee’s Android app to examine its source code and confirm that it contained the exposed credential. We also created an Applebee’s account with dummy account data, which allowed Wiggins to retrieve our information from the company’s database.
The exposed database contained customer names, email addresses (including whether or not the customer verified their email), dates of birth, phone numbers, and ZIP codes. The data also included veteran status, the number of times customers had logged in, when their accounts were created, and the IP addresses of their most recent log-ins, which can be used to reveal the person’s approximate location.
Wiggins was unable to alert Applebee’s or its parent company, Dine Brands, as neither have ways to report security issues. Wiggins asked TechCrunch for help in disclosing the security issue to the company.
A spokesperson for Dine Brands, who did not provide their name, said in an emailed statement on Friday: “We appreciate TechCrunch and the security researcher for bringing this matter to our attention. Our security team promptly launched an investigation and has not currently found any evidence of unauthorized access.”
When asked by TechCrunch, the spokesperson would not say if the company has server logs that it can review to determine whether anyone accessed the database, or if it has any logs at all.
“Our investigation is ongoing, and we will take appropriate steps based on our findings,” the company added.
It’s unclear how many customers were affected by the data exposure. Wiggins said that figuring out the number of customers in the database would have required the AI model to unnecessarily access potentially every customer record.
Applebee’s had at least 8.5 million customers enrolled in its rewards program as of last year, though the company would not provide a number of how many customers had their personal information exposed by this security flaw.
TechCrunch asked the company if it would alert customers or U.S. regulators about the incident, including whether it would file a disclosure with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, as publicly traded companies are required to do for material cybersecurity incidents. We also asked the company how long the exposed credential had been in the Applebee’s app, but we did not get a response.
We’ll update this article if the company responds.

articles.title: Doomformer: Diese KI wurde in Doom geschaffen – was sie leisten kann
articles.text:
Doomformer: Diese KI wurde in Doom geschaffen – was sie leisten kann
Egal, ob in der Google-Suche oder auf einem Satelliten der ESA: Doom wurde mittlerweile auf so vielen verschiedenen Plattformen spielbar gemacht, dass die meisten Gamer:innen wohl schon lange mit dem Zählen aufgehört haben. Etwas seltener sind die Versuche, etwas anderes als einen Ego-Shooter aus Doom zu machen. So versucht es derzeit der Entwickler, der sich auf GitHub den Nicknamen „mottopanikeiku“ gegeben hat.
Doom als KI? Wie das funktionieren soll
Sein Projekt trägt den Namen „Doomformer“ und ist eine Wortneuschöpfung aus Doom und einem Transformermodell. Im Grunde hat er den Ego-Shooter in ein neuronales Netzwerk umgewandelt, das in der Lage ist, Arithmetik durchzuführen. Um das zu realisieren, nutzt er sogenannte „Voodoo Dolls“ aus Doom. Das sind Klone der Spielfigur, die immer dann auftauchen, wenn das Spiel einen zusätzlichen Spielerstartpunkt im Level entdeckt.
Um das neuronale Netzwerk zu bauen, werden laut dem Entwickler 1.355 Voodoo-Puppen genutzt, die zusammen ein MNIST-Netzwerk auf der Map bilden. Die Puppen fahren auf Bahnen hin und her und überqueren dabei Linien, die als Gewichtungen fungieren. Kommt es zu einer Aktivierung der Puppen, wird eine bestimmte Anzahl über eine Treppe nach oben in die zweite Ebene befördert. Das passiert, weil das Überqueren jeder Linie das Licht und die Ebenenhöhe verändern kann. So können sie Elemente im Spiel verändern und etwa Zahlen anzeigen.
Um die Fertigkeiten des Netzwerks zu testen, hat der Entwickler auch die Spielfigur etwas modifiziert. Spieler:innen können auf einem vorgefertigten Bereich die linke Maustaste gedrückt halten, die eigentlich zum Schießen in Doom gedacht ist. In der modifizierten Version malt das Gedrückthalten auf den Boden. Wird die Spielfigur bewegt, malt sie also auf den Boden.
Kann sich die Doom-KI selbst spielen?
Das neuronale Netzwerk ist in der Lage, so gemalte Ziffern zu erkennen. Sobald die Puppen an ihrer Position angekommen sind, vergleicht ein Python-Skript die Werte miteinander. In einem Test mit 10.000 Versuchen konnte „Doomformer“ insgesamt 9.716 der Zahlen korrekt identifizieren. Doch damit sind die Fertigkeiten der Doom-KI nicht am Ende.
Der Entwickler experimentiert derzeit damit, dass die Doom-KI selbst Doom spielen kann. Dabei werden die Screenshots des Spiels an 1.345 Voodoo-Puppen geschickt, die zusammen eine Entscheidung treffen, was die Spielfigur als Nächstes tun soll. Noch ist das aber fernab von einem „spielbaren“ Zustand, wie der Entwickler schreibt. Eine Entscheidung benötigt etwa 22 Sekunden. Für die Tests wurden deshalb Dämonengegner eingefroren, solange die KI überlegt.

articles.title: Waiting for an AI law is a poor compliance strategy
articles.text:
Waiting for an AI law is a poor compliance strategy
India's courts and sectoral regulators have already begun assigning liability for AI failures. Businesses that are holding out for a statute are preparing for the wrong deadline.
A bank has an AI system in place to flag suspicious transactions and take the call to freeze accounts. While the workflow has a human sign-off in place, clearing around 400 cases a day has resulted in the approval system becoming a formality. So, when a wrongly-frozen account takes the system to court, the bank becomes unable to prove what the human actually reviewed. This, unfortunately, is no longer a hypothetical scenario.
On July 2, 2026, the Supreme Court of India quashed orders passed by the National Company Law Tribunal and the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal in the Pooja Ramesh Singh v. Jammu and Kashmir Bank Ltd. case. The orders had rested on citations generated by an AI tool and attributed to the Supreme Court itself. This directed the Bar Council of India to constitute a committee to prescribe disciplinary norms for advocates who file AI-generated citations.
This is a business story as much as a legal one. Despite two tribunals and several rounds of proceedings, the parties had to carry the cost of a machine error that no human caught before filing. No AI statute was required to reach that outcome. Ordinary law, applied by judges, did the work.
The regulators are moving faster than the legislature
For most Indian companies, the sharper edge is coming from sectoral regulators rather than from the bench.
In early June this year, the Reserve Bank of India gave banks and other regulated entities until June 30 to submit gap assessments on frontier-AI cyber risk. Instead of having the CISO to file the note, the RBI had asked the board to sign one.
Later, on June 24, the RBI publicly released a draft 'Guidance on Regulatory Principles for Model Risk Management' to establish a comprehensive enterprise-wide model governance framework for the financial sector. Here 'models' extend to third-party models, AI, and machine learning (ML) systems used by commercial banks, small finance banks, payments banks, NBFCs, and other financial institutions. So if a lending decision is influenced by a model licensed from a vendor, the model risk sits on the one putting the AI system to use and not the vendor who built it.
Meanwhile, India's legislative position is still a work-in-progress. On October 8, 2026, Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw had assured that the time has come for India to get an AI law. In a first step towards this, the government will be launching a consultation paper on regulating artificial intelligence.
However, any business that is treating a pending law as its compliance milestone has their sequencing backwards. Even when the statute arrives, it can only land on top of existing case laws and sectoral circulars, not in place of them. Regardless of what law comes into place, the Digital Personal Data Protection Act takes full effect on May 13, 2027. Businesses will be held accountable even if the data is being processed by an external vendor as the DPDPA will be applicable wherever an AI system handles personal data.
What does this ask of a business?
Behind all the legal vocabulary, the requirements across all the domains are the same—one needs to show their working.
For any consequential decision made by an AI system, organisations must be able to have the visibility regarding which model produced the output, what data it drew on, whether a retrieval step was involved, who reviewed it before it went out, and whether that record still exists six months later.
Multiple Indian firms have written a policy, appointed a committee, and deployed systems but can still not answer any of the above questions. This is clearly an architecture question before it is a policy-related one. Recording the model version, prompt, retrieved data and human sign-off for every AI decision is only cheap if it is thoughtfully designed for. It can, however, become close to impossible to reconstruct afterwards.
It is important for businesses to question an AI vendor before procuring a model. Does the system record which model version handled each request? Can that record be exported and retained? Where does inference physically happen? What happens to inputs after processing? Where in the workflow is a human required to act? Vendors that cannot answer plainly are transferring risk to the buyer.
Build the record now
There is not much point in waiting for an AI law. AI adoption is already in full swing, and when unprepared, the chain is only waiting to break. In the case of the tribunal matter, that chain broke at the review step. In an RBI-regulated entity, the chain is most likely to break earlier, at provenance, if nobody logged which version of which model scored the application.
The current strategy, albeit unglamorous, is to ensure that the record of every AI-assisted decision made can survive being read aloud. So while the law may still be pending, the question is not. When it does come, the answer will have to exist already.
(The article has been authored by Ramprakash Ramamoorthy, Director - AI Research, Zoho Corporation)

articles.title: Netflix, HBO Max, évènements sportifs : Canal+ casse le prix de son offre Ciné Séries
articles.text:
24,99 € par mois pour profiter de Netflix, Apple TV, Paramount+, HBO Max et de plusieurs chaînes Canal+ : c’est la nouvelle promotion proposée sur l’offre Ciné Séries. Attention toutefois, ce tarif n’est appliqué que durant les 12 premiers mois. Ensuite, la facture augmente de 10 euros pour passer à 34,99 € par mois. Dans tous les cas, cette promotion a de quoi retenir l’attention.
Canal+ lance une promotion pour son offre Ciné Séries
Alors que les prix des différentes plateformes de streaming augmentent régulièrement, Canal+ vient de lancer une nouvelle promotion pour son offre Ciné Séries. Concrètement, il est question d’un engagement sur 24 mois. Durant les 12 premiers mois, l’abonné bénéficie d’un tarif réduit de 24,99 € par mois, au lieu de 29,99 €. Les 12 mois suivants, le prix passe à 34,99 € par mois. Pour rappel, l’offre Ciné Séries donne accès à Apple TV, HBO Max (abonnement Standard), Netflix (Standard avec Pub), Paramount+ (Standard), Ciné+ OCS et Insomnia (la plateforme de streaming dédiée au cinéma d’horreur). Côté chaînes, cette offre intègre Canal+, Canal+ Box Office, Canal+ Grand Écran, Canal+ Sport 360, Canal+ Docs, Canal+ Kids et Canal+ Cinéma(s).
Les abonnés à cette offre peuvent donc profiter des films et séries proposés sur les principales plateformes de streaming, tout en ayant accès aux événements sportifs retransmis par Canal+. Le groupe précise que tous ces services, pris séparément, reviendraient à 74 € par mois. À noter que cette offre est valable jusqu’au 9 novembre 2026 inclus.
Une offre très intéressante, mais il faut retenir un point
Comme nous l’avons précisé, l’offre est proposée à 24,99 € par mois durant les 12 premiers mois, avant de passer ensuite à 34,99 € par mois. Sur deux ans, cela représente donc une moyenne de 29,99 € par mois. Dans tous les cas, ce prix reste assez attractif vu le nombre de services auxquels l’offre donne accès. À noter qu’un abonnement sans engagement à Ciné Séries est également proposé à 34,99 € par mois.

articles.title: Aspiration et lavage avec deux brosses dédiées : le Dyson V16 Submarine passe à 664,05 € avec notre code exclusif
articles.text:
L’aspirateur laveur Dyson V16 Piston Animal Submarine est à 664,05 € (-34 %) avec le code LESNUMS10
Le Dyson V16 Piston Animal Submarine aspire et lave avec deux brosses distinctes. Le code exclusif LESNUMS10 le ramène à 664,05 € chez Dyson.
Dyson affiche ce modèle à 699 €, contre 999 € barrés. Le code LESNUMS10, exclusif aux lecteurs des Numériques et valable jusqu’au 30 novembre inclus, applique ici 5 % supplémentaires au panier. Le total descend à 664,05 €, soit 334,95 € d’économie et environ 34 % de réduction. La livraison est gratuite et une station d’accueil indépendante, annoncée à 130 €, est actuellement offerte.
Deux brosses pour aspirer puis laver
L’aspirateur sans fil Dyson V16 Piston Animal Submarine associe une brosse d’aspiration à deux rouleaux coniques et une tête lavante Submarine 2.0 pour les sols durs. Il se transforme également en aspirateur à main, avec une mini-brosse motorisée pour les textiles.
Le passage au lavage nécessite de changer de brosse. Avec la tête Submarine, l’appareil n’aspire plus : il faut donc dépoussiérer le sol au préalable. Un bouton remplace la gâchette à maintenir enfoncée.
Un lavage efficace, mais un entretien exigeant
Notre test relève de bons résultats sur les taches, notamment le vin et les traces grasses. L’entretien constitue toutefois une limite : la brosse doit être nettoyée manuellement et son bac d’eau sale manque d’étanchéité. Le poids au poignet se fait également sentir.
Dyson affiche une moyenne de 3,9/5 pour 1 937 avis, commune aux fiches V16 Piston Animal et Submarine. Cette note ne correspond donc pas exclusivement à la version lavante.
