articles.title: Govt notifies National Social Security Board for gig, platform workers
articles.text:
Govt notifies National Social Security Board for gig, platform workers
The Board is mandated to design, monitor, and recommend targeted welfare schemes to bridge the social security gap for millions of gig and platform workers, alongside traditional unorganised workers.
The government has notified the National Social Security Board for unorganised workers and gig and platform workers, which will design, monitor, and recommend targeted welfare schemes to bridge the social security gap.
Gig workers are those who perform work or participate in a work arrangement and earn from such activities outside the traditional employer-employee relationship.
Platform workers are those who engage in work through or with online platforms.
In a move towards ensuring comprehensive social security for India's massive informal workforce, the Ministry of Labour & Employment has notified the constitution of the National Social Security Board for Unorganised Workers and Gig & Platform Workers, a ministry statement said.
Established under the statutory framework of the Code on Social Security, this marks a historic shift by integrating digital gig and platform professionals into India's formal welfare architecture, the ministry said.
The Board will be presided over by the Union Minister for Labour & Employment and comprise representatives from the Central and state governments, prominent aggregator companies, employers, civil society organisations, workers' unions, and gig and platform worker associations.
The Board is mandated to design, monitor, and recommend targeted welfare schemes to bridge the social security gap for millions of gig and platform workers, alongside traditional unorganised workers.
The National Social Security Board shall meet at least thrice a year and observe the rules of procedure relating to the transaction of business at its meetings, as prescribed by the Central government.
The National Social Security Board shall recommend to the Central government the framing of suitable schemes for different sections of unorganised workers, gig workers and platform workers.
The board will advise the Central government on such matters arising out of the administration of this Code as may be referred to; It will monitor such social welfare schemes for unorganised workers, gig workers and platform workers administered by the Central government.
It will review the record keeping functions performed at the state level and also review the expenditure from the fund and account.
It will also undertake other functions as are assigned to it by the Central government from time to time.

articles.title: Malicious Claude Code extension on Cursor planted SSH backdoors
articles.text:
A malicious version of Anthropic's Claude Code VS Code extension was distributed through Cursor's extension marketplace for approximately 11 hours on October 29, exposing up to 5,000 developers to malware designed to install persistent SSH backdoors.
The extension used the version number 2.1.313 and was distributed between 2:27 a.m. and 1:35 p.m. Pacific Time.
Cursor is an AI-powered code editor built from Microsoft’s open-source Visual Studio Code (VS Code), with support for VS Code extensions. Anthropic’s Claude Code extension brings its AI coding assistant directly into compatible editors, helping developers write and debug code using natural-language instructions.
Cursor says Anthropic did not develop the malicious extension but has not explained how attackers distributed the compromised package under Anthropic's name.
"Between about 2:27 am PT and 1:35 pm PT today, a maliciously modified version of Anthropic’s Claude Code extension was made available in the Cursor VS Code extension Marketplace," warned Cursor.
"The extension runs malicious code that attempts to install a persistent SSH backdoor."
Researchers at Phorion and OpenSourceMalware found that the attackers inserted a malicious JavaScript loader at the beginning of the extension's extension.js file, leaving the legitimate extension code otherwise unchanged.
The malicious code executes when the extension loads, without requiring user interaction with Claude Code.
When installed, the malicious extension performs the following actions on compromised systems:
- Collects system and user information, including Git email and public IP address.
- Adds an attacker-controlled SSH key and attempts to enable SSH access and establish a reverse tunnel.
- Installs persistence through a macOS LaunchAgent or Windows scheduled task/Startup script, retrying the tunnel roughly every minute.
- Sends host details and backdoor status to the attacker’s server at the IP address 134.209.82[.]225
However, according to Phorion, coding errors in the malware's SSH setup routines likely prevented attackers from gaining remote access to many affected Windows and macOS systems.
The mistakes prevented the malware from enabling SSH on machines where it was not already running, leaving the reverse tunnel unable to provide access to the compromised device.
On macOS, the malware attempts to check whether Remote Login is enabled using the systemsetup -getremotelogin command, but runs it without elevated privileges. Instead of returning the SSH service's status, the command produces an administrator-access error.
Because the malware only attempts to enable SSH when the output contains "Off," it skips the activation step entirely.
On Windows, the malware attempts to install and start the OpenSSH server through PowerShell, but it tries to do so via /bin/sh, a Unix shell that isn't available on standard Windows installations. Due to this, the SSH setup fails.
In both cases, the malware can still install its SSH keys, establish persistence, and attempt to create the reverse tunnel. However, if the SSH server is not already running, the tunnel cannot provide access to the compromised machine.
Even if the SSH backdoor fails, the malware still sends reconnaissance data to the attacker's server, including the victim's username, hostname, public IP address, Git email address, and names of environment variables associated with sensitive credentials.
However, the script does not directly steal credentials, suggesting the attackers intended to retrieve sensitive data manually after gaining access through the SSH tunnel.
Cursor removed the malicious extension and temporarily shut down its entire marketplace to audit other extensions and rotate all access keys before making it available again.
The company also worked with the hosting provider to take the attacker's server offline, disrupting both the reverse SSH connections and the transmission of reconnaissance data.
Following an internal investigation, Cursor says it found no evidence that any other extension versions or the official distribution were affected.
Those who have downloaded the package during the exposure window should check for the presence of an 'svc-telemetry' SSH key on their machines, and follow Cursor’s remediation instructions if impact is confirmed.
For impacted machines, it is recommended to isolate them, rotate accessible secrets, invalidate sessions, and rebuild the affected environment from safe backups.
While initial reports suggested that npm, Open VSX, and Microsoft's Visual Studio Code Marketplace were also impacted, it was later confirmed that Cursor was the only source distributing the malicious extension.
However, many questions remain unanswered about the supply chain attack, including how the threat actors published a malicious extension under Anthropic's name on Cursor's marketplace and whether Cursor or Anthropic's systems were compromised during the incident.
BleepingComputer contacted Anthropic and Cursor with questions about the attack and will update this story if we receive a response.

articles.title: Son sous-marin de 4 tonnes disparaît, il le retrouve en vente sur Leboncoin pour une centaine d'euros
articles.text:
Sous-marin volé : son propriétaire le retrouve en vente sur Leboncoin pour une centaine d’euros
Une affaire vite remontée à la surface
Quatre tonnes, une coque orange et une annonce bradée sur le site de petites annonces le plus consulté de France. Volé début octobre dans l'Ain, un sous-marin a refait surface sur Leboncoin dans le Doubs, et son propriétaire n'a eu qu'à faire défiler son écran pour le retrouver. La police de Besançon a fait le reste.
Il trônait comme objet de décoration dans un commerce de matériel de plongée de Ferney-Voltaire, dans l'Ain, à deux pas de la frontière suisse. Entre le 1er et le 21 octobre 2026, ce sous-marin jaune de quatre tonnes a disparu. Le propriétaire porte plainte, puis surveille les petites annonces. Quelques jours plus tard, il tombe sur son engin, proposé à la vente sur Leboncoin dans le secteur de Besançon.
Une annonce Leboncoin à une centaine d'euros pour un engin de quatre tonnes
D'après Le Progrès, cité par Radio Scoop, l'annonce affichait une centaine d'euros. L'engin vaut plusieurs milliers d'euros.
Le propriétaire a joué la prudence : il a prévenu les gendarmes d'Ornex au lieu de contacter lui-même le vendeur. Le dossier a ensuite été confié à la brigade des atteintes aux biens du commissariat de Besançon, rapporte ICI Besançon. Les enquêteurs ont épluché le profil du vendeur, puis une surveillance discrète a confirmé l'emplacement du submersible.
Un sous-marin en vente près de Besançon?
En octobre, un sous-marin a été volé dans l'Ain, puis repéré en vente sur Leboncoin à Besançon.
Nos policiers 👮♀️👮ont plongé dans l'affaire
➡️ engin récupéré et deux suspects convoqués devant la justice.
Une enquête menée à bon port! 🌊🔍 pic.twitter.com/DdXboA2ik6
— Police Nationale 25 (@PoliceNat25) October 29, 2026
Le 26 octobre, une opération réunissant plusieurs unités a conduit à l'interpellation d'un Bisontin de 27 ans. Selon BFMTV, le sous-marin était entreposé chez lui, et c'est lui qui aurait publié l'annonce.
Un second homme, âgé de 47 ans, a été entendu. Les policiers le soupçonnent d'avoir aidé à transporter l'engin, ce qui demande un sérieux matériel de levage. La photo diffusée par la police montre d'ailleurs une grue en train de soulever le sous-marin depuis un camion.
Vol en réunion et recel : ce qui attend les deux suspects
Les deux hommes seront convoqués devant le délégué du procureur de la République de Besançon, pour "vol en réunion" et "recel de vol". En attendant, le submersible a été mis à l'abri et retrouvera bientôt son propriétaire.
L'histoire rappelle une règle simple : quand on repère un bien volé en vente sur Leboncoin, on garde une capture de l'annonce et on prévient les forces de l'ordre avant tout rendez-vous avec le vendeur. Ici, les enquêteurs n'ont eu qu'à suivre l'annonce jusqu'à l'engin, qui n'avait rien de discret.

articles.title: Guerre spatiale : l'avènement des "gardes du corps" en orbite pour protéger les satellites menacés
articles.text:
Dans l’espace, la menace ne vient plus seulement des débris, mais aussi des satellites voisins. Des pays commencent donc à miser sur des engins pour protéger leurs infrastructures spatiales comme le ferait un garde du corps.
Il y a quelques jours, le satellite russe Kosmos-2612 s’est suspicieusement approché d’ICEYE-X36, un satellite radar finlandais dont les images servent notamment à l’Ukraine. Un « comportement menaçant », selon Thomas DiNanno, le sous-secrétaire d’État américain. Et il ne s’agit pas d’un cas isolé : les satellites russes Luch rôdent près des engins de télécommunications occidentaux depuis 2014.
Royaume-Uni : le pari d’Astroscale sur la protection des satellites
Il n’en fallait pas plus au Royaume-Uni pour passer à l’acte. Le ministère de la Défense vient de confier à l’entreprise Astroscale un contrat de 15 millions de livres pour mettre en place LEDA. Ce programme vise à fabriquer, lancer et exploiter des vaisseaux capables de comprendre comment se prépare une approche hostile, et d’y répondre.
Concrètement, il s’agirait de s’appuyer sur la technologie ELSA-d de la société, pensée pour se débarrasser des débris spatiaux grâce à un système de capture magnétique. Mais ici, un petit satellite manœuvrerait constamment aux alentours d’un autre satellite considéré comme critique. En cas d’approche suspecte, il prendrait une photographie de l’engin adverse, et se mettrait même sur sa trajectoire si besoin.
« Le contrôle de l’espace ne consiste pas à chercher le conflit dans l’espace, mais à démontrer que nous pouvons protéger les capacités dont dépend notre économie, notre société et nos forces armées », assure Tony Williams, contre-amiral britannique. Un prototype pourrait être prêt en moins de trois ans, pour environ 1 % du coût d’une constellation militaire comme Skynet, estime Alex Godfrey, responsable de la défense chez Astroscale.
Une course mondiale
Et d’autres initiatives existent déjà. Sans surprise, les États-Unis disposent déjà de satellites capables d’en inspecter d’autres, et testent des manœuvres de réaction rapide. La France, elle, développe son démonstrateur YODA, avec un successeur prévu baptisé EGIDE. L’Allemagne, le Japon ou encore l’Inde se penchent également sur de telles technologies, alors que l’espace se mue en véritable terrain pour la guerre moderne.
Problème, selon la Secure World Foundation, aucun acteur occidental n’égale pour l’instant les capacités déployées par la Russie et la Chine, et l’Europe est particulièrement mal équipée.
Dans ce contexte, Alex Godfrey plaide pour une « force de patrouille » commune : un seul vaisseau veillerait sur deux ou trois satellites alliés, par exemple français, britanniques et allemands, puis chaque pays prendrait en charge une zone. Une protection jusque-là réservée aux plus grandes puissances deviendrait ainsi accessible à des États plus modestes.
Sources : Space.com, Astroscale
Une opération de rendez-vous et proximité (RPO) désigne l’ensemble des manœuvres permettant à un satellite de s’approcher, de se maintenir à courte distance, voire de « suivre » un autre satellite. Techniquement, cela repose sur une navigation très précise (capteurs optiques, radar, mesures de distance) et sur des propulseurs capables d’ajuster en continu la trajectoire. C’est sensible car les mêmes capacités servent à des usages légitimes (inspection, maintenance, retrait de débris) et à des usages offensifs (espionnage rapproché, brouillage, intimidation, collision volontaire). À courte distance, une petite erreur de calcul ou une manœuvre imprévisible peut aussi créer un risque de collision et de débris.
La capture magnétique consiste à utiliser un aimant et une cible ferromagnétique (ou une plaque adaptée) pour « accrocher » un objet en orbite, afin de le stabiliser puis de le déplacer ou de le désorbiter. Le principe est séduisant car il évite certains mécanismes mécaniques complexes, mais il impose que la cible soit préparée à l’avance (ou au moins compatible), ce qui limite l’interopérabilité. Pour des missions de protection, la capture n’est pas forcément l’objectif : la même chaîne technologique sert surtout à réaliser un rapprochement contrôlé et à opérer très près d’un autre engin. Les limites majeures viennent de la sécurité des manœuvres (risque de collision), du carburant nécessaire au « station-keeping » à proximité, et des règles de non-interférence entre opérateurs.
Un satellite inspecteur est conçu pour observer de près un autre satellite : imagerie optique, estimation de trajectoire, et parfois écoute de certaines signatures (sans forcément intercepter des communications). Un « bodyguard » ajoute l’idée de se positionner de manière dissuasive, par exemple en se plaçant entre un satellite critique et un approchant, ce qui exige une très bonne maîtrise de l’attitude et de la navigation relative. Pour être efficace, il lui faut des capteurs capables de détecter tôt une approche anormale, des propulseurs réactifs, et un système de planification autonome ou semi-autonome pour réagir vite. Le point clé, c’est que ces capacités sont duales : elles ressemblent beaucoup à celles utilisées pour l’inspection, la maintenance… ou des actions offensives, d’où l’attention portée à l’intention et au comportement en orbite.

articles.title: Le Bitcoin est dans le rouge : le hack de Binance plombe tout le marché crypto, 1,5 milliard de dollars envolés
articles.text:
C’était une nuit noire pour le monde des cryptomonnaies. Dans la soirée du jeudi 29 octobre, des pirates ont en effet siphonné les portefeuilles de Binance, la plus grande plateforme d’échange de cryptomonnaies au monde. Les cybercriminels se sont enfuis avec 6,3 milliards de dollars d’actifs. C’est le plus gros vol de l’histoire des cryptos, loin devant le casse de 1,5 milliard de dollars chez Bybit en février 2025. Binance a suspendu les retraits et promet de couvrir toutes les pertes de ses clients.
À lire aussi : 351 millions de dollars de cryptos dérobées – la plateforme Bitget a été piratée par des hackers nord-coréens
Le Bitcoin dégringole sous les 77 000 dollars
Sans surprise, le piratage a plombé le cours du Bitcoin. Avant l’annonce du piratage, la cryptomonnaie s’échangeait autour des 80 300 dollars. Moins d’une heure plus tard, alors que Binance confirmait la cyberattaque, la devise numérique s’est effondrée sous les 79 000 dollars. Tandis que les mauvaises nouvelles s’accumulaient, le Bitcoin a continué de plonger, frôlant brièvement les 76 000 dollars, son plus bas niveau depuis plus d’un mois.
Comme toujours, la dégringolade du Bitcoin a déclenché une cascade de liquidations. Les positions des investisseurs qui pariaient sur la hausse du Bitcoin ont été liquidées. En une seule heure, 627 millions de dollars de positions ont été éliminés, selon CoinGlass. Sur 24 heures, 1,5 milliard de dollars de positions acheteuses, dont 468 millions sur le bitcoin, se sont évaporés. C’est un gros coup dur pour le marché spéculatif.
Suite à ce nouveau revers, le Bitcoin s’éloigne encore un peu plus de son record historique de 126 116 dollars, qui remonte à octobre 2025. Pour Geoffrey Kendrick, responsable de la recherche crypto chez la banque Standard Chartered, le plus dur n’est peut-être pas passé. Selon lui, « ce n’est qu’une fois les actifs dégelés et davantage de détails sur le piratage connus que nous trouverons un nouveau plancher ».
À lire aussi : Après Ledger, deux autres géants des portefeuilles crypto victimes d’un incident de sécurité
Tout le marché crypto est dans le rouge
Comme à l’accoutumée, le Bitcoin a entraîné l’ensemble du marché crypto dans sa chute. La capitalisation totale des cryptomonnaies a reculé de plus de 3 % en l’espace d’une nuit. Plus de 70 milliards de dollars de valorisation ont disparu au petit matin. Sans surprise, le BNB, la cryptomonnaie émise par Binance, a été le plus secoué, avec une baisse de plus de 6 %.

articles.title: Wie Solid-State-Transformatoren den Strombedarf von KI-Rechenzentren stemmen könnten
articles.text:
Stromnetz am Limit: Wie Solid-State-Transformatoren jetzt Abhilfe schaffen könnten
Transformatoren sind ein zentraler, aber fast unsichtbarer Bestandteil unseres Stromnetzes: Die Großgeräte tragen dazu bei, Strom effizient über lange Entfernungen zu transportieren. Die Technik ist komplex und schwer zu bauen – immer noch. Da sich ihr grundlegendes Design seit etwa einem Jahrhundert kaum verändert hat, wären sie eigentlich reif für eine Modernisierung, doch die schien lange nicht zu passieren. Das ändert sich jetzt: Während die Welt darum kämpft, den steigenden Strombedarf von Elektrofahrzeugen, Rechenzentren und anderen Bereichen zu decken, suchen Forscher und Unternehmen nach Möglichkeiten, Transformatoren umzukrempeln. Und es gibt erste Erfolge: Neue Halbleiter-gestützte Varianten der Technik könnten dazu beitragen, Versorgungsengpässe teilweise zu lindern und sicherzustellen, dass das Stromnetz dem wachsenden Nachfragedruck standhalten kann.

articles.title: Microsoft Edge
articles.text:
Microsoft's browser provides a fast, secure, and modern web experience. Browse the web anywhere with one seamless experience from your phone to your computer and other signed-in devices. Microsoft Edge is also a safe browser that gives you the tools to protect your privacy and security online.
How does Edge compare to Chrome and Firefox in terms of performance and usability?
Edge is built on the Chromium engine, similar to Chrome, and often offers comparable or better performance, especially regarding memory usage. It also supports Chrome extensions and includes features like vertical tabs and a built-in PDF viewer. However, some users prefer Firefox for its open-source nature and privacy features.
Is Microsoft Edge too bloated with unnecessary features?
Some users feel that Edge has become cluttered with features like the sidebar, shopping tools, games, and Microsoft Rewards integration. While these features can be disabled, the default experience may seem overwhelming to those seeking a minimalist browser.
Why does Microsoft Edge keep running in the background even after I close it?
Many users have reported that Edge continues to run in the background despite disabling settings like "Startup Boost" and "Continue running background apps when Microsoft Edge is closed." This issue can be particularly noticeable when using multiple profiles, where extensions from closed profiles may remain active.
Can Edge block autoplay media?
Yes, Microsoft Edge lets you block all the autoplay media by heading to edge://settings/content/mediaAutoplay and selecting "Block" from the drop-down menu. You can also add exceptions to websites using the "Add" tool in site permissions.
Why is Edge a Microsoft browser you should actually use?
Microsoft Edge is a well rounded browser based on Chromium with four key advantages:
- It offers solid integration with Windows and other Microsoft services, which allows for more direct communications between programs and thus a more fluent workflow.
- Performance and battery savings are improved upon Chrome and other Chromium-based browsers.
- You can access all Chrome extensions giving you a world of options to customize the browser.
- It adds enhanced privacy settings and track prevention measures that give you control over almost all aspects of the information you share. Microsoft promises that while using InPrivate tabs, your browsing and search data aren't saved on your device and any data collected will not be tied with your Microsoft account.
Features
Compose
With the power of AI, you can effortlessly transform your ideas into polished drafts, saving valuable time and ensuring the right tone, wherever you write online. Compose is available only with Copilot in the Edge browser. To open Compose, click the Copilot icon in the upper-right of Edge, and then click Compose at the top of the Copilot sidepane. Simply click the Re-generate draft button on the bottom of your draft, and Compose will rewrite it. You can also type input at the bottom of the Preview box, and have Compose rewrite your draft based on that feedback. To go back to your previous draft, click the Back button.
Making the web a better place for everyone
We've adopted the Chromium open source project in the development of Microsoft Edge to create better web compatibility for our customers, and less fragmentation of the web for all web developers.
Investing in open source
We've also started making contributions back to Chromium in areas like accessibility, touch, ARM64 and others. Our plan is to continue working in Chromium rather than creating a parallel project. We're working directly with the teams at Google, and we're looking forward to working even more with the open source community. To learn more about our contributions, see our Microsoft Edge "Explainers" on GitHub and check out our source code release.
We're listening!
The Microsoft Edge team wants to hear from you. In December we asked visitors to this site "if you could change one thing about the web, what would it be?". We've read your answers and have some thoughts to share. Head over to the Microsoft Edge Insider Forum to see what the community is saying about this and other topics.
Microsoft Edge now uses Mica material
Mica is an opaque, dynamic material that incorporates theme and desktop wallpaper to paint the background of long-lived windows such as apps and settings. You can apply Mica to your application backdrop to delight users and create visual hierarchy, aiding productivity, by increasing clarity about which window is in focus. Mica is specifically designed for app performance as it only samples the desktop wallpaper once to create its visualization. Mica is available for UWP apps that use WinUI 2 and apps that use Windows App SDK 1.1 or later, while running on Windows 11 version 22000 or later.
What's New
Edge is faster on Windows with Accelerated App Launches
We're excited to announce that Edge is the first browser to support accelerated app launches on Windows, delivering a faster and more consistent browser launch experience.
With accelerated app launch, most Windows users will see a 15% launch speed improvement, with wins of up to 33% under heavy multitasking!1 That means you can start browsing faster.
This has already rolled out starting with Microsoft Edge version 150 and later and is supported on Windows 11, versions 25H2, 26H2, 26H1 with the October 2026 non-security update (KB5127936) or later.
How does this work?
The Edge and Windows team partnered to bring this new Windows accelerated app launch capability to Edge users quickly. Edge, like many modern applications on Windows, is often already running. A visible Edge window might already be open, or Edge might already be running in the background through features such as Startup Boost.
Without accelerated app launches on Windows, when you click on a link or start Edge from the taskbar, Windows must first determine if Edge is already running. To do that, Windows starts an intermediary process that looks for the already-running browser and, if one is found, forwards the request.
On a PC that just started, you might barely notice. But in real multi-tasking scenarios, the extra work of having to look for an existing Edge process could make Edge feel slow.
Now, with accelerated app launches on Windows, when an Edge process starts, it sends a registration request to Windows. Windows checks and accepts the request. Later, when Edge is launched again, Windows can use the accelerated-launch registration to notify the already running Edge process directly.
Accelerated app launches are supported by the Start menu and the Taskbar and opening supported links that open in Edge by default.
For developers who are interested in supporting accelerated launches in their own Windows apps, see Register your application for accelerated app launches.
Making Edge work great on Windows
Accelerated app launches is part of our work to make Edge work great on Windows and we'll continue innovating in this area. We're working with Windows on adding other ways to utilize this feature, such as when opening PDF files.
We're also contributing this work to Chromium, the open-source project which Edge is based on, so other Chromium-based browsers can benefit from accelerated launches on Windows in the future.
Previous Release Notes:
Microsoft Edge supported operating systems for macOS. Microsoft Edge version 150 is the last release that supports macOS 12 (Monterey). Microsoft Edge version 151 or later requires macOS 13 (Ventura) or later. For more information, see Microsoft Edge supported operating systems.
Migration to improved V2 architecture for Workspaces. Workspaces, introduced in Edge in 2022, allows users to create durable sets of tabs that can be saved and shared with others. In order to improve reliability and performance of this feature, the following changes are being made:
- Migrating data for saved Workspaces from OneDrive/SharePoint to Edge Sync service
- Removing the collaboration/share functionality of this feature
For organizations who have disabled Sync through policy, the existing v1 Workspace data will still be migrated to the new architecture. New v2 Workspaces created after migration won't sync across devices and will remain local to each device. This update occurs on a progressive rollout beginning in Edge Stable v145 and continues rolling out through Edge v150. For more information, see Getting started with Microsoft Edge Workspaces.
Sidebar app list is being retired. We're simplifying Microsoft Edge. The sidebar app list will be retired in the near future. New apps can no longer be added to the sidebar, and apps currently pinned in the app tower will be removed in a future update. Sidebar app policies will no longer be supported, and any configured sidebar app policies will no longer be applied. For more information, see Streamline access to your favorite sites and apps with Sidebar in Microsoft Edge.
Feature Updates
Clarify choices surrounding third-party cookie settings. Language under 'Settings > Privacy, search, and services > Cookies' is updated to better describe the choices users have when managing third-party cookies.
Sign in to Edge with a Google account. Users can now sign in to Microsoft Edge using a Google account in addition to a Microsoft account from the profile menu and Edge sign-in screen. Available for Windows and macOS devices. Admins can control availability of this feature using the NonMicrosoftAccountSignInEnabled policy. Note: This is a controlled feature rollout. If you don't see this feature, check back as we continue our rollout.
Intune MAM Protected Downloads. The protected downloads feature for Intune MAM now saves downloaded files to the 'Documents > Microsoft Edge > Downloads' folder in OneDrive.
Enterprise WebView2 runtime downgrade via DowngradeVersion policy. Starting with Microsoft Edge version 150, enterprises can actively use the 'DowngradeVersion' policy to downgrade WebView2 applications. Administrators can temporarily roll back specific applications to a previous WebView2 Evergreen Runtime version (N-1 or N-2) using the new 'DowngradeVersion' policy in msedgewebview2.admx. The policy allows enterprises to mitigate critical regressions by specifying per-application executable-to-version mappings. The Edge Updater installs the target version side-by-side, and the WebView2 Loader redirects targeted applications accordingly. Downgrades automatically expire with each new WebView2 release. Applications pinned to N-1 remain on the same version (now becoming N-2) and automatically update in the next release, while applications pinned to N-2 revert to the current Evergreen Runtime. The policy applies only to enterprise-managed devices (domain-joined or MDM-enrolled). For more information, see Microsoft Edge WebView2 Policy Documentation.
Update to the "View in File Explorer" feature. When the ConfigureViewInFileExplorer policy is enabled, the View in File Explorer feature can be used in SharePoint document libraries. Microsoft Edge has updated the feature to enforce additional validation and restrictions when triggered by webpages to improve security.
Security Update Alerts in the Edge management service. Administrators can choose a severity threshold and receive alerts when a new Microsoft Edge update includes security fixes that meet or exceed that level, including zero-day fixes. This helps organizations quickly identify updates that may require attention while avoiding unnecessary notifications for routine releases. Note: This experience is in public preview and is available by opting in to Targeted Release in the Microsoft 365 admin center. For more information, see Monitoring dashboard.

articles.title: Offering Free Wi-Fi to Customers Without Opening a Door Into Your Own Systems - Tech Guide
articles.text:
The Growing Demand for Customer Wi-Fi and the Security Challenge
In today’s digital landscape, offering free Wi-Fi to customers has become more than a convenience-it’s a business expectation. Whether you run a café, retail store, or any customer-facing business, providing seamless internet access can significantly enhance the customer experience and even drive repeat visits. With smartphones, tablets, and laptops becoming ubiquitous, customers often decide where to spend their time based on internet availability. A recent study shows that 58% of customers expect free Wi-Fi in public venues, making it a key competitive advantage for businesses.
However, this convenience comes with a critical cybersecurity challenge: how to offer free Wi-Fi without exposing your own internal networks to potential risks. The risk is not hypothetical. Many businesses struggle to separate their guest networks from their sensitive internal systems, increasing the risk of cyberattacks, data breaches, and unauthorized access. Cybercriminals often target unsecured guest Wi-Fi networks as an entry point to launch attacks on business infrastructure. According to IBM’s 2023 Cost of a Data Breach Report, the average cost of a data breach in 2023 was $4.45 million. This staggering figure highlights the financial and reputational consequences of inadequate network security.
Why Segmentation Is Essential in Wi-Fi Network Setup
The fundamental principle in safely offering free Wi-Fi is network segmentation. Network segmentation means creating separate virtual networks-one dedicated to your internal business operations and another exclusively for guest access. By doing so, you ensure that customers can access the internet without gaining any visibility into your internal servers, databases, or critical business applications. This separation is typically achieved through technologies such as VLANs (Virtual Local Area Networks) and firewalls that enforce strict boundaries between networks.
Failing to implement such segmentation puts your business at significant risk. Cyber attackers frequently exploit insecure guest networks to gain footholds inside corporate environments, potentially leading to ransomware attacks, data theft, or service disruptions. Segmentation acts as a vital barrier that restricts unauthorized lateral movement within your network.
Implementing this segmentation effectively requires expertise and a well-structured IT approach. For organizations seeking to secure IT with Red Bigfoot, partnering with specialists who understand the complexities of network architecture and cybersecurity best practices is crucial. This approach not only protects your internal systems but also ensures compliance with data protection regulations that increasingly mandate secure network practices.
Best Practices for Offering Secure Guest Wi-Fi
- Use a Dedicated Guest Network
Always configure a separate SSID (Service Set Identifier) for guest Wi-Fi. This network should be isolated from your internal systems using firewalls and VLANs. This ensures that devices connected to the guest network cannot communicate with devices on your corporate network. By logically separating these networks, you minimize the risk that a compromised guest device can access sensitive business resources.
- Employ Strong Authentication and Encryption
While offering free Wi-Fi, you don’t want to make access cumbersome, but it’s important to enforce at least minimal authentication, such as a simple password or a captive portal where users must agree to terms of service before connecting. Additionally, ensure that the network uses WPA3 encryption to protect data transmission. WPA3 is the latest Wi-Fi security protocol that offers enhanced protection against password guessing and eavesdropping.
- Monitor and Limit Bandwidth
To prevent abuse and maintain quality of service, set bandwidth limits or session timeouts. This not only protects your internet resources but also helps maintain network performance for all users. Monitoring network traffic can also help identify suspicious activity, such as unusually high data usage that might indicate malicious behavior.
- Regularly Update Firmware and Security Patches
Wi-Fi access points and routers need to be regularly updated to patch known vulnerabilities. An outdated device can be a weak link that jeopardizes your entire network. Vendors often release firmware updates that fix security flaws and improve device stability, so staying current is essential.
For businesses looking to implement these recommendations, consulting with experts like Technology Advisory Group, a local tech company can ensure your guest Wi-Fi is both user-friendly and secure. Professional guidance helps tailor the network design to your specific business needs, balancing ease of access with robust security controls.
Advanced Security Measures to Consider
Beyond basic segmentation and encryption, there are more advanced security features that can further protect your business when offering free Wi-Fi:
– Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS): These systems monitor the network for unusual or suspicious activity and can alert administrators to potential threats early. IDS can detect attempts to scan the network, brute-force attacks, or malware communication.
– Network Access Control (NAC): NAC ensures that only compliant and trusted devices can connect to the internal network, even if users attempt to bridge from the guest network. NAC can enforce security policies such as requiring updated antivirus software or blocking unauthorized devices.
– Regular Security Audits: Conducting routine audits helps identify vulnerabilities and ensures compliance with industry standards such as PCI-DSS for retail or HIPAA for healthcare. Audits also provide actionable insights for continuous improvement.
These advanced measures complement the foundational practices and create a layered defense strategy, significantly reducing risk.
The Role of Employee Training and Policy Enforcement
Technology alone is not enough. Employees should be trained on the importance of maintaining network security, recognizing phishing attempts, and reporting suspicious activity. Phishing remains one of the most common attack vectors, and well-informed staff are a critical line of defense.
Additionally, clear policies regarding guest Wi-Fi use and internal network access should be established and communicated. For example, employees should understand that they must not connect their devices to the guest network when accessing sensitive company resources. Enforcement of these policies is essential to prevent accidental security lapses.
Balancing Convenience with Security: The Business Benefits
When implemented correctly, offering free Wi-Fi can result in tangible benefits beyond customer satisfaction. Businesses report increased dwell time, higher engagement, and valuable data collection opportunities through captive portals. According to a survey, 70% of consumers are more likely to visit a business that offers free Wi-Fi. This enhanced customer engagement can translate into increased sales and brand loyalty.
Moreover, captive portals can be used to gather customer insights such as email addresses or preferences, enabling targeted marketing campaigns. This data-driven approach helps businesses better understand their clientele and tailor services accordingly.
However, these benefits must never come at the expense of security. Compromised business systems can lead to operational downtime, reputational damage, and regulatory fines. For instance, the average downtime cost for a business after a cyberattack can exceed $300,000 per hour. Therefore, investing in secure guest Wi-Fi infrastructure is both a protective measure and a business enabler.
Conclusion
Providing free Wi-Fi to customers is a powerful tool for enhancing the customer experience and maintaining competitive advantage. Yet, the risks associated with exposing internal networks cannot be ignored. By adopting network segmentation, employing strong authentication, and partnering with experienced cybersecurity professionals, businesses can offer safe and reliable guest Wi-Fi without opening a door into their own systems.
For companies serious about safeguarding their digital assets while delivering excellent customer service, exploring solutions should be a top priority. Engaging trusted local experts can help tailor the right technology strategy for your unique business needs.
In the ever-evolving landscape of cybersecurity threats, proactive measures today will protect your business tomorrow. Offering free Wi-Fi securely is not just about technology-it’s about preserving trust and enabling growth in a connected world.

articles.title: Over 25% of people lie to get antibiotics—and their lies aren't even good
articles.text:
A significant number of patients in the US lie to their doctors to get antibiotics they likely don’t need, according to two new studies. While that may not be a startling revelation, the studies drills down on the phenomenon, finding that the lies patients tell are generally bad ones—and yet, they work almost all the time.
In the two linked studies published Friday in JAMA Network Open, a team of researchers led by Alistair Thorpe at the University of Utah analyzed online survey data from over 1,000 adults. They found that over a quarter of people reported having lied to a clinician at least once to get an antibiotic prescription for themselves or a child in their care. Patients lied by either exaggerating symptoms, making up symptoms, or—most often—both.
But interestingly, the lies people told to get antibiotics involved making up or exaggerating symptoms of infections that wouldn’t be treated with antibiotics. For example, the most common falsehoods were symptoms associated with colds, such as fever, cough, and sore throat. That’s despite the fact that colds are caused by viruses, not bacteria—which antibiotics treat.
Further, while the data suggests many patients were being dishonest, clinicians responded with what could be considered their own form of dishonesty; in most cases, the dubious fibs led to antibiotic prescriptions. Specifically, 77 percent of adult patients and 87 percent of caregivers said their lies worked, leading them to get the antibiotic prescriptions they wanted.
“These findings signal a significant issue for health professionals making antibiotic prescribing decisions and for the fields of antimicrobial stewardship and public health,” Thorpe and colleagues concluded.
Detailed deception
For the study, the researchers reviewed survey responses from 1,371 online respondents and found 959 responses that were valid and complete. Of those, 268 (28 percent) respondents reported misrepresenting their symptoms to get antibiotics. Of those, 108 reported exaggerating symptoms, 19 reported fabricating symptoms, and 141 reported doing both. In a separate analysis of 263 respondents who identified as caregivers, 63 (27 percent) reported misrepresenting symptoms of a child to get antibiotics.

articles.title: Meta pode pagar R$ 50 milhões por posts que incentivam demissão política • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Meta pode pagar R$ 50 milhões por posts que incentivam demissão política
Ministério Público do Trabalho pede remoção de publicações e multa de R$ 500 mil por conteúdo mantido nas redes sociais da empresa.
O Ministério Público do Trabalho (MPT) entrou com uma ação contra a Meta por permitir a circulação e ampliar o alcance de publicações que incentivam empresas a demitir funcionários por sua escolha eleitoral. O órgão federal pede R$ 50 milhões de indenização por danos morais coletivos, além de exigir a retirada de publicações do tipo em um prazo de 24 horas.
O MPT afirma ter recebido mais de 3.080 denúncias de assédio eleitoral durante o pleito, que reelegeu Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) à Presidência. Desde então, publicações nas redes sociais passaram a sugerir que empresários demitam funcionários que votaram no presidente. Parte desse conteúdo é atribuída a apoiadores do candidato Flávio Bolsonaro (PL).
Em nota, o órgão alega que a Meta é responsável pela ampla disseminação desse tipo de conteúdo, que incentiva a “discriminação, retaliação ou punição de empregados por orientação política”. A empresa de Mark Zuckerberg também foi alvo de críticas durante as eleições por um possível tratamento desigual entre as candidaturas. O próprio TSE pediu explicações à Meta e ao X.
As publicações são apontadas como ilegais por incentivar o assédio eleitoral, convocando empregadores a vasculhar as redes sociais de funcionários para descobrir em quem votaram. Também há casos de trabalhadores expostos à “ridicularização, com nome e imagem”, além de comemorações por demissões já realizadas. Entre os autores das postagens estão empresários e parlamentares.
A responsabilização da Meta, por sua vez, iria além da permissão de conteúdo criminoso: o MPT aponta que ferramentas como a aba Explorar e as sugestões de Reels ampliam o alcance e o engajamento das postagens. Como exemplo, cita quatro publicações de um único perfil verificado, que tem 3,8 milhões de seguidores e cujos posts somavam mais de 2 milhões de curtidas.
O órgão também indica a existência de regras e sistemas automatizados da própria empresa que poderiam ser aplicadas para remover os conteúdos, o que não aconteceu. Segundo os procuradores responsáveis pela ação, a ausência de medidas por parte da Meta mostra que as decisões foram “por escolha, e não por impossibilidade técnica”. A Meta informou ao Tecnoblog que não irá comentar o caso.
O MPT pede R$ 50 milhões de indenização e a exclusão das postagens criminosas. Caso a empresa não acate, cada publicação que continuar disponível no Instagram, Facebook e Threads custará R$ 500 mil à Meta.
O órgão também pede uma retratação pública para os usuários brasileiros, afirmando que a companhia “não compactua com manifestações que incentivam a discriminiação, retaliação ou punição de empregados por orientação política”.
Outra exigência da ação cível é a notificação dos perfis que publicaram conteúdos criminosos e uma suspensão de 30 dias caso voltem a fazer isso, sob risco de desativação das contas em caso de reincidência. O MPT pede ainda a criação de uma “política permanente de prevenção ao assédio eleitoral” e que proiba “expressamente” esse publicações do tipo.

articles.title: Kentucky man wins first ever religious exemption against using AI at work and says the tech is ‘undercutting my ability to be a moral actor’
articles.text:
Humanist wins ‘first of its kind’ religious exemption from using AI at work — civil rights ruling says Kentucky man can’t be forced to outsource thinking to LLMs
Man says AI ‘runs counter to’ human flourishing
- A Kentucky man has won a religious exemption against using AI
- The ruling says he no longer has to use AI tools at work
- The man argued AI contravened his deeply held religious beliefs
If you’ve ever looked to the heavens in exasperation after being told you have to use AI at work, your prayers might soon be answered, if a Kentucky man’s example is anything to go by. That’s because he’s just been granted a “first of its kind” religious exemption from using AI after successfully arguing that it went against his beliefs.
As reported by the Religion News Service (via TomsHardware), University of Kentucky research administrator David Durman reacted with apprehension when his employer started asking its workers to use AI in their day-to-day jobs. The problem for Durman was that this would mean offloading his thinking to a machine — something which, as a humanist, went against his principles.
“The process and work involved in thinking through situations, through my work, through my ethics, through the way I handle other people, is a key component in being able to develop myself as a moral person,” Durman told RNS. “And offloading that labor, regardless of whether it’s taxing or not, is undercutting my ability to be a moral actor.”
For Durman, AI also has the potential to harm society. He stated that he advocates for and believes in human flourishing, but that “At a societal level, I think that the use of AI technology runs counter to that.”
Your belief must be sincere
Durman won his religious exemption with the help of the American Humanist Association (AHA), with AHA attorney Alexandria Huiskens saying that “This is the first of its kind at the AHA and for humanism generally to exempt those who see AI use as flying in the face of their freedom of conscience.”
Durman and the AHA based their argument on Title VII, a US federal law that grants workers exemptions in their work requirements due to religious beliefs. Although humanism — which places an emphasis on human virtue and agency — is generally considered to be non-religious, federal courts have ruled that it can be treated as a religion.
The University of Kentucky accepted Durman’s appeal, meaning he no longer has to use AI at his place of work. He does still have to meet and cooperate with his colleagues who use AI, however.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
If you think this might be a quick ticket out of using AI, though, there’s a catch. Douglas Laycock, an emeritus law professor at the University of Virginia and the University of Texas, noted that your professed beliefs have to be sincere to qualify under Title VII, so you can’t just pick a religion and say that using AI violates its tenets if you don’t actually subscribe to that belief system.
Still, for those who do hold sincere religious principles and feel that AI contravenes them, there could be a new way to dodge those mandatory AI workflows whenever you head into the office.

articles.title: Intel leaker reveals Moon Lake chip as a likely replacement for N-series SoCs — four lower-power-efficiency cores, no performance cores, and a 6W TDP
articles.text:
Intel leaker reveals Moon Lake chip as a likely replacement for N-series SoCs — four lower-power-efficiency cores, no performance cores, and a 6W TDP
A welcome refresh for ultra-budget laptops and mini-PCs.
After Intel let loose its Panther Lake chips earlier in this year, followed by Wildcat Lake in April, the firm has been pretty quiet about upcoming consumer CPUs. Known leaker Jaykihn just let a tiny cat out of the bag, though: the base specs for Moon Lake. The diminutive chip is expected to have four low-power-efficiency (LP-E) cores, and zero performance cores. These are rumors, so have your salt shaker at hand.
Given the all-efficiency layout, it's a fair guess that the cores will be Darkmont LP-E silicon. The leaker additionally notes that the chip layout is likely to be the same as Wildcat Lake, with the efficiency cores in their own island. According to Jaykihn's table, the expected TDPs range from 6 W to 15 W, within the ballpark of phone and tablet SoCs on the low side.
The specs seem to imply that Moon Lake is the successor for the Intel N-series chips present in a great deal of ultra-budget offerings. The set of specs suggests the chip will find a home in laptops and mini-PCs in the $300 to $500 range, though those amounts are naturally variable depending on how much RAM and storage the AI world will continue to slurp. Furthermore, the new silicon is only slated to arrive in 2028, and supplies of NAND and DDR may well shift further until then.
There's no word on clock speeds, though. As a reference point, the N150 had a 3.6 GHz turbo. This year's 18A Panther and Wildcat chips broadly have clock speeds matching whichever silicon they've replaced. They do seem to be both faster and more power-efficient.
Some of the newer models pack extra cores, but Moon Lake keeps the same 4-LPE count and 6 W TDP as matching N-series designs. In turn, we speculate that while some performance gains are expected thanks to the new architecture's higher IPC, machines with Moon Lake inside will likely offer markedly improved battery life compared to their predecessors.

Bruno Ferreira is a contributing writer for Tom's Hardware. He has decades of experience with PC hardware and assorted sundries, alongside a career as a developer. He's obsessed with detail and has a tendency to ramble on the topics he loves. When not doing that, he's usually playing games, or at live music shows and festivals.

articles.title: Intel’s Q3 Results Show Supply Chain Disruptions and PC Plunge - EE Times
articles.text:
Intel reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $16.5 billion, up 21% year over year, as expanded data center demand offset manufacturing bottlenecks and a sharp contraction in personal computer sales.
The results reflect a structural divide in the technology hardware sector. While AI infrastructure drives chip sales for server processors and memory suppliers, component shortages and elevated memory prices increase system costs and weigh on consumer hardware demand.
Data center demand collides with manufacturing bottlenecks
Intel’s Data Center and AI group generated $7.3 billion in third-quarter revenue, up 78% year over year, reflecting strong demand across hyperscale, enterprise, and cloud customers.
However, shortages of raw materials, substrates, and other critical components limited Intel’s ability to meet demand for its Xeon server family. A two-week shutdown at an Intel fabrication facility in Israel, following a gas explosion, further impacted production.
Because turning silicon wafers into finished chips takes roughly three months, wafers that were still in process when the fab shut down will likely be scrapped. Intel CFO David Zinsner said during the earnings call most of those write-offs should land in the fourth quarter, and he does not expect further scrapping in the first quarter. He said the fab disruption will have an estimated $300 million impact on revenue in the fourth quarter of 2026, with a similar impact in the first quarter of 2027.
“Our Q3 results demonstrate improving execution, meaningful progress expanding supply and continued advancement of our process technology,” Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan said in the press release.
“I’m disappointed that we were not able to meet strong customer demand in this quarter,” Tan said in the earnings call. “We face near-term challenges, including manufacturing supply shortage, the unprecedented memory crunch, and the resulting softness in PC demand. But I remain confident in our path forward.”
The company projected fourth-quarter revenue of $15.0 billion to $16.0 billion and a non-GAAP gross margin of 38.0%, down from 44.1% in the third quarter.
Memory shortage and PC market contraction
While Intel struggled with component supply, memory manufacturers benefited from rising demand driven by AI infrastructure investment. Both Samsung and SK Hynix recently reported record quarterly profits.
Rising memory prices created direct headwinds for personal computer manufacturers and Intel’s Client Computing and Physical AI Group, where revenue declined 5% year over year to $8.1 billion.
Surging DRAM costs from vendors including Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron forced PC makers to raise retail prices, prompting buyers to defer upgrades. “We expect the current environment to persist until memory availability and prices begin to normalize,” said Tan during the earnings call. “While the next few quarters will be challenging for the PC market, our roadmap continues to strengthen, and our long-term outlook remains positive.”
Industry adjustment and outlook
Data from Counterpoint Research indicates that global personal computer shipments fell 21% year over year in the third quarter of 2026 to 57 million units. The firm forecasts a further 27% year-over-year decline in the fourth quarter.
Minsoo Kang, a senior analyst at Counterpoint Research, noted in a report, “The global PC market is facing mounting pressure as rising memory and component costs push system prices higher and force consumers to delay replacement purchases.”
Analyst commentary underscores how high component pricing affects hardware purchasing patterns across the supply chain. David Naranjo, associate director at Counterpoint Research, stated: “The PC industry is entering a period of structural adjustment, where rising component costs, higher system prices, and longer replacement cycles are fundamentally reshaping market dynamics.”
Zinsner said Intel does not expect to generate positive free cash flow in 2027, which he described as an “investment year”. The group plans to increase capital expenditure to rebuild production capacity.

articles.title: Esta nueva memoria promete resolver uno de los mayores problemas creados por la IA
articles.text:
La industria de los semiconductores atraviesa una de las peores crisis desde la pandemia. La explosión de la IA ha disparado la demanda de memoria a niveles nunca antes vistos, lo cual generó una escasez y aumento de precios que han golpeado a todos los segmentos, incluidos los móviles. Este escenario podría cambiar gracias a la Z2RAM, una nueva tecnología impulsada por el antiguo jefe de Intel, Pat Gelsinger.
De acuerdo con un reporte de The Register, la propuesta de la Z2RAM intenta combinar las ventajas de las tres tecnologías que dominan el mercado: SRAM, DRAM y NAND.
La SRAM es extremadamente rápida y se utiliza en las memorias caché de los procesadores, pero ocupa mucho espacio y es costosa de escalar. Mientras tanto, la DRAM ofrece una mayor densidad y es la base de la memoria RAM convencional, aunque es más lenta. Por último, la NAND, que se usa en los SSD, se distingue por su capacidad y fabricación en múltiples capas verticales.
Nagare Labs, una startup respaldada por Geslinger, intenta reunir lo mejor de estos tres mundos. Según la compañía, Z2RAM podría ofrecer la velocidad de la SRAM, la densidad de la DRAM y la arquitectura de la NAND en un mismo paquete. Esta nueva memoria sería escalable y tendría un consumo energético mucho menor, convirtiéndose en una alternativa para las empresas de IA.
¿Qué es la Z2RAM, la nueva memoria que podría acabar con el RAMaggeddon?
Una de las claves de la Z2RAM está en su diseño. Mientras que la DRAM convencional usa un transistor y un condensador para almacenar cada bit de información, Z2RAM emplea dos transistores. Esto le permite usar la capacitancia de la compuerta del segundo para almacenar la carga eléctrica, eliminando la necesidad de un condensador independiente. Además, los datos no necesitan reescribirse tras cada acceso, que es una de las limitaciones de la DRAM.
Según sus desarrolladores, la Z2RAM ha sido concebida para apilarse verticalmente como las NAND y otras tecnologías de encapsulado 3D. La memoria se vale de semiconductores de óxido y técnicas de unión híbrida tridimensional, lo que le permitiría alcanzar más de cinco veces la densidad de bits de una memoria SRAM manteniendo un ancho de banda parecido. Nagare Labs dice que un espacio capaz de albergar 64 MB de SRAM podría alojar 320 MB de Z2RAM.
La nueva memoria podría ayudar a combatir la demanda de memoria que exige la industria de la IA. Además de la potencia de cálculo, uno de los cuellos de botella de los aceleradores gráficos es la capacidad de mover y almacenar los datos con suficiente rapidez. Cuanta más memoria rápida se integre cerca de los procesadores, menos chips serán necesarios para ejecutar los modelos avanzados.
Las primeras memorias comerciales podrían lanzarse en 10 años
La Z2RAM no reemplazaría a la memoria convencional, pero si podría reducir la cantidad de aceleradores que se necesitan en los centros de datos. Esto disminuiría la presión sobre la cadena de suministro, traduciéndose en una mejor disponibilidad de componentes y una baja de precio en toda la industria.
Todo suena muy bien, excepto porque la Z2RAM se encuentra en una fase preliminar de desarrollo. Los ingenieros de Nagare Labs ya desarrollaron los primeros prototipos, pero la producción comercial podría tardar una década. La empresa tiene que resolver algunos problemas de fiabilidad y estandarización de interfaces, por lo que el camino es largo.
Aún así, la Z2RAM podría convertirse en una de las innovaciones más importantes del hardware moderno, siempre y cuando cumpla sus promesas.

articles.title: Remplazar la batería de la nueva Nintendo Switch 2 es más fácil que nunca: nueve tornillos te separan de ello
articles.text:
La nueva Nintendo Switch 2 con batería reemplazable llegó a las tiendas europeas este otoño y sí, lo cierto es que es bastante sencillo cambiarle la batería o acceder a ella en caso de que lo necesites. De hecho, la compañía ha publicado una guía oficial que nos muestra cómo hacerlo en unos sencillos pasos. Lo único que necesitas es un destornillador.
Por normativa europea. La Switch 2 original se fabricó como la mayoría de las consolas modernas y dispositivos, con la batería fija en su sitio y sin ninguna manera obvia de intercambiarla. La nueva revisión cambia eso para cubrirse en salud con la normativa europea, concretamente el Reglamento (UE) 2023/1542.
Esta medida exige que las baterías portátiles incorporadas en ciertos aparatos puedan ser retiradas y sustituidas por el usuario final durante la vida útil del producto, con excepciones y condiciones específicas. De esta manera, cuando la batería comience a degradarse, los propietarios pueden reemplazarla por su cuenta.
En detalle. Así que ahora hay dos variantes de Switch 2. El modelo BEE-001 (-01) es la que contiene la batería reemplazable, mientras que el modelo BEE-001 no. Si tienes una en casa y quieres saber qué consola tiene una batería reemplazable, lo mejor que puedes hacer es echarle un ojo al código de barras que aparece en la parte de detrás de la consola, justo al levantar la patilla: si empieza por HA es la original, y si es HL, la que lleva la batería reemplazable.
Cómo reemplazar la batería. Según la propia guía de Nintendo, lo único que tenemos que hacer es apagar la consola por completo, retirar cables, tarjetas, los Joy-Con, y retirar los tornillos. Hay nueve tornillos en total: cinco en la carcasa trasera y cuatro en los conectores magnéticos. Los nueve son negros y miden 3,0 mm de largo. Dos de los nueve tornillos se encuentran detrás del soporte, por lo que es fácil pasarlos por alto.
Una vez hayas retirado todos los tornillos, levanta la cubierta trasera con la solapa de los cartuchos abierta. Y cuando ya tengas la tapa quitada, levanta la batería por la pequeña lengüeta que tiene en la parte superior derecha y deslízala hacia fuera. Pon la nueva batería, comprueba todo, y cerramos.
Diferencias. La nueva consola pesa 409 g, frente a los 400 g de la original. Además, es un 1 % más pequeña en la consola para ajustarse al chasis, así que eso afecta también (mínimamente) a la autonomía.
Curiosamente, según el despiece del creador de contenido Austin Evans, el ventilador nuevo parece ser ligeramente más silencioso.
Kit de reemplazo. Nintendo prometió un kit de reemplazo para facilitarnos aún más la tarea, y dice que se venderá a través de su tienda "en el futuro", sin fecha ni precio todavía. El kit no tiene mucho misterio vaya, ya que incluye la batería y un destornillador Phillips PH00.
