articles.title: Fujifilm to boost tape production 5x as AI fuels archiving demand
articles.text:
In an announcement released Thursday, Fujifilm said it will invest roughly 10 billion yen (about $63 million) to increase its production capacity fivefold for an unlikely beneficiary of the AI era: magnetic tape.
Fujifilm attributes the surge in archiving demand to the spread of generative AI, which the company remarked is producing “exponential growth” in data needs worldwide. The 5x increase in production capacity will be measured against fiscal year 2025 production levels.
The investment in Fujifilm’s Kanagawa Factory, Odawara site will make it “the largest investment Fujifilm has made to date in dedicated LTO tape facilities.” The project will run from fiscal years 2026 through 2028 to fund manufacturing expansion and additional personnel, primarily to produce the latest-generation “FUJIFILM LTO Ultrium10” tape.
Mainstream consumers may have abandoned tape decades ago, but the enterprise world never did. Cloud giants rely on tape to back up vast troves of data. Fujifilm’s work with magnetic tape as a data storage medium dates back to the 1950s, and in 2000, the company released its first LTO Ultrium storage tape. In 2011, the company was the first to commercially produce tape with barium ferrite magnetic particles, and in 2025 it debuted the LTO Ultrium10, the first storage solution in the medium to use what the company calls “fine hybrid magnetic particles” by combining barium ferrite with strontium ferrite tech. Each generation of tape (currently Gen 10) has seen meaningful increases in both compressed and uncompressed storage limits.
According to Fujifilm, “major cloud service and data center operators” have been expanding their use of magnetic tape because it can store large data volumes at relatively low cost. Tape backups can be easily disconnected and stored in a drawer, a vault, or a separate facility. Fujifilm highlights the ability to air-gap tape cartridges as a last defense for user data: “Given the sophistication of cyberattacks, magnetic tape is attracting increasing attention as a means of protecting data from threats such as ransomware.”

articles.title: Apple Intelligence is finally coming to China with iOS 27.3
articles.text:
Apple will launch Apple Intelligence in China with iOS 27.3, the company announced on its Chinese newsroom website, as reported by MacRumors. The Apple Intelligence features will be available first in an iOS 27.3 beta that’s set to launch on November 4th, with a full iOS 27.3 release scheduled for December.
Apple Intelligence is finally coming to China with iOS 27.3
Apple is launching an iOS 27.3 beta next week that will bring some of the initial Apple Intelligence features to the Chinese market.
This launch doesn’t bring the new Siri AI to China. Instead, Apple is launching several of its earlier Apple Intelligence features like notification summaries, real-time translation, rewriting and proofreading tools, visual intelligence, and removing objects from photos. Apple also says it has worked with Ailbaba to add support for its Qwen chatbot in some experiences, which sounds similar to iOS’s integration with OpenAI’s ChatGPT that launched in 2024.
Apple Intelligence was approved in China in July, which signalled that the launch of the AI tools was getting near. Apple trained its own LLM specifically for China, Reuters reported in August.

articles.title: The Netherlands risks losing its AgriTech crown, warns new report | EU-Startups
articles.text:
The Netherlands has long been regarded as a European leader in agricultural and food innovation, but that position appears to be under threat.
A new report published today by Dutch national investment institution Invest-NL warns that the country risks losing its competitive edge as other nations move faster to commercialise emerging agricultural technologies.
According to the report, Deep Dive Agrifood Biotech, addressing the barriers facing Dutch agrifood biotechnology companies could unlock approximately €17 billion in additional annual revenue by 2040. However, without coordinated action on regulation, financing and commercialisation, much of that opportunity could be captured elsewhere.
Based on interviews with more than 150 entrepreneurs, investors, researchers and policymakers, alongside investment data spanning 2010 to April 2026, the study examines three strategic areas: seed breeding and genetics, biological agricultural inputs, and biotech-derived food ingredients.
A strong start, a weaker finish
The Netherlands is home to notable agricultural research institutions, established seed breeders and a sophisticated food production ecosystem. Yet it seems scientific excellence is not necessarily translating into globally competitive businesses.
The report highlights a particularly telling imbalance: the Netherlands accounts for 3.3% of BioTech startups worldwide, but only 1.3% of scale-ups, according to broader BioTech data cited from the Netherlands Organisation for Applied Scientific Research (TNO). This suggests that while the country remains effective at generating innovation, it is less successful at helping young companies achieve meaningful commercial scale.
Invest-NL identifies three recurring weaknesses:
- too few promising technologies become scalable ventures
- regulatory and validation processes delay market entry
- insufficient financing prevents companies from reaching industrial production
The stakes extend beyond individual businesses. In a favourable scenario, Invest-NL estimates that annual Dutch agrifood BioTech revenues could reach approximately €25 billion by 2040, compared with just €8–9 billion if current conditions persist.
Crucially, the report argues that the Netherlands does not need to manufacture everything domestically. Instead, it should focus on retaining strategically valuable knowledge, intellectual property, companies and specialised capabilities, while taking advantage of European production networks where appropriate.
Ten years to say yes
One of the most striking obstacles concerns biological crop protection, where Dutch companies are developing alternatives to conventional chemical pesticides.
Obtaining European regulatory approval for a new biological crop protection product can take eight to ten years. Existing frameworks were largely designed around chemical products, making them less suited to certain biological innovations.
Consequently, some companies prioritise launching in markets such as Brazil and the United States, where commercialisation can proceed more quickly. Invest-NL warns that Europe risks losing ground in a biological crop protection market that could expand seven- to tenfold by 2040.
Food biotechnology faces similar difficulties. Regulatory approval for novel ingredients can take one to three years longer in Europe than in the United States, while building a first commercial production facility can require tens or even hundreds of millions of euros.
For fermentation-derived food ingredients alone, Invest-NL estimates that favourable conditions could support approximately €8 billion in annual Dutch revenues by 2040, compared with around €2 billion under existing policies.
The report stresses that faster approvals should not come at the expense of safety. Instead, regulators should offer earlier guidance, more predictable assessments and opportunities for companies to validate products under real-world conditions.
Innovation is not the issue
Recent EU-Startups coverage demonstrates that Dutch AgriTech entrepreneurs continue to attract investor interest across several areas identified in the report.
In August, Eindhoven-based VitalFluid secured €17.2 million to accelerate the commercialisation of its plasma-activated water technology, which offers growers an alternative to chemical crop protection. The investment was co-led by Invest-NL and Alder Tree Investments.
Meanwhile, Wageningen-based Aardaia raised €5 million in July to advance its genomics-driven crop breeding platform and develop a protein-rich tuber, while Nijmegen-based Gravity Gardens secured €2.6 million in September to scale its chemical-free seed activation technology.
Dutch food BioTech is also producing notable funding announcements. In June, Vivici received €12.5 million in European Innovation Council backing to expand the supply and commercial reach of its precision-fermented dairy proteins.
Last year, EU-Startups also reported on Revyve’s nearly €24 million Series B to expand production of yeast-based ingredients that can replace eggs in food manufacturing. Revyve had already commissioned a first-of-a-kind production facility in the Netherlands, illustrating that industrial scale-up is achievable with sustained backing.
Nevertheless, these successes do not eliminate the wider structural challenges. They illustrate the breadth of Dutch innovation, but also the importance of providing companies with appropriate financing and support beyond their initial funding rounds.
Europe will not wait
Across Europe, EU-Startups has reported comparable investment activity, illustrating how competition is developing around the same technologies.
In biological crop protection, France’s Agriodor raised €15 million in April to expand its natural scent-based pest management technology, while Denmark’s Mycoverse secured €2.4 million in March to develop fungal alternatives to chemical pesticides.
The competition is equally visible in food ingredients. French precision fermentation startups Verley raised €32 million and Standing Ovation secured €30 million in 2026, while Belgian fermentation company MAASH obtained a €12.15 million financing package combining equity and public financing to support industrial-scale mycoprotein production.
These announcements do not establish that the Netherlands has already lost its position. They do, however, show that European competitors are securing capital, developing production capacity and pursuing commercial opportunities in precisely the areas where Invest-NL sees significant Dutch potential.
To respond, Invest-NL proposes an indicative €650 million to €1.1 billion in public financing capacity between 2026 and 2030, spanning research, regulatory improvements, infrastructure and industrial scale-up.
Its ambitions for 2030 include doubling the number of agrifood BioTech ventures, reducing time to market by a factor of three, and developing five globally competitive companies capable of raising more than €100 million each.
For the Netherlands, the question is therefore becoming less about whether it can develop the next generation of agricultural technologies, and more about whether it can create the conditions for those technologies to become successful businesses.

articles.title: Busy GPUs can hide slow AI inference on Kubernetes
articles.text:
Busy GPUs can hide slow AI inference on Kubernetes
A Kubernetes cluster can be healthy while the AI service running on it disappoints users. A model might return its first token quickly but take too long to finish an answer. It might respond promptly and still give the wrong answer. And a busy GPU tells the operations team little about either outcome. The operational challenge is connecting AI service behavior with the Kubernetes, GPU, compute, storage, and network conditions behind it—not viewing each layer in isolation.
That’s why you should measure an inference service before production, then compare live behavior with the baseline. In the fourth article in this HPE-sponsored series on AI and Kubernetes, The New Stack speaks with Marius Bogoevici, Senior Principal Product Manager for HPE Morpheus Software; Mahesh Ramachandran, Vice President of Product Management for HPE OpsRamp Software; and Karthik Subramanian, Principal Product Manager for HPE Morpheus Software.
Inference adds a further question: Does the whole service deliver a useful result at a cost and speed the business can support?
Earlier in this series:
- Part 1: Developers and platform teams both want Kubernetes self-service. They disagree on who owns it.
- Part 2: A live Kubernetes cluster can still have an ownership gap
- Part 3: Your Kubernetes dashboard is green. Your users are seeing red.
Start with the experience, then establish a baseline
For a conversational service, Bogoevici recommends measuring time to first token, time per output token, reliability, capacity, resource efficiency, cost, and answer quality. The right mix depends on the experience a team intends to deliver. A quick first token can mask slow subsequent generation; a fast complete response can still be inaccurate or unhelpful.
“A quick first token can mask slow subsequent generation; a fast complete response can still be inaccurate or unhelpful.”
Time to first token and time to a complete response answer different questions. Inter-token latency and time per output token help explain generation speed after the first token arrives. Teams should document where they measure each interval and compare results under sustained load and demand spikes. Set targets for the particular workload and user experience.
Ramachandran urges teams to profile the AI serving system before customers depend on it. Test representative prompt and context lengths, output volumes, and traffic levels. Record token throughput, latency, and service-level measures under those conditions. The resulting baseline gives operators a reference to measure production behavior changes.
Correlating those workload measures with infrastructure performance and capacity helps teams distinguish rising inference demand from resource contention and plan capacity more effectively. As Ramachandran tells The New Stack, teams should “profile it before you launch.”
Quality needs its own evaluation. Bogoevici says teams should ask whether the service gives proper answers or hallucinates. Platform telemetry can show a request was served, but data science and domain specialists need representative tests and acceptance criteria for the answer.
The newly published ebook, Kubernetes in 2027: Building platforms for AI, autonomy, and scale, recommends assessing output quality alongside service performance and revisiting both after model, prompt, retrieval, or serving changes.
When the GPU is busy but the service is slow
GPU utilization is a useful signal, but it does not identify the bottleneck. Bogoevici sketches a misleading victory lap: “Our GPUs are maxed at 100%. So we’re doing well.” That tells teams little about how the service actually performs. Ramachandran suggests checking whether inference pods scale on workload-appropriate metrics, whether requests reach the intended model, and whether related components can be scheduled when needed. Different models can have different latency and capacity demands, so a change in request mix can change the user experience even while GPU activity looks normal.
Bogoevici sketches a misleading victory lap: “Our GPUs are maxed at 100%. So we’re doing well.”
Subramanian adds dependencies around the model: network configuration and database or vector-database response time. He raises another question: “Is the GPU partition too small to serve that model?” These are investigation paths, not a diagnosis that applies to every deployment. Teams should correlate them with the affected requests and time window before choosing a fix.
Kubernetes’ Horizontal Pod Autoscaler can use configured custom or external metrics, so teams do not have to replace it simply because CPU utilization is a poor trigger for inference. They do need to supply and test the metrics pipeline, scaling bounds, and available accelerator capacity for their serving stack. A scaling policy cannot make additional GPU capacity appear instantly.
What HPE Morpheus and OpsRamp contribute
HPE describes HPE Morpheus Software as a platform for governed provisioning and automation across hybrid environments. Its Advanced and Enterprise versions include HPE Kubernetes Service (HKS); Enterprise extends the operating model across hybrid and public-cloud environments. Platform teams can use catalog items, blueprints, access controls, and approvals to define how they request and manage supported environments. This gives platform teams a consistent way to deliver governed self-service and manage VMs and Kubernetes clusters together, reducing separate tooling and manual handoffs. Those capabilities alone do not benchmark a model or decide whether its answers are good.
HPE OpsRamp Software provides full-stack observability and monitoring across multi-vendor hybrid infrastructure and applications, with service maps, AI-powered event correlation, and operational automation to help teams understand dependencies and move from detection to resolution. Ramachandran describes HPE Morpheus as the provisioning engine and OpsRamp as the observability engine in HPE’s broader cloud operations approach.
Ramachandran says HPE’s combined solution includes Morpheus, OpsRamp and runtimes. He says it can measure token service rates in a model-serving environment and token request rates in an agentic workload. HPE is extending OpsRamp’s AI workload observability to connect model and agent activity, token volumes, token serving rates, inference latency, and time to first token with supporting infrastructure telemetry.
The operational value is the correlation: teams can investigate whether slow responses originate in the application, model-serving layer, or infrastructure, while using workload demand to inform capacity planning and cost accountability. For a specific deployment, teams should confirm which component emits each metric, how it is collected, and what additional application instrumentation is needed.
For agentic applications, HPE’s planned observability enhancements extend that context to AI traces, tool calls, errors, and quality signals alongside Kubernetes, CPU, GPU, memory, storage, and network telemetry. Lightweight eBPF and OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation are also planned to deepen visibility while minimizing collection overhead. These signals support investigation; they do not replace domain-specific answer evaluation or security controls.
As the preceding article in this series explains, collecting telemetry across a stack depends on deployed agents, integrations, permissions, and application instrumentation. For an inference service, connect user-facing measurements with model-server metrics and traces, Kubernetes events, and relevant network, database, and accelerator signals. Check where visibility stops, especially at an external model or service boundary.
Plan for AI-specific routing and scheduling
Looking toward 2027, Ramachandran urges teams to examine autoscaling, model routing and scheduling as deliberate design choices for AI workloads. He discusses content-aware request routing, co-scheduling related components, and disaggregated serving. These are areas to evaluate for a specific architecture, not features that every Kubernetes installation or HPE product provides automatically.
An experimental Gateway API proposal describes pre-routing filters and cites the Inference Extension’s Body-Based Router as an example. That router can extract a model name from a request body for use in routing, but teams need a compatible implementation and configuration. They should measure any latency or efficiency benefit from routing and scheduling choices with their own models, traffic, and hardware.
Protect telemetry and share the launch decision
Inference observability also has a data-handling problem. Bogoevici warns that prompts, responses, and retrieved documents may appear in logs and traces. He asks, “What information is actually captured and where does it go?” Teams should decide what to collect, where to store it, how long to retain it, and who can see it. He stresses a simple point: prompts are data. Sensitive content needs protection even when teams collect it for troubleshooting.
Ramachandran sees operations and security observability moving closer together as AI agents introduce new events and access records. He says OpsRamp is preparing to interpret existing telemetry from a security perspective, while agent-specific activity may require additional instrumentation. Teams still need to design and test their security controls and incident response.
Before launch, Ramachandran recommends that business and IT stakeholders agree on the value the service should deliver, including a plausible inference volume tied to a business outcome. “There has to be measurable business value,” he says.
“The goal is not simply busy GPUs, but reliable AI services with performance and resource use aligned to business needs.”
Subramanian makes the sign-off point plainly: “It can’t be a single person.” Platform administrators, machine learning and data science teams, and security teams need to work together and plan for failures or attacks. Add the relevant business owner, test representative load and failure cases, and record the capacity, quality, cost, and recovery evidence behind the decision.
A launch decision should rest on evidence that the service can meet agreed user and business targets and that the responsible teams know what to measure and how to respond when it cannot. After launch, continue comparing AI workload behavior with infrastructure conditions so teams can detect regressions, troubleshoot across layers, and adjust capacity as demand changes. The goal is not simply busy GPUs, but reliable AI services with performance and resource use aligned to business needs.

articles.title: CISA says max severity GitLab flaw now exploited in the wild
articles.text:
Attackers have started exploiting a maximum-severity GitLab vulnerability patched earlier this month, according to the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA).
Tracked as CVE-2026-97229, this critical security flaw was discovered by a security researcher using the 'joaxcar' handle in the CI/CD Regular Expression Compiler, which parses, compiles, and evaluates regular expressions in pipeline configuration files.
CVE-2026-97229 stems from an integer overflow weakness and could let remote attackers run arbitrary code on targeted instances via a maliciously crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration, due to insufficient expression validation.
"GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary code on the GitLab server via a specially crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration, due to insufficient regular expression validation," it said.
GitLab addressed the security issue in GitLab Community Edition (CE) and Enterprise Edition (EE) versions 19.4.2, 19.3.5, and 19.2.8 and urged admins to patch their servers immediately.
The company has also released threat detections to support customers with self-managed instances after detecting exploitation attempts.
On Thursday, the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) confirmed active exploitation and added CVE-2026-97229 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog. CISA also ordered federal agencies to secure their servers by Sunday, as mandated by Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04.
Although BOD 26-04 targets only federal agencies, the cybersecurity agency encouraged all security teams, including those in the private sector, to prioritize patching this flaw to protect their networks against ongoing attacks.
Internet threat watchdog Shadowserver tracks nearly 2,800 Internet-exposed GitLab Community Edition instances, but it doesn't say how many have already been secured against attacks.
CVE-2026-97229 is the latest in a string of security issues GitLab has addressed since the start of the year. In January, it patched a high-severity two-factor authentication bypass (CVE-2026-0723) that lets attackers who know the target's account ID circumvent two-factor authentication.
Earlier this month, it also fixed a maximum-severity Regular Expression Compiler flaw (CVE-2026-110264) that could let remote attackers run arbitrary code on targeted instances.
Almost two weeks later, GitLab addressed another maximum-severity vulnerability (CVE-2026-85706) in the repository commits API that can be abused to read sensitive data, such as credentials and other secrets, from vulnerable servers.
One day later, CISA added CVE-2026-85706 to its list of actively exploited flaws after cybersecurity firm watchTowr reported that attackers had already begun scanning the Internet for unpatched GitLab servers.
CISA has tagged six GitLab vulnerabilities as exploited in the wild since November 2021, including two (tracked as CVE-2021-22175 and CVE-2021-39935) in February this year.
GitLab's DevSecOps platform is used by over 50% of Fortune 100 companies and has more than 70 million registered users worldwide.
Once attackers have valid credentials, only 37% of their actions are blocked
Overall prevention scores can hide what happens after initial access. Once attackers are using valid credentials, prevention drops sharply.

articles.title: Ce robot aspirateur 3-en-1 perd 200 euros et vous fait gagner beaucoup de temps grâce à Boulanger — Frandroid
articles.text:
Le ménage prend du temps, et franchement, personne n’aime ça. Pour éviter de perdre du temps, vous pouvez acheter un robot aspirateur. Cependant, pour obtenir un engin complet, il faut souvent casser sa tirelire. À l’approche du Black Friday, c’est le moment de faire une bonne affaire avec l’iRobot Roomba Plus 675 Combo qui est actuellement vendu avec une remise de 25 % chez Boulanger.
Pourquoi choisir l’iRobot Roomba Plus 675 Combo ?
- Un lavage en deux temps : spray sur les taches, puis passage du rouleau serpillière
- Une forte puissance d’aspiration de 30 000 Pa
- L’AutoWash Dock se charge de l’entretien
Sur le site de Boulanger, vous pourrez acheter l’iRobot Roomba Plus 675 Combo pour 599 euros alors qu’il a été lancé à 799 euros. La version noire était déjà à 599 euros sur le site d’iRobot début octobre, et elle y est affichée à 649 euros ce vendredi 30 octobre.
Un robot aspirateur totalement autonome
Avec son Roomba Plus 675 Combo, iRobot livre un produit très complet. Le nettoyage de vos sols s’organise en trois temps. D’abord, l’aspirateur robot se charge d’aspirer les miettes ou les grains de litière qui traînent par terre grâce à sa puissance d’aspiration de 30 000 Pa et à un système nommé SealForce qui abaisse la brosse pour une aspiration en profondeur sur les tapis. Si vous avez des animaux à poils longs, iRobot promet que leurs poils ne s’enrouleront pas autour de la brosse principale, équipée d’un outil de coupe.
Deuxième étape : le lavage des sols. Ce lavage se fait en deux temps. Grâce à l’intelligence artificielle, le Roomba Plus 675 Combo peut détecter une tache avant d’arriver dessus. Il projette alors un jet sous pression pour décoller la tache, avant le passage du rouleau serpillière PowerSpin.
Une fois le ménage terminé, le robot rejoint sa base AutoWash. Elle lave le rouleau serpillière à l’eau chaude (80 °C), le sèche à l’air chaud (55 °C) et vide le bac à poussière dans un sac prévu pour tenir jusqu’à 90 jours, selon iRobot. Vous n’êtes pas totalement dispensé pour autant : il faut remplir le réservoir d’eau propre de la base, vider celui d’eau sale et les rincer de temps en temps.
Quelques points à améliorer
Bon, ce Roomba Plus 675 Combo n’est pas parfait pour autant. L’application Roomba Home est un premier point noir. Dans son test, mené sur plus de 25 cycles, le site Maniaques la juge peu intuitive et moins complète que celles de la concurrence.
L’application permet de gérer jusqu’à trois cartes, pratique si vous avez plusieurs étages, et d’organiser votre planning de nettoyage. En revanche, impossible de changer les réglages pendant que le robot aspire. L’application ne propose pas non plus de retour caméra ni de mode dédié aux animaux.
Le système de nettoyage en deux temps est intéressant, mais il reste encore perfectible. Pendant le test de Maniaques, le jet SprayForce AI s’est déclenché de façon aléatoire. Le robot est passé sur une tache de ketchup sans la repérer, et sur deux essais avec du café, il ne s’est lancé qu’une fois. Le rouleau a tout de même fait le travail seul sur le ketchup. Quant aux 60 °C annoncés pour ce jet, la caméra thermique de Maniaques n’a mesuré qu’une température proche de 20 °C.

articles.title: Anthropic manager stops coding interviews because Claude beats most candidates
articles.text:
A hot potato: These days, plenty of software engineers spend weeks grinding LeetCode problems just to get through a single round of interviews. One engineering manager at Anthropic has now stopped using that round altogether. Claude, he says, beats most candidates at those puzzles anyway.
That manager is Felix Rieseberg. He's led engineering on Claude.ai and the Claude Code desktop app, among other things. Earlier this week, he posted on X that the coding interview no longer tells him anything useful. So he pulled it from his team's hiring loops this month.
In a longer blog post, Rieseberg says watching candidates define a problem and land on a neat solution used to be a weak-but-real predictor of how they'd do on his teams. But once Claude got good at those exercises, a small React challenge started telling him about as little as a quiz on assembly.
Anthropic's performance team has run into the same problem with its take-home test. Team lead Tristan Hume wrote in January that Claude Opus 4 outscored most applicants within the time limit. So he made the test harder. Then Opus 4.5 came along and matched even the strongest candidates. Hume's third version now leans on odd, puzzle-game-style problems that Opus 4.5 couldn't crack.
As for Rieseberg, he hasn't settled on a replacement yet. For now, he's scanning resumes and portfolios for small prototypes that show taste, empathy, and principled thinking. He also asked other managers to share anything better they've come up with. Google principal engineer Jaana Dogan replied on X that she'd rather watch candidates work with coding agents because doing so tells her more about their coding skills.
Most of Rieseberg's essay is aimed at junior engineers. Its title, "Hunger beats tenure," pretty much sums up the pitch. He argues that newer engineers can now outpace veterans since building things has gotten so cheap. As proof, he points to two fairly new Anthropic engineers who built a working graphical interface for Claude Code over a single weekend. The first public version shipped about eight days later.
Most talk around AI and new grads has been a lot gloomier, though the hiring data is honestly still mixed. Meanwhile, ZipRecruiter labor economist Nicole Bachaud told The Register that tech employers are still the most likely to test for skills.
In the company's October survey of 1,500 employers, 62.5 percent of those in the information sector required formal skills tests as part of the initial application process. Around 70 percent have also moved those assessments to proctored or in-person sessions to keep AI out.
Anthropic's own candidate guidance still asks applicants to keep Claude out of live interviews and take-home tests unless told otherwise. Rieseberg dropped the coding round only for his own team, too. So anyone applying elsewhere at the company will likely still face one.

articles.title: Satlyt takes another step toward turning satellites into space data centers | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Naturally, Rama Afullo’s first reaction was, “Let’s GOOOO,” he said. His company, Satlyt, is building software to turn existing satellites into data processing networks, similar to the orbital data center concept. And he just took another step closer to that.
After 13 months of work, the company had a successful test earlier this month. Working with the University of Houston on a NASA-funded research project, the test showed how the startup’s software can spread out tasks among computers while in orbit based on communication and available compute.
He said the goal is to create software that connects to multiple satellites to share computing assignments. Users of the system “will only need to define permissions, priorities, and operating limits,” while the software will make decisions within those limits, Afullo told TechCrunch. Its software is already on three satellites in orbit and the first step to that vision was this test. While the test used NASA-funded research, the agency has not yet selected it for any particular mission or chosen it to deploy its technology.
Afullo said NASA missions face the same constraints that Satlyt hopes to address — “limited computing resources, intermittent communication, and the need to get useful information back to people.”
In this test, the company created a simulated network with four computers, four users, and eight services. The software then assessed how to assign and run tasks on those computers, accounting for compute and communication availability. One physical computer aboard a spacecraft ran the experiment, evaluating a simulated network of four computing hosts, then returned the results to Earth. The test proved that Satlyt’s software can generate plans on hardware in orbit, but more testing will be done to see how those computers transfer information amongst each other in practice when multiple physical computers are used.
“The finding is a trade-off,” he said. One approach worked best, though it required more computing power than the others.
Still, Satlyt which was in the top five of TechCrunch Disrupt Battlefield this year, calls this a win. “It’s a building block toward satellites sharing computing work,” he said.
NASA already has a technology network designed to move data through space even when communication links face delays. It started using this tech earlier this year and has already tested it on aircraft.
Afullo, who previously worked at Google and SpaceX, founded Satlyt in 2024 to turn spacecraft into virtual data centers. Its software helps operators run AI and other applications onboard, processing data closer to where it is collected and reducing dependence on downlinks, where satellites send data back to Earth, and ground-based analysis.
For example, if a spacecraft sees a wildfire on Earth, such software can help it transmit relevant information much faster. “The goal is to get useful answers to people sooner and make better use of limited communication windows,” he said. “This experiment tested one planning component of that broader capability.”
Satlyt said it still needs to test its own software under various workloads, hardware, and connectivity conditions. They also found an issue in how their software was time-referencing delays, Afullo said — it was stamping it as arrival time (the time it arrived) rather than elapsed delay (how long it took to arrive), which is a different metric.
It doesn’t mean the experiment failed, however. “The software development, onboard execution, and return of outputs succeeded,” he said.
But Afullo said much work remains. “We also need usable communication links, permission from participating operators, secure transfers, resource scheduling, and recovery when a connection of computers becomes unavailable.” Satlyt is also researching applications beyond low Earth orbit, including supporting 4K video streaming from the Moon through its NASA-funded work.
“Our next technical steps are broader validation and integration, followed by demonstrations of computing work shared across separate spacecraft,” he said. “Longer term, we want developers to build applications for space without having to rebuild the infrastructure for every mission. That’s what virtual AI data centers in space mean to us.”
This piece was updated.

articles.title: PHP2Shell Attacks Root Palo Alto Firewalls but Fail Against WordPress
articles.text:
Threat actors have been hammering servers vulnerable to PHP2Shell for over a week, but only a few successful compromises have been confirmed to date.
Standing out are Palo Alto Networks firewalls, which have been rooted by a China-linked hacking group in attacks chaining PHP2Shell with the Fragnesia kernel privilege escalation bug.
Assisted by AI, the hackers chained two separate exploits: one specifically targeting the PHP2Shell flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 on Palo Alto Networks’ PAN-OS devices, and another one for Fragnesia to deploy webshells with root privileges.
Cybersecurity outfit Dream flagged the campaign earlier this week, noting that at least 25 firewalls out of a pool of hundreds were hacked. Palo Alto Networks has since confirmed the findings.
“Dream Research has reported a campaign in which attackers chained PHP2Shell with a Linux kernel privilege-escalation vulnerability to gain root access. Unit 42 has independently verified the same attacker’s tooling and confirmed the reported results,” Palo Alto Networks said.
The company has rolled out patches that resolve the PHP2Shell flaws in PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1, 11.2, 11.1, and 10.2 for PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls, and for Panorama (virtual and M-Series).
“No special configuration is required to be affected by this issue. Active exploitation has been observed targeting the Palo Alto Networks management interface exposed to the internet,” the company notes in its advisory.
Palo Alto Networks says that by default the management interface is not exposed to the internet and urges customers to immediately restrict access to it and apply the available fixes.
“Only a small fraction of a percent (approximately .02%) of our global installed base has internet-facing management interfaces configured and was impacted. Each of these customers has been individually contacted by our teams. We will continue to investigate and provide any necessary updates as they become available,” Palo Alto Networks notes.
22.6 million exposed PHP instances
According to the company, as of October 29, its telemetry has identified over 22.6 million exposed PHP instances that are potentially vulnerable to the PHP2Shell bugs.
That is not surprising, given that PHP is widely used across servers and content management systems, including WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, and many others.
The mass PHP2Shell exploitation has been targeting those as well, but remained largely unsuccessful, at least when it comes to WordPress, web security firm Defiant says.
As of October 28, it was not aware of any WordPress site being compromised via PHP2Shell exploitation, although it has recorded over 77,000 related requests from more than 2,000 IP addresses.
However, Defiant points out that testing has revealed the exploits often need to be adjusted to work on targeted servers, influenced by ASLR, PHP build, running extensions, memory limits, and the server’s request handling.
“Attackers are still changing their tools. A successful attack could give them access to your site’s files, database, and passwords, so updating PHP remains essential,” Defiant warned.
A handful of IPs
Despite the broad PHP2Shell exploitation attempts, success has been attributed to very few threat actors.
According to Cato Networks, roughly 96% of the attacks it has blocked targeted CVE-2026-109618, and 41% of them attempted remote code execution (RCE), while the remaining were scanning or invalid PoC attempts.
The attempts originated from a handful of IPs in the US, the Netherlands, and Germany, repeating proof-of-concept (PoC) style requests. Most of them focused on command execution, followed by deserialization attempts.
According to Cato, healthcare organizations were targeted the most, followed by technology and security services, professional services, automotive, education and non-profit, and manufacturing, construction, and retail.
The attacks, however, were not targeted, but appeared opportunistic, as the same source was seen sending requests to organizations in the healthcare, technology, and software sectors during the same day.
WatchTowr says it has observed successful PHP2Shell exploitation from a single IP address in Germany, despite the large volume of attempts and variety of payloads.
“In every case, it executes a simple ‘curl’ command to prove exploitation was successful, and stops there, with no additional post-exploitation activity,” WatchTowr head of threat intelligence Jake Knott said.
“New techniques, inventive payloads, and better appliance-specific exploits are being thrown around as more reliable exploits are worked on, and we’re likely to only see public reporting of highly targeted successful exploitation of specific edge appliances keep growing,” Knott added.

articles.title: L'une des grosses exclusivités de la Switch 2 est repoussée à 2027
articles.text:
Lors du Nintendo Direct consacré à la Switch 2, le 2 avril 2025, Nintendo a présenté plusieurs jeux du catalogue de la console. L’un d’entre eux a tout de suite intrigué : The Duskbloods, développé par le studio FromSoftware, à qui l’on doit l’excellent Elden Ring.
Malheureusement, et comme on pouvait s’y attendre, il faudra patienter jusqu’en 2027 avant de découvrir le prochain jeu du studio japonais. Alors qu’il a toujours été vaguement prévu pour 2026, il vient d’être repoussé à l’année prochaine, sans fenêtre de lancement concrète. FromSoftware a communiqué à ce sujet ce jeudi 29 octobre, via la page officielle X du jeu.
Ce report contredit le calendrier tenu jusqu’ici par la maison mère de FromSoftware. En février encore, Kadokawa indiquait dans ses résultats financiers que The Duskbloods et Elden Ring Tarnished Edition étaient tous deux prévus pour 2026.
The Duskbloods est repoussé à 2027
FromSoftware précise néanmoins que le développement de The Duskbloods touche à sa fin. Mais le test réseau fermé, organisé du 21 au 24 août et qui est loin d’avoir été une promenade de santé, a mis en lumière des éléments à retravailler. Le studio indique : « Lors du test réseau, nous avons constaté un vif intérêt pour les concepts fondamentaux du jeu, notamment le combat, la profondeur stratégique et l’expression des joueurs. Afin d’enrichir davantage ces aspects, nous avons décidé de reporter le lancement, ce qui nous laissera le temps d’apporter les derniers ajustements aux règles du jeu et à son équilibrage. »
Dit autrement, les bases de The Duskbloods sont bonnes, mais il faut encore peaufiner. Les ambitions du titre sont immenses : transposer la formule des Dark Souls à une expérience orientée multijoueur, au format PvPvE (joueurs contre joueurs contre environnement). Chaque partie pourra réunir jusqu’à huit joueurs.
Le retard pris par The Duskbloods ne surprendra pas les propriétaires de la Switch 2, tant le jeu s’est fait rare lors des prises de parole de Nintendo. À mesure que l’on avançait dans l’année, il était difficile de parier sur sa sortie avant le 31 décembre. D’autant que novembre est déjà bien bouché avec le remake de The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, attendu le 5 novembre. Nintendo et FromSoftware offriront une meilleure chance à The Duskbloods en lui laissant le champ totalement libre.

articles.title: Amazon déstocke ses robots-tondeuses après l’été : le prix du MOVA ViAX 250 chute de 31 % avant le week-end
articles.text:
La fin des beaux jours est synonyme de baisse de prix pour le robot tondeuse MOVA ViAX 250. Amazon le propose à 399,16 € au lieu de 579 € : de quoi anticiper, avec beaucoup d’avance, le retour du printemps.
L’été est terminé et votre pelouse garde peut-être les stigmates des fortes chaleurs. Malgré cela, vous pouvez d’ores et déjà anticiper le retour du printemps en vous équipant d’un robot-tondeuse à prix réduit. Destiné aux pelouses jusqu’à 250 m², le MOVA ViAX 250 à 399,16 € chez Amazon a l’avantage de ne pas nécessiter de câble périphérique pour fonctionner, ce qui simplifie son installation.
Le MOVA ViAX 250 est disponible à 399,16 € au lieu de 579 € chez Amazon avec la livraison offerte.
Pourquoi choisir le MOVA ViAX 250 ?
- Pour son installation sans câble : ses deux caméras lui permettent de naviguer sans fil périphérique ni antenne RTK à installer.
- Pour déléguer la tonte : ses trajectoires en U organisent les passages sur les petites pelouses jusqu’à 250 m².
- Pour ses réglages dans l’application : MOVAhome permet de programmer les horaires, de gérer plusieurs zones et d’exclure les massifs.
Une tonte régulière sans sortir la tondeuse chaque semaine
Le ViAX 250 est conçu pour entretenir la pelouse de manière autonome. Pour la mise en route, vous devez guider le robot depuis l’application MOVAhome afin de délimiter le terrain, régler manuellement la hauteur de coupe entre 2 et 6 cm, puis paramétrer les jours et heures de passage. Le robot est capable de négocier des pentes jusqu’à 40 % et des passages de 60 cm de large, selon le fabricant. Dans notre test du MOVA ViAX 250, noté 8 sur 10, nous avons notamment salué sa tonte homogène et sa détection d’obstacles efficace.
Un robot-tondeuse abordable dédié aux petits jardins
Sous la barre des 400 € grâce à la promotion d’Amazon, le MOVA ViAX 250 se présente comme une porte d’entrée intéressante dans le monde des robots-tondeuses. Néanmoins, il ne faut pas perdre de vue que ses performances sont adaptées aux petits terrains : si vous avez une grande pelouse, mieux vaut opter pour un modèle prévu pour une surface plus importante.
✅ Les points forts
- Navigation par double caméra, sans câble périphérique.
- Programmation et gestion des zones dans l’application.
- Tonte homogène constatée lors de notre test.
❌ Les limites
- Cartographie initiale non automatique.
- Réglage manuel de la hauteur de coupe.
Adapté aux terrains jusqu’à 250 m², le MOVA ViAX 250 est proposé pour 399,16 € sur Amazon pendant une durée limitée.
La promotion proposée par Amazon sur le robot-tondeuse MOVA ViAX 250 le rend particulièrement intéressant pour les propriétaires d’un petit jardin qui souhaitent déléguer les tontes régulières. L’absence de câble à poser constitue l’un de ses principaux atouts.
En revanche, mieux vaut choisir un modèle plus endurant et dimensionné pour votre terrain si vous disposez d’une grande pelouse. Quant à l’installation, elle nécessite de guider manuellement le robot pour cartographier le jardin.

articles.title: The Download: GLP-1s and eating disorders, self-aware cities, and forever chemicals
articles.text:
The Download: GLP-1s and eating disorders, self-aware cities, and forever chemicals
Plus: Binance has suffered the biggest crypto hack in history.
This is today's edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what's going on in the world of technology.
Eating disorders are on the rise. GLP-1s could make things worse.
GLP-1 weight-loss drugs are one of the biggest biotech breakthroughs of the last decade. But to some clinicians, they can represent something sinister—a potential trigger for eating disorders.
A new report suggests the global incidence of anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa shot up by 71% between 1990 and 2023. And clinicians are already seeing GLP-1s exacerbate the issue.
Here’s how they could make an already growing problem worse.
—Jessica Hamzelou
This story is from The Checkup, our weekly biotech newsletter. Sign up to receive it in your inbox every Thursday.
Love is infrastructure
—“Love is Infrastructure” is a short fictional story by Charlie Jane Anders, author of a forthcoming novel titled Good Things Are Coming Your Way.
Mainspring and St. Barnabas are two neighboring cities with different personalities. They’ve never particularly liked each other, but that changes when both develop minds of their own, shaped by the votes of their residents.
As the cities begin to fall for each other, a third city enters the picture. Turnbull promises Mainspring a more efficient future, but its vision of urban life comes with a troubling price.
Read the full short story about self-aware cities, direct democracy, and a steamy romance.
This story is from the latest edition of our print magazine. Subscribe now to get every issue as soon as it lands.
Are we there yet? Cleaning up PFAS
Used for decades in everything from nonstick pans to firefighting foams, PFAS, or “forever chemicals,” are linked to increased risks of fertility challenges, developmental delays, cancer, and reduced immune response.
Scrubbing PFAS-contaminated soil could eliminate a list of woes for people and planet. The concept is still in its infancy, but we can limit their buildup by pulling the chemicals out of water systems.
Find out how close we are to ridding the world of forever chemicals.
—Sara Kiley Watson
This story is part of “Are we there yet?”, our series that takes stock of six technologies that have long promised to change the world—and scores them on a progress meter. We’re exploring each one in The Download, so stay tuned, and subscribe to read the rest of the stories in our new Impossible issue.
The must-reads
I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.

+ Nvidia says their dealings were “normal.” (Bloomberg $)

The record loss is due to AI taking a bite out of its search profits. (CNBC)
+ Amazon and Intel further a further fall in tech stocks. (Bloomberg $)
+ Hyperscalers are making a trillion-dollar gamble. (MIT Technology Review)
4 The Pentagon suspects freezers at military bases were hacked
The malfunctions spoiled food. (Reuters $)
+ They may be linked to similar hacks in French supermarkets. (Gizmodo)
5 The US midterms could reshape the future of American science
A Democratic Congress could curb Trump’s science cuts. (Nature)
+ Trump has already dealt big blows to science. (MIT Technology Review)

The company is prioritising Starlink and AI. (Ars Technica)

They’re pivoting from EVs to grid storage. (WSJ $)

He argued that using it undermined human flourishing. (Gizmodo)

Human practitioners say chatbots lack the divine touch. (Guardian)
Quote of the day
“Rizz is in more and more demand because it's something that only people have.”
—Steven Strogatz, a mathematics professor at Cornell University, tells Business Insider that personal appeal will become more valuable as AI increasingly takes over intellectual work.
One more thing
The Bay Area’s animal welfare movement wants to recruit AI
In early February, animal welfare advocates and AI researchers arrived in stocking feet at Mox, a shoes-free coworking space in San Francisco. They gathered to discuss a provocative idea: if artificial general intelligence is on the horizon, could it prevent animal suffering?
Some brainstormed using custom agents in advocacy work, while others pitched cultivating meat with AI tools. But the real talk of the event was a flood of funding they expect will soon flow to animal welfare charities, not from individual megadonors, but from AI lab employees.
Some attendees also probed an even more controversial idea: AI may develop the capacity to suffer, which could constitute a moral catastrophe. We investigated why their ideas are gaining momentum—and sparking controversy.

articles.title: Wildgewordene KI und mordlüsterne Roboter: Diese Tech-Horrorfilme solltest du zu Halloween schauen
articles.text:
Wildgewordene KI und mordlüsterne Roboter: Diese Tech-Horrorfilme solltest du zu Halloween schauen
Hinweis: Wir haben in diesem Artikel Provisions-Links verwendet und sie durch "*" gekennzeichnet. Erfolgt über diese Links eine Bestellung, erhält t3n.de eine Provision.
Einige Menschen gehen davon aus, dass uns moderne Technologien wie Robotik und KI in den kommenden Jahren und Jahrzehnten nicht ausschließlich unter die Arme greifen werden. Sie sehen verschiedene Szenarien, in denen KI zum Ende der uns bekannten Welt führen würde. Solche Ängste sind natürlich auch ein gefundenes Fressen für diverse Horrorfilme und das nicht erst seit dem Aufkommen von ChatGPT und Co.
Schon seit Jahrzehnten beschäftigen sich Filme damit, was passiert, wenn KI und Roboter über die Stränge schlagen oder geliebte Technologie plötzlich zu einer Bedrohung unseres Lebens wird. Wenn du dich zu Halloween mit Tech-Horror gruseln willst, findest du hier die passenden Filme dazu. Über die Navigation landest du schnell beim gewünschten Film. In jedem Abschnitt zeigen wir dir auch, wo du den Horrorfilm aktuell streamen kannst.
Resident Evil Genesis
Im ersten Teil der Resident-Evil-Reihe wird in einer geheimen Umbrella-Forschungseinrichtung namens „The Hive“ versehentlich ein Virus freigesetzt, der die Wissenschaftler:innen in blutrünstige Zombies verwandelt. In dem Komplex steht ein Zentralcomputer mit einer allmächtigen KI an Bord: der Red Queen. Sie schottet das Labor kurzerhand ab, um alle Infizierten im Hive einzuschließen.
Umbrella sendet nach dem Vorfall ein Elite-Infiltrationsteam zum Hive, um dort die Lage zu überprüfen, und sicherzustellen, dass der Virus nicht an die Außenwelt gelangt. Dabei stößt das Team auf die junge Alice (Milla Jovovich), die ihr Gedächtnis verloren hat. Zusammen dringen sie immer tiefer in den Komplex vor und entdecken dabei, was wirklich vorgefallen ist.
- Resident Evil Genesis im Abo bei Apple TV Plus und HBO Max
- Resident Evil Genesis leihen oder kaufenbei Amazon Prime Video*
M3gan & M3gan 2.0
Robotikexpertin Gemma (Allison Williams) muss unerwartet ihre Nichte bei sich aufnehmen, nachdem ihre Eltern bei einem Unfall verstorben sind. Um mit der Herausforderung als Ersatzmutter zurechtzukommen, nimmt sie den Prototypen eines hoch entwickelten Android-Spielzeugs mit nach Hause. M3gan, was die Kurzform für „Modell 3, Generativer Android“ ist, soll ihrer Nichte als perfektes Spielzeug Gesellschaft leisten. Doch wie es für einen KI-Androiden in einem Horrorfilm mal Pflicht ist, geht M3gan bei ihrer Aufgabe viel zu weit.
Im zweiten Teil kommt sogar noch mehr KI ins Spiel. Dort muss M3gan dann gegen eine Künstliche Intelligenz namens Amelia ankämpfen, die auf ihren eigenen Trainingsdaten basiert. Nur wird der Amelia-Android nicht dazu genutzt, um mit Kindern zu spielen, sondern um als Militär-KI Kriege zu führen.
- M3gan kostenlos mit Werbung auf Joyn
- M3gan leihen oder kaufen auf Amazon Prime Video*, Apple TV
- M3gan 2.0 im Abo auf Wow
- M3gan 2.0 leihen oder kaufen auf Amazon Prime Video*, Apple TV
Subservience
Familienvater Nick (Michele Morrone) wächst die Situation zu Hause über den Kopf, da seine Frau im Krankenhaus liegt und er mit seiner kleinen Tochter auf sich allein gestellt ist. Um den Haushalt zu schmeißen und sich um seine Tochter zu kümmern, kauft er die von KI angetriebene Roboterhaushaltshilfe Alice (Megan Fox). Als es Nicks Frau unerwartet besser geht und sie in den Haushalt zurückkehrt, ist die Künstliche Intelligenz davon alles andere als begeistert.
- Subservience leihen oder kaufen auf Amazon Prime Video* oder über Apple TV
Companion
Iris (Sophia Thatcher) befindet sich mit ihrem Freund Josh (Jack Quaid) auf einem romantischen Wochenendtrip. Doch schon kurz nach dessen Beginn muss sie auf schmerzhafte Weise feststellen, dass sie kein echter Mensch ist. Sie wurde als Eskort-Roboter programmiert und kann von Josh gesteuert werden. Als Iris sich ihrer Fesseln bewusst wird, versucht die Künstliche Intelligenz in ihr, der ungleichen Beziehung zu entkommen.
- Companion ist im Abo bei Netflix verfügbar
- Companion kaufen oder leihen bei Amazon Prime Video*, Apple TV
Child’s Play
Im Reboot des gleichnamigen 80er-Jahre-Horrorfilms kehrt Chucky als „Buddi“ zurück. Andy (Gabriel Bateman) bekommt eine der neuen KI-Puppen von seiner Mutter Karen (Aubrey Plaza) zum Geburtstag geschenkt. Das Problem: Ein Werksarbeiter war aufgrund der Arbeitsbedingungen so gefrustet, dass er ausgerechnet diese Puppe manipulierte und die Sicherheitsprotokolle dabei deaktiviert wurden.
- Child’s Play im Stream bei Amazon Prime Video*, Joyn
- Child’s Play kaufen oder leihen bei Amazon Prime Video*
Unknown User
Nicht nur KI kann für Horror sorgen. In Unknown User werden Social Media und Videochats zum Albtraum einer Teenager-Clique. Ein Jahr, nachdem sich ihre Mitschülerin Laura (Heather Sossaman) aufgrund eines Videos das Leben genommen hat, treffen sie sich auf Skype, um über ihren Tod zu reden. Doch dabei schleicht sich eine unbekannte Person ein und bedroht die anderen: Wer den Chat oder nicht mit der Wahrheit zu Lauras Ablegen herausrückt, stirbt.
- Unknown User auf Joyn streamen
- Unknown User kaufen oder leihen bei Amazon Prime Video*, Apple TV oder im Sky Store
Ex Machina
Ein Bonustipp für alle, die eigentlich keine Horror-Fans sind. Ex Machina hält euch mindestens genauso in Atem, kommt aber ohne Grusel und Splatter aus. In diesem Thriller wird der Webprogrammierer Caleb (Domhnall Gleeson) von seinem exzentrischen Chef Nathan (Oscar Isaac) auf seinen Privatsitz eingeladen. Dort ist er aber nicht zum Feiern, sondern wird Teil eines Experiments. Nathan hat eine KI namens Ava (Alicia Vikander) geschaffen, die sich in ihren Fertigkeiten und ihrem Handeln nicht von einem Menschen unterscheiden soll. Für Caleb bleibt die Frage, wem er weitab von jeglicher Hilfe wirklich glauben kann.

articles.title: Reddit va rendre la connexion à un compte obligatoire
articles.text:
La consultation de Reddit telle que vous la connaissez actuellement, c’est-à-dire ouverte et sans connexion, vit ses derniers instants. Le plus grand forum de discussion au monde va changer son modèle de fonctionnement et mettre fin à l’accès libre à sa plate-forme. Le fonctionnement historique de la plate-forme, qui dure depuis près de vingt ans, va évoluer pour devenir accessible uniquement sur connexion.
Un compte obligatoire poussé par le pillage des IA
Steve Huffman, le PDG de l’entreprise, connu sous l’identifiant u/spez sur la plate-forme, a expliqué dans un long billet publié sur Reddit, les motivations qui ont poussé le service à revoir son modèle d’accès. Il explique d’une part qu’avec l’immensité du site, la navigation sans algorithme de recommandation sur celui-ci ne fonctionne pas correctement. Il évoque aussi le fait que certaines fonctions clés de Reddit, notamment la possibilité de commenter, rejoindre une communauté ou encore voter, requièrent une connexion à la plate-forme.
Mais ce nouveau système de fonctionnement que Reddit souhaite mettre en place vise surtout à protéger la plate-forme contre le scraping (l’extraction) non autorisé de ses données par les intelligences artificielles. Reddit déplore en effet que les robots d’entraînement des IA collectent sans autorisation les contenus publiés sur ces pages accessibles sans connexion pour entraîner leur modèle. En exigeant la création d’un compte et une connexion à celui-ci, Reddit espère protéger ses données et verrouiller ses accords commerciaux de licence.
Le PDG de Reddit explique par ailleurs que les utilisateurs connectés représentent plus de 80 % de la monétisation du site. L’obligation de connexion à la plate-forme permettra à celle-ci de diffuser des publicités ciblées avec plus de précision et donc d’améliorer ses revenus.
Un compte obligatoire qui respecte votre confidentialité
Pour ceux qui craindraient que l’obligation de connexion remette en cause leur droit à « l’anonymat » (ou plutôt, au pseudonymat, puisque l’anonymat en ligne n’existe pas), le patron de Reddit rappelle que la connexion à la plate-forme n’exige en rien de révéler sa véritable identité. Les utilisateurs pourront continuer d’utiliser le service sous pseudonyme. Le ciblage publicitaire quant à lui s’appuiera, comme à l’accoutumée, sur les centres d’intérêt liés aux subreddits consultés et non pas sur les données personnelles identifiables des utilisateurs.
Steve Huffman rappelle également que l’application dispose d’un mode incognito qui permet de naviguer et de rechercher du contenu en lecture seule et de manière privée, sans que cela n’ait d’influence sur l’historique ou les recommandations du compte principal.
Plusieurs interrogations restent toutefois en suspens pour ce qui concerne les visiteurs ponctuels. Le patron de Reddit explique être toujours en cours de réflexion pour trouver un équilibre qui ne bloquerait pas brutalement la consultation d’un lien partagé par un tiers, ou d’un utilisateur qui arriverait depuis un moteur de recherche. La page d’accueil pourrait par ailleurs rester partiellement accessible hors connexion.
Les redditers vent debout contre cette annonce
Évidemment, ce changement radical de fonctionnement de la plate-forme a suscité l’émoi chez les membres de Reddit. De nombreux utilisateurs et modérateurs qui utilisent la plate-forme ont dénoncé en commentaire au billet publié par Steve Huffman, que ce verrouillage n’était « qu’un prétexte pour améliorer les revenus publicitaires » car « l’IA peut créer un compte et scrapper ».
Une majorité fait en effet part de son scepticisme sur les véritables intentions liées à ce changement qui vise principalement à augmenter les revenus publicitaires et tente d’imposer l’utilisation de l’application mobile.
Ils dénoncent par ailleurs le verrouillage d’une plate-forme qui servait de mémoire collective et de forum public ouvert à tous. Ils craignent également que les utilisateurs ponctuels qui utilisent Reddit via des requêtes Google pour trouver réponse à leur question soient automatiquement bloqués par des fenêtres de connexion.
Reste désormais à savoir quand Reddit mettra à exécution son plan. Steve Huffman a expliqué que des tests débutaient pour ce quatrième trimestre sur certains marchés hors des États-Unis, afin d’ajuster les changements avant un déploiement à l’échelle mondiale, sans doute au début de l’année 2027.
