articles.title: Eating disorders are on the rise. GLP-1s could make things worse.
articles.text:
Eating disorders are on the rise. GLP-1s could make things worse.
Emerging evidence suggests some people with eating disorders are misusing weight-loss drugs.
GLP-1 weight-loss drugs are one of the biggest biotech breakthroughs of the last decade. But to some clinical psychologists, they can represent something more sinister—a potential trigger for eating disorders.
A new report suggests that the global incidence of anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa shot up between 1990 and 2023—by a whopping 71%. By 2023, there were an estimated 18.1 million people living with one of these two disorders.
What’s worse is that the number is likely to be much higher than that once we factor in other eating disorders. And, disturbingly, those in the field are already starting to see GLP-1 weight-loss drugs exacerbating the issue.
Cheri Levinson is a clinical psychologist at the University of Louisville in Kentucky who has specialized in eating disorders for almost 20 years. She says she’s now seeing more patients with more severe symptoms than at any other time in her career, and that many of them are misusing GLP-1s. “This is the worst I’ve seen things,” she says.
Eating disorders are mental health conditions in which people’s eating behaviors impact their health. They include anorexia nervosa (defined by a fear of weight gain), bulimia nervosa (in which people binge and purge), binge eating disorder, and others.
It’s thought that some people have a genetic predisposition to certain eating disorders, but that some external factor is what triggers their onset. That might be stress, or social pressure to be skinny. Often, simply restricting food intake can trigger an eating disorder, says Levinson.
Eating disorders—along with the pressure to look thin—were already prevalent in the 1990s (the heroin chic era springs to mind). To find out how things might have changed since then, Ruhai Bai at the Children’s Hospital of Nanjing Medical University in China and his colleagues pulled together data from studies and surveys conducted on populations around the world. The team used statistical models to fill in any data gaps.
That research allowed the researchers to estimate the annual incidence of two eating disorders—anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa—for each of 204 countries and territories between 1990 and 2023. They also estimated the impact those disorders had on global health by calculating their disability-adjusted life years (one DALY represents a year of healthy life lost).
The findings, published in JAMA Psychiatry on Wednesday, are unsettling. Between 1990 and 2023, there was a 71% increase in the incidence of those two eating disorders, the team found. Those conditions had a huge impact on global health, too. In 2023, they “cost the world the equivalent of about 3.83 million years of healthy life,” says Bai.
Bai and his colleagues expect these figures to continue to rise. In 2023, an estimated 18.1 million people had either anorexia nervosa or bulimia nervosa; by 2050, the team predict, the two conditions could affect 21.8 million people.
It gets worse. Those two conditions represent less than half of all eating disorders, says Levinson, who was not involved in Bai’s study. The true impact of these disorders is “probably three times the rate that they’re reporting,” she says.
Bai and his colleagues didn’t explore the reasons for this rise (although Bai points out that it can’t be entirely explained by population growth). So how did we get here?
Social media may have played a role. “Social media comparisons, influencers, challenges, diet trends can all be precipitating … events for an eating disorder,” says Cynthia Bulik, a clinical psychologist at the University of North Carolina, who was not involved in the new study. Bulik has been studying and treating eating disorders since the early 1980s. “Between 1990 and 2023 there has clearly been an upsurge of those types of environmental exposures,” she says.
Many social media users are exposed to filtered and modified images of skinny influencers who may have undergone cosmetic surgery or extreme dieting and who are promoting “thinspiration” or “fitspiration” content. But users with eating disorders appear to be more likely to engage with this content—and to be fed more of it as a result.
When researchers at the University of Melbourne investigated this phenomenon a couple of years ago, they found that the algorithms of TikTok users with eating disorders delivered 4343% more “toxic eating disorder videos” than those of users who didn’t have the disorders. They also got more content focused on dieting or exercising. Many were fed over 1000 problematic videos per month. Bulik describes social media as “quicksand” for people with, or at risk of, eating disorders.
The covid-19 pandemic—and the social isolation that accompanied lockdowns—also appears to have contributed to the rise in eating disorders. Research conducted in 2021 found that the number of people hospitalized with eating disorders in the US doubled between 2018 and 2020.
Researchers don’t yet have good data on how trends in eating disorders might have progressed since 2023. But anecdotally, things seem to be getting even worse. “There are more eating disorders, more severe eating disorders… and we’re seeing earlier ages of onset,” says Levinson. “We’re seeing eight- and nine-year-olds with eating disorders.”
“From what I’m hearing and seeing, I am not going to be surprised if that number isn’t at least doubling again,” she adds.
Levinson particularly worries about the impact of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs, which have exploded in popularity in recent years. A Gallup survey conducted earlier this year suggested that 15% of Americans had used one of these drugs for weight loss. And they’re becoming more accessible—drug companies are working on new formulations that are both easier to take and more effective, and many people can buy versions of these drugs from compound pharmacies or dubious online sources.
In a small study published earlier this year, Levinson and her colleagues found that 30% of people with eating disorders had used GLP-1 drugs. The drugs might benefit some of those people. But 10% appeared to have misused the drugs. And Levinson thinks that figure is also an underestimate.
Levinson says she and her colleagues have seen children develop eating disorders after being prescribed GLP-1s for medical reasons. They’ve seen others—even children as young as 11—buy versions of these drugs over TikTok.
“We’re very concerned that GLPs will lead to even faster and more extreme weight loss in people with anorexia nervosa, and that patients will come to us in even more advanced stages of illness that become difficult to reverse,” says Bulik.
Both Bulik and Levinson are continuing to study the impacts of these drugs in eating disorders. In the meantime, both urge medical professionals to consider the risks GLP-1s might pose to people with those disorders. Bulik contributed to a set of research and clinical guidelines, published earlier this month, that recommends doctors screen for eating disorders before prescribing the drugs, for example. The guidelines also recommend more patient education and more robust monitoring of people who take GLP-1s.
If you think you or someone you know might have an eating disorder, you can find information and support at the National Eating Disorders Association.

articles.title: Gastos com IA acendem alerta financeiro para Meta e Anthropic
articles.text:
A corrida para ampliar a infraestrutura de inteligência artificial (IA) começa a pesar na avaliação de risco de algumas das empresas mais importantes do setor. A Meta teve sua perspectiva de crédito rebaixada pela S&P Global Ratings, enquanto a Anthropic pode receber uma classificação considerada especulativa após uma eventual abertura de capital.
Os dois casos têm ponto em comum: a preocupação com a capacidade das empresas de transformar os investimentos bilionários em IA em receitas suficientes para compensar os custos crescentes.
No caso da Meta, a S&P manteve a classificação de crédito em AA-, mas mudou a perspectiva de estável para negativa. A agência citou incertezas sobre o elevado volume de investimentos em infraestrutura e o fluxo de caixa livre negativo da companhia.
Já a Anthropic pode receber uma nota na faixa BB, segundo previsão atribuída à Blackstone em reportagem do Financial Times. A classificação ficaria abaixo do nível considerado grau de investimento, colocando a empresa na categoria de crédito especulativo, conhecida no mercado como junk.
Meta recebe perspectiva negativa da S&P
- A mudança na avaliação da Meta está relacionada principalmente ao aumento dos investimentos em IA e à dificuldade de prever quando eles começarão a gerar retornos expressivos;
- A S&P questionou a capacidade da companhia de monetizar suas tecnologias de IA em comparação com concorrentes que também estão gastando pesado na construção de data centers. Segundo a agência, ainda não está claro quando produtos como o aplicativo de agente de IA Muse e os modelos da empresa poderão gerar receitas relevantes o suficiente para superar os custos crescentes;
- A Meta contestou a avaliação. Em comunicado, um porta-voz afirmou que a empresa discorda da interpretação da S&P sobre sua capacidade de monetizar a IA e disse enxergar oportunidades significativas em produtos e negócios;
- A preocupação da agência ocorre depois de a companhia registrar fluxo de caixa livre negativo de US$ 2,12 bilhões (cerca de R$ 11,66 bilhões) no terceiro trimestre. Foi a primeira vez que a empresa ficou no vermelho nesse indicador;
- A Meta também prevê investimentos de capital entre US$ 135 bilhões e US$ 145 bilhões (aproximadamente R$ 742,5 bilhões a R$ 797,5 bilhões) em 2026. O montante inclui gastos relacionados à expansão de sua infraestrutura de IA.
Leia mais:
- Justiça manda Meta apagar posts que incentivam demissão por voto
- Meta deixa julgamento sobre vício em redes sociais; Snapchat segue como único réu
- Com IPO, Anthropic terá de provar que consegue lucrar, dizem especialistas
- De uso malicioso a perda de controle: os riscos da IA que preocupam a Anthropic
Empresa planeja captar R$ 522,5 bilhões
A pressão financeira também aparece nos planos de financiamento da Meta. Na segunda-feira (26), a companhia anunciou a intenção de levantar US$ 95 bilhões (cerca de R$ 522,5 bilhões) para financiar suas iniciativas de IA.
A estratégia prevê primeira captação de US$ 35 bilhões (aproximadamente R$ 192,5 bilhões) por meio de ofertas públicas de ações subscritas. Depois, a empresa pretende levantar outros US$ 60 bilhões (cerca de R$ 330 bilhões) por meio de programa de venda de ações no mercado.
A reação dos investidores também foi negativa após a divulgação dos resultados trimestrais. Mesmo com receita acima das expectativas, as ações da Meta caíram 7% depois do balanço. Outubro terminou com recuo de 15% nos papéis, o pior desempenho mensal da companhia em quatro anos.
A S&P espera que o crescimento dos investimentos de capital comece a perder força a partir de 2028, mas demonstrou menos confiança de que a empresa realmente reduzirá os gastos no ritmo previsto anteriormente.
Anthropic pode receber classificação de crédito especulativa
A situação da Anthropic envolve avaliação diferente. A empresa, responsável pelo desenvolvimento da família de modelos Claude, pode receber classificação de crédito na faixa BB após eventual abertura de capital.
A previsão, atribuída à Blackstone e divulgada pelo Financial Times, representa perspectiva menos favorável do que a estimativa anterior, segundo a qual a companhia poderia alcançar o grau de investimento antes de 2027.
Na escala de classificação de crédito, notas abaixo de BBB- são consideradas especulativas. Empresas nessa categoria podem enfrentar custos mais elevados para captar recursos, já que investidores enxergam maior risco de inadimplência.
Uma classificação nessa faixa poderia dificultar o financiamento dos planos de expansão da Anthropic, especialmente diante da necessidade de ampliar sua capacidade computacional para desenvolver e operar modelos de IA.
A previsão, porém, não representa uma nota oficial já atribuída à empresa. A avaliação também não significa que a Anthropic esteja inadimplente, mas indica que seu perfil de crédito pode ser considerado mais arriscado por investidores e credores.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Desk Phones vs Apps: Choosing a Business Phone System When Everyone Already Has a Mobile - Tech Guide
articles.text:
The Evolution of Business Communication
In today’s digitally connected world, business communication has undergone a profound transformation. The proliferation of smartphones and high-speed internet means nearly every employee carries a mobile device capable of voice, video, and messaging. Yet, despite this ubiquity, many organizations continue to rely on traditional desk phones or explore app-based communication platforms to meet their needs. Choosing between desk phones and mobile app-based systems is complex, especially when balancing cost, reliability, security, and user experience.
Understanding these options is crucial for companies aiming to optimize communication efficiency and employee productivity. This article explores the advantages and challenges of desk phones and app-based systems, offering insights to help businesses select the most effective phone system in an era where mobile devices are already in everyone’s hands.
Understanding the Role of Desk Phones in Modern Offices
Desk phones have been the backbone of business communication for decades. Their dedicated hardware and infrastructure provide a reliable, consistent calling experience valued by many professionals. These devices are designed for high call volumes in environments like call centers, customer service departments, and executive offices where call clarity and uninterrupted connectivity are paramount.
A key advantage of desk phones is their ability to maintain high-quality voice transmission without relying heavily on fluctuating internet connections. This reliability translates into fewer dropped calls and less interference, critical for customer-facing roles. Additionally, desk phones project a professional presence with features like customizable caller ID and dedicated buttons for frequent contacts or emergency numbers.
However, desk phones come with challenges. Physical installation requires wired connections, which can be costly and time-consuming to set up and maintain. Scaling the system as the company grows may involve significant expenses. To address these issues, many businesses partner with a managed IT provider in New Hampshire, which streamlines installation, maintenance, and integration with existing IT infrastructure. These providers handle hardware procurement, software updates, and network management, ensuring minimal downtime and optimal performance.
Despite the rise of mobile communication, desk phones remain a staple in many organizations due to their reliability, ease of use for frequent callers, and the familiarity they offer employees accustomed to traditional telephony.
The Rise of App-Based Phone Systems
The rapid advancement of mobile technology and cloud computing has paved the way for app-based phone systems, also known as Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) or Unified Communications (UC) platforms. These systems enable voice and video calls, instant messaging, and collaboration through file sharing-all within a single app accessible on smartphones, tablets, and desktops.
App-based systems offer unparalleled flexibility. Employees can communicate seamlessly whether in the office, working remotely, or on the go. This adaptability is especially valuable in today’s hybrid work models, where staying connected from any location is a critical business requirement.
According to a recent survey, 85% of businesses have adopted some form of mobile or app-based communication tools to support remote workforces. This shift reflects the growing recognition that app-based platforms enhance employee mobility and foster real-time collaboration beyond voice calls.
Moreover, app-based systems often come with rich features such as video conferencing, screen sharing, call recording, and integration with business applications like Customer Relationship Management (CRM) software. These capabilities can significantly boost team productivity and streamline workflows.
Nevertheless, app-based phone systems depend heavily on internet connectivity quality. Network congestion, low bandwidth, or unstable Wi-Fi can lead to poor call quality or dropped connections. To mitigate these challenges, companies can leverage resources such as NetAccess’ on-demand tech support, which provide rapid technical assistance, network optimization, and troubleshooting services. These support structures are vital for maintaining smooth communication and minimizing disruptions in mission-critical operations.
Key Considerations When Choosing Between Desk Phones and Apps
Cost Efficiency
Cost is often a primary consideration when evaluating phone systems. Desk phones require upfront investment in hardware, wiring, and installation. Ongoing maintenance and upgrades add to the total cost of ownership. Conversely, app-based systems usually operate on subscription models, offering lower initial costs but recurring monthly fees depending on users or features.
Businesses must conduct a thorough cost-benefit analysis, factoring in direct expenses and indirect costs such as employee training, system downtime, and scalability. For small to medium-sized enterprises, app-based systems may offer a more budget-friendly and flexible solution, while larger organizations with stable office environments might find desk phones more cost-effective over time.
User Experience and Productivity
User experience is pivotal for communication effectiveness. Desk phones provide a tactile interface with physical buttons, which many employees find intuitive, especially for frequent or complex calls. Features like dedicated hold buttons, speakerphones, and headset compatibility contribute to efficient call management.
App-based platforms unify multiple communication channels-voice, video, messaging-into a single interface. This integration can enhance productivity by reducing tool switching and enabling quicker decision-making through instant collaboration.
A study by McKinsey found that companies using integrated communication apps experienced a 32% improvement in team collaboration. This often translates into faster project turnaround times and better customer service.
Security and Compliance
Security is paramount, especially for industries handling sensitive or regulated information like healthcare, finance, and legal services. Desk phones can operate on isolated, private networks, limiting exposure to cyber threats. Physical control over hardware and connections simplifies compliance with regulations such as HIPAA or GDPR.
In contrast, app-based systems transmit data over the internet and rely on encryption protocols to safeguard communications. While many platforms offer robust security features, including end-to-end encryption and multi-factor authentication, cyber risks remain a consideration.
Engaging a managed IT provider ensures the chosen phone system incorporates tailored security measures and complies with industry-specific regulations. This partnership can include regular security audits, employee training, and rapid incident response.
Scalability
Scalability is essential for businesses anticipating growth or fluctuating workforce sizes. App-based phone systems excel here, allowing companies to add or remove users easily without physical hardware changes. This flexibility supports dynamic teams and seasonal staffing variations.
Desk phone systems may require purchasing additional hardware, rewiring, or upgrading network infrastructure to accommodate expansion. While this provides predictable control over communication, it can result in higher capital expenditures and longer deployment timelines.
Integrating Mobile Devices Into the Business Phone System
Since employees already rely heavily on mobile devices, integrating these tools into the broader business communication strategy is vital. Many modern phone systems support “bring your own device” (BYOD) policies, enabling secure access to company communication apps on personal smartphones while maintaining separation between personal and corporate data.
This integration facilitates seamless communication across devices and locations, empowering employees to switch between desk phones, mobile apps, and computers without losing call continuity or collaboration features.
Hybrid communication models combining desk phones, app-based platforms, and mobile integration offer the best of all worlds. They accommodate diverse working styles, from office-centric roles needing desk phones to remote employees relying exclusively on mobile apps. Such flexibility promotes inclusivity and ensures all team members remain connected regardless of location.
Future Trends in Business Phone Systems
The communication landscape continues to evolve rapidly, influenced by emerging technologies and changing workplace dynamics. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning are beginning to play roles in phone systems, offering features like automated call routing, voice transcription, sentiment analysis, and virtual assistants.
Cloud-based communication platforms are expected to dominate, driven by scalability, cost-effectiveness, and integration capabilities. The global cloud telephony market is projected to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 15.9% from 2021 to 2028.
Moreover, the rise of 5G networks promises to improve mobile connectivity quality, potentially narrowing the gap between desk phones and app-based systems in terms of call reliability and latency.
Businesses should stay informed about these trends and adapt their communication infrastructure to leverage new capabilities that enhance operational efficiency and employee satisfaction.
Making the Right Choice for Your Business
Choosing between desk phones and app-based systems is not one-size-fits-all. It depends on factors including company size, industry requirements, workforce distribution, budget, and security needs.
Engaging technology partners, managed service providers, and communication consultants can provide valuable insights. These experts assess unique organizational needs, evaluate existing infrastructure, and recommend solutions aligned with strategic goals.
While mobile devices offer unprecedented flexibility, desk phones still hold value by providing reliability, professionalism, and dedicated hardware functionality. Meanwhile, app-based systems bring flexibility, integration, and scalability suited to modern, mobile-first workforces. A thoughtful balance of these options, supported by expert guidance and tailored to operational realities, ensures effective communication channels that drive growth and productivity.

articles.title: Smaller Components Complicate BGA Rework Heating- EE Times
articles.text:
Smaller components and denser boards are creating new thermal challenges for ball grid array (BGA) rework. Miniature passives can be located within a millimeter or two of rework targets. This tightens thermal profile windows and raises the stakes for precision heat delivery. Traditional hot-air systems that operated at larger scales struggle to meet the demands of today’s high-density assemblies.
The SMT miniaturization trend behind modern PCB design
The drive toward higher functionality in smaller form factors has pushed surface mount technology (SMT) miniaturization to the forefront of PCB design priorities. Designers are packing more components into less space, with passive components such as 0201 and 01005 footprints increasingly used in high-density applications.
The International Electronics Manufacturing Initiative (iNEMI) electronics roadmap identifies component miniaturization and increased packing density as important industry drivers, with HDI microvia sizes continuing to shrink as manufacturers push toward finer geometries. This trend creates new challenges for rework operations that were engineered around larger geometries.
Proximity and warpage risks in high-density assemblies
As spacing tightens, the gap between a target BGA and its neighboring 0201 or 01005 passives can fall below a millimeter. Standard hot-air nozzles weren’t designed for this proximity.
Airflow meant to reflow a single package can reach adjacent passives and cause unintended reflow, misalignment, or physical displacement. Thinner substrates and multi-layer stackups add warpage concerns when uneven thermal gradients stress the PCB during heating and cooling cycles.
Proper thermal profiling practices show that warpage occurs when temperature gradients exceed acceptable limits. Bottom-side preheaters with adjustable nozzles help reduce localized substrate stress.
A peer-reviewed heat shield study found that strategic heat shield placement resulted in up to an 8.18% reduction in adjacent-component peak temperatures. It also found that keeping center and corner BGA temperatures below 195° Celsius and 210° Celsius, respectively, cut solder joint cracking rates by more than half. Some facilities are reportedly adopting focused laser rework systems and micro-convection stations that establish much narrower thermal zones.
Solder voids and capillary effects at micro geometries
Thermal profile windows tighten as solder ball diameters shrink. At the scale of SMT miniaturization, airflow turbulence from convective heating can disrupt the surface tension of molten solder. This poses a risk of defects, such as capillary wicking or vapor-pressure-driven voiding, in underfilled fine-pitch BGAs.
Even minor package or PCB warpage during the cooling phase can cause solder bridging between adjacent balls or open joints where contact fails to establish. The margin for error becomes nearly invisible. Heating methods that worked reliably at 0.5-mm pitch often struggle at 0.3 mm. A finer pitch requires tighter process control windows and more precise thermal delivery systems.
How convective hot air heating works
Energy transfer in convective heating happens through circulated airflow directed via sized nozzles. Responsive control over ramp rates and cooling phases makes the method effective for many rework scenarios. As component geometries shrink, however, maintaining airflow uniformity becomes more challenging, and that uniformity can affect thermal delivery consistency.
For instance, a nozzle sized for a 15-mm BGA may create edge effects or turbulence when operators attempt to confine heat to a 5-mm device surrounded by delicate passives. The physics favor larger-scale applications where spatial margins allow airflow to spread predictably.
The physics behind radiant and infrared heating
Radiant heating, including infrared (IR), delivers energy via electromagnetic radiation rather than relying on airflow. However, while this removes turbulence concerns, it introduces a different set of variables for operators evaluating the BGA rework process. Top-to-bottom thermal uniformity depends heavily on whether the station includes a focused bottom hot-air feature.
Stations without this feature can’t ensure that radiant energy is distributed evenly from the top of the BGA to the bottom of the PCB. Operators often need to compensate by raising under-heater temperatures, and the required temperature delta varies significantly across different equipment designs.
Hot air and IR station capabilities become critical when facilities need consistent, repeatable results on high-density boards, where even small thermal imbalances can cause joint failures or damage to nearby packages. The temperature can vary by up to 100° Celsius from the software setpoint in some machines, so it’s important to calibrate and monitor temperatures to create a reliable profile.
Thermal profiling for high-density PCB rework
Equipment selection comes down to matching heating physics to board architecture. While convective systems offer ramp control, they often struggle with proximity constraints.
Radiant approaches can reduce turbulence, though engineers must pay careful attention to top-to-bottom uniformity. The IPC-7530 thermal profiling standard provides the formal framework for temperature profiling in mass soldering processes like reflow. This gives engineering teams a consistent basis for evaluating rework equipment capabilities.
Why heating method choice now defines rework success
Choosing a heating method is a primary equipment decision. As geometries shrink and assembly densities rise, thermal delivery physics in the BGA rework process affects yield in high-value assemblies. Matching rework heating systems to current and future board designs protects production efficiency and assembly integrity. Designers can only expect the industry to push further into sub-millimeter spacing in the next few years.

articles.title: How Stelcore helps brands go global without building everything from scratch
articles.text:
How Stelcore helps brands go global without building everything from scratch
Taking a brand global means navigating more than just new markets. At TechSparks 2026, Stelcore Group founder Bharat Mandot explained how the company connects importing, payments, logistics and compliance.
Selling internationally can open new markets for a brand. But behind every order lies a web of logistics, payments, product certifications, customs rules, and local compliance requirements. As businesses expand, managing these moving parts across countries can become a challenge of its own.
This is where Stelcore Group steps in.
At TechSparks 2026, Founder and Chairman Bharat Mandot explained how the company connects trade infrastructure, compliance, and technology to help brands navigate global markets.
One integration for multiple markets
“Stelcore is about trade infrastructure, compliance infrastructure, and technology for global markets,” Mandot said, describing how the company supports brands entering international markets.
Stelcore says it has worked with more than 30,000 brands and sellers from India over 14 years of operations. It has a presence in more than 14 countries, including the US, Canada, the UK, Europe, the UAE, Singapore, Australia and South Korea.
Rather than requiring brands to establish a separate entity in every destination market, Stelcore brings together importing, storage, payments, last-mile delivery and returns.
When an order arrives through a marketplace or a brand’s direct-to-consumer (D2C) store, the system coordinates warehouse allocation and delivery. Stelcore’s local entity can act as the seller of record and importer, handling applicable compliance and logistics requirements.
Mandot described the model as a way to give brands international reach through one operating partner, without having to rebuild the process for every new market.
Compliance before the shipment moves
Cross-border commerce involves more than getting products from one warehouse to another. Brands must also meet destination-market requirements for product registration, packaging, labelling, certifications and technical documentation.
Mandot demonstrated Stelcore’s compliance assessment tool, which allows sellers to select a destination country and product category to identify relevant tests, reports, import procedures and certifications.
“The tool is free of cost,” he said, explaining that sellers can assess requirements for a product category across different countries in 10 to 15 minutes.
The platform also provides a central repository for product information, including HSN codes and other market-specific details. This can help brands respond to queries from logistics providers and customs authorities, reducing the risk of shipments being held up over documentation.
Mandot distinguished between business and product compliance. While businesses can choose different arrangements, such as working with a distributor or a local entity, product compliance remains necessary regardless of the operating model.
Connecting the entire order journey
Stelcore’s technology brings order processing, warehouse allocation, and last-mile delivery into one view. Brands can access this information through an application programming interface (API) and build their own management systems around it.
The platform also supports services such as tax registration, VAT, customs procedures, intellectual property support, and payment reconciliation.
For brands entering unfamiliar markets, the challenge is not simply finding customers. It is building the operational infrastructure to serve them consistently. Stelcore’s approach is to connect these moving parts through one operating partner, helping businesses expand internationally without having to assemble every layer themselves.

articles.title: Drupal warns of critical Commerce Core flaw exploited in attacks
articles.text:
Drupal warned admins to patch a critical access bypass vulnerability in the Commerce Core module that attackers are exploiting in the wild.
Tracked as CVE-2026-118539, this flaw stems from a missing authorization weakness that can be abused by unauthenticated attackers and affects Commerce Core versions 0.0.0 through 2.41 and 3.0.0 through 3.3.13.
The Drupal security team asked admins on the 3.x branch to upgrade immediately to Commerce Core 3.3.13 (or Commerce Core 8.x-2.41 for earlier versions) and audit orders for inconsistencies, since threat actors are exploiting this vulnerability in attacks.
"This module enables you to sell goods and services to customers through an included shopping cart and checkout form or through decoupled applications via APIs," Drupal said in a Wednesday advisory tagged as highly critical.
"The module doesn't sufficiently protect certain routes and entity fields, leading to an access bypass that may financially impact the vendor. This vulnerability is being actively exploited in the wild."
Commerce Core is a community-developed Drupal module used by more than 42,000 websites, including many high-profile organizations such as Fortune 500 companies and research universities.
The module provides a software framework for building and running e-commerce sites and shopping apps on top of the Drupal Content Management System (CMS).
In May, Drupal also warned that attackers were exploiting an SQL injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-9082) in the database abstraction API that could lead to privilege escalation, information disclosure, and remote code execution.
Days later, the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog and ordered federal agencies to patch their systems within three days.
Two weeks ago, Drupal patched two more remote code execution security issues (CVE-2026-108097 and CVE-2026-108099) that could allow threat actors to execute code remotely, and urged admins to apply updates as soon as possible because attackers could develop exploits "within hours or days."
Over the last several years, CISA has flagged 5 Drupal vulnerabilities exploited in the wild, two of which have also been abused by ransomware gangs.
Once attackers have valid credentials, only 37% of their actions are blocked
Overall prevention scores can hide what happens after initial access. Once attackers are using valid credentials, prevention drops sharply.

Boulanger propose ce téléviseur à 799 €, contre un prix de référence affiché de 1 099 €, soit 300 € de réduction immédiate. L’ODR de 50 € porte l’économie totale à 350 €, environ 32 %. Le produit neuf est vendu et expédié par Boulanger, avec la livraison offerte.
Une ODR de 50 € à demander sur dossier

TCL demande notamment la facture, les coordonnées bancaires, une photo du numéro de série et du code-barres découpé sur le carton. Un avis produit est également demandé dans le parcours. Le remboursement intervient sous six à huit semaines après réception d’un dossier conforme, dans la limite d’une demande par foyer.

articles.title: Plus cher que l'iPhone Duo, Samsung dévoile son nouveau smartphone pliant ultra luxueux
articles.text:
Comme chaque année, Samsung propose un modèle spécial de smartphone pliant pour le marché chinois. Après quelques jours de teasing, le constructeur coréen vient de lever le voile sur le Samsung W27, un modèle qui s’adresse clairement aux personnes qui aiment les produits exclusifs et qui sont prêts à payer le prix fort.
Un design luxueux et des entrailles de mastodonte
Le Samsung W27 est un smartphone haut de gamme qui partage une grande partie de la fiche technique du Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra. Il fait ainsi toujours 8,9 millimètres d’épaisseur pour un poids de 215 grammes. Il se différencie de son homologue par un cadre et un bloc caméra dorés, ainsi qu’une finition texturée sur les tranches et un dos rouge foncé ou bleu sombre. Le tout est protégé par du verre Gorilla Glass Ceramic 3 et profite d’un indice de protection IP48.
Pour faire tourner la bête, Samsung compte toujours sur le processeur Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 pour Galaxy, épaulé par une batterie de 5 000 mAh et deux dalles OLED : un écran interne de 8 pouces et un écran externe de 6,5 pouces. Côté photo, le bloc caméra arrière intègre un module principal de 200 mégapixels, un ultra grand-angle de 50 mégapixels et un téléobjectif x3 de 10 mégapixels. Enfin, les selfies sont assurés par des caméras frontales de 10 mégapixels placées sur chaque écran.
Un prix salé et quelques accessoires
Côté stockage et mémoire vive, Samsung fait l’impasse sur la version avec 12 Go de RAM pour proposer directement 16 Go de RAM et 512 Go ou 1 To de stockage. Pour s’offrir le modèle de base avec 512 Go, il faut débourser 18,999 yuans, soit environ 2 548 euros. De son côté, la version 1 To grimpe à 21,999 yuans, soit environ 2950 euros.
Pour rappel, le Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra est vendu en France à 2199 euros et l’iPhone Duo d’Apple à 2339 euros. Pour mieux faire passer la pilule, Samsung intègre quelques accessoires dans la boîte, comme une coque magnétique en Kevlar, un chargeur de 45W ainsi qu’un câble USB-C.

articles.title: Los sindicatos se rebelan contra Óscar Puente por señalar al controlador de Adif: "Sus declaraciones nos parecen lamentables"
articles.text:
Si algo nos ha quedado claro del fatídico accidente de Urda (Toledo) en el que han fallecido, al menos, 69 personas es que se dio una cadena de errores que provocó que un tren AVE chocara contra un Iryo detenido en la vía a una velocidad de entre 160 y 200 km/h. En esa cadena de errores, el ministro Óscar Puente puso el foco en uno muy concreto: la orden dio el responsable de circulación al AVE.
Ahora los sindicatos defienden que desde el Ministerio de Transportes no se ha dudado en señalar directamente al trabajador, piden la dimisión de Puente y señalan los audios filtrados como "interesados".
La rueda de prensa. Concretamente, la que dio Óscar Puente la tarde del 28 de octubre, día en el que se produjo el fatídico choque entre un AVE y un Iryo que circulaban en el mismo sentido en el corredor andaluz de alta velocidad. Es ahí donde, por primera vez, el ministro de Transportes pone el foco en el trabajador de Adif del CRC de Atocha.
"Es inexplicable", con estas palabras describió Puente la decisión del controlador ferroviario de ordenar al AVE a circular "con normalidad" cuando la señalización marcaba que no podía continuar y tenía un Iryo detenido en la vía unos kilómetros por delante.
En ese momento, Puente señala al operario como uno de los máximos responsables del accidente a pesar de que éste interviene porque se ha caído el sistema LZB en la línea en un tramo de más de 60 kilómetros.
"Nos parecen lamentables". La respuesta del Sindicato de Circulación de Ferrocarriles (SCF) es contundente. Preguntados sobre las declaraciones de Puente en la rueda de prensa del primer día, Ana María Galisteo, portavoz de SCF, nos contesta lo siguiente:
"Las declaraciones de Oscar Puente nos parecen lamentables. Que a pocas horas de que se dé el accidente y con una investigación recién iniciada se atreva a sentenciar públicamente a un trabajador, el más vulnerable del sistema... Si es o no culpable, lo tendrá que decir un juez. En toda empresa, cuando algo falla,  el empleador es el máximo responsable y en el sector ferroviario parece que es más conveniente poner nombre y apellidos a estos trágicos accidentes. Los audios también convenientemente filtrados para reforzar este linchamiento hacia el trabajador.
Los audios. Es la otra gran acusación que se le hace al ministerio de Transportes. Y es que el mismo día del accidente cuando ya caía la noche, los audios del CRC de Atocha se filtran a la prensa. Cadena Ser es el primer medio que tiene acceso a dichos audios. En ellos se escucha una conversación entre el maquinista y el responsable de circulación que da informaciones confusas. En un momento dado, se escucha cómo ordena al AVE que impacta contra el Iryo a circular "con marcha normal".
Estos audios han sido tachados por SCF como "interesados" para desviar el problema principal: la caída del sistema LZB. La filtración, además, pone el foco en el desempeño del trabajador y difundirlos implica que cualquiera puede juzgar la labor del mismo aunque no tenga los conocimientos para ello. Tampoco se distorsiona la voz del empleado por lo que a esta persona se le podría reconocer por ella.
El rechazo sindical. SCF no es el único sindicato que ha mostrado su repulsa a los audios filtrados y a que se haya puesto el foco en el trabajador. UGT señalaba en declaraciones recogidas por 20Minutos que "tiene nuestra total repulsa y vamos a ir a investigar quién ha sido, cómo ha sido y por qué y lo denunciamos categóricamente".
En ese mismo artículo, Pepa Páez, secretaria general del sector ferroviario de CCOO, pedía que "no se ponga el foco en el último eslabón, en un trabajador, sin saber en qué situación está trabajando". Esto último, de hecho, es una reivindicación constante de SCF quien alertó hasta en dos ocasiones a Adif de que existía una falta de personal alarmante.
Ana María Galisteo, SCF, pone el foco en esto en declaraciones a Xataka:
"Hay una falta de personal que llevamos denunciando durante años. Las ofertas públicas no son suficientes, solo han servido para reponer, los que entran por los que salen (relevo generacional). Pero no suponen un incremento real que permita atender a las necesidades del servicio. La evolución de la actividad ferroviaria no ha ido acompañada de un aumento proporcional de los recursos humanos"
Dimisión. Las declaraciones de Óscar Puente y las condiciones de trabajo a las que están sometidos los trabajadores en Atocha han llevado a los sindicatos a pedir la dimisión de Óscar Puente. Son declaraciones que ha hecho el Central Sindical Independiente y de Funcionarios (CSIF) pero también la sección sindical ferroviaria de CCOO. En ambos casos se denuncia que se está poniendo el foco en el trabajador para utilizarlo como chivo expiatorio.
De momento, en su última rueda de prensa, Óscar Puente ha negado que se esté planteando la dimisión. "Mi forma de ser responsable es dar la cara", ha señalado.
Angrois. Poner en el disparadero al operario, independientemente de sus condiciones de trabajo, ya se hizo con el accidente ferroviario de Angrois. En él, fallecieron 80 personas cuando un Alvia descarriló en la curva de A Grandeira en Angrois (Santiago de Compostela). De él se hizo responsable a Francisco Garzón, maquinista del tren. En la sentencia del juicio, Garzón y Andrés Cortabitarte, director de Seguridad en la Circulación de Adif, fueron condenados a 2 años, 6 meses y 1 día de prisión por el delito de 79 homicidios.
A pesar de que sobre ambos recayeron las culpas, se confirmó que la señalización antes de llegar a la curva alertando de la reducción de velocidad hasta los 80 km/h era insuficiente. Incluso, otros maquinistas confirmaron en las investigaciones que tomaban referencias visuales propias porque no existía una señalización previa suficiente.
De igual modo que esta vez, en aquella ocasión no se tardó en filtrar los audios en los que se escuchaba al maquinista lamentarse de haber superado la velocidad máxima a la que podía circular.

articles.title: Waymo usará autos de Toyota para sus robotaxis en Japón y el Reino Unido, con pruebas desde 2027
articles.text:
Toyota fabricará los autos eléctricos que Waymo usará como robotaxis en Japón y el Reino Unido. Las dos empresas anunciaron el 30 de octubre que las pruebas del modelo bZ4X comenzarán en el país asiático en 2027, con despliegue posterior en territorio británico y en otros mercados donde opera la filial de Alphabet.
Según el comunicado de la automotriz, los vehículos se construirán en la planta de Takaoka, en la ciudad de Toyota, prefectura de Aichi. Todo el proceso ocurrirá en el mismo lugar: desde el armado del auto base hasta la instalación del hardware de conducción autónoma de Waymo.
El modelo llevará puertas automáticas, portón trasero eléctrico, iluminación ambiental y más espacio para las piernas en el asiento trasero. Toyota presentó el proyecto como el primer servicio de transporte totalmente autónomo de Japón con vehículos fabricados en el país.
Los autos serán de nivel 4, es decir, el sistema conduce por sí solo en condiciones definidas y no requiere conductor. Waymo comenzará por los mercados donde se maneja por la derecha. “Empezaremos con los mercados de conducción por la derecha, Japón y el Reino Unido”, dijo el codirector ejecutivo, Dmitri Dolgov, recogió Reuters.
Dolgov afirmó que la alianza con Toyota permitirá llevar la tecnología de Waymo a una operación comercial a gran escala. La empresa nipona sostuvo en su comunicado que el objetivo es reducir los accidentes causados por errores humanos y facilitar la movilidad de quienes no pueden desplazarse con facilidad.
Sin cantidad de autos ni ciudad definida
Las empresas no informaron cuántos bZ4X desplegarán al inicio ni en qué zona de Japón operarán, indicó Reuters. Hiroki Nakajima, de Toyota, dijo que las primeras operaciones usarán pocos vehículos. Dolgov afirmó que no hay otros países ni plazos para compartir.
El diario japonés Asahi Shimbun informó que los detalles, como la empresa de taxis que operará el servicio, se definirán más adelante. El anuncio llega 18 meses después del acuerdo preliminar firmado en abril de 2025 para explorar una plataforma de vehículos autónomos. TechCrunch señaló que el pacto se parece más a un contrato convencional de proveedor de autos.
Waymo prueba hoy autos Jaguar I-Pace en Japón y mantiene un piloto con ellos en 2027, dijo Dolgov a Reuters. En Londres, TechCrunch informó que la empresa los prueba desde hace meses y lanzará el servicio cuando obtenga los permisos necesarios.
Más allá del robotaxi: autos particulares
Toyota y Waymo también seguirán estudiando cómo llevar la tecnología autónoma a autos Toyota de propiedad particular. Junto con Woven by Toyota, evaluarán otras iniciativas para reducir accidentes, con datos de la operación real de Waymo.
Nakajima dijo que la automotriz asiática seguirá explorando cómo la integración de los vehículos con la infraestructura vial puede hacer las calles aún más seguras. Toyota también fabrica versiones con volante a la izquierda del bZ4X, pero quiere ganar experiencia en Japón antes de buscar otras oportunidades.
El primer hito confirmado es el inicio de las pruebas y la validación de la flota de bZ4X autónomos en Japón en 2027.

articles.title: Bethesda cierra un juego fan de Fallout generado por IA
articles.text:
El proyecto de Fallout: New York estuvo poco tiempo abierto al público. El 28 de septiembre de 2026, Chris First publicaba un juego online (construido, según su autor, con Claude Opus 5.5) que llevaba al mundo de Fallout a Nueva York. No era necesario instalar nada.
Se trataba de un juego web que, según First, traía misiones, árbol de diálogos, el sistema de combate V.A.T.S. y un Pip-Boy (el aparato de muñeca de Fallout) que funcionaba. Además, según su autor, tenía 117 localizaciones diferentes. También contaba con 112 personajes y 46 armas.
Chris First aseguraba en su presentación que “cada edificio, arma, rostro y sonido está generado por código”. No había archivos de texturas o sonidos. En esta publicación de presentación se han superado los 3,5 millones de visualizaciones en X.
En el anuncio de cierre del 1 de octubre también criticaba que Bethesda no hiciera otro Fallout y se pedía perdón a los que habían disfrutado del juego.
Las reglas de marca y el dominio
Por otro lado, podemos entender mejor el conflicto gracias a las reglas de marca de ZeniMax (actualizadas el 2 de mayo de 2024). En ellas se indica que, sin autorización por escrito o permiso explícito, no se pueden utilizar los elementos de marca en los nombres de productos o dominios. Además, no deben dar a entender que hay alguna clase de afiliación o aprobación por parte de la compañía.
Por tanto, alguien que quiera mostrar una demo tiene que tener en cuenta el dominio. Por otro lado, en las directrices se indica que se pueden mencionar los juegos de manera informativa siempre que no induzcan a confusión. Sin embargo, si se trata de mostrar un producto propio usando el nombre de una franquicia, estamos en un caso diferente. Esto es así aunque el código haya sido regenerado.
Otro aspecto en el que puede haber confusión es que existe un mod de Fallout: New York. Se trata de un proyecto de voluntarios realizado con Creation Kit. En su página web se aclara que no están afiliados a Bethesda Game Studios. Este proyecto es diferente al de First (que usaba un dominio diferente, fallout.nyc y no falloutnyc.com).
Este proyecto es un ejemplo de programación por conversaciones con una IA (también llamada “vibe coding”). Ya hemos tratado los límites de esta práctica. Se trata de una práctica en la que conseguimos un programa que funciona, pero que requiere de revisiones posteriores. En este caso han sido el propio nombre y la elección de distribución (dirección) los que han estado en el centro de la reclamación.
Los cambios que anunció Chris First
Sin embargo, Chris First no ha desechado todo el trabajo. En su respuesta del 4 de octubre indicaba que ZeniMax había sido amable y que le había solicitado que retirara el material. También indicaba que iba a entregarles el dominio.
El mismo día comentaba que había hecho algunos cambios en el juego. Seguía trabajando en la historia. Incluso ofrecía un enlace privado para que pudieran probarlo. Decía que con estos cambios se eliminaba el conflicto de derechos (sin que esto implique una autorización de ZeniMax).

articles.title: RTX 5070, 32 Go de RAM et écran 2,5K : l'Asus ROG Strix 18 perd 300 euros avant le Black Friday — Frandroid
articles.text:
GTA VI sort le 19 novembre sur PS5 et Xbox Series, mais Rockstar n’a toujours pas annoncé de version PC. Vous pouvez préparer son arrivée dès maintenant, puisque Boulanger anticipe le Black Friday, prévu le 27 novembre, en retirant 300 euros au prix de l’Asus ROG Strix 18. Il s’agit d’un PC portable gamer de 18 pouces, équipé d’un AMD Ryzen 9 8940HX à 16 cœurs et d’une NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070.
Que retenir de l’Asus ROG Strix 18 ?
- L’AMD Ryzen 9 8940HX et 32 Go de RAM
- La NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070
- 1 To de stockage
L’Asus ROG Strix 18 est actuellement disponible à 2 199,99 euros au lieu de 2 499,99 euros sur le site de Boulanger. Le marchand l’affiche à 2 299,99 euros, et le code GAMER100 retire 100 euros de plus jusqu’à ce dimanche 1er novembre.
Une configuration taillée pour le jeu en 2,5K
Cet Asus ROG Strix 18 devrait faire l’affaire pour GTA VI le jour où il arrivera sur PC, mais ce serait réducteur de le limiter à un jeu qui n’est pas encore sorti. La machine d’Asus fera tourner la plupart des jeux AAA sur son écran de 18 pouces en 2 560 x 1 600 pixels, en s’aidant du DLSS, avec un taux de rafraîchissement de 240 Hz.
