articles.title: Algo extremadamente raro está pasando en el ártico: la rotura del vértice polar más temprana desde que tenemos registros
articles.text:
El lunes 26 de octubre, con los datos de las 12 de la noche, 18 de los 50 escenarios que calcula cada día el Centro Europeo de Predicción a Medio Plazo decían que el vórtice polar iba a romperse en los quince días siguientes. Doce horas después eran 23. El martes, 43. El jueves 29, los 50 decían eso mismo.
No es solo algo de Europa. En los últimos tres o cuatro días, los principales modelos de predicción han ido confluyendo en la misma idea: que el vórtice va a sufrir una inversión (con los vientos de la estratosfera cambiando de sentido) entre el 4 y el 10 de noviembre.
Si ocurre, tendremos entre manos un calentamiento súbito estratosférico, sí; pero no uno cualquiera. El más temprano desde 1958: unas tres semanas antes del que hasta ahora tenía el récord. Esto lo podemos dar casi por hecho. Lo que pase luego, nadie lo sabe.
¿Qué es exactamente el vórtice polar? Se trata de una corriente de fuertes vientos (oeste → este) que gira en torno a las grandes reservas de aire frío que se encuentran sobre los polos del planeta. Se forma en la estratosfera; es decir, a unos 16–48 kilómetros de altura. En sentido metafórico (o 'periodístico' si me apuran), el vórtice polar es lo que encierra el frío en el polo.
La lógica nos dice que, en verano, el vórtice se reduce hasta la mínima expresión y, aunque es cierto que nunca lo hemos visto desaparecer del todo en estas fechas, se hace tan débil que apenas influye en el tiempo del hemisferio.
Pero en invierno la situación cambia y lo hace de forma radical. Muy a menudo el vórtice crece y, aunque "suele ser una criatura solitaria" e inofensiva, es habitual que se desborde y acabe afectando al resto del hemisferio. Eso es lo que parece que vamos a ver estas semanas.
¿Y el calentamiento súbito estratosférico? Para entender bien este proceso es bueno recordar que la atmósfera es una "lasaña de capas de aire" y cada una de ellas sigue sus propias lógicas. Es decir, funcionan de forma bastante diferente e independiente; pero nunca independientes del todo.
Es lo que ocurre entre la circulación del aire en la troposfera (la que está más pegada a la superficie) y la circulación en la estratosfera (la capa directamente superior): están relacionadas, sí; pero, en lo sustancial, cada una va por su lado.
Durante los "calentamientos súbitos estratosféricos", unas ondas atmosféricas que suben desde la troposfera irrumpen en la estratosfera y la calientan rápidamente provocando una profunda alteración de la circulación a gran altura. Es decir, durante semanas, todo se pone patas arriba.
¿Y qué va a pasar ahora exactamente? Pues bien. Hacia el 24 de octubre los vientos del vórtice estratosférico tocaron su máximo de la temporada, unos 23 metros por segundo. El viernes 30, a medianoche, marcaba 13,2 metros por segundo. Esto es raro porque la media para la fecha ronda los 23 o 24 metros por segundo. Esta fue la primera pista.
Pero, como digo, no es algo normal. La NOAA registra unas seis inversiones de este tipo cada década. Lo que no ha registrado nunca es una tan pronto en el calendario. Este nivel de alteración "es más habitual en enero y febrero", explicaba esta semana Judah Cohen, del MIT, en Gizmodo.
Vale, pero ¿qué consecuencia tiene todo esto? Nadie lo sabe a ciencia cierta. Como señalaba Víctor González el año pasado, "la facilidad para predecir un calentamiento súbito estratosférico a medio plazo contrasta mucho con la dificultad de anticiparse a sus consecuencias". De ahí que sepamos ya con casi absoluta seguridad que algo va a pasar en la estratosfera del polo norte, pero no esté claro qué va a pasar.
Imagen | PolarWx
En Xataka | Un gran "calentamiento súbito estratosférico" está cerca de romper vórtice. La pregunta es cómo nos afectará
Ver 2 comentarios

articles.title: DJI acaba de solucionar una de las mayores preocupaciones de los robots aspiradores
articles.text:
DJI entró hace tiempo en el segmento de los robots aspiradores con el ROMO, con un diseño bastante rompedor pero unas especificaciones de gama alta, actualizado posteriormente con el Romo 2. Ahora la compañía da un paso más allá y ha anunciado un cambio de paradigma en el software de sus robots aspiradores: el control local.
De esta forma, la compañía ofrece una alternativa a la nube y a sus problemas de privacidad, ofreciendo a los usuarios la posibilidad de controlar el robot sin dejar rastro en internet. ¿Cómo funciona? El modo de datos locales desconecta la aplicación DJI Home de internet y mantiene los datos de los usuarios almacenados y procesados localmente en sus dispositivos, incluyendo las funcionalidades avanzadas de los mismos.
No obstante, la primera puesta en marcha sigue necesitando conexión a internet. DJI confirma que en la primera puesta en marcha de ROMO se conecta a internet para crear un mapa de su entorno, pero que, una vez que se activa el modo de datos locales, esos datos de mapeo se almacenan de forma local y no en la nube.
De ese momento, y con el modo local activado, todos los mapas, imágenes y otros datos utilizados en la navegación y evasión de obstáculos se almacenan y procesan localmente en el dispositivo, reduciendo el riesgo de exposición externa o acceso no autorizado por parte de terceros a los datos de tu casa.
Con todo, si permites que el robot mantenga la conexión a Internet, DJI aplica un cifrado de extremo a extremo que protege los datos durante la transmisión y evita que terceros puedan acceder a ellos, por lo que en cualquiera de las dos opciones la privacidad está garantizada; ahora solo se ofrece ir un paso más allá para tener control total sobre tus datos y tu casa.
Sobre su disponibilidad, el modo de datos locales estará disponible para ROMO 2 desde hoy mismo. No obstante, deberás actualizar; deben actualizar el robot al firmware más
Reciente para que sea compatible con el modo de datos locales, que también llegará a la primera versión, pero será más adelante.

articles.title: What five P99 CONF talks reveal about database trade-offs
articles.text:
What five P99 CONF talks reveal about database trade-offs
P99 CONF is a virtual conference on high-performance, low-latency applications. Its 2026 event ran October 21–22. Here, we cover five of its 60-plus sessions. The recordings are available on demand at p99conf.io after registration.
Database storage design balances read amplification, write amplification, and space amplification (RUM conjecture). Improving one can increase another, depending on the workload and configuration. The five talks below show how engineers make those trade-offs across different database systems.
“Can Everything be an LSM?”
Almog Gavra, Co-Founder at Responsive (now Databricks)
Gavra frames database design around read amplification (data read per result), write amplification (data written per logical write), and space amplification (storage used relative to live data). A log favors fast writes but makes reads work harder; a sorted array does the reverse. As Gavra put it, “I think about LSM trees as a mechanism for tuning between these two extremes.”
LSMs were built for local disks, but their immutable files also fit object storage. Gavra points to Amazon S3’s lower storage cost, durability, and availability, then names the trade-offs: objects must be replaced rather than edited, each GET and PUT has a price, and cold reads are slower. In his example, a local NVMe cache miss takes about 150 microseconds, versus 20–30 milliseconds for S3 Standard — roughly two orders of magnitude. LSMs batch writes into immutable files; caching helps keep object-store reads off the hot path.
Gavra’s SlateDB is an open-source, object-store-native LSM library. It exposes a key-value interface over stores such as S3, GCS, and R2, so developers can build data systems without implementing their own LSM.
How ScyllaDB Eliminates Read Amplification at Scale
Michael Litvak (Senior Software Engineer) and Felipe Cardeneti Mendes (Technical Director), ScyllaDB
ScyllaDB’s presentation examines Logstor, an opt-in storage engine for read-intensive key-value workloads, not a replacement for its existing LSM engine. For each key, an in-memory index stores a hash and the record’s location on flash. A read can return a cached value or find the record with one disk I/O, avoiding an LSM search across SSTables, Bloom Filters, and Indexed data structures. Tables using either engine can run in the same cluster with ScyllaDB’s existing drivers and consistency options.
The speakers’ preliminary read-dominant test sustained 1.1 million reads per second with p99.9 latency below one millisecond and p99.99 latency around 1.5 milliseconds. That test used 2 KB values; the earlier LSM examples in the talk used 1 KB values, so the results are not direct comparisons. They also reported similar throughput and sub-millisecond p99.9 latency in an 80% read, 20% write workload.
Logstor pays for those reads with a larger RAM index and more work on writes. Even a small update writes the full new value to a log, leaving the old record as dead space; segment compaction later reclaims it. The speaker positions it for bounded key sets, frequent overwrites, and point lookups where the extra memory is acceptable. During this talk, Mendes called the trade-off “optimized for time at the sacrifice of space.”
The Vertical Scaling Wall, and How Valkey Gets Over It
Madelyn Olson, Principal Software Engineer at AWS
Not every bottleneck is storage. Olson begins with Amazon ElastiCache customers who saw sudden p50 latency spikes, then tests where Valkey’s main execution thread reached its limit.
In Olson’s unpipelined GET benchmark, with about three million keys and 650 clients, p50 latency rose sharply near 150,000 requests per second. Valkey already had I/O threads, but they sat idle while the main thread executed commands. The team used lockless queues to keep network I/O and command parsing active on those threads while command execution stayed on the main thread.
Olson reported a new ceiling of about 1.2 million requests per second in that workload — roughly eight times the earlier threshold. (This is the talk’s workload-specific result, rather than a general throughput guarantee.)
For horizontal scaling, Valkey 9.0 introduced atomic slot migration. The source shard keeps ownership while it streams a snapshot and subsequent changes to a target, then transfers ownership once the target catches up. Olson said a roughly 40 GB, three-to-four-shard test ran about 10 times faster without load and about five times faster under a heavy GET workload. If a migration fails before handoff, the staged transfer can be aborted without losing end-user data.
The I/O threads can be added or removed as workload demands change. Olson’s operating advice is to use horizontal scaling for baseline capacity and vertical scaling for short bursts, while keeping command execution single-threaded for now. Her guiding principle? “Efficiency trumps headline numbers.”
Searching 100B Vectors on Object Storage @ 200ms P99
Nathan VanBenschoten, Chief Architect at turbopuffer
VanBenschoten described turbopuffer’s search index at a scale of 100 billion vectors, representing more than 200 TiB of dense vector data. The company reports 200 ms p99 latency at more than 1,000 queries per second and 92% recall in early results. Object storage is the durable backing store, but this high-query-rate workload pins its data in local SSD caches. Hierarchical clustering groups nearby vectors; RaBitQ binary quantization shrinks a shadow index to one bit per dimension, allowing the search to narrow candidates before reranking a small subset using full-precision vectors.
The uncompressed search was limited by the bandwidth needed to move vectors from storage into memory. Quantization shifts more work into higher cache tiers, but it also increases arithmetic intensity, making the system CPU-bound.
“Often when you push down one bottleneck, a new one emerges,” VanBenschoten said. That gives the team a different optimization target, including more efficient vector instructions.
To hold an index this large on SSDs, turbopuffer splits it across machines. VanBenschoten says its separated compute-and-storage architecture favors fewer, larger shards: a replacement machine can point to object storage and hydrate its local cache instead of receiving a full shard from another node. Queries fan out to the shards, and a coordinator combines their top results.
The Fastest Object Storage Client in the World*
Georg Kreuzmayr, Software Engineer at TigerBeetle
TigerBeetle is a financial transactions database. In this talk, Kreuzmayr describes the concept of “diagonal scaling”: keeping hot data on local NVMe while extending the storage hierarchy to shared object storage for colder data.
A failed machine doesn’t need to reconstruct data already stored in object storage. As a scale illustration, he estimates that recovering 128 TB over a 100 Gbps network takes about three hours at line rate; if recovery takes longer than the interval between failures, a cluster can enter a failure spiral.
That design needs an object storage client compatible with TigerBeetle’s single-core transaction processing. Kreuzmayr cites the AWS C++ SDK’s blocking `getaddrinfo` call as one mismatch: A call on that core would stall transaction work. SDK thread pools, runtime allocation, and dependencies also conflicted with the project’s design goals.
TigerBeetle therefore built its own multi-cloud client rather than adapting the official SDKs. It supports S3, Azure, and GCP and can be tested with simulated I/O and injected faults.
Built in Zig, the client includes custom DNS, TLS, and HTTP components, uses `io_uring` and zero-copy sends, and allocates its working memory at startup. Kreuzmayr says the implementation is under 40,000 lines of code and has no dependencies beyond its toolchain. Those choices follow TigerStyle’s three principles: safety, performance, and developer experience.
In the talk’s S3 `PutObject` test — 8 MB requests over plain HTTP without checksums on an AWS `c7gn.metal-24xlarge` instance — Kreuzmayr reports uploads around 20 times faster than official SDKs and five times faster than a research implementation. For `GetObject`, he reports about three times the SDK throughput and roughly 25% more than the research implementation. He attributes the smaller download gain to the cloud TCP receive path. These are results for the stated test setup. The conference summarizes the broader client comparison as 4–10 times faster than official GCP and AWS SDKs.
Kreuzmayr’s takeaway is that building the client required more upfront work but made the code easier to test and tune. As he puts it, “code stops being technical debt and ends up being an asset.”
Performance is a process
Across the five talks, engineers identify different bottlenecks in storage, search, networking, and scaling. Their designs improve specific workloads while introducing new costs or complexity elsewhere.
Watch these and more than 200 other P99 CONF talks on demand at p99conf.io. Registration is required. P99 CONF is a ScyllaDB community.

articles.title: Build a Validated Kubernetes Runtime for NVIDIA Dynamo | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.text:
Teams building AI applications need a repeatable path from a model configuration to a working inference endpoint. NVIDIA Dynamo is a distributed inference framework that coordinates model serving across GPU workers. Deploying it on Kubernetes is only a first step. A successful model deployment requires more: GPU drivers, resource allocation, scheduling, networking, and monitoring must all work together. Resolving these dependencies takes time away from testing model behavior, serving performance, and application integration.
The NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform brings together technologies to help the ecosystem design, build, and operate more efficient AI factories, and Dynamo is one of them. To make management of those infrastructure dependencies easier, the platform contains NVIDIA AI Cluster Runtime (AICR). It packages NVIDIA Dynamo and its supporting infrastructure into validated recipes. Each recipe defines a configuration for a specific environment and workload, including pinned component versions, compatibility constraints, and validation checks. AICR gives platform teams a repeatable way to deploy and check the runtime, providing developers with a consistent foundation for serving models and testing applications.
This walkthrough covers the infrastructure that supports Dynamo on Kubernetes, compares two routing options, and shows how to deploy and validate the runtime with AICR.
Why the underlying runtime matters for Dynamo
Running a model with Dynamo on Kubernetes starts with a DynamoGraphDeployment that specifies how vLLM, SGLang, or NVIDIA TensorRT LLM should run in pods on the cluster. But the graph is only the top of the stack. A production inference cluster also needs a runtime layer below it. It has to answer questions like:
- Is the NVIDIA GPU Operator installed with a driver stack that matches the nodes?
- Are GPU nodes labeled and discoverable?
- Does the cluster expose GPUs through the expected Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) driver?
- Can the scheduler place GPU workers with the required topology and gang scheduling semantics?
- Are node health signals available before workloads land on a degraded node?
- Is Prometheus reachable for Dynamo and accelerator metrics?
- Is the Gateway API / Endpoint Picker (EPP) path configured when the deployment should be Kubernetes-native at ingress?
AICR captures these runtime requirements in the recipe.
What AICR ships for Dynamo
An AICR Dynamo recipe packages both Dynamo and the cluster runtime components it depends on.
AICR ships version 1.4.2 of the dynamo-platform chart, which includes the Dynamo operator, Dynamo runtime images, and resources such as the nvidia.com/v1beta1 DynamoGraphDeployment CustomResourceDefinition (CRD). v1beta1 replaces the former v1alpha1 API version.
Table 1 lists the supporting infrastructure components included in the recipe.
| Prerequisite | Requirement | Component in the AICR recipe | 
|---|---|---|
| GPU driver stack | Driver and GPU software stack that matches the nodes | NVIDIA GPU Operator | 
| GPU discovery | GPU nodes labeled and discoverable for placement | Node Feature Discovery | 
| GPU allocation | GPUs exposed through Kubernetes-native Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) | DRA Driver for NVIDIA GPUs | 
| Scheduling | GPU workers placed with the required topology and gang scheduling | KAI Scheduler | 
| Inference Workload Orchestration | Multi-component serving graphs started, placed, and scaled as coordinated groups | Grove | 
| Node health | Health signals available before workloads land on a degraded node | NVSentinel and Nodewright, where supported by the selected recipe | 
| Metrics | Cluster, accelerator, and Dynamo service metrics collected | Prometheus stack | 
| Ingress | Gateway / EPP path configured when ingress is Kubernetes-native | agentgateway and Gateway API resources, described in the routing sections | 
In addition, the recipe pins component versions and records configuration values, node selectors, tolerations, checksums, and validation expectations to make deployment reproducible.
With Dynamo 1.4, frontends, workers, optional Gateway API Inference Extension (GAIE) / Endpoint Picker Plugin (EPP) components, and other Dynamo services discover each other through Kubernetes resources. AICR’s default path therefore no longer uses NATS, and the dynamo-platform chart no longer installs it by default. NATS remains available as an opt-in for deployments that need it.
Agentic workloads repeatedly extend long token prefixes, including system prompts, tool definitions, conversation history, and tool results. If a turn reaches a worker without that prefix in GPU memory, the system reprocesses intermediate tokens instead of reusing cached results. Dynamo routes requests to workers that already hold the relevant KV blocks, either through its frontend router or through GAIE/EPP integration at the Gateway API layer.
Dynamo can also separate prompt processing (prefill) from token generation (decode), an architecture known as disaggregated serving. On KV-cache misses, all or part of the prompt must be reprocessed by the prefill pool. Decode workers then take over token-by-token generation, which has different GPU, memory, latency, and batching characteristics. The cache miss rate depends on the workload. Long-running agentic sessions behave differently from one-off chat requests. Disaggregated serving enables operators to scale and tune prefill and decode capacity independently for a given request mix.
The request plane and KV-cache event plane are separate. In Dynamo 1.4.2, the default AICR Kubernetes path uses TCP for requests and ZMQ for KV-cache events. Each vLLM worker engine emits raw KV-cache events through a local ZMQ publisher, for example, with the following vLLM configuration:
--enable-prefix-caching --kv-transfer-config \
  {"enable_kv_cache_events": true, "publisher": "zmq", "endpoint": "tcp://*:5557"}
Dynamo’s worker runtime then subscribes to that local vLLM event source, normalizes the events, and republishes them onto the Dynamo event plane. Both the native Dynamo Frontend router and the GAIE/EPP path use this Dynamo-managed KV-cache state to make routing decisions.
What are the Dynamo routing paths on Kubernetes?
Dynamo supports two routing paths on Kubernetes. The first uses the Dynamo Frontend router for worker selection. The second uses a Kubernetes Gateway API implementation for ingress and Dynamo EPP for endpoint selection. AICR ships and validates the Dynamo runtime for either topology.
Path 1: Dynamo Frontend router
The default path exposes a Dynamo Frontend behind a Kubernetes Service. Running with DYN_ROUTER_MODE=kv, the Frontend tokenizes each request, scores eligible workers using prefix overlap and current load, selects a worker, and dispatches the request through the Dynamo request plane, which uses TCP by default.
This path is suitable when an application team owns a model-specific endpoint or an existing edge proxy only needs to forward traffic to the Dynamo Frontend Service. It is the smallest topology for deploying and validating a Dynamo graph and is the most production-proven serving option. It does not require the additional gateway and EPP components used in Path 2.
Path 2: Gateway API Inference Extension and Dynamo EPP
This path integrates Dynamo with the Gateway API and Gateway API Inference Extension (GAIE). In the AICR example, agentgateway resolves an HTTPRoute to an InferencePool. The Dynamo operator creates that InferencePool from the DynamoGraphDeployment: its selector identifies eligible worker pods, while its endpointPickerRef identifies the Dynamo EPP Service.
The gateway invokes the Dynamo EPP through GAIE’s endpoint-selection interface. The EPP tokenizes the request and uses Dynamo’s KV router to select an endpoint. It returns the selection and routing metadata to the gateway implementation, which is the actual HTTP proxy. In this mode, each routable worker pod includes a Dynamo Frontend sidecar that receives the request from the gateway and forwards it to the local worker container. The Frontend runs with --router-mode direct, so it applies the EPP selection without rerouting.
This path is suitable when the platform team manages shared Kubernetes ingress and needs to configure model endpoint worker selection, timeouts, retries, and fallback through Gateway API mechanisms. Note that both routing approaches can work behind a Gateway API HTTPRoute. The difference is which component manages the transport to the worker: the Dynamo Frontend or the Gateway itself.
Note: This post covers Dynamo’s operator-managed DynamoGraphDeployment integration with GAIE; the experimental standalone vanilla vLLM on-ramp is a separate integration. In Dynamo 1.4, this path uses GAIE’s Go EPP framework with Dynamo’s Rust KV router embedded through CGO and configured through eppConfig.
Outlook: Starting with Dynamo 1.5, a native Rust EPP replaces the Go/CGO bridge. It implements GAIE’s Lightweight Endpoint Picker (ext_proc) interface directly, runs the full Dynamo router in-process, and uses DYN_* environment variables in place of the eppConfig plugin and scheduling profiles. Aggregated and disaggregated routing are handled directly from the worker roles registered through Dynamo discovery. The surrounding Kubernetes topology remains unchanged. Removing the Go plugin framework and CGO boundary also reduces per-request EPP overhead.
A client request enters through a gateway, such as agentgateway, and matches an HTTPRoute backed by an InferencePool. The Gateway invokes the Dynamo EPP, which performs just the token-aware KV selection and returns the selected endpoint and routing metadata. The Gateway then forwards the request to the selected worker’s Frontend sidecar in direct mode, which sends it to the vLLM worker over the Dynamo request plane. Worker KV-cache state reaches the EPP through the Dynamo event plane, while the Dynamo operator creates the EPP and InferencePool from the DynamoGraphDeployment.
Choosing a path
The routing path depends on whether the Gateway or the Dynamo Frontend should handle the forwarding of requests to the workers, including timeouts, retries, and fallback management. Table 2 compares the Dynamo Frontend and Gateway API/EPP paths.
| Decision | Dynamo Router | GAIE / EPP | 
|---|---|---|
| Ingress owner | Dynamo Frontend Service | Gateway and HTTPRoute | 
| Worker selection | The Frontend selects and dispatches to a worker | The EPP selects an endpoint; the Gateway forwards the request | 
| Request path | Client → Frontend → worker | Client → Gateway → worker Frontend sidecar → worker | 
| Best fit | A model-specific Dynamo endpoint with the smallest serving topology | A shared Kubernetes ingress managed through Gateway API resources | 
| Additional infrastructure | None beyond the Dynamo frontend and workers | GAIE-compatible Gateway, InferencePool, EPP, and worker frontend sidecars | 
| KV-cache behavior | Dynamo KV-aware routing from worker-published cache and load state | The same Dynamo KV-aware routing at the Gateway layer | 
Both paths use worker-published KV-cache events for precise cache-aware placement. Dynamo can instead be configured to predict KV-cache state from where it sent each request. Prediction cannot see evictions, so the router’s view can drift from what each worker actually holds, and routing quality can degrade, especially under memory pressure. The AICR configuration in this post enables live events, so both paths route using the workers’ reported KV-cache state.
How the AICR recipe flow works
AICR separates runtime setup from application deployment. First, it captures the existing Kubernetes cluster and generates a matching Dynamo recipe. The runtime bundle is then rendered, deployed, and validated before the application’s DynamoGraphDeployment is installed and its inference endpoints are tested.
Step 1: Snapshot the cluster
The snapshot captures the cluster state that AICR uses for recipe selection and validation:
aicr snapshot \
  --namespace aicr-validation \
  --output snapshot.yaml
When no placement flags are specified, AICR automatically targets nodes labeled nvidia.com/gpu.present=true and tolerates GPU-node taints. The --node-selector and --toleration flags provide more specific placement when required by the cluster.
Step 2: Generate the Dynamo inference recipe
AICR uses the snapshot to identify the Kubernetes distribution, GPU accelerator, and GPU-node operating system. The command specifies the workload intent and platform:
aicr recipe \
  --snapshot snapshot.yaml \
  --intent inference \
  --platform dynamo \
  --output recipe.yaml
The generated recipe records pinned component versions, environment-specific configuration, compatibility constraints, and validation checks. For the Amazon EKS Dynamo inference recipe for NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 and NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems, AICR v1.0.0 selects the following Helm chart versions:
| Component | Version | 
|---|---|
| NVIDIA GPU Operator | v26.7.1 | 
| Node Feature Discovery | 0.19.0 | 
| cert-manager | v1.20.2 | 
| AWS EBS CSI Driver | 2.59.0 | 
| AWS EFA | v0.5.29 | 
| NVSentinel | v1.25.0 | 
| NodeWright Operator | v0.19.0 | 
| NVIDIA DRA GPU Driver | 0.5.0 | 
| KAI Scheduler | v0.16.9 | 
| Grove | v0.1.0-alpha.13 | 
| Dynamo Platform | 1.4.2 | 
| Agent Gateway | v1.5.0 | 
| Agent Gateway CRDs | v1.5.0 | 
| Kube Prometheus Stack | 84.4.0 | 
| Prometheus Operator CRDs | 28.0.1 | 
| Prometheus Adapter | 5.3.0 | 
| Kubernetes Ephemeral Storage Metrics | 1.19.2 | 
The AICR team tested these component versions together on the specified platforms and hardware. The following validation steps verify that the cluster meets the selected recipe’s requirements.
Optional offline check
Recipe selection already uses the cluster facts in snapshot.yaml, so validating the generated recipe against that same snapshot adds little. Offline validation is useful when testing a recipe against a different captured cluster snapshot without contacting Kubernetes. It evaluates declarative constraints, while behavioral checks are reported as skipped.
aicr validate \
  --recipe recipe.yaml \
  --snapshot candidate-snapshot.yaml \
  --no-cluster \
  --output dry-run.json
Step 3: Render the runtime bundle
AICR renders the recipe into deployment-ready Helm values and manifests:
aicr bundle \
  --recipe recipe.yaml \
  --accelerated-node-selector nodeGroup=gpu-worker \
  --accelerated-node-toleration dedicated=worker-workload:NoSchedule \
  --accelerated-node-toleration dedicated=worker-workload:NoExecute \
  --system-node-selector nodeGroup=system-worker \
  --system-node-toleration dedicated=system-workload:NoSchedule \
  --system-node-toleration dedicated=system-workload:NoExecute \
  --set-json agentgateway:allowedSourceRanges='["<your-cidr>"]' \
  --deployer helmfile \
  --output bundle
These placement flags reflect the test cluster used for this walkthrough. The flags can be adapted or omitted for clusters with different labels and taints. If the cluster has no default StorageClass, the command also requires --storage-class.
Step 4: Deploy the runtime
For a local deployment without an in-cluster GitOps controller, Helmfile provides a deployment option. With Helm and the helm-diff plugin available locally, the following commands inspect the AICR-generated release graph before applying it:
helmfile -f bundle/helmfile.yaml diff
helmfile -f bundle/helmfile.yaml apply
AICR encodes component dependencies in the generated Helmfile bundle. Helmfile processes those dependency tiers in order and applies independent components within a tier concurrently. Rerunning apply reconciles the installed Helm releases with the generated configuration.
If Helmfile is not available, the bundle can be regenerated with AICR’s default Helm deployer. Its generated deploy.sh script is a lightweight fallback for an interactive test drive:
aicr bundle \
  --recipe recipe.yaml \
  [... all the flags setting node selectors and tolerations ...] \
  --set-json agentgateway:allowedSourceRanges='["<your-cidr>"]' \
  --deployer helm \
  --output bundle-helm
chmod +x bundle-helm/deploy.sh
 ./bundle-helm/deploy.sh
For production, AICR also renders GitOps bundles with --deployer argocd, --deployer argocd-helm, and --deployer flux.
Step 5: Validate the installed runtime
After installation, deployment and conformance validation check the live cluster before the application workload is installed. Because no snapshot is supplied here, AICR captures the current cluster state before running the validator Jobs.
aicr validate \
  --recipe recipe.yaml \
  --node-selector nodeGroup=gpu-worker \
  --toleration dedicated=worker-workload:NoSchedule \
  --toleration dedicated=worker-workload:NoExecute \
  --phase deployment \
  --phase conformance \
  --output report.json
The application DynamoGraphDeployment is installed only after these checks pass. Performance validation runs separately because it deploys a temporary serving workload and consumes the GPUs under test.
What does AICR validation check?
AICR validates the installed runtime against the checks and constraints encoded in the selected recipe. Checks vary by recipe. For a Dynamo inference recipe, deployment and conformance validation typically cover the following:
| Area | What is checked | 
|---|---|
| Cluster baseline | Expected cluster resources, GPU allocatable capacity, and a functional nvidia-smi on accelerator nodes | 
| Platform health | GPU Operator health and version, plus Dynamo platform and operator health | 
| Accelerator access | DRA support and secure accelerator access | 
| Scheduling and scaling | Gang scheduling, pod autoscaling, cluster autoscaling, and robust controller behavior | 
| Observability | Prometheus-backed accelerator and AI service metrics | 
| Ingress | Gateway API and agentgateway readiness for Kubernetes-native ingress | 
These checks verify that the installed runtime meets the selected recipe’s requirements before an application is deployed.
AICR combines a versioned runtime configuration with checks that verify whether the cluster meets the selected recipe’s requirements.
Get Started
NVIDIA AI Cluster Runtime (AICR) and NVIDIA Dynamo are open-source components of the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform. Teams deploying Dynamo on Kubernetes can use AICR’s recipes and deployment examples to configure, deploy, and validate the infrastructure supporting their inference workload.
- Additional projects and community resources are available through the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory GitHub.
- Discussion is available in the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Slack community. The NVIDIA DSX OS AI Inference and Contributor Workshop provides hands-on experience with AICR during KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America. Registration is required, as seating is limited.
- The NVIDIA booth #170 at KubeCon features Kubernetes deep dives and live demos.

articles.title: Invictus, l'avion hypersonique européen qui vise Mach 5 pour 2032, franchit une étape clé
articles.text:
En aéronautique, rien ne se perd, tout se transforme. Dans les années 1990, l’entreprise britannique Reaction Engines Limited se met en tête de créer un avion spatial nommé Skylon. Son moteur hybride Sabre devait fonctionner comme un réacteur jusqu’à Mach 5 (cinq fois la vitesse du son), puis comme une fusée pour emmener l’appareil jusqu’en orbite.
Mais au bout de plusieurs décennies de tests, d’études et de partenariats, notamment avec le groupe BAE Systems et l’Agence spatiale européenne (ESA), le projet tombe à l’eau : faute d’avoir trouvé de nouveaux investisseurs, Reaction Engines fait faillite fin octobre 2024.
Hypersonique et réutilisable
Pourtant, l’ESA garde dans un coin de sa tête cette idée de moteur hybride, et sa pièce maîtresse (un échangeur qui refroidit en une fraction de seconde l’air brûlant aspiré par le moteur) est reprise pour un autre projet : Invictus. Cet avion hypersonique expérimental doit pouvoir voler à cinq fois la vitesse du son, décoller et se poser sur une piste classique. Le programme a franchi une étape clé, comme l’a annoncé le 23 octobre Stephan Carroll, ingénieur en chef d’Invictus chez Frazer-Nash, le cabinet d’ingénierie britannique qui pilote le projet, dans une publication sur LinkedIn.
Invictus a passé en mars 2026 sa première revue des exigences système (SRR-1, pour System Requirements Review 1). En clair, le cahier des charges de l’avion a été validé une première fois, et l’appareil, tel qu’il est conçu, doit pouvoir atteindre les objectifs fixés en vitesse, en aérodynamique et en propulsion. Frazer-Nash a attendu sept mois avant de l’annoncer, le temps de caler la suite du programme avec l’ESA et l’agence spatiale britannique (UKSA). Invictus est donc sur de bons rails, au moins jusqu’à la prochaine revue, SRR-2, prévue en octobre 2027 comme le précise le site European Spaceflight.
L’ESA a conclu un contrat à 7 millions d’euros avec Frazer-Nash en juillet 2025 pour lancer la conception de l’appareil. Invictus reprend une partie des travaux menés pour Skylon, mais il reste beaucoup à faire pour obtenir un avion hypersonique réutilisable. Frazer-Nash visait un premier vol au début de 2031. Or, David Perigo, responsable technique d’Invictus à l’ESA, évoquait en juin 2026 des essais de propulsion intégrée autour de 2032 : selon European Spaceflight, le premier vol risque donc de glisser d’au moins un an. L’appareil doit atteindre Mach 5, soit environ 6 000 km/h, deux fois et demie plus vite que le Concorde (Mach 2), en haute atmosphère.
Un secteur concurrentiel
Du côté de l’ESA, les ambitions autour d’Invictus sont nombreuses. L’agence y voit un banc d’essai pour de futurs avions spatiaux, capables de décoller d’une piste comme un avion puis de rejoindre l’orbite comme une fusée. Sarah Wilkes, directrice générale de Frazer-Nash, met aussi en avant des applications militaires. Le moteur doit fonctionner à l’hydrogène, présenté comme moins émetteur que le kérosène. Invictus reste toutefois un démonstrateur sans passagers, et aucun vol commercial à Mach 5 n’est prévu à ce stade.
Autre argument en faveur de ce projet : la concurrence progresse également. La Nasa teste en vol depuis octobre 2025 son avion supersonique silencieux X-59, un appareil bien moins rapide (autour de Mach 1,5) conçu pour atténuer le bang supersonique. La Chine, elle, progresse discrètement sur son projet d’avion spatial réutilisable, dont le renseignement militaire américain vient de publier la première image nette. Par ailleurs, Invictus n’est pas le seul projet du genre en Europe puisque Dassault Aviation travaille aussi sur son avion spatial Vortex. Lancé par une fusée, il doit revenir de l’orbite à vitesse hypersonique, puis se poser sur une piste comme un avion de ligne.

articles.title: Alerte WordPress : 22 failles corrigées, les pirates ont riposté en 9 minutes chrono
articles.text:
Des hackers cherchent à s’engouffrer dans une brèche qui peut exposer un site WordPress pendant sa mise à jour. La version 7.1.4 corrige le problème depuis le 28 octobre, mais Wordfence a déjà repéré plus de 18 500 requêtes suspectes.
Il n’a fallu que quelques heures pour que des attaquants tentent de profiter de l’une des failles corrigées par WordPress 7.1.4. Le 28 octobre dernier, Wordfence, le spécialiste de la sécurité des sites WordPress, a ainsi repéré une première requête suspecte neuf minutes seulement après l’activation de sa règle de protection, elle-même déployée environ trois heures après la publication de la mise à jour.
Le piège se cache dans les fichiers temporaires
La faille, signalée par le chercheur Umut Bayram, concerne le cœur de WordPress, des versions 4.7 à 7.1.3. Lors de certaines mises à jour utilisant un paquet complet du logiciel, les fichiers sont décompressés dans un dossier temporaire au nom prévisible, sous wp-content/upgrade. Cette copie contient un installateur auquel un visiteur peut accéder si le serveur laisse ce répertoire accessible et autorise l’exécution de PHP. Dans ces conditions, un attaquant sans compte peut parvenir à exécuter du code sur le serveur.
Les hackers doivent toutefois accéder à l’installateur temporaire avant que WordPress ne supprime les fichiers. Selon les essais rapportés par Wordfence, ils ne disposent que de quelques secondes. Ils envoient donc des requêtes à répétition dans l’espoir de surprendre un site au moment où sa mise à jour est en cours. Au total, le spécialiste de la sécurité aurait comptabilisé plus de 18 500 requêtes en 21 heures. Ce chiffre comptabilise les requêtes suspectes détectées sans permettre de savoir combien de sites ont réellement été piratés.
- moodVersion d'essai disponible
- settingsHébergé / pré-installé
- storage1 Go à 200 Go de stockage
- extensionPlugins disponibles
- format_paintThemes disponibles
- shopping_bagAdapté aux sites e-commerce
Bloquer l’accès public au dossier wp-content/upgrade ?
WordPress 7.1.4 rend notamment le nom du dossier temporaire aléatoire et renforce les protections autour de l’installation. Cette version corrige aussi des failles permettant d’injecter du code dans des pages, de divulguer des informations ou de contourner certaines permissions, pour un total de 22 vulnérabilités traitées.
Les administrateurs peuvent contrôler leur version dans Tableau de bord > Mises à jour. Des correctifs sont également proposés pour les anciennes branches jusqu’à la 4.7, mais seule la version la plus récente bénéficie d’un support actif.
Un pare-feu peut compléter la mise à jour, à condition de disposer des règles adaptées et d’être correctement configuré. Chez Wordfence, le mode Extended Protection permet aussi de filtrer les accès directs aux fichiers PHP. Enfin, les administrateurs peuvent également demander à leur hébergeur de bloquer l’accès public au dossier wp-content/upgrade. Au jeu du chat et de la souris, qui sera le plus rapide ?
Sources : WordPress et Wordfence via Cybersecuritynews

articles.title: People are taking an unapproved weight-loss drug. AI found something surprising
articles.text:
People are taking an unapproved weight-loss drug. AI found something surprising
- Date:
- October 21, 2026
- Source:
- University of Pennsylvania School of Engineering and Applied Science
- Summary:
- Researchers analyzing nearly 150,000 Reddit posts uncovered unexpected symptom reports linked by users to unapproved versions of retatrutide, including increased appetite, sleep disturbances, and elevated heart rates. The findings differ from clinical trial results and highlight how AI could help identify potential drug safety signals that warrant further investigation.
- Share:
An experimental weight-loss drug that has not yet received regulatory approval is already attracting users willing to obtain unapproved versions online. Now, scientists are using artificial intelligence to investigate their experiences, uncovering unexpected symptom reports that differ from those documented in clinical trials.
The drug, retatrutide, belongs to a new generation of GLP-1 medications designed to help regulate appetite and body weight. Although it remains under investigation and is not approved for use, people are purchasing unapproved formulations that are not intended for human consumption and discussing their experiences on internet forums.
Researchers at the University of Pennsylvania analyzed nearly 150,000 Reddit posts and comments from approximately 40,000 users to investigate these accounts. Their study, published in JAMA Network Open, provides the first systematic examination of potential side effects reported by people claiming to use unapproved retatrutide.
One finding stood out. Among users whose reported symptoms could be classified, increased appetite was the most common complaint. That was particularly unexpected because retatrutide is designed to suppress hunger, and its Phase 2 clinical trials primarily identified digestive problems as the most frequent side effects.
AI Uncovers Unexpected Weight-Loss Drug Reports
"Our goal is to identify hypotheses in online conversations that we could test. AI helps us find recurring patterns in people's self-reports, including experiences that may be missed by conventional drug-safety monitoring," says Sharath Chandra Guntuku, Research Associate Professor in Computer and Information Science (CIS), Director of Penn's Computational Social Listening Lab and senior author of the study.
However, the researchers emphasize that the findings should not be interpreted as proof of previously unknown side effects. Reddit users represent a very different population from clinical trial participants, and their accounts cannot establish whether the drug caused the symptoms they described.
There is also considerable uncertainty about what these individuals are actually taking. Products sold outside regulated medical channels may differ from the genuine experimental medication in their ingredients, purity, and dosage.
"We can't say that retatrutide is causing these symptoms, or even that Reddit users are actually taking genuine retatrutide, since the drug is not legally available, and gray market formulations vary," says Lyle Ungar, Professor in CIS and a co-author of the study.
Rather than confirming new risks, the research offers scientists an opportunity to identify questions that warrant more rigorous investigation.
"This is the first glimpse into the experiences of a population that is otherwise outside conventional drug safety monitoring because they are taking unapproved versions of a drug that has yet to finish clinical trials," says Neil Sehgal, the study's first author and a doctoral student in CIS.
How Researchers Analyzed 150,000 Reddit Posts
The project builds on previous research by the University of Pennsylvania team. In that earlier investigation, scientists used large language models (LLMs), the type of artificial intelligence that powers many modern chatbots, to examine more than 400,000 Reddit posts discussing semaglutide and tirzepatide.
That analysis revealed reports of possible side effects, including menstrual irregularities, that may not have been fully documented in clinical trials or official drug safety records.
"We wanted to apply the same methodology to gray-market retatrutide," says Sehgal.
Retatrutide is particularly interesting because it works differently from existing GLP-1 medications. Semaglutide acts on one hormone receptor involved in blood sugar control and appetite regulation, while tirzepatide targets two. Retatrutide activates three receptors, potentially producing a different combination of effects throughout the body.
To investigate what people were experiencing, the researchers used AI to examine nearly 150,000 Reddit posts and comments. They identified approximately 14,000 users who claimed to have personally taken an unapproved version of retatrutide.
The AI systems then extracted descriptions of symptoms that users associated with the medication and translated those descriptions into standardized medical terminology. This allowed researchers to compare reports even when different people used different words to describe similar experiences.
After excluding expected effects such as weight loss and reduced appetite, the team identified 7,823 users who reported at least one symptom that could be medically classified.
"A researcher might be able to examine a few thousand Reddit posts by hand, but looking at nearly 150,000 would be an enormous undertaking," says Sehgal. "AI makes it possible to analyze these conversations at scale, identifying patterns in what people are sharing that would otherwise be difficult to recognize."
A Surprising Appetite Paradox Emerges
The most striking difference involved hunger.
In retatrutide's Phase 2 clinical trials (the drug is currently in Phase 3 trials, the final step before FDA approval), participants most commonly experienced gastrointestinal complaints, including nausea. These effects are familiar concerns with medications that influence appetite and digestion.
But among Reddit users who reported taking unapproved retatrutide, the pattern looked different. Increased appetite emerged as the most frequently described classifiable symptom, despite the substantial weight-loss effects demonstrated in clinical testing.
The researchers also compared the new findings with their earlier analysis of semaglutide and tirzepatide.
Compared with those earlier Reddit reports, discussions involving unapproved retatrutide contained proportionally more mentions of appetite-related changes, sleep disturbances, increased heart rate, and muscle-related symptoms. Reports of nausea and other digestive complaints were proportionally less common.
These differences could reflect how retatrutide interacts with the body. However, they could also result from differences between the groups of people discussing the medications, their other drug use, or the contents of the unapproved products.
"Retatrutide works differently from existing GLP-1 drugs, so it's possible that its effects on the body are different, too," says Jena Shaw Tronieri, Senior Research Investigator at Penn's Center for Weight and Eating Disorders and a co-author of the study.
"But the people discussing it on Reddit also may be different," she notes. "Users willing to obtain an unapproved medication on the gray market likely differ from other clinical populations. Some may be taking multiple experimental peptides, and we can't verify exactly what they're taking. We need more research to understand what, if anything, these differences in self-reported symptoms mean."
Can AI Detect Drug Safety Concerns Earlier?
Beyond the findings about retatrutide, the study demonstrates how AI could potentially improve the early detection of drug safety concerns.
Traditional monitoring systems depend heavily on clinical trials, reports submitted to regulators, and information collected by healthcare professionals. People obtaining experimental medications through unapproved channels may not be represented in those systems.
Social media offers another source of information, allowing researchers to identify recurring experiences that might otherwise escape attention. However, these reports must be independently investigated before they can be considered reliable evidence of a drug-related problem.
The Penn team has already seen an example of how this approach can help guide further research.
In their previous investigation of semaglutide and tirzepatide, researchers identified online reports of menstrual irregularities. Those findings subsequently encouraged another scientific team to examine similar symptoms using the FDA's database of reported adverse drug events.
The follow-up study, published in Obstetrics & Gynecology, also detected disproportionate reports of certain menstrual changes. Although those findings did not establish causation, they provided additional reasons to investigate the potential connection.
The researchers hope their retatrutide findings will lead to similar independent studies, particularly as the drug advances through clinical development.
"That's what we hope will happen with this study," says Sehgal. "Other researchers can take what we find on Reddit and look for the same patterns in other datasets, using entirely different methods. Whether those signals hold up or not, the goal is to build a better understanding of what people are actually experiencing."
The research was conducted through the University of Pennsylvania's School of Engineering and Applied Science and Perelman School of Medicine. Benjamin Rader of Boston Children's Hospital also contributed as a co-author. Funding was provided in part by the University of Pennsylvania's Penn Medical Communication Research Institute. Tronieri disclosed receiving an investigator-initiated grant from Novo Nordisk on behalf of the University of Pennsylvania, along with consulting fees from Currax Pharmaceuticals, LLC. No conflicts of interest were reported by the other authors.

articles.title: Hero MotoCorp to increase EV capacity to 80,000 units per month by Q2 FY28
articles.text:
Hero MotoCorp to increase EV capacity to 80,000 units per month by Q2 FY28
The automaker's electric two-wheeler capacity was at 15,000 units per month at the end of the financial year 2026. The capacity currently stands at 30,000 units.
India's largest two-wheeler maker Hero MotoCorp plans to increase the production capacity of its Vida electric two-wheeler to 45,000 units by March-end and further boost it to 80,000 units by the second quarter of FY28, according to a senior company official.
Hero MotoCorp CEO Harshavardhan Chitale said supply is a constraint, with dealer inventory of just around one day.
"Our dealer inventory continues to be low. We are working with a dealer stock of just about one day, which shows that we are still capacity constrained and there is a strong demand for our product," he said.
The automaker's electric two-wheeler capacity was at 15,000 units per month at the end of the financial year 2026. The capacity currently stands at 30,000 units.
"We have already doubled the capacity. We are well on our way to take it to 45,000 units a month in the fourth quarter. Looking at the demand, we are expanding further, which will take our capacity to over 80,000 units a month by the second quarter of FY28," he said.
The electric two-wheeler market is witnessing strong demand with penetration exceeding 20% in the scooter segment. As per the data from FADA, registration of electric two-wheelers jumped 33% in the Navratri period to 75,758 units, while the total two-wheeler registration fell almost 3% to 8.34 lakh units.
TVS Motor is the market leader, followed by Bajaj Auto, Ather Energy and Hero MotoCorp. All the top four OEMs are ramping up their capacity to meet the surge in demand.
Both TVS and Bajaj are increasing capacity to 80,000 units per month by March, while Ather is targeting around 95,000 units capacity by July-September with its new facility.
"Right now the industry as a whole is definitely capacity constrained. There is far more demand. As and when anyone brings on capacity online and if the product is good, there is an immediate bump up in share," Chitale said.
Hero MotoCorp's capacity ramp comes as the automaker looks to expand its Vida distribution. Currently, it is selling Vida at around 700 of its retail outlets.
"When we put it in the context that we have close to 8,500 points of sale, there is a lot more retail expansion that is going to come to further drive the growth," he added.

articles.title: OLED 4K, 120 Hz et Ambilight : le téléviseur Philips 55OLED801 est à 762,70 €
articles.text:
Le téléviseur OLED Philips 55OLED801 de 55 pouces est à 762,70 € (-49 %)
Avec sa dalle OLED 4K de 55 pouces et son éclairage Ambilight, le Philips 55OLED801 est proposé à 762,70 € sur Amazon par le vendeur Icoza.
Le téléviseur est vendu et expédié par Icoza sur la marketplace Amazon, avec la livraison gratuite. À 762,70 €, il coûte 736,30 € de moins que son prix de lancement de 1 499 €, soit environ 49 %. Cette comparaison prend donc pour référence le tarif de lancement du modèle.
Une dalle OLED accompagnée de l’Ambilight
Le téléviseur Philips 55OLED801/12 utilise une dalle OLED de 55 pouces, soit environ 139 cm, affichant 3 840 × 2 160 pixels. Son rafraîchissement natif atteint 120 Hz. Le traitement d’image repose sur le processeur P5 avec IA, avec notamment la prise en charge du Dolby Vision.
L’Ambilight sur trois côtés constitue sa particularité : des LED placées derrière l’écran projettent sur le mur des couleurs liées à l’image affichée. Ce dispositif ajoute ainsi un éclairage d’ambiance autour du téléviseur, sans nécessiter de bandeau lumineux supplémentaire.
Du jeu en 4K à 120 Hz et l’interface Titan OS
La connectique HDMI 2.1 permet de recevoir un signal 4K à 120 Hz depuis une source compatible. Le téléviseur dispose de quatre entrées HDMI et de deux ports USB. La barre de jeu Gamebar 2.0 donne accès aux réglages dédiés.
L’interface Titan OS propose notamment Netflix, Disney+, YouTube et Prime Video, avec les abonnements correspondants lorsqu’ils sont nécessaires. La partie sonore repose sur deux haut-parleurs totalisant 20 W, avec une compatibilité Dolby Atmos et DTS.

articles.title: Fini les allers-retours : Gemini permet enfin de modifier vos documents directement dans l'application
articles.text:
L’application Gemini intègre désormais de nouvelles fonctionnalités qui vont vous permettre d’éditer beaucoup plus facilement vos fichiers, qu’il s’agisse d’un document texte, d’une présentation ou de lignes de code. Il est désormais possible de modifier les fichiers générés directement dans l’interface de conversation de Gemini, ce qui évite de faire des allers-retours entre différents logiciels.
Nouveaux outils et formats pris en charge
Sur le chat de Gemini, vous pouvez désormais agrandir les documents en mode plein écran pour modifier plus facilement votre document, surligner du texte pour poser des questions ciblées, ou encore demander à l’intelligence artificielle de modifier le contenu ou les visuels. Dans l’exemple de la vidéo ci-dessous, Google montre qu’il devient par exemple possible de sélectionner un tableau pour que Gemini le transforme en graphique.
La prévisualisation et l’édition des fichiers PDF sont prises en charge aussi bien sur le web que sur mobile. En revanche, les autres formats comme les documents Google Docs, les feuilles de calcul Google Sheets, les présentations, les fichiers Markdown, les fichiers TXT ainsi que le code sont pour l’instant réservés à la version web.
Disponible pour tous les utilisateurs de Gemini
Ces nouveautés de Gemini sont déployées dès aujourd’hui pour tous les utilisateurs de l’application, dans toutes les langues où le service de Google est disponible. Cette évolution rapproche l’IA de Google des fonctionnalités déjà proposées par des concurrents comme Anthropic sur Claude, tout en complétant les intégrations qui existent déjà au sein des applications Google Workspace.

articles.title: When the Internet Drops Mid-Shift: Backup Connections and Failover for Small Offices - Tech Guide
articles.text:
The Critical Role of Internet Connectivity in Small Offices
In today’s fast-paced business environment, reliable internet connectivity is no longer a luxury but a fundamental necessity, especially for small offices. These businesses often depend heavily on cloud-based applications, VoIP phone systems, video conferencing, and real-time communication tools that require continuous internet access to function effectively. When the internet unexpectedly drops mid-shift, it can disrupt workflows, delay customer service, and ultimately impact revenue and reputation.
Recent studies reveal that 35% of small businesses experience internet outages several times a year, with each outage lasting an average of four hours. This kind of downtime can lead to significant losses, not only in employee productivity but also in customer satisfaction and trust. Moreover, 60% of small businesses that suffer a major data loss or extended downtime close within six months. These statistics underscore how critical it is for small offices to prepare for unexpected internet disruptions.
Understanding Backup Connections and Failover Systems
To mitigate the risks associated with internet downtime, small offices must implement robust backup connections and failover solutions. A backup connection is a secondary internet link that automatically activates when the primary connection fails. Failover systems are designed to monitor the health of the primary connection continuously and switch to the backup without manual intervention, ensuring seamless business continuity.
For example, a local business like Lakeside Motors for BMW Vehicles understands the importance of maintaining constant communication with customers and suppliers. By having a failover system in place, they avoid potential revenue losses and maintain service quality even during internet outages. This proactive approach ensures that critical operations such as order processing, customer support, and internal communications remain uninterrupted.
Failover technology can be as simple as a router configured to switch to a cellular network when the primary broadband fails, or as advanced as multi-WAN load balancing systems that distribute traffic across multiple connections for both redundancy and performance improvements.
Types of Backup Internet Connections
Small offices have several viable options when it comes to backup internet connections, each with its own advantages and limitations:
– DSL or Cable as Primary, Cellular as Backup: Many small businesses use a fixed broadband connection as their primary internet source and a cellular connection via 4G or 5G as backup. Cellular failover is popular due to its ease of setup, mobility, and widespread coverage. It provides an automatic switch during outages, minimizing disruption.
– Dual Broadband Connections: Some offices opt for two broadband providers, such as cable and fiber, to eliminate dependence on a single ISP. This approach lowers the risk of simultaneous outages since each provider typically uses different physical infrastructure.
– Satellite Internet: Although satellite connections have higher latency and can be affected by weather conditions, they serve as an emergency backup in remote or rural areas where terrestrial options are limited or unavailable.
– Fixed Wireless Access (FWA): This option uses radio signals to provide internet service and can be a reliable backup in areas with good line-of-sight to a wireless tower.
Each option comes with trade-offs regarding speed, reliability, latency, and cost. For instance, while cellular backup is convenient, data caps and variable speeds may limit its use during prolonged outages. Small businesses should evaluate their specific operational needs, budget constraints, and geographic location when selecting a backup solution.
The Importance of Professional IT Support
Implementing and managing backup connections and failover systems can be complex and requires technical expertise to ensure they function correctly when needed. Many small offices lack the in-house IT resources to design, configure, and maintain these solutions effectively. This is where professional IT services become invaluable.
For instance, InfoTECH for Lafayette businesses offers managed IT services tailored for businesses in Lafayette, providing continuous monitoring, rapid response to connectivity issues, and regular failover testing. Partnering with such providers ensures that failover systems are properly configured, tested regularly, and updated as technology evolves, substantially reducing the risk of unexpected downtime.
Professional IT support can also help small offices assess their network vulnerabilities, recommend the most cost-effective backup solutions, and provide training to staff on best practices during outages. This partnership enables businesses to focus on their core operations without worrying about internet reliability.
Cost Considerations and Return on Investment (ROI)
While the upfront costs of backup internet connections and failover equipment might seem significant, the return on investment (ROI) often justifies the expenditure. According to a Gartner study, the average cost of network downtime for small businesses is approximately $8,000 per hour. Avoiding even a single extended outage can save substantial amounts of money.
Additionally, uninterrupted internet service improves customer trust and satisfaction, which are critical for small businesses competing in crowded markets. Reliable connectivity also enhances employee productivity by minimizing frustration and downtime. These intangible benefits can lead to increased customer retention, positive word-of-mouth, and new business opportunities.
When calculating ROI, businesses should consider both direct costs, such as lost sales and labor, and indirect costs, including damage to brand reputation and employee morale. Investing in backup internet and failover solutions is a strategic move to protect against these risks.
Best Practices for Backup Internet and Failover Implementation
To maximize the benefits of backup connections, small offices should follow these best practices:
- Assess Bandwidth Needs: Determine the minimum bandwidth required during failover to maintain essential operations. This ensures that the backup connection can handle critical applications like VoIP calls, email, and cloud access.
- Choose Diverse Providers: Avoid using ISPs that share the same physical infrastructure to reduce the risk of simultaneous outages caused by cable cuts or local disruptions.
- Regular Testing: Schedule periodic failover tests to ensure automatic switching works correctly and that staff know how to respond during outages.
- Monitor Network Health: Use monitoring tools that provide real-time alerts on connection status, enabling proactive troubleshooting before issues escalate.
- Plan for Scalability: As the business grows, ensure that backup solutions can accommodate increased internet usage without compromising performance.
- Secure Failover Connections: Implement security measures such as firewalls and VPNs on backup connections to protect sensitive data during failover.
- Document Procedures: Maintain clear documentation of failover configurations and response protocols accessible to IT staff and relevant employees.
Additional Considerations for Small Offices
Beyond technology, small offices should consider the human factor in managing internet disruptions. Training employees on contingency plans during outages can reduce panic and confusion. For example, staff can be instructed on how to switch to alternative communication channels or access offline resources.
Moreover, reviewing and updating internet service contracts can sometimes provide options for service level agreements (SLAs) that guarantee minimum uptime or faster repair times. Engaging with ISPs about these options can provide additional peace of mind.
Finally, staying informed about emerging technologies such as 5G and software-defined WAN (SD-WAN) can offer new opportunities for more resilient and flexible network architectures in the near future.
Conclusion
Internet outages can severely disrupt small office operations, but with strategic planning and the right technology, businesses can safeguard against downtime. Backup internet connections and failover systems provide a safety net that keeps workflows running smoothly, even when the unexpected occurs.
By understanding available options, leveraging professional IT support, and investing wisely, small offices can protect their productivity and reputation. In an era where connectivity is king, being prepared for internet disruptions is essential for any business aiming to thrive.
Ensuring your small office has a robust backup and failover strategy is not just a technical decision-it’s a business imperative that supports growth, customer satisfaction, and long-term success.

articles.title: Pedro, conductor de autobuses: "¿Quién decidió que el asiento del autobús debía parecer un fondo de pantalla de los años ochenta?"
articles.text:
Los asientos de autobuses y autocares tienen una estética muy reconocible, con formas geométricas imposibles y colores chillones que parecen sacados de un catálogo de los años ochenta. Pedro, conductor de autobuses, se hace la pregunta con humor en un Reel de Instagram: “¿Quién decidió que el asiento del autobús debía parecer un fondo de pantalla de los años ochenta?”. Y es que, aunque parezca un capricho de diseño anticuado, la respuesta que da él mismo tiene mucho que ver con el mantenimiento.
Una tela pensada para durar. El vídeo lo ha compartido la empresa Autocares Grupo Benidorm en su cuenta de Instagram, y en él Pedro promete explicar por qué “estos estampados llamativos llevan décadas apareciendo en el transporte”. De hecho, la moquette, que es la tela de este tipo de asientos, llegó al transporte público londinense en los años veinte, según la historia que recoge el Museo del Transporte de Londres, y se eligió en parte porque es un tejido duro y duradero.
Mucho uso y normas de seguridad. Pero la tapicería de un autocar no es una tela cualquiera, ya que tiene que aguantar el paso constante de pasajeros que se sientan y apoyan mochilas o maletas, además de roces continuos y limpiezas frecuentes. “La tapicería del autobús debe soportar mucho uso, roces constantes, limpieza frecuente y unas exigencias de seguridad específicas. Por eso se utilizan tejidos de transporte diseñados para durar”, explica Pedro.
Entre esas exigencias está el comportamiento frente al fuego, que regula el Reglamento n.º 118 de la Comisión Económica de las Naciones Unidas para Europa (CEPE) para autobuses interurbanos y autocares, y que se aplica a los materiales del habitáculo, tapicería de los asientos incluida.
El estampado hace de camuflaje. Aun así, por muy resistente que sea el material, en un transporte que utiliza tanta gente el desgaste y las manchas acaban apareciendo, y ahí es donde entran los famosos dibujos. Las formas geométricas, las rayas superpuestas y los contrastes de color sirven para disimular la suciedad y el deterioro, algo que también señala el mismo museo londinense. Un tejido liso o de un solo color, en cambio, dejaría a la vista cualquier roce o mancha de líquido. Vamos, que el estampado está ahí para que no se note lo que el asiento ha vivido.
Identidad para el interior. Pedro añade otra función, ya que según él “los colores y patrones ayudan a dar identidad al interior y a mantener una apariencia uniforme durante años de servicio”. Y lo resume con una frase que lo engloba todo: “Ese estampado que parece aleatorio combina diseño, persistencia y mantenimiento”.
De esta manera, esas formas aparentemente aleatorias absorben a la vista las imperfecciones y permiten que el interior del vehículo mantenga un aspecto cuidado y limpio durante años de servicio continuado, o sea que esa estética que recuerda a los ochenta tiene una razón muy práctica detrás.

articles.title: Desarrollan un robot inspirado en insectos que promete revolucionar la exploración en entornos extremos
articles.text:
Un equipo de la Universidad de California, Los Ángeles, (UCLA) y la Universidad de California en Davis (UC Davis) desarrolló un diminuto robot volador inspirado en insectos que puede recuperar el vuelo después de colisiones y soportar compresiones extremas. El dispositivo, presentado en la revista Science Robotics, busca operar en espacios estrechos o zonas inaccesibles para otros robots y para las personas, según TechXplore, el portal especializado en ciencia y tecnología.
El prototipo genera una fuerza ascendente equivalente a tres veces su propio peso, despega sin asistencia y asciende a una velocidad promedio de 40 centímetro por segundo. También pudo volver a volar después de recibir un golpe con un matamoscas o de ser aplastado por cargas de unas 11.000 veces su peso.
Diseño íntegramente hecho con polímeros
El robot pesa apenas 185 miligramos —menos de un quinto de gramo— y está construido por completo con polímeros, materiales formados por largas cadenas de moléculas enlazadas. Combina un músculo blando activado por electricidad con alas flexibles de forma cónica.
Qibing Pei, profesor de los departamentos de Ciencia e Ingeniería de Materiales e Ingeniería Mecánica y Aeroespacial de la UCLA y autor principal del estudio, explicó que su laboratorio trabaja desde hace años en robótica blanda y tomó como referencia la forma en que los insectos sobreviven a choques y otras perturbaciones físicas. “Muchos robots del tamaño de un insecto dependen de componentes frágiles, lo que dificulta su funcionamiento fuera del laboratorio. Vimos la oportunidad de utilizar materiales poliméricos sensibles a la electricidad para crear un diseño más simple y resistente”.
Yuan Zhu, investigador posdoctoral del departamento de Ciencia e Ingeniería de Materiales, también de la UCLA, y primer autor del trabajo, detalló que el músculo de las alas es una película delgada de un polímero ferroeléctrico relajador, un material plástico que reacciona y se deforma al recibir una carga eléctrica. “La expansión del material inducida por el campo eléctrico, conocida técnicamente como electrostricción, es enorme y reversible. Podemos aprovechar el movimiento de la película para generar potentes aleteos con una respuesta muy rápida”.
El polímero se dobla con rapidez y mueve las alas directamente, sin requerir un sistema mecánico de transmisión independiente. Hanxiang Wu, investigador posdoctoral de UCLA y el también primer autor, señaló que esa solución simplifica la estructura del vehículo aéreo.
La geometría aerodinámicamente asimétrica y las deformaciones parciales durante cada aleteo permiten generar sustentación. Al mismo tiempo, la flexibilidad de las alas hace que se deformen al entrar en contacto con una superficie sin doblarse de manera permanente, una propiedad que las protege frente a los impactos.
Tecnología y aplicaciones más allá del laboratorio
Los investigadores conectaron el primer prototipo a una fuente eléctrica externa mediante cables. Luego evaluaron su capacidad para despegar, resistir compresiones con cargas pesadas, reiniciar el vuelo tras colisiones y mantener una velocidad media de ascenso.
Wenzhong Yan, investigador del departamento de Ingeniería Mecánica y Aeroespacial de la UC Davis, resumió: “Nuestro robot generó una sustentación de hasta tres veces su propio peso y pudo volver a volar después de ser golpeado o aplastado”.
Para Yan, el comportamiento del aparato expresa una forma de “inteligencia mecánica”: “Respuestas útiles incorporadas en los materiales y la estructura, como adaptar pasivamente la morfología de las alas para generar sustentación y deformarse durante el contacto para luego recuperarse. Ese enfoque podría ayudar a los diminutos robots voladores a resistir las interacciones impredecibles que encontrarían fuera del laboratorio”.
Para funcionar de forma autónoma, una versión futura del robot deberá incorporar una fuente de energía propia, componentes de control de vuelo y sensores. El equipo también planea mejorar los giros y aterrizajes, y aumentar la capacidad de carga, con miras a probar el robot en aplicaciones concretas como el monitoreo ambiental, la polinización agrícola y las operaciones de búsqueda y rescate en zonas de difícil acceso.

articles.title: Steve Huffman, CEO de Reddit dice adiós a la web abierta:"El modo de IA no genera tráfico. Ni para nosotros ni para nadie"
articles.text:
Hubo un tiempo en el que escribías una duda en Google, añadías la etiqueta "reddit" al final y casi siempre aparecía un hilo con la respuesta a tu problema explicada por alguien que ya había pasado por lo mismo y lo había solucionado. El CEO de Reddit ha anunciado que ese atajo va a estar cerrado a partir de ahora. Si quieres obtener información de Reddit tendrás que entrar e iniciar sesión con tu usuario.
El origen del problema es un viejo conocido: los resúmenes con IA de Google. El buscador ya no envía a los usuarios a los hilos como hacía antes, así que Reddit ha decidido poner una puerta a su red social. Su consejero delegado, Steve Huffman, contaba en una entrevista para Axios que se resistió a dar el paso por su fe en la web abierta. "Para mí, cuya vida ha estado marcada por internet, supone un gran cambio. Pero he llegado a la conclusión de que esta es la decisión correcta para nuestra plataforma y para nuestro negocio", señalaba Huffman en un comunicado publicado en Reddit.
Un millón de visitas menos cada semana. El pasado jueves, Reddit presentó sus resultados del tercer trimestre y soltó la advertencia en su carta a los accionistas. En octubre, el tráfico desde buscadores ha caído "en más de un millón de referencias de media por semana". Si el ritmo de caída se prolonga en el tiempo, los usuarios diarios podrían bajar en un porcentaje de dos dígitos en el cuarto trimestre.
Los usuarios activos diarios de la red social en EEUU pasaron de 53,2 millones en el segundo trimestre a 50,7 millones en el tercero, un 2% menos que hace un año. Es el primer descenso desde su salida a bolsa y, como, recogía Reuters, desde que se conocieron estos datos, las acciones de Reddit se hundieron un 18% tras el cierre.
Google rastrea igual, pero no manda visitas. Huffman puso nombre y apellidos al problema en su llamada con los inversores. "Google nos sigue rastreando con la misma intensidad de siempre, así que la demanda tampoco ha cambiado desde su punto de vista". Y añadió que "la realidad es que el modo de IA no genera tráfico, ni para nosotros ni para nadie, que yo sepa".
Para Huffman, el principal cambio es el funcionamiento del buscador en sí mismo. "Antes generaba tráfico, ahora ya no", recogió The Verge. Y matizó que el contenido de Reddit sigue siendo muy buscado. "La gente sigue queriendo usar Reddit. Simplemente indica que Google ya no los dirige a Reddit como antes", resaltando que el problema no estaba en el contenido de sus hilos, sino en la forma en la que los usuarios accedían a él. Un estudio de Pew Research Centre sobre los hábitos de clic de los usuarios en los resúmenes de IA de Google confirman las palabras de Huffman: con el resumen de IA, se hace clic en la fuente de la información solo en el 8% de las visitas. Con la búsqueda tradicional de Google en el 15%.
La misma película que viven los medios. El escenario que está enfrentando Reddit no es nuevo. Es la misma historia que los medios editoriales sufren desde que Google implementó su Modo IA en las búsquedas. El usuario que hace una búsqueda ya no va a las fuentes de la información como antes, y menos clics significan menos anuncios vistos y, con ellos, menos ingresos. Penske Media, editora de Rolling Stone y Variety, demandó a Google por los resúmenes de IA. Google respondió que envía "miles de millones de clics" cada día a sitios web de toda la red.
Sin embargo, el caso de Reddit tiene una vuelta de tuerca adicional: Google está pagando unos 60 millones de dólares al año a Reddit por entrenar a sus modelos de IA con los hilos del foro. Es decir, la IA que se alimenta de contenido como el suyo, es la misma que ahora le está recortando las visitas y mermando sus ingresos en concepto de publicidad.
Una puerta con cuenta. La respuesta de muchos medios editoriales fue cerrar sus contenidos tras muros de pago. La de Reddit ha sido poner una puerta intermedia en forma de registro de usuario gratuito. Los usuarios con sesión y los de la app ya suponen más del 80% de la monetización. Pero 76,8 millones de los 130,3 millones de usuarios diarios del trimestre no habían iniciado sesión.
Huffman defendió el cambio con un argumento de negocio: "cuando los usuarios inician sesión, pasan más tiempo en Reddit, y así podemos conocer mejor sus intereses y, por lo tanto, segmentar mejor los anuncios", aseguró a Axios. Las pruebas para el nuevo sistema de uso con registro arrancarán este trimestre en mercados fuera de EEUU. En su comunicado en Reddit, Huffman recuerda que "prácticamente todas las grandes plataformas basadas en publicidad han pasado por esta transición". Su meta a cinco años, según dijo Huffman, es que Reddit sea "más Reddit".
