articles.title: Windows 11: So räumst du dein Rechtsklickmenü endlich auf
articles.text:
Windows 11: So räumst du dein Rechtsklickmenü endlich auf
Da Microsoft die Funktion schrittweise ausrollt, ist sie nach der Installation des optionalen Updates KB5127936 vom Oktober möglicherweise nicht sofort sichtbar. Sie lässt sich mithilfe des kostenlosen Open-Source-Werkzeugs „ViVeTool“ aber in wenigen Minuten aktivieren – und zwar so.
So bekommt ihr das kostenlose Open-Source-Werkzeug „ViVeTool“
Als erstes müsst ihr „Einstellungen“ > „Windows Update“ öffnen und auf „Nach Updates suchen“ klicken. Falls das Update KB5127936 nicht angezeigt wird, aktiviert die Option „Die neuesten Updates erhalten, sobald sie verfügbar sind“ und sucht erneut. Sobald ihr das Update KB5127936 installiert habt, startet ihr den PC neu. Führt auch den Befehl „winver“ aus, um sicherzustellen, dass ihr Build 26200.9818 oder 26300.9818 verwendet.
Dann klickt ihr im Datei-Explorer mit der rechten Maustaste auf eine beliebige Datei. Wenn ihr unten den Eintrag „Menü anpassen“ seht, habt ihr laut windowslatest.com Glück – in diesem Fall benötigt ihr ViVeTool nicht. Falls die Funktion bei euch, wie wohl bei den meisten Nutzer:innen, noch nicht vorhanden ist, müsst ihr ViVeTool von der offiziellen Github-Seite herunterladen. Entpackt die ZIP-Datei dabei so, dass sich die Datei „ViVeTool.exe“ unter „C:\ViVeTool“ befindet.
Zwei Befehle müssen ausgeführt werden
Klickt dann mit der rechten Maustaste auf die Start-Schaltfläche, öffnet das Terminal als Administrator:in und führt nacheinander die folgenden beiden Befehle aus:
cd C:\ViVeTool
vivetool /enable /id:60813048
Wenn die Meldung „Successfully set feature configuration(s)“ erscheint, könnt ihr den PC neu starten und erneut mit der rechten Maustaste auf eine Datei klicken.
Software-Nostalgie: Kennt ihr diese Programme noch?
Statt 25 Einträgen nur noch acht
Das neue Menü enthält am unteren Rand die Schaltfläche „Menü anpassen“, die direkt zu den Einstellungen unter „Personalisierung > Kontextmenü“ führt. Laut Microsoft ist für die Nutzung der Standardkonfiguration kein weiteres Handeln erforderlich. Wer dennoch das alte Menü im Stil von Windows 10 bevorzugt, kann dies weiterhin aufrufen, indem er beim Rechtsklick auf den Desktop oder eine Datei die Umschalttaste gedrückt hält.
Vor dem Update erschienen laut windowslatest.com bei einem Rechtsklick auf eine Bilddatei unterhalb der Symbole für „Ausschneiden“, „Kopieren“, „Umbenennen“, „Freigeben“ und „Löschen“ 20 weitere Einträge. Diese überladen wirkende Systematik könnt ihr dann beispielsweise so anpassen, dass das neue Standardmenü für eine solche Bilddatei nur noch acht Einträge enthält.

articles.title: Enzi’s Oji Udezue Says Africa Needs Cheaper AI
articles.text:
Africa’s ability to benefit from artificial intelligence will depend on bringing down the cost of using it, Oji Udezue, president of Enzi, told Moonshot by TechCabal in Lagos.
Udezue said reducing the cost of inference, the process through which AI models generate responses and perform tasks, was essential to making the technology affordable for businesses and individuals across the continent.
“Our goal is to make AI cheaper for Africa and America,” he said. “The future of AI really goes through inference.”
His argument shifts attention from the race to build more powerful models to the economics of putting them to work. For businesses using AI to answer customer enquiries or support employees, the expense recurs each time the system performs a task. Those costs can determine whether a promising application becomes viable for everyday use.
Udezue highlighted the gap between the cost of using AI and what many Africans earn, warning that access to a tool means little if people cannot afford to use it consistently.
The distinction matters as companies seek to integrate AI into their operations. A service affordable for occasional queries may prove too expensive when used throughout the working day or offered to thousands of customers. Lower inference costs could make those applications more commercially practical.
Affordability is one part of a wider infrastructure challenge. The World Bank’s Digital Progress and Trends Report 2025: Strengthening AI Foundations identifies connectivity, computing resources, locally relevant data and digital skills as foundations for AI adoption. Its findings underline the importance of the systems and capabilities needed to put the technology to use.
For African developers, that also means ensuring models can work in local languages and respond to the circumstances of the people using them. A cheaper service will have limited value if its answers are poorly suited to customers’ needs.
Udezue emphasised practical demonstrations as a way to show what developers could achieve. His focus was on turning improvements in the technology into tools people could afford to use.
The economic test, in his account, is whether AI becomes cheap enough to support routine work across a much wider market. More capable models may expand what the technology can do; the cost of running them will help determine who can benefit.

articles.title: Preview web apps live as your coding agent builds them with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Preview web apps live as your coding agent builds them with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime
Coding agents now build working web apps: a dashboard, a product page, a prototype that a product team wants to try. The fastest way to review that work is to open the app, use it, ask for a change, and check the result. That loop works well when the app keeps running where the agent edits it, so each change shows up in the browser within seconds. When the app must be copied out and deployed somewhere else first, every change waits for a deployment, and the review slows down to that pace.
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with your choice of agent framework and foundation model (FM). AgentCore runtime, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, runs each agent session in its own isolated microVM. With Session endpoints, you can open an app running in that session from your own browser. Session Endpoints give each session an authenticated URL that forwards each request’s HTTP method, path, query string, and body, and WebSocket connections, to the ports you allow. You can watch the page update as the agent saves each file.
In this post, you deploy a coding agent that keeps a Vite website running in its session, then open one local page with a chat on the left and the live website on the right. You ask the agent to switch the site to a dark color theme, follow its steps as they stream in, and watch the website change without a refresh. Finally, you look at what happens internally: a second port in the same session, and the requests the Session endpoint refuses.
The complete sample, including the notebook this post follows, is in the 14-remote-access folder of the agentcore-samples GitHub repo.
How Session endpoints work
Each session gets its own Session endpoint, and six details shape how you use it.
You choose which ports it reaches. You set allowedPorts when you call CreateAgentRuntime: 1–5 entries, each a single port or a range within 8000–12000, excluding the reserved platform ports. Allowing a port doesn’t start a server, so your application must listen on it, bound to 0.0.0.0.
The URL arrives with the session. The InvokeAgentRuntime response carries it in the X-Amzn-Bedrock-AgentCore-Runtime-Session-Endpoint-Url header, which SDKs that model it expose as sessionEndpointUrl.
Every request is authenticated. For a runtime that uses AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM), each HTTP request, HTTP/2 stream, and WebSocket handshake carries a Signature Version 4 (SigV4) signature. The caller also needs bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeProxy on the runtime and its runtime endpoint. For a runtime with an inbound JSON Web Token (JWT) authorizer, each request carries a bearer token instead. Knowing the URL doesn’t grant access.
The host name selects the port. Your client connects on port 443 regardless of the target port, and a prefix on the host name chooses the port inside the session:
It carries the protocols your server speaks. HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 requests, including server-sent events and gRPC, and WebSocket connections all pass through. This walkthrough uses HTTP/1.1 and WebSocket.
It’s scoped to one session. The URL needs credentials on every request and lasts only as long as the session, so use it to build, test, and review what your agent produces. To serve an app to your users, deploy it to a hosting service such as AWS Amplify Hosting.
A browser can’t add a SigV4 signature or a bearer token to the requests a page makes on its own, so the Session endpoint client in the bedrock-agentcore SDK can open a local endpoint on your machine. Your browser opens http://localhost:8088, and the local endpoint adds your credentials to each request and WebSocket handshake before forwarding it.
A Session endpoint is different from a runtime endpoint, which AgentCore runtime already provides. Use a runtime endpoint, such as DEFAULT, to reach your agent, which controls which version of it callers will reach. InvokeAgentRuntime calls resolve through it, so you can keep development and production on different versions and promote or roll back without changing callers. Use a Session endpoint to see what your agent runs in its session, such as a web preview. It’s an authenticated URL that reaches only the ports you allow, works with whichever version the session runs, and stops working when the session ends. For complete documentation, refer to Connect to runtime sessions through a session endpoint.
Solution overview
The sample has four parts. A coding agent runs in the session on port 8080 and edits the website’s files with four tools: list, read, write, and edit. The agent starts a Vite development server on port 8090, which serves the website and pushes each saved change to the browser over its hot-reload WebSocket. On your machine, PreviewApp serves the preview page, sends your prompts to InvokeAgentRuntime, and opens a local endpoint for the website. As Figure 1 shows, the preview page loads the website from the Vite development server on port 8090 through the local endpoint and the Session endpoint, and sends your prompts through InvokeAgentRuntime to the agent on port 8080. The numbers show the order of the steps for one request.
Before step 1, PreviewApp has already called InvokeAgentRuntime once to start the session, which starts the agent and the Vite development server. PreviewApp read the Session endpoint URL from that response and opened a local endpoint for port 8090. The numbered steps in Figure 1 then follow one request for a change:
- The site pane of the preview page loads the website from the local endpoint on localhost:8088. The local endpoint adds your credentials to each request and the WebSocket handshake, and forwards them to the Session endpoint. The Session endpoint checks the signature and the port against allowedPorts, then forwards them to the Vite development server on port 8090. The page keeps the Vite hot-reload WebSocket open.
- You send a prompt from the chat pane. PreviewApp sends it to InvokeAgentRuntime as a standard AWS API call signed with your AWS credentials, and the runtime delivers it to the agent on port 8080. The agent’s steps stream back to the chat pane as it works.
- The agent calls Claude Haiku 5.5 in Amazon Bedrock to decide what to change.
- The agent reads the site’s files and saves the ones it changes. The Vite development server serves those files and watches them for changes.
- When a file is saved, Vite pushes the change over the WebSocket opened in step 1, back through the Session endpoint and the local endpoint, and the site pane updates without a refresh.
- From the notebook, PreviewApp reads the agent’s /status route on port 8081 through the same Session endpoint. Only the port changes.
Port 8080 isn’t in allowedPorts, because InvokeAgentRuntime reaches the agent without going through the Session endpoint.
Prerequisites
To follow the walkthrough, you need:
- An AWS account in an AWS Region where AgentCore runtime Session endpoints are available, with credentials configured.
- Permissions to create an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) role, upload to Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3), and create a runtime, plus bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntime and bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeProxy on that runtime and its DEFAULT runtime endpoint. For details, refer to IAM permissions for AgentCore runtime.
- Python 3.10 or later, with bedrock-agentcore 1.25.2 or later and boto3 1.43.122 or later.
- Git, to clone the sample repo, and a Jupyter environment, such as JupyterLab or Visual Studio Code with the Jupyter extension, to run the notebook.
- Access to Claude Haiku 5.5 in Amazon Bedrock. For model availability by Region, refer to Regional availability by models.
- Node.js 22 or later with npm, which the deployment script uses to package the agent and the website.
The sample deploys the agent as a zip file in Amazon S3 with direct code deployment for Node.js, so you don’t need Docker or an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. Session endpoints work with microVM runtimes, not with the Instances compute type, and Session endpoint URLs are reachable over public HTTPS. AWS PrivateLink isn’t supported for inbound connections.
Deploy the agent and its website
First, you deploy the runtime, and the configuration you choose here decides which ports the Session endpoint can reach. The deployment script bundles the agent into one file, adds the website and its dependencies for the runtime’s Linux on Arm64 system, uploads the zip to Amazon S3, and creates the runtime.
The following excerpt from deploy.py shows the two settings that matter for this post. protocolConfiguration says where the agent listens for InvokeAgentRuntime, and allowedPorts lists the ports the Session endpoint can reach: 8090 for the website and 8081 for the agent’s status route. Port 8080 isn’t in the list, because InvokeAgentRuntime reaches the agent without it. For the port and path settings, refer to Configure your agent’s serving port and invocation path.
The website’s Vite configuration makes the development server reachable from the Session endpoint. It listens on 0.0.0.0 at port 8090 and doesn’t restrict the Host header (server.allowedHosts is true), because requests arrive under a host name the runtime assigns rather than localhost. The Session endpoint authenticates every request before it reaches the server, so the server doesn’t need its own host check.
To deploy the runtime:
1. Clone the sample repo and change to the sample folder:
2. Open session_endpoints_preview.ipynb from the sample folder.
3. Run the install cell, which installs the Python dependencies.
4. Run the %run deploy.py cell. Deployment takes a few minutes, mostly waiting for the runtime to reach the READY status.
Open the preview
With the runtime ready, you start the preview. One call does three things: it starts a session (which starts the website), opens a local endpoint for port 8090, and serves the preview page on localhost:8087.
Inside start(), the calls that use Session endpoints are short. The first InvokeAgentRuntime call returns the URL in a response header, session_endpoint_url reads it, and the Session endpoint client opens a local endpoint for port 8090:
To open the preview:
- Run the cell that starts PreviewApp.
- Open the printed link, http://localhost:8087, in your browser.
The page shows the website on the right, served from port 8090 in the session, and a short guide with suggested requests on the left.
Ask the agent for a change
Now you ask for a change and watch it arrive. Each prompt goes to the agent through InvokeAgentRuntime. The agent reads the files it needs, writes the ones it changes, and reports each step as it happens. When a file is saved, the Vite development server pushes the change over its WebSocket, through the Session endpoint and the local endpoint, and the website updates in place.
To ask for a change:
- On the preview page, choose Switch this website to a dark coffee-house color theme.
- Follow the agent’s steps in the chat pane as it reads and saves files.
- Watch the site pane. It changes when the agent saves the stylesheet, and a banner names the file the change came from.
The following video shows the preview page while the agent works through several requests. Choosing a suggested request sends it to the agent, the chat pane lists each file the agent reads and saves, and the site pane on the right updates without a refresh, from the dark theme to a green Order ahead button.
The steps stream because the agent answers with server-sent events when you ask it to. You can send the same prompts from Python with app.ask, which reads the stream with iter_events from the bedrock-agentcore SDK. The open page updates in the same way:
The output of this Python script should resemble the following:
Reach a second port in the same session
The website isn’t the only server you can reach. The agent serves /status on port 8081, which lists each prompt and the files it changed. The same Session endpoint reaches it, and the only difference is the port argument.
The output of this Python script should resemble the following:
What the Session endpoint refuses
When the runtime refuses a request, it answers with an HTTP status, an empty body, and an error code in a response header, so you can tell its refusals from errors your application returns. The notebook sends a request to a port outside allowedPorts and a request without credentials, and the runtime refuses both with 403 AccessDenied.
The following table lists the refusals you’re likely to meet while you build with Session endpoints.
| Request | Response from the runtime | 
| A port that isn’t in allowedPorts | 403 AccessDenied | 
| A request without valid credentials | 403 AccessDenied or 401 AuthenticationRequired | 
| An allowed port with nothing listening on it | 502 PortNotReachable | 
| A URL whose session no longer exists | 404 SessionNotFound | 
How access to your session is protected
The runtime removes its own authentication headers before it forwards a request, so the website doesn’t receive your signature. Requests are recorded in AWS CloudTrail as InvokeAgentRuntimeProxy events, with the event source bedrock-agentcore.amazonaws.com. The local endpoint acts with your credentials, so it limits who can use it. It listens on 127.0.0.1 only, answers only requests addressed to its own local address, and refuses WebSocket connections opened by pages from other origins. Run the local endpoint only while you use the preview. For more information, see Log session endpoint requests in CloudTrail.
The access controls don’t separate the website from the agent. Both run in the same session, so give the execution role only the permissions the agent needs. If the runtime replaces the session’s compute, open connections close, and the agent’s edits might not survive unless the session uses persistent storage. Refer to File system configurations for AgentCore runtime if you need the files to outlast the compute.
The agent’s file tools resolve every path inside the site folder and refuse paths outside it, so a prompt can’t make the agent change other files in the session. If other people can send prompts to your coding agent, consider Amazon Bedrock Guardrails to filter harmful prompts and responses, and review the agent’s changes before you publish them.
Clean up
To avoid ongoing charges, stop the preview and delete the resources the sample created. The website the agent edited lives in the session, so it goes with the session.
To clean up:
1. Run the stop cell, and press Enter when the notebook asks. This stops the preview page, the local endpoint, and the session.
2. Run the %run cleanup.py cell, which deletes the runtime, the uploaded code, and the IAM role.
Conclusion
Session endpoints give you authenticated access to the applications in an AgentCore runtime session from your own tools over HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and WebSocket, on the ports you allow. In this post, you deployed a coding agent with a Vite website in its session, opened the live website in your browser through a local endpoint, asked the agent for a dark theme, and watched the change arrive as the agent saved the file. You also reached a second port in the same session and confirmed what the Session endpoint refuses.
To go further, run the notebook with your own site in the site folder, or change the agent’s tools to match how your coding agent works. For the full set of options, including port ranges, OAuth, HTTP/2, and gRPC, refer to Connect to runtime sessions through a session endpoint.
To change the port or path that InvokeAgentRuntime uses in your own agent, refer to Configure your agent’s serving port and invocation path. If your agent also needs to run build or test commands in the same session, refer to Execute shell commands in AgentCore runtime sessions. To deploy your own Node.js agent from a zip file the way this sample does, refer to Direct code deployment for Node.js. For everything else the service offers, start with Host agent or tools with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime, and find more examples in the agentcore-samples GitHub repo.

articles.title: Hackers steal $6.3 billion from Binance in record crypto heist
articles.text:
Binance has suspended all withdrawals after the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange fell victim to what appears to be the biggest heist in history.
The exchange put the “estimated total impact” of the hack at about $6.3 billion and said around $3 billion of affected assets, mainly stablecoins that act as cash for the crypto market, had been frozen.
But analysts at Elliptic said the attacker had changed about $3.3 billion into digital assets that could not be frozen and was working to cash those out as traditional currency.
An “initial investigation” suggested hackers had been able to compromise an engineer’s laptop and withdraw funds from the platform, Binance said, adding on Friday morning that further investigation “has uncovered additional points of breach.” The company is working with law enforcement.
Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs linked the hack with a North Korean unit known as TraderTraitor, saying that the sums involved would make it “the largest crypto theft on record.” Last year, North Korean hackers stole crypto worth $1.5 billion in an attack on exchange Bybit.
Peter Ward, of the Sejong Institute in Seoul, said North Korea had considerable expertise and offered “near-total protection to its hackers.”
“Things may get a lot worse going forward,” he said.
Binance said on Friday that it had “already reserved over $6.34 billion of company funds to cover this incident,” with $5 billion of the funds “already held in the exact token assets that were impacted.”
The company said it was actively buying more tokens in order to cover the remaining amount. “This step can take longer because some tokens may have low liquidity,” and settlement “also takes time,” it said.
The hack is a major blow to Binance, which was co-founded in 2017 by Changpeng Zhao and holds about $140 billion of digital assets. In 2023, the company pleaded guilty to US criminal charges related to breach of anti-money laundering laws and paid a $4.3 billion fine.

articles.title: Coveo buys Y Combinator alum to bolster AI commerce search | BetaKit
articles.text:
Coveo has acquired a Y Combinator alum as it looks to improve its search and recommendation platform in the age of AI assistants.
The news: Montréal-based Coveo acquired Silicon Valley-based Anglera for an undisclosed amount, the company announced on Thursday alongside its second-quarter earnings report. Coveo CFO Karine Hamel said on the company’s earnings call that the acquisition was funded with cash on hand, and that the deal was a “modest upfront investment,” with another potential payment coming in early 2028 based on commercial performance.
Anglera’s platform extracts and manages hundreds of technical attributes from products, such as dimensions, materials, and compatibility. Coveo hopes to make those detailed product specifications more accessible through its intelligent search and recommendation platform, making it easier for AI assistants to find and compare products on behalf of consumers.
From the source: On Coveo’s earnings call, co-founder and CEO Laurent Simoneau said Anglera automates data enrichment that a lot of its customers are struggling to do manually.
“Ultimately, it creates a lot of value in the form of additional conversion, revenue per visit, margin, et cetera,” Simoneau said. “The ability to surface content to those external AI assistants in the context of commerce is a growing priority for customers in retail, especially, and we believe that this acquisition will provide a lot of value here.”
The context: Coveo’s stock trades on the Toronto Stock Exchange under the symbol $CVO. Its Q2 earnings report showed an eight-percent revenue jump compared to Q2 last year, with the company earning $40.4 million USD ($56.4 million CAD) in the fiscal period. The company also improved its net loss to $3.1 million USD, up from $4.4 million USD in the same period last year.
Coveo’s stock saw a 1.5-percent bump the morning after its earnings report, trading at $4.84 per share; still a far cry from the $8 per share it was trading at during the same time last year.
Final thought: As more consumers turn to AI assistants to help with their shopping, more companies like Coveo see value in bolstering their generative engine optimization capabilities. Coveo claims that a 30-day Anglera A/B test with an apparel retailer saw a 120-percent jump in organic landing-page traffic to product pages equipped with its extracted data, as well as a 270-percent increase in AI-referred visits, compared to a control group.
Feature image courtesy Coveo.

articles.title: Berlin’s Greentech Alliance to acquire Intermobility to connect mobility startups with investors and cities | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Greentech Alliance (GTA), a Berlin-based global connection network for sustainable technology businesses, has agreed to acquire Intermobility, a Paris-based transport and mobility network connecting more than 1,000 companies, public authorities, and ecosystem players.
The combined entity will span more than 5,000 members and partners across 25 countries on six continents. The network links climate investors, startups, corporates, and policymakers in one of Europe’s most challenging sectors to decarbonise.
“Europe does not have a mobility technology problem, it has a coordination problem. The capital, the startups and the cities are all there, but they rarely meet. Bringing Intermobility into Greentech Alliance puts the people who build, fund and buy mobility solutions in one network, and we are inviting investors and companies who want a seat at that table to join us,” said Charles Newton Price, CEO, Greentech Alliance.
The acquisition, whose financial terms were not disclosed, comes as Europe grapples with transport emissions that have remained stubbornly above 1990 levels and as startup funding continues to decline. According to the European Environment Agency, transport emissions were 25.3% above 1990 levels in 2023 and accounted for around 31% of total EU emissions.
Transport & Environment, a Brussels-based clean-transport advocacy group, estimates the sector needs €310 billion in annual investment by 2030 to meet climate targets. However, data from Via ID and Dealroom show European mobility startups closed 654 funding rounds in 2025, down from 785 the year before, raising $10.1 billion in total private funding. Greentech Alliance says the acquisition is designed to bridge this gap.
Founded in Berlin in May 2020 by Lubomila Jordanova, Simon Thies, Hannah Kromminga, and Jan-Jaap Verhoeve, Greentech Alliance is a curated global network for ventures, investors, educators and partners building what it describes as a more regenerative economy. The organisation is incorporated as both a Canadian not-for-profit and a German for-profit company.
It currently counts more than 3,000 community members and partners across six continents, including more than 700 investor members, and has facilitated more than 2,000 introductions.
Intermobility was founded in 2022 by François Hoehlinger as a European network of transport and mobility players spanning private companies and public institutions. By bringing Intermobility’s operators, cities and public authorities into the same network as GTA’s climate investors, startups, and corporates, the deal paves the way for a mobility solution to mature from pilot to scale.
For investors, GTA membership will now offer curated access to mobility ventures from both communities, alongside introductions to co-investors, corporates and public buyers. For companies. It opens direct channels to customers, pilots and capital across Europe and beyond.
The two organisations will also explore joint ventures and financing projects, including work linked to GTA’s Climate Zero programmes, subject to separate approval. Hoehlinger will join GTA’s board to help shape the Alliance’s direction as it scales internationally.
“Mobility only changes when founders, investors, operators and public authorities move together. Intermobility built that table in Europe. Greentech Alliance gives it international reach and access to capital, while keeping a grounded European perspective at its heart,” said Hoehlinger, founder, Intermobility.
Since its inception, GTA has successfully connected members on its network and with the acquisition of Intermobility, it has an opportunity to move beyond connection. Using its proven model of trusted introductions and curated membership, the alliance will aim to bridge the gap between climate solutions and funding shortfall.

articles.title: Fresh WordPress Vulnerability in Attackers’ Crosshairs
articles.text:
Threat actors started exploiting a new high-severity WordPress vulnerability within hours of patches rolling out, Defiant warns.
Patched on October 28 in WordPress 7.1.4, the security defect impacts the WordPress update process and can be exploited for remote code execution.
According to Defiant, it is a race condition in WordPress’s Core update process that can be exploited without authentication. The attack complexity, however, is high. No CVE identifier has been assigned to the vulnerability yet.
The weakness stems from predictable, web-accessible staging paths during the upgrades. New files are unpacked into a predictable directory that is accessible from the web on many servers.
“The attacker needs a full-package update containing the installer files, public web and PHP access to the staging tree, a predictable or discovered staging path, and enough time to complete the attack before WordPress cleans up the temporary files,” Defiant explains.
According to the web security firm, threat actors are already attempting to exploit the vulnerability, polling the vulnerable paths repeatedly in their attempts to hit the seconds-long exploitability window.
While an attacker does not need an account on the site to exploit the flaw, they do need “to hit a very narrow window while WordPress is unpacking a complete Core update,” Defiant says.
To address the security bug, WordPress now randomizes the staging directory, adds an index guard, and prevents the unsafe promotion of staged configuration data.
“Wordfence telemetry shows that threat actors are already actively attempting to exploit the vulnerability. The first match for our new firewall rule arrived nine minutes after deployment. During the first 21 hours, we recorded more than 18,500 requests targeting staged setup-config.php installer paths,” Defiant says.
Wordfence has not reported successful compromises.
Fixes for the vulnerability were included in WordPress 7.1.4 and backported to branches through WordPress 4.7.
WordPress 7.1.4 includes patches for 22 security defects, including several XSS flaws, interactivity API issues, an unauthenticated information disclosure bug, and an authorization weakness, and also updates the bundled root certificates to reflect the recent eMudhra revocation.

articles.title: North Korean hackers blamed for stealing record $6.3B in Binance breach | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Hackers working for the North Korean regime have been blamed for a record cryptocurrency heist following a cyberattack at crypto exchange Binance. The hackers stole at least $6.3 billion in crypto from the company’s wallets, though about half of that amount was frozen as the stolen crypto traveled across various blockchains, according to security researchers.
The breach is by far the largest known theft of crypto in history, though the incident has not been confirmed yet to be resolved, and the amount of crypto stolen may change.
In a post on X, Binance said its initial investigation showed that the hackers broke into the company’s network after targeting a “compromised” Binance engineer’s laptop, which “allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions.”
Binance said it has seen no evidence of a leak of its private keys, which would grant the hacker near-unfettered control over the company’s stores of crypto.
The crypto exchange — the world’s largest — said it has now suspended all deposits and withdrawals while its investigation into the breach continues. TechCrunch reported on Thursday that the exchange had paused withdrawals across some of its blockchains.
Binance said “user funds are safe,” but did not immediately provide proof of this claim. The company said it will “publish an updated proof of reserves once the remediation is complete.”
Spokesperson Andie Cooper said in a statement shared with TechCrunch on Friday that some $3 billion has been frozen by industry partners. The spokesperson said Binance has “begun recovering affected assets for users and continues to work with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace, freeze and recover additional funds.”
It’s unclear how the hack went down or under what circumstances the employee’s laptop was compromised, but it’s not uncommon for security incidents to stem from the use of compromised software on employee devices.
Software is generally built from many components, including open source projects, which hackers regularly target, compromise and modify in order to steal data from devices that the affected software is installed on. Other times, malware bundled with regular-looking apps and games can allow hackers to steal usernames, passwords, and session tokens from infected computers, which may let them log in as if they were a legitimate employee.
Binance will face questions about why the company’s security allowed a single employee’s laptop to access systems capable of controlling billions of dollars in funds.
Spokespeople for Binance did not respond to an email with questions about the breach. TechCrunch has also asked the company who, if anyone, performed a security audit of Binance’s network and systems prior to the hack. Companies regularly ask third-party companies to stress-test their security to identify weaknesses that could be exploited by attackers, but it’s unclear if Binance sought such a review.
Security researchers at TRM Labs, a blockchain intelligence and forensic company, attributed the breach to North Korean hackers, and called it the “largest hack in history.”
Researchers describe the network of hackers, known in the cybersecurity industry as TraderTraitor, as a North Korean cell focused almost exclusively on stealing crypto from large companies and exchanges. This group was also blamed for the now-second-largest heist on record, a $1.4 billion theft from crypto exchange Bybit in 2025.
According to TRM, the theft of Binance’s billions in crypto took about 20 minutes.
Blockchain security firm Elliptic also attributed the Binance theft to North Korean hackers. Elliptic said some of the stolen funds ended up in the same wallet that was used in a previous cyberattack on crypto exchange Bitget earlier this year, in which hackers stole $351 million.
The U.S. government and its allies have long warned about the threat from North Korea, which remains cut off from the U.S. and the global financial system for its ongoing development of its nuclear weapons program. Researchers say the breakaway country’s sole motivations are to steal as much crypto as possible in order to continue developing its sanctioned weapons of mass destruction.
Updated with statement from Binance.

articles.title: Confira o Olhar Digital News na íntegra (30/10/2026)
articles.text:
Veja os destaques do Olhar Digital News desta sexta-feira (30/10).
Justiça manda Meta apagar posts que incentivam demissões por escolhas políticas
A Justiça do Trabalho determinou que a Meta remova publicações que incentivam empresários a vigiar, expor e demitir funcionários por suas escolhas políticas. A decisão também obriga a empresa a exibir avisos contra a discriminação por convicção política e o assédio eleitoral no trabalho no Instagram, Threads e Facebook. A Meta terá 24 horas para excluir os conteúdos e deverá manter os avisos nas três plataformas durante cinco dias consecutivos.
Avião espacial secreto da China é flagrado acoplado a satélite misterioso
Uma imagem divulgada pela Agência de Inteligência de Defesa dos Estados Unidos revela detalhes inéditos do avião espacial chinês Shenlong. O registro mostra a nave acoplada a outro satélite em órbita, com as portas do compartimento de carga abertas. A imagem foi feita pelo satélite WorldView 3. Com resolução de 4,5 centímetros por pixel, o registro integra um relatório tornado público recentemente pelas autoridades dos EUA e que aborda a dimensão e o alcance das ameaças espaciais de países rivais.
Após ataque hacker histórico, Binance garante que investimentos de brasileiros estão seguros
A corretora de criptomoedas Binance afirmou nesta sexta-feira (30) que os investimentos de clientes brasileiros permanecem seguros após um ataque hacker que resultou no roubo de US$ 6,3 bilhões (cerca de R$ 34 bilhões) em ativos digitais da plataforma. Segundo a empresa, o dinheiro dos clientes brasileiros é armazenado em cold wallets (carteiras frias), que mantêm as chaves de acesso desconectadas da internet.
O desafio de trazer amostras de Marte para a Terra
Amostras coletadas pelo rover Perseverance estão armazenadas em tubos na superfície de Marte. Trazê-las de volta à Terra, porém, envolve desafios tecnológicos, custos elevados e protocolos rigorosos para evitar a contaminação do material. Enquanto os Estados Unidos reavaliam seus planos, a China desenvolve a missão Tianwen-3, que tem como objetivo trazer material marciano à Terra até 2031. Se os cronogramas forem cumpridos, o país poderá trazer material de Marte antes da missão norte-americana.
Alessandro Di Lorenzo é editor do Olhar Digital e formado em jornalismo pela Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul (UFRGS).

articles.title: Hollywood dice adiós a Patrick Stewart: las despedidas de Ian McKellen, Hugh Jackman y más
articles.text:
El pasado jueves 29 de noviembre nos enterábamos de la triste noticia de la muerte de Patrick Stewart. El legendario actor de sagas como Star Trek o X-Men fallecía a los 86 años tras una breve batalla contra el Alzheimer y la demencia. Por supuesto, los mensajes de despedida tanto de sus fans como de personas destacadas de la industria no se han hecho esperar.
Probablemente la despedida a Patrick Stewart que más interés generaba era la de su gran amigo Sir Ian McKellen. El actor de Magneto emitió a través de redes sociales un comunicado recordando a su compañero, el Profesor X. "Por encima de todo, lo que definía a Patrick era haber nacido y crecido en Yorkshire, ese orgulloso condado del norte de Inglaterra al que amó hasta el final", comienza el escrito.
"Se notaba en su acento y en la severa honestidad con la que te decía lo que pensaba y sentía. Los yorkshireños no toleran las medias verdades ni eludir los temas importantes. Llevaba el corazón en la mano, lo que lo convertía en un hombre en el que se podía confiar, a quien admirar y, en mi caso, amar", prosigue.
"Nos conocimos hace medio siglo, cuando éramos dos jóvenes actores ambiciosos en la Royal Shakespeare Company, aunque no participábamos en las mismas producciones. Mi primer recuerdo nítido fue unos años más tarde, cuando me lo encontré por la calle en el centro de Londres y me habló de una oferta para asumir un papel protagonista en Star Trek. «Pero, Patrick, piensa en tu carrera teatral en el Reino Unido. ¿De verdad quieres arriesgarte a perderte en Hollywood durante años y años?»", rememora Ian McKellen sobre Patrick Stewart.
"Pues bien, asumió el riesgo. Y, por suerte para todos nosotros, lo hizo no solo por sus devotos trekkies, sino también por el público del cine y del teatro, que se maravilló de cómo aprovechó su fama internacional para protagonizar una serie de éxitos cinematográficos (como X-Men, por supuesto) y grandes obras clásicas de Shakespeare, Ibsen, Arthur Miller, Peter Shaffer, Pinter y Beckett en Stratford-upon-Avon, en el West End londinense y en Broadway", añade.
"Estados Unidos era su hogar adoptivo, donde conoció a su adorada Sunny, que le ha cuidado en la salud y en la enfermedad, en las buenas y en las malas. Pero nunca renunció a sus orígenes: y el logro del que más se enorgullecía este actor —el más respetado y querido de su generación a ambos lados del Atlántico— fue su nombramiento como rector de la Universidad de Huddersfield, en Yorkshire", afirma McKellen. "Su actuación de despedida aún está por ver en Avengers: Doomsday", sentencia.
Hollywood se despide de Patrick Stewart
Otra emotiva despedida a Patrick Stewart la firma Hugh Jackman, compañero inseparable de su Profesor X al dar vida a Lobezno en toda la saga X-Men. "Hoy hemos perdido a uno de los grandes del teatro y el cine. Y, en mi opinión, a un amigo y a un hombre extraordinario. Aprendí muchísimo de él. Te echaré de menos todos los días de mi vida", escribe en su cuenta de Instagram junto a una foto en el set de rodaje.
Hablando de X-Men, la joven Dafne Keen, estrella de la película Logan, tampoco ha tardado en mostrar su dolor y condolencias por el fallecimiento de Patrick Stewart. "Me he enterado hoy mismo del fallecimiento de Patrick, lo cual resulta curioso, como si fuera una coincidencia del destino, teniendo en cuenta que anoche, a última hora, estaba redactando un correo electrónico para enviárselo, algo que hacía tiempo que no hacía", reconoce.
"Era un hombre muy amable, auténtico, divertido, único, cariñoso y encantador. Recuerdo sus bromas interminables, su carácter bondadoso y sus coloridas gafas de lectura. Cada uno de los días que pasé trabajando a su lado fue un honor y un privilegio que aún me cuesta creer que haya tenido. Era un maestro andante de su oficio y de la vida. Uno de los más grandes de nuestra época, tanto en el escenario como en la pantalla", le celebra la actriz española.
"Siempre lo he admirado, y siempre lo haré. Como actor y como persona. Tenía una forma maravillosa de envolver en asombro, diversión y emoción cada antigua lección que impartía. Siempre recordaré su calidez y el respeto que mostraba hacia todos los que le rodeaban. Guardaré para siempre en mi corazón esos meses que pasamos juntos, y siempre pensaré en él como una parte fundamental de mi forma de ver el mundo que me rodea. Así que descansa en paz, gigante, leyenda entre los hombres. La hermosa obra, la humanidad y la bondad que dejas atrás perdurarán para siempre", concluye Keen, con una tierna imagen de los dos jugando en el set de Logan.
En lo referido a su otra gran saga, Star Trek, Patrick Stewart también ha recibido hermosas palabras tras su muerte. Entre ellas, las de William Shatner, el eterno capitán Kirk. "Qué semana tan desgarradora ha sido. Sir Patrick Stewart era un amigo, un compañero y un magnífico actor. Desde los escenarios hasta el puente de la Enterprise, aportó inteligencia, elegancia y un profundo sentido de la humanidad a todo lo que hacía. El capitán Picard representaba lo mejor de nosotros, al igual que el hombre que lo interpretaba. Sentía un gran cariño y admiración por él y por su trabajo. Mi más sentido pésame a Sunny y a su familia. Le echaremos mucho de menos", publica en su perfil de Facebook.
Alex Kurtzman, cocreador de Star Trek: Picard, escribía lo siguiente. "Es difícil, en realidad imposible, expresar lo agradecido que estoy por haber compartido esos momentos con él. Agradecido en el sentido de que es algo que «solo ocurre una vez en tu carrera». Desde nuestro primer encuentro, dejó claro que la única razón para volver a interpretar a Picard era abrir nuevos caminos. Su reto era claro: Picard tenía que ser el hombre que conocíamos y amábamos, pero también completamente diferente, al igual que lo era el propio Patrick treinta años después de haberse puesto el uniforme por última vez".
"Por encima de todo, quería estar orgulloso de la obra porque sabía que Jean-Luc Picard sería su legado. Me parte el corazón, y al mismo tiempo me llena de orgullo, saber que ese legado sigue vivo a día de hoy. Un legado que también incluye su valentía a la hora de defender abiertamente aquello en lo que creía. Legado que incluye la forma en que amaba a su mujer y cuidaba de su familia. Legado que se manifestaba de manera tan hermosa en cómo se acurrucaba junto a cualquier pitbull que veía, y en cómo estas criaturas, supuestamente temibles, simplemente le devolvían el cariño. Era mágico. Era mi amigo. Me enseñó cuál era el verdadero sentido de Star Trek. Y, al fin y al cabo, fue y siempre será mi capitán", concluye.

articles.title: South Korea clamps down on Tesla drivers for unlocking restricted full self-driving feature, $15,000 fines and prison possible sentences — suspects imported hardware from Europe and China, then traded tips on concealing activation logs
articles.text:
South Korea clamps down on Tesla drivers for unlocking restricted full self-driving feature, $15,000 fines and prison possible sentences — suspects imported hardware from Europe and China, then traded tips on concealing activation logs
Tesla’s FSD jailbreak crackdown comes with a $15,000 sting and possible prison time
South Korean authorities have identified 80 Tesla drivers who allegedly forced Full Self-Driving (FSD) onto cars that were never cleared for it, Electrek reports. The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency says it confiscated 21 of the devices used to switch the feature on. The unlock modules reportedly connect to the car’s CAN bus (the internal network that links its electronic control units) and get around the regional software lock that keeps FSD disabled. That works because Tesla builds the same computer into every car, whether or not the feature is approved locally.
Some suspects bought ready-made units from Europe and China, and one reportedly plugged a European-made module into his own Tesla. Others skipped the shopping. One suspect, an IT worker, built his device using information he found on GitHub, which suggests the barrier to entry for this kind of modification is lower than it sounds. The group also traded tips online, including how to stop the car from keeping any record that FSD had been activated. Concealing the activation history is likely an attempt to avoid detection by Tesla, which has been looking for these devices itself.
Then there is the legal risk, where prosecutors are using the Motor Vehicle Management Act, which bans unauthorized software changes that could affect vehicle safety. In Korea, the maximum penalty is two years in prison or a fine of up to 20 million won, or roughly $15,000, a steep price for a driver-assistance feature that many of these owners had already paid for.
South Korea’s transport ministry first flagged suspicious activations to police in April. “Safety risks were confirmed, including the possibility that FSD may fail to properly recognize driving conditions or operate differently from the driver’s intentions,” a police official said then.
Notably, the root of the problem is a certification gap. Tesla began offering FSD (Supervised) in South Korea in late 2025, but only on US-built Model S, Model X, and Cybertruck units, which skip local safety certification under the Korea-US free trade agreement. The Model 3 and Model Y arrive from Giga Shanghai and have yet to pass. Nobody agrees on how many Korean Teslas are eligible, although Carisyou Data Lab figures cited by MK last month indicate 47,458 of 229,311 cars (20.7%).
The South Korean investigation follows Tesla’s own efforts to stop unauthorized activation. In April, the company began remotely detecting unlock devices and disabling FSD access on affected vehicles. It has also warned owners that unauthorized modifications could void warranty coverage and leave them liable for crashes. Moreover, the restrictions are not the first time Tesla’s software protections have come under scrutiny. In August 2023, researchers exploited a hardware security flaw in the AMD processor powering Tesla’s media control unit to unlock certain paid features. The exploit targeted the car’s AMD-based system-on-chip, although researchers did not confirm that every premium feature could be unlocked.
Tesla has also faced regulatory scrutiny over software restrictions. In December 2021, the US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration investigated the company after an over-the-air update allowed drivers to play certain games while their vehicles were moving. The case highlighted how software changes can raise safety concerns when features are accessible under conditions regulators consider unsafe. Hardware reliability is another challenge for Tesla. Last year, the company detailed how it identifies defective processor cores in its Dojo AI supercomputers, where a single faulty component can compromise lengthy training runs.

articles.title: Google’s satellite AI server transmits its first response to Earth
articles.text:
Google’s AI chip-equipped satellite has generated its first response from space. In a blog post on Friday, Google says it successfully booted up the satellite’s Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), allowing the on-board Gemma 4 model to follow through on a prompt to create a haiku about being in space:
Google’s satellite AI server transmits its first response to Earth
The Project Suncatcher satellite generated a haiku about being in space.
Blue marble below
Data streams in silent grace
Starlight feeds my core. ✨
Google says it tried out other space-themed limericks and telemetry prompts as well. The test is part of Google’s Project Suncatcher, an experimental initiative that could eventually put AI data centers in space. Google launched the satellite into orbit earlier this month.
“Next, we will continue with a series of tests to evaluate how TPUs perform under thermal stress and radiation exposure in orbit,” Google says. “Verifying our TPUs can reliably execute workloads in space paves the way for our next milestone of twin interconnected satellites in 2027.”

articles.title: Windows 11 : plus besoin d’Adobe Acrobat, Microsoft Edge va devenir le meilleur lecteur de PDF
articles.text:
Il existe plusieurs façons d’ouvrir des documents PDF dans Windows 11. La première, en passant par un outil dédié, comme SumatraPDF, Foxit Reader ou encore Adobe Reader.
Il est également possible de faire appel à des services en ligne, mais la manœuvre est généralement déconseillée, d’autant plus s’il s’agit de PDF contenant des données sensibles.
Enfin, la dernière option existante pour ouvrir vos PDF est d’utiliser tout simplement votre navigateur Web. Qu’il s’agisse de Chrome, Edge ou encore de Firefox, tous les navigateurs Web actuels sont capables d’ouvrir ces fichiers. Certains proposent même quelques outils d’édition basiques qui permettent de remplir, signer ou encore d’annoter vos documents.
Mais jusqu’à présent, pour la gestion même de ces documents et des pages qui les composent, seules les applications dédiées étaient dotées du nécessaire. Les choses devraient toutefois changer, puisque Microsoft prévoit d’intégrer de nouvelles fonctions pour gérer plus facilement vos PDF directement depuis son navigateur Web Microsoft Edge.
Comme l’ont repéré nos confrères de Windows Latest, Microsoft prépare une importante mise à jour du lecteur PDF intégré à son navigateur Web Microsoft Edge. D’après la feuille de route mise en ligne par la firme de Redmond, cette mise à jour introduira, entre autres, une fonction pour fusionner et organiser vos documents de manière native, sans avoir à passer par un logiciel tiers, à utiliser de service en ligne tiers, ou à payer pour Adobe Acrobat.
Microsoft Edge pourra bientôt organiser vos pages et fusionner vos documents
Concrètement, Microsoft Edge va intégrer un outil qui vous permettra de fusionner plusieurs documents PDF entre eux. Vous pourrez ainsi combiner un document ouvert avec d’autres fichiers PDF, ouverts dans d’autres onglets ou stockés localement sur votre PC, pour en faire un document unique.
Microsoft Edge vous autorisera par ailleurs à organiser manuellement les pages qui composent votre document. Vous pourrez a priori sélectionner des pages pour les extraire, les supprimer, modifier leur ordre d’apparition dans le document, ou encore pour les faire pivoter si elles ne sont pas affichées dans le bon sens.
Le lecteur PDF intégré à Edge fournira par ailleurs un outil d’extraction de contenu (texte, images, etc.) qui fonctionnera même sur les documents ayant été numérisés, grâce au module de reconnaissance optique de caractères (OCR) intégré nativement dans Windows 11.
Microsoft prévoit également d’afficher un nouveau volet dédié aux outils d’annotation dans lequel seront centralisés les commentaires, notes manuscrites et autres surlignages. Vous pourrez ainsi rechercher facilement dans vos annotations, les filtrer, ou encore ajouter ou modifier vos commentaires.
Autre nouveauté qui devrait avoir son importance, le lecteur PDF de Microsoft Edge prendra en charge la traduction de vos documents PDF (jusqu’à 62 langues). Comble de l’ironie, pour proposer cette fonctionnalité gratuitement et vous éviter d’acheter Adobe Acrobat, Microsoft s’appuie sur les technologies d’Adobe. La firme de Redmond avait en effet abandonné, en 2023, son moteur PDF historique au profit du moteur Adobe Acrobat PDF Engine.
Des documents traités localement
Toutes ces nouvelles fonctionnalités de gestion de PDF dans Microsoft Edge seront traitées entièrement localement sur votre PC. Toutes les opérations de modification, de fusion ou d’annotation seront exécutées directement sur votre ordinateur, sans qu’aucune donnée ne transite par les serveurs de Microsoft, d’Adobe ou de tout autre service cloud.
Et la bonne nouvelle, c’est que les opérations réalisées sur vos documents PDF sont non destructrices. Les fichiers PDF sources ne seront pas modifiés. Le module PDF intégré à Microsoft Edge générera automatiquement un nouveau fichier PDF dès qu’une modification sera apportée.

articles.title: Google Home peut désormais vous aider à repérer les appareils qui consomment trop d'électricité
articles.text:
Google Home s’enrichit d’une nouvelle fonction pour surveiller la consommation électrique de certains objets connectés. La mise à jour du 29 octobre apporte également plusieurs améliorations aux caméras Nest et à Gemini, avec une bonne dose de correctifs pour rendre la maison connectée moins capricieuse.
Entre les appareils qui restent en veille, les radiateurs électriques et les équipements branchés en permanence, difficile de savoir précisément ce qui consomme de l’électricité à la maison. Les prises connectées capables de mesurer cette consommation existent depuis longtemps, mais encore faut-il pouvoir consulter leurs données facilement. Google entend simplifier les choses avec une nouvelle mise à jour de son application Home, qui permet désormais de retrouver certaines mesures électriques directement dans l’interface. Une petite nouveauté qui pourrait se révéler bien pratique pour garder un œil sur ses dépenses énergétiques.
Google Home affiche enfin la consommation de vos appareils Matter
Dans ses notes de mise à jour du 29 octobre, Google annonce la prise en charge des données énergétiques remontées par les prises connectées et les compteurs compatibles avec le protocole Matter.
Concrètement, lorsqu’un appareil prend en charge cette fonction, Google Home peut désormais afficher deux informations : sa puissance électrique instantanée, exprimée en milliwatts (mW), et sa consommation cumulée, en kilowattheures (kWh).
Les mesures apparaissent directement sur la vignette de l’appareil et dans son écran de contrôle. Plus besoin, donc, de jongler systématiquement entre Google Home et l’application du fabricant pour consulter ces informations.
En branchant un appareil électrique sur une prise connectée compatible, on peut observer sa consommation lorsqu’il fonctionne, mais aussi vérifier ce qu'il continue de tirer sur le réseau lorsqu’il semble éteint. Une manière de mieux identifier certains équipements énergivores, notamment ceux que l’on laisse branchés toute la journée.
Attention toutefois, Google Home ne mesure pas lui-même la consommation électrique. L'application se contente d’afficher les informations transmises par les équipements Matter capables de les fournir. Toutes les prises connectées ne sont donc pas concernées, même lorsqu’elles sont compatibles avec ce protocole.
Autre limitation importante : cette nouveauté est pour le moment annoncée sur Android uniquement. Google ne précise pas quand elle sera proposée dans la version iOS.
La mise à jour ajoute également un raccourci permettant de régler rapidement les thermostats compatibles sur une température plus économe en énergie. Une fonction particulièrement bienvenue à l’approche de l’hiver.
Les caméras Nest et Gemini profitent aussi de plusieurs correctifs
Google ne s’est pas contenté d’améliorer le suivi énergétique. Cette mise à jour s’attaque également à plusieurs défauts qui pouvaient compliquer l’utilisation quotidienne de ses objets connectés.
Les anciennes caméras Nest bénéficient notamment de corrections concernant la stabilité de leur connexion Wi-Fi, la synchronisation du son et de l’image ou encore le déclenchement de la vision nocturne. La Nest Doorbell filaire de première génération profite également d’une meilleure détection des personnes et des visages familiers lorsque les visiteurs se trouvent plus loin de la caméra.
L'application Google Home corrige aussi plusieurs problèmes de lecture vidéo pour les possesseurs de caméras de surveillance. Sur iPhone, la navigation dans l’historique des événements devient plus fiable, tandis que les smartphones Android pliants ne devraient plus rester bloqués sur un écran de chargement lors du passage entre les deux formats d'affichage.
Du côté de Gemini pour la maison, Google améliore la compréhension des demandes de transfert de musique d'une pièce à l’autre. L’assistant distingue également plus efficacement les minuteurs classiques de ceux destinés à arrêter la lecture musicale.
Google promet enfin de mettre un terme à un comportement assez agaçant : certaines enceintes pouvaient annoncer spontanément qu’elles n’avaient pas compris une demande, alors que personne ne leur avait adressé la parole.
Ces ajustements s’inscrivent dans une série de mises à jour destinées à améliorer la fiabilité de Google Home, après plusieurs mois marqués par des bugs parfois surprenants.
Les nouveautés sont en cours de déploiement. Google prévient toutefois que certaines fonctions peuvent mettre un peu de temps à apparaître, même lorsque l’application est déjà à jour.
- Un logiciel compatible avec de nombreux appareils connectés Google
- Des outils complets associés à des commandes simples
- Une interface intuitive adaptée à tous les publics

articles.title: Sam Altman, creador de ChatGPT: "El mundo debería aceptar que sucedan algunas cosas malas" en aras de los beneficios de la IA
articles.text:
Sam Altman, director ejecutivo de OpenAI, cree que el mundo tendrá que convivir con algunos daños de la inteligencia artificial para aprovechar sus ventajas, y lo presenta como uno de los puntos que le separan de Anthropic. "Creemos que el mundo debería aceptar que sucedan algunas cosas malas a cambio de los beneficios de esta tecnología y de que la gente tenga capacidad de decisión", explicó en una entrevista el 4 de octubre de 2026. Y es que entre su empresa y la de Dario Amodei hay, según él, "mucha distancia".
Dos caminos desde OpenAI. OpenAI lanzó ChatGPT a finales de 2022, un lanzamiento que desató el auge comercial de la IA. Pero a finales de mayo de 2026 Anthropic, fundada en 2021 por antiguos directivos de OpenAI, superó la última valoración conocida de la empresa de Altman.
Además, según Politico, Anthropic lleva tiempo considerada la defensora más firme de la regulación dentro de la industria, algo que hasta hace poco chocaba con el enfoque más ligero de la creadora de ChatGPT.
Más cerca de lo que parece. Y eso que sus posiciones se han ido acercando. En septiembre de 2026, Altman respaldó la petición de Amodei de frenar el desarrollo de los modelos más avanzados. Según contaba Forbes el 12 de septiembre, esa propuesta pasaba por permitir auditorías externas y alertaba de riesgos como los ciberataques o la toma de internet por parte de bots autónomos.
La acusación de captura regulatoria. Eso sí, Altman aprovechó una crítica que asesores cercanos a Donald Trump lanzan contra Anthropic, a la que reprochan utilizar la regulación para blindar su posición, para marcar distancias con su rival. Es la acusación de "captura regulatoria" que formuló David Sacks, responsable de IA de la Casa Blanca.
Altman no se sumó a ella, pero tampoco a la postura que atribuye a quienes piden más control: "No estoy de acuerdo, pero entiendo el punto de vista de quienes piensan: 'Esta tecnología va a ser tan potente y tan peligrosa que un único laboratorio de San Francisco debería tenerla para asegurarse de que no pase nada malo y, en cierto modo, decidir cómo repartir los beneficios'". Para él, eso sería "una contrapartida completamente inaceptable", contraria a la "postura reguladora más ligera" que defiende OpenAI.
De la extinción al optimismo. Durante años, Altman advirtió de los riesgos existenciales de la IA, hasta el punto de firmar en 2023 una declaración sobre el riesgo de extinción que pedía tratarlo como una prioridad global. En Decoded, en cambio, defendió que "la gente hará muchísimas más cosas buenas que malas, órdenes de magnitud más".
Pero esa tolerancia tiene un límite, y Altman lo dejó claro más adelante en la conversación: no acepta "los riesgos realmente catastróficos", entre ellos "una grave pérdida de control a manos de la IA".

articles.title: Cette “pierre de Rosette martienne” pourrait enfin révéler si la vie a existé sur la planète rouge
articles.text:
Cette “pierre de Rosette martienne” pourrait enfin révéler si la vie a existé sur la planète rouge
Tombée dans le Sahara, la météorite martienne Teghaza 001, âgée de plus de 4,1 milliards d'années, s'impose comme une fascinante capsule temporelle pour la communauté scientifique. Cette véritable “pierre de Rosette” extraterrestre offre un accès inédit à l'enfance de la planète rouge, documentant une époque cruciale où Mars possédait encore de l'eau liquide, un champ magnétique et une atmosphère propice à la vie.
C'est une capsule temporelle extraordinaire qui livre ses secrets. Découverte dans le désert du Sahara (au Mali) en 2022 et minutieusement analysée dans une étude majeure tout juste publiée dans la revue Science, la météorite martienne Teghaza 001 fascine la communauté scientifique. Avec un âge estimé à plus de 4,1 milliards d'années, cette roche rose de 800 grammes s'impose d'emblée comme l'un des témoins les plus anciens de la planète rouge jamais mis au jour sur Terre.
	
Nous n'avons pas d'autres échantillons comme celui-ci, il est unique : il est pratiquement impossible que nous en obtenions une autre comme celle-ci de sitôt.
Un voyage direct dans les archives de l'ancien Mars
La majorité des météorites martiennes connues proviennent d'impacts plus récents et documentent des époques géologiques plus tardives. Teghaza 001 change radicalement la donne en nous propulsant directement aux origines de Mars, à une époque où la planète disposait probablement encore d'une atmosphère dense, de vastes étendues d'eau liquide en surface et potentiellement d'un champ magnétique protecteur.
Carl Agee, du département Sciences de la Terre et planétologie, résume l'importance de l'ère géologique à laquelle Teg 001 appartient :“C'est le plus tôt, et c'est à ce moment-là que peut-être Mars avait encore un champ magnétique, et il était protégé des radiations, et il y avait des eaux de surface. Il y avait une atmosphère plus dense. Si la vie primitive était abondante sur Mars, c’est à ce moment que cela a dû se produire.”
	
Une critique du journal l'a nommée "la Pierre de Rosette" martienne !
“C'est comme remonter le temps et aller arracher un morceau d'affleurement rocheux vieux de 4 milliards d'années sur Mars pour voir ce qui s'y passait réellement”, soulignent les chercheurs. Un enthousiasme partagé par les évaluateurs de la revue Science, dont l'un n'a pas hésité à qualifier ce caillou d'exception de véritable « Pierre de Rosette » pour décoder l'histoire primitive de la planète voisine.
Une rareté géologique inégalée
Grâce à des analyses isotopiques et minéralogiques poussées menées par des laboratoires de pointe, les scientifiques ont pu retracer la genèse de cet objet hors du commun et même identifier treize zones sources potentielles dans les hautes terres cratérisées du sud de Mars.
Pour les planétologues, aucun échantillon n'est aussi précieux pour combler les immenses lacunes de notre compréhension géologique martienne : “Nous n'avons encore fait qu'affleurer la surface de ce qu'elle a à nous raconter”, prédisent les auteurs. Alors que les agences spatiales rêvent toujours de ramener un jour des échantillons du sol martien via de coûteuses missions complexes, cette pierre tombée du ciel s'offre à nous comme un cadeau cosmique inestimable pour réécrire l'histoire de notre voisine du système solaire.

articles.title: OPINION: You can’t scale with a startup mindset | EU-Startups
articles.text:
The best advice once your company achieves product-market fit? Don’t get stuck on things that got you there, keep adjusting your architecture and workflow to fit your new realities and sizes.
Starting strong is one thing, but the real point is pushing past the growth ceiling without crashing: McKinsey found 78% of products launched successfully only to fail later on. Having worked in international expansion, I have seen how the practices that help a startup gain traction can cause troubles as it grows. Here is my top-5 of what’s better to be changed once a company is too big for a startup mode, and what habits are worth keeping in mind.
Money moves faster than decisions
Congratulations, it’s been your big funding round. Having more capital can feel like you have almost unlimited freedom to chase everything at once. This money mostly goes to ideas that already work, more on tests, all at once. In a ten-person startup, the founder knows every ongoing experiment. In a 100-person company, nobody does. Tests overlap, compete for the same target audience, and rarely get switched off. Meanwhile, decision-making slows down as more people have something to say. More money won’t fix messy operations, it just makes the mistakes more expensive.
The Turkish quick-commerce company Getir expanded to nine countries by the end of 2021 and bought Berlin rival Gorillas for €1.13 billon ($1.2 billion) in December 2022. Yet, in a few years the company chose to exit Germany, the UK and the Netherlands to focus back on its core Turkish business. Having enough money to go global doesn’t automatically mean it’s the right move. Sustainable scaling requires strong research: diving into local consumer behavior, understanding specific market nuances, and adapting your model to what local buyers actually want.
To grow without burning capital, build a fixed and transparent framework of your experiments: a single log where every project has one owner, a set budget, a clear deadline, and kill criteria agreed before launch. Each ongoing test should be backed by a specific hypothesis and (ideally) data. If an experiment went great in one market, don’t hurry to move forward – assess whether the conditions that made it work still apply in other regions.
Customer behaviour, channel preferences, and acquisition costs vary from country to country, so goals need to be tailored to actual team capacity and adapted market by market.
Hiring and ownership need a system
In a startup mode, team members do everything at once, no matter the difficulty level. Quite often, juniors jump in wherever they’re needed, keep going, and naturally become team leads. Loyalty is important, but management requires a different skillset. Wharton professor Peter Cappelli points out that top individual contributors who get promoted often make the weakest managers.
The same applies at the executive level. When founders are responsible for each new decision, they’re likely to slow down processes in their own business. Getting advice and seeing fresh perspectives from someone who has their own area of responsibility creates a clear structure with solid boundaries.
Bringing in senior leadership only works if you fix how responsibility is assigned. As headcount grows, each person assumes someone else is handling it. Psychologists call this diffusion of responsibility. Every project needs one named owner with the authority to execute, and clear processes for who decides and who reports progress. If a project has two owners, in practice, it has none.
AI will not replace everyone
Every company that’s actively growing now feels pressure to automate more and hire less. But implementation itself is a huge project, and for plenty of everyday tasks, a skilled person is still faster, cheaper, and far less painful to manage.
In May 2025, Klarna backtracked their earlier beliefs that AI has a potential to replace human work. A bit more than a year earlier, the company paused hiring customer service agents in favour of their AI assistant. The bot took 75% of the company’s customer chats in more than 35 languages. It sounded high-potential at first, but then there was: lower quality of support. Klarna began recruiting human agents again, while AI keeps handling simpler requests.
The point is to define for your business when to use AI, and when human touch is a super power. Everything repetitive and predictable can go to the AI team, and situations that win from empathy and critical thinking, are better left for people. The next step is to start educating your team to make sure they’re staying flexible and are using modern solutions for the new way of living.
AI is way more than just right prompting. Show employees how they can make their own simple tools for their daily workflows – through online courses, internal bootcamps, hackathons, or any other solutions that work best for your business. Developers can then turn the most promising ideas into advanced solutions.
Plan beyond the next quarter
Startups live month-over-month. Meanwhile, scaling needs a longer horizon, with a solid six-month and a year plan, all while maintaining a flexible approach. Your core metrics have to evolve, too.
A longer perspective also offers you a unique view of which temporary fixes no longer work and need to be redone in favour of a stronger infrastructure. Spreadsheets and manual workarounds are fine at a hundred orders a day, not at a hundred thousand. A McKinsey survey revealed that about 30% of CIOs said more than 20% of their new-product budget is diverted to fixing tech debt.
To keep everything aligned, run a strategy session every six months. On a more routine basis, make it a norm to have bi-weekly leadership syncs to review progress, track unit economics, and adjust tactics before small operational cracks can turn into a real problem.
Growth makes centralisation a necessity
As you grow, your operational architecture has to go through changes, including a call on what stays central and what lives in-market. Having worked in international expansion, I’ve seen how companies hit a ceiling when they try to manage global growth from two extreme ends: either micro-managing every local solution or letting regional teams operate like separate startups.
Core product decisions, CRM, brand guidelines, and customer support standards require consistency, so they are best managed centrally. Where you can really leave room for local teams is in what they know best: local landscape, relationships and competitors, regional traditions, preferences, and behaviors. The real challenge here is finding the right balance. Centralization cuts out messy duplication and keeps your brand cohesive, but excessive control from the top will blindside you to market-specific realities.
Scale up, but keep the best of the startup mindset. Stay adaptable. Keep testing (but make it wisely and don’t waste resources). Count money the way you did when there was very little of it, because the budget is never infinite, no matter how big the last round was.

articles.title: 2027 Nissan Rogue Hybrid: Drives like an EV, but there's no plug involved
articles.text:
Nissan has a new version of its bestselling Rogue SUV, and it’s launching the model here with the latest version of its e-Power hybrid system, which Ars tested in February. Most hybrid cars you can buy today are parallel hybrids, which means that they have an internal combustion engine and an electric motor, both of which drive some or all of the wheels—everything works in parallel. But there’s another approach. Instead of connecting the engine to the wheels via a transmission, it can act as a generator and charge the traction battery, which in turn powers the electric motor. Since the engine and motor work in series, this is known as a series hybrid.
That’s mostly how the Chevrolet Volt worked. As does Honda’s hybrid CR-V. Well, mostly; engineers worked out it was more efficient for those cars’ gasoline engines to directly drive the wheels at highway speeds, something that to this day makes a certain subset of hybrid car enthusiasts irrationally angry. If you know anyone like that in your life, send them to wherever the nearest Nissan dealership is, because the 2027 Rogue Hybrid is exactly what they’ve been asking for.
Series hybrids
Under the hood, with its crisp shut line and slim horizontal lights that give me something of a Range Rover vibe, there’s a 1.5 L, three-cylinder turbocharged direct-injection engine that generates 148 hp (110 kW). It only revs to 5,200 rpm because it’s optimized to charge the battery, not cope with the various loads of an engine connected to a gearbox and the wheels. That also allows the engine to operate at a rather impressive 42 percent thermal efficiency—we would need to look at Formula 1 engines to find higher.
This charges a 1.67 kWh lithium-ion traction battery that has been optimized for its charge and discharge ability, which in turn powers a pair of electric motors. At the front axle sits a 202 hp (150 kW), 243 lb-ft (330 Nm) permanent synchronous magnet motor, at the rear another PSM providing 134 hp (100 kW) and 144 lb-ft (195 Nm), although given the battery’s limitations, combined power output is 225 hp (168 kW). And as you would expect, the motors will regeneratively brake under deceleration to return as much energy to the battery for reuse as possible.

articles.title: Drupal Commerce Core Vulnerability Exploited Against Online Stores
articles.text:
Drupal is urging online store owners to patch a highly critical access bypass vulnerability in the Commerce Core module, warning that it is being exploited in the wild.
Tracked as CVE-2026-118539, the issue affects a contributed module that adds e-commerce features to Drupal websites, including a shopping cart and checkout process. Drupal’s statistics show the module is used on more than 42,000 sites.
“The module doesn’t sufficiently protect certain routes and entity fields, leading to an access bypass that may financially impact the vendor,” Drupal explains in its advisory.
The Drupal security team gave the issue a risk score of 21 out of 25. According to the score, unauthenticated attackers can exploit the flaw no matter how the module is set up.
Drupal has confirmed the attacks but has not said how the bug is being exploited, who is behind the activity, or how many sites have been targeted. It has also not said whether the vulnerability was exploited as a zero-day, before patches became available.
The vulnerability affects 3.x versions before 3.3.13 and earlier releases before 8.x-2.41. Administrators should update to one of the two fixed versions and review their store orders.
“Sites should audit their orders for inconsistencies as this vulnerability is being actively exploited,” the advisory reads.
The 38 other advisories Drupal published on October 28 address vulnerabilities in 21 contributed projects. Nearly a dozen are rated critical, including bugs that could lead to remote code execution, account takeover, or Commerce orders via Stripe being marked as paid without payment.
The CAPTCHA module also received a fix for a moderately critical bug that allows a protected form to be submitted again without solving a new challenge. Drupal’s rating indicates that exploit code for this bug exists in the wild, although the advisory doesn’t mention active exploitation.
Drupal’s ratings also indicate that proofs of concept exist for two information disclosure bugs, one in Commerce Core and one in Media Alias Display.
On October 14, Drupal announced fixes for two critical remote code execution bugs: CVE-2026-108097 in core’s Field UI module and CVE-2026-108099 in the Entity List module. Neither component exposes the flaws on its own, but certain other contributed modules or custom code make exploitation possible, in some cases without authentication.
Ahead of its October 14 security releases, Drupal cautioned that exploits might appear within hours or days. So far, however, there have been no public reports of the flaws being exploited in the wild.
CVE-2026-9082, a highly critical SQL injection issue in Drupal core’s database abstraction API that affects PostgreSQL-backed sites, did attract exploitation attempts in May.
