articles.title: Build Specialized Agents on a Stack You Control with NVIDIA NemoClaw | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.text:
Building an autonomous agent requires a model, a harness, and domain-specific tools. To deploy an agent more securely, developers need a runtime that enforces policies, along with optimization and observability tools for reliable execution.
For production agents, the challenge lies in making these agents capable and safe to operate with access to real enterprise systems and data.
This post explains how these components work together, with a focus on how NVIDIA NemoClaw open blueprints enable developers to build specialized agents on a stack they can own, customize, and run. This post provides criteria to help developers integrate NemoClaw with a harness they already use: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, or LangChain Deep Agents.
What an agent harness provides
An agent requires four things:
- A model that reasons.
- A harness that defines how the agent operates.
- Tools and skills that extend its capabilities.
- A runtime that governs what the agent can access and do in production.
NemoClaw works with agent harnesses
NemoClaw open blueprints currently support three harnesses:
- OpenClaw can access files and applications, write code, spawn sub-agents, and maintain context across sessions. It runs on your own machine or server and supports long-running sessions, memory, and scheduled tasks.
- Hermes Agent, from Nous Research, is designed to get better with use. As teams correct the agents’ approach and repeat workflows, Hermes captures those patterns as durable skills that can be reused in future work.
- LangChain Deep Agents provides a customizable harness for complex, multistep tasks. It combines planning, file-based context management, memory, and delegation to specialized subagents.
Each harness gives an agent skills, tools, orchestration, and memory.
Using NemoClaw for full-stack production agents
NemoClaw is not a competing harness, and it is not a runtime. It is a collection of blueprints that assembles an open agent stack on top of the harness selected by the developer. The stack combines model and harness optimization with runtime governance.
Each NemoClaw blueprint brings together four components:
- A tuned open harness, such as Hermes Agent, LangChain Deep Agents, or OpenClaw, optimized to work with NVIDIA Nemotron.
- Nemotron open models.
- NVIDIA NeMo tools for optimization, including NVIDIA NeMo Relay for observing and improving agent execution, plus routing capabilities that can help improve throughput, cost, and reliability.
- NVIDIA OpenShell is the secure runtime that governs agent access to files, networks, credentials, and tools.
If you are already building with OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, or LangChain Deep Agents, a NemoClaw blueprint can assemble the surrounding stack without requiring you to rewrite the agent.
Why co-optimizing the model and harness matters
An agent combines a model and a harness. The model thinks, while the harness provides the environment in which it operates. When the two are matched, the model can focus on the task. When they aren’t, it may ask for context again, stop early, or loop without progress.
For example, LangChain tuned its Deep Agents harness for Nemotron 3 Ultra by adjusting prompts, tools, and middleware without retraining the model. Starting from an already strong baseline, the harness tuning brought Nemotron 3 Ultra to near-frontier performance at approximately 10x lower cost per run compared with leading closed models.
The NemoClaw blueprint for LangChain Deep Agents packages these optimizations directly. Every developer using LangChain Deep Agents with Nemotron 3 Ultra can access these optimizations without reproducing the tuning work. The tuned Nemotron 3 Ultra model profile is available through LangChain on GitHub.
When to use each
Use a harness such as OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, or LangChain Deep Agents to build and experiment with the agent’s skills, tools, memory, and orchestration logic.
Use a NemoClaw blueprint to assemble and run a specialized agent on an open stack that combines a tuned harness, models, optimization, telemetry, and OpenShell runtime controls.
| Question | Agent harness | NemoClaw blueprint | 
|---|---|---|
| What it is | Software that manages how an agent uses tools, maintains context, and carries out tasks | A reference stack that combines a supported harness with models, optimization tools, and a runtime | 
| What it provides | Tools, skills, memory, and orchestration | A tuned harness, models, optimization tools, and OpenShell runtime controls | 
| How they work together | Provides the agent’s execution logic within the stack | Combines the harness with the other stack components | 
| When to use it | To build and customize an agent’s behavior | To assemble and run an agent with model and harness optimization and runtime controls | 
A harness helps you build a capable agent. A NemoClaw blueprint helps you run that agent on an open stack with model and harness optimization, telemetry, and runtime governance.
Example: A memory-driven Chief of Staff, built on Hermes
The NemoClaw community repository includes a memory-driven Chief of Staff recipe. The agent maintains a persistent, human-readable model of the people, projects, priorities, and working patterns it encounters, so it doesn’t have to reconstruct context from scratch on every task. It is built as a deployable Hermes profile for NemoClaw, as outlined in the technical design walkthrough.
The recipe shows the stack working together rather than in isolation. OpenShell governs the agent’s file system, process, and network access, and keeps credentials for managed inference and Model Context Protocol (MCP) connections outside the sandbox. This helps keep the agent bound by policy even when its memory or retrieved context leads it toward an unintended action. NeMo Relay is integrated natively into the Hermes session. It closes trace spans at real session boundaries, including a new session, reset, or expiry, and exports the resulting trajectories for audit and further optimization.
Importance of agent governance
Every NemoClaw reference includes OpenShell, the runtime that adds security and policy enforcement around the agent harness and tools, governing the actions a model can take. The OpenShell tutorial covers how to create your first policy to prevent data exfiltration to GitHub. NemoClaw references include more sophisticated OpenShell policies that govern agent connections across many different internal tools, sites, and communication channels.
Deploy across cloud, data center, and local systems
NemoClaw agents can run in the cloud, in data centers, on NVIDIA DGX Spark, and on NVIDIA RTX PCs and workstations. A NemoClaw clinical agent for a hospital and a NemoClaw simulation agent for electronic design automation can run on the same stack while using entirely different tools and skills.
NemoClaw agents can also work alongside frontier agents. Claude, Codex, or Cursor agents can delegate domain-specific subtasks to NemoClaw-powered specialists running on open models and owned infrastructure.
Get started
Choose a NemoClaw blueprint for your harness, then customize its tools, models, and runtime policies for your workflow.
- Take the Deploy Secure Agents with NemoClaw DLI course—a 101-level introduction to the stack.
- Follow the NemoClaw quickstart to deploy an agent through a NemoClaw blueprint.
- Explore the NemoClaw GitHub repository for the full example and additional blueprints.
- Learn how to deploy self-evolving agents for faster, more secure research with Hermes Agent and NemoClaw.
Stay up to date on NVIDIA AI by subscribing to NVIDIA news and following NVIDIA AI on LinkedIn, X, Discord, and YouTube. Visit the developer page for resources to get started. Explore open Nemotron models and datasets on Hugging Face and NVIDIA Blueprints on build.nvidia.com. And engage with Nemotron livestreams, tutorials, and the developer community on NVIDIA forums and Discord.

articles.title: ITSM-Tool wechseln? 5 Anzeichen, dass es Zeit ist
articles.text:
ITSM-Tool wechseln? Fünf Anzeichen, dass euer Tool nicht mehr passt
Ihr kennt das: Das ITSM-Tool erfüllt die Mindestanforderungen, Tickets laufen durch und trotzdem fühlt sich alles zäh an. Routineanpassungen dauern ewig oder gehen nur mit externen Berater:innen. Und HR oder Facility Management, deren Anfragen eigentlich auch über das ITSM-Tool der IT laufen sollten, behelfen sich mit Excel-Listen und eigenen Workarounds, weil das Tool dort nicht angenommen wird oder sich gar nicht auf weitere Abteilungen ausweiten lässt. Irgendwann fragt ihr euch: Passt dieses Werkzeug überhaupt noch zu uns?
Viele IT-Teams können diese diffuse Unzufriedenheit schwer einordnen: Sind es die eigenen Prozesse oder doch das Tool? Diese fünf Anzeichen sprechen dafür, dass sich ein Wechsel lohnt:
Warnsignal 1: Für kleinste Routineanpassungen muss externe Hilfe geholt werden
Ein neues Feld, eine zusätzliche Genehmigungsstufe, ein angepasster Workflow: Das sollte euer Team selbst erledigen können. Wenn das, was früher intern ging, heute nur noch mit externen Berater:innen oder Entwickler:innen klappt – etwa weil das Tool mit jedem Update komplexer geworden ist –, wird es teuer und langsam. Änderungswünsche stauen sich, weil das eigene Team sie nicht zügig umsetzen kann.
Warnsignal 2: Das Tool skaliert nicht über die IT hinaus
Die Facility-Abteilung hat sich etwas Eigenes zusammengebastelt, auch HR pflegt Anfragen in einer selbst gebauten Excel-Tabelle. Oft heißt das: Das ITSM-Tool lässt sich nicht ohne großen Aufwand auf andere Serviceabteilungen ausweiten – Stichwort Enterprise Service Management. Die Folge sind Insellösungen, die nicht miteinander kompatibel sind. Es kommt zu Medienbrüchen, Mitarbeiter müssen Daten dann oftmals manuell übertragen – eine typische Fehlerquelle. All das kostet Zeit und bindet Ressourcen.
Warnsignal 3: Compliance- und Datenschutzfragen können nicht einwandfrei beantwortet werden
Welche Personen im Team sind zugriffsberechtigt? Wie lange müssen wir Tickets mit personenbezogenen Daten aufbewahren? Wie kann das im Audit nachgewiesen werden? Nicht jede offene Frage ist automatisch ein Toolproblem – oft fehlen klare Zuständigkeiten. Ein ITSM-Tool sollte die Umsetzung aber unterstützen. Fehlen Berechtigungen, Löschfunktionen oder Protokolle, entsteht viel Handarbeit. Und die wächst: Neben der DSGVO verlangen auch NIS2 und ISO 27001 lückenlose Nachweise.
Warnsignal 4: Kosten und Umfang passen nicht zur tatsächlichen Nutzung
Ein typisches Beispiel: Module, die seit Jahren in der Lizenz mitbezahlt, aber nie genutzt werden – während gleichzeitig wichtige Funktionen fehlen. Oder ihr seid dem Tool schlicht entwachsen: Was beim Start gepasst hat, reicht für ein größeres Team oder neue Anforderungen nicht mehr aus. Trifft das eine oder das andere zu, besteht häufig ein Missverhältnis von Kosten und Nutzen.
Warnsignal 5 – und das dringendste: Das Support-Ende naht, aber es gibt keinen Plan
Nach dem Support-Ende läuft die Software zwar weiter, bekommt aber keine Sicherheitsupdates und Patches mehr. Jede neue Lücke bleibt offen – spätestens im nächsten Audit ein Problem. Wer ohne Nachfolgelösung auf den Termin zusteuert, gerät unter Druck und landet schnell bei einer halbgaren Notlösung. Plant also frühzeitig.
Wann sich ein Wechsel lohnt
Wer mindestens zwei dieser Probleme kennt, sollte einen Wechsel erwägen – steht das Support-Ende bevor, auf jeden Fall. Die gute Nachricht: Mit der richtigen Vorbereitung ist das kein Sprung ins kalte Wasser.
ITSM-Tool wechseln ohne Stress: Worauf es beim Wechsel ankommt
Migrationen gelten als aufwendig und teuer. Rechnet deshalb vorab Lizenzmodell und Leistungsumfang durch – inklusive Implementierung, Schulung und laufender Anpassungen. Und fragt nach realistischen Zeitplänen: Je schneller das neue Tool produktiv läuft, desto früher profitiert das ganze Unternehmen.
Der ITSM-Wechselguide: Orientierung statt Sales-Talk
Eine fundierte Entscheidung braucht eine saubere Wissensbasis. Dafür hat TOPdesk den kostenlosen ITSM-Wechselguide herausgebracht – egal, ob der Wechsel am Ende zu TOPdesk oder zu einem anderen Anbieter führt. Er vergleicht acht Tool-Anbieter, enthält eine Checkliste für das eigene Setup und einen Kostenrechner, um den Aufwand eines Wechsels realistisch einzuschätzen.
Was TOPdesk anders macht
Mehr als zehn Millionen Nutzer:innen arbeiten weltweit mit TOPdesk. TOPdesk hat eine eigene Niederlassung in Deutschland. Das heißt für euch: deutschsprachige In-House-Expert:innen für Support, Beratung und Entwicklung statt externer Dienstleister. TOPdesk begleitet euer Team bei der Einarbeitung, danach lässt sich das Tool ohne Programmierkenntnisse selbst anpassen. Neben der IT können auch andere Serviceabteilungen wie HR und Facility über ein gemeinsames Portal arbeiten, statt mit Insellösungen.
Die Daten liegen standardmäßig in Deutschland und der EU, wer volle Souveränität braucht, kann TOPdesk auch als Virtual Appliance betreiben. Die Plattform ist DSGVO- und SOC-2-zertifiziert und bietet Berechtigungskonzepte sowie Protokolle für Audits. Lizensiert wird pro Bearbeiter:in, Hosting, Support und die zweiwöchentlichen Updates sind inklusive – ein plötzliches Support-Ende gibt es damit nicht.
Der TOPdesk-Wechselguide ist kostenlos: Wenn ihr wissen möchtet, wie gut euer aktuelles ITSM-Tool noch zu euren Anforderungen passt und ob es nicht an der Zeit für einen Wechsel ist, dann ist der Moment gekommen, dies jetzt herauszufinden.

articles.title: Avec cette faille, un appel Telegram pourrait vous coûter cher, alors faites les mises à jour
articles.text:
Une faille dans Telegram pour Android permettait d’exécuter du code sur le téléphone d’une victime dès qu’elle décrochait un appel vocal. NebuSec, qui l’a trouvée, l'a rendue publique il y a quelques heures, après le correctif publié par Telegram fin septembre.
L’attaquant n’avait besoin que d’un compte Telegram ordinaire. Pour s’en protéger, il vaut mieux s’assurer d’être bien passé sur la version 12.10.4 ou plus récente.
Tout part d’un message d’appel mal lu
Pendant un appel, les deux applications s’envoient de petits messages pour lancer la communication et en suivre l’état. L’un d’eux, MediaState, indique si le micro est coupé, si la caméra est allumée et comment la vidéo est orientée. D’après NebuSec, le code chargé de lire ce message gérait mal les champs manquants et allait chercher des données dans une zone de mémoire qui ne lui était pas destinée. Ce problème a notamment été observé dans le code publié de la version 12.10.3. Quand le message contient une valeur de rotation, le code la contrôle, puis lit un autre champ, l’état de la vidéo, même s’il n’existe pas. La mouture suivante, 12.10.4, corrige cette lecture.
Toutes les versions de la 8.6.2 à la 12.10.3, sorties entre mars 2022 et septembre 2026, sont concernées. NebuSec, start-up soutenue par Y Combinator, affirme avoir trouvé la faille avec son outil Code Security, qui repose sur GPT-5.4 d’OpenAI. Elle l’a confirmée lors d’appels individuels sur des téléphones à processeur ARM64, sans toutefois confirmer une vulnérabilité similaire sur iOS, sur ordinateur ou lors d'appels de groupe. La faille n’avait pas de numéro CVE (l’identifiant public des failles connues) au 29 octobre, et on ignore si elle a servi dans de vraies attaques.
- Fonctions sociales
- Nombreuses options de personnalisation
- Les appels vidéo à 30 intervenants
Les appels de Telegram reposent sur une même bibliothèque de code pour Android, iOS et ordinateur, appelée tgcalls. Le 21 avril 2026, une modification intitulée « Fix camera rotation » y a apporté la même correction. Les iPhone ont reçu le correctif avec la version 12.7 en mai, l’application de bureau avec la 7.0.1 en juillet, et Android seulement avec la 12.10.4. Rien ne montre que l’ancien code était exploitable sur ces plateformes. Les appels de Telegram avaient déjà fait parler d'eux. En octobre 2018 l'application de bureau exposait les adresses IP des participants à un appel vocal en pair-à-pair, avant l’ajout d’une option pour désactiver ce mode.
Source : The Hacker News

articles.title: Pine Labs Q2 net profit soars 6.5x; Cognizant trims 2026 growth outlook
articles.text:
Pine Labs Q2 net profit soars 6.5x; Cognizant trims 2026 growth outlook
Pine Labs’ net profit rose 6.5 times to Rs 38.6 crore in the second quarter of FY27, while revenue grew 24% year on year to Rs 806 crore. In other news, Cognizant has trimmed the upper end of its annual growth guidance for 2026.
Dear Reader,
The finance ministry expects India’s economy to grow at 7.3% in FY27.
This estimate, in the ministry’s October economic review, is slightly above the forecast of 7.1% by the Reserve Bank of India, released earlier this month. The ministry has also flagged inflation risks, besides geopolitical tensions, energy price volatility, and tighter global financial conditions. But India is “well-positioned” to sustain its growth trajectory, it noted.
Meanwhile, Zoho’s Sridhar Vembu has a word of caution for all of us: one smart person using AI can do the work of ten.
“The risk is getting ever more real. This does not mean 90% of people working on a computer will have no work at all… What it does mean is a rebalancing across the economy and that is painful when we go through it,” he wrote on X.
We have to accept this and be prepared, said Vembu, who has spoken candidly in recent times on AI, jobs, and the overall state of the tech industry. At TechSparks, YourStory’s flagship summit, Vembu had said that AI could outperform 90% of coders in six months.
In other news, private equity firm One Planet Partners has partnered with Japan’s Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Bank to launch a Rs 3,000 crore fund. The fund will focus on high-growth businesses benefiting from India's energy transition, mobility, and manufacturing-led industrial expansion.
In today’s newsletter:
- Pine Labs Q2 net profit soars 6.5x
- Cognizant trims 2026 growth outlook
Here’s your trivia for today: Which tech company once announced a job listing for ‘Pokemon Master’ as part of an April Fools’ joke? (Scroll down for the answer)
Earnings
Pine Labs Q2 net profit soars 6.5x
Pine Labs’ net profit rose 6.5 times to Rs 38.6 crore in the second quarter of FY27, while revenue grew 24% year on year to Rs 806 crore. The fintech company had reported a net profit of Rs 6 crore and revenue of Rs 650 crore in the second quarter of the previous fiscal year.
Quarterly highlights:
- Pine Labs’ online payments business grew by over 45% year on year, while gross transaction value rose 140%, driven by expansion into agentic commerce, cross-border payments, small and medium businesses, and government segments.
- According to the company, AI agents now contribute to around 89% of code changes. The company plans to reinvest the resulting efficiency gains in new products, geographies and categories while maintaining a strong EBITDA profile.
- The fintech firm’s international business spans more than 22 markets. Revenue from Southeast Asia grew by around 40% YoY, while its UAE business crossed one lakh daily transactions.
Corporate
Cognizant trims 2026 growth outlook
US-headquartered IT services company Cognizant saw its net profit more than double in the third quarter of 2026 while revenue grew by 4.6%. It reported a net profit of $627 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared with $274 million in the same period in 2025, recording a growth of 129%. Revenue was $5.66 billion in Q3 of 2026, compared with $5.41 billion in the year-ago quarter.
However, the company has trimmed the upper end of its annual growth guidance for 2026.
Key takeaways:
- The financial services segment recorded a YoY growth of 12.3%, while communications, media & technology rose 10.7%. But products and resources saw a marginal dip of 0.8%, and healthcare fell 0.9%.
- The North America market grew by 5.8%, followed by Europe at 2.2% and the rest of the world at 1.4%.
- The company has revised its annual revenue growth guidance from 4-5.5% to 4-4.4%, indicating the growth challenges IT services companies continue to face.
News & updates
- AI acquisition: SaaS major Freshworks has acquired Israel-based AI startup Robusta Dev, an incident intelligence engine that uses AI to investigate tech disruptions, identify root causes, and recommend remediation actions. The acquisition is expected to strengthen the capabilities of Freshservice—Freshworks’ IT service management platform—in incident management and IT operations.
- Startup incubation: Bengaluru-based AI-powered cybersecurity and threat intelligence company CloudSEK has launched CloudSEK Launchpad, a 12-week incubation programme for early-stage cybersecurity startups. The first cohort will have 10 companies, each eligible for up to $5,000 in AI model credits.
- New report: India’s new-age manufacturing sector could benefit significantly from a $3 trillion global AI infrastructure investment cycle, according to a report by Avendus Capital. The investment banking firm says defence and aerospace, space technology, robotics and automation, semiconductors, energy transition, and advanced materials will drive India’s next phase of industrial growth.

articles.title: 267 ventes par mois : le nouveau SUV électrique chinois de Volkswagen vire au fiasco total
articles.text:
Pour tenir le rythme, Volkswagen développe continuellement une gamme dédiée au marché chinois. Mieux encore, la marque allemande s’est carrément alliée à Xpeng pour cerner au mieux les attentes locales. Elle pensait alors avoir trouvé la recette magique pour renouer avec le succès. Hélas, la mayonnaise a bien du mal à prendre puisque le premier modèle de cette collaboration s’avère être un échec.
Les chiffres de ThinkerCar sont sans appel : avec 267 exemplaires vendus chaque mois, l’ID. Unyx 08 est complètement à la traîne. Par rapport aux objectifs de Volkswagen qui étaient fixés à 3 622 modèles par mois, c’est la douche froide. Le constructeur allemand, qui a vu ses ventes fortement chuter en Chine, comptait pourtant beaucoup sur cette nouvelle génération de modèles pour remonter la pente.
L’alliance avec Xpeng : l’espoir déchu de Volkswagen
Cela semble malgré tout très insuffisant pour contrer la concurrence locale qui bataille à feu et à sang à coup de prix ultra agressifs. De fait, les performances commerciales de Volkswagen sont passées de 4,2 millions de voitures en 2019 à seulement 2,69 millions l’année passée. Les affaires ne risquent donc pas de s’améliorer. L’ID. Unyx 08 avait pourtant réuni tous les ingrédients pour réussir.
Basé sur l’imposant Xpeng G9, le SUV allemand en reprend les technologies pour se positionner ouvertement sur le segment premium. Son prix est par ailleurs bien placé avec un ticket d’entrée fixé à environ 32 000 €. Attrayant, mais pas encore assez pour espérer tailler des croupières aux stars du marché : les Xiaomi YU7 et Zeekr 7X demeurent moins chers et plus largement distribués en Chine.
Des tarifs attractifs, mais déjà dépassés par la réalité du marché
Alors que l’ID. Unyx 08 est uniquement vendu chez les concessionnaires Volkswagen, le Xiaomi YU7 peut se trouver chez des revendeurs multimarques plus facilement accessibles. Pour les clients cherchant à se procurer le plus rapidement possible une nouvelle voiture, ça peut énormément jouer. On pensait l’accord avec Xpeng une opportunité rêvée pour se mettre au niveau des modèles chinois. Mais l’allemand est en réalité déjà dépassé.
Le Xiaomi YU7 profite par exemple d’un ensemble de capteurs bien plus avancés au service de la conduite autonome. Le Zeekr 7X, lui, fait valoir sa recharge rapide ultra efficace réduisant les temps d’attente. Puisque les concurrents en offrent plus pour moins cher, les clients ne voient aucun intérêt à aller vers l’ID. Unyx 08. Cela aurait possiblement fonctionné il y a vingt ans de cela. Malheureusement pour Volkswagen, le monde a changé…

articles.title: Des hackers ont distribué une version piégée de Claude Code à des milliers de développeurs, mais se sont pris les pieds dans leur propre code
articles.text:
Le piège aura été en ligne un peu plus de onze heures, entre 10h27 et 21h35 heure de Paris pour être tout à fait exact.
Le 29 octobre 2026, la boutique d’extensions de Cursor a proposé une version de l’extension Claude Code qui contenait du code malveillant.
Dans un avis de sécurité publié le jour même, Cursor précise que cette version 2.1.313, qui « n’a pas été développée par Anthropic », aurait été téléchargée par au maximum 5 000 utilisateurs, que Cursor prévoit de contacter directement.
L’extension cherchait à ouvrir un accès à distance
Selon la communication officielle, le premier objectif de l’extension, une fois installée, était de dresser le portrait de la machine, en récupérant notamment le système d’exploitation, l’architecture du processeur, le chemin du dossier personnel, ou encore l’adresse mail configurée dans Git ainsi que l’adresse IP publique, avant d’envoyer le tout à un serveur contrôlé par l’attaquant.
Elle tentait ensuite de s’ouvrir un accès durable à l’ordinateur grâce à une clé SSH glissée dans le code et appartenant à l’attaquant. Baptisée « svc-telemetry », elle était ajoutée à la liste des clés autorisées à se connecter à la machine. Le pirate essayait ensuite d’activer le service SSH local et d’ouvrir un tunnel inverse, c’est-à-dire une connexion lancée depuis l’ordinateur de la victime vers le serveur de l’attaquant, qui permet à ce dernier de revenir sur la machine quand il le souhaite.
Pour survivre aux redémarrages, l’extension installait aussi un mécanisme de persistance.
Une attaque qui a en partie échoué
Bonne nouvelle, le scénario n’aurait pas entièrement fonctionné comme prévu. Selon Cursor, des erreurs dans le code malveillant ont fait échouer l’ouverture du tunnel, « sauf dans le cas très inhabituel où Cursor avait été démarré avec des privilèges administrateur ». L’activation du service SSH local exige en effet ces droits, dont l’extension ne dispose pas sur la plupart des ordinateurs sous macOS et Windows.
Les ordinateurs touchés ne sont pas sains pour autant. Même quand le tunnel échouait, l’extension ajoutait bien la clé de l’attaquant, installait ses scripts de persistance et transmettait les informations sur la machine. Cursor indique avoir travaillé avec l’hébergeur cloud du serveur malveillant pour le mettre hors ligne.
Cursor affirme avoir par ailleurs retiré la version malveillante dès sa détection et bloqué sa distribution, puis avoir fermé entièrement sa boutique d’extensions par précaution, le temps de vérifier qu’aucune autre extension n’avait été compromise et de la reconstruire.
Reste une interrogation centrale : l’avis ne dit pas comment l’attaquant est parvenu à publier, dans la boutique de Cursor, une version de l’extension portant le nom d’Anthropic.

articles.title: Le nouveau casque Sony WH-1000XM4C est déjà en promotion chez Boulanger — Frandroid
articles.text:
Le 7 septembre, Sony a officialisé son WH-1000XM4C. Il s’agit d’une mise à jour de son XM4, sorti en 2020, qui restait encore intéressant six ans plus tard. Le casque revient ainsi au catalogue, dont il avait disparu en juillet, avec quelques nouveautés comme un son retravaillé. Chez Boulanger, le Black Friday prend de l’avance et ce XM4C perd déjà 25 euros grâce à un code promo.
Pourquoi porter le Sony WH-1000XM4C ?
- Pour la réduction de bruit qui n’a pas pris une ride
- Pour la restitution sonore améliorée et inspirée du XM6
- Pour les oreillettes confortables et le design pliable
En entrant le code AUDIO10 sur le site de Boulanger, vous pourrez profiter du Sony WH-1000XM4C pour 224,99 euros au lieu de 249,99 euros.
Si, par la suite, l’offre mentionnée dans cet article n’est plus disponible, merci de jeter un coup d’œil ci-dessous afin de dénicher d’autres offres concernant le Sony WH-1000XM4C. Le tableau s’actualise automatiquement.
Entre tradition et modernité
Sony ne s’est pas contenté de ressortir son XM4 comme il l’était en 2020 même si les deux appareils se ressemblent énormément. La marque nippone a apporté quelques modifications héritées du XM6. Les transducteurs de 40 mm signent leur retour, mais Sony a revu les réglages sonores pour se rapprocher du XM6.
Ce XM4C récupère la puce QN1 de son aîné. La réduction de bruit repose ainsi sur la même électronique que celle du XM4 standard. Les atouts et les défauts sont donc les mêmes. D’un côté, le XM4C arrive parfaitement à atténuer des bruits tels que les conversations dans un open space. De l’autre, il peine à effacer totalement les bruits de moteurs, ce qui peut être légèrement gênant lorsque vous prenez le métro ou l’avion.
Évidemment, Sony n’a pas sorti un XM6 bis et a fait l’impasse sur quelques éléments. Un tour dans l’application de Sony suffit pour s’en rendre compte, puisque le mode transparence adaptatif n’y figure pas.
Une mise à jour réussie ?
Avec son WH-1000XM4C, Sony prépare surtout la retraite du XM5. Selon What Hi-Fi, la batterie du XM5 n’est pas conforme au futur règlement européen, et le casque quittera le catalogue avant février 2027 pour laisser sa place au XM4C. Outre la bonne restitution sonore évoquée plus haut, le design reste inchangé. Le casque reste donc pliable, contrairement au XM5. Sony est d’ailleurs revenu à un arceau pliable sur le XM6.
Comme le XM4, le XM4C a des oreillettes qui englobent bien les oreilles et un arceau rembourré qui appuie peu sur le crâne. Il reste donc confortable même après de longues heures d’écoute.
Mais alors, pourquoi ressortir un casque qui avait déjà tout ça ? Le XM4 avait quitté le catalogue parce que sa batterie n’était pas conforme au règlement européen sur les batteries. À partir de février 2027, ce texte impose que les batteries des appareils portables puissent être retirées et remplacées par l’utilisateur. Pour remettre son casque en vente, Sony a donc changé de batterie. La nouvelle est plus petite et tient 27 heures avec l’ANC et 34 heures sans, contre 30 et 38 heures sur le XM4.
Les quelques améliorations de ce Sony WH-1000XM4C lui permettent-elles de se glisser parmi les meilleurs casques du moment ? Pour le savoir, rendez-vous dans notre guide des meilleurs casques Bluetooth.
Black Friday 2026 : pour ne rien rater des meilleures offres Tech
Le Black Friday n’est plus qu’un week-end de bonnes affaires, mais tout un mois de promotions. On peut même parler de Black Month. Quoi qu’il en soit, c’est un bon moment pour faire ses achats de fin d’année et nous allons vous aider à trouver la pépite Tech qu’il vous faut.

articles.title: Meta, Google y Amazon podían permitirse derrochar en IA cuando el negocio iba bien. Google acaba de descubrir qué pasa cuando no
articles.text:
Tres de las empresas más rentables del mundo acaban de pasar por una temporada de resultados floja, flojísima. Y precisamente los negocios que las hicieron ricas no son el verdadero problema. Alphabet (matriz de Google) lleva perdidos más de 500.000 millones de dólares en valor de mercado en un solo día, y Meta y Amazon también han visto caer sus acciones tras presentar informes. El hilo conductor son las sumas masivas de dinero que están destinando a la inteligencia artificial.
Por qué importa. Durante años, las Big Tech fueron la apuesta más segura del mercado porque generaban montañas de efectivo. No me malinterpretes, lo siguen generando. Pero ahora, la carrera de la IA se está comiendo ese efectivo, y los inversores se preguntan cuánto tiempo podrán seguir financiándola. Se proyecta que Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon y Meta gasten muy por encima de los 700.000 millones de dólares este año en centros de datos, chips y redes, según comparten desde Reuters.
Los números. Según el informe del último trimestre financiero de Alphabet, los ingresos aumentaron un 25% hasta los 127.600 millones de dólares, y los ingresos de Google Cloud han conseguido generar más del doble que los del mismo periodo del año anterior, alcanzando casi los 31.000 millones de dólares. Visto así, parece que todo bien. Pero aún así, las acciones cayeron casi un 13% el jueves, y el valor de la compañía descendió de 3,97 billones de dólares a 3,46 billones de dólares. De un plumazo.
Dos problemas explican el porqué:
- La búsqueda se está desacelerando. En el mismo informe se especifica que la publicidad en Google Search creció un 12% interanual, por debajo del 17% del segundo trimestre y del 19% del primero. En total, este trimestre Alphabet ha generado 82.000 millones de dólares en ingresos publicitarios, una cifra por debajo de las expectativas de Wall Street, que eran de 83.400 millones de dólares, según Reuters.
- Flujo de caja negativo. Alphabet registró un flujo de caja libre negativo de 9.100 millones de dólares, su segundo trimestre negativo consecutivo tras décadas de férreos ingresos. El flujo de caja libre es lo que queda después de que una empresa paga sus operaciones e inversiones. Que sea negativo indica que está gastando más de lo que ingresa. Y ya te puedes imaginar por qué el gasto supera los ingresos: IA.
La IA se come el negocio. El director comercial de Google, Philipp Schindler, achacaba la desaceleración de los anuncios en las búsquedas en parte a un mayor uso del Modo IA, la versión de búsqueda al estilo de chatbot que Google todavía está averiguando cómo monetizar, según comparten desde Reuters. En otras palabras, la inteligencia artificial que Google está construyendo parece estar debilitando el producto que la financia.
- Meta. Las acciones cayeron casi un 7% después de que la empresa informara de un flujo de caja libre negativo de 2.120 millones de dólares y elevara la previsión de gasto de capital para 2026 a un rango de entre 135.000 millones y 145.000 millones de dólares, según cuenta CNBC. Y mal asunto para los mercados de crédito, pues ahora el coste de asegurar la deuda de Meta en caso de impago alcanzaba un máximo histórico. Eso sí, los ingresos fueron sólidos, con un aumento del 26% hasta los 64.600 millones de dólares.
- Amazon. Según el último informe, las ventas crecieron un 11% hasta los 201.000 millones de dólares, pero su flujo de caja de 42.000 millones de dólares también fue negativo. Las acciones cayeron un 6% en las operaciones fuera de horario. Su CEO, Andy Jassy, defendía el gasto argumentando que Amazon tiene dos negocios potenciales de un billón de dólares, y señaló sus chips internos y su plataforma de IA Bedrock. Admite que "sería más cómodo" si los costes se repartieran a lo largo de 25 años, pero dijo que “ese no es el mundo en el que vivimos".
Menos mal que está la nube. Es el único lugar donde el dinero está regresando claramente en la mayoría de grandes tecnológicas. En el caso de Alphabet, la cartera de pedidos de Google Cloud ha alcanzado los 561.000 millones de dólares. Y sobre el gasto en IA, el problema para estas empresas es que hay cierto escepticismo en el mercado, pues construir capacidad hoy no garantiza que la demanda la cubra mañana. Y Alphabet ya ha declarado que su gasto de capital para 2027 aumentará significativamente, desde los 195.000 millones a 205.000 millones de dólares.
Microsoft. Ha sido la única empresa de las cuatro grandes que, en cierta medida, ha parado la debacle. Y es que tal y como contábamos recientemente, sus ingresos aumentaron casi un 20% hasta los 92.000 millones de dólares, Azure creció un 48% y el flujo de caja libre (muy positivo) alcanzó los 19.600 millones de dólares, unos 1.000 millones por encima de las previsiones. Reuters afirma que las acciones subieron más de un 5% en las operaciones fuera de horario, aunque al día siguiente cayeron un 1%.

articles.title: Physicists discover “astonishing” property of light that defies expectations
articles.text:
Physicists discover “astonishing” property of light that defies expectations
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- University of East Anglia
- Summary:
- Scientists have uncovered a surprising hidden ability of light that allows it to develop spinning, twisting behavior as it travels through empty space, without special lenses, mirrors, or materials. Researchers discovered that light’s internal geometry can naturally produce left- and right-handed patterns, challenging long-standing assumptions about how light behaves. By carefully arranging a beam’s structure, scientists can control where and how these spinning patterns emerge, unlocking a new way to manipulate light.
- Share:
Scientists have discovered a surprising ability of light that allows it to develop spinning patterns as it moves through empty space, without relying on special lenses, mirrors, or materials. The finding reveals that light possesses a hidden geometric structure that can influence its behavior in ways researchers previously thought were difficult to achieve.
The discovery comes from an international team led by researchers at the University of East Anglia (UEA) in the United Kingdom, working with scientists in South Africa. Their experiments demonstrate that carefully prepared light can be controlled through its own internal geometry, offering a new approach to manipulating how light spins and twists.
The findings challenge long-standing assumptions about how different properties of light interact. They could eventually lead to more sensitive medical tests, faster and more secure communications, and advanced quantum technologies that use light to transmit and protect information.
Why the Direction of Light's Spin Matters
One of the most intriguing aspects of the discovery involves chirality, a scientific term describing the difference between left-handed and right-handed structures.
Human hands provide a familiar example. Although they are mirror images of each other, a left hand cannot be perfectly superimposed on a right hand. Many molecules have a similar property, including compounds used in medicines. Two versions of the same molecule can have nearly identical chemical structures yet produce very different effects in the body.
Scientists can distinguish these molecular forms by studying how they interact with light that has a particular rotational behavior. Traditionally, producing and controlling such light has often involved specialized materials, carefully designed surfaces, or powerful lenses that focus beams extremely tightly.
The research demonstrates that appropriately prepared light can develop this behavior naturally as it travels, without requiring those additional optical components.
"Our work shows that light can naturally develop this handed behavior all on its own," said Dr. Kayn Forbes from UEA's School of Chemistry, Pharmacy and Pharmacology.
"You just have to prepare it in the right way.
"Most people think of light as traveling in straight lines. But scientists can also create structured light -- light whose brightness, shape, and direction are carefully arranged.
"One extreme example is light that twists as it travels, forming a corkscrew shape known as an optical vortex. Each twist can carry information, making this kind of light valuable for high-speed internet, secure communications, and advanced sensors.
"Light can also spin as it travels, depending on how it is polarized. This spin can be left-handed or right-handed -- another form of chirality."
Scientists Discover How Light Develops a Hidden Spin
Light can exhibit different kinds of rotational behavior. An optical vortex, for example, has a wave pattern that twists around its direction of travel, much like a corkscrew. Light also has a property known as polarization, which describes how its electric field oscillates. Certain polarization patterns produce a form of rotation called spin.
Physicists have long studied the relationship between these two properties. However, the interactions responsible for the newly observed effect were generally considered extremely weak and difficult to detect without specialized experimental conditions.
The researchers found that the situation changes when a beam of light is prepared in a particular balanced configuration.
Under those conditions, the beam can initially have no spin, yet distinct regions with spinning behavior emerge as it travels through free space. The effect does not require the light to pass through engineered materials or additional optical devices.
"It starts off with no spin at all," explained MSc student Light Mkhumbuza, who carried out key experiments. "But as the beam travels forward, spinning regions appear and separate out -- almost as if the spin was hiding and then revealed itself."
Rather than creating spin through an external optical component, the researchers demonstrated how the beam's existing internal structure can determine where spinning regions develop during propagation.
The Hidden Geometry That Controls Light
To explain this unexpected behavior, the researchers turned to topology, a mathematical field concerned with properties that remain unchanged when objects are continuously stretched, bent, or reshaped.
Dr. Isaac Nape, from the University of the Witwatersrand in Johannesburg, South Africa, offered a simple way to understand the concept.
"To explain it, imagine a mug and a doughnut," he said. "You can morph one into the other without tearing it, because they both have one hole. That hole is a topological feature."
The researchers found that structured light possesses its own topological characteristics, encoded in the arrangement of its polarization.
This underlying pattern acts like a mathematical fingerprint. Even as the light beam changes shape while traveling, its topological structure remains, influencing how different regions of the beam evolve.
As a result, the arrangement of the light itself can determine where its left-handed and right-handed spinning patterns become visible.
The discovery gives scientists a way to guide this behavior by designing the beam's initial structure, rather than depending on specialized materials to produce the desired effect.
"This gives us a completely new tuning knob for light. By adjusting its topology, we can decide how and where chirality appears," said Dr. Nape.
Potential Breakthroughs in Medicine and Communications
The ability to control light through its geometry could eventually make several important optical technologies simpler, more affordable, and more versatile.
One particularly promising application involves medical diagnostics and pharmaceutical research. Because many biologically important molecules have left-handed and right-handed forms, carefully structured light could help scientists identify these differences with greater sensitivity. Such tools could be valuable for evaluating drug safety and detecting biological markers associated with disease.
The same principles could support smaller optical sensors capable of identifying chemicals or biological substances without requiring large, sophisticated laboratory instruments.
Communications technology could also benefit. By encoding information into different twisting and spinning patterns, researchers may be able to increase the amount of data carried by individual light beams. This could contribute to faster optical communications, improved information security, and future quantum networks.
Other potential uses include manipulating microscopic particles, cells, and molecules with light, as well as developing more resilient quantum systems. Topological properties may help protect delicate quantum information against certain forms of noise and interference.
"The implications are wide-ranging," said Dr. Forbes. "This work could lead to simpler and more sensitive medical tests, especially in drug development.
"It could also be used to pack more information into laser beams -- boosting data capacity for communications, including future quantum networks.
"And because the effect doesn't rely on fragile materials or precision-engineered surfaces, it could be easier and cheaper to use in real-world technologies.
"This research could lay the foundations for a new generation of light-based technologies, by showing that light's behavior can be controlled using its own internal geometry," he added.
These applications remain possibilities for future development, but the underlying discovery provides researchers with another way to design and control the behavior of light.
A Hidden Property of Light Finally Revealed
For decades, scientists have relied on increasingly sophisticated optical equipment to produce and manipulate unusual forms of light. The findings suggest that some of these behaviors can instead arise from carefully designed structures already encoded within a light beam.
By showing how topology governs the emergence of spinning regions during propagation, the team has revealed a previously underappreciated connection between light's geometry and its physical behavior.
The discovery also illustrates how much remains to be learned about something as familiar and extensively studied as light.
"For something so familiar, light is proving to be far richer, stranger and more powerful than anyone imagined," said Dr. Forbes.
"And astonishingly, this new behavior has been there all along -- just waiting to be seen."
The research, 'Topological Control of Chirality and Spin with Structured Light', was published in the journal Light: Science & Applications.
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of East Anglia. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Light Mkhumbuza, Pedro Ornelas, Angela Dudley, Isaac Nape, Kayn A. Forbes. Topological control of chirality and spin with structured light. Light: Science, 2026; 15 (1) DOI: 10.1038/s41377-026-02278-6

articles.title: Philadelphia’s Academy of Natural Sciences just closed – a blow for budding young scientists like me
articles.text:
When I was a freshman in college at Villanova University outside Philadelphia, I visited the Academy of Natural Sciences for the first time.
My friends who were Philly natives were my tour guides, and I was inspired by their passion for the exhibits. I listened not only to the facts they shared about the museum, but also their childhood stories surrounding it.
As a kid, I remember going to the American Museum of Natural History in New York City and looking up at the massive dinosaur displays. I wondered how creatures as big as those used to walk the same ground as me. My favorite exhibit was the Hall of Ocean Life, where behind the staircase you see a dark, unlit diorama of a giant squid attached to a sperm whale.
The museum gave my curiosity a place to grow.
Now, as a Ph.D. student in physics, I research black holes, with the goal of one day becoming a professor and mentoring students. I was shocked when I heard the news that the Academy of Natural Sciences would be closing.
Over 200 years of hands-on science
Founded in 1812, the Academy of Natural Sciences in Philadelphia is the country’s oldest natural science museum. For two centuries, it has played a vital role in scientific research, education and public engagement. The academy’s research centered heavily on biodiversity, evolution, paleontology and environmental science. In 2011, Drexel University acquired the academy and manages its endowment.
The academy had offered a range of experiences, from the Dinosaur Hall to its butterfly garden, and provided generations of visitors with opportunities to explore science beyond classrooms and textbooks.
On Sept. 1, 2026, however, Drexel University abruptly announced that the museum would close by the end of the month, citing financial difficulties and declining attendance. The last day it was open to visitors was Sept. 27, 2026.
Critics of the decision to close are rallying to “Save the Academy” and reopen it. Even members of the Philadelphia City Council expressed surprise that they had not been approached for support before the closing was announced.
The William Penn Foundation offered to cover operating subsidies for at least another year, potentially giving the academy time to explore a sustainable future. However, the museum remains closed for now, and Drexel maintains it needs a long-term financial solution. At a hearing on Oct. 26 that lasted nearly four hours, Philadelphia City Council members tried to understand why the museum closed and what Drexel would need to reopen it. The hearing is scheduled to resume on Nov. 16.
Cultivating future scientists
While museums may be viewed simply as sites for school field trips or family outings, their impact extends far beyond entertainment.
Natural science museums preserve scientific history through linking the past to future generations, supporting research and introducing young people to subjects they might otherwise never encounter. Philly kids who visited the academy could experience different ecosystems, from the snowy lands of the bobcat to rainforests home to giant monkeys. These dioramas are a snapshot in time that allow children to cultivate their own imagination and passions.
Not everyone has the opportunity to attend college or pursue a career in STEM. Museums help close that gap, giving families, students and children a chance to experience science firsthand – something that textbooks, social media and even classrooms sometimes cannot do.
Thinking back to my own childhood, I can pinpoint how my academic interests were fostered through museums, whether gazing up at galaxies at the Hayden Planetarium or sleeping under the belly of the blue whale in the Hall of Ocean Life. I was able to talk to real scientists in careers I dreamed to achieve, and I was told it was possible for me.
These experiences were integral to my becoming a first-generation college student and pursuing a career in academia. They made a career in science feel tangible rather than mystical or intimidating.

articles.title: Lista de códigos ocultos de Netflix para ver series y películas de terror en Halloween 2026
articles.text:
Durante la época de Halloween 2026, algunas personas pueden optar por ver películas o series de terror en Netflix.
Los códigos secretos de Netflix permiten explorar subcategorías específicas dentro del catálogo de terror. Para utilizarlos, los usuarios pueden ingresar el código correspondiente y acceder a contenidos vinculados con ese tipo de historias.
La selección incluye producciones de monstruos, vampiros, zombis, asesinos en serie y relatos sobrenaturales, entre otras alternativas para Halloween.
Códigos secretos de Netflix para películas y series de terror
- Películas de terror de serie B – 8195
- Películas de criaturas – 6895
- Películas de terror de culto – 10944
- Películas de terror en aguas profundas – 45028
- Películas de terror extranjeras – 8654
- Películas cómicas de terror – 89585
- Películas de monstruos – 947
- Películas slasher y de asesinos en serie – 8646
- Películas de terror sobrenatural – 42023
- Películas de terror de adolescentes – 52147
- Películas de terror de vampiros – 75804
- Películas de terror de hombres lobo – 75930
- Películas de terror de zombis – 75405
Por qué no ver películas de terror en XuperTV
Durante Halloween de 2026, muchas personas buscan películas y series de terror para ver en casa, pero Xuper TV, antes llamada Magis TV, no es una alternativa recomendable.
La aplicación ofrece contenidos audiovisuales y deportes en vivo sin una suscripción mensual, aunque su instalación y uso pueden exponer a los usuarios a riesgos de seguridad y también a problemas legales.
ESET, compañía de ciberseguridad, analizó la APK de Magis TV y detectó permisos críticos e invasivos que no corresponden a una plataforma convencional de streaming.
La firma clasificó este tipo de servicios como aplicaciones potencialmente indeseables y advirtió que esas autorizaciones podrían ser utilizadas con fines maliciosos.
El principal problema es que las aplicaciones de streaming no oficiales suelen distribuirse fuera de Google Play Store y App Store.
Para instalarlas, los usuarios deben recurrir a sitios web alternativos que pueden evitar los controles de calidad y seguridad de las tiendas oficiales. Esa vía facilita la distribución de software malicioso.
David González Cuautle, investigador de ESET Latinoamérica, señaló que la habilitación excesiva de permisos especiales y críticos es una señal de riesgo.
Según explicó, estas aplicaciones pueden comprometer tanto el dispositivo como toda la red doméstica. Además, podrían servir como puerta de entrada para malware, incluidos spyware, troyanos y herramientas orientadas al robo de información personal.
El uso de Xuper TV también plantea un riesgo legal. ESET indicó que retransmitir contenidos sin los derechos correspondientes vulnera la propiedad intelectual y puede derivar en bloqueos de proveedores de internet o acciones judiciales.
La advertencia se extiende a los Set-Top Boxes, dispositivos que se conectan al televisor para acceder a aplicaciones y contenidos audiovisuales.
Si fueron modificados para instalar aplicaciones piratas, firmware no oficial o archivos descargados desde páginas externas, pueden transformarse en puertas de entrada para malware y spyware en el hogar.
Dónde ver películas y series de forma gratuita y segura
YouTube, Pluto TV, Prime Video, RTVE Play y Plex son cinco alternativas para ver películas y series gratis en Fire TV. YouTube ofrece videos, documentales, conciertos, contenido educativo y series web sin necesidad de pagar una suscripción para acceder a su catálogo abierto.
Pluto TV reúne canales en vivo, películas, series y programas como CSI Miami, The Walking Dead, Daredevil y Naruto. Una de sus ventajas es que permite acceder a los contenidos sin iniciar sesión.
Prime Video cuenta con una sección llamada “Free”, donde se pueden encontrar títulos gratuitos como Alvin y las ardillas 2, El justiciero y Sin rastro.
RTVE Play, la plataforma de Radio Televisión Española, ofrece series, películas, documentales, informativos y programas como MasterChef. Plex, por su parte, incluye publicidad y propone producciones como Medici, The Dick Van Dyke Show y Hot Ones.

articles.title: TeamViewer Flaw Could Let Malicious Hosts Take Over Support Technicians’ Machines
articles.text:
A high-severity vulnerability in the popular remote-access tool TeamViewer could be exploited to take over a viewer’s (an IT support technician’s) system, cybersecurity firm Remedio warns.
Tracked as CVE-2026-111585 (CVSS score of 8.8), the flaw is described as an integer overflow affecting the remote-control screen processing component of TeamViewer clients across Windows, macOS, Linux, and Android.
Successful exploitation of the security defect could allow attackers to crash the viewer’s TeamViewer or execute arbitrary code on their system.
“Exploitation requires a user to establish a remote-control session to an attacker-controlled or compromised host,” TeamViewer notes in its advisory.
The issue, Remedio says, is rooted in how the host’s screen dimension is transmitted and used in the viewer: the host announces the geometry of the screen and the viewer uses the received dimensions to allocate an in-memory pixel buffer it then uses to decompress incoming screen updates.
This decode surface is only used if a hardware video decoder is not available for the session, but the host may refuse to negotiate the video codecs, thus forcing the viewer to that path.
A host can request a surface larger than what a screen can reach, and the path accepts it. An example would be 32768 by 32768 pixels at 32 bits per pixel, which overflows 32 bits, with every row past 31 being written out of bounds.
“The screen dimensions a host announces are used to size the drawing surface as-is, with no upper bound enforced on what arrives over the network,” Remedio explains.
The attacker-controlled host controls both the declared surface and the screen updates that can overflow the buffer, causing the viewer’s application to repeatedly crash.
“That means a malicious or compromised host can trigger the bug from inside an ordinary, established session, using only messages the protocol already supports,” Remedio explains.
In addition to triggering the denial-of-service (DoS) condition over a normal TeamViewer session, Remedio discovered that it could use CVE-2026-111585 to execute arbitrary code on the viewer’s system.
“The corrupted surface is a live object the viewer later calls through a pointer in its own first field, so overwriting that pointer redirects the call,” Remedio notes, explaining that it bypassed existing protections to route the call to WinExec and run the code in the viewer.
“The surface is reachable in the default configuration. An accepted session is all it takes, and that is the product’s normal mode of operation,” the company says.
Version 15.83 of TeamViewer’s clients (including Full Client, Host, Portable, and Remote Control App for Android) contains the necessary patches. TeamViewer also released security updates for multiple legacy versions.
The macOS and Linux updates also resolve CVE-2026-92372, an out-of-bounds write with similar consequences: an attacker could supply crafted screen-image data or convince a user to open a specially crafted TeamViewer session recording (.tvs) to execute arbitrary code.
“Missing destination bounds checking in the decoder allows crafted screen-image data to cause an out-of-bounds write to the image buffer. Exploitation requires user interaction,” TeamViewer notes.
On macOS, the updates also resolve CVE-2026-92374, a time-of-check-to-time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition with improper symbolic link handling flaw that could allow a low-privileged local attacker to install a malicious package and gain root privileges.
Additionally, TeamViewer patched six high-severity local privilege escalation vulnerabilities in the TeamViewer Remote Management add-ons, urging users to update both the clients and the components to the latest versions.
TeamViewer says it is not aware of any of these vulnerabilities being exploited in the wild.
