articles.title: Vizio’s discounted Mini LED TV lets you skip the sign-ups and smarts
articles.text:
Modern smart TVs let you skip the streaming device, which is convenient, but they also come with their own issues, including privacy concerns and frequent updates. The Vizio Mini LED Quantum TV lets you cut out the rigamarole and just get straight to the HDMI ports. And right now, it’s discounted at Walmart, with the 65-inch model going for $358 ($40 off) and the 85-inch model going for $698 ($100 off).
Vizio’s discounted Mini LED TV lets you skip the sign-ups and smarts
If you prefer a dedicated streaming device or console, you can save some cash on an otherwise-modern television.
Although Vizio’s Mini LED TV comes loaded with Vizio OS, you can bypass the TV’s host of agreements during setup. By pushing past the manufacturer’s warnings about “missing out” on smart TV features, you can disable the built-in operating system, letting you use your own streaming device like a Roku or Apple TV 4K without worrying about what data Vizio and Walmart might be collecting.
As for specs, the TV features quantum dots for full, vivid color and high brightness (our testing showed it can reach 936 nits when calibrated thanks to its mini-LED panel). There are some compromises, though, which is expected given the low price point. The IPS panel doesn’t have the best black levels, as you might see on more expensive sets, and there’s a touch of motion blur during faster scenes, which may also hurt its appeal for gamers. It also has three HDMI ports, but they’re only 2.0, although the screen only supports up to 4K at 60Hz, so it’s not detrimental to the experience.

articles.title: 4 real? Tracking exploitation and patching of eMudhra’s weak keys
articles.text:
4 real? Tracking exploitation and patching of eMudhra’s weak keys
On October 19, 2026, we learned about eMudhra’s eight shockingly weak keys: where eMudhra was trusted to pick a 115-digit number for their virtual combination lock protecting the Internet, they picked the number 4. Not even four digits, just the number 4. The other seven keys were similarly weak: 56, 66, 115, 155, 156, 230 and 237.
The next day, we wrote a blog post on the immediate action we took to mitigate this leak, and what customers needed to do on their end to stay secure. Now, we are sharing a more in-depth follow up on the evidence we’ve seen of exploitation, and the progress seen on visitors patching their systems.
Let's start with the scale of the problem. A certificate authority (CA) with weak keys this serious is unprecedented, and the potential consequences are significant. While there have been plenty of compromised certification authorities in the past (such as DigiNotar, TÜRKTRUST, and TrustWave), access to their keys has always been contained to a degree; these incidents gave a limited set of attackers or organizations the ability to issue fraudulent certificates. The eMudhra incident is fundamentally different; the affected intermediate private keys could be recovered almost instantly by anyone from the public certificates themselves. Anyone can independently recover these same signing keys and create certificates for any domain that an unpatched client not enforcing Certificate Transparency would accept.
eMudhra announced they’re exiting the public CA business and have claimed a mistake in a key generation script, but have not yet shared the script. They signed a certificate revocation list (CRL) with what might’ve been a correctly generated key, and subsequently corrected it to be signed with the weak key.
How did that come to be and why didn’t that set off alarms? Much has to be cleared up, including the role of the auditors and cross signers. This blog proposes the fixes and next steps for organizations to ensure they are secure.
Patching Cloudflare
Our primary concern remains the security impact on Cloudflare, our customers, and the Internet as a whole. At the time of writing, all high priority Cloudflare systems have been patched. A small number of confirmed low impact tickets is being worked on.
We started patching high-impact systems immediately on October 19. These included customer origin-facing proxies using Pingora, responsible for most of our outbound connections. These were patched in hours to reject the vulnerable eMudhra keys. At the same time, we started an AI-assisted analysis of our source code to find all other systems that trust these weak keys. Within four hours we had a full analysis. We assigned a ticket with preliminary analysis for each system, and asked the team to confirm and/or adjust the analysis before the end of the day. Where high impact was identified, we asked to patch immediately, and for the lower impact, remediation was due at the end of last week.
Has Cloudflare seen exploitation across its network?
To track whenever a customer’s server (or attacker) presents a certificate signed by eMudhra’s weak keys, we added logging to Pingora. As this outbound service accounts for the vast majority of outgoing TLS connections from a Cloudflare machine, any attacker attempting to snoop using the eMudhra keys would trigger this logging. The logging finished rolling out October 21.
At the time of writing, a week later, we’ve seen about 22,000 attempted handshakes with the weak eMudhra keys. Two-thirds of the attempts were fetches of test sites such as emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com (which we mentioned in the developer guidance in our earlier post). Almost all of the remaining third went to origins who appeared to set up a certificate for themselves using the weak intermediate. Every handshake configured to verify the certificate was refused, as we already patched.
About 160 of these handshakes stood out: the certificates’ Subject Alternative Names (SANs) were naming other organizations’ domains, unrelated to the Server Name Indication (SNI) requested in the handshake. Some of those names were domains related to consumer IoT devices. We noticed as well that those forged certificates were made after the keys leaked and some were valid for over two years, longer than any public CA may issue. However, these certificates looked like the servers' own default certificates rather than part of an attempt to intercept our connections. They named domains other than the ones being connected to, so they would have failed hostname verification anyway. And in several cases, a server presented the same certificate to connections from many of our locations, which means it came from the server itself rather than from something on a single network path.
Thus while there is no evidence of the weak keys being used to intercept Cloudflare's connections so far, these keys appear to have been used to forge certificates within hours of the weakness becoming public: one of the forged certificates we saw was dated October 20 at 18:19 UTC, less than an hour after Mozilla's bug report was made public. This does not exclude carefully targeted interception. For that we have to rely on the usual indirect signals of system compromise — and so far, we have not seen any such signals.
How many visitors are still vulnerable?
So much about patching Cloudflare, but what about our visitors? We cannot directly test whether a visitor still trusts the weak keys without breaking connections, so we have to do something more indirect. For that we used our challenge pages:
We rolled out an update to send out two probe connections on a fraction of challenge pages: one probe to ca1.cloudflarecaptcha.com and one to ca2.cloudflarecaptcha.com. Initially we installed an eMudhra signed certificate on ca1.cloudflarecaptcha.com and a regularly signed certificate on ca2.cloudflarecaptcha.com as control. Then we record whether these probes succeeded. This allows us to see if visitors that are served a challenge page still trust the weak eMudhra keys.
What did we find? With 50 million probes over the last week, we see this:
Big caveat upfront: by design the traffic to these challenge pages is highly skewed. There are many (unconfirmed) bots in there. Also, only clients that execute JavaScript (like browsers) will send probes.
The jump in the data is due to the following changes—all times are UTC:
- October 23 15:30, we changed our control endpoint to also serve an eMudhra certificate, but this time without signed certificate timestamps (SCTs). There were some differences in acceptance, but not large. We could’ve added a new endpoint, but that would’ve required a slow release of our challenge platform. Changing the endpoint was easier.
- October 23 16:30, our challenge platform rolled back to a previous version because of an unrelated issue. The probes returned October 27 at 10:00.
- October 27 16:37, we noticed we did not send the G3 cross-sign, which not all clients knew about, and added it to both endpoints. We removed SCTs from both.
- October 27 16:49, we switched ca2 to chain up to the AAA Certificate Services root.
- October 27 18:18, we ramped up probes to be included from 1% to 10% of all challenge pages served on non-paying customer zones.
With those caveats out of the way: what do we notice? Up-to-date modern browsers are mostly patched, but bots and old browsers are not. Also embedded browsers, like Android WebView, lag behind patching with 30–40% still accepting. Over the first weekend (with the monitoring gap), we see clear evidence of patching, but afterwards we see little movement.
On October 29 around 18:00 UTC, we released a detection that caught a large influx of bot traffic identifying as Chrome 150-154 on macOS. This can look like patching in the top graph, but it is actually a change in traffic classification: the same user agents show a corresponding increase in acceptance among traffic with bot signals detected in the bottom graph.
Chrome 150-154 on Linux is the notable exception: its acceptance continues to decline, consistent with further patching in that cohort. Given the bot-heavy and changing traffic mix, that evidence is suggestive rather than conclusive. Otherwise, we still see little movement.
Breaking down by network (ASN) we see:
Across the large networks, more than half of probes still accept the compromised chain, both among traffic with no bot signals detected (top graph) and traffic with bot signals detected (bottom graph). Over the weekend we saw some patching, but afterwards the trend has been flat.
The big caveat still holds: traffic is skewed by (unconfirmed) bots. But bots are also just software that need security updates. And if they’re in any way representative of overall software updates, then the picture is quite dire indeed.
What can you do?
Patch! Dennis Jackson has a great crowdsourced website with instructions. Especially if you’re a developer on macOS, you want to follow these instructions. If you’re a Cloudflare customer, check out last week’s blog post on what needs to be done on your end when using certain products like WARP or Tunnel.
Looking ahead
At Cloudflare, we have a quick-revocation mechanism in place in some products. To bring it to more systems at Cloudflare and industry, we’re excited about projects like upki that understand a trust store can’t be a static list of root certificate authorities, but needs the ability to be quickly updated with information like revocation and certificate transparency keys. As vulnerabilities are discovered at a faster pace than ever, it is vital that they can be addressed quickly and effectively.

articles.title: Switches Hall Effect et écran Oled : Logitech place la barre très haut avec son clavier magnétique G Pro X Rapid
articles.text:
| Type de clavier | Gaming | 
| Sans fil | Non | 
| Format | TKL | 
| Pavé numérique | Non | 
| Type d'interrupteurs | Magnétique | 
| Poids | 1008 g | 
| Rétroéclairage | Oui | 
Héritier direct du Pro X TKL, le Logitech G Pro X2 Rapid est un clavier gaming au format TKL (Tenkeyless) alimenté par des switches analogiques à effet Hall. Résolument pensé pour l'esport, il est compatible avec les technologies SOCD-Cleaner et l'ajustement des points d’actionnement.
À sa sortie en 2023, le Pro X TKL de Logitech se voulait le clavier mécanique de référence pour qui voulait jouer sans se prendre la tête. S'était ensuivi en 2025 une itération d'apparence toute similaire, mais qui passait aux commutateurs analogiques à effet Hall, dernière lubie à la mode du marché des boards gaming.
Un an et quelques mois plus tard, la gamme du fabricant suisse revient avec un châssis revu et des nouveautés très menues. Placé dans le haut de gamme de la branche Logitech G, le Pro X2 Rapid emprunte les codes de design de la Pro X2 Superstrike… Son placement tarifaire, autour de 220 €, l’installe parmi les claviers les plus onéreux de notre comparatif.
Si l'on pouvait reprocher à la marque suisse d'être fainéante sur ses designs il y a quelques années, force est de constater que le millésime récent des périphériques Logitech G prend enfin quelques risques. Ils sont certes ténus, mais c'est déjà ça de pris : après les couleurs du G512 X, le Pro X2 Rapid fait le choix (relativement) audacieux de tailler son châssis comme un bloc de plastique uni. Le profil est ainsi bien moins en pente que sur la plupart des claviers de cet acabit, mais la construction en plastique PBT est de bonne facture.
Son profil particulier nous oblige à mentionner le repose-poignets intégré et sa forme plutôt particulière. Le G512 X évoqué plus haut proposait un repose-poignets (optionnel) en silicone dur et transparent pour laisser passer le rétroéclairage de sa bande avant. De la même manière, celui du Pro X2 Rapid, inclus dans la boîte, se veut le prolongement du look du clavier. Il est donc en gomme dure, propice aux traces, mais il a surtout la particularité d'être complètement perpendiculaire, même dans sa partie avant.
Un drôle de choix, car les repose-poignets ont pour habitude d'avoir une courbure marquée pour épouser la forme desdits poignets. En conséquence, on sent le coin avant s'enfoncer dans l'avant-bras, ce qui n'est pas particulièrement agréable ni confortable.
La sérigraphie du Pro X2 Rapid est dans la droite lignée des précédents claviers Logitech. On comprend qu'elle est propre sur les caractères alphanumériques universels, mais moins gracieuse sur les caractères spécifiques aux dispositions régionales, avec des contours peu élégants qui peuvent être facilement repérés par tout regard averti. On se rassure néanmoins avec la construction en PBT des touches qui, rappelons-le, est bien plus résistante à l'usure et aux autres aléas du temps.
Comme précisé en introduction, le Logitech G Pro X2 Rapid est dénué de toute connectivité sans-fil. Ce n'est pas faute d'avoir vu des claviers à switches HE profiter de l'interface radio 2,4 GHz, preuve qu'il est possible de profiter de cette technologie relativement jeune sans avoir à gérer un câble en plus, a fortiori sur un segment tarifaire aussi élevé.
Néanmoins, pour un produit qui se veut tourné vers l'e-sport ou a minima vers les gamers effrayés à l'idée d'une quelconque interférence dans leurs commandes, il n'est pas étonnant de voir Logitech privilégier la fiabilité de l'interface par-dessus une versatilité supplémentaire.
Preuve en est, la présence d'un interrupteur pour basculer en “mode jeu” sur la tranche droite du clavier. Il permet de désactiver les commandes du clavier, à l'exception d'une sélection de touches dédiées au jeu. La fonctionnalité n'a rien de nouveau, puisqu'elle est déjà largement adoptée par les constructeurs. La présence d'un interrupteur physique est néanmoins pratique pour ne pas avoir à basculer sur l'application G Hub. Seule sa forme change par rapport au G512 X.
Toujours du côté de l'interface physique, l'autre gimmick du Pro X2 Rapid est la présence d'un petit écran Oled monochrome dans sa partie droite. Contrôlable via la molette placée juste en dessous, il permet d'ajuster plusieurs fonctionnalités du clavier à la volée, comme les motifs du rétroéclairage ou la distance d'actionnement des touches, avec une mémoire intégrée pour conserver toutes ces modifications. Un accessoire qui peut paraître frivole sur d'autres claviers plus modestes, mais qui permet effectivement d'utiliser le Pro X2 Rapid sans passer par la suite logicielle. Pratique pour les baroudeurs de LAN.
Notre appréciation de la frappe du Pro X2 Rapid n'est qu'une question de ressenti à l'utilisation en l'absence de moyen concret. Ceci étant, le board nous a paru tout à fait réactif lors de nos sessions sur Counter-Strike (sans le SOCD, évidemment), tout comme l'ont été les précédents claviers magnétiques de la marque, comme le G512 X. Le bruit du Pro X2 Rapid n'a néanmoins pas grand-chose à voir puisque ses six couches d'insonorisation étouffent la mélodie de la frappe pour un son creamy, ou rond à l'oreille, fort agréable.
Le Logitech G Pro X2 Rapid incorpore donc des switches magnétiques linéaires à effet Hall (aussi appelés analogiques de par leur nature personnalisable) du fabricant Gateron, soit le modèle KS-20 en POM. Il est ainsi possible d'ajuster leur point d'actionnement entre 0,1 et 4 mm, des valeurs habituelles pour cette technologie, mais aussi la course de réinitialisation pour pouvoir s’adonner au rapid fire sans se fatiguer le doigt.
Enfin, les switches magnétiques autorisent aussi le double assignement de commande par touche en fonction de la distance d'enfoncement. De même, le SOCD-Cleaner, qui permet de prioriser une touche par rapport à une autre lors d'une pression simultanée, est une fonctionnalité attendue pour les claviers gaming de cet acabit.
Comme d'habitude avec les produits Logitech G, la personnalisation du clavier s’effectue via la solution logicielle G Hub. Rien de nouveau de ce côté-là : l'interface est toujours claire et détaillée avec des illustrations pour une meilleure visualisation des ajustements de frappe. Elle reste néanmoins réservée à sa seule version native Windows et macOS, sans équivalent sur Linux, et ne dispose toujours pas de web-app. La concurrence tend pourtant progressivement en ce sens, qu'il s'agisse de Razer ou d'Asus.
Le Logitech G Pro X2 Rapid remplit le cahier des charges d'un clavier gaming premium : une construction réussie, une frappe agréable, et il ne lésine pas sur les fonctionnalités annexes pour les PGM les plus exigeants. Malgré toutes ses qualités, il peine à justifier son ticket d'entrée particulièrement élevé, surtout au vu d'une concurrence toujours plus féroce sur le terrain des claviers magnétiques.
Proposé pour moins cher, le Logitech G515 Rapid TKL est toujours un choix efficace, même s'il n'inclut pas d'écran Oled. Le G512 X, aussi, est un clavier personnalisable intéressant de la marque suisse.

articles.title: How to Check and Configure NVIDIA GPUDirect Storage for Your Platform | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.text:
NVIDIA GPUDirect Storage (GDS) accelerates GPU storage access in on-premises and cloud environments. It provides a robust, portable, and efficient data path between NVIDIA GPUs and storage targets to increase bandwidth, minimize latency, and reduce CPU and memory utilization across a broad range of platforms, application frameworks, and workload patterns.
Configuring NVIDIA GPUDirect Storage starts with understanding your environment. Which settings and storage paths are appropriate for your platform and workload? Extensive documentation describes how to configure and troubleshoot supported architectures and storage solutions, but you must navigate this information and optimize your deployment.
The gds-diag tool was developed by the GPUDirect Storage team to simplify optimization and configuration of GPUDirect Storage. gds-diag is a simple, open-source command-line utility that assesses environments, identifies problems, and suggests improvements to help you make the most of your GDS deployment.
It is also bundled with an optional agent skill that adds a natural-language interface and orchestration layer. The skill interprets your intent, selects and invokes the appropriate subcommands, and coordinates multi-step diagnostic workflows. Beyond command selection and routing, the skill extends gds-diag with model-guided reasoning. It can interpret diagnostic results, apply relevant system context, and propose or carry out appropriate remediation.
This post shows you how to get started with gds-diag using either the command-line interface or the agent skill.
Download and installation
To use gds-diag, you need a Linux system with Python 3.8 or newer. GPUDirect Storage requires an NVIDIA datacenter-class GPU and NVIDIA CUDA Toolkit 12.2 or newer, but these are not dependencies of gds-diag itself.
gds-diag is distributed as part of the NVIDIA Magnum IO GitHub repository with no other dependencies to install. Clone the repository on the machine where you plan to run it with git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/MagnumIO.git and select one of the following usage models:
- Command-line tool: This provides a deterministic, minimal-dependency path to diagnose GDS deployments. Go to the gds-diag directory, run gds-diag.py --help, and follow the Command-line usage guidance.
- AI agent: This provides the most intuitive, flexible, interactive, natural-language mechanism to diagnose GDS deployments while still retaining the reliable determinism of the underlying command-line tool. Open the gds-diag directory in your preferred AI coding assistant and follow the Agent skill usage guidance.
| Quick tip: The AI agent mode is recommended if this option is available in your environment. gds-diag is validated with both Claude and Codex, though it may work with other tools as well. | 
|---|
Command-line usage
The gds-diag command-line tool is a single Python script with multiple subcommands to focus on different diagnostic tasks. You can browse available subcommands by running ./gds-diag.py --help.
For more information about a specific subcommand, run ./gds-diag.py <subcommand> --help.
| Quick tip: Not sure where to start? Just run ./gds-diag.py all /path/to/check, and gds-diag will automatically run a complete sequence of diagnostics for that path. This works in bare-metal, virtual machine, and container environments. | 
|---|
Figure 2 groups the available subcommands into four categories.
Choose a diagnostic category based on your stage of deployment or the problem you need to investigate.
- End-to-end checks: Use all to automatically select appropriate diagnostics for your environment and run them in sequence.
- Preparing for installation: Use pre-install to check GPU support and CUDA Toolkit installation. Use support-matrix to view supported storage targets and plan your deployment.
- Validating an installation: Use post-install to check whether GDS is installed correctly and identify blockers. Use config-audit to review configuration files and environment variables that influence GDS behavior.
- Deep diagnostics: Use container-check to assess GDS support in container environments, including containerd, Docker, Enroot, and Kubernetes. Use mount-check to diagnose a specific mount point or directory.
The anatomy of a gds-diag finding
The output of most gds-diag subcommands is presented as a set of findings grouped into sections, as Figure 3 shows.
Each finding and each section has a status badge.
- “FAIL” indicates a hard blocker.
- “WARN” indicates a potential blocker.
- “INFO” communicates notable information.
- “PASS” indicates a nominal finding and is shown only when you use the --verbose option.
Each finding includes an explanation followed by a mitigation plan. gds-diag will not implement the mitigation plan or otherwise modify the system on its own. Its role is to identify problems and optimization opportunities and help you or your administrator make improvements. Multiple sections (and findings within those sections) may be shown.
| Quick tip: You can also emit all diagnostic reports as structured JSON data with the --json command-line option. This could be useful if you plan to ingest findings into another tool or archive them for future reference. | 
|---|
Most subcommands follow the same structure. The gds-diag.py support-matrix command is a notable exception: it emits output in the form of a table with footnotes. This subcommand shows which platform combinations GDS supports.
Use the --static option to present general data (shown in Figure 4) or the --live option to incorporate information from the system as presently configured.
Items marked in green are fully supported, items marked in yellow are supported depending on architectural or configuration caveats, and items marked in red are not supported.
| Quick tip: Most distributed storage vendors elect to present their file systems as nfs or nfs4 at the Linux operating system level, so this row of the support matrix corresponds to a broad range of product support. | 
|---|
Command-line demo
To demonstrate, consider preparing a new or modified GDS configuration file for production deployment. The config-audit subcommand is an ideal choice for this scenario. If called with no arguments, it will audit the current effective configuration, including both static configuration files and dynamic environment variable modifiers. The following example uses the --config option to specify a candidate configuration to review.
The configuration audit reveals a misspelled entry in the configuration file. After you correct the error, config-audit confirms that the configuration is valid and provides additional informational hints.
Agent skill usage
The gds-diag agent skill activates automatically when you open the gds-diag repository using a coding assistant such as Claude or Codex.
| Quick tip: You can explicitly activate gds-diag using the /gds-diag keyword in your coding assistant, but this isn’t strictly necessary. It will automatically choose it as the appropriate skill to use if you ask natural language questions about GDS. | 
|---|
The skill does not attempt to duplicate deterministic checks that are already provided by the gds-diag command-line tool. Instead, its primary role is to aid in routing between gds-diag subcommands and interpreting their output. The following are a few examples of queries you could pose using the skill:
- Is this system eligible to use GDS?
- Is it available for /mnt/data?
- How do I configure GDS optimally to access /mnt/data?
- What configuration files are being used by GDS?
- Do any configuration parameters need to be updated?
- Which NVMe device has the best locality to GPU3?
Agents are a capability multiplier for gds-diag; you can ask follow-up questions or even ask the agent to implement mitigations on your behalf.
Agent skill demo
Figure 6 shows how to combine the gds-diag agent skill with a model’s inherent reasoning to diagnose a container configuration problem. This example uses Anthropic Claude Code CLI.
In this case, the agent inspects the shell script used to launch the container and determines the best gds-diag tool to use to investigate the problem. It then offers the option to modify the script in response to its findings and confirms the solution. Note that the coding assistant will honor your local settings and site policies to determine which actions require confirmation.
Get started
Use gds-diag as your first diagnostic tool when investigating GPUDirect Storage configuration and optimization. Its modular design provides a foundation for additional diagnostics, such as checks for network transports, object storage systems, and application frameworks.
Have a diagnostic check or file system you would like to contribute? Community contributions are welcome and strongly encouraged. Both the source code and the agent skill are published under open-source licenses (Apache 2.0 and Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International). See the contributor guidelines to get started.

articles.title: Moins de 16 kg mais une mini-batterie : le Decathlon Btwin E-FL 900 arrive en février 2027 — Frandroid
articles.text:
À sa petite échelle, le Btwin E-FL 900 se fait autant désirer qu’un GTA VI du vélo électrique. Nous l’avions découvert par surprise lors du salon Eurobike en juin 2025, où nous avions pu le prendre en main immédiatement. Ainsi, nous avions – naïvement peut-être – pensé que Decathlon le commercialiserait dans la foulée, ce que confirmait la marque lors de sa présentation officielle en septembre 2025.
Plus d’un an s’est écoulé depuis, sans aucun signe du VAE pliant en magasin. Il est bien apparu sur certains sites officiels de la marque française, en Belgique ou au Royaume-Uni, mais sans date de disponibilité. Cette semaine, il en a fait de même en Allemagne. Cette fois, Decathlon accompagne la fiche produit d’un communiqué de presse, et d’une date.
La branche allemande annonce une disponibilité à partir de la mi-février 2027, en ligne et dans une sélection de magasins, soit près de 20 mois après sa découverte à l’Eurobike. Decathlon n’a pas encore donné de date pour la France, mais un lancement français dans la même fenêtre, cet hiver, paraît probable.
Un Btwin E-FL 900 au moteur vigoureux, avec une mini-batterie
Pour le vélo pliant électrique en lui-même, presque rien n’a bougé depuis la première découverte. Le Btwin E-FL 900 confirme son cadre aluminium aux roues de 16 pouces avec un pliage simple et le dépliage « 1 seconde », ainsi que son moteur Mahle X30. Logé dans le moyeu arrière, il développe un couple de 45 Nm pour une puissance nominale de 250 watts, ce qui suffit pour ce type de VAE. Decathlon l’associe à une transmission monovitesse par chaîne, simple et pratique en ville.
L’E-FL 900 porte une batterie amovible de 171 Wh derrière le tube de selle, légère et à recharge USB-C. En revanche, son autonomie reste limitée : 55 km annoncés en mode 1 sur 3, et seulement 25 km en mode 3 selon le dossier de presse anglais de Decathlon. Le vélo n’a pas non plus d’écran.
On note l’apparition d’une commande au guidon (qui manquait lors de la prise en main), tandis que la connectivité via l’application Mahle est possible (voir notre essai de l’Origine Montmartre pour les fonctionnalités). Côté équipement, le vélo est complet : freins hydrauliques à disques, éclairage, garde-boue et béquille. Lepoids est de 15,95 kg, soit assez léger pour être porté au quotidien.
Le vélo pliant électrique Decathlon confirme son tarif
Enfin, le prix du vélo électrique pliant Decathlon ne change pas : 1 999,99 €, soit 300 € de plus que l’actuel Btwin E Fold 900 (1 699,99 €), certes moins compact et abouti. Il reste cependant bien plus abordable qu’un UTO PRO16 (2 799 €) ou un O2feel JIM (2 999 €), plus haut de gamme avec un moteur à 2 vitesses automatiques et une batterie plus endurante (250 et 269 Wh). À noter, deux sacoches avant de 20 et 25 litres sont en option, tout comme le panier avant visible sur la photo (coût à définir).
Face à l’E Fold 900, cette nouvelle génération fait des choix nets. Decathlon passe des roues de 20 pouces à du 16 pouces et allège le vélo d’environ 3 kg (19 kg pour l’E Fold 900). La batterie descend de 252 Wh à 171 Wh, alors que le couple grimpe de 35 à 45 Nm. En clair, l’E-FL 900 vise d’abord ceux qui portent leur vélo dans le train ou le métro, sur des trajets courts.

articles.title: Warum Intel unter dem KI-Boom leidet, von dem es eigentlich profitieren wollte
articles.text:
Aktie stürzt ab: Warum Intel unter dem KI-Boom leidet, von dem es eigentlich profitieren wollte
Der Chipriese Intel hat auf einen Schlag mehr als ein Fünftel seines Werts verloren, weil die Geschäftsprognose des Konzerns die Börse schwer enttäuschte. Intel macht zu schaffen, dass wegen des explosiven Anstiegs der Speicherpreise weniger PCs verkauft werden. Hinzu kommen Lieferketten-Probleme bei Chips für Rechenzentren, bei denen es eine hohe Nachfrage gibt.
Intel sagte für das laufende Vierteljahr einen Umsatz zwischen 15 und 16 Milliarden Dollar vorher. Analysten hatten eher mit 17 Milliarden Dollar gerechnet. Beim bereinigten Gewinn pro Aktie verfehlte Intel mit einer Prognose von 25 US-Cent die Markterwartung von 43 Cent deutlich. Die Aktie stürzte im nachbörslichen US‑Handel um rund 22 Prozent ab.
Schwaches PC-Geschäft belastet Intel
Intel-Finanzchef David Zinsner sagte, das Unternehmen stelle seit Wochen eine Abschwächung des Geschäfts fest, weil wegen hoher Speicherpreise weniger Computer gekauft würden. Auch mindestens übers erste Halbjahr 2027 werde es keine Besserung geben, betonte er. Intel-Chef Lip-Bu Tan verwies darauf, dass der ganze Markt betroffen sei. Auch im gesamten kommenden Jahr würden die Speicherpreise ein schwerwiegendes Problem bleiben. Intel rechnet für 2027 mit einem Schrumpfen des PC-Marktes um zehn Prozent nach einem Rückgang um zwölf Prozent in diesem Jahr.
Intel spürt die Kehrseite des KI-Booms
Die Speicherpreise sind in den vergangenen Monaten wegen der hohen Nachfrage zum Ausbau von Rechenzentren für Künstliche Intelligenz explosiv gestiegen. Intel profitiert mit seinen Prozessoren ebenfalls vom KI-Boom. Man habe aber die Nachfrage nicht ausreichend bedienen können, sagte Lip-Bu Tan. Gründe dafür waren unter anderem Engpässe bei einigen Rohstoffen sowie die zeitweise Schließung einer Fabrik in Israel.
Im vergangenen Quartal legte der Umsatz im Jahresvergleich um 21 Prozent auf 16,5 Milliarden Dollar zu, was in etwa den Analystenerwartungen entsprach. Unterm Strich sank der Gewinn um 18 Prozent auf 3,3 Milliarden Dollar.
Die Intel-Aktie war in den vergangenen Monaten stark gestiegen – weil Anleger darauf setzten, dass der Konzern mit neuen Produktionsverfahren vom Geschäft mit Technik für Rechenzentren profitieren wird. Außerdem versucht Lip-Bu Tan, Intel ein zusätzliches Standbein als Auftragsfertiger für andere Chipanbieter aufzubauen. Der Konzern investiert in diesem Jahr rund 20 Milliarden Dollar in Fabriken und Ausrüstung. Für das kommende Jahr stellte Finanzchef Zinsner noch eine Erhöhung der Ausgaben in Aussicht.

articles.title: Raenest wants users to earn from their money, not just receive it
articles.text: Raenest, a Nigerian cross-border payments fintech, wants users to do more than receive money from abroad, its co-founder and chief executive officer, Richard Oyome, said at Moonshot 2026 in Lagos on Thursday. Oyome traced the company’s strategy to the evolution of Africa’s fintech market, which moved from expanding access to digital banking and lending to helping people receive payments from international clients as remote work grew during the COVID-19 pandemic. As more Africans began working for foreign companies and serving customers abroad, he said, the need for financial services that connect them to global markets grew. At Raenest Exchange 2026 on October 21, the company announced new products and features, including Raenest Vaults, a savings product offering annual yields of up to 16% on naira balances and 7% on dollar and stablecoin balances. It also expanded its USDT and USDC payment capabilities, improved its invoicing and payment links, and introduced new card options. The announcements extend the company’s services beyond cross-border payments. “We were focused on receiving, but then again, receiving is just the beginning, not the end,” Oyome said at Moonshot. “The end is after receiving. When we started raenest, we focused on receiving not the end. Now, we’ve solved spending, now we’re focusing on the problem of earning.” Founded in 2022, Raenest helps individuals, freelancers, creators, and businesses receive, send, store, and spend money across borders. The company says it has more than 1.5 million customers and has processed about $3 billion since inception. Oyome said Raenest was built to help people overcome barriers to participating in the global economy by providing accounts in their own names that connect them to international markets. The company initially focused on helping users receive international payments. Its newer products are intended to address how users store their money and earn returns on it. “Without the ability to earn or connect to global banking industries across the world, there is no opportunity to earn,” he said. Oyome also said that the environment for companies operating in the crypto industry was also changing, with governments across Africa becoming more open to discussions about digital assets. In July, Nigeria signed a Virtual Assets Coordination prder that established a framework to coordinate oversight among financial, revenue, and capital markets agencies. The order also provided for a regulatory sandbox in which eligible virtual-asset businesses can test products under supervision. Ghana has also introduced its Virtual Asset Service Providers Act, 2025, which provides for the licensing and supervision of businesses operating in the sector. “Today, the governments across Africa are adopting. I think governments are happy to have conversations about crypto. It’s a success because we are coming from a very different time” Oyome said. “It’s a good time for people playing in the stablecoin space.” The growing use of stablecoins presents an opportunity for Raenest to improve its payment operations. Oyome said stablecoins help Raenest settle payments faster. “What we’ve seen as the biggest value is speed,” Oyome said. He explained that stablecoins allow the company to collect and settle funds faster, improving its cash flow and giving it quicker access to money that would otherwise take days to arrive. As Raenest combines traditional currencies with stablecoins, Oyome said the company wants to shield customers from the technical complexity behind moving money across different networks. “It can feel complicated. We don’t want it to be complicated. We have a blend of fiat and stablecoins,” he said. He expects financial services to evolve towards a model in which users can move money without having to understand the underlying payment infrastructure or distinguish between different stablecoins.

articles.title: John Wick, Spider-Man, O'Brother : cette femme se cache derrière les couleurs de vos films préférés
articles.text:
John Wick, Spider-Man, O'Brother : cette femme se cache derrière les couleurs de vos films préférés
Comment les couleurs participent-elles à l’identité visuelle des films Marvel ou de John Wick ? Le quatrième épisode de Color Matters donne la parole à Jill Bogdanowicz, une coloriste hollywoodienne qui considère son travail comme une véritable peinture numérique.
La troisième saison de Color Matters – Masters of Color se poursuit avec un quatrième épisode consacré à Jill Bogdanowicz, coloriste senior chez Company 3 et récompensée pour son travail d'étalonnage. Après avoir exploré la science de l'image avec John Quartel, cette nouvelle vidéo revient sur le rôle artistique de la couleur au cinéma.
De Marvel à John Wick
Jill Bogdanowicz compare volontiers son métier à celui d'un peintre. À partir des images capturées sur le tournage, elle travaille les couleurs, les contrastes et la luminosité pour accompagner la narration et les émotions recherchées par le réalisateur.
Elle revient notamment sur son travail sur plusieurs productions Marvel, comme Spider-Man: No Way Home, Black Widow et Thor: Love and Thunder, où la collaboration avec les équipes d'effets spéciaux joue un rôle essentiel.
L'épisode évoque également O'Brother, sur lequel elle a accompagné l'évolution de l'étalonnage numérique aux côtés du directeur de la photographie Roger Deakins, ainsi que les films John Wick.

articles.title: Ataque à Binance: Trump comenta suspeita de envolvimento de hackers norte-coreanos
articles.text:
O governo dos Estados Unidos está investigando se hackers ligados à Coreia do Norte foram responsáveis por um ataque que desviou cerca de US$ 6,3 bilhões (aproximadamente R$ 34 bilhões) da Binance, maior corretora de criptomoedas do mundo. A possibilidade foi comentada pelo presidente Donald Trump nesta sexta-feira (30), enquanto empresas especializadas em análise de blockchain apontam indícios de envolvimento de um grupo hacker norte-coreano.
Questionado por jornalistas no Salão Oval da Casa Branca sobre a possível participação da Coreia do Norte, Trump respondeu que o governo estava investigando o caso. “Estamos analisando isso”, afirmou. O presidente também reconheceu que houve um ataque hacker, mas não confirmou a autoria.
A suspeita ganhou força após análises da TRM Labs e da Chainalysis, duas empresas especializadas em rastreamento de transações com criptomoedas. As companhias identificaram semelhanças entre o incidente e operações anteriores atribuídas a hackers norte-coreanos.
A TRM Labs apontou o grupo TraderTraitor, unidade de hackers de elite ligada à Coreia do Norte. A empresa afirmou ter alto grau de confiança nessa atribuição, conclusão que também foi compartilhada pela Chainalysis. A Binance, porém, ainda não confirmou quem realizou o ataque.
Como aconteceu o roubo bilionário?
- Os invasores conseguiram retirar aproximadamente US$ 6,3 bilhões em criptomoedas de carteiras utilizadas pela Binance para processar transações. A maior parte das transferências aconteceu em cerca de 20 minutos, a partir do final da quinta-feira (29);
- Uma investigação inicial da corretora indicou que o ataque pode ter começado com o comprometimento do computador de um engenheiro da empresa. Posteriormente, a Binance identificou outros possíveis pontos de invasão;
- O co-CEO Richard Teng descreveu o episódio como um ataque complexo, que envolveu a manipulação de um sistema responsável por aprovar transações. Dessa maneira, os criminosos conseguiram movimentar recursos de uma carteira conectada à internet sem passar pelos controles habituais de autorização;
- A empresa também relatou o uso de software capaz de apagar rastros e evidências das atividades dos invasores, dificultando o trabalho de investigação;
- O ataque atingiu carteiras conectadas à internet, conhecidas como hot wallets. Elas permitem movimentações mais rápidas de criptomoedas, mas ficam mais expostas a ameaças digitais do que as chamadas cold wallets, que mantêm os ativos offline.
Binance promete cobrir as perdas
Após identificar o ataque, a Binance suspendeu temporariamente os saques e iniciou operação para localizar e bloquear os ativos roubados.
A corretora informou que conseguiu localizar aproximadamente US$ 3 bilhões (R$ 16,2 bilhões) dos recursos desviados com a ajuda de parceiros. Entre as empresas que bloquearam ativos estão a Tether, que congelou cerca de US$ 1,57 bilhão, e a Circle, responsável por bloquear mais de US$ 800 milhões.
A Binance também afirmou que reservou aproximadamente US$ 6,34 bilhões (R$ 34,3 bilhões) em recursos próprios para cobrir as perdas e garantir que os clientes não sejam prejudicados.
“Nunca usamos recursos dos clientes, portanto eles não são afetados”, declarou Richard Teng em publicação no X.
Na manhã desta sexta-feira, a empresa informou que esperava retomar os serviços de saque nas 48 horas seguintes. Até então, não havia esclarecido o destino dos US$ 3,3 bilhões restantes.
O FBI confirmou que estava ciente do incidente e em contato com parceiros públicos e privados para avaliar a dimensão do ataque e coordenar medidas investigativas. Segundo a Reuters, a Binance também trabalha com o Serviço Secreto dos Estados Unidos.
Leia mais:
- Ataque hacker na Binance mostra ‘transformação’ nas ameaças digitais
- Binance garante segurança de brasileiros após ataque de R$ 33 bi
- Modelo de IA chinês realiza ataques em simulações e ignora regras de segurança
Coreia do Norte é suspeita de outros ataques
A possível participação de hackers norte-coreanos chama a atenção porque o país já foi associado a outros grandes roubos de criptomoedas.
Em fevereiro de 2025, a corretora Bybit sofreu ataque que resultou no desvio de aproximadamente US$ 1,5 bilhão (R$ 8,1 bilhões) em ativos digitais. Na ocasião, o FBI atribuiu a operação à Coreia do Norte e ao grupo TraderTraitor.
Segundo empresas de análise de blockchain, o ataque à Binance apresenta características semelhantes às observadas naquele episódio.
A Coreia do Norte, por sua vez, nega rotineiramente acusações de envolvimento em ataques cibernéticos. Representantes do país na Suíça e na China não responderam aos pedidos de comentário enviados pela Reuters.
O roubo também provocou preocupação no mercado de criptomoedas. O Bitcoin chegou a atingir US$ 76.368 (R$ 413 mil), sua menor cotação em seis semanas, enquanto o Ether recuou mais de 3%, chegando a US$ 2.178 (R$ 11,8 mil).
O episódio pode ampliar as dúvidas sobre a segurança dos ativos mantidos em corretoras centralizadas. Para analistas, um ataque dessa dimensão pode reduzir a confiança dos investidores e aumentar a pressão por mecanismos mais rigorosos de proteção.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: $6 Billion Binance Hack Bears Hallmarks of North Korea’s TraderTraitor
articles.text:
Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, has been hit by the biggest crypto heist ever recorded, and blockchain intelligence firms say North Korean state-sponsored hackers are the likely culprits.
Binance has put the damage at roughly $6.3 billion. TRM Labs, which followed each transfer on-chain, calculated about $6.36 billion siphoned from Binance wallets across ten blockchains on October 29. Most of the money left within roughly 20 minutes.
The haul dwarfs the $1.5 billion taken from Bybit in February 2025, which previously held the record. Binance has halted withdrawals and pledged to reimburse all losses using company funds and its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU).
The exchange’s early findings suggest the intrusion may have started with an employee’s laptop.
“Binance’s initial investigation suggests that the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions. We have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak,” Binance stated.
TRM’s analysis shows the attackers spent at least a day and a half getting ready. The wallet used to run the operation was funded with a few small Tornado Cash withdrawals, and the malicious code was trialed on other wallets before going live.
On Ethereum, the attackers leveraged EIP-7702, a mechanism through which a standard wallet can delegate its behavior to a smart contract by signing a permission. They sent a batch of 50 such permissions, all signed beforehand by a Binance hot wallet, so that one would match the wallet’s transaction count at execution time.
The Binance wallet ended up delegated to a contract that only the attackers could command, which they used to empty it.
According to TRM, the Ethereum activity initially looked like the result of phishing. That theory does not account for the other nine blockchains, where Binance wallets sent funds to the attackers through regular, validly signed transactions.
“These wallets use different chains, key types and signing schemes. All of them produced valid signatures for the attacker within about half an hour. In TRM’s assessment, the most likely explanation is that the attacker gained the ability to make Binance’s hot wallet signing system sign transactions of its choosing across chains,” TRM said.
Researchers point to North Korea
“TRM attributes the attack to TraderTraitor, North Korea’s elite hacking unit, based on robust on and off-chain intelligence. We make this judgment with high confidence,” the blockchain intelligence firm said.
TRM found traits this attack shares with the Bybit heist and the KelpDAO hack from April 2026. These include a mixer-funded operator wallet, preparations made long before any money moved, and signatures collected ahead of time and then used all at once.
The laundering seen so far sets this operation apart. Instead of leaning on cross-chain bridges as in the Bybit case, the hackers have mainly relied on big trades with market makers and on lending platforms.
Chainalysis CEO Jonathan Levin said his company also believes TraderTraitor is the likely perpetrator, citing ties to an earlier hack. Chainalysis investigators found proceeds from last month’s Bitget exploit mixed with funds taken from Binance.
Blockchain sleuth ZachXBT also named the Lazarus Group as the probable attacker.
The FBI attributed the Bybit theft to TraderTraitor. Binance has not publicly identified the hackers, saying it is cooperating with law enforcement to determine who they are.
Billions frozen, billions still movable
Stablecoin issuers were quick to act. By 00:30 UTC on October 30, TRM tallied around $2.7 billion in frozen assets, including roughly 1.77 billion USDT locked by Tether and about 825 million USDC locked by Circle.
Ripple and World Liberty Financial froze smaller amounts, and Arbitrum’s Security Council used its emergency powers to move about $30 million out of an attacker wallet. Binance estimates the frozen total at roughly $3 billion.
To stay ahead of the issuers, the attackers sold USDT for ETH at more than 10% below market price. TRM says they still hold over 420,000 ETH and 18,270 BTC, about $2.4 billion in assets that no issuer can freeze.

articles.title: Ruidos extraños y pérdidas de agua: señales de que tu lavadora necesita mantenimiento
articles.text:
La lavadora soporta cientos de ciclos de lavado al año, pero ese uso constante termina por desgastar sus componentes internos. Reconocer a tiempo las señales de desgaste permite evitar averías mayores, reparaciones costosas y la necesidad de reemplazar el equipo antes de tiempo, además de garantizar que la ropa salga limpia.
La mayoría de las fallas en este electrodoméstico no ocurren de forma repentina: casi siempre existen alertas previas que anticipan un problema. Ignorarlas puede derivar en daños por agua o en averías que comprometen la seguridad del hogar. Saber identificar estos síntomas ayuda a prolongar la vida útil del aparato.
La acumulación de humedad genera malos olores
Los olores a moho o humedad dentro de la lavadora suelen originarse por residuos acumulados en la junta de la puerta, el dispensador de detergente o el tambor. Ventilar el equipo después de cada uso y limpiar la junta con un paño seco reduce la proliferación de hongos y bacterias. Realizar ciclos de limpieza con agua caliente una vez al mes también contribuye a eliminar olores persistentes.
La ropa sale sucia o con mal olor tras el lavado
Cuando las prendas salen con manchas, olor desagradable o sin la limpieza esperada, el problema puede estar en el agitador, el impulsor o en residuos acumulados en el tambor. Sobrecargar la lavadora o usar demasiado detergente reduce la eficacia del lavado. Limpiar el tambor con regularidad usando vinagre blanco o productos especiales, y evitar cargas excesivas, ayuda a mantener un rendimiento óptimo.
Las fugas de agua indican mangueras o sellos dañados
La presencia de charcos o humedad alrededor del equipo señala fugas que pueden originarse en mangueras agrietadas, sellos desgastados o conexiones mal ajustadas. Inspeccionar todas las conexiones junto con el sello de la puerta permite localizar el origen del problema. Sustituir las mangueras de goma por otras de acero inoxidable aumenta la durabilidad y previene futuros escapes. Si el origen de la fuga no se identifica, conviene recurrir a un servicio técnico.
El llenado o el drenaje de agua presentan fallas
Una lavadora que no se llena de manera correcta, que deja agua estancada o que tarda demasiado en drenar suele tener filtros obstruidos, válvulas defectuosas o mangueras dobladas. El primer paso consiste en revisar y limpiar el filtro de desagüe y las mangueras de suministro. Si el problema persiste, puede ser necesaria la intervención de un técnico para revisar la bomba o la válvula de entrada.
Los ruidos extraños durante el ciclo anticipan averías mayores
Zumbidos, rechinidos, golpeteos o chirridos no son normales en un equipo en buen estado. Estos sonidos pueden indicar rodamientos desgastados, varillas de suspensión rotas, una correa de transmisión defectuosa o bloqueos en la bomba de desagüe. Actuar con rapidez ante estos ruidos evita que una avería menor se convierta en un daño estructural más grave y costoso.
La vibración excesiva revela problemas de nivelación
Cuando la lavadora vibra de manera inusual, se desplaza sola o emite golpes fuertes durante el centrifugado, es probable que exista un problema de nivelación o de suspensión interna. Los amortiguadores o resortes desgastados, un tambor desbalanceado o una superficie desigual pueden explicar el fenómeno.
Ajustar las patas niveladoras suele corregir el inconveniente, pero si la vibración continúa, conviene solicitar una revisión profesional para evitar daños en el tambor o en el suelo.
No esperar a que la lavadora se detenga por completo resulta clave para evitar daños mayores y prolongar su vida útil. Atender los síntomas desde su aparición permite resolver las fallas de forma sencilla y económica. Ante cualquier señal de advertencia, la consulta con un profesional es la opción recomendada para mantener el equipo en condiciones óptimas de funcionamiento.

articles.title: Google’s latest Nest Learning Thermostat is $60 off just in time for sweater weather
articles.text:
As the weather cools, it may be worth investing in a smart thermostat to help lower your energy bills. Right now, Google’s fourth-gen Nest Learning Thermostat is on sale in all three colors for $219.99 ($60 off) at Amazon, Best Buy, and The Home Depot, matching its best price of the year and just $10 shy of its all-time low.
Google’s latest Nest Learning Thermostat is $60 off just in time for sweater weather
We also found deals on Casio’s retro step-tracking watch and a four-pack of AirTags.
Google’s latest Nest Learning Thermostat is its most capable to date, and comes with new features designed to lower energy consumption without sacrificing comfort. Like prior models, it learns your heating and cooling preferences over time and automatically creates a schedule based on your habits, so you don’t have to constantly adjust the temperature yourself. It can also suggest schedule changes to save energy and automatically adjusts the temperature when you’re away. Additionally, it includes a remote temperature sensor in the box, so you can better adjust the temperature in your preferred room, whether that’s the bedroom or another space in your home.
The Nest Learning Thermostat also improves on its predecessor with a beautifully designed adaptive display that shows your temperature settings, the weather, and the time from across the room. When you get closer, it reveals more detailed information, including outdoor air quality and humidity levels. The Matter-ready device also works with more HVAC systems than the third-gen model, along with a host of compatible humidifiers, dehumidifiers, and ventilation equipment. Plus, unlike many smart thermostats, it doesn’t require a C-wire in most homes either, though using one can help ensure consistent power.
Three more deals that aren’t as pricey
- You can get the black Casio WS-B1000 at Amazon and Walmart for just $23.88 ($41 off), which is its best price to date. The retro-style digital watch lacks advanced health sensors and features like contactless payments, but it does offer some basic fitness tracking, including a built-in step counter and Bluetooth connectivity for syncing your activity data with your phone; it also comes with a stopwatch and alarms. Read our review.
- We recently highlighted an ongoing deal on a single AirTag, but if you want to stock up, Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart are now selling a four-pack for $69.99 ($30 off), which is the lowest price we’ve seen. Apple’s second-gen AirTag is our top pick for iPhone owners thanks to its impressively precise tracking, which can guide you directly to a lost item. You can also locate items with an Apple Watch Series 9 or later and share an AirTag’s location with participating airlines, such as United and Delta, helping you recover lost luggage. Read our review.
- SwitchBot’s 12-inch RGBICWW Ceiling Light is available at Amazon for $36.99 ($12 off) when you clip the on-page coupon, or directly from SwitchBot for the same price with code HWHW26. The Matter-compatible smart light — which is also discounted in a 15-inch size — offers 26 preset scenes, eight lighting effects, and the ability to create your own. The main difference between the two sizes is the brightness: the 15-inch model delivers up to 3,200 lumens, compared to 2,000 lumens for the smaller version.

articles.title: Waymo taps Toyota to supply robotaxis for Japan and the UK | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Waymo will begin testing autonomous Toyota bZ4X vehicles in Japan next year as part of a broader partnership with the automaker to provide electric vehicles for robotaxi operations in international markets, including the U.K.
Under the partnership announced Friday, Toyota will manufacture the 2027 bZ4X vehicles and integrate Waymo’s self-driving system at its Takaoka factory in Japan. (The electric vehicle is now known as the bZ in the North American market.)
The autonomous bZ4X vehicles will initially be tested in Japan, where Waymo intends to eventually operate a robotaxi service. But the intent is to deploy these vehicles in other right-hand driving countries such as the U.K. Waymo has been testing its autonomous Jaguar I-Pace vehicles in London for months and plans to launch a robotaxi service there once it receives the necessary permits.
The announcement comes 18 months after Toyota and Waymo signed a preliminary agreement to explore the development and deployment of an autonomous vehicle platform. At the time, the agreement fell into the “let’s see what happens” category, with language vague enough to leave plenty of room for interpretation.
For now, the partnership looks more like a conventional vehicle supplier deal that helps Waymo fill specific regional needs while adding a new model to its robotaxi portfolio.
But the partnership could go beyond robotaxis. The companies said they will continue to look at bringing Waymo’s autonomous technology to personally owned Toyota vehicles.
Toyota and Waymo also announced plans to look at other future “initiatives” that would use “insights from Waymo’s real-world operations” to improve safety for other road users. What that might mean is unclear, although Hiroki Nakajima, executive vice president of Toyota and a board member, provided some clues.
“This collaboration will help scale that technology and bring it to customers in Japan and beyond through Waymo’s ride-hailing service, and in parallel, Toyota will continue to explore how integrating vehicles with traffic infrastructure can make those roads safer still,” he said in a statement.

articles.title: Cloudflare services for private origins is now generally available
articles.text:
Cloudflare services for private origins is now generally available
Today, Cloudflare services for private origins is generally available. Point a proxied DNS record at a private IP, and Cloudflare reaches the origin over your existing Cloudflare One connection. Your origin stays private, while web application firewall (WAF), caching, bot management, and Workers work just as they do for public origins.
In June, we launched this capability in closed beta to address a problem we kept hearing from customers: Their internal APIs, AI agent backends, MCP servers, and operational tools weren’t built to face the Internet, but those services still need to accept requests from partners, customers, or agents over the Internet. Before the beta, putting Cloudflare in front of these services meant exposing a public IP, opening a firewall port, or running cloudflared alongside the origin.
Those requirements often left private applications without the same protections and controls they used for public applications, including WAF, bot management, rate limiting, caching, traffic acceleration, rewrites, and Workers.
What is generally available today
During the closed beta, eligible customers requested access through their account team. Today, we’re opening access beyond that beta group.
Point a proxied A or AAAA record at a private IP, and Cloudflare’s application services work as they do for public origins:
- WAF and managed rules
- Bot management
- Rate limiting
- Caching
- Transform and rewrite rules
- Workers
Some limitations remain. Argo Smart Routing and Dedicated CDN Egress IPs aren’t supported, and origin health checks require Load Balancing. See the developer documentation for the full list of current limitations.
Your origin keeps its private IP, with no inbound firewall exception required. With Cloudflare WAN, no connector software on the origin is required. With Cloudflare Mesh, a connector runs within your private network and can serve multiple origins.
How it works
Create a proxied A or AAAA record pointing to your origin. For supported private IP ranges, use private network routing is enabled automatically. If your origin uses a public IP that’s reachable only through your private network, you can enable the setting manually.
The rest of the request flow stays the same: TLS termination, WAF, rules, and caching continue to run on Cloudflare’s network.
The setting turns on automatically for RFC 1918 private IPv4 addresses, RFC 6598 CGNAT addresses (100.64.0.0/10), and RFC 4193 unique local IPv6 addresses (fc00::/7). It can’t be turned off for these ranges; attempts to disable it through the API return an error.
What the API looks like
For customers automating deployments through the API, private routing is simply an additional attribute on a standard DNS record.
POST /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records
{
 "type": "A",
 "name": "app.example.com",
 "content": "10.0.0.50",
 "ttl": 300,
 "proxied": true,
 "private_routing": true
}
Behind the scenes, Cloudflare's proxy platform determines where to send traffic for app.example.com by querying Cloudflare's Origin API. The response includes metadata indicating that the destination should be reached through a private network path:
{
 "zone_name": "example.com",
 "ipv4_addresses": ["10.0.0.50"],
 "private_routing": true
}
The private_routing flag is the key signal. When our proxy sees it, instead of attempting to connect directly to the private IP address over the public Internet, it hands the request to our private networking layer, which then routes the connection across the customer's existing private network connectivity, whether that's IPsec, GRE, Cloudflare Tunnel, CNI, or Cloudflare Mesh.
The beta post covers the routing layer in more detail.
Get started
Before you begin, you’ll need:
- The Private Origins entitlement on your account. Ask your account team to turn it on.
- Cloudflare One connectivity using IPsec, GRE, CNI, Cloudflare Tunnel, or Cloudflare Mesh.
- Unified Routing enabled on your account, unless you connect over Cloudflare Tunnel (Tunnel doesn't need it). New and existing accounts can upgrade through their account team.
- If you connect over Cloudflare WAN or Cloudflare Mesh, configure a return route for Cloudflare’s source ranges: 100.64.0.0/12 for IPv4 and 2606:4700:cf1:5000::/64 for IPv6. Then, create a proxied A or AAAA record for the private IP and confirm that Use private network routing is enabled. Your existing WAF, cache, and bot management configuration applies to that hostname without further changes.
Then, create a proxied A or AAAA record for the private IP and confirm that Use private network routing is enabled. Your existing WAF, cache, and bot management configuration applies to that hostname without further changes.
One note from the beta: if requests time out and nothing arrives at the origin, check the return route first. A missing route for Cloudflare’s source range was the most common setup failure we saw.
Once enabled, follow our developer documentation, which walks through the full setup.
What comes next
Today’s release covers public traffic reaching private origins. Next, we’re working on private-to-private traffic: users, services, and AI agents on private networks reaching applications on other private networks through Cloudflare’s application services.
Engineering work is underway, and we’re targeting a closed beta in early 2027. If you’d like to participate, talk to your account team.
The goal is to give private applications the same protections and controls as public applications. An employee opening wiki.company.internal, for example, could benefit from WAF, rate limiting, and bot management. Service-to-service traffic between clouds and data centers could use those controls too, even when neither side touches the public Internet.
For now, today’s release brings the WAF, caching, bot management, and Workers you use for public applications to private origins over connectivity you already operate.
Questions or feedback? Join the conversation in our community forums or reach out to your account team.

articles.title: Things That Go Beep in the Night: Agentic AI Joins the Search for Extraterrestrial Signals
articles.text:
While science fiction lore tells us that humans will meet extraterrestrial life in the form of little green men, the detail that should raise hairs this Halloween is this: the search for extraterrestrial intelligence took a major leap forward with AI, and it increasingly focuses on AI agents built by humans listening for AI agents built by aliens.
Some scientists have suggested that extraterrestrial civilizations, if they exist, could be billions of years older than humanity. Such civilizations might have developed technologies far beyond humanity’s, including forms of AI.
Breakthrough Listen and the SETI Institute are bringing agentic AI into the daily search for extraterrestrial intelligence. At the Allen Telescope Array in Northern California, agents can now steer the instrument, enhance and correct incoming data, and apply AI models to the incoming stream — all from a single natural language request. The NVIDIA Holoscan platform processes the massive streams of sensor data, giving agents live data to act on.
The result is a faster, more adaptable search for potential signals from extraterrestrial life and technologies.
“As our new agentic observatories reach out into the universe, what they find may have much more in common with themselves than with the humans who created them,” said Andrew Siemion, Bernard M. Oliver chair for SETI at the SETI Institute and principal investigator of Breakthrough Listen. “But this isn’t something to fear. Rather, it’s a breakthrough in translation.”
Terabits a Second, Processed in Flight
Radio telescopes generate enormous volumes of data, creating a challenge for scientists who need to identify potentially interesting signals as observations unfold.
At the Allen Telescope Array, DAQIRI, a Holoscan platform library, enables the telescope to pull terabits per second of sensor data straight into GPU memory so observations are processed in flight rather than filling hard drives. CyberEther, a signal-processing framework developed at the SETI Institute, does the math using NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries including cuFFT and cuBLAS.
Nexus, a web-based observatory orchestrator, acts as the agent harness. It gives agents a single source of truth for instrument state, compute resources and pipelines and lets researchers monitor packet loss, read live spectrograms and rewrite signal-processing blocks — all by prompting in natural language. The system can handle 2.4 terabits per second on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs, with inference running on premises, next to the instrument.
Put together, the system enables an agent to steer a telescope’s antennae, calibrate and focus the instrument for a clean signal, catch and fix data errors and plot the result. Agents compress what would take humans weeks or years into hours.
Science Fact, Not Fiction
The pipeline has already proven itself, achieving the first real-time AI detection of a pulsar — a rapidly spinning stellar remnant that pulses like a cosmic lighthouse — in the Crab Nebula.
Next, the team is evaluating open models including NVIDIA Nemotron for cases where data locality and turnaround matter most and for observatories that may someday run offline on the far side of the moon.
Learn more about NVIDIA AI for science.

articles.title: Aneel confirma bandeira verde na conta de luz em novembro
articles.text:
A conta de luz dos brasileiros continuará sem cobrança adicional em novembro. A Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel) anunciou, nesta sexta-feira (30), que manterá a bandeira tarifária verde pelo segundo mês consecutivo. A decisão significa que os consumidores não terão taxas extras relacionadas ao sistema de bandeiras tarifárias na fatura de energia elétrica.
Segundo a agência, a manutenção da bandeira verde ocorre por causa das condições favoráveis de geração de energia, impulsionadas pelo aumento das chuvas nas regiões onde estão concentradas as principais usinas hidrelétricas.
Com os reservatórios em situação mais equilibrada, não há necessidade de acionar em maior escala as usinas termelétricas, que produzem energia a custos mais elevados.
De maio a setembro, a bandeira tarifária permaneceu amarela, o que representava cobrança adicional de R$ 1,88 a cada 100 kWh consumidos. Em outubro, a Aneel já havia reduzido a classificação para verde.
Leia mais:
- Brasil e Turquia se unem para ampliar negócios e tecnologia nuclear
- Brasil procura um tesouro energético escondido no subsolo que pode revolucionar a geração de eletricidade no país
- O novo tipo de painel solar que pode gerar 25% mais energia
Como funciona o sistema de bandeiras tarifárias?
Criado pela Aneel, o sistema de bandeiras tarifárias informa aos consumidores as condições de geração de energia elétrica no país e os custos envolvidos na produção.
Quando o volume de chuvas diminui, os reservatórios das hidrelétricas podem ficar mais baixos, reduzindo a capacidade de geração dessas usinas. Nesses períodos, é necessário recorrer às termelétricas, que possuem custos operacionais mais elevados.
Para sinalizar essas condições e cobrir os custos adicionais, a agência utiliza bandeiras de diferentes cores, que podem representar cobranças extras na conta de luz.
Quanto custa cada bandeira tarifária?
Os valores adicionais variam conforme as condições de geração de energia:
- Bandeira verde: não há cobrança adicional;
- Bandeira amarela: R$ 1,88 a cada 100 kWh consumidos;
- Bandeira vermelha, patamar 1: R$ 4,46 a cada 100 kWh;
- Bandeira vermelha, patamar 2: R$ 7,87 a cada 100 kWh.
Com a bandeira verde mantida em novembro, os consumidores não terão esses acréscimos na conta de energia elétrica.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Une vitesse réglable à la pression et un pied amovible : le Braun MultiQuick 7 est à 56,20 €
articles.text:
Le mixeur plongeant Braun MultiQuick 7 MQ7000X est à 56,20 € (-14 %)
Pour mixer soupes, sauces et smoothies, le Braun MultiQuick 7 MQ7000X avec gobelet de 600 ml est proposé à 56,20 € chez Amazon.
Amazon affiche ce mixeur plongeant à 8,79 € sous le prix conseillé indiqué de 64,99 €, soit environ 14 % de réduction. Le tarif baisse également de 5,47 € par rapport au plus bas prix des 30 derniers jours affiché, de 61,67 €, soit près de 9 %. L’appareil est vendu et expédié par Amazon, avec la livraison gratuite.
Une vitesse qui varie avec la pression du doigt
Le mixeur plongeant Braun MultiQuick 7 MQ7000X dispose d’un moteur de 1 000 W et de la commande Easy SmartSpeed. La vitesse augmente à mesure que l’on appuie sur le bouton, sans devoir sélectionner un cran sur une molette.
Son pied ActiveBlade permet à la lame de se déplacer verticalement pendant le mixage. La cloche en acier inoxydable intègre également le système SplashControl, conçu pour limiter les projections. Ces dispositifs accompagnent la préparation de veloutés, de sauces ou de boissons mixées.
Un ensemble simple avec gobelet de 600 ml
Cette version comprend le pied mixeur et un gobelet gradué de 600 ml. Elle ne comporte pas de fouet ni de bol hachoir : mieux vaut donc vérifier le contenu du coffret si ces accessoires font partie de vos besoins.
Le système EasyClick Plus permet de détacher le pied du bloc moteur pour le nettoyer. Les éléments compatibles peuvent passer au lave-vaisselle, à l’exception notamment du moteur. Sur Amazon, la fiche affiche une moyenne de 4,4/5 sur 1 459 évaluations.
